factors.trading_idea: Basket/program trades (ETF creation-redemption arbitrage, index programs) execute every constituent in proportion to its capitalisation weight, not in proportion to its fundamental beta, so the price displacement they cause is roughly weight-per-unit-depth, i.e. proportional to the inverse of a name's dollar turnover. Fundamental market-wide news, by contrast, should move a name by its beta. I therefore detect program bars from the *shape* of the cross-sectional volume-allocation vector (does today's deviation of each name's dollar-volume share from its own trailing norm point in the direction of the index-weight vector?), accumulate the program-weighted market return over bars t-7..t-2 (lagged so the fast Epps/staleness catch-up has already completed), and fade it in proportion to each name's mechanical elasticity in *excess* of its estimated beta. The claim is falsifiable: the wedge (inverse-turnover rank minus beta rank) must beat inverse-turnover alone and must beat beta alone, the program-shape weighting must beat equal weighting of the same market moves, and inverting the sign must lose. It survives arbitrage because market-neutral books hedge index exposure with beta, leaving the weight/depth heterogeneity of mechanical basket impact un-hedged, and harvesting it requires simultaneous many-name execution inside a one-minute window.
factors.name: Index-flow impact elasticity vs beta wedge snapback

factors.trading_idea: Basket/program executions allocate dollars by capitalisation weight rather than by fundamental beta, so their price displacement loads on a name's weight-per-unit-depth elasticity kappa = marketCap / dollar-volume, a characteristic that is orthogonal to beta only after explicit projection. Rather than *assuming* the mechanical push equals kappa times the cap-weighted market return (the parent's single common scalar, which makes every cross-sectional bet a static pattern timed by a beta-like market signal), I *measure* it: each bar I run a cross-sectional regression of returns on the beta-orthogonalised elasticity exposure and read off the realised 'mechanical factor return' g_t — the actual displacement per unit of impact elasticity, cleanly separated from the information (beta) channel. Accumulating g_t with an exponential memory only over bars whose cross-sectional volume-allocation vector tilts toward the cap-weight vector (the basket footprint) isolates uncompensated liquidity demand, which must relax; the signal is minus the name's orthogonal elasticity exposure times that accumulation. It survives arbitrage because market-neutral books hedge index exposure with beta, leaving the depth-heterogeneous mechanical component un-hedged, and capturing it requires simultaneous many-name execution inside a one-minute window.
factors.name: Program-gated elasticity factor-return snapback

factors.trading_idea: The parent's edge was a beta-lag catch-up, but its trailing 6-bar wedge is a crude proxy for the unincorporated part of the market shock, so its predictive mass drifted to ~12 bars. Instead of a wedge, estimate each name's distributed-lag impulse response to the cap-weighted market (loadings b_1..b_6 on lagged market returns) and analytically fold those loadings against the *already observed* market path to form E[sum of next 6 bar returns] — a forecast whose kernel is matched by construction to the fixed 6-bar offset, so no adjustment mass is left outside the evaluation window. The response persists because slow repricers (names whose mid does not update on many bars, whose recent traded volume is thin relative to normal, and whose holder base is mandate-constrained income capital) are exactly where staleness accumulates and where second-scale arbitrage capital is least attentive; the effect is falsified if the lagged loadings carry no more information than a single lag-1 beta, or if the staleness/clientele gate does not discriminate.
factors.name: Horizon-Matched Lagged-Beta Kernel Catch-Up (staleness gated)

factors.trading_idea: The parent showed that income-clientele names carry an unclosed beta-implied gap after a market move, but because their holders are slow, the gap's *unconditional* closing time is long (IC peaked at 12 bars) — the clientele score tells you WHO has a gap, not WHEN it closes. The child adds the missing timing variable: a gap only closes when an intermediary actually shows up, so I condition the residual gap on (a) a Hawkes-style trade-arrival intensity in the name itself (EWM volume over its own long-run ADV) and (b) evidence that repair has already begun (this bar's beta-residual return pointing in the gap's direction). Conditional on arrival plus initiation, the *remaining* gap is a first-passage problem with a short expected completion time, which pulls the predictive mass onto the fixed 6-bar offset instead of 12+. It survives arbitrage because the profitable subset is exactly the intersection of slow-holder names, a fresh market shock and a live liquidity event — a state that is only identifiable jointly and is too transient and capacity-limited for slow discretionary capital to pre-empt.
factors.name: Clientele Gap Repair Hazard Relay

factors.trading_idea: The parent measured per-name lag-6 autocorrelation of the idiosyncratic displacement over 100 minutes of bars: with an effective sample of ~100 non-overlapping observations its standard error (~0.1) dwarfs the true coefficient (~0.02), so the estimate was essentially static noise plus a static fundamental prior — which is exactly why its IC was ~0 at the pinned 6-bar offset and only appeared at 12 bars as a slow tilt. The child estimates the same horizon-matched response coefficient by *pooling the cross-section*: at every bar I regress each name's realised standardised 6-bar residual move on its own non-overlapping displacement six bars earlier, across all names, so one bar yields N observations instead of one, and I smooth those Fama–MacBeth slopes exponentially to obtain a coefficient that is both precise and genuinely time-varying. Because the reversal↔continuation crossover point of idiosyncratic displacement moves with the state of liquidity provision, the pooled slope is estimated separately for slow, mandate-constrained payout clienteles versus fast holders and for currently active versus quiet names (traded displacement is informational and continues; quiet quote drift snaps back), then shrunk toward the all-name pooled slope. The forecast is the fitted conditional expectation kappa_state × current displacement, so the signal flips sign endogenously in real time at exactly the 6-bar offset; the edge survives arbitrage because it requires simultaneous beta-residualisation and cross-sectional coefficient estimation at second frequency, and the clientele composition that generates the dispersion cannot re-optimise intraday. Falsified if the time-varying pooled slope has no relation to realised 6-bar residual continuation (i.e. a constant coefficient does as well), or if the clientele/activity split adds nothing over the all-name slope.
factors.name: Pooled cross-sectional 6-bar response coefficient, clientele × activity gated

factors.trading_idea: The parent assumed that a well-revisited price level supplies a restoring force; the realised sign says the opposite, and the correct reading is Kyle/Glosten rather than 'pinning': a level the mid keeps returning to is a level that is expensive to leave, so a displacement that ends there had to consume genuine resting depth and is therefore informative and permanent, whereas a displacement achieved for almost no volume in a rarely-visited region is a cheap, inventory-driven excursion that is refilled away. The child therefore measures the *price paid* for the last minute of displacement two independent ways — volume per unit of realised path length (a path-form inverse-Amihud depth estimate) and the local-time recurrence density of the level the price arrived at — and relays the move only when the move was expensive, fading it when it was free. Because endpoint mid-quotes carry bid-ask/quote-flicker noise that mechanically fights continuation at a 60-second offset (which is why the parent's |IC| only grew past 12 bars), the move itself is measured as the displacement of a 3-bar averaged typical price rather than close-to-close, isolating the slow propagator component at the fixed horizon. The edge survives arbitrage because it is a few ticks per episode, requires per-name real-time estimation of both a nonparametric path statistic and a volume-normalised depth, and its cause — permanent impact accruing after real depth is consumed by split metaorders — is a structural property of order books, not a mispricing that can be deleted.
factors.name: Liquidity-cost-confirmed smoothed displacement relay

factors.trading_idea: Parent A shows that the signed beta-implied catch-up wedge pays when the shareholder base is mandate-constrained income capital, while Parent B's negative IC says its extra machinery — the response beyond the truncated horizon — carries the OPPOSITE sign: at 10-second scale a name that has already OVER-delivered its beta-implied response is not a liquidity-provider overshoot owed back, it is a name carrying genuine idiosyncratic information that arrived alongside the market shock, so it keeps going. The child therefore splits the wedge on the sign of the delivered-versus-implied gap (measured against a whitened-innovation distributed-lag long-run beta, which is unbiased at second scale where contemporaneous beta is Epps-attenuated) into an under-delivery leg and an over-delivery leg, and lets a slow-capital state variable — payout clientele score blended with the impulse-response lag centroid — SCALE the under-delivery leg but ROUTE THE SIGN of the over-delivery leg (revert it for slow income clienteles whose overshoot is inventory-driven, continue it for fast growth clienteles whose overshoot is news). The interaction is the edge: A pooled both legs with one sign and so diluted the information leg, while B applied the extended-lag object uniformly across a cross-section dominated by fast clienteles and hence realized the flipped sign; conditioning the leg sign on clientele slowness makes the two mechanisms additive rather than cancelling.
factors.name: Clientele-routed over-delivery sign split of the beta catch-up wedge

factors.trading_idea: Parent A asserts a fixed sign convention — quiet-bar (quote-repricing) drift continues, active-bar (paid-impact) drift reverts — and therefore has to be read at whatever horizon that assumption happens to hold, which is why its edge migrates out to 24 bars; Parent B has the right statistic (Rice's scale-free link between adjacent sign-flip frequency and lag-1 correlation) but spends it as a blunt on/off gate that mostly shrinks the signal. The child instead *inverts* Rice's formula inside each volume stream, rho_sign = cos(pi * P(flip)), to obtain a robust, magnitude-insensitive estimate of each stream's own lag-1 persistence, and shrinks that estimate toward zero in proportion to its disagreement with the ordinary Pearson lag-1 correlation (large disagreement = the autocorrelation is carried by a handful of jumps / stale prints, i.e. exactly A's falsification case). Each stream's recent decay-weighted drift is then propagated through the horizon-matched AR(1) cumulative kernel K(rho) = rho(1 - rho^6)/(1 - rho), so continuation versus reversion and its magnitude are *estimated* per name and per stream rather than hard-coded, and the forecast is literally scaled to the fixed 6-bar offset. The interaction carries edge neither parent has: A cannot distinguish informative quote shading from stale-mid noise nor calibrate its sign to a 60-second offset, while B's pooled-gate use of the flip statistic throws away its real content — the sign-robust persistence coefficient itself, which is what converts a raw drift into a horizon-correct expected return.
factors.name: Rice-Inverted AR(1) Kernel Forecast of Volume-Stream Drift

factors.trading_idea: Inside a comparability cell the *ordering* of names by valuation multiple is a sticky structural object (a pecking order): a cell-wide repricing is a monotone shift that leaves the ordering invariant, so a name's rank displacement isolates purely idiosyncratic dislocation without assuming a common beta and is immune to the fat-tailed common shocks that contaminate median-demeaned spread levels. Mapping that rank displacement back into log-price units through the cell's current quantile-function slope (local peer density) gives a dislocation sized by how far the name actually had to travel to jump its neighbours — by construction a small, fast-relaxing perturbation whose reversion mass lands inside the next minute, unlike the parent's level-space spread whose reversion accrued over many minutes. The edge should exist only for names whose 6-bar rank drift is historically small (a genuine, persistent pecking order); if reversion strength is invariant to that ordinal-persistence gate, the signal is just repackaged peer-relative reversal and the hypothesis is falsified. It survives arbitrage because relative-value desks trade large multiple z-scores, while ordinal micro-inversions require continuously maintaining a cross-sectional quantile function in multiple space at 10-second resolution and carry per-trade profits below most participants' cost threshold.
factors.name: Pecking-Order Rank Inversion, Peer-Density Rescaled

factors.trading_idea: A dealer or stat-arb desk repairs a name's peer-idiosyncratic dislocation only if it can offset the resulting inventory cheaply, and the cheapest offset is another name in the same industry and same valuation tier that is dislocated in the OPPOSITE direction: that pair trade is self-financing and factor-neutral, so it consumes almost no risk capital and can be put on within seconds. When the same-tier peer cross-section is stretched one-sidedly (no opposite-signed substitute is live), the only offset is against the market factor, which costs risk capital, so the dislocation is not repaired on a one-minute clock. The child therefore measures, at each instant, the tradeable opposite-side dislocation capacity available to each name (in risk units, volume-weighted, leave-one-out, restricted to same industry and same valuation tier) and scales the peer-residual reversal by that capacity share. Falsifiable: the reversal coefficient on the 6-bar industry-residual return must increase monotonically in the netting-capacity share and vanish as that share goes to zero; the edge survives arbitrage because netting capacity is an exogenous state of the contemporaneous cross-section that no arbitrageur can manufacture on demand.
factors.name: Internal netting-counterparty capacity gated peer-residual snapback

factors.trading_idea: Observed mid = efficient price + a transient deviation (quote bounce, discreteness, unwinding impact); over a 60-second horizon the *only* reliably forecastable part of the observed mid change is the reversal of that deviation, which is exactly the term the parent subtracted out — hence its declared sign was contradicted. This child identifies the noise variance exactly (invariantly to how rough the efficient price is) from mean-absolute displacements at three geometrically spaced scales (1/4/16 bars), since Var(D_k)=A·k^(2H)+2σ²_ε implies the closed form 2σ²_ε=(V₄²−V₁V₁₆)/(2V₄−V₁−V₁₆); the resulting noise-to-signal ratio q fixes each name's steady-state local-level Kalman gain K=(√(q²+4q)−q)/2, so the transient deviation is measured as the price minus a per-name-bandwidth EWMA rather than a common-lookback deviation. The forecast is −ε̂ (fade the estimated transient) plus the fractional-Gaussian block memory ρ=2^(2H−1)−1 applied to the *filtered* efficient displacement (follow genuinely persistent efficient paths), all in units of the name's 6-bar efficient volatility. The edge persists because reversion desks apply one common filter bandwidth and one common reversion coefficient to the whole book: the residual is the cross-sectional dispersion of the optimal bandwidth and of the noise-purged roughness, worth only a few basis points per name and requiring continuous per-name re-estimation.
factors.name: Kalman-gain transient deviation with noise-purged path memory

factors.trading_idea: Split the sqrt-impact law by trade direction: for each bar measure the price move achieved per unit of sqrt(normalised traded volume), then take its exponentially-weighted conditional mean separately on down bars and up bars. When down-moves suddenly become much *cheaper* in volume terms than up-moves (a fresh one-sided liquidity vacuum), the fall was produced by depth withdrawal rather than by information, so it is mechanically reversed as depth refills; volume-backed one-sided moves are informative and are not. Because genuinely distressed capital structures (high debtToAssets / netDebtToEbitda) have structurally cheaper downside liquidity — equity is a call on assets, so credit-sensitive names legitimately gap on thin books — the innovation is demeaned nonparametrically inside sector x leverage-tercile buckets, leaving only the transient, unjustified component. Freshness matters at a 60-second horizon, so the residual is amplified when the last three bars actually moved in the vacuum's direction and damped when the move has already been absorbed. The edge persists because direction-split impact cost conditioned on balance-sheet distress buckets is not a screen short-horizon liquidity providers run; their reversion coefficients are direction-symmetric and leverage-blind.
factors.name: Leverage-bucketed asymmetric impact-cost vacuum snapback

factors.trading_idea: The parent proved that basket/program bars (detected from the cross-sectional geometry of dollar-volume-share deviations pointing toward the capitalisation-weight vector) contain mechanical, weight-per-depth price displacement that must relax; but it expressed that idea through a single per-bar scalar times an almost static elasticity-minus-beta rank, so its cross-section was one fixed portfolio being timed. The child moves the attribution to the name level: each name gets its own footprint score (the individual term of that cross-sectional correlation, positive only when its own volume anomaly points along its own index weight), and I accumulate only the *over*-push part of its beta-purged return — the component that moved further in the market's direction than its beta warrants — because the opposite sign (under-shoot) is stale-quote lag whose mechanics predict catch-up, not reversal, and pooling the two cancels the signal. The per-name over-push is scaled by its own idiosyncratic volatility and amplified by inverse-turnover elasticity, since for thin, high-weight-per-depth names a given excess co-move is far more likely mechanical than informational. The edge persists because market-neutral books hedge index exposure with beta and therefore leave the weight/depth heterogeneity of basket impact un-hedged, and because deciding *which* names a program actually touched requires simultaneous cross-sectional volume-share geometry plus many-name execution inside a one-minute window.
factors.name: Name-level basket-footprint attributed over-push relaxation

factors.trading_idea: The parent proved that displacement from a valuation-comparable peer anchor is informative, but it hard-coded the sign and magnitude of the response (always fade, weighted by a slow 60-bar anchor), which is why its IC grew monotonically out to 24 bars: it held displacement whose relaxation mass sits mostly beyond the fixed 6-bar offset. The child estimates, online and per name, the actual mapping from a 6-bar peer-relative displacement to the NEXT 6-bar peer-relative return — a trailing OLS of x_t (the realised forward-6 change starting at t-6) on x_{t-6} (the displacement that preceded it), which is a purged, causal, horizon-matched regression — and then forecasts directly with that slope times the current displacement. Because the slope is measured rather than assumed, the factor automatically fades names whose 6-bar impact really is transient, follows names whose 6-bar flow really is persistent (metaorder continuation), and puts near-zero weight on slow reverters whose relaxation leaks past the horizon; the noisy per-name slope is empirical-Bayes shrunk toward the median slope of its sector×valuation-tercile cell with a weight set by the regression's own explained variance. The edge survives arbitrage because the sign of short-horizon peer-relative predictability is name- and regime-specific and must be inferred from a low signal-to-noise trailing sample, and monetising it requires warehousing the peer-relative spread while that inference stays uncertain.
factors.name: EB-shrunk self-calibrated 6-bar peer-displacement slope

factors.trading_idea: Both parents estimate the same latent nuisance parameter — the decay clock of an idiosyncratic price deviation — by two methodologically independent nonparametric routes: parent A's zero-crossing spacing T of the deviation (a Kac level-crossing statistic) and parent B's Rice-inverted sign concordance rho of adjacent non-overlapping 6-bar block displacements (rho = cos(pi*p_flip)); both are dimensionless, jump-robust, monotone in 'slowness' of the clock. The child fades the standardised deviation with a weight that is (i) an ASYMMETRIC slowness gate rather than A's symmetric sech^2 kernel — because B's realized direction shows the edge lives on the slow/persistent side (rho > 0 names are being pushed by sliced metaorder flow whose impact is transient and snaps back over the next minute), while on the fast side (rho < 0, T << h) the deviation is pure bounce that has already decayed before t+6, so any signed bet there is noise — and (ii) multiplied by an AGREEMENT gate that shrinks size when the two independent clock estimators disagree, i.e. when the clock is unidentified (regime shift or noise-dominated tape). The interaction carries edge neither parent has alone: A discards exactly the slow-clock names where fading pays and has no way to tell a badly-estimated clock from a real one, while B multiplies by a *signed* rho and therefore bets on continuation in fast/bouncy names where the correct answer is 'no position' — the child uses rho only as a non-negative gate, never as a sign flip, and requires two-estimator consensus before sizing.
factors.name: Clock-consensus asymmetric-slowness deviation fade

factors.trading_idea: Both parents' realized signs agree on one microstructural fact that neither declared: at 10-second scale a peer-residual mid displacement that arrives *with* abnormal trade keeps going, while a displacement that arrives on an empty tape gets pulled back. That is order-splitting/self-excitation, not propagator relaxation — a burst bar is one slice of a metaorder whose remaining slices land inside the next ~60 seconds, whereas a quiet mid move is a market maker skewing quotes on inventory or staleness, which snaps back as soon as real flow tests it (relaxation of the traded leg only shows up later, which is why Parent A kept magnitude out to 12-24 bars). The child therefore takes Parent A's *decomposition* (valuation-comparability peer residual split by bar participation share into a traded leg and a quiet leg, each propagator-weighted with a 3-bar kernel) and uses those two legs as the axes of Parent B's pooled, horizon-matched, double-centred nonparametric response surface, so the continuation/reversal amplitude is *learned* per (traded, quiet) configuration instead of assumed additive, and combines that interaction forecast with the sign-corrected additive wedge (traded minus quiet). The interaction carries edge neither parent has alone because Parent B's raw signed-displacement axis confounds the two components — its slow surface averaged over regimes with opposite conditional means and inverted out of sample — while Parent A imposed a single global sign on legs whose relative strength is state dependent; conditioning the surface on already-decomposed, volatility-normalised legs makes the cell means far more stationary, and a fast (≈1 hour) exponential pooling tracks the configuration where a quiet stale quote is being actively contradicted by a traded burst in the same name.
factors.name: Peer propagator-leg grid interaction wedge

factors.trading_idea: A name's deviation from its *valuation-comparable* basket (same industry AND same size half, because dealers hedge inventory with similar-cap same-industry names) is repaired at a speed that differs per name and is proportional to how much hedging capacity is live in that basket right now. The parent measured the dislocation and gated it with coarse 2x2 activity cells but fitted a single pooled loading, so names whose natural repair half-life is far from 60 seconds diluted the 6-bar signal (its IC peaked at 24 bars); the child instead estimates each name's own horizon-matched repair loading by a trailing OLS of the realised 6-bar comparable-relative return on the lagged, noise-averaged dislocation, and scales it by a continuous repair-capacity clock = (peer leave-one-out activity) x (statistical hedge quality of the basket for that name). Falsifiable predictions: (i) names with an empirically fast, well-identified 6-bar repair loading carry essentially all of the 6-bar edge and names with weak/slow loadings carry none; (ii) the same dislocation predicts a strictly smaller repair when its comparables are quiet or poorly correlated with it. The edge survives arbitrage because it is a capacity constraint, not a mispricing: closing an idiosyncratic dislocation consumes hedging capital and simultaneous comparable-basket liquidity, and in the states where that liquidity is absent nobody can force the repair inside a minute.
factors.name: Comparable-basket dislocation with per-name repair rate on a peer-activity clock

factors.trading_idea: Parent A knows *where* a name stands relative to its valuation-comparable peers but not *why* it got there, so it has to wait passively for relaxation — which is why its edge only matures at 24 bars. Parent B knows *how* a displacement was built (compressed increments = a live sliced metaorder; tail-heavy increments = a liquidity-withdrawal overshoot) but measures that drift on raw returns, where market-wide moves swamp the relative-value content. The child applies Parent B's nonparametric Wilcoxon location shift and Mood scale-compression statistic to the *peer-residual* log increments of Parent A's sector x valuation-tercile comparable basket, then uses the compression state as a regime switch on the displacement: dispersed (overshoot) names get the freshly-built peer displacement faded, compressed (grind) names get the peer-relative drift ridden, damped by how much room is left before the peer anchor. The interaction is the edge neither has alone: the shape statistic converts A's slow, state-ambiguous relative-value gap into an immediately actionable, horizon-matched signal, while the peer residualisation gives B's rank-drift a genuine convergence anchor instead of a naked directional bet.
factors.name: Increment-shape switched peer displacement (fade vs ride)

factors.trading_idea: Parent A says slow, mandate-constrained income clienteles leave a beta-implied catch-up owed after a market move; Parent B says mid-drift printed in quiet bars is permanent quote repricing while drift printed on thin volume in excess of the square-root impact law is transient. The child fuses them by *auditing which channel actually delivered the owed beta response*: a name's realised move is split into quiet-bar quote repricing (full credit as genuine delivery) and traded-bar displacement credited only in proportion to sqrt(volume backing) — so an unbacked taker push looks like delivery to Parent A but is really transient and leaves the backlog intact (and adds a reversal on top). The residual backlog is then gated by the payout-clientele score (who is slow to arbitrage) and by Parent B's maker/taker disagreement gate, which selects exactly the discordant, tug-of-war state that must be settled at the next few liquidity events — pulling the edge inside the fixed 6-bar offset instead of the parents' 12-24 bar peaks. The interaction carries edge neither parent has alone: Parent A cannot tell delivered from fake delivery, and Parent B has no notion of how much adjustment is owed.
factors.name: Clientele Beta Backlog with Channel-Permanence Credit

factors.trading_idea: Parent B identified *which* names give back trade-driven pushes in seconds — the per-name negative cross-lag between the within-bar body (move made while trades arrived) and the following seam (pure quote relocation) is a slowly-varying fingerprint of how fast liquidity providers reciprocate transient impact — but it hard-coded the trade as 'always fade the push'. Parent A had the right estimation machinery (a pooled, exponentially-weighted nonparametric response surface on an ordinal state grid, so no direction is ever assumed) but the wrong second state axis (own-history volume) and it threw away everything except the double-centred interaction, leaving a noise-dominated residual whose sign flipped out of sample. The child replaces the volume axis with the seam-reciprocation state and estimates E[market-neutral 6-bar return | body-push bin × absorption-reciprocation bin] non-parametrically, then removes only the absorption-bin *level* effect so what remains is the push-response curve *shape within each absorption regime*. The interaction carries edge neither parent has: absorption-high names should show a steep negative (snapback) push-response and absorption-low names a flat-to-positive (continuation) one, and letting the data set both the slope and the curvature per regime keeps the sign self-calibrated instead of asserted, while purging the absorption level keeps it orthogonal to plain liquidity-state factors.
factors.name: Absorption-state conditioned pooled push response surface

factors.trading_idea: The parent proved that stale names owe catch-up to observed market moves, but it folded six separately-estimated one-bar lag betas against raw trailing market sums — so it (a) counted owed mass from market wiggles that were immediately retraced and (b) could not tell a genuinely lagging name from one whose beta-adjusted deviation came from permanent idiosyncratic news, which is why its predictive mass leaked outside the 6-bar window and flipped sign by 12 bars. The child replaces that with a single robust aggregation estimator: the total (long-run) response beta from a trailing regression of the name's 6-bar cumulative return on the market's 6-bar cumulative return, and a lag-share statistic (total beta minus contemporaneous beta, normalised) that measures what fraction of the total response arrives late; the owed amount is then the beta-adjusted 6-bar gap, admitted only when its sign is concordant with the sign of the market move (genuine under-reaction) rather than discordant (over-reaction / idiosyncratic news, which is permanent), and only when the market path over those 6 bars was efficient (|sum m| / sum|m| high), i.e. a real level shift rather than a round trip. The edge persists because collecting one to two basis points of catch-up in names that do not update their mid on many shock bars requires paying a wide spread in thin, low-attention names, so second-scale arbitrage capital is systematically absent exactly where the conditional non-response hazard P(mid frozen | large market shock) is highest. It is falsified if the concordant and discordant halves of the gap forecast forward returns identically, if the path-efficiency gate does not discriminate, or if the lag-share/non-response-hazard conditioners add nothing over the raw beta-adjusted gap.
factors.name: Concordant under-reaction gap gated by lag-share and non-response hazard

factors.trading_idea: Transient impact does not relax on the wall clock — it relaxes as passive depth is rebuilt, and depth rebuilding is paced by trade arrivals, i.e. it runs on a volume clock. The parent's unpaid-immediacy displacement therefore reverts after a name-specific number of *traded* bars, which is why its IC peaked near 12 calendar bars: the panel mixes fast names (already repaid inside 6 bars) with sleepy names (repayment still pending). The child (i) carries each bar's displacement forward with an explicit volume-clock decay exp(-kappa * volume-since/ADV), so what is faded is only the *still-unpaid* residue, and (ii) scales the fade by the fraction of that residue expected to be repaid within exactly the 6-bar horizon, 1 - exp(-kappa * forecast 6-bar volume/ADV), where the forecast uses the strong short-run persistence of trade-arrival intensity (Hawkes-type clustering). Falsifiable: sorting on the predicted completion fraction should move the reversion IC peak of the raw displacement from ~12 bars (low-completion names) to ~6 bars (high-completion names), and the completion-weighted signal should beat the unweighted one at the fixed 6-bar offset; the edge survives arbitrage because the displacement is compensation paid to whoever supplies immediacy and warehouses inventory over the refill window, not a free mispricing.
factors.name: Refill-completion-fraction gated unpaid immediacy fade

factors.trading_idea: Parent A shows a price deviation only pays a 6-bar reversal when the name's own zero-crossing period matches the 6-bar holding window; Parent B shows that displacement paid for by executed flow is transient impact while unexplained (quiet) repricing is a near-permanent belief update. The child estimates the crossing clock *separately for each of the two channels*: the flow-explained (transient) deviation is faded only when its resilience clock matches the horizon (an impact that replenishes in 1 bar is already gone, one that replenishes in 100 bars is still outstanding at t+6), while the unexplained deviation is carried as continuation only when its clock is slow, i.e. it is a genuine drift rather than an oscillator. The two-channel split is trusted in proportion to the cross-sectional rank of the impact regression's uncentred R-squared, and where flow explains nothing the signal collapses gracefully to the clock-matched fade of the total deviation. The interaction is the edge: A's kernel cannot know *which* deviation is mechanically resilient versus informational, and B's decomposition cannot know whether either component actually turns over inside a 6-bar window — only the clock measured per component tells you both which side to take and whether it pays by t+6.
factors.name: Flow-split displacement with crossing-clock matched permanence blend

factors.trading_idea: The parent's edge is mechanical: the block of prints about to fall out of a trailing-window anchor is already known, so the part of the anchor's future move that comes from drop-out is deterministic today, and anchor-followers' flow tracks it. Two things blunt the parent: (i) its 'anomaly' term (block mean minus local median) still contains the local trend, and a trending expiring block produces an anchor move that trend-followers have already priced — only the *non-trend residual* of the expiring block is genuinely unpriced mechanical drift; (ii) it guesses which windows the crowd uses and how strongly they react. The child purges the trend by fitting a causal local OLS line on the bars immediately *preceding* the expiring block and extrapolating it to the block's centre, then multiplies each window's mechanical drift by that name's own *measured* response polarity to the corresponding anchor gap (trailing correlation of returns with the lagged normalised price-minus-anchor distance): names whose price is pulled back toward the anchor amplify the drop-out drift, while names whose price runs away from the anchor (breakout clientele) invert it. The edge persists because each expiry event is tiny, the deterministic part only pays out over the exact span of the drop-out, and taking the other side means standing in front of flow that keeps arriving for the whole expiry window; it is falsified if IC at 6 bars is no better than the trend-contaminated parent, or if the polarity gate carries no incremental information.
factors.name: Trend-purged window-expiry dropout drift, gated by measured anchor-response polarity

factors.trading_idea: Relative-value market makers do not hedge a name against its industry average; they hedge it against the peers that price the *same kind* of cash-flow claim, i.e. peers sitting at a similar point in multiple space (P/B, P/S, P/OCF), because those peers share discount-rate duration and business mix so the hedged spread is a genuinely stationary object. A 30-second dislocation of a name from its valuation-matched, beta-hedged peer basket is therefore an inventory/liquidity artefact that the hedgeable-pair arbitrageur closes within about a minute, and the speed of closure should increase in how well the basket actually explains the name's returns (its hedge R-squared) and decrease when the move is backed by abnormal traded volume, which signals permanent information rather than transient pressure. The child replaces the parent's slow level-dislocation-from-EWMA object (whose IC peaked at 24 bars) with a 3-bar hedged-residual impulse, which mechanically reverts on the 6-bar scale, and replaces the parent's peer-dispersion gate with a hedgeability (R-squared) gate that is the actual economic prerequisite for fast arbitrage. Falsifiable: if snapback strength is flat in hedge R-squared, or if a valuation-matched kernel basket does no better than the plain industry-mean basket, the valuation-matched-hedgeability mechanism is wrong and the signal is just generic peer reversal; the edge persists because joining point-in-time per-share fundamentals to a 10-second tape to define comparability is operationally awkward for pure microstructure arbitrageurs, and capacity is limited to the small number of tight valuation neighbourhoods.
factors.name: Valuation-matched peer hedge residual snapback

factors.trading_idea: Parent B estimated a per-name lag-6 block autocorrelation by inverting Rice's sign-concordance law (rho = cos(pi*p_flip)) and applied it to the current 60-second displacement, but it pooled block pairs across two physically opposite states, so the pooled coefficient is a state-frequency-weighted average of a positive (metaorder continuation) and a negative (inventory bounce) coefficient — which is exactly why its unconditional forecast realized the wrong sign. Parent A supplies the missing state variable: the local-time / recurrence density of the market-purged relative-value level, which distinguishes a level the path habitually revisits (an accepted value, where the flow is bounce and displacement snaps back) from fresh, never-visited territory (a live excursion, where sliced flow keeps pushing). The child therefore estimates Rice's concordance coefficient *separately* in the pinned and fresh recurrence states — weighting each historical block pair by the state that prevailed when that block began — and forecasts with the coefficient belonging to the name's state right now. The interaction is the edge: A's occupancy state has no per-name coefficient and no direction, B's coefficient is contaminated by state mixing; conditioning one on the other de-mixes the two regimes and lets the same displacement reverse in pinned names and continue in fresh ones, self-calibrated per name.
factors.name: Recurrence-state conditional Rice block-memory forecast

factors.trading_idea: Parent B says a laggard's precision-whitened dislocation converges toward the phase of the measured leader field; Parent A says the local-time (recurrence) density of a path tells you whether the current level is a well-supplied, habitually-revisited equilibrium or fresh, unvisited territory — and its realized sign says the pinned/high-recurrence state is where moves persist, because a level the path keeps returning to is that name's *accepted* level, not a dislocation. The child measures local time in the right coordinate: not on raw mid price (where it is mostly a volatility/staleness artefact) but on the Epps-corrected precision-whitened relative-value spread itself. A spread sitting at a level it has occupied for much of the last ten minutes is a fair relative value that no entrainment will pull — the leader field will converge to it, not it to the field — whereas a spread standing at a level it has essentially never visited is a genuine fresh excursion, and only there does the Kuramoto entrainment force (leader phase minus own phase, weighted by measured lagginess) actually get delivered inside six bars. The interaction is the edge: amplitude and phase alone cannot distinguish an equilibrium spread from an excursion spread, and recurrence density alone has no direction — together they say 'converge now' only for a laggard that is both phase-turning and standing in unvisited spread territory.
factors.name: Spread local-time freshness gated leader-field entrainment

factors.trading_idea: Parent A shows that whether a hedged idiosyncratic excursion is inventory noise (fade) or information (follow) is a market-WIDE state, measured by the share of cross-sectional return variance carried by the equal-weighted market factor; Parent B shows that within a single name the excursion splits into quote-driven repricing printed in (near-)zero-volume bars (continues) and drift paid for with aggressive volume (mechanically decays). The child applies the regime gate only where it is economically valid: the TRADED leg is temporary price impact whose repayment depends on factor-level risk transfer, so its reversal is amplified when commonality is high and flips to continuation when commonality collapses into a dispersion/news regime; the QUIET leg is unpaid-for quote shading, i.e. a dealer's private adverse-selection belief, so it is weighted UP in dispersion regimes and DOWN when high commonality means quiet mids are merely stale drag on the market factor. The interaction carries edge neither parent has alone: Parent A gates one sign onto a drift that mixes two microstructurally opposite components (diluting the gate), while Parent B holds a static sign split that averages the profitable high-commonality impact-repayment regime with the loss-making dispersion regime — routing the regime state to the correct component sharpens both.
factors.name: Commonality-gated quiet-quote vs traded-impact hedged drift split

factors.trading_idea: The parent measured occupancy of the mid at its CURRENT (post-move) level and then assumed that occupancy described depth already consumed — hence its continuation prediction; the realized IC was negative on both legs, which is exactly what you get if occupancy instead describes the resting/latent liquidity standing AHEAD of the displaced price. I keep the parent's peer-orthogonal dislocation and its doubly-centred occupancy gate but re-read the state variable correctly and upgrade it from a bar-count local time to a volume-weighted local time (latent depth accumulates in proportion to volume transacted at a level, Bouchaud's latent-liquidity/market-profile picture), so a whitened idiosyncratic displacement into a heavily-traded level meets a replenishing wall and is absorbed back inside seconds, whereas the same displacement into a level the tape has barely visited meets a vacuum, forcing market makers to re-quote around the new level, and the move persists. To place the response inside the fixed 6-bar offset (the parent's |IC| leaked out to 24 bars because both its dislocation and its state were slow), the dislocation is shortened and decay-weighted, the occupancy window and its time z-score are shortened, and the signal is scaled by an onset weight that keeps only names whose dislocation is at its own 8-bar extreme right now — absorption and re-quoting both resolve immediately after the displacement completes. The edge survives arbitrage because it is a conditional sign flip: unconditionally (gate centred in time and cross-section) the factor has zero loading on reversal or momentum, so it is invisible to standard screens, and exploiting it requires paying the spread at exactly the levels where depth is thinnest.
factors.name: Volume-at-level wall vs vacuum idiosyncratic dislocation flip

factors.trading_idea: Both parents measure the same 100-second path but different components of it, and their realized (sign-flipped) evidence is only apparently contradictory: heavy-volume wick asymmetry — excursion that was NOT converted into net displacement — precedes continuation toward the probed side (the endpoint mid is a stale sample of where aggression actually reached), while beta-residual net displacement that WAS realised through a level is transient impact and snaps back. The child computes a single scale-free conversion ratio c = |residual net displacement| / (|residual net displacement| + probed excursion path), both in units of the name's own robust grid quantum, and uses it to switch continuously between the two polarities: low c (probe absorbed, no net move) loads long the excursion side, high c (clean sweep, path fully converted) loads against the displacement. The whole thing is scaled by a saturating absorption gate in window volume relative to ADV, because both mechanisms require real traded size to have probed the book. Neither parent can flip sign — each applies one polarity everywhere and therefore averages a continuation regime against a reversion regime, which is exactly why both showed |IC| of only a few basis points with contradicted signs; c is the state variable that separates the two and is only computable from both parents' quantities jointly.
factors.name: Conversion-ratio switch: absorbed probe excursion vs swept displacement

factors.trading_idea: Each 10-second bar splits into two microstructurally distinct legs: the within-bar body (close-open), which is the move accomplished while trades were arriving, and the seam (open minus previous close), which is a pure quote relocation between bar boundaries. If a name's liquidity providers are absorbing aggressive flow, the seams systematically walk back the previous bar's body — a measurable, slowly-varying per-name fingerprint (negative cross-lag correlation between body and next seam) that identifies which names give back trade-driven pushes in seconds rather than minutes. The child therefore fades the freshly accumulated peer-neutral *body* push only in names whose seams habitually reciprocate it, and only once the recent seams have already begun reciprocating; unlike the parent's level-based peer displacement (whose OU relaxation only fully lands by 24 bars), this object is intrinsically a 2-6 bar reciprocation clock. The edge survives arbitrage because capturing it means posting passive size against possibly-informed aggressive flow for a fraction of the spread — a market-making inventory risk, not a directional trade an arbitrageur can lift.
factors.name: Seam-vs-body absorption pushback

factors.trading_idea: A corporation is the only participant whose trading side is known in advance and price-insensitive, so an active repurchaser leaves a one-sided footprint in the *duration statistics* of its own price path: excursions below a short trailing anchor are truncated by the standing 10b-18 bid, while a net issuer's excursions above the anchor are truncated by corporate supply. I therefore split Parent B's Kac/level-crossing clock by side — the mean length of *completed negative* versus *completed positive* excursions of the market-neutral log-price deviation — and fade the dislocation only where (i) the corporate hinge says that side is the supported one, (ii) that side's realised excursion clock matches the fixed 6-bar horizon via the scale-free kernel 4Th/(T+h)², and (iii) the duration asymmetry itself confirms the standing order is *live today*. The interaction is the edge neither parent has: quarterly issuance data says who *can* support the tape but not whether the algorithm is working this session and not how fast repair happens, while a sign-symmetric crossing clock pools corporate-absorbed dips (fast, mechanical, horizon-matched repair) with genuinely informed dips (no repair at all), which is exactly why Parent B's IC leaks out to 24 bars. Conditioning the horizon-match on the corporate side, and the corporate side on the side-asymmetry of dwell times, isolates dislocations that are both mechanically absorbed and absorbed on the 6-bar clock.
factors.name: Corporate hinge × side-split excursion-clock match

factors.trading_idea: Basket / program flow (ETF create-redeem, index programs) pushes each name in proportion to cap-weight-per-unit-depth rather than beta, so the mechanical over-push in name i is approximately (rank(-log turnover) - rank(beta)) x the program-weighted market move (Parent B).  Whether that over-push relaxes or extends is not universal: it depends on whether the displaced price now faces resting liquidity in the direction it was pushed, which is exactly what Parent A's volume-occupancy profile measures — an excess of local occupancy mass ahead of the push (dense, anharmonic node in the push direction) means dealer inventory and resting limit orders absorb and reflect the flow, whereas a low-density gap ahead means nothing is there to take the other side and the mechanical displacement keeps going.  The child therefore signs Parent B's flow-elasticity wedge by an absorption score built from Parent A's occupancy geometry evaluated *in the direction of the estimated push* (kernel centre-of-occupancy-mass excess times the push sign, plus local-vs-wide relative density).  The interaction carries edge neither parent has: B fades every name's basket push uniformly and is blind to where resting liquidity sits; A knows the occupancy geometry but not why the price is displaced or whether the displacement is mechanical liquidity demand at all — and A's realized (contradicted) sign is precisely 'price moves away from vacated mass', which is consistent with absorption-and-reflection once the push direction is known.
factors.name: Occupancy-absorption gated basket-flow over-push

factors.trading_idea: Parent A shows that only the *name-specific* part of within-bar displacement is liquidity cost that snaps back (the sector/market part is information and persists); Parent B shows that whether a path snaps back at all depends on its conversion ratio c — how much of the probed excursion was actually converted into net displacement. The child uses c as a slow regime state and the common/idiosyncratic decomposition as a second, orthogonal state, and routes the fast payload accordingly: in absorbed regimes (low c) it loads WITH the participation-weighted unconverted probe excursion, while in swept regimes (high c) it fades only the sector- and beta-purged displacement (weighted by the name's idiosyncratic variance share) and simultaneously loads WITH the common component, which is information rather than immediacy cost. The interaction is the edge: c alone averages a reverting idio component against a persisting common component (Parent B's dilution), and the idio purge alone averages a sweep regime against an absorption regime (Parent A's dilution) — only the joint routing gets both polarities right on the same bar. Crucially the state variables (c, idio share, absorption) are estimated on slow 60–240 bar windows while the payload (displacement, wick asymmetry, close-location) is measured over just 4 bars, so the signal decays with the 6-bar horizon instead of the 24-bar one the parents drifted toward.
factors.name: Conversion-state routed idio/common displacement vs absorbed probe

factors.trading_idea: Parent A's valuation-space peer spread reverts, but its edge sat at 24 bars because the impulse it fed the pooled estimator mixed two objects with very different clocks: a name-specific dislocation against its valuation neighbours (closable in seconds by one desk trading one stock against a small basket, so it pays at ~6 bars) and a neighbourhood-common re-rating of the whole valuation tier (which requires trading the entire tier and therefore decays over many minutes). Parent B's second-stage purge is exactly the operator that separates them, so the child replaces A's time-scale (fast/slow) decomposition of the impulse with B's cross-sectional one: the kernel-neighbour-average dislocation is projected out of each name's dislocation, and the name-specific residual and its tier-common projection enter A's trailing, pooled, no-intercept ridge regression on the *realised 6-bar* forward spread change as two separate regressors, fitted inside cells of B's hedgeability state (trailing R-squared of the name's dislocation on its tier factor) and shrunk to the all-observation fit. The interaction is the edge: because the response surface is anchored on the fixed 6-bar offset, the tape itself assigns the fast-paying name-specific leg a large loading and the slow tier-common leg a near-zero (or opposite-sign) one — curing A's horizon mismatch — while B gains a fundamentals-anchored, beta-hedge-free impulse and a calibrated, sign-flexible loading in place of its hand-set '-1 x z x R-squared' scaling, so it no longer assumes the purged part always snaps back at the same speed in every liquidity state.
factors.name: Tier-purged pooled horizon-matched multiple dislocation

factors.trading_idea: Parent B isolates a clean *state* variable — the fraction of a fresh one-sided variance burst that is mechanical (variance per unit participation, after removing the slow structural asymmetry a name's capital structure justifies) — but it fires the moment the burst is detected, while the liquidating flow is still arriving. Parent A supplies the missing *clock*: a pressure-driven displacement only pays back once the one-sided flow decays off its own peak and price has lifted off the burst extreme. The child makes purity and completion interact as a two-sided switch rather than two multiplicative filters: an unexplained one-sided burst that is thin-book (high variance-per-volume) AND whose side-aligned Hawkes-style flow intensity has decayed from its 12-bar peak is traded as a snapback, whereas the same burst with commensurate participation and intensity still at its peak — especially in high-leverage names, where a down-move carries genuine asset-value news (Merton/Christie) — is traded as continuation. Neither parent can express this sign flip: A has the exhaustion clock but no measure of whether the displacement was mechanical to begin with, and B has the purity measure but no notion of whether the pressure has finished, so it dilutes reverting and continuing bursts into one long-only-reversal book.
factors.name: Exhaustion-switched vacuum-purity semivariance residual

factors.trading_idea: The parent proved that quote-driven (thin-volume) mid drift continues while volume-paid drift decays, but it pooled the quiet leg over a 12-bar decay window, turning it into a slow state variable whose IC only peaked at 12 bars. The child measures the object that actually resolves inside the forecast horizon: the *pending* displacement accumulated over the current, still-unbroken silence spell (cumulative vol-scaled return since the last volume-bearing bar, scaled by sqrt of spell length) — this is exactly the repricing that the next arriving order must validate or erase. It is gated by a horizon-matched reignition probability p = 1-(1-lambda)^6, where lambda is the name's recent trade-bar frequency, standardised cross-sectionally so a market-wide lull is purged: a name likely to be hit within the next 6 bars has its pending quiet drift confirmed (continuation), while a name whose expected silence exceeds the horizon is showing stale-quote flicker that mean-reverts, and a busy name is mostly carrying transient impact that decays. The edge survives arbitrage because harvesting it requires crossing the spread in names that are, at that instant, quiet and thinly quoted; it is falsified if pending-spell displacement predicts forward returns independently of the 6-bar reignition probability, or if the paid leg does not revert more strongly in high-arrival-rate names.
factors.name: Reignition-hazard gated pending silence displacement vs paid impact

factors.trading_idea: Parent B says each name owes a computable amount of catch-up to market information it has already seen (distributed-lag loadings b_1..b_6 folded against the observed market path, kernel-matched to the 6-bar offset), but it is agnostic about *how* that debt gets paid; Parent A says repricing that happens in quiet bars (quote shading) persists while repricing paid for with aggressive volume decays, but it cannot tell genuine sequential quote shading from stale-mid noise. The child estimates the lagged-market impulse response *separately inside each volume stream* — loadings for bars that are quiet (near-zero volume, i.e. pure quote repricing) and loadings for bars that are active (traded impact) — folds each set against the already-observed market path, and mixes them by the trailing probability of each channel to get the owed catch-up decomposed into a quote-delivery leg and a trade-delivery leg. Parent A's stream-specific Rice sign-flip excess (observed adjacent-flip frequency minus the Gaussian null arccos(rho)/pi, measured inside each stream) then sets the trust on each leg: the quiet leg is loaded only when it is grind-carried (negative excess = many small same-signed increments = real sequential quote walking, not a stale gap), and the active leg's loading flips sign with its excess — positive (jump-carried impact into thin depth) gets faded, negative (a still-working sliced order) gets followed. The interaction is the edge: B's forecast magnitude becomes channel-attributed and its delivery mechanism verified, while A's grind/jump state stops being a raw drift gate and instead conditions a horizon-matched, market-information-anchored forecast, which is exactly what neither parent has at the fixed 6-bar offset.
factors.name: Channel-Split Lagged-Beta Owed Catch-Up, Rice Grind/Jump Gated

factors.trading_idea: Parent B shows that a peer-relative dislocation only reverts once its own velocity has turned back toward the anchor (the metaorder has stopped pushing), while Parent A shows that the repair of an *idiosyncratic* dislocation is only fast when the hedge legs — the peer basket — are simultaneously tradable, and that peer activity is a state variable rather than a standalone signal. The child fuses these into a single differential state, the hedgeability wedge h = (leave-one-out peer activity) − (own activity): h is large exactly when the name's own flow has ceased AND its peers are live, i.e. a liquidity provider can absorb the idiosyncratic gap and instantly hedge it in the basket, so the transient-impact relaxation is front-loaded into the next ~60 seconds instead of dribbling out over many minutes. The wedge subsumes Parent B's own-volume flow-cessation gate and Parent A's peer-activity gate in one variable, and the traded impulse is further damped when the peer basket itself is displaced versus the market (unhedgeable common factor risk that neither parent separated at this speed) — this interaction is what pulls the edge forward to the fixed 6-bar offset, which both parents missed by peaking at 24 bars.
factors.name: Peer-hedgeability-wedge gated reversion-onset displacement

factors.trading_idea: Most short-horizon participants price off *trailing-window* anchors (N-bar moving averages, rolling fair-value or VWAP-style estimators). Such an anchor moves over the next h bars for two reasons: new prints entering (unforecastable under a martingale) and old prints mechanically dropping out (fully known now). If the block of bars that is about to expire from an N-bar window sat anomalously *below* its own local neighbourhood — a spike/outlier rather than a trend — then over exactly the next h bars every anchor-follower's estimate will drift mechanically *upward* with no new information, and the resulting anchor-chasing flow pushes price up; the reverse holds for an anomalously high expiring block. The signal is computed only from prices located N−h to N bars in the past (mean of the expiring block minus the median of its surrounding neighbourhood, in units of the name's own volatility), so it is orthogonal to current momentum/reversal by construction, is zero-mean under a random walk, and is falsified if its IC is flat at the 6-bar offset. It survives arbitrage because each individual expiry event is tiny, its exploitation requires guessing which window lengths the crowd uses, and taking the other side means fighting mechanical flow that keeps arriving for the whole expiry span.
factors.name: Rolling-window expiry anchor drop-out drift

factors.trading_idea: Parent A measured the rank-shape of a name's 'idiosyncratic' path but only market-median-demeaned it, so a slow lagged-beta catch-up drift (exactly parent B's object) masqueraded as an idiosyncratic 'grind' — which is why A's declared sign inverted. The child first estimates each name's distributed-lag impulse response to the cap-weighted market (loadings b_0..b_6), subtracts the full lag response to obtain a genuinely purged idiosyncratic path, and applies A's Kendall time-concordance-versus-displacement wedge to that purged path only: at a 60-second offset a rank-monotone purged grind is order-splitting long-memory flow that keeps pushing (continuation), while a displacement that is lumpy for its size is a liquidity-vacuum sweep that overshoots and snaps back. The component removed from the path is not discarded — it is exactly B's horizon-matched owed catch-up (b_l folded against already-observed trailing market sums, amplified by a frozen-mid / thin-volume staleness gate), which should be *followed*. The interaction is the blending weight: the common-explained share of the last 20 bars of displacement decides whether the move is read as a mechanically-owed beta repair (follow B) or as a private execution footprint whose shape decides continuation versus snapback (read A) — neither parent can tell those two states apart alone.
factors.name: Owed-catch-up purged grind-vs-sweep path attribution

factors.trading_idea: A pinned-level break impulse is the superposition of two things: a mechanical transient overshoot that every short-horizon price move carries (bid-ask bounce, inventory pressure, transient impact) which mean-reverts and which the existing book already spans, and a queue-clearing information component (the resting size at the touch was actually consumed and the next level is thinner) which continues. The parent summed them, so its realized IC took the sign of the reverting component that dominates in variance — and the harness's own diagnostic confirms the decomposition: the parent's raw IC was -0.0055 while its book-orthogonal part was +0.0076. The child therefore keeps only the component of the pin-break state that is cross-sectionally orthogonal, bar by bar, to the generic reversal carriers (1-, 6- and 24-bar returns plus recent volume intensity), and gates it on two independent pieces of queue evidence: volume absorbed while the mid was pinned (there really was a large resting queue) and volume printed in the break bar itself (the queue was consumed rather than evaporating). Falsifiable: the purged residual should show positive 6-bar IC while the projected-away part shows negative IC; if both are negative the queue-clearing story is dead. It survives arbitrage because each event is worth a fraction of a tick in exactly the low-turnover, grid-bound names where crossing costs a full tick, and because the informative part is orthogonal to the generic reversal everyone else is trading.
factors.name: Reversal-purged pin-clearing continuation residual (jitter)

factors.trading_idea: Parent B knows *where* a name is relative to its valuation-comparable peers but not *how* it got there, which is why its edge only matures at 12-24 bars; Parent A knows that a fresh one-sided variance burst produced on abnormally little volume (high variance-per-participation, a thin-book vacuum) is mechanical inventory/impact and snaps back inside a minute, but it throws away the direction and the relative-value anchor. The child trades the negated peer-relative displacement only when that displacement is *directionally concordant* with a fresh 12-bar downside-vs-upside semivariance innovation created in a vacuum: a name pushed below its peer anchor by a downside-heavy variance burst that no volume justifies is a liquidator's footprint, so its relaxation is front-loaded and lands at the fixed 6-bar offset, whereas the same displacement accompanied by commensurate volume is news and is left alone. The interaction is the edge: displacement supplies the size and sign of the mispricing (A cannot), while the vacuum/asymmetry concordance supplies the clock that tells you the relaxation is happening now rather than over the next four minutes (B cannot); the composite is demeaned within leverage-tercile x size-half buckets so the slow Merton/Christie structural part of semivariance asymmetry is not mistaken for a dislocation.
factors.name: Vacuum-concordant semivariance-gated peer displacement

factors.trading_idea: Parent B's precision-whitened deviation (Sigma^{-1} applied to the last 6 bars of vol-standardised returns, orthogonalised against the plain move) isolates moves that violate the recent correlation structure — but it pools two economically opposite populations, which is exactly why its declared reversal sign was contradicted: on average, at a 10-second clock, a low-variance-direction deviation in a thin name is *slow information diffusion* (Epps/staleness catch-up) and therefore continues, not noise. Parent A supplies the missing state variable that separates the populations: the cross-sectional volume-allocation tilt toward the capitalisation-weight vector (the basket/program footprint) together with a name's mechanical impact elasticity in excess of its beta (rank(-log turnover) − rank(beta)). When the bar carries a program footprint AND the name is weight-fragile, the whitened deviation is mechanical liquidity demand pushed in proportion to weight/depth rather than information, so it must relax; when flow is un-basket-like, the same deviation in the same fragile name is genuine idiosyncratic repricing that keeps drifting. The child therefore trades the whitened dislocation with a *sign that switches* on the program-footprint × elasticity-wedge interaction — an edge neither parent has: A never looks at name-level correlation-structure dislocation (only the market-wide move), and B never conditions on the flow's basket geometry, so its two regimes cancel.
factors.name: Program-footprint-gated precision dislocation split

factors.trading_idea: The parent fades the *level* of an idiosyncratic deviation, so its information is about total remaining reversion and mechanically accrues over many bars (IC rose monotonically to 24 bars) — at the fixed 6-bar offset the level is the wrong estimand. If a name's market-purged price deviation behaves as a quasi-periodic excursion (sliced metaorder pushes price away, liquidity provision pulls it back), then what is predictable exactly 6 bars ahead is not the amplitude but the PHASE: with a half-period T and a backward recurrence time tau since the last zero crossing, the expected 6-bar increment is amp*(sin(min(omega(tau+6),pi)) - sin(omega*tau)) with omega=pi/T — i.e. young excursions (tau << T/2) are predicted to EXTEND and aged excursions (tau -> T) to snap back, a sign flip conditional on excursion age that no plain reversal or momentum factor in the book can span. The clock is identified twice, methodologically independently — nonparametric crossing counting (Kac) and the Rice spectral-moment ratio pi*sd(dev)/sd(ddev) — and the position is shrunk when the two disagree (non-Gaussian/jumpy/nonstationary tape, unidentified clock) and when the clock is faster than half the horizon (unresolvable bounce). The edge should persist because it requires per-name estimation of both an oscillation clock and an excursion age from noisy 10-second data and pays only inside a 60-second window, where capacity is tiny; crowding in naive reversal actually manufactures the oscillation the phase model exploits.
factors.name: Excursion-phase (Kac/Rice clock) horizon-matched projection

factors.trading_idea: Parent A showed that transient impact debt is repaid on the trade clock, but it treated every push as equally repayable; Parent B showed that repair only happens when the *hedge legs* are live, yet its fundamental-multiple impulse was too slow for a 6-bar offset. The child keeps A's state variable — an outstanding impact-debt stock discounted by volume actually traded since each push — but splits the push into a peer-idiosyncratic part (name minus industry median) and a peer-common part (industry median minus market), and runs the idiosyncratic debt on a *bottleneck hedge clock*: the harmonic mean of the name's own relative flow and its leave-one-out peer-basket relative flow, since unwinding an idiosyncratic dislocation consumes liquidity on both legs simultaneously. The interaction carries edge neither parent has alone: two names with identical debt stocks and identical own volume get very different 6-bar repayment fractions when one has a live comparables basket to hedge into and the other does not, while genuinely peer-common debt is discounted with a much slower kernel because factor risk cannot be laid off at all.
factors.name: Bottleneck hedge-clock repayment of idiosyncratic vs peer-common impact debt

factors.trading_idea: Unsigned 10-second volume cannot separate informed from uninformed trading — it is essentially a marker of liquidity DEMAND — so the parent's assumption that idiosyncratic bursts flag information-bearing metaorders was mis-specified, and its realized IC sign says so: over a ~60-second horizon the Bouchaud propagator's transient (depth-refill) component dominates the permanent component, while genuine information at second scale arrives mainly as quote repricing between trades. The child therefore stops asking whether the activity was common or idiosyncratic and instead asks WHERE inside the window the displacement was produced relative to the activity: the volume-time-weighted mean increment minus the calendar-time-weighted mean increment (the wedge) isolates displacement bought with abnormal demand while algebraically cancelling the plain 6-bar reversal level the book already spans. The second, timing ingredient is that transient impact only relaxes once the demand stops, so the fade is conditioned on flow extinction — excess activity in the two most recent bars being small relative to the window average — which sets the clock for when the give-back actually lands inside the 6-bar horizon. Falsifiable on two counts: if demand-concentrated displacement does not underperform (wedge IC ≥ 0), the transient-impact attribution is wrong; and if the extinction gate does not amplify the wedge's IC versus the ungated wedge, the relaxation-timing claim is wrong. It survives arbitrage because monetising it requires panel-wide, per-name volume-clock estimation at second resolution and offers only spread-limited, one-minute capacity, so market makers harvest it on their own inventory rather than as a cross-sectional relative-value trade.
factors.name: Activity-timed displacement wedge with flow-extinction timing

factors.trading_idea: The parent truncated each name's market impulse response at exactly the forecast horizon (L=H=6), which implicitly assumes the catch-up never overshoots; on 10-second bars the true response kernel has a *negative* tail at lags 7-18 (transient impact being unwound / quote bounce), and that omitted mass is precisely why the parent's IC was strongly negative at 12-24 bars and nearly zero at the pinned 6-bar offset. This child estimates the kernel out to 3H lags and folds every loading against its exactly matched already-observed market window (trailing l-bar sum for l<=H, an H-bar market window lagged l-H for l>H), so the 6-bar forecast nets still-owed catch-up against already-owed overshoot correction name by name. Conditioning is sharpened from ad hoc clientele proxies to the kernel's own geometry: the 'owed share' = fraction of total |kernel| mass that is actually deliverable inside the next 6 bars, times microstructural staleness (frozen-mid fraction, thin relative volume), and the whole cross-section is trusted only when the recent index move is permanent (market variance ratio > 1). The edge persists because separating catch-up from overshoot requires per-name multi-lag kernel estimation and pays off mainly in slow, thin names where second-scale arbitrage capital faces impact costs; it is falsified if the far-lag loadings (7-18) add nothing over the L=6 truncation, or if owed-share fails to discriminate.
factors.name: Overshoot-Extended Lag Kernel, Owed-Share Folded

factors.trading_idea: The parent's grind-vs-jump split was right in spirit but was estimated on a 120-bar window, so the signal only turned over on a multi-minute clock and its information peaked at 12-24 bars rather than the fixed 6-bar offset. This child measures the same structural distinction inside the *forecast-length window itself* and adds the missing conditioning channel: two exact, scale-free Dirichlet nulls for share concentration. Over the last 6 bars, squared log-return shares are Dirichlet(1/2) under an i.i.d. Gaussian price null (so E[HHI]=3/(k+2)) while volume shares are Dirichlet(1) under an i.i.d. exponential flow null (E[HHI]=2/(k+1)); the wedge between the two excesses says whether the recent move was carried by price concentration *without* matching trade concentration (a liquidity vacuum: few contracts moved the mid a lot, depth was thin, so the move overshoots and snaps back) or by evenly-sliced increments arriving with clustered flow (Lillo-Farmer parent-order splitting, which keeps working). Interacting the signed wedge with the same-window volatility-normalised drift therefore predicts the next 60 seconds with the drift continuing when flow concentration dominates and reversing when price concentration dominates; it survives arbitrage because desks monitor autocorrelation, realised vol and volume separately and almost never compare the *concentration* of variance against the concentration of the flow that produced it, and the residual is largest exactly in the thin, small-cap names whose illiquidity caps capacity.
factors.name: Dirichlet concentration wedge: price-variance vs trade-flow concentration

factors.trading_idea: A hedged residual against a valuation-matched peer basket mixes two very different objects: single-name inventory pressure, which one arbitrageur can close in under a minute by trading one stock against a small basket, and a *tier-level* shock (a discount-rate or business-mix re-rating shared by everything in the same valuation neighbourhood) which is a genuine omitted common factor and therefore does not revert on a one-minute clock, because closing it requires simultaneously trading the whole neighbourhood. The child therefore projects each name's 1-bar hedged residual on the kernel-weighted average residual of its own valuation neighbours and bets only on the *purged*, doubly-orthogonalised part, gated by hedgeability (trailing R-squared of the name on its basket) since only a well-hedgeable name is cheap enough to arbitrage quickly. Falsifiable: if the cluster-common residual component snaps back just as fast as the name-specific part (i.e. purging it does not raise IC over the parent's plain hedged residual), the omitted-tier-factor mechanism is wrong and the parent's edge is generic peer reversal. The edge persists because joining point-in-time per-share fundamentals to a 10-second tape to define the neighbourhood, and then estimating a second-stage loading on that neighbourhood's own residual factor, is operationally awkward for pure microstructure arbitrageurs, and capacity is capped by the small number of tight valuation neighbourhoods.
factors.name: Cluster-common-purged valuation-peer hedge residual snapback

factors.trading_idea: Parent B showed that a 100-second path splits into probed-but-unconverted excursion (continuation) and converted net displacement (snapback), with the conversion ratio c as the switch; but it applies the *same* snapback polarity to every converted move, which is wrong when the move was produced by a live scheduler. Parent A's volume-share evenness is exactly the state that separates those cases: an evenly sliced participation profile (high per-name entropy percentile) means an unfinished metaorder is still paying for the displacement, so the converted move is permanent and continues, whereas volume mass concentrated in one or two bars means a single sweep whose impact decays as depth refills, so the converted move snaps back. The child therefore lets the evenness state *sign* the displacement leg (weight c·e) and only *modulate* the absorbed-probe leg (weight (1-c)·(1-0.5e), stronger after a bursty absorbed sweep because the endpoint mid is a stale sample of where aggression reached). The interaction carries edge neither parent has alone: Parent A had no way to know whether the directional path was converted flow or unabsorbed probing (hence its contradicted sign and 94% overlap with the book), and Parent B averaged a scheduler-continuation regime against a burst-reversion regime inside its single -c·D leg.
factors.name: Evenness-switched conversion polarity: schedule vs burst on probe/sweep

factors.trading_idea: Transient price impact from sliced flow relaxes at a name-specific rate kappa, so the *outstanding* deviation at time t is the price minus an exponentially-weighted anchor whose half-life equals that name's own clock, and the part of it that is actually repaid inside a fixed h-bar window is dev*(1-2^(-h/halflife)) — a quantity that is maximised at an interior half-life of order h and vanishes for very slow clocks. The parent fed a *fixed* 60-bar deviation into a monotone 'slower is better' gate, which is why it loaded on names whose repayment happens far beyond the fixed 6-bar offset (its IC peaked at 24 bars and was spanned by the book's slow reversal factors). The child estimates each name's half-life causally by two independent routes (Rice/Blomqvist sign-flip inversion of the lag-1 autocorrelation, and a second-moment mean-squared-displacement inversion at lag h), then reads the deviation off a *bank* of EWMA anchors with a kernel that selects the scale matching the estimated half-life and weights it by the theoretical 6-bar repaid fraction, shrinking size when the two clock estimates disagree. The edge survives arbitrage because the decay clock is a latent nuisance parameter: liquidity providers who fade with a mis-matched window either pay the spread on already-decayed bounce or carry inventory past the horizon, so correct scale-matching is a modelling edge rather than free money.
factors.name: OU half-life matched multiscale transient fade
