factors.trading_idea: Parent A showed that the Epps/lag-1-corrected precision-whitened 6-bar dislocation carries relative-value information the book does not span, but it had no state variable telling it whether a dislocation will be paid back or pushed further inside one minute; Parent B built exactly such a state variable (a scale-free local-time recurrence density of the mid at its current level) but applied it to the raw 6-bar move, whose market-wide component swamped the interaction and whose declared sign was contradicted. The child conditions A's *peer-orthogonal* dislocation on B's *cross-sectionally purged* occupancy state, with B's empirically realized direction and a mechanism that explains it: a name that displaces itself relative to its whitened peer basket while its mid sits on a high-occupancy, well-supplied level must have consumed genuine resting depth, which is costly, informed flow that keeps eating the queue (continuation); the identical displacement achieved in a low-occupancy vacuum is fleeting, trade-unbacked quote drift, i.e. pure transient impact that relaxes within six bars (reversal). The interaction carries edge neither parent has alone because whitening removes the common-factor moves that make vacuum extensions look like information (B's failure mode), while occupancy supplies the missing convergence-capacity clock that A's oscillator only proxied — and A's lag-1 antisymmetric lead/lag role is reused to size the vacuum-relaxation leg, since only measured laggards owe a repayment while leaders' vacuum moves are price discovery.
factors.name: Local-time-backed precision dislocation role split

factors.trading_idea: Parent B's participation-weighted range-position displacement measures where inside a heavy-volume bar the mid ended up, i.e. the unpaid cost of immediacy that relaxes as depth refills; Parent A's shock-selected distributed-lag kernel measures how much systematic move the name still OWES the market impulse. The child first *purges* the displacement of the part that is mechanically explained by the owed-delivery gap (trailing per-name OLS residual of displacement on the gap), so the fade is applied only to displacement nobody was entitled to, and then routes between the two channels with a state variable neither parent uses: the participation-weighted wick share of the last 6 bars (range minus body over range), which distinguishes bars where aggressive size was absorbed and retraced from clean directional body moves. Where absorption is high the un-owed displacement is pure liquidity provision and snaps back; where bars are body-dominated the displacement is beta delivery in progress and the owed-catch-up direction carries the sign. The interaction is the edge: B cannot tell a low close inside a heavy range from legitimate downside beta delivery, and A has no within-bar geometry to know whether the push was absorbed or accepted.
factors.name: Absorption-wick routed, un-owed transient snapback

factors.trading_idea: The parent showed that quote-driven (zero/thin-volume) mid drift persists while volume-paid drift decays, but it pooled 30 bars of flat-weighted drift, so its information was a slow state variable that only fully paid off many minutes out. The child fixes the timescale two ways: (i) the two legs are decay-weighted over just 12 bars so the newest repricing dominates, and (ii) the split is conditioned on a genuinely new variable — the name's activity innovation *after removing the market-wide lull* (per-name log-volume innovation, cross-sectionally demeaned). Mechanism: when a name goes quiet while its peers keep trading, the silence is name-specific liquidity withdrawal (a dealer shading quotes ahead of expected flow), so the quiet drift is information that completes as the next order arrives within ~1 minute; when the whole cross-section is quiet, thin-bar mid moves are stale-quote flicker and carry no drift, while a name that is idiosyncratically busy is mostly paying transient impact that decays. The same gate doubles as a precision weight (the up-weighted leg is always the one estimated from more bars), and the edge survives arbitrage because harvesting the quiet leg requires crossing the spread in names that are, at that instant, the least liquid in the cross-section. Falsified if the continuation of quiet-bar drift is independent of relative activity (gate adds nothing over the ungated parent) or if traded-bar drift does not revert faster when activity is idiosyncratically elevated.
factors.name: Idiosyncratic-Silence Gated Quiet vs Traded Drift Split

factors.trading_idea: Parent A showed that within-bar displacement is only worth fading once the part a name still *owes* the market impulse has been projected out; Parent B's realized (negative) IC says an efficient multi-bar grind accompanied by unusually EVEN bar-volume shares is not an unfinished metaorder to ride but mechanical, scheduled impact that relaxes — because the even-participation footprint means the price is being pushed by a size-driven scheduler rather than by information, and the permanent component of such flow is small. The child therefore builds TWO un-owed transient channels at different timescales — the participation-weighted within-bar close-location displacement (A, 3 bars) and the signed path-efficiency drift (B, 18 bars) — each orthogonalised per name against A's shock-identified owed-beta gap, and fades their average with a router that multiplies A's within-bar absorption meter (wick share) by B's cross-bar schedule meter (normalised volume-share entropy minus its own trailing mean); when the router is low (bursty, body-dominated, informed acceptance) the sign is handed back to the owed systematic catch-up gap instead. The interaction is the edge: B alone cannot tell scheduled impact from legitimate owed beta delivery (which is exactly why its declared sign inverted), and A alone has no cross-bar participation-shape state to know whether the un-owed displacement is still being re-pressed by a live scheduler or has been abandoned.
factors.name: Schedule/absorption-routed un-owed dual-scale transient fade

factors.trading_idea: Parent A says an under-responded (beta-implied) displacement gets repaired with a lag when the holder base is slow income capital; Parent B says a displacement only pays at a fixed 6-bar offset if its own oscillation clock is comparable to 6 bars. The child measures the displacement on the *beta-residual* path (so the clock being counted is the idiosyncratic repair clock, not the market's own oscillation that contaminates raw-price crossings), reads that name's repair clock from zero-crossings of the residual deviation, stretches the clock by a payout-clientele score (mandate-constrained income holders re-optimise slowly, so their true repair period is longer than the noisy crossing estimate suggests), and then (i) measures the displacement at the lookback scale matched to that clock and (ii) trades it with a sech^2 horizon-match weight peaking where the clock equals 6 bars. The interaction is the edge: A's wedge is blind to whether repair lands before or after t+6, B's clock is estimated on a market-contaminated series and has no economic prior on who is slow — jointly, a residual displacement whose clientele-adjusted clock sits on the 6-bar holding window is exactly the subset in which slow-capital catch-up is both real and cashable at the fixed offset.
factors.name: Clientele-clocked beta-repair scale mixture

factors.trading_idea: Transient impact is repaid at the speed at which visible depth replenishes, so the *same* within-bar overpush pays back at very different clock speeds across names. I estimate each name's replenishment rate directly as the trailing AR(1) persistence phi of its own realized inverse-depth (bar range per unit sqrt-participation): a liquidity shock decays like phi^k, so the outstanding transient deviation is the phi-matched exponential stock of past pushes, and the fraction of it that is repaid inside exactly six 10-second bars is 1 - phi^6. Ranking the sector-purged, phi-matched push stock scaled by that delivery fraction moves the parent's edge from 24 bars onto the fixed 6-bar offset, because it stops mixing slow-refill names (whose repayment arrives after the horizon) with fast-refill names (whose repayment is complete inside it). The edge survives arbitrage because harvesting it requires posting passive size into the very thin, slowly-replenishing depth that created the displacement, so capacity is bounded by the illiquidity that generates the signal.
factors.name: Depth-refill AR(1) horizon-matched push repayment

factors.trading_idea: Parent B shows that a name's expected next-6-bar return splits into (i) the market impulse response still *owed* — its distributed-lag loadings convolved with exactly the observed market slices that deliver inside t+1..t+6 — and (ii) the horizon-folded AR(1) continuation of its own idiosyncratic innovation; Parent A shows that the owed piece only fires when a market impulse has actually landed and where repricing is slow (frozen mids, thin volume, mandate-constrained income clientele). The child makes the *mix* of the two pieces state-dependent instead of additive: a logistic router in the standardised size of the already-observed 6-bar market shock shifts weight toward the owed catch-up when a genuine common impulse is in flight, and toward the idiosyncratic overshoot term when the tape is quiet and there is simply nothing owed. The second, sharper interaction is that staleness is *asymmetric* across the two pieces — frozen mids and thin volume are exactly what create unincorporated market information (up-weight catch-up) but are also what manufacture spurious Roll/stale-price autocorrelation in the residual (down-weight overshoot) — so each component is gated by an opposite-signed function of the same microstructural state, an interaction neither parent can express since each applies one single 'slowness' gate to everything it forecasts.
factors.name: Impulse-Routed Owed Catch-Up vs. Residual Overshoot (staleness-asymmetric)

factors.trading_idea: Read together, both parents' realized (negative) ICs state one law from opposite sides: a displacement produced in a liquidity vacuum — high price variance per unit of traded volume, price walking into rarely-visited territory — is mostly TRANSIENT impact on a thin book and gives back within a minute, while a displacement that cost real volume and had to break away from a level the mid has repeatedly revisited (a defended, well-queued price) is PERMANENT repricing by informed size and continues. The child therefore trades the peer-relative 6-bar break with a POSITIVE (continuation) loading gated by permanence, and the synthesis is an AND-gate over two structurally different liquidity proxies neither parent combines: a path-geometry proxy (scale-free local-time recurrence density of the mid at the level it now stands on, from A) and a flow proxy (impact purity = variance burst per unit participation burst, from B). Permanence is only asserted when the two concur — geometric-mean magnitude with the shared sign, zero when they disagree — so the signal is silent exactly in the ambiguous states where each parent alone was diluted, and a short side-aligned flow-freshness weight (halflife 2 bars, 6-bar peak) concentrates the bet on live episodes so the edge lands at the fixed 6-bar offset rather than at 24 bars.
factors.name: Concordant permanence gate on peer-relative break

factors.trading_idea: A multi-bar mid pin with volume executing at it identifies a level where a patient, self-replenishing queue rests (a market maker or a working parent order that re-posts after each fill). The parent factor assumed every break of such a level is a queue clearing and must continue; the data said the opposite, and the microstructural reason is that most pin breaks are quote *withdrawal/repricing*, not consumption — the resting supply is still there, re-posts, and pulls the mid back, so the beta-residual displacement is transient (a propagator-style relaxation toward the magnet level). The break only becomes information when the aggression in the break bar actually exceeds the absorption rate the level was sustaining: the estimated depletion fraction phi = V_break / (V_break + A_pinned/run) separates 'the queue was withdrawn' (phi < 1/2, reversion) from 'the queue was swept and the next level is thinner' (phi > 1/2, continuation). The edge persists because each event pays a fraction of a tick and can only be captured by crossing a spread that is at least one tick wide in exactly the low-turnover, grid-bound names where pins occur; it is falsified if the 6-bar IC of the beta-residual break is flat in phi (i.e. reversion is uniform across depletion fractions) or if the high-phi bucket reverts too.
factors.name: Pinned-level queue-depletion fraction: refill reversion vs sweep continuation

factors.trading_idea: Decompose each name's 10-second log price into an efficient component plus a stationary transient component (quote bounce + un-relaxed transient impact). A k-bar aggregated return loads the transient term with +1 while the NEXT k-bar return loads it with -1, so the block-lag-1 autocorrelation of k-bar returns is mechanically negative and its magnitude equals the transient (noise) share of the last k-bar move; estimating that coefficient at exactly k = 6 bars makes the forecast horizon-matched by construction instead of being a slow level dislocation whose relaxation leaks past the window (the parent's defect: IC rose monotonically to 24 bars). The path is first hedged against a valuation-comparable peer basket (sector x slow valuation tercile) with a trailing OLS beta, because common-factor moves are information that must not be faded, and the per-name coefficient is shrunk toward the cross-sectional pooled coefficient with weight equal to the hedge R^2 (residual purity). The edge survives arbitrage because harvesting it means standing as the marginal liquidity supplier in a name whose transient share is only estimable statistically, and the per-event profit is a fraction of a spread relative to the inventory risk carried. Falsifiable: IC should PEAK near 6 bars and fall by 24 (opposite of the parent's profile), and sorting on the estimated |block autocorrelation| within displacement deciles must add IC — if the amplitude modulation is worthless the factor collapses to plain 6-bar reversal and the child fails.
factors.name: Peer-hedged block-autocorrelation noise-share reversal

factors.trading_idea: A directional mid move printed while essentially nothing trades cannot be information being impounded — by Milgrom–Stokey logic, information that nobody trades on is not paid for — so such a move is mostly one-sided quote withdrawal / stale-mid artefact that is reclaimed once competitive makers refill the depleted side; this is why the parent's declared continuation sign came out negative in the report, and the child adopts the snapback direction as the mechanism rather than as a sign flip. Instead of the parent's magnitude-based path efficiency, the child tests the quiet excursion with a distribution-free statistic whose null is exact: Lévy's arcsine law says that for a driftless walk the *time* of the running maximum has CDF (2/pi)·arcsin(sqrt(theta)), so late-max / early-min timing plus a terminal value pinned at the excursion extreme is scale-free evidence of true one-way relocation. The fade is then conditioned on the silence being idiosyncratic — peers actively trading while this name abstains — because a market-wide lull can host a genuine common repricing that should stick, whereas a name-specific abstention has no witness and no validation. Falsifiable: the edge dies if the arcsine timing statistic adds nothing over raw quiet displacement magnitude, or if the fade does not strengthen with relative abstention; it persists because harvesting it means quoting or crossing a momentarily thin, quiet book where the 60-second round-trip cost swamps the small reclaim for slower arbitrageurs.
factors.name: Arcsine-Law Extreme-Timing Test of Unbacked Quiet Quote Drift

factors.trading_idea: The parent confirmed that flow-paid displacement reverts, but it ranked a *level* of transient impact, so the reversion arrived on the market's own clock (IC peaked at 12 bars, not the fixed 6). Obizhaeva-Wang/Bouchaud resilience is a volume-clock phenomenon: depth replenishes when trades arrive, so the accumulated transient-impact stock decays at a rate proportional to contemporaneous trade intensity, not to wall-clock time. I therefore build a per-name impact stock with an activity-dependent propagator (I_t = (1-kappa_t)I_{t-1} + f_t, kappa_t rising with normalized volume) and multiply it by the *expected fraction that will decay over exactly the next 6 bars*, using the strong short-run autocorrelation of volume (Hawkes-style clustering) as the forward-intensity forecast — turning a slow state variable into a horizon-matched forecast of the next 60 seconds. The edge persists because execution algorithms keep working schedules that pay this transient cost while market makers price impact with a single global calendar half-life; correctly timing the resilience clock per name requires the joint estimate (impact scale x predicted intensity) and is capacity-limited, so it is not arbitraged away.
factors.name: Volume-clock resilience: expected 6-bar decay of the transient impact stock

factors.trading_idea: Parent A showed that valuation-peer-residual displacement decomposes into a trade-attributable leg and a quiet quote-relocation leg with *opposite* forward coefficients, but it forced one universal sign on the traded leg; Parent B showed that whether a trade-driven push is given back is a slowly-varying per-name fingerprint, measurable as the negative cross-lag correlation between a bar's body and the next bar's seam (quote relocation). The child therefore routes the traded leg's sign by that absorption fingerprint: in names whose seams habitually walk back bodies the accumulated trade-attributable push is transient impact and is faded, while in names whose seams extend bodies the same push is a live metaorder and is followed — and the quiet, unbacked leg is faded with strength proportional to the absorption state, because it is precisely absorbing market-makers who retract unsupported quote relocations. The interaction carries edge neither parent has alone: A supplies the fundamentally-comparable peer hedge and the participation-based attribution that isolates *which* part of the move is impact, B supplies the per-name clock that tells you whether that impact relaxes inside 60 seconds, resolving A's contradicted sign instead of blindly flipping it.
factors.name: Absorption-state routed traded/quiet peer displacement split

factors.trading_idea: The parent asked, episode by episode, whether an untraded mid excursion was 'efficient' relative to a k^(-1/2) random-walk null — but with k = 2..10 quiet bars that per-path statistic has enormous sampling error, so its excess-efficiency term was mostly noise and the realized IC collapsed onto the unconditional effect (quiet, trade-unconfirmed displacement reverts), which is why the declared sign was contradicted. The child estimates the *same latent quantity* — whether a name's mid process behaves as a relocating random walk or as a bounce/flicker process while nobody trades — by pooling many quiet episodes into a trade-conditional Lo–MacKinlay variance ratio: lag-1 and lag-2 autocorrelations of mid returns computed only over consecutive runs of quiet bars, Bartlett-weighted to the 6-bar horizon. That variance ratio is the *polarity* of the pending untraded excursion: VR < 1 (bounce-dominated quoting, stale-mid wobble) implies the open displacement snaps back toward the last traded anchor, VR > 1 (genuine reservation-price relocation) implies it extends; the signal is displacement × (VR−1)/2 × the probability that trading resumes within 6 bars, then cross-sectionally orthogonalised against the unmodulated displacement so the factor carries only the polarity information. The edge survives arbitrage because monetising it requires crossing the spread in names that are momentarily quiet and thin — unattractive round-trip cost for slower participants — and because the state variable is a second-moment estimate conditional on trade *absence*, which almost no standard signal library computes.
factors.name: Quiet-clock conditional variance ratio × untraded excursion polarity

factors.trading_idea: Each bar's idiosyncratic move splits multiplicatively into a trade-backed leg (return x trailing volume percentile) and an unbacked quote-drift leg (return x one minus that percentile): only the backed leg transfers inventory and therefore creates a repayment obligation, while unbacked drift is pure quote relocation that must either be confirmed by later aggressive flow or snap back. Because the two legs feed each other — absorbed pushes provoke quote relocation, and unbacked drift attracts flow that validates or refutes it — the expected return over exactly the next 6 bars is the 6-step summed impulse response of the *bivariate* system, not the mass of a single-equation body->seam lag kernel; cross-channel feedback makes the intermediate-horizon response hump-shaped or sign-flipped, which is precisely why the parent's single-equation kernel leaked its power to 12 bars. So we fit a 2x2 VAR(1) per name by trailing ridged Yule-Walker, shrink it toward the pooled cross-sectional system, iterate the companion matrix six steps, and gate the forecast by the eigenvalue-implied fraction of total response mass that lands inside the window, 1 - rho^6, shrinking out names whose repayment is too slow to complete by t+6. The edge survives arbitrage because collecting it means posting passive size against possibly-informed aggression for a fraction of the spread (inventory risk that cannot be lifted directionally), and because the per-name coefficients and the backing split are re-estimated continuously rather than imposed.
factors.name: Trade-backing split bivariate VAR with 6-bar window-mass gate

factors.trading_idea: The parent's realized sign says the propagator reading is wrong at a 10-second granularity: transient impact from a metaorder slice relaxes in well under one bar, so what survives to the bar close of a *traded* displacement is mostly the permanent, information-bearing component (Hasbrouck's trade-innovation permanent impact), while mid displacement that arrives with little or no print is largely quote flicker / one-sided depth withdrawal that snaps back once the queue refills. Rather than asserting either sign, the child *estimates* the wedge: it runs a causal, cross-sectionally pooled two-regressor OLS of realized 6-bar peer-residual return on the lagged kernel-weighted traded leg and quiet leg, and uses the fitted coefficients to combine today's two legs into a forecast. The edge persists because harvesting it means providing liquidity against possibly-informed bursts while fading quote noise, and because the sign of the wedge is regime-dependent (it inverts between calm and stressed depth), so a static-sign version of the same decomposition — like the parent — averages the two regimes to nearly zero. Falsifiable: if the pooled coefficients on the traded and quiet legs are statistically indistinguishable, or if they are unstable noise so that the fitted combination has no more IC than either leg alone, the child dies.
factors.name: Pooled permanence regression: traded vs quiet displacement

factors.trading_idea: Sixty-second liquidity provision is only compensated when a name's deviation from its beta- and sector-hedged path is inventory noise rather than news; whether it is one or the other is a *market-wide* state, not a per-name one. I measure that state scale-free as the share of average cross-sectional return variance captured by the equal-weighted market factor (E[m_t^2]/E[mean_i r_it^2] over a trailing window ≈ average pairwise correlation): when commonality is high, quotes move together and a single name's residual excursion is dealer/index inventory imbalance that is repaid within a few bars, so fade it; when commonality collapses (dispersion regime, idiosyncratic news arrival), residual excursions are private information being impounded and continue, so the same cross-sectional score must flip sign. Repayment also needs a live queue, so the fade is tilted toward names whose own recent volume is high relative to their own history. The edge survives arbitrage because the profitable leg is inventory-bearing liquidity supply (a genuine risk premium), and because almost all deployed short-horizon reversal signals are sign-static in time — they average the profitable high-commonality regime with the loss-making dispersion regime, leaving the conditional version un-arbitraged.
factors.name: Commonality-share regime-flipped hedged idiosyncratic reversal

factors.trading_idea: Transitory price impact does not decay at a fixed autoregressive rate: empirically (Bouchaud et al.) the impact of a liquidity-demanding metaorder relaxes on the timescale of the metaorder itself, roughly as I(t) ~ (1 + t/T)^{-beta} measured from the moment execution stops. The parent tried to learn that timescale from a 900-bar variance curve with two hard-wired decay constants, so its filter loaded on a near-random-walk slow component and its edge only matured at 24 bars. The child instead *observes* the clock in real time: the trailing age distribution of excess volume is moment-matched to a uniform execution window, yielding the burst duration T = sqrt(12)*sd(age) and the time-since-cessation a = mean(age) - sqrt(3)*sd(age); the displacement is then measured over exactly the window (a+T) that the burst spans, split by the square-root impact law into a 'justified' part (only ~1/3 of which relaxes) and an unjustified over-push (which relaxes fully), and only the analytic fraction 1 - ((T+a+h)/(T+a))^{-beta} that is repaid inside 6 bars enters the ranking, killed by a liveness gate while the burst is still adding impact. The edge survives arbitrage because collecting it means absorbing the inventory the burst's counterparty is shedding, and because a pooled reversal signal cannot distinguish a 30-second sweep (which pays back inside a minute) from a 10-minute VWAP program (which does not) — they have opposite 60-second payoffs and net out in any un-conditioned reversal book.
factors.name: Metaorder duration/age moment-matched impact relaxation (60s delivery)

factors.trading_idea: At the 10-second scale a mid-price displacement is either *paid for* by order flow (informed metaorder slicing: repricing happens where the trades are) or *unpaid* (thin-book quote drift, dealer inventory shuffling, absorption elsewhere). A single name cannot tell these apart over one minute — the estimate is pure noise — but the whole cross-section can: each bar, the Spearman concordance between names' self-normalised volume and their self-normalised absolute repricing is a high-power, dimensionless read on which regime the market is in. When concordance is abnormally high, one-sided flow is unfinished informed flow and fresh sqrt-volume-weighted pressure continues over the next ~minute; when concordance collapses, displacement is being generated without flow backing it, so it is transient inventory/quote noise and relaxes. The parent showed that fresh pressure unconditionally *reverts* (IC < 0); this child asserts the reversion is a regime average and that the sign of the conditional IC is governed by the panel-wide flow–move coupling, i.e. IC_conditional ≈ a + b·g with a<0 and b>0, so the pure interaction earns b·Var(g) > 0. The edge survives arbitrage because exploiting it requires recomputing a panel-wide dependence statistic in real time and *flipping the sign* of a short-horizon flow signal within a minute — most desks run either a momentum or a reversal book, not a state-switching one, and the net-of-spread capacity at this scale is tiny.
factors.name: Cross-sectional volume–move concordance regime flip on fresh flow pressure

factors.trading_idea: Parent A shows that price change printed in (near-)zero-volume bars is quote-shading that continues while volume-paid displacement decays, but its edge accrues slowly (IC peaks at 24 bars) because it never asks how much of that continuation is actually payable inside the next six bars; Parent B supplies exactly that machinery — a horizon-matched distributed-lag kernel folded against already-observed information, mixed by channel probabilities — but it is anchored to the market path only and has weak standalone signal. The child attributes BOTH its own increments and the cap-weighted market increments to the bar's volume state, so a source is one of four: own-quiet quote walking, own-active paid impact, market moves that arrived while this name was silent (information it has seen but not yet traded against), and market moves that arrived while it was active (already absorbed); each source gets its own trailing per-lag response kernel on lags 1..6, signal-to-noise-shrunk and pooled cross-sectionally, and only the kernel mass deliverable within the fixed 6-bar offset is folded against the realised trailing sums. The interaction is the edge: the sign of continuation vs reversal is no longer imposed by hypothesis but estimated per name per channel, and the silence-sourced debt legs are scaled by the name's current trade-arrival rate relative to its own long-run rate — the debt only gets paid at the speed trading resumes, which is precisely what converts A's slow quiet/traded wedge into a 6-bar-matched forecast and gives B's kernel a state variable (own silence) it never had.
factors.name: Silence-Sourced Response Kernel with Activity Delivery Rate

factors.trading_idea: Firms are the one class of participant whose trading direction is known in advance and is price-insensitive: an active repurchaser has a standing algorithmic *bid* working the tape all day (Rule 10b-18 VWAP slicing), while a net issuer (ATM/secondary/option-driven supply) is a standing *offer*. This makes short-horizon liquidity provision asymmetric at the firm level: an idiosyncratic dip in a heavy repurchaser is absorbed by corporate demand and snaps back within a minute, whereas a rally in a net issuer is capped by corporate supply — so the reversal coefficient should be a hinge in the sign of the dislocation interacted with the sign of net corporate share issuance, not a symmetric linear reversal. Because participation is capped as a fraction of contemporaneous volume, the support strength scales with current relative volume. The edge survives arbitrage because intraday buyback schedules are never disclosed (only quarterly totals), so an arbitrageur cannot distinguish a corporate-supported dip from genuine adverse information ex ante and must warehouse inventory risk; it is falsified if downside reversion at 6 bars is identical for repurchasers and issuers, i.e. if the hinge interaction adds nothing over symmetric reversal.
factors.name: Corporate Net-Demand Hinge (asymmetric intraday dislocation)

factors.trading_idea: What makes 60-second returns autocorrelated is order splitting, not price level per se: an institution that must rebuild a position because the firm's cash-flow path actually changed keeps sending same-signed child orders for minutes, whereas a pure inventory shock is a one-off that market makers unwind. The latest earnings report tells us cross-sectionally which names have a live fundamental repricing story — a large surprise whose EPS and revenue legs agree is a genuine change in fundamentals, while a small or internally contradictory surprise (EPS beat on a revenue miss, i.e. cost/accrual/share-count driven) leaves fair value untouched. The child therefore predicts the SIGN of short-horizon impulse persistence from a direction-free earnings news-intensity-and-concordance score: continuation where the news is big and concordant, reversal where it is absent or contradictory. It survives arbitrage because it requires joining quarterly accounting concordance to 10-second impulses; a market maker who standardises impulses by realised volatility hedges the move but not its conditional persistence, and direction-free concordance scores carry no static factor tilt that a risk model would already neutralise.
factors.name: Beat-concordance gated impulse persistence flip

factors.trading_idea: Parent B splits each bar's idiosyncratic mid move into permanent (quiet bar = quote re-anchoring, continues) versus transient (heavy bar = metaorder concession, reverts), but it treats ALL heavy-flow bars as transient; Parent A knows that heavy volume which arrives *metronomically* is a working VWAP/POV parent order whose remaining child orders keep pushing price, while bursty volume is one-off aggression whose displacement decays. The child therefore uses Parent A's per-name volume-regularity shock not as a multiplicative gate on aggregate drift but as a *shift of the permanence threshold* in Parent B's bar-level decomposition: gate_t = -tanh(a_t - s), where a_t is the two-way-demeaned per-bar flow innovation and s is the smoothness (negative CV) z-score. When volume has just turned metronomic the boundary between 'permanent' and 'transient' moves up, so scheduled-heavy bars are accumulated as continuation; when volume has turned bursty the boundary moves down, so even mildly active bars are faded. The interaction carries edge neither parent has: A applies one sign to a 30-bar aggregate and cannot tell which individual bars were scheduled, while B mislabels the scheduled-flow bars — exactly the bars with the largest, most persistent displacement — as transient.
factors.name: Metronome-shifted flow-permanence threshold

factors.trading_idea: The parent imposed a fixed sign on quiet-vs-traded drift (quote repricing persists, paid-for impact reverts) and measured it over slow 30-120 bar statistics, which is why its information only matured near 24 bars. This child keeps the economics but *estimates* them instead of assuming them, and does so at exactly the forecast scale: over a trailing hour it runs a per-name, no-intercept OLS of the current volatility-normalised 6-bar block return on the immediately preceding non-overlapping 6-bar block return and on that block's return interacted with its standardised log volume. The two fitted, precision-shrunk coefficients are the name's current one-lag propagation of price moves and the elasticity of that propagation to how much volume paid for the move; applying them to the just-completed block gives a direct forecast of the next 6 bars. It is falsifiable: if per-name block-AR coefficients and their volume interaction are pure estimation noise (not persistent over ~1 hour) the IC is zero. The edge survives arbitrage because the sign of minute-scale serial dependence differs by name and drifts with liquidity conditions, so no static momentum or reversal trade harvests it; the residual payoff is compensation for supplying liquidity to names currently in a reverting, volume-heavy state at a horizon where spread costs bite.
factors.name: Horizon-matched learned impact-decay elasticity

factors.trading_idea: The parent forecast a latent AR(1)-plus-AR(1) pricing error with infinite-memory exponential filters, so its ranking was still dominated by dislocations that amortise far beyond 60 seconds (its IC kept rising to 24 bars). The child drops the latent-state model entirely and estimates the object we are actually scored on — the conditional mean of the NEXT 6-bar idiosyncratic block return — by a model-free best linear projection onto the two immediately preceding non-overlapping 6-bar blocks, using the name's own trailing raw second-moment matrix; any component of a dislocation whose repayment falls outside the 6-bar window contributes almost nothing to the block-lag covariances and therefore receives a near-zero gain automatically, which is the horizon-matching the parent tried and failed to impose by assumption. Two blocks (not one) are used because the sign pattern distinguishes sustained one-way liquidity demand (same-sign blocks, a live metaorder that keeps pushing) from an overshoot that has already begun retracing (opposite-sign blocks, a finished metaorder being unwound), and the projection gains are estimated separately in heavy- and light-flow states (recent 6-bar volume rate above vs below the name's own normal rate) because a live metaorder and a completed one imply opposite repayment dynamics for the same observed path. The edge survives arbitrage because collecting it means absorbing inventory at exactly the moment liquidity providers are unwinding it, and because the ranking needs each name's own block-scale second moments conditioned on its own flow state — objects invisible to a pooled short-term reversal signal.
factors.name: Flow-state conditional horizon-exact block projection

factors.trading_idea: A beta-implied catch-up wedge (Parent A) only closes if some agent is actually working the repricing; the shape of a name's own volume tells you whether that agent is present. When a slow-capital, income-clientele name lags its beta-implied response to a market move AND its bar volume has just turned metronomic (low own-CV versus its recent norm — a VWAP/POV scheduler grinding the reprice through), the residual gap is unfinished order flow and closes within the next minute; when volume has just turned bursty, the apparent gap is one-off aggressive impact and depth-refill noise, so the gap widens/reverses instead. The interaction carries edge neither parent has alone: Parent A cannot distinguish a genuinely stale price from a liquidity-shock print, and Parent B's volume-regularity gate is applied to raw drift with no economic anchor for where price *should* be, so its gate mostly modulates momentum noise; anchoring the gate to a beta-implied target and to a clientele of slow holders makes the schedule fingerprint informative about closure rather than about drift.
factors.name: Schedule-gated clientele beta catch-up closure

factors.trading_idea: Parent A measures the beta-implied move a slow-clientele name still owes the market but treats every realised tick as genuine delivery of that debt; Parent B shows that ticks printed in quiet (near-zero-volume) bars are permanent quote repricing only when they are grind-carried (many small same-signed increments, Rice sign-flip excess < 0), while ticks bought with aggressive volume are largely transient impact. The child therefore discounts the *delivered* part of the beta debt by stream: quiet-bar move counts fully, active-bar move only fractionally (transient), so the residual debt is what remains genuinely unpriced — and that residual is trusted only when the name's quiet stream is currently grind-carried, i.e. its mid is actually being walked tick by tick rather than sitting stale (Rice gap inside the quiet stream). A second leg fades active-bar drift that the active-stream Rice gap flags as jump-carried impact into thin depth. The interaction is the edge: A cannot distinguish a name whose quote is lagging-but-updating (debt will be paid within tens of seconds) from a frozen/stale quote (debt is a measurement artefact), and B has no notion of how much move is *owed* at all, so it applies one blunt sign-persistence gap to an undirected drift.
factors.name: Rice-Delivery-Discounted Beta Debt Catch-Up

factors.trading_idea: A corporate repurchase bid is not a free-floating 'standing bid': Rule 10b-18's safe harbour makes it a MECHANICALLY SCHEDULED one — it cannot be the opening transaction, cannot trade in the last ten minutes of the session for actively traded names, cannot bid above the last independent price (so it only ever absorbs downticks), is capped at 25% of ADV per day, and desks are benchmarked to the session VWAP so they lean hardest when price sits below cumulative VWAP. Those four constraints define an observable eligibility state — interior-of-session, unexhausted daily volume budget, price below session VWAP — during which an idiosyncratic dip in a net repurchaser meets price-insensitive demand and repairs within a minute, and outside which the same dip is unsupported. Net issuers (ATM/secondary/option-driven supply) face none of these constraints and if anything supply more into the close, so their rallies are capped with the opposite clock tilt: the reversal coefficient is a hinge in dislocation sign interacted with corporate net demand AND with the safe-harbour clock. The edge survives arbitrage because programme participation is never disclosed intraday (only quarterly totals and monthly average prices), so an arbitrageur cannot separate a corporately supported dip from informed selling ex ante and must warehouse inventory risk; it is falsified if the repurchaser dip-repair at 6 bars is the same inside and outside the safe-harbour window and is unrelated to daily volume-budget exhaustion.
factors.name: 10b-18 Safe-Harbor Clock: budget-gated VWAP-dip absorption

factors.trading_idea: Parent A's quiet/active bar classification is not just a signal — it is the correct *sample selector* for Parent B's price-impact regression: near-zero-volume bars contribute only stale-mid noise and pure quote revisions, so including them biases the no-intercept lambda toward zero and depresses its R-squared. I therefore estimate the per-name impact coefficient lambda and its uncentred R-squared on ACTIVE bars only, then use the resulting trust score to interpolate continuously between B's fine decomposition (short only the flow-explained transient part of traded displacement, long the unexplained permanent residual) and A's cruder fallback (short the whole traded drift) whenever flow genuinely fails to explain returns; quiet-bar displacement is always held long as pure belief-driven repricing. The interaction carries edge neither parent has: A cannot tell which portion of its active-bar drift is mechanically decaying impact versus genuine information, and B cannot tell when its lambda is trustworthy because its lambda is contaminated by exactly the quiet bars A isolates. The whole displacement window is decay-weighted with an effective memory of ~4 bars so the signal is matched to the fixed 6-bar offset rather than the 12-24 bar peak both parents drift toward.
factors.name: Active-sample lambda with trust-blended quiet/traded repricing split

factors.trading_idea: Both parents need the same missing quantity — the per-name adjustment clock — but each fails on a different side: parent A estimates the clock nonparametrically yet has to shrink size to zero whenever its two estimators disagree, and parent B bets that a beta-implied backlog closes within exactly 6 bars without ever estimating whether that name closes gaps that fast. The child converts both of A's clock estimators into a single per-bar persistence phi (crossing spacing via the Rice inversion phi=cos(pi/T), and the 6-bar block concordance via phi=rho^(1/6)), and uses B's payout-clientele score as an *empirical-Bayes prior on phi* — mandate-constrained income holders re-optimise slowly, so their dislocations are genuinely persistent — so that estimator disagreement now routes to a fundamentally-grounded prior instead of to no position. The clock then enters as a horizon-matched hump weight phi*(1-phi^6): full size only where the expected closure lands inside the fixed 6-bar offset, and it scales two channels whose mix is itself set by the clientele score — income/slow-capital names trade B's beta backlog (delivery of an owed market move), fast low-payout names trade A's idiosyncratic deviation fade (transient metaorder footprint). The interaction is the edge: the clock says *when* a gap closes, the clientele says *which kind* of gap is outstanding and supplies the prior when the clock is unidentified.
factors.name: Clientele-Prior Clock Closure: Beta Backlog vs Idio Fade

factors.trading_idea: Hidden resting liquidity is identified not by volume alone but by volume traded per unit of price displacement: a bar that absorbs unusually heavy flow while travelling an unusually small range is a bar in which a deep, largely invisible queue sat in the book. Conditioning the bar's failed-excursion asymmetry (upper wick minus lower wick, expressed as a fraction of the bar range, so it is a scale-free shape statistic needing no diffusion-scale estimate) on this Kyle-inverse depth measure isolates probes that were genuinely absorbed rather than mid-quote flicker; the surviving iceberg keeps capping the probed side for the next few bars, so price drifts toward the untested side. Because the effect lives in the residual life of a specific hidden queue, it decays in seconds, so the child weights only the freshest bars (exponential halflife of 2 bars) instead of smearing 18 bars — which is why the parent's edge leaked out to 24 bars and was weak at the fixed 6-bar offset. It persists against arbitrage because the size being inferred is never quoted: exploiting it requires crossing the spread against concealed depth, a cost that quote-only statistical arbitrageurs will not pay. Falsified if depth-gated wick asymmetry carries no more forward sign than raw volume-weighted wick asymmetry, i.e. if the interaction with volume-per-range is flat.
factors.name: Depth-gated fresh wick asymmetry (absorption imbalance)

factors.trading_idea: The parent showed that the grind/jump decomposition of short-horizon drift carries real information but with the OPPOSITE sign to its stated story and only over slow (12-24 bar) windows, because a 120-bar rolling autocorrelation is far too sluggish to describe the state of a 60-second forecast. The child keeps the decomposition but measures it locally and adds the microstructural variable the parent lacked: whether the price movement was actually traded through. Mechanism: over the last ~90s, the inverse-participation ratio of increments (m*sum r^4 / (sum r^2)^2, Gaussian null = 3) says whether the drift arrived as one or two large increments (information arrival) or as many small same-signed ticks, and the movement-weighted relative volume says whether those increments were absorbed by real size or were a quiet quote walk. Information-bearing, volume-backed jumps are under-reacted to and keep drifting for the next minute, whereas a diffuse, low-volume grind is a stale-quote / inventory-driven walk that snaps back — so the interaction (concentration + flow-backing) x normalised drift should predict the 6-bar return positively, and I orthogonalise it cross-sectionally against plain normalised drift so the signal is a pure conditioning effect rather than repackaged reversal. It survives arbitrage because desks trade the level of short-horizon momentum/reversal, not its magnitude-concentration-times-volume-participation conditioning, and the residualisation deliberately strips the crowded part.
factors.name: Flow-backed jump vs quiet grind: concentration relay of 90s drift

factors.trading_idea: Parent B knows WHERE fair value is (an industry-peer log-multiple spread) but not WHY the spread moved, so it fades informed trade-driven dislocations together with uninformed quote drift and therefore only pays off at long offsets; Parent A knows how to attribute a displacement to traded order flow via a Bouchaud power-law propagator, but its anchor is the name's own price path, and its realized sign showed that at 10-second granularity flow-explained displacement CONTINUES (order-splitting autocorrelation dominates kernel decay) while the flow-orthogonal piece snaps back. The child attributes the peer-multiple dislocation itself: it filters the propagator impact convolution with the same fast EWMA used to build the dislocation, regresses the dislocation on it per name to get a live impact coefficient lambda, and splits the dislocation into a flow-explained part and a flow-orthogonal (quiet quote-revision) part. It fades only the flow-orthogonal part, scaled by the model-implied fraction of it that an AR(1)/OU fit says reverts within exactly 6 bars, and simultaneously rides the flow-explained part forward using the trailing persistence of signed flow (geometric sum of the flow AR(1) over the next 6 bars). The interaction is the edge: valuation space supplies the fair-value anchor neither propagator alone has, flow attribution supplies the adverse-selection filter that makes the relative-value leg work at the fixed 6-bar offset instead of 24, and the OU clock plus flow-persistence clock horizon-match both legs to the same 60 seconds.
factors.name: Flow-attributed peer-multiple dislocation with OU convergence clock

factors.trading_idea: Parent B established that mid drift accrued since a name's last trade is an *open* quote relocation that the next incoming order tends to confirm; Parent A established that the increment-concentration (inverse-participation ratio) of a drift is worthless as a standalone signal but informative as a state variable describing *how* the drift was assembled. The child fuses them by computing the IPR on exactly the increments of the silent segment — using cumulative sums of r^2 and r^4 anchored at the last active bar, so the window length is the name's own silence age rather than an arbitrary 9- or 120-bar window — and using it to scale the hazard-gated pending displacement. A quiet displacement built from one or two decisive increments is a genuine reservation-price relocation by a maker who has repriced for inventory/adverse-selection reasons and will be confirmed when the silence breaks; the same net displacement built from many micro-ticks is stale-quote diffusion or a rounding walk with no reservation-price content, so it carries much less forward information. The interaction has edge neither parent has alone: Parent B treats all untraded drift as equally open (blending real relocations with stale-mid noise), and Parent A measured concentration on a fixed clock over bars that had already been traded through, which is precisely why its declared jump-continuation story failed — the concentration state only discriminates on the *untraded* segment, where the displacement has not yet been consummated.
factors.name: Untraded Displacement Shape Gate (IPR of Silent Increments × Arrival Hazard)

factors.trading_idea: A multi-bar pin with trades printing is direct evidence of a large resting queue at one grid level, but the parent's gate (total volume absorbed while pinned) grows mechanically with pin length, so it selected long, sleepy pins whose 10s mid changes are mostly transient quote/bounce noise — which is exactly why the realised sign was reversal, not continuation. The right discriminator is not how much was absorbed in total but the absorption *rate* (queue evidence per pinned bar) and whether the exit bar was *paid for*: a pin that ends on a volume burst of several times normal bar volume is a genuine queue clearing whose displacement is permanent, whereas a pin that ends with little or no trade is the provider stepping away or a quote drifting into a vacuum, and the mid is pulled back as the resting queue re-posts at the same level. So the child measures the *live, continuously re-estimated* beta-residual gap from the abandoned level (not a frozen break impulse), fades it toward the level, and lets the exit-bar volume burst flip the sign toward continuation; the magnet memory is consumed in volume time, not clock time, because it is trades — not seconds — that clear the level's remaining depth. The edge survives arbitrage because each event is worth a fraction of a tick in exactly the low-turnover, grid-bound names where crossing the spread destroys it: it is harvestable only by re-posting passively where the resting provider already stands.
factors.name: Abandoned-pin magnet: vacuum-vs-clearing split on the live gap

factors.trading_idea: The informative content of a bar's shadows is *which side's probe was rejected*, but only bars that actually traded size probe the book — a shadow printed on a quiet bar is mid-quote flicker, and the parent contaminated the statistic by mixing both and then dividing by a noisily-estimated trailing volatility (an estimation-noise term that fit in-sample and broke out-of-sample). Normalising each bar's shadow asymmetry by that same bar's own range makes it a scale-free, regime-invariant statistic in [-1,1], so the cross-section compares probe rejection rather than volatility levels, and gating on above-median traded volume keeps only genuine probes into concealed resting size (icebergs, refreshed passive depth). Recency-weighting the gated asymmetry over ~100 seconds keeps the reading fast enough to bite at the fixed 6-bar offset: if heavy-volume upside probes were just pushed back, real supply is still resting above and price should drift toward the untested side. The edge survives arbitrage because harvesting it means competing for queue position against the same concealed size while paying spread to impatient aggressors, and the state refreshes every ten seconds; it is falsified if the volume gate is irrelevant (i.e. quiet-bar and heavy-bar shadow asymmetry carry the same forward sign) or if the gated aggregate has no sign at 6 bars.
factors.name: Volume-gated range-normalised shadow rejection

factors.trading_idea: Parent A shows that a name carries a *measurable backlog* of market information — fold its distributed-lag loadings b_1..b_6 against the already-observed market path and you get a forecast whose kernel exactly matches the 6-bar offset — but it assumes one universal impulse response. Parent B shows that the shape of bar volume tells you *who* is trading: metronomic volume (collapsed own coefficient of variation) is a working VWAP/POV schedule that will keep repricing the name, while bursty volume is one-off aggression whose displacement is transient impact. The child therefore estimates the lag kernel *separately in the two volume-shape regimes* and folds the currently-active kernel against the observed market path: in scheduled regimes the lagged loadings are positive so the owed catch-up is delivered over the next minute, whereas in bursty regimes the same lagged loadings turn negative (the gap was slammed shut and overshot by aggressive flow) so the forecast flips sign endogenously. The interaction is the edge: A cannot tell whether a backlog will be closed or has already been over-paid, and B has no measure of how much market-driven repricing is actually owed — only a regime-conditional impulse response answers both at once, and the sign flip is estimated from data rather than imposed.
factors.name: Metronome-regime-conditional lagged-beta closure kernel

factors.trading_idea: The parent assumed a peer-relative dislocation relaxes monotonically along a power-law propagator, so its signal was a slowly-decaying *level* whose predictability leaked out to 24+ bars. Finite inventory capacity of liquidity providers means relative-value residuals do not relax monotonically: providers over-correct, so the residual behaves like a damped oscillator with a characteristic ringing period of tens of seconds, and the sign of its change over the next minute depends on the residual's PHASE (level AND recent velocity), not on its level. I therefore estimate, per name, a two-lag autoregression of the peer-relative residual on a lattice whose spacing is exactly half the forecast horizon (3 bars) via trailing Yule-Walker on the lag-3 and lag-6 autocorrelations, and forecast exactly two lattice steps ahead (= 6 bars) with the companion-matrix map, weighting by the model's own trailing R^2. Because the object forecast is the 6-bar *change* of the residual (which mechanically decorrelates inside the horizon) and because oscillatory names get a sign-flipped forecast while overdamped names get plain reversion, the edge is horizon-matched to 6 bars instead of bleeding out to 24. The edge survives arbitrage because harvesting the phase term requires per-name estimation of ringing dynamics plus minute-scale turnover for a few-basis-point payoff, while slower relative-value capital is paid for the level leg.
factors.name: Lattice AR(2) ringing-phase peer-residual forecast

factors.trading_idea: The parent's Kuramoto entrainment term is real but arrives on the wrong clock: phase gaps close as *hedging trades* execute, not as wall-clock seconds pass, which is why its IC kept building out to 24 bars. Three mechanism changes move the delivery into the fixed 6-bar window: (i) the entraining mean field is the *cap-weighted* order parameter, because index/ETF-arb baskets hedge in capitalisation weights, so that is the timing reference individual names are actually pulled toward; (ii) the pull is only credible for names that are demonstrably entrained, measured by the trailing phase-locking value PLV = |E[e^{i(theta-psi)}]| between the name and the mean field — a large detuning name is running free and its phase gap carries no forecast; (iii) the amount of entrainment delivered over the next 6 bars is proportional to elapsed *event time*, so the term is multiplied by a Hawkes-style forecast of near-term trade intensity (fast/slow volume ratio), concentrating the same economics into the fixed horizon. The edge persists because lead-lag arbitrage is estimated in the amplitude/return domain (betas, correlations) and cannot see a correctly-sized but quarter-cycle-late name, and because harvesting it requires simultaneous multi-name phase estimation plus a volume-clock forecast at 10-second granularity. Falsified if the 6-bar IC does not exceed the parent's, if restricting to low-PLV (unlocked) names retains the edge, or if removing the volume-clock multiplier leaves the horizon profile unchanged.
factors.name: Cap-weighted phase-lock entrainment on the volume clock

factors.trading_idea: Parent A's propagator split (fade the flow-explained transient displacement, ride the unexplained permanent repricing) is only economically meaningful when the name's per-bar price-impact regression actually fits — Parent B's active-bar, no-intercept impact R-squared measures exactly that. When R-squared is high, flow genuinely prices the tape: the still-undecayed impact remainder relaxes over the next minute and the flow-orthogonal residual is real reservation-price relocation that keeps propagating; when R-squared is low the same residual is mostly stale-mid / one-sided quote wobble, which the next aggressor trades straight back through, so its sign must FLIP to snapback (this is the direction Parent B realised but mis-declared, and why the naive average of the two mechanisms cancels). Parent B's Hawkes arrival hazard then times only the transient leg: impact relaxes inside the 6-bar window when no further aggression is expected (low hazard → fade hard), whereas a high hazard means the metaorder is still splitting so the transient part is defended and should be faded only weakly. The interaction carries edge neither parent has: A never conditions its residual sign on the identifiability of its own regression, and B never applies its trust/clock state to a properly propagator-decomposed active displacement.
factors.name: Impact-fit-trust gated propagator permanence flip

factors.trading_idea: Parent A knows *how much market-shock catch-up a laggard still owes* over exactly the next 6 bars (distributed-lag loadings folded against the already-observed market path), but is agnostic about whether the book will let that catch-up be paid; Parent B knows *which side of the book hosts a deep, invisible queue* (range-normalised wick asymmetry gated by volume-per-unit-displacement), but has no view on where price needs to go, which is why its standalone sign is near zero. The child aligns them: owed upward catch-up is paid fast when the untested side is the upside (a fresh absorbed probe sits below, floor supported, ceiling permeable) and is blocked when a fresh absorbed probe just capped the upside — so the signed interaction, not either term, sets both the magnitude and the reliability of the 6-bar forecast. The same absorption statistic also replaces Parent A's clunky dividend-clientele staleness proxy with a directly measured microstructural one: high volume per unit displacement plus frequent frozen mids marks exactly the names whose mid lags market information, so the catch-up is largest there.
factors.name: Owed catch-up vs hidden-barrier side alignment

factors.trading_idea: Parent B splits a name's 6-bar industry-demeaned valuation-multiple change into three sources with different permanence (idiosyncratic-flow-backed impact, sector-basket-flow-backed impact, and an unbacked 'quiet' residual) but hard-codes their signs (+idio, -basket, -quiet); Parent A shows the repair of a peer-relative dislocation only happens when the hedge legs — the peer basket — are actually tradable, and that the right way to load such an impulse is a trailing, robust, pooled sign-slope fitted on the horizon-matched forward return. The child fits a separate sign-slope loading b = sum(sign(x)y)/sum|x| for EACH attributed channel INSIDE cells of leave-one-out peer activity, so the question 'does basket pressure fade or persist, and does unbacked quiet repricing snap back?' is answered by the data conditional on hedge-leg liveness rather than assumed. The interaction is the edge: attribution tells you *which* part of the dislocation is repairable in principle, liveness tells you *whether it can be repaired in the next six bars*, and the per-cell robust slope converts that joint state into a calibrated, sign-flexible forecast — Parent A dilutes informed single-name flow into its fade leg, Parent B fades basket and quiet pushes even in states where no peer liquidity exists to complete the arbitrage.
factors.name: Flow-attributed valuation-dislocation channels with liveness-split sign-slope loadings

factors.trading_idea: The parent's insight — that the *shape* of the volume path, not its level, tells you whether a price move is an unfinished sliced parent order (continue) or a one-off aggression (fade) — survived out-of-sample only weakly because its gate was a three-layer construct (CV, then a 120-bar per-name z-score, then tanh) whose per-name normalisation is contaminated by market-wide diurnal volume waves. I replace it with one dimensionless, self-normalising statistic: the Lo-MacKinlay variance ratio of bar volume, Var(sum of k bars)/(k*Var(1 bar)). Clustered (Hawkes-like, burst/news) volume gives VR>1 because arrivals are self-exciting; metronomic scheduler participation gives VR near or below 1 because a fixed slice rate makes aggregated volume dispersion grow only linearly. Because VR is homogeneous of degree zero in volume it needs no level normalisation, and ranking it cross-sectionally at each bar removes the common diurnal clustering component, so the gate measures purely *relative* clustering geometry. The edge persists because the unexecuted residual of a scheduled parent must trade regardless of who is watching (mechanical, not informational), while harvesting the fade leg means standing in front of aggressive, adversely-selected flow — capacity-limited and unrewarding for slow capital.
factors.name: Cross-sectionally ranked volume variance-ratio gate on short drift

factors.trading_idea: Both parents measured *owed* repricing — Parent A the market-beta backlog it estimated from a distributed-lag kernel, Parent B the fresh-minus-stale sqrt-volume-weighted one-sided pressure — and both realized IC signs opposite to their declared direction, which is exactly what you expect if the panel is dominated by names whose mid re-quotes almost every bar: for those names the 'owed' move has already been over-delivered inside the measurement window, so what remains over the next 6 bars is transient-impact relaxation (reversal), not delivery. The child therefore makes the per-name re-quote hazard the *sign-switching* state variable rather than an amplifier: with Poisson deliverable share d = 1 - exp(-lambda*H), fast repricers (high d) over-deliver and mean-revert, while slow repricers (low d) have physically unfinished repricing and continue. It applies that single latency switch to BOTH channels jointly — market-purged fresh-minus-stale sqrt-volume pressure (Parent B) and the un-reflected market backlog beta*M_H - r_H (Parent A, in closed form) — and outputs their pure cross-sectional interaction, so the factor is orthogonal to either main effect. The edge neither parent has: knowing the *direction* of the signal requires the capacity variable, and knowing which names have capacity requires the flow/backlog magnitude — the interaction, not the levels, is what fast market makers do not warehouse.
factors.name: Re-quote capacity flipped pressure & backlog interaction

factors.trading_idea: Parent B measures ONE flow->price response kernel per name and forecasts the next 6 bars as sum_k f_{t-k}[S(k+6)-S(k)]; but that single kernel averages two physically opposite responses, because Parent A's state variable says the same signed flow means different things depending on how the path was assembled — a few large, volume-backed increments (information arrival, permanent impact, response still building) versus many small increments on quiet bars (inventory-driven quote walk, transient impact, response already turning over). The child therefore estimates TWO kernels, indexed by the state prevailing when each unit of flow arrived: the state is the local inverse-participation ratio of increments (m*sum r^4/(sum r^2)^2 vs the Gaussian null 3) combined with movement-weighted relative volume, split at the cross-sectional median. Each kernel is fitted as a POOLED panel regression (cross-sectional sum of rz*f_{t-l} over trailing 300 bars divided by the pooled flow second moment) rather than per name, which kills the per-name estimation noise that made Parent A's in-sample edge collapse, and the horizon-matched cumulative-response difference S_s(k+6)-S_s(k) is then applied to each past flow bar under its own state. The interaction carries edge neither parent has: Parent A knew which drifts were information-bearing but had no calibrated map from state to expected 6-bar return (hence its wrong declared sign), while Parent B had the calibrated map but blended continuation-type and relaxation-type flow into a single, sign-diluted kernel.
factors.name: State-split pooled flow response kernel (traded jump vs quiet grind)

factors.trading_idea: The parent had the right robust statistic (Rice's inversion rho = cos(pi*P(sign flip)) gives a fat-tail-immune lag correlation) but forced it through an AR(1) compounding kernel, which imposes a geometric decay shape on the response; at 10-second frequency the true response of a quote-repricing bar versus a paid-impact bar is NOT geometric — it is hump- or oscillation-shaped (bid-ask bounce at lag 1, transient-impact relaxation over lags 2-8), so an AR(1) fit calibrated to lag 1 mis-scales the 6-bar sum and pushes the realised edge out to 24 bars. The child estimates the whole *term structure* rho_k for k=1..8 directly by Rice-inverting the lag-k sign-flip frequency, conditional on the volume state (zero/low-volume 'quiet' vs traded 'active') of the anchor bar, and builds the exact horizon-matched projection weight W_i = sum_{k=i+1}^{i+6} rho_k for each of the last three bars — a nonparametric cumulative impulse-response over precisely the 6-bar forecast offset, no AR(1) assumption anywhere. Each rho_k is shrunk twice: by disagreement with the uncentered Pearson lag-k correlation (large disagreement = the autocorrelation is carried by a few jumps or stale prints, not a genuine grind) and by pair count (Rice's estimator has std ~ pi*sqrt(p(1-p)/N)). The edge survives arbitrage because the traded object is the price displacement, whereas what is estimated here is the *shape* of the decay curve conditional on liquidity state — a slow, sign-only statistic requiring hundreds of bars to estimate, which competition compresses in amplitude but does not flatten in shape.
factors.name: State-conditioned Rice lag-term-structure impulse kernel

factors.trading_idea: Parent B's realized IC (strongly negative against a declared 'residual persists' hypothesis) is not noise: at 10-second resolution the flow-orthogonal part of a mid-price move — displacement that no trade paid for under the square-root law — is mostly quote flicker, queue-position jitter and one-sided quoting that snaps back, whereas the trade-paid part carries the permanent (informational) share and keeps going while the metaorder is still working. Parent A supplies the missing state variables: WHERE inside the window the move was produced on the volume clock, and WHEN the demand died. The child therefore fades the sqrt-law *unpaid* displacement, amplifying the fade by A's activity-vs-calendar wedge computed on that unpaid channel (unpaid drift concentrated in the window's quietest bars is demand-uncorroborated and reverts hardest; unpaid drift that at least co-occurred with heavy demand is corroborated quote revision and reverts least) and by A's flow-extinction gate (relaxation only lands inside 6 bars once the pressuring flow has stopped), while adding a small continuation tilt on the paid component that is largest while flow is still running. The interaction is the edge: A's wedge alone still mixes paid impact into its carrier, and B's residual alone lumps corroborated and uncorroborated quote revisions together, so only conditioning the sqrt-law residual on the volume-clock timing isolates the purely unbacked drift that reverts.
factors.name: Unpaid-displacement snapback timed by the volume clock

factors.trading_idea: The parent conflated two opposite responses to the same recent market path: genuine distributed-lag catch-up (which shows up in bars 1-3) and transient over-reaction that is handed back later (which is why its IC turns negative by 12-24 bars); at the fixed 6-bar offset the two nearly cancel, hence the weak standalone IC. This child estimates the lag kernel properly — solving the trailing Yule-Walker/Toeplitz system Gamma*b = c so the loadings b_0..b_6 are deconvolved from market autocorrelation instead of being contaminated univariate Dimson betas — and then splits the response into a permanent part (trailing beta of 18-bar cumulative own return on 18-bar cumulative market return) and a fast total part (sum of b_0..b_6). The 6-bar forecast is the horizon-matched owed catch-up folded against the already-observed market path MINUS the give-back implied by the excess of fast total over permanent response, with the give-back leg amplified and the catch-up leg damped by relative traded volume (impact-driven over-reaction happens where volume was heavy; staleness-driven owed catch-up happens where volume was thin), and the whole prediction shrunk by the kernel's explained-variance share so noisy loadings are not traded. The edge persists because deconvolving a 7-lag kernel and separating permanent from transient market response at 10-second scale requires estimation machinery that fast, latency-focused arbitrage capital does not deploy on the slow-repricing tail of the cross-section; it is falsified if the permanent/transient wedge carries no incremental information over the raw owed catch-up, or if the volume interaction does not discriminate the two legs.
factors.name: Toeplitz-solved lag kernel: owed catch-up minus transient give-back

factors.trading_idea: Parent B shows that drift printed in (near-)zero-volume bars (quote repricing) and drift paid for with aggressive volume (transient impact) must be forecast with opposite signs, but it hard-codes those signs as +1/-1 and treats all traded drift alike; Parent A shows that the sign and size of the traded response is not a constant at all — it flips from repayment to propagation depending on whether the flow arrived as one sweep (high volume Herfindahl = burst) or as an even schedule (drip). The child therefore first decomposes the last ~2 minutes of idiosyncratic drift into a disjoint quiet channel and a flow-weighted traded channel (B's mechanism), and then attaches to each channel its OWN state-local, horizon-matched through-origin beta estimated by trailing state-weighted regression of the realized 6-bar return on the same channel push measured exactly 6 bars earlier (A's mechanism): the traded beta is interpolated on the burst/drip volume-concentration state, and the quiet beta is interpolated on a staleness state (the within-name percentile of the quiet-bar share), which is exactly B's own falsification axis — genuine maker repricing in an otherwise active name should continue, while drift printed by a chronically silent, stale mid should not. The interaction carries edge neither parent has: A destroys the quiet channel by volume-weighting it to zero and so can never price silent repricing, while B cannot know that a burst-delivered traded push is repaid and a dripped one propagates, so its fixed-sign traded leg averages two opposite regimes and dilutes itself; because the two channels live on disjoint bars they are near-orthogonal, so separate univariate state-local betas are an unbiased, low-variance way to let the data set both signs and both magnitudes at the traded horizon.
factors.name: Quiet/traded channel split with burst-drip state-local horizon-matched betas (h=6)

factors.trading_idea: The parent's realized sign says the truth is not 'probe rejection' but transient price impact: on a 10-second bar, heavy traded size pushes the mid through finite visible depth and the bar closes far from the range extreme it printed, and that displacement is mostly the temporary cost of immediacy which decays as passive depth replenishes over the next ~minute — so a name that closes LOW inside a heavy-volume range subsequently bounces. The parent diluted this by mixing two economically opposite components: the sector/market-wide part of within-bar displacement is information (index and sector flow) and persists, while the name-specific part is liquidity-provision cost and reverts; purging the group mean and up-weighting names whose returns are dominated by idiosyncratic variance (low market R-squared) isolates the reverting component. The edge persists because capturing it means posting passive size against impatient aggressors into the same thin depth that created the displacement, so capacity is bounded by the very illiquidity that generates it, and the state resets every ten seconds. Falsifiable: if the group-purged and unpurged range-position signals carry the same forward sign, or if reversion strength is unrelated to idiosyncratic variance share, the mechanism is wrong.
factors.name: Idio-purged, participation-weighted range-position snapback

factors.trading_idea: Parent A knows *how much* of a standing peer-relative displacement should unwind inside the next 6 bars (the propagator's front-loaded decay fraction at the excursion's measured age) but is blind to *what built* the displacement; Parent B knows the displacement's microstructural origin (silent maker quote-walking vs traded impact) but has no horizon-matched decay clock. The child decomposes the very same leaky-integrated peer-relative displacement into its traded-bar-origin and silent-bar-origin components, then routes each through the mechanism that actually governs it: only the traded-origin part is transient Bouchaud impact, so it is faded in proportion to the propagator's remaining-within-6-bars fraction g(age) and the name's self-calibrated 6-bar reversion coefficient; the silent-origin part is an inventory search ramp that keeps walking while nobody trades against it, so its *fresh rate* is followed in proportion to the trailing persistence of silence, and its *accumulated level* is faded only in the state where trading has resumed (probability of silence low) and the propagator says the correction is due now. The interaction is the edge: neither parent can tell an old, trade-tested silent ramp (about to be corrected within the minute) from a young traded push (already half-relaxed by the horizon), and the age-weighting is exactly what pulls the peer-displacement information from its 24-bar level payoff down to the fixed 6-bar offset.
factors.name: Origin-attributed propagator age relaxation vs silence ramp

factors.trading_idea: Parent A shows that mid-drift printed in (near-)zero-volume bars is autonomous quote repricing that continues, while drift paid for with aggressive volume is transient impact that reverts; parent B shows that the transient part only unwinds to the extent that counterparty volume actually arrives within the pinned window (clear = expected 6-bar volume / (expected volume + |inventory|)). The child uses that single observable trade-clock variable to ROUTE weight between the two legs instead of averaging them: the reversion leg is the dealer-inventory-implied displacement lam*Q (an impact-elasticity-scaled, exponentially-decayed signed-flow stock) weighted by clear, and the continuation leg is the quiet-bar drift ORTHOGONALISED to that same lam*Q by a trailing per-name OLS, weighted by (1 - clear). The interaction carries edge neither parent has: silent repricing only survives 60 seconds when the trade clock is too slow for anyone to test it (low clear), and traded impact only snaps back when there is enough arriving volume to clear the imbalance (high clear) — and by projecting the quiet drift off the inventory-implied push, the continuation leg is stripped of the stale-impact tail that parent A's raw quiet drift silently contained. All memories (inventory half-life, quiet-drift EW kernel, volume forecast) are matched to the pinned 6-bar offset rather than the 30-bar / 18-bar kernels that pushed both parents' IC out to 24 bars.
factors.name: Clearing-capacity routed quiet repricing vs inventory snapback

factors.trading_idea: The same size of trade-backed price push means two economically opposite things depending on HOW it was delivered: a push delivered in one bar-sized burst is a liquidity event — one aggressor sweeps resting depth, market makers take unwanted inventory and repay the transient push over the following bars — whereas the identical push dripped evenly across several bars is the signature of a patient, informed schedule, whose price impact is permanent and tends to continue. The parent estimated one per-name repayment kernel and averaged these two regimes together, which is exactly why its mass leaked past the 6-bar window and its standalone IC was weak; the child conditions the response on execution *concentration* (a trailing Herfindahl of bar volumes over the push window) and estimates two state-local through-origin betas — burst-state and drip-state — by trailing state-weighted regression of the realized 6-bar close-to-close return on the 6-bar trade-backed push measured at exactly a 6-bar offset, so the forecast is horizon-matched by construction rather than by summing a hand-truncated kernel. Falsifiable claim: beta_burst is systematically more negative (repayment/reversal) than beta_drip (propagation/continuation) for the same names, and interpolating between them on the current concentration state beats the unconditional beta at the fixed 6-bar offset. The edge survives arbitrage because monetising it means posting passive size against possibly-informed aggressive flow for a fraction of a spread — adverse-selection risk-bearing, not a free directional trade — and because the burst/drip discrimination requires per-name, per-state estimation over long trailing windows rather than a single reversal formula.
