factors.name: Burst-vs-drip flow concentration state, horizon-matched repayment beta (h=6)

factors.trading_idea: Transient price impact relaxes in *event (volume) time*, not calendar time: a dislocation decays after a roughly fixed amount of liquidity-demanding flow has arrived to be absorbed. The parent measured its displacement on a fixed 8-bar calendar window and therefore mostly loaded on names whose relaxation clock is slow, which is exactly why its IC kept growing out to 24 bars while the run's forecast offset is 6. The child fixes the clock mismatch on both sides: (i) the displacement is measured over a per-name *volume budget* (a fixed multiple of the name's typical 6-bar traded volume), so every name's dislocation is expressed in the same event-time units, and (ii) the signal is scaled by the expected fraction of that decay budget that will actually arrive in the next 6 calendar bars, estimated from the strongly autocorrelated local trade-arrival intensity, so weight goes only to names whose reversion is due *now*. The edge survives arbitrage because harvesting it means supplying inventory precisely during high-arrival bursts, where adverse selection and per-event dollar profit are worst, and because the volume-clock alignment must be recomputed per name per bar to be exploitable.
factors.name: Volume-budget-matched peer residual snapback, arrival-rate scaled

factors.trading_idea: Parent B builds a genuinely informative object — the Epps-corrected, precision-whitened relative-value dislocation p — but it never asks *why* a name is dislocated, so its forecast averages mechanical over-push with real information and dies at ~0.01 IC. Parent A knows the why (basket/program flow displaces a name in proportion to capitalisation-weight-per-unit-depth, i.e. its inverse-turnover elasticity in excess of beta) but only ever observes the *aggregate* market move, which is a blunt proxy for the actual displacement. The child projects the cross-section of whitened dislocations directly onto Parent A's elasticity-wedge vector each bar: the loading g_t is the realised, per-bar magnitude of weight-proportional mechanical push, and its fitted part g_t·wedge_i is faded with strength proportional to Parent A's basket-footprint state (volume-share deviations tilting toward the cap-weight vector), while the orthogonal residual dislocation is traded only through Parent B's measured laggard role as a catch-up. The interaction is the edge: neither the dislocation alone (it mixes information with liquidity demand) nor the wedge×market-return alone (it assumes the push instead of measuring it) can separate the mechanically-owed component from information, and the state-dependent re-weighting of the two channels is invisible to both parents.
factors.name: Program-footprint attribution of precision-whitened dislocations

factors.trading_idea: In the Merton framework equity is a levered claim on assets, so the elasticity of an equity return to the underlying asset-value shock is roughly the firm's financial leverage: a 30bp equity move in a 5x-levered name implies a ~6bp asset shock, while the same move in an unlevered name implies a full 30bp shock. Over a 60-second window true asset values essentially cannot move that much, so an equity impulse that de-levers into a *large* implied asset shock is prima facie non-fundamental — one-sided liquidity demand — and should snap back, whereas the same equity move in a highly levered name is mechanically consistent with a tiny asset shock and need not revert. The child therefore replaces the parent's slow 120-bar semivariance *level* (which only paid at 24 bars) with a 6-bar signed semivariance *impulse*, de-levered by balance-sheet elasticity, sector-demeaned to keep only the idiosyncratic part, and amplified when the move happened on thin volume (price change per unit of participation abnormally high = liquidity vacuum rather than information). It survives arbitrage because market-makers standardise impulses by realised volatility, not by capital-structure elasticity, so the leverage-conditioned part of the dislocation is left un-hedged; the claim is falsifiable in that dividing by leverage must beat multiplying by it, and the vacuum interaction must have positive sign.
factors.name: De-levered asset-shock reversal, liquidity-vacuum gated

factors.trading_idea: Both parents measure a *quote that has not yet moved*, but they diagnose two physically different sources of staleness: Parent A's trade-anchored gap is staleness created by size actually transferring (market makers skew the mid away from the volume-weighted transaction anchor while managing inventory, and arriving flow drags it back), whereas Parent B's distributed-lag kernel is staleness owed to an *already observed* market path on names that simply are not being repriced. These two states are mutually exclusive at 10-second scale, and the same microstructural variable — trailing volume-activity z-score together with the frozen-mid fraction — tells you which one you are in, so the child uses it as a soft switch: on active names it trades the anchor-minus-mid snapback, on quiet/frozen names it trades the horizon-matched owed beta catch-up (kernel folded exactly onto 6 bars, gated by whether the market actually moved and by mandate-constrained income clientele). The interaction adds a second edge neither parent has: in the overlap region where both legs are defined, sign concordance between the transaction-anchor gap and the owed market catch-up distinguishes true un-updated quotes (amplify) from genuine idiosyncratic repricing where trades pushed price away from the market-implied level (damp), which is precisely the false-positive set that caps Parent A's standalone IC and makes Parent B's stand-alone IC near zero.
factors.name: Activity-switched trade-anchor staleness vs owed market catch-up

factors.trading_idea: Parent A measured HOW liquidity demand arrived (even, scheduler-like volume shares vs. concentrated bursts) but not whether the resulting displacement was actually retained; parent B measured intra-bar retention (permanent body vs. rejected shadow) but not whether the flow behind it was mechanical or informational. The child multiplies the *retained* displacement channel (recency-weighted range-normalised body, the permanent-repricing accumulator parent B deliberately threw away as a nuisance) by a two-part per-name transient-share state: evenness innovation of volume shares (A) plus innovation in the unsigned shadow share, i.e. the fraction of each bar's travel that already decayed inside the bar (B). Both parents' realized ICs contradicted their continuation stories, which is exactly what a propagator world says at a 60-second offset: when a push is delivered by evenly paced slices AND visibly gives back most of its intra-bar travel, the mid sits above the efficient price on transient impact and snaps back as soon as the slice pauses; when volume mass is concentrated in a few bars and the travel is retained in the bodies, the move is genuine repricing and persists. Neither state variable alone can tell mechanical over-push from information — only their interaction with the retained-body channel identifies displacement that is measurably transient AND mechanically sourced, which is the leg that reverts.
factors.name: Sliced-flow / transient-share gated body snapback

factors.trading_idea: Parent B shows that a bar closing low inside a heavy-volume range is mostly transient cost of immediacy and snaps back, and it estimates the transient share statistically (low market R-squared = idiosyncratic, hence liquidity-driven). Parent A shows the same mixing weight has a fundamental determinant: a name whose fair value is pinned by realised, tangible, distributed cash flow has a narrow rational value band, so a within-bar push is far more likely inventory pressure than news. The child uses B's fast, freshness-weighted, sector-purged within-bar displacement as the carrier (short 3-bar decay so the payback lands inside the fixed 6-bar offset, unlike A's 30-bar VWAP anchor whose reversion was too slow) and gates it by the JOINT transience score built from A's point-in-time valuation-anchor composite plus B's idiosyncratic-variance share, then orthogonalises row-by-row against both the ungated displacement reversal AND B's share-gated version. What survives is pure fundamental-transparency conditioning of 10-second impact decay: neither parent has it, because the statistical idio-share gate cannot tell an opaque high-multiple name from a cash-yielding one with the same beta, and the fundamental gate alone has no fast enough carrier at 6 bars.
factors.name: Anchor-tightness dual-purged within-bar snapback

factors.trading_idea: The parent proved that probe excursion (unconverted wick, size-backed) and beta-residual net displacement both carry information, but it imposed the polarity switch with a hand-built conversion ratio, so its predictive mass leaked out to 24 bars — a hand-set state variable is only right on average, and averaging a continuation regime against a reversion regime leaves a slow, low-frequency residual. Here the polarity is made endogenous and horizon-locked: for each name we estimate, from its own trailing record at exactly the 6-bar lead, the correlation between each channel measured at t-6 and the realised 6-bar residual displacement ending at t, and use those (soft-thresholded, empirical-Bayes shrunk toward the cross-sectional pooled value) as the channel loadings. Because the loading is fitted at the same offset at which we trade, the signal is a direct 6-bar forecast rather than a slow proxy, and its sign flips per name as its liquidity-provision regime alternates between inventory absorption (probes precede catch-up) and information (displacement is permanent). The edge survives arbitrage because there is no fixed sign to arbitrage — a trader fading a static polarity is whipsawed whenever the regime rotates, and recovering the regime requires per-name, horizon-matched estimation on 10-second data.
factors.name: Horizon-matched polarity calibration: probe excursion vs residual displacement

factors.trading_idea: Each bar's return splits into a flow-supported (permanent) part and an unsupported (transient, dealer-inventory) part; the split is identified by comparing the bar's move-per-unit-flow to that stock's own trailing elasticity for bars of the SAME sign, and converting the excess into a bounded unsupported share w = d/(1+d) so only genuinely vacuum-driven displacement is faded and volume-confirmed moves contribute nothing. The transient parts do not sit in the price forever: they leak out at a stock-specific resilience rate that is observable causally from the negative lag-1 serial correlation of the stock's idiosyncratic returns, so the outstanding ('unpaid') vacuum displacement is an exponentially-decayed stock of transient increments whose decay constant is matched to that measured resilience rather than a flat box-sum. The parent's flat 6-bar box kept fading displacement that had already been repaid in fast-reverting names and truncated still-outstanding displacement in slow-reverting ones — exactly the symptom of its IC peaking at 24 bars instead of at the 6-bar target; matching the kernel should move mass back onto the target horizon and cut its correlation with existing box-sum reversal factors. The edge survives arbitrage because each repayment is a few basis points, below single-name round-trip cost, and is only harvestable as a diversified cross-sectional overlay, while the cause (intermediaries absorbing uninformed liquidity demand at 10-second scale and unwinding within a minute) recurs mechanically.
factors.name: Unpaid vacuum displacement with resilience-matched decay kernel

factors.trading_idea: After a sharp market-wide move, slow-capital (income/payout clientele) names carry a measurable beta-implied catch-up debt: their realised move falls short of beta x market move. Whether that debt is actually paid inside the next minute depends on the local liquidity state on the *required* side of the book: Brownian-bridge standardised failed excursions reveal which side hosts concealed resting size, so a name that owes an up-move while its upside probes keep being rejected (hidden supply above) will stay stuck, whereas a name owing an up-move whose upside is untested (rejections concentrated below) completes the adjustment fast. The child therefore multiplies the volatility-normalised catch-up wedge by a directional clearance gate built from the signed absorption asymmetry, amplifying wedges that face a clear path and damping wedges that face concealed opposing size. Neither parent has this: A's wedge fires indiscriminately regardless of whether the path is blocked (slow, noisy convergence), and B's absorption asymmetry has no view on where price *should* be, so it only pays off over long horizons; conditioning one on the other concentrates the edge into the fixed 6-bar offset by shortening the wedge and absorption windows.
factors.name: Absorption-Cleared Clientele Beta Catch-Up

factors.trading_idea: The parent proved that the lag-1 cross-covariance of a 10-second panel carries real information, but it used that matrix only as a crude scalar 'lead/lag role' gate multiplying a whitened dislocation — throwing away who leads whom and mixing two estimation errors. Here the same object is used as what it actually is: the coefficient matrix of a regularised vector autoregression, Phi = Cov(z_t, z_{t-1}) Cov(z_{t-1})^{-1}, estimated on 3-bar (30-second) blocks where Epps attenuation is far milder than at one 10-second lag, so the estimated cross-lags are propagation rather than staleness noise. The model-implied expected return over exactly the next two blocks, (Phi + Phi^2) z_t, with the diagonal of Phi zeroed and the output cross-sectionally purged of the name's own 3- and 6-bar move, is a pure peer-to-name information-transmission forecast: it says a laggard should catch up in the direction its measured leaders just moved, and it is by construction not own-name momentum or bounce reversal. The edge persists because it requires a stably regularised, dimension-aware lagged panel regression refit intraday and expresses itself in thin two-sided relative-value legs whose capacity is far below what latency arbitrageurs monetise.
factors.name: Block-VAR cross-lag propagation forecast (own-lag purged)

factors.trading_idea: A name's dislocation from its size-matched sector anchor is a superposition of components with very different characteristic timescales, and at a *fixed* 6-bar (60-second) offset only components whose natural period is on the order of 2h can actually deliver realized reversion — slower components (the ones a 10-minute anchor loads on) drift back too slowly, faster ones have already snapped back. So instead of trading the broadband displacement level with an ad-hoc velocity gate, isolate the band-limited dislocation with a difference-of-EWMA filter (halflives 1.5 and 8 bars), estimate its local angular frequency from the Rice/Vanmarcke ratio sd(Δx)/sd(x), and propagate it forward exactly 6 bars with the narrow-band free-oscillation identity x_{t+h}=x cos(ωh)+(ẋ/ω) sin(ωh); the ranked *predicted 6-bar change* automatically shrinks toward zero for names whose dislocation is too slow to pay inside the window and reaches its maximum (−2x) only where ω̂h≈π. The edge survives arbitrage because harvesting it means supplying inventory against a dislocation whose phase and local frequency are only noisily identifiable in real time, and because the per-event dollar edge is small relative to that inventory risk. Falsified if (i) replacing the two-term quadrature propagation with the level-only predictor −x leaves the 6-bar IC unchanged, or (ii) names in the slow-frequency bucket (ω̂h ≪ π) show the same 6-bar IC as the matched-frequency bucket.
factors.name: Quadrature-propagated band-limited peer dislocation

factors.trading_idea: Quote-driven repricing (mid moves printed in bars where almost nothing trades) is a market maker walking their quotes under inventory / adverse-selection pressure, and such walking has a *ramp lifecycle*: near-constant velocity while the pressure is live, then visible deceleration as the maker finishes adjusting. The parent measured only the accumulated level of that ramp, so its information was spread evenly over minutes (IC grew like sqrt(h)); measuring the ramp's *local state* — endpoint velocity plus curvature from a causal local-polynomial fit of the silence-weighted price path — and extrapolating that quadratic exactly 6 bars ahead front-loads the prediction: live ramps continue over the next minute, decelerating (exhausted) ramps flip and give back the last leg. Trade-paid displacement is treated separately with the opposite sign and with a recency kernel, because transient impact decays fastest immediately after it is paid. The edge survives arbitrage because harvesting it requires crossing the spread on thin, quiet names precisely in the live phase of a ramp, and distinguishing live from exhausted ramps needs bar-level curvature estimation rather than the plain cumulative momentum most fast participants trade.
factors.name: Quiet-Repricing Ramp Curvature Extrapolation

factors.trading_idea: An observed 10-second mid dislocation is a mixture of real repricing and measurement noise (quote wobble, bounce, stale mid), and the *reversal-vs-continuation* sign is entirely a function of that noise share — which is why both parents' unconditional signs came out backwards. This child builds one cross-domain credibility score for the same gap from three near-independent noise proxies: Parent B's size-neutral fundamental anchor precision (high earnings/FCF yield, tangible asset base ⇒ tight, liquid, low-bounce names whose mid gaps are real; opaque intangible-heavy glamour names have wide fair-value bands and noise-dominated mids that snap back), Parent A's active-bar no-intercept price-impact R² (does flow actually explain this name's returns, or is its motion bounce?), and the trade-backing share of the very path that built the gap (how much of the recent |return| was accumulated on no-trade / bottom-decile-volume bars). The gap is loaded long-continuation where the channels agree it is credible and long-reversal where they agree it is noise, scaled by Parent A's Hawkes conditional probability that a trade arrives inside the 6-bar window (only then can either the splitting continuation or the aggressor-driven snapback actually print), and finally orthogonalised to the raw unconditional gap so the factor is pure interaction — an edge neither parent has, since A never sees the fundamental fair-value band and B never checks whether its dislocation was even printed against flow.
factors.name: Gap-credibility flip: transparency- and trade-backing-conditioned dislocation

factors.trading_idea: The parent proved that income-clientele names owe the market a beta-implied response, but it measured the *whole* accumulated backlog, so most of its information landed beyond the fixed 6-bar offset. Here I estimate each name's full distributed-lag (Dimson) response kernel b_1..b_12 of its own 10-second return on the cap-weighted market return, and then form only the kernel mass that is still *undelivered inside the next 6 bars*: pred_t = sum_j m_{t-j} * (b_{j+1}+...+b_{j+6}). Because per-name kernels are noisy at second-level sampling, each b_k is shrunk toward the pooled kernel of the name's payout-clientele tier (dividend yield, payout ratio, FCF yield, negative share growth), which encodes the economic prior that mandate-constrained, slow-re-optimising holders share a common repair speed. The edge persists because it requires jointly estimating a 12-lag response kernel per name and cross-sectionally pooling it by shareholder-clientele tier — a slow, high-variance estimation problem that fast arbitrage capital does not run on the marginal illiquid income name; it is falsified if the horizon-mass convolution has no more 6-bar predictive power than the parent's raw cumulative wedge, or if tier pooling adds nothing over own-name kernels.
factors.name: Clientele-Pooled Dimson Kernel Horizon-Mass Drift

factors.trading_idea: The parent's conversion ratio was the right state variable but it was multiplied by a slow, decay-weighted 10-bar carrier, so its predictive mass leaked out to 24 bars; and it collapsed both sides of the book into one scalar. This child separates the two roles explicitly: (i) the STATE is estimated slowly and per side — over 60 bars I measure, for up and down pressure separately, what fraction of volume-backed probing was converted into net body displacement (c_up, c_dn) versus rejected into wicks, which is a direct proxy for the hidden replenishment asymmetry of that name's book; (ii) the CARRIER is a 3-bar innovation (fresh wick asymmetry and fresh beta-residual displacement, each purged of its own trailing 30-bar mean), so the signal is a surprise whose information is consumed within the next handful of bars rather than a persistent trend statistic. Mechanically, unconverted probing on a side whose book is impermeable (low c on that side) means unfilled aggression remains and the stale mid catches up (continuation), while displacement realised through a side whose book is permeable (high c) is transient impact through thin liquidity and snaps back; both effects live only where real size traded, hence the saturating absorbed-volume gate. The edge survives arbitrage because it needs joint per-side geometry, volume backing and a slowly-updated latent permeability estimate from noisy 10-second OHLCV — it is a liquidity-provision rent for absorbing/replenishing on the impermeable side, not a free directional bet.
factors.name: Side-split book permeability switching a fresh probe/displacement innovation

factors.trading_idea: Parent A splits a name's 6-bar industry-demeaned valuation dislocation into three physically distinct pieces (displacement backed by idiosyncratic aggressive flow, displacement pushed by sector-basket flow, and an unbacked 'quiet' quote-shading residual) but then hard-codes the sign and size of each piece, so it pays a dilution cost whenever the assumed permanence is wrong. Parent B shows that the *loading* on a valuation dislocation is state-dependent and should be measured by a trailing pooled robust sign-slope fitted inside cells of hedge-leg liveness (leave-one-out peer activity), but its regressors are too coarse (only peer-idio vs peer-common move), so each slope mixes permanent and transitory pushes and the estimate is noisy — hence its near-zero standalone IC and its usefulness only as a conditioner. The child feeds Parent A's flow-attributed channels — plus the unhedgeable peer-common channel — as *separate* regressors into Parent B's horizon-symmetric sign-slope estimator, fitted separately when the peer basket is live versus quiet and shrunk to the pooled fit. Because the channels have genuinely different permanence, the pooled estimator finally sees separable signal, and because the loading is measured rather than assumed, the child can follow informed single-name push and fade basket/quiet push with data-calibrated, state-dependent magnitudes and signs at exactly the fixed 6-bar offset.
factors.name: Flow-attributed valuation-dislocation channels with hedge-liveness-calibrated sign slopes

factors.trading_idea: Basket/program executions push each constituent by (its cap weight)/(its depth), i.e. in proportion to an inverse-dollar-turnover elasticity kappa, whereas information moves names by beta. Rather than *assuming* that push equals (kappa - beta) x market move (the parent's degenerate structure: one scalar times an almost-static cross-sectional vector), I *measure* it: in every bar I run a cross-sectional regression of beta-purified, vol-standardised returns on kappa, which yields the realized per-bar impact loading lambda_t and its explanatory purity R^2_t; the mechanical push predicted for name i is p_i = lambda_t * kappa_i. Only the part of a name's realized residual that the elasticity model predicted AND the price actually realized is reversible, so I fade the sign-agreeing overlap sign(p)*min(|p|,|z|) accumulated over an exponentially-decayed window (halflife = horizon) of bars whose volume-allocation shape carries a basket footprint. The edge persists because market-neutral books hedge index exposure with beta, leaving weight/depth heterogeneity of mechanical impact unhedged, and harvesting it requires simultaneous many-name execution inside a one-minute window; it is falsifiable because the confirmed-overlap truncation must beat using either the fitted push alone or the raw residual alone, the R^2 purity gate and program-shape gate must add IC, and sign inversion must lose.
factors.name: Confirmed basket-push projection fade

factors.trading_idea: Decompose a name's recent path into two channels with opposite short-horizon dynamics: (i) intra-bar directional pressure — where the mid finished inside each bar's own excursion, volume-weighted, which measures the direction of the marginal order flow and inherits the strong positive autocorrelation of split meta-orders at the 10-second scale, so it keeps being delivered into price; and (ii) net multi-bar displacement, which once flow direction is controlled for is mostly transient price impact that liquidity providers unwind. A trailing per-name OLS of vol-standardised 6-bar displacement on that pressure estimates the name's own flow-to-price pass-through coefficient, and the residual is the part of the move that its own observable flow does not explain: a positive residual is displacement without flow (unbacked overshoot, reverts), a negative residual is flow that has not yet been delivered into price (queue still being consumed, gets delivered). The edge should persist because harvesting it requires simultaneously taking the reversal side of unbacked displacement and the continuation side of undelivered flow within the same name — a two-channel conditioning that neither plain short-term reversal nor plain order-flow momentum spans, and which carries real 60-second inventory risk.
factors.name: Intra-bar pressure pass-through residual (undelivered flow)

factors.trading_idea: Parent B measures an owed, beta-implied move that a slow-clientele name has not yet delivered, but it cannot tell whether the non-delivery is friction (the move is coming) or genuine idiosyncratic news (it never comes). Parent A's grid-pin state is exactly that discriminator: when a name's mid sits pinned inside half a tick-quantum while volume is still being absorbed at the touch, its price is mechanically dammed behind a resting queue, so the market-implied move is a backlog rather than an opinion. The child therefore takes the beta catch-up wedge and gates it on live pin-friction (fraction of the last 6 bars pinned x absorbed-while-pinned volume) instead of on a static payout proxy alone, keeping the clientele score only as a mild slow-capital prior. The interaction carries edge neither parent has: the *direction* comes from an exogenous market-wide move (so it is not the own-return bid-ask bounce that inverted Parent A's sign), while the *conditioning* comes from the microstructural evidence that the move is undelivered rather than declined — and a final cross-sectional purge of the 1-bar return strips the residual bounce carrier that both parents were partly trading.
factors.name: Pin-Dammed Beta Backlog Catch-Up

factors.trading_idea: Parent A knows *who* moved the mid (idiosyncratic silence => dealer repricing that completes; idiosyncratic busyness => paid impact that reverts) and therefore supplies the sign of the next 60 seconds, but it treats a 0.5-sigma flicker and a balance-sheet-implausible 4-sigma lurch as equally informative. Parent B knows *how implausible* the move is — a given equity impulse de-levered by the Merton elasticity (assets/equity) implies a far larger asset shock for a low-leverage name, and over one minute fundamentals cannot move that far — but it built that magnitude into a slow signed leg whose edge only matures at 24 bars. The child keeps A's fast decay-weighted 6-bar quiet-versus-traded drift legs as the *timing and sign* carrier and uses B's de-levered impulse amplitude (ranked against both the name's own trailing norm and the cross-section) purely as a *conviction multiplier*, applied harder to the traded reversal leg than to the quiet continuation leg. The interaction is the edge: amplitude without attribution does not tell you whether to fade or follow, and attribution without amplitude wastes risk on noise-scale mid moves, so scaling A's fast legs by B's implausibility concentrates the position exactly where a non-fundamental move of known provenance is about to resolve within the 6-bar window.
factors.name: De-levered implausibility-scaled silence-gated quiet/traded drift split

factors.trading_idea: Transient (liquidity-cost) price displacement relaxes roughly exponentially with a name- and state-specific timescale tau, so the fraction of an observed displacement that is actually paid back between now and a FIXED 6-bar horizon is exp(-delta/tau)*(1-exp(-6/tau)): unimodal in tau, near zero both for bid-ask-bounce names (tau<1 bar — the displacement has already decayed before we can measure it at the bar close, and what is left is unharvestable quote noise) and for informational/slow names (tau>>6 — the payback lies beyond the horizon and shows up as 24-bar IC instead). I therefore estimate each name's payback timescale causally as the first moment of its trailing negative return-autocovariance kernel (the empirical relaxation profile of its transient component), and weight the fresh participation-weighted, sector-purged range-position displacement by a log-Gaussian matched filter centred at tau* ~ 3.5 bars plus the measured transient variance share. This should relocate the parent's IC peak from 24 bars onto the fixed 6-bar offset; the edge survives arbitrage because harvesting it requires posting passive size into exactly the thin depth that created the displacement, so capacity is capped by the illiquidity that generates the signal. Falsifiable: if realized 6-bar reversion IC is monotone (not peaked) in the estimated tau, or if the matched-filter weighting leaves the IC-vs-horizon profile unchanged, the relaxation-timescale mechanism is wrong.
factors.name: Relaxation-clock matched transient-impact payback

factors.trading_idea: In bars with no trade the mid can only move because a quote-setter revises, and there are two distinguishable generators: many participants repricing on information, or a single maker mechanically walking its quote in fixed tick steps to unload inventory / avoid a stale quote. The two are separated by the *dispersion* of the untraded increment magnitudes: for a driftless Gaussian random walk the coefficient of variation of |increments| has the exact null value sqrt(pi/2 - 1) ~= 0.7555, while a one-agent ladder produces near-identical steps (CV far below the null) and simultaneously a highly efficient (near-monotone) path. The parent showed that efficient quiet displacement predicts the *opposite* of continuation, which is exactly what this generator implies: a uniform, ladder-like, untraded drift is unvalidated quote skew, not information, so it snaps back once the silence breaks and competing liquidity replenishes at the old level. It persists because harvesting it requires crossing the spread in names that are momentarily quiet and thin against an actively stepping maker, a round trip too costly for slow arbitrageurs; it is falsified if quiet displacement reverts just as strongly when its increment CV sits at or above the Gaussian null.
factors.name: Quiet quote-ladder step-uniformity snapback

factors.trading_idea: A 60-second industry-relative dislocation is only absorbed (and therefore only snaps back) if a liquidity provider can put on the offsetting peer leg *at the same instant*; average peer volume, the parent's gate, is the wrong state variable because peer flow can be plentiful yet arrive in bars where the name itself is untradeable. The sharper conditioning variable is the excess joint-arrival probability — the trailing frequency of bars in which the name trades AND at least half its industry peers trade, minus the product of the two marginal arrival rates — i.e. a co-arrival 'lift' that measures arrival clustering (Hawkes-style cross-excitation) rather than arrival volume. Prediction: the reversal slope on the 6-bar industry-relative return is materially more negative for names in the high co-arrival-lift state and near zero in the low-lift state, and is further damped when the dislocation was itself backed by abnormal own volume (informed, hence permanent). The edge persists because it is a capacity/executability constraint: hedging an idiosyncratic valuation gap consumes both capital and *simultaneous* peer liquidity, so in asynchronous-arrival states no one can arbitrage it away, and the compensation for immediacy in the synchronous states is a fee, not a mispricing.
factors.name: Co-arrival-lift gated peer-relative snapback

factors.trading_idea: Observed 10-second mid-price displacement = a permanent component whose increments are positively autocorrelated (metaorder splitting produces long-memory signed flow) plus a transient component (bid-ask bounce, quote flicker, decaying impact) that dies inside roughly one 60-second block. Because the transient/noise term contaminates the covariance of *adjacent* blocks with a strictly negative bias and leaves lags of two or more blocks untouched, the parent's adjacent-block Rice statistic estimated the noise share, not the persistence coefficient — which is exactly why its declared sign was contradicted. This child therefore estimates block persistence only from lag-2 and lag-3 block sign concordance (rho = cos(pi*p_flip), a jump-robust, tick-size-free estimator), a noise-null identifying restriction, and trades the *cross-sectional deviation* of that persistence times the current standardised displacement. The edge persists because HF desks apply one common reversion/continuation coefficient across the book: the level of persistence is arbitraged, its per-name dispersion requires continuous heavy-tail-robust re-estimation with tiny per-name payoff that only diversifies away in a broad book.
factors.name: Noise-nulled lag-2 Rice persistence dispersion

factors.trading_idea: Parent A splits a name's fresh displacement into idiosyncratic-flow-backed, sector-basket-flow-backed and unbacked 'quiet' parts but *assumes* the permanence of each channel (follow idio, fade basket and quiet); Parent B shows that how much of a trade-driven push a name gives back is directly *measurable* from the seam leg (open minus previous close is pure quote relocation, so corr(body_{t-1}, seam_t) is a per-name walk-back gain) and works best as a conditioning state. The child measures a separate reciprocation gain per attribution channel: it regresses the next bar's peer-neutral seam on each of the three per-bar body components (Kyle-lambda x idiosyncratic flow, Kyle-lambda x basket flow, and the flow-unexplained body grind), giving an empirical, per-name, per-source estimate of how much of that channel's push the liquidity providers walk back within seconds. Forecast reversal is then the gain-weighted sum of the decay-weighted 6-bar channel pushes, with the basket and quiet legs (which are relative-value trades needing peer hedges) scaled by leave-one-out peer liveness and amplified when the transitory push pushed the name away from its industry-demeaned valuation-multiple anchor. The interaction is the edge: channel signs and magnitudes stop being assumptions and become measured per name, so an idiosyncratic push in a name whose seams habitually reciprocate it is faded while a basket push in a name whose seams never give it back is followed — a distinction neither parent can make.
factors.name: Flow-attributed body push with per-channel seam reciprocation gains

factors.trading_idea: The parent showed that a *slow* (120-bar) Rice/Gaussian sign-flip gap forecasts a slow object — its |IC| peaked at 12-24 bars and was empirically the OPPOSITE sign to the order-splitting story, i.e. magnitude-concentrated drift continued while sign-persistent drift reverted. This child keeps the Rice-null DNA but puts every traded quantity on the horizon's own clock: sign persistence is measured as the *live* run length of consecutive same-signed 10s mid increments, scored against the geometric null implied by Rice's formula (continuation probability p = 1 - arccos(rho)/pi, so E[L] = pi/arccos(rho)), and magnitude concentration is measured on exactly the last 6 bars. Mechanism: a long run of small same-signed mid ticks is mostly quote relaxation / a queue walking through stale levels — it exhausts itself and reverts once the walk completes; a single large, volume-confirmed increment is a depth-consuming information event whose impact keeps being propagated by followers and Hawkes-type self-excitation, so it continues over the next minute. Signal = (volume-confirmed concentration excess − run-length surprisal) × recent vol-normalised drift; it is falsified if grind runs continue and volume-backed jumps revert, and it survives arbitrage because the state resets every few bars (capacity-limited, event-clock, not a tradeable slow factor) and desks trade signed flow or raw reversal rather than decomposing sign persistence against a geometric renewal null.
factors.name: Geometric run-surprisal vs volume-confirmed jump split

factors.trading_idea: Parent A splits a 2-minute mid displacement into a flow-explained transient impact level (which relaxes as the book refills, so fade it) and a flow-orthogonal residual (which it always rides as permanent repricing); Parent B shows that untraded one-way mid relocation is often stale-mid / one-sided quote withdrawal that snaps back, especially when the silence is idiosyncratic.  The child reconciles them: it subtracts the exponentially-decayed, tick-rule-signed flow impact level lambda*F from the log-price to build an explicit flow-purged *residual path*, runs Levy's arcsine extreme-timing test (late running max / early running min plus terminal value pinned at the excursion extreme) on that residual path to measure the direction and genuineness of the purely non-flow relocation, and then signs it by relative trade witness — ride the relocation when the name is trading more than its peers (real information the tape saw but did not cause), fade it when the name is abnormally silent (no witness, hence quote withdrawal).  The interaction is the edge: Parent A cannot tell validated repricing from an unwitnessed quote-withdrawal artefact, and Parent B measures relocation on the raw path, so its 'quiet' excursions are still contaminated by not-yet-decayed impact of the few trades that did print; purging impact first makes the arcsine timing test a clean test of quote-side relocation, and the witness variable supplies the sign the pooled statistic otherwise averages away.  The transient leg is retained with its confirmed fade sign so the child keeps A's liquidity-provision premium at the same 6-bar offset.
factors.name: Witness-signed arcsine relocation of the propagator residual path

factors.trading_idea: The parent's forecast factorised into (name-specific lag loading) x (common market path scalar), so cross-sectionally it merely bought high-lag-beta names whenever the market had just moved — it never asked how much of the implied response each name had *already delivered*. Since high estimated lag/total loadings at 10-second frequency belong to the high-vol names that typically over-shoot a common impulse, that construction is close to minus the economically correct object, which is exactly why its realized IC came out negative while the 12-24 bar IC turned positive (the true loading relationship only reasserts itself later). The child measures the signed *deficit*: cumulative realized (vol-normalised) return since the last genuine common shock minus the path implied by the name's own impulse-response kernel, where the kernel theta_0..theta_6 is estimated by trailing local projections of the name's return on lagged market shocks using only the large-|z| shock subsample (the sample where news transmission, not bid-ask bounce, dominates). Both mechanisms that operate at the one-minute scale push the same way — a slow name that has under-delivered still owes catch-up, and an over-delivered name has absorbed transient liquidity-demand impact that decays — so a positive deficit should precede positive 6-bar returns; the edge survives because closing it means supplying liquidity against sub-minute transient impact where spread and impact cap capacity, and because each name's response speed (the kernel shape) must be re-estimated event-conditionally and is non-stationary.
factors.name: Event-anchored kernel-implied response deficit

factors.trading_idea: The square-root impact law (Tóth/Bouchaud/Almgren) says the *transient* part of a price move produced by traded flow is about Y·sigma·sqrt(Q/V_normal) in volatility units; anything beyond that threshold is not paid-for impact but genuine quote revision (information), and the two components have opposite continuations — transient impact relaxes over tens of seconds while quote revision keeps walking. So instead of the parent's 286-operator Rice/quiet-versus-traded gate, the child compares one scale-free number to a theory-implied threshold: the vol-normalised 6-bar idiosyncratic displacement |d| versus sqrt(relative participation), fades the min(|d|,thr) part and follows the (|d|-thr)+ part. This preserves the only robust content of the parent (drift printed on little or no volume continues; drift commensurate with the volume that paid for it reverts) while removing every fitted branch, and the edge should persist because the reverting leg is inventory/adverse-selection rent earned by liquidity providers who must warehouse the same flow, not a free arbitrage. Falsifiable: conditioning on participation must matter — if 6-bar forward returns are negatively related to displacement uniformly across participation buckets (i.e. the (|d|>thr) continuation leg has zero or negative IC), the child is wrong and plain reversal is the whole story.
factors.name: Square-root-law soft-threshold displacement split

factors.trading_idea: Relative-value desks do not hedge a name against its whole industry — they hedge it against its handful of *valuation twins*: same-industry names whose point-in-time multiples (P/B, P/S, EV/EBITDA) and operating characteristics (gross margin, size, asset turnover) are nearly identical, because only those price a genuinely substitutable cash-flow claim. A 10-second-scale dislocation of a name against that fundamentally-defined twin basket is therefore closed by hedge-rebalancing flow, and the *speed* of the closure is a measurable property of that particular spread, so I forecast it with a self-calibrated AR(1) on strictly 6-bar spread increments (E[Δs_{t→t+6}|Δs_{t-6→t}] = ρ̂·Δs), which pins the predictor to the fixed forecast offset instead of relying on a slow EWMA deviation whose signal power lives at 24 bars. Closure additionally requires the hedge leg to be tradable, so the signal is scaled by the twin basket's dollar-liquidity coverage of the name. Falsifiable on three counts: (i) if ρ̂ is uninformative (signal invariant to the sign/size of the trailing lag-6 autocorrelation) the horizon-matching claim dies; (ii) if the twin-kernel basket adds nothing over an industry-median basket the fundamental similarity metric is decorative; (iii) if reversion strength is invariant to basket liquidity coverage the hedge-flow channel is wrong. The edge persists because everyone hedges with the sector/industry basket, so the residual against a fundamentally-matched twin set is exactly the component the crowded hedge leaves unspanned.
factors.name: Valuation-Twin Kernel Spread, Horizon-Matched AR(6) Snapback with Hedgeability Gate

factors.trading_idea: A liquidity provider who has absorbed a run of one-sided marketable flow carries an inventory imbalance and skews quotes to shed it, so part of the current mid is a transitory inventory overshoot rather than information. That overshoot unwinds in *trade time*, not calendar time: it can only be cleared by counterparty volume actually arriving, so the fraction of the dislocation that reverts inside a pinned 60-second window is the ratio of the volume expected in the next six bars to the size of the outstanding imbalance — a saturating, not linear, function of the imbalance. The child therefore converts exponentially-decayed tick-rule signed flow into return units with a trailing per-name impact elasticity (a Kyle-lambda at the inventory horizon), and multiplies by that clearing-capacity fraction, so huge imbalances in a name that has gone quiet get almost no forecast while moderate imbalances in an actively trading name get nearly full reversion. The edge survives arbitrage because harvesting it means standing in front of the inventory the dealer is trying to shed and bearing the adverse-selection risk that the flow was informed; it is falsifiable because if impact were permanent (or reversion were calendar-timed) the clearing interaction would add nothing over the raw signed-flow term and the IC would be zero or positive.
factors.name: Dealer-inventory overshoot with trade-clock clearing capacity

factors.trading_idea: Parent A splits each bar's move into the part the square-root impact law says the flow paid for and an unpaid (quote-revision) remainder but only knows WHEN the transient relaxes; parent B knows nothing about how much of a move was paid for but precisely locates WHERE inside the window displacement was produced relative to liquidity demand (a level-cancelling volume-clock minus calendar-clock wedge). The child applies B's wedge to A's *unpaid* increments only: unpaid displacement produced in the name's busiest bars is immediacy overshoot beyond what the impact law justifies and is given back once demand dies, whereas unpaid displacement produced in quiet bars is genuine limit-order repricing and is retained — a distinction neither parent can make, since A's residual leg mixes both and B's wedge mixes paid impact with unpaid overshoot. A's realized (sign-corrected) evidence supplies the two conditioning legs: the unpaid displacement *level* reverts, and the paid (sqrt-law) component reverts while one-sided flow is still running but continues once the burst has ceased, because by then the transient depth-refill has already relaxed inside the trailing window and only permanent impact remains. The interaction — overshoot attribution (paid vs unpaid) × placement in volume-time × flow-cessation clock — times the give-back inside the 6-bar horizon rather than betting on an unconditional reversal.
factors.name: Paid/unpaid displacement split with activity-clock wedge and cessation timing (jitter)

factors.trading_idea: Parent A showed that at 10-second scale a name's displacement funded by its OWN excess trading relaxes (transient Bouchaud impact of a metaorder slice consuming depth), while displacement that arrived on market-wide synchronous bursts persists (staggered adjustment to common information — the Epps effect means slow names are still catching up), which is exactly why A's declared idio-continuation sign was contradicted. Parent B showed that this only matters when the path was actually CONVERTED into net displacement (high conversion ratio c = paid-for sweep); when c is low the probed excursion was absorbed and the endpoint mid is a stale sample, so the mechanism is continuation toward the probed side instead. The child therefore uses B's conversion ratio as the state variable that switches A's attribution machinery on and off: in high-c (swept) states it goes SHORT the idio-activity-weighted residual displacement and LONG the common-activity-weighted residual displacement; in low-c (absorbed) states it drops the attribution contrast entirely and loads the volume-gated wick-asymmetry continuation, but only for names whose probing was idiosyncratic (a market-wide synchronous probe carries no relative-value information). The interaction is the edge: A diluted its attribution contrast across absorbed states where there is no impact to relax, and B applied a single displacement polarity everywhere because it cannot see who funded the sweep.
factors.name: Conversion-gated activity-attribution polarity switch

factors.trading_idea: Treat the trailing volume-weighted distribution of visited price levels as an empirical occupancy density; its negative log is an effective potential in which the current price sits. Resting liquidity and dealer inventory accumulate at frequently transacted levels, so price is absorbed (pinned) at occupancy nodes and traverses low-occupancy gaps quickly — the deterministic part of the next minute's drift should point down the log-occupancy gradient, i.e. toward the nearest node. The smooth, quadratic (harmonic) part of that potential is nothing but ordinary mean reversion toward the window mean and is already arbitraged, so I extract only the ANHARMONIC component: the difference between the local, horizon-matched-bandwidth centre of occupancy mass and the wide-bandwidth centre of mass, and amplify it where the current price sits in a locally sparse gap (low local relative density → faster escape). It persists because the drift is created by the same resting liquidity that limits how much can be traded against it: extracting it needs per-name intraday density estimation with a bandwidth matched to a 60-second horizon, it is invisible to first-moment reversal/momentum screens, and each episode is worth only a few ticks.
factors.name: Occupancy-potential anharmonic gap pull

factors.trading_idea: Parent B established (against its own stated story) that at a 60-second offset the threshold-exceeding part of mid-price drift CONTINUES while the small-increment diffusive part REVERTS; parent A established that the useful conditioner is not bulk volume but whether the bars that actually moved were the heavy-volume bars, and that residualising against plain drift is what makes the signal orthogonal to the crowded reversal book. The child fuses them: Mancini-threshold split of the last 6 bars against a jump-robust bipower scale (B's measurement), with the continuation/reversion weights driven by A's movement-weighted relative volume rather than B's blunt window participation, then cross-sectionally residualised on the total normalised drift (A's orthogonalisation). The interaction carries edge neither parent has because the two error modes are complementary: B's decomposition is sharp but its gate is contaminated by quiet bars inside the window, while A's flow witness is sharp but multiplies an undecomposed drift in which continuation (jump) and reversion (grind) cancel. Economically, a depth-consuming displacement that was NOT traded through is an unfinished quote cascade — the rest of the book reprices to the new level within the next minute rather than refilling the old one — whereas a small-increment grind that WAS traded through on heavy size is market-maker absorption of a temporary imbalance, and the inventory is unwound, so it snaps back.
factors.name: Flow-witnessed threshold drift split, residualised on drift

factors.trading_idea: A maker repricing quotes with no trades against them is not drifting randomly: it is walking the quote toward a new reservation price, and each name has a characteristic total walk size set by its inventory/tick/spread economics. Consequently the expected displacement over the *next* few bars is the *residual* of that walk, so continuation is hump-shaped in distance already travelled — rising while the walk is only partly consumed and turning into overshoot-reversal once the quiet displacement exceeds the name's own typical completed walk (a bounded-support renewal 'expected residual life' argument). Traded-bar displacement, by contrast, is mostly temporary price impact and should fade monotonically at the same 6-bar offset, so the two legs enter with opposite and functionally different shapes. This survives arbitrage because acting on a quiet, un-witnessed walk means crossing the spread on a name that nobody is currently trading, and because the completion threshold is a slowly drifting per-name quantity rather than a universal constant. Falsified if quiet displacement forecasts forward returns linearly (in which case the saturation/flip term adds nothing over the parent) or if the quiet leg's sign flips at zero rather than near the typical walk size.
factors.name: Quiet Quote-Walk Completion Saturation Split

factors.trading_idea: At 10-second resolution the order-flow process is long-memory (order splitting, Hawkes self-excitation): when a bar's peer-residual mid displacement arrives *with* trade volume, the remaining slices of the same metaorder keep arriving faster than the propagator's transient impact relaxes, so over the next ~60 seconds continuation dominates relaxation — which is exactly why the parent's declared 'traded impact relaxes' sign came out inverted. Displacement that arrives with essentially no prints is instead quote flicker / inventory skew by the market maker, which re-centres once the quote is refreshed, so that channel mean-reverts. Rather than *declaring* either sign, the child makes the sign an estimated parameter: for each name it runs a trailing, horizon-matched (6-bar) OLS beta of realised forward residual return on each channel's decayed accumulation, and shrinks the per-name betas toward the contemporaneous cross-sectional mean beta (empirical-Bayes pooling), then forms the fitted forecast. The edge survives arbitrage because harvesting the traded leg means trading in the direction of possibly-informed persistent flow (you bear adverse selection) while the quiet leg pays for supplying liquidity against transient quote noise (you bear inventory risk); neither is a free option, and the attribution requires joining bar-level trade intensity with peer-residualisation.
factors.name: Shrunk horizon-beta calibration of participation-split displacement

factors.trading_idea: Model the observed 10-second mid as efficient price plus a short-lived component (quote bounce, discreteness, unrelaxed transient impact): p = m + u.  Two things then determine the horizon-matched forecast of the next 6-bar block move, and the parent only used one of them: (i) the efficient block autocorrelation rho = 2^(2H-1)-1, estimated from robust mean-absolute displacements at 24 and 96 bars where the transient component is negligible, and (ii) phi, the share of the 6-bar displacement variance that the downward extrapolation of that same coarse scaling law canNOT explain — i.e. the transient share, which mechanically reverses in expectation over the following block (E[u_{t+1}-u_t]=-u_t).  Combining them gives a parameter-free signed gain g = rho*(1-phi) - phi applied to the current standardised displacement: the parent forecast g = rho only, so its gain was positive for essentially every name and it degenerated into a cross-sectional momentum bet at a 60-second horizon, which is exactly why its realised IC came out negative.  The edge persists because desks apply one common reversion gain to the whole book, whereas the tradable residual is per-name dispersion in transient share, which needs continuous heavy-tail-robust (q=1) two-scale re-estimation and pays only a few bps per name; it is falsifiable because reversal strength must increase monotonically in the measured phi and weaken (even flip) for low-phi, high-rho names.
factors.name: Transient-share signed block gain (coarse-scale efficient extrapolation)

factors.trading_idea: The parent's durable asset was the scale-free, jump-robust sign statistic p_flip — the frequency with which a name's adjacent 6-bar displacements change sign — but it used that statistic *in-sample*, so a name in the middle of a directional run mechanically got a high estimated continuation coefficient and the factor ended up buying long runs; the realized negative IC says those runs are exactly what reverts, which is why the declared direction was contradicted. The child keeps the per-name sign statistic but reverses its role: p_flip, estimated on a window purged of the current run, defines a per-name geometric null for how long same-signed 60-second displacements should persist, and the *surprisal* of the observed contiguous run, (L-1)·(-ln(1-p_flip)), measures how much of the run cannot be explained by the name's own memory. Excess persistence of that kind is produced by an exogenous, finite liquidity demand (a sliced metaorder or a withdrawn liquidity provider), and finite demand terminates: the un-owed part of the displacement is transient impact that relaxes over the next minute, so the child forecasts reversal in proportion to run surprisal times the standardised cumulative run displacement. The edge persists because reversion desks apply one common reversion speed to the whole cross-section, whereas the tradable residual is the per-name *calibration* of what counts as surprising persistence — it requires continuous re-estimation of p_flip per name, pays a few basis points per name, and only becomes economic when diversified across a broad book.
factors.name: Block-run surprisal versus per-name flip baseline

factors.trading_idea: A mid that walks one way while nobody trades carries no trade-validated information: with zero executions there is no new consensus, so a monotone untraded excursion is the signature of one-sided quote withdrawal / inventory shading by the resting maker, not of genuine repricing. The parent measured this excursion correctly (excess path efficiency above the k^(-1/2) random-walk null) but mis-signed it — its IC was negative at every horizon from 1 to 24 bars, a sign-coherent pattern that points to a transitory component rather than noise — so the child fades the efficient quiet drift instead of chasing it, and sharpens *what it conditions on*: (i) only the market-beta *residual* part of the quiet drift is faded, because common-factor moves printed during silence are real information while idiosyncratic maker wobble is not, and (ii) the unproven Hawkes forecast of the next trade is replaced by the *observed* resumption of trading (recent volume vs the name's own norm), since the unbacked level is only tested and repaired once flow actually returns. The edge survives arbitrage because harvesting it means quoting or crossing in names that are momentarily thin and just re-opening, where round-trip cost deters slow capital; it is falsified if the peer-residual restriction destroys rather than sharpens the effect, or if efficiency-filtered quiet displacement shows no more reversal than raw quiet displacement.
factors.name: Peer-Residual Quiet Drift Fade on Trade Resumption

factors.trading_idea: Parent B shows that fading a name's deviation from a slow anchor pays at 6 bars only when the deviation's zero-crossing clock is near the holding horizon; Parent A's Rice sign-concordance estimator failed in level because tick discreteness and quote staleness inflate the adjacent-block flip frequency for every name, so the inverted rho = cos(pi*p_flip) looked mean-reverting across the board and bet reversal on 60-second residual displacements that actually continue (order-splitting flow) — but its cross-sectional *ordering* is exactly the dispersion its own hypothesis pointed at. The child therefore uses B's crossing clock as a state variable that *partitions the cross-section between the two mechanisms*: where the anchor deviation oscillates on a ~6-bar clock the horizon-matched fade is the whole forecast, and where the clock is far from 6 bars (deviation either already-decayed noise or still-outstanding drift, i.e. no 6-bar reversal edge) the weight moves to A's mechanism applied with the common bias removed — the cross-sectionally centred concordance coefficient times the current standardised 6-bar displacement, so relatively high-concordance names are followed and relatively flip-prone names are faded. The interaction is the edge: neither parent knows *when* its own mechanism is the right one at a fixed 6-bar offset, and the clock is precisely the sufficient statistic that says whether a deviation's decay or a displacement's persistence governs the next 60 seconds.
factors.name: Clock-partitioned relative-concordance continuation vs anchor fade

factors.trading_idea: The parent traded the *level* of a peer-relative dislocation, whose mean-reversion half-life is tens of bars — which is exactly why its IC kept growing out to 24 bars and added nothing at the fixed 6-bar offset. The child instead trades the *increment process*: when a relative-value gap is actually being closed, the closing is done by a sliced metaorder (arbitrageur / inventory unwind) executed in the name itself over roughly a minute, so residual-space increments are positively autocorrelated conditional on being convergent, while divergent (news-driven) increments are not. The signal therefore extrapolates the last few bars of convergence — direction −sign(prior gap) — scaled by convergence speed, remaining gap capacity (no extrapolation past the anchor), the share of the closure attributable to the name's own move rather than the peer basket, and elevated (not quiet) traded volume, which is the footprint of the execution. This is front-loaded by construction: the predicted quantity is the continuation of an order-splitting schedule whose natural timescale is seconds, and the edge survives because taking the other side means supplying liquidity to an informed, still-running metaorder with tiny per-event profit relative to the minute-scale inventory risk.
factors.name: Convergence-execution persistence in peer-gap space

factors.trading_idea: Parent A shows that the tradeable relative-value coordinate at a 10-second clock is the *lag-1-corrected* (Epps-de-biased) precision-whitened dislocation, and that the same lag-1 cross-covariance matrix tells you who leads and who lags the panel; Parent B shows that what actually predicts the next few bars is not the size of a dislocation but its *timing* — where the name sits on its oscillation cycle relative to a mean field. The child puts the oscillator in the corrected precision metric instead of raw band-passed price (so the phase is measured on a genuine relative-value spread, not on a staleness artefact) and, crucially, builds the mean field from the *measured leaders only*, weighting names by the antisymmetric row-sums of the lag-1 correlation matrix: the leaders' phase is literally where the laggards' spreads will be a few bars from now, so the entrainment term κ·ρ·(−sinθ)·R_L·sin(ψ_L−θ) closes at the fixed 6-bar offset rather than the 24-bar offset an all-names order parameter produced. The coupling weight κ is itself the measured lead/lag role (strong laggards are entrained and converge, strong leaders have negative effective coupling and extend their move), so the interaction encodes exactly the role split Parent A confirmed while adding the cycle-timing information Parent A is blind to — a laggard whose spread is still widening gets nothing, while one at its turning point behind the leader field gets full size.
factors.name: Leader-field Kuramoto entrainment of Epps-corrected precision dislocations

factors.trading_idea: The parent showed that the *mechanically known* part of a trailing-window estimator's future move forecasts returns, but a moving-average anchor drifts diffusely, which is why its IC kept building out to 24 bars. Breakout/stop traders instead condition on trailing extremes (N-bar Donchian high/low), and an extreme is a *discrete* object: if the running N-bar high was printed inside the block of bars that expires over the next h bars, then the resistance level falls to the second-highest survivor with certainty and no new information, so the conditional probability that a driftless path triggers stop-buy/breakout orders jumps at a known instant; symmetrically an expiring N-bar low lifts the support level and makes stop-sell triggers easier. Converting the known level shift into a barrier-hit-probability change with the reflection principle (2Φ(−d/σ√h)) makes the signal fire only when price is close enough to actually reach the level within exactly the next 6 bars, so the edge should be concentrated at the target horizon rather than smeared across 24 bars. It resists arbitrage because each event is tiny and window-specific, the profit requires guessing which lookbacks the crowd watches, and the counter-trade means standing in front of mechanically arriving trigger flow.
factors.name: Donchian expiry level-shift breakout-trigger drift

factors.trading_idea: Parent B splits a name's 6-bar industry-demeaned valuation dislocation into three sources with different permanence (idiosyncratic-flow-backed, sector-basket-flow-backed, and unbacked 'quiet' quote shading) but hard-codes their signs (+, -, -); Parent A shows the loading on a dislocation must be *measured* by a robust pooled sign-slope inside states where the repair is actually executable, yet fits a single loading to the whole undecomposed move and so dilutes information with pressure. The child fits Parent A's trailing pooled sign-slope estimator separately to each of Parent B's three attributed channels, against the horizon-matched target (cross-sectionally demeaned realised 6-bar return paired with regressors lagged 6 bars), and — this is the interaction — gates each channel with the state variable its own repair mechanism requires: the two flow-backed channels are conditioned on leave-one-out peer-basket activity (hedging the peer legs consumes simultaneous peer liquidity), while the unbacked quiet channel is conditioned on the name's own activity (stale quotes only snap back once the name itself trades and quotes refresh). Neither parent can express this: the permanence of basket pressure versus quote shading flips with *different* liquidity states, so a single gate or a single loading averages away signal that the channel-by-state grid keeps.
factors.name: Flow-attributed dislocation channels with dual-gated sign-slope loadings

factors.trading_idea: The parent showed that unexplained downside-heavy realised semivariance predicts returns, but as a slow 120-bar *level* it only pays off over many minutes. The tradeable, fast expression of the same idea is the *end* of the one-sided burst: a liquidation only reverses once the flow that caused it abates, so I require (i) short-run (12-bar) semivariance asymmetry well in excess of the name's own 240-bar structural asymmetry, (ii) volume in the last 3 bars contracting relative to the burst window, and (iii) price having lifted off the burst extreme (close not at the 12-bar low/high). The new conditioning interaction is that leverage now *dampens* rather than explains the signal: for a Merton-style levered claim a genuine down-move carries real asset-value information and should continue, whereas in low-leverage / low-debt-to-assets names the same one-sided burst is far more likely pure liquidity pressure and snaps back. It survives arbitrage because market makers condition on order-flow imbalance and spread, not on semivariance-asymmetry-versus-own-structural-norm gated by flow exhaustion and balance-sheet leverage; falsification is direct — if reversal strength does not decrease in leverage, or if removing the exhaustion gate leaves the 6-bar IC unchanged, the mechanism is wrong.
factors.name: Semivariance-burst exhaustion snapback, leverage-weighted

factors.trading_idea: The parent assumed that consuming the resting queue at a pinned level reveals information and therefore continues; the harness says the opposite, and monotonically more so with horizon. The mechanism that actually explains a reverting break is limit-order resiliency: at the level where the mid has been resting, quotes replenish faster than they are consumed, so the anchor survives its own break and keeps pulling the mid back until a *new* queue has been paid for. The child therefore measures displacement from a dwell-weighted anchor (the average mid over the bars in which the mid did not leave its level, i.e. the price at which time and resting size accumulated) in tick-quantum units, and scales the expected snapback by the share of window volume that was absorbed while the mid was at rest rather than spent moving it — a large resting-absorption share means the excursion was achieved with little volume and so nothing has been repriced. This is a passive, fraction-of-a-tick effect in grid-bound names where crossing costs a full tick, so it survives arbitrage: capturing it requires simultaneous passive inventory capacity across many names, not a takeable trade.
factors.name: Dwell-anchor refill pull on unbacked excursions

factors.trading_idea: Parent B shows that displacement printed in near-zero-volume bars is quote repricing that continues while volume-paid displacement contains temporary impact that decays, but it cannot separate a genuine unpaid-for revision from a stale mid — which is why its edge only matured 12-24 bars out. Parent A shows the fix is arrival ordering: flow that shows up AFTER the print validates it. The child keeps B's clean quiet/active decomposition but (i) slices the *fresh* displacement (bars t-2 … t-9, i.e. 20-90 seconds old, whose two follower bars are already observed) into witnessed vs unwitnessed quiet legs and still-working vs exhausted traded legs, and (ii) modulates the leg coefficients by a genuinely new slow state variable — the name's trailing empirical *witness rate*, the fraction of its quiet bars that got traded against within two bars, i.e. an inverse stale-quote propensity. The interaction pays at the fixed 6-bar offset because the fast half of the mechanism is loaded hardest: unwitnessed quiet drift in habitually stale names and exhausted traded impact snap back within a minute, while the slow permanent-repricing continuation leg (the part that only accrues by 24 bars) is deliberately down-weighted and only switched on for names whose quotes are habitually validated.
factors.name: Witness-rate weighted fresh repricing snapback

factors.trading_idea: An outstanding beta-implied gap (a name that has not yet delivered its market-shock response) is a *stock*, not a flow: it only converts into realised return once attentive capital actually engages the name, and until then it can sit unresolved for minutes — which is why the parent's undifferentiated wedge only paid off around 12 bars. The observable footprint of engagement is that the gap has already *started* closing: idiosyncratic drift in the last few bars pointing in the owed direction, while the market factor is no longer supplying new gap. Conditioning the remaining backlog on this closure-onset velocity selects the sub-population whose delivery clock has already started, so the residual adjustment lands inside the fixed 6-bar offset instead of dribbling out over 12-24 bars; income-clientele (dividend-yield / payout) names remain the population where slow holders let the gap open in the first place. The edge persists because measuring it requires jointly estimating a per-name beta, decomposing the recent path into a disjoint older-shock gap and a fresh idiosyncratic closure leg, and trading only the engaged slice — an operation with negligible capacity relative to index-level arbitrage and one that is destroyed by the fees a slower, unconditional beta-lag trade would incur.
factors.name: Closure-Onset Gated Beta Backlog Delivery

factors.trading_idea: Bouchaud-style transient impact relaxes along a power-law propagator G(t)=(1+t/t0)^-beta, so the *fraction* of a displacement that unwinds inside a fixed 6-bar window depends almost entirely on the AGE of the excursion, not on its level: a gap that opened 3 bars ago sheds ~45% of its transient component in the next minute, while a gap that has been open 30+ bars sheds only ~10% (its remaining decay is spread over many minutes, which is exactly why the parent's level-based peer displacement had its IC peak at 24 bars rather than at 6). The child therefore scales the negated peer-relative displacement by the propagator's *remaining-decay-within-6-bars* fraction, evaluated at each name's own measured excursion age (bars since the peer-relative residual last sat at its anchor), and by an empirical-Bayes-shrunk, self-calibrated per-name 6-bar reversion coefficient kappa = 1 - beta_OLS(z_t on z_{t-6}), which lets genuinely trending names keep their sign instead of being forcibly faded. The edge persists because harvesting the front-loaded slice requires fast turnover for a small per-event dollar profit while warehousing inventory in a name whose remaining relaxation is only probabilistically identifiable, and because the arbitrageurs who do trade this relative-value gap are compensated on the slow (multi-minute) leg, not the first minute. Falsified if (a) replacing the age weight g(age) by a constant leaves the 6-bar IC unchanged, (b) old-excursion names (top age tercile) revert at 6 bars as strongly as young ones, or (c) the IC term structure still peaks at 24 bars rather than flattening/peaking near 6.
factors.name: Excursion-age front-loaded propagator relaxation of peer displacement

factors.trading_idea: Parent B showed that the bar-endpoint dislocation from the high-low range centre is mostly transient microstructure noise plus decaying impact and pays to fade; Parent A's realised (sign-contradicted) evidence says the opposite about *who* caused the pressure — directional pressure delivered under unusually EVEN volume participation reverts, while pressure delivered when volume mass collapses into one or two bars persists. That is exactly the metaorder-impact result: a scheduler's mechanical footprint is transient and unwinds once the child fills stop, whereas a concentrated aggressive print is information and is repriced permanently. The child therefore uses the trailing self-rank of volume-share evenness (Parent A's state variable, made non-parametric and bounded) as a *switch* on Parent B's endpoint dislocation: fade the dislocation hard when the last five minutes of volume arrived evenly, and flip to continuation only when evenness just fell into the bottom quartile of its own recent history. The interaction carries edge neither parent has: A conditioned the state on a 5-minute path-efficiency momentum signal that turned out 94% collinear with the book, and B faded blindly without knowing whether the dislocation came from an algorithmic schedule (transient) or an informed burst (permanent).
factors.name: Participation-evenness switched endpoint dislocation

factors.trading_idea: Replace the parent's fixed 6-lag linear fold with an explicit Amihud–Mendelson partial-adjustment state: each name carries a latent value anchor that moves with its long-run market loading, and the leaky accumulation of (loading x market return - realised return) is the outstanding gap between that anchor and the traded mid. The bar-level closure speed kappa_i is not assumed but *measured* by trailing OLS of the name's non-systematic return on its own lagged gap, using only bars in which the mid actually repriced, so kappa is a per-*event* speed; multiplying by the name's trailing repricing frequency converts it into the expected number of closure events inside the fixed 6-bar window, giving a delivered fraction 1-(1-kappa)^(6a) that is horizon-matched by construction and mechanically caps the mass that leaks past 6 bars (the parent's sign flip at 12-24 bars). Two sharper conditioners replace the parent's crude staleness/clientele gate: an empirical-Bayes trust weight from the t-statistic of the measured kappa (names whose closure is not statistically identified are shrunk toward the pooled speed) and the path-efficiency of the gap's own innovations (a gap built by coherent, one-directional lag is real catch-up; a gap built by churning innovations is quote bounce). The edge persists because exploiting it requires jointly estimating a name-specific event clock and the market path at 10-second resolution in exactly the names that reprice infrequently, where crossing the spread costs more than the gap for most participants; it is falsified if replacing kappa_i with its cross-sectional mean, or removing the coherence gate, leaves the IC unchanged.
factors.name: Partial-adjustment gap closed on the name's own repricing clock

factors.trading_idea: The parent's grind-vs-jump idea has the right sign but the wrong estimator: the Rice flip-frequency null assumes a Gaussian copula for adjacent increments, which is badly misspecified for 10-second mid returns (fat tails, heteroskedasticity, ties), so its gate injected noise and the 245-operator construction cost marginal IC. Record statistics give the same grind/jump distinction from a *universal, distribution-free* null: by the Sparre-Andersen theorem the probability that a random walk sets a new running extreme after m steps is C(2m,m)/4^m regardless of the increment distribution, so the count of new m-bar highs minus new m-bar lows over a trailing window is a magnitude-blind, jump-immune estimator of true directional persistence. The child takes the wedge between this ordinal drift and the ordinary magnitude-scaled drift over the same window: a metaorder being sliced walks the price through many sequential new extremes with modest total displacement (ordinal >> magnitude, and order-splitting autocorrelation says the parent order keeps working), while a single print into thin depth produces a large displacement with almost no records (magnitude >> ordinal, and Bouchaud-style transient impact decays). The edge survives arbitrage because it is mechanically generated by execution of large parent orders whose remaining size cannot be traded away without paying the same impact, and because magnitude-based momentum/reversal signals — what almost everyone runs — are by construction blind to the ordinal path shape that separates the two cases.
factors.name: Sparre-Andersen Record-Excess vs Magnitude-Drift Wedge

factors.trading_idea: Treat the panel as a weighted graph whose edges are the *excess* short-horizon return correlation (pairwise correlation minus the median off-diagonal correlation, i.e. the market mode removed), and treat belief revision across correlated names as a discrete diffusion on that graph: over the next few bars each name's standardized deviation relaxes toward the average deviation of its graph neighbourhood, so the causal one-step heat-kernel expansion -tau*L*x + (tau^2/2)*L^2*x (L = random-walk Laplacian, x = own-vol-standardized 6-bar return) is a market-neutral forecast that is simultaneously a lone-mover snapback and a laggard catch-up. The genuinely new ingredient is that the local diffusivity tau is not constant but set by the *geometry* of the neighbourhood: by the curvature-robustness relation (Ollivier/Forman-Ricci curvature, here measured as weighted triangle flux (W^3)_ii/(deg_i^2-(W^2)_ii)), positively curved nodes sit in redundant, mutually-confirming clusters where perturbations dissipate fast, while flat/negatively curved bridging nodes relax slowly, so the same raw deviation should mean-revert far more over 60 seconds for high-curvature names.
