It has not been arbitraged because the state variable is a whole-panel geometric quantity, not a pairwise beta: standard beta-hedged reversal signals span the first-order Laplacian term but not the curvature-dependent gain, and the payoff is compensation for bearing genuine idiosyncratic-news risk at a 60-second horizon, which is capacity-limited rather than free.
factors.name: Curvature-gated graph heat-diffusion catch-up

factors.trading_idea: On a penny-grid book the mid sits on a half-tick lattice, so the *granularity* of a mid increment identifies who moved: a net move of one lattice unit (which necessarily flips the parity of mid/half-tick, i.e. flips the parity of the spread) can only come from ONE side of the quote relocating, whereas even-parity / multi-unit moves are symmetric relocations or trade-driven impact. A single-sided step is an unfinished repricing — the maker has revised its reservation price and the opposite quote has not yet followed — so it is confirmed over the next few tens of seconds; in particular a step that widens the spread (tight->wide, i.e. a quote pull) is liquidity withdrawal / adverse selection and continues, while a step that narrows it (wide->tight, someone posting inside) is mechanical mid displacement from liquidity *supply* and fades. Multi-unit moves are consensus relocations and impact overshoots and revert. The edge survives arbitrage because it lives in the discreteness of the quote lattice: any pipeline that works in percentage returns, VWAP bars or smoothed prices destroys the parity/granularity information, and harvesting it requires crossing a spread that is comparable to the predicted drift, so only lattice-aware very-short-horizon books can see it.
factors.name: One-sided tick-step parity quote drift split

factors.trading_idea: The parent showed that downside-heavy realised variance in excess of what capital structure justifies mean-reverts, but it measured a 120-bar *stock* of asymmetry, so its information arrived slowly and the IC kept growing out to 24 bars. The structural (Merton/Christie) component of semivariance asymmetry is by construction slow-moving, so the *fast* component is the 12-bar innovation of asymmetry relative to the name's own long-run asymmetry and relative to peers with the same leverage and size — that innovation is dated to the last two minutes and must therefore pay off within the next minute, if at all. Whether such a one-sided variance burst is a dislocation or news is determined by how much volume was needed to produce it: when short-run variance rises far more than short-run participation (a thin-book vacuum, high variance-per-unit-volume versus the name's own norm), the displacement is mechanical inventory/impact and snaps back; when it comes with commensurate volume it is informed and does not. The edge survives because HFT liquidity providers gate on spread and depth, not on a balance-sheet-conditioned semivariance decomposition scaled by participation, so the fee-insensitive liquidator is still the counterparty.
factors.name: Vacuum-gated downside semivariance innovation

factors.trading_idea: Treat each name's trailing return distribution as a point on the Gaussian statistical manifold and measure how far it has moved from its own 15-minute reference distribution, decomposing that motion into the two orthogonal Fisher channels: a mean channel (drift displacement in noise units, i.e. a t-statistic) and a scale channel (log-scale innovation in its own estimator z-units). The claim is that the *same* recent drift has opposite forward dynamics depending on which channel accompanied it: drift delivered while the name's idiosyncratic scale is expanding relative to the cross-section is a drift-burst / liquidity-withdrawal event — market makers priced the move under elevated variance and it overshoots, so it retraces within roughly a minute — whereas drift delivered while scale contracts is uncertainty resolution or a patiently sliced metaorder walking the price with *falling* noise, which persists. The edge survives arbitrage because it is a pure first-moment × second-moment interaction with zero unconditional exposure to either momentum or volatility (the gate flips sign across the panel), so linear factor models and conventional short-term-reversal books do not span it, and its strongest leg lives exactly in the names whose spreads are widest at that instant, which caps capacity. Falsified if the scale-channel gate is uninformative (IC of the interaction ≈ 0 while the plain drift t-statistic keeps its own IC), or if vol expansion instead marks genuine news arrival, in which case the interaction's sign reverses.
factors.name: Fisher–Rao scale-channel gated drift displacement

factors.trading_idea: A name's distributed-lag response to market information should depend on whether the name was *being traded when the news arrived*: market moves that land while the name is silent hit a stale, unattended quote and are absorbed slowly over the following bars, whereas moves that land while the name is actively trading are absorbed (or over-absorbed) immediately by the aggressive flow already in the book. So instead of splitting the loadings by the future response channel (which must be forecast, as the parent did with trailing channel probabilities and then trusted with an imposed Rice grind/jump sign rule), the child splits the *regressor*: market return at each lag is decomposed into the part that arrived during this name's quiet bars and the part that arrived during its active bars, giving two disjoint, fully observed regressor streams whose loadings are estimated on the full sample (no masked, small-n regressions) and whose signs are learned rather than assumed — an over-absorbed trade-arrival channel simply produces negative loadings and fades itself. Each leg is then traded only in proportion to a verified trust weight: the trailing correlation between that leg's own fitted one-step response and realised returns, so names whose channel-split lag model does not actually explain their returns are switched off. The edge persists because exploiting it requires per-name, per-arrival-channel impulse-response estimation on 10-second bars plus real-time knowledge of which names were silent when the market moved; the residual staleness is the compensation paid to whoever refreshes an unattended quote.
factors.name: Arrival-Channel-Attributed Lag-Kernel Catch-Up (fit-verified)

factors.trading_idea: The parent's realized sign says the opposite of its story: heavy-volume upside excursions beyond the bar's endpoints precede HIGHER returns, so the intra-bar shadow is not a rejected probe into hidden supply but the transient-impact footprint of an impatient trader's metaorder slice — depth refills inside the ten seconds (price returns to the endpoint), yet the child-order arrival process is self-exciting, so further same-side aggression arrives over the next minute and re-pushes the mid. I therefore replace the binary volume gate with a square-root-impact mark sqrt(volume/ADV) on each side's excursion and accumulate the two sides as exponentially decayed (halflife 3 bars) marked-Hawkes intensities, scoring the shrunk, scale-free intensity imbalance. Because a plain 'close low in its range' statistic (endpoint / microstructure-noise reversion) would produce the same sign and is already spanned by the book, the imbalance is cross-sectionally purged of trailing range position and past 6-bar return, so only the slicing-persistence channel survives. Falsifiable: the purged imbalance should keep a positive sign at 6 bars and should weaken monotonically as the volume mark shrinks (quiet-bar excursions should carry no sign, or reverse); the edge persists because harvesting it means racing the same metaorder's next slice by paying spread on a state that refreshes every ten seconds.
factors.name: Volume-marked excursion intensity, endpoint-purged

factors.trading_idea: Bouchaud-style transient price impact relaxes in *trade time*, not clock time: the propagator decays with the volume that has traded since the impact was created, so a peer-relative dislocation only unwinds as fresh flow arrives to absorb it. The parent measured displacement against a fixed 60-bar clock-time anchor and then selected names whose flow had *stopped* — precisely the names whose relaxation clock is ticking slowest — which is why its IC kept growing out to 24 bars instead of landing at 6. The child rebuilds the anchor as an exponential filter in cumulative-volume time (decay per bar = bar volume / a characteristic volume scale, plus a tiny clock leak) so the displacement it measures is by construction a short-lived, event-time object, and then gates *long* on high incoming flow intensity (volume clustering makes recent flow a strong predictor of the next 60 seconds of flow), i.e. names whose relaxation will complete inside the fixed 6-bar horizon. The edge survives arbitrage because taking the other side means warehousing inventory in a name during its heaviest flow, when the split between transient impact and permanent information is least identifiable in real time. Falsified if replacing the volume-time anchor with a clock-time EWMA of equal average half-life leaves 6-bar IC unchanged, or if flipping the flow-intensity gate to the parent's quiet-name (negative-slope) version does not shift the IC peak back out toward 24 bars.
factors.name: Volume-clock propagator relaxation of peer displacement

factors.trading_idea: The parent showed that mid-drift printed in (near-)zero-volume bars continues while drift paid for with volume reverts, but its IC kept rising out to 24 bars — a sign that its exposure is dominated by the slow, *concordant* state where quote-setters and takers push the same way (genuine information, priced over minutes). The fast-resolving state is the *discordant* one: quotes are being walked one way during silence while aggressive flow pushes the other way, i.e. a maker-inventory / taker-liquidity tug-of-war that must be settled at the next few liquidity events, so its resolution lands inside ~60 seconds. The child therefore keeps the quiet-continuation / traded-reversal wedge but multiplies it by a smooth disagreement gate (near 1 when the two channels contradict, near 0 when they agree) and deflates the traded leg by sqrt(volume) so that displacement in excess of the square-root impact law — the part that is transient — carries the reversal. The edge survives arbitrage because capturing it means paying spread in exactly the thin, quiet names where the state arises, and the state itself dies within tens of seconds.
factors.name: Maker–Taker Disagreement Gated Quiet/Traded Wedge

factors.trading_idea: Treat each name's 10-second tape as a 4-state Markov chain on the lattice (sign of the bar return) x (activity above/below its own trailing median volume). If the chain were time-reversible, Kolmogorov's criterion holds and the net circulation around the 2x2 cycle is zero; a non-zero circulation (an entropy-producing cycle flux, computable as an antisymmetric lag-1 cross-covariance of the two binary channels, i.e. a discrete Levy area on the sign lattice) identifies WHICH participant is marginal: counter-clockwise flux means directional legs die at activity peaks (market-maker inventory pressure terminates aggressive flow, so fade when busy / drift when quiet), clockwise flux means direction flips during the quiet pauses of a working program and extends when the scheduler accelerates (so continue when busy). Because the marginal-participant regime persists for many minutes while the cycle itself has a period of only a few bars, the trailing flux tells you the sign of the NEXT quarter-turn given the current quadrant, giving the forecast -flux x direction-state x activity-state. It survives arbitrage because the statistic is second-order and time-asymmetric — it is identically zero for any process in which volume and direction are merely contemporaneously coupled, so it is invisible to linear volume/volatility/momentum screens — and because its economic content (who is the marginal trader right now) is regenerated by every new program rather than destroyed by trading it.
factors.name: Direction-activity cycle flux (detailed-balance) phase forecast

factors.trading_idea: The parent kept a real microstructural object — mid displacement split into quiet-bar quote repricing and impact-deflated taker push — but estimated each channel's forward polarity by regressing completed 6-bar returns on the same predictors lagged 6 bars, an overlapping-window covariance with forward returns whose sampling error dwarfs the true coefficient (and which carries the classic overlapping-regression / Stambaugh downward bias), so the fitted weight was essentially sign-random and the realized IC came out with the wrong sign. But for a stationary series that same population quantity IS the Lo-MacKinlay variance ratio minus one, B = VR_k - 1 = 2*sum_{j<k}(1-j/k)rho_j: it can be estimated from the channel's OWN trailing autocovariances, i.e. from second moments of in-window increments, which uses roughly k times more effective observations, needs no forward data, and is unbiased in sign. The child therefore keeps the two-channel decomposition and replaces the noisy forward regression with per-channel triangle-weighted autocovariance sums, then shrinks each name's coefficient toward the cross-sectional pooled value by a Spearman split-half reliability factor so that only genuinely dispersed polarity is traded. The edge persists because arbitrageurs either hard-code one polarity per channel (fading every push, following every quote) or try to learn it from forward-return regressions that are hopeless at this signal-to-noise, while liquidity-supply regimes that flip the sign of quote-led versus trade-led persistence are refreshed exogenously.
factors.name: Channel variance-ratio polarity (split-half shrunk)

factors.trading_idea: Transitory pricing error in a 10-second mid is not one object: part of it is a market-wide inventory/liquidity displacement shared across names, and part is name-specific. A dealer can lay off an idiosyncratic inventory shock against the pool within seconds, so the idiosyncratic error is repaid inside a 60-second window; a *common* displacement requires the whole basket to be absorbed (and is partly slow information), so it amortises over many minutes — which is exactly why the parent's undifferentiated error signal kept strengthening out to 24 bars while only a sliver was collectible at the pinned 6-bar offset. The child therefore (i) extracts the current pricing error with a per-name steady-state Kalman local-level filter whose gain is set by a two-scale noise-to-signal estimate, (ii) projects out the loading on the contemporaneous cross-sectional transitory-error factor, and (iii) weights the surviving idiosyncratic error by the fraction analytically repaid in 6 bars, using a decay rate identified from the *ratio* of the name's second to first return autocovariance. The edge persists because collecting it means warehousing precisely the inventory a liquidity provider is shedding, and because the ranking needs each name's noise share, its own error-decay rate, and its loading on the common noise factor — three objects a pooled short-term reversal signal conflates into one.
factors.name: Commonality-purged Kalman pricing error with own-decay repayment

factors.trading_idea: A quoted price move is only permanent once trades have paid for it, so the *efficient* price is best estimated by an average of past mids weighted by the flow that occurred at them: I build an EWMA of the mid whose smoothing coefficient is a_t = 1 - exp(-dollar_volume_t / Q_t), i.e. an anchor that forgets in VOLUME time and freezes completely through bars with no trading. The log gap between the current mid and this flow-validated anchor is therefore a pricing error accumulated by quote repricing that flow never confirmed, and dealer inventory rebalancing pulls it back within roughly a minute; the parent expressed the same idea as a sum of per-bar elasticity excesses, which decayed slowly and was 53% correlated with the book, whereas the level (state) form both matches the reversion clock and can be purged of plain reversal. To keep only the flow-conditioning and not the over-mined reversal level, I take the trailing OLS residual of the volume-time gap on the clock-time EWMA gap (same nominal half-life) and neutralise it within sector, since a *common* unvalidated drift is index-level information arriving through the quote (futures-to-cash lead-lag) and should not be faded, while a name-specific unvalidated drift is inventory/stale-quote noise. Falsifiable: the residual (flow-conditional) part of the gap must forecast reversal at 6 bars while the clock-time gap alone, and gaps built up on heavy volume, must not; the edge persists because each snapback is a few basis points, below single-name round-trip cost, and is only harvestable as a diversified sector-neutral overlay.
factors.name: Volume-time validated anchor gap reversal

factors.trading_idea: The parent measured *time*-at-price (local-time recurrence) and assumed pinned levels restore price; the realized IC says the opposite, and the reason is that time-at-price says nothing about how much liquidity a move had to *pay for*. Replace it with *volume*-at-price measured strictly before the move began: if the last 6 bars traversed a price band where an unusually large share of the prior window's volume had been executed, the mover had to consume a thick shelf of resting inventory — only size with information (or a genuine inventory need) pays that cost, so the impact is permanent and the move continues; if instead the move crossed a volume desert, it was cheap, quote-driven and mechanical, so it snaps back as liquidity replenishes. The signal is the pure interaction (standardized move x centred transit-density gate), weighted toward episodes where price is still sitting at the unretraced extreme of the traversal, which is what makes the resolution fast enough to land inside the fixed 6-bar offset. The edge survives arbitrage because it requires a per-name nonparametric volume-at-price profile updated every 10 seconds and pays only a tick or two per episode, while its cause — where previously executed liquidity actually sits — is a structural property of order books rather than a mispricing.
factors.name: Traversed volume-shelf gated move permanence

factors.trading_idea: When a sector is swept by basket/index-style aggressive flow, an intermediary is working a multi-name hedge: the pressure it imparts to each name is proportional to that name's loading on the sector's ex-self signed flow, and the *phase* of the sweep decides whether that pressure keeps building or unwinds. While the sector's aggressive-flow intensity is still accelerating (Hawkes-style self-excitation of the sweep), the hedger has more to do, so the loading-weighted push continues over the next few bars; once intensity decays past its peak the hedger is done and the differential push on the over-loaded names is pure inventory that reverts as market makers reprice. The child therefore replaces the parent's stale quarterly-valuation anchor (per-share fundamentals are constant over six 10-second bars, so the parent's 'multiple dislocation' collapsed into an already-spanned industry-demeaned return) with a single falsifiable interaction: sector-demeaned basket-attributed displacement times the sign of the sweep-intensity derivative. The edge persists because it needs real-time cross-sectional flow attribution plus a live estimate of each name's basket-impact loading, and harvesting the fade leg means warehousing inventory exactly when a hedger is unwinding — a risk-bearing service, not a free arbitrage.
factors.name: Sector sweep-phase gated basket-loading displacement wedge

factors.trading_idea: The parent's IC came out with the opposite sign to the propagator story, and at a 60-second horizon that is exactly what microstructure predicts: order-splitting and self-excited flow clustering last minutes, so a bar whose peer-residual mid displacement arrives together with abnormal trade volume is the visible slice of a still-running metaorder — more same-side flow keeps arriving and the price continues; relaxation only begins after the parent order is finished, i.e. after the arrival intensity falls back to baseline. Mid displacement that arrives with little or no print is the opposite object: an unvalidated quote skew (inventory/latency-driven repricing that no execution confirms), and it is pulled back on the next quote refresh — the more of the recent window was a trade drought, the larger that flicker share. The child therefore keeps the fundamentally-defined valuation-tier peer map (which stripped common moves and gave the parent its independence) but replaces the fixed propagator kernel with a state switch: the Hawkes-style intensity ratio (fast/slow EWM volume) signs the traded leg (+ while the cluster is live, − once intensity has decayed below baseline and impact really does relax), while the quiet leg is always faded, scaled by trade-drought staleness. The edge persists because harvesting it means standing on the same side as possibly-informed live flow at 10-second latency inside fundamentally-comparable peer cells — a joint microstructure/fundamental-map problem neither desk owns; it is falsified if the traded leg's forward coefficient does not flip sign across the intensity-vs-baseline threshold, or if the quiet leg's reversal is unrelated to trade-drought share.
factors.name: Hawkes-liveness switched traded continuation vs quiet-quote flicker reversal

factors.trading_idea: A 2-minute mid-price displacement has two economically distinct origins: the transient price impact of liquidity-taking flow (Bouchaud's propagator — the book is walked, then refills, so this component mechanically decays over the next minute), and repricing that happened without trades absorbing it (quote revisions driven by correlated-asset / market-maker information, which has no impact to relax and is therefore permanent, and is still being propagated by slower quoters). The parent's OOS evidence pointed exactly this way — volume-backed concentrated moves reverted while quiet grinds persisted — so I model the split directly instead of via kurtosis: I project the m-bar move onto an exponentially-weighted (tau≈6 bars, matched to the 6-bar horizon) tick-rule-signed relative-volume flow kernel, calling the fitted part transient (fade it) and the orthogonal part permanent (ride it). The edge persists because monetising it means providing liquidity against the very flow that just moved the price at a one-minute horizon, and because the signal conditions on the *origin* of a move rather than its level, so it is nearly orthogonal to the crowded momentum/reversal factors desks actually trade.
factors.name: Propagator split: transient traded impact vs permanent quiet repricing

factors.trading_idea: Quiet-bar (unwitnessed) mid drift is quote-setters shading toward a new belief and it keeps walking only while the silence lasts; traded-bar drift contains transient impact that is given back once the aggressor stops. The predictive content over the *next 60 seconds* therefore depends on what the next 60 seconds will be made of: I estimate each name's two-state (quiet/traded) Markov transition matrix from trailing bar-activity counts, propagate it analytically 6 steps from the current state, and weight the per-quiet-bar drift by the expected number of quiet bars in the forecast window and the per-traded-bar drift (with negative sign) by the expected number of traded bars. This converts the parent's undated 5-minute drift difference into an explicit horizon-6 conditional-mean forecast, and predicts a new interaction: silent drift should only continue in names whose silence is self-persistent, and should be unwound in names whose trade-arrival clock is about to fire. The edge survives arbitrage because harvesting it means crossing the spread in exactly those names that are quiet/thin during that minute, so the gross move is small relative to immediate execution cost for anyone who cannot post passively.
factors.name: Markov regime-composition weighted quiet/traded drift forecast

factors.trading_idea: Bouchaud-style transient impact says the part of a price move that was *paid for* by trade decays over the following tens of seconds, while a move that appeared on little or no trade is a belief/quote revision with no inventory to unwind and therefore no mechanical payback. I isolate exactly that paid-for part by contrasting two weighted averages of the same trailing 6 bars of beta-hedged, sector-demeaned, vol-normalised returns: one weighted by each bar's share of window volume (flow clock) and one weighted only by the propagator decay kernel (calendar clock). Their difference is, by construction, orthogonal to the plain kernel-weighted 6-bar reversal signal that the existing book already spans — it is nonzero only when the displacement is *concentrated* in the volume-heavy bars — so it carries the transient-impact component rather than generic short-term reversal, and I fade it, amplified by how much volume actually traded in the window. Falsifiable: the negative-wedge signal should predict positively over the next 6 bars, its power should rise monotonically with window volume, and it should vanish (by construction) for names with flat volume shares or no trade; the edge survives arbitrage because the profitable leg is inventory-bearing liquidity supply against a fresh sweep, a compensated risk rather than a free mispricing.
factors.name: Flow-clock vs calendar-clock displacement wedge

factors.trading_idea: Parent A shows that a short path splits into probed-but-unconverted excursion (which precedes continuation toward the probed side) and net residual displacement (which snaps back), with the conversion ratio c as the mixing state. Parent B's *contradicted* sign is the missing piece: evenly-spread participation does not mark an unfinished metaorder at 10-second resolution — it marks unbacked quote drift, and its displacement is the part that reverts, whereas displacement delivered by volume concentrated in one or two bars is a genuine depth-consuming sweep whose repricing is permanent and continues. The child therefore keeps A's conversion switch for *how much weight* the displacement channel gets, but lets B's participation-concentration state decide the *sign* of that channel (a Herfindahl-based concentration innovation shifted by a fade prior), so the same converted displacement is faded when it arrived evenly and extrapolated when it arrived in a burst. Neither parent can express this: A hard-codes one polarity on displacement and averages the two regimes together, while B applies its evenness gate to every path, including round-trips whose excursion was never converted, diluting the interaction that actually carries the edge; all windows are shortened to the 6-bar forecast scale so the edge sits at the pinned horizon rather than at 24 bars.
factors.name: Concentration-signed permanence inside the conversion switch

factors.trading_idea: Whether a one-minute price push is transient (dealer inventory shock, snaps back) or permanent (informed metaorder, extends) depends on the probability that the flow driving it is informed — the Kyle / Glosten–Milgrom adverse-selection channel. Cross-sectionally, informed-trading intensity is structurally higher for informationally opaque firms (R&D- and intangible-heavy, accrual-heavy earnings far from cash flow, non-dividend-payers), where private research yields bigger edges and liquidity providers cannot confidently lean against flow; it is lowest for transparent, cash-generative, dividend-paying firms, where dealers absorb order flow and price reverts. The child therefore keeps the parent's mean-zero *interaction* architecture (standardized idiosyncratic push × gate) but replaces the price-level 'wear' gate — which the book already spans and which contributed +0.0000 marginal IC — with a fundamental-opacity gate that is cross-sectionally residualized on volatility, dollar-volume and size ranks and then sector-demeaned, so only the fundamental-opacity component that microstructure factors cannot observe survives. The edge persists because it is compensation for adverse selection (a structural payment to liquidity suppliers, not a mispricing) and because exploiting it requires joining point-in-time quarterly fundamentals into a 10-second microstructure stack for a payoff of a tick per minute — a data join HFT desks skip (they treat fundamentals as event risk) and slow fundamental investors cannot use.
factors.name: Fundamental-opacity gated impact-permanence split

factors.trading_idea: Volume that executes while a name's mid stays glued to one grid level is evidence of liquidity SUPPLY, not of a queue being exhausted: the touch kept refilling, so the flow that hit it was absorbed by patient market makers rather than informed. The break of such a heavily-defended level is therefore mostly transient price impact from one impatient taker, and the vacated level stays a magnet — the beta-residual excursion away from it decays back over the next minute, with pull strength rising in the per-bar volume absorbed while pinned (a direct inverse-lambda depth proxy), fading with time since the break, dying once the price re-pins at a new level (acceptance), and vanishing for displacements of many grid quanta (those are genuine information, not noise). This is exactly why the parent's declared continuation sign was contradicted: its gate loaded on the highest-absorption breaks, which are the most transient. The edge survives arbitrage because each event is worth a fraction of a tick and can only be harvested by re-posting liquidity at the vacated level in low-turnover, grid-bound names whose spread is at least one tick — takers pay the whole edge away, and passive harvesters bear adverse selection when the break is real news.
factors.name: Defended-pin magnet: size-kernel transient-impact snapback

factors.trading_idea: Parent A asserts that income/payout-clientele names, held by slow mandate-constrained capital, complete their beta-implied response to a market-wide shock with a lag; parent B shows that whether a block displacement continues or reverts is a state-dependent quantity that must be estimated per name with a robust sign-concordance (Rice) estimator rather than assumed. The child estimates, per name, the lag-6 block autocorrelation of the BETA-PURGED (idiosyncratic) 60-second displacement separately in market-shock bars and quiet-market bars, and shrinks those estimates empirical-Bayes toward the cross-sectional median of the name's payout-clientele tercile, then applies the state-matched coefficient to the current idiosyncratic displacement. The interaction carries edge neither parent has: A imposes a hand-set clientele multiplier and a fixed 12-bar-ish beta wedge (so it is horizon-mismatched and its sign is assumed), while B applies a magnitude-state coefficient to a market-contaminated displacement and overfits per-name thresholds; here the clientele variable enters only as a pooling prior (the data decides whether slow-capital names revert faster), the state split is the common, low-parameter market-shock switch, and the coefficient is self-calibrated at exactly the 6-bar delivery horizon.
factors.name: Clientele-Pooled Shock-State Block Autocorrelation Catch-Up

factors.trading_idea: The parent proved that mid-drift printed in quiet (near-zero-volume) bars and drift paid for with volume are two distinct channels, but it imposed a hand-set polarity (+0.5 quiet, -1 traded) and therefore loaded mostly on the slow, concordant 'information' state — hence its IC kept climbing out to 24 bars. Rotate the two standardised channels into an orthogonal pair: a COMMON component s = (quiet+traded)/2 (corroborated repricing, priced over minutes) and a WEDGE component d = (quiet-traded)/2 (maker-inventory vs taker-liquidity standoff, settled at the next few liquidity events), then let the data assign each component's weight by estimating, per name, a trailing two-variable OLS of the realised return over exactly a 6-bar offset on the lagged (s,d) pair, shrunk toward the cross-sectionally pooled coefficient matrix and ridged. Because the regression target IS the 6-bar-ahead return, any component whose information resolves on a minutes horizon receives near-zero weight at this offset, so the factor is horizon-matched by construction rather than by tuning. The edge survives arbitrage because the loadings drift with liquidity regime (they must be re-estimated continuously) and harvesting the wedge leg requires paying spread in exactly the thin, quiet names where the standoff arises.
factors.name: Rotated Maker/Taker Channel with h=6 Response-Calibrated Weights

factors.trading_idea: The parent proved that the Epps/lag-1-corrected, precision-whitened, peer-purged 6-bar dislocation carries relative-value information the book does not span, but its realized IC was negative (dislocations *revert*, they do not extend) and grew in magnitude with horizon — the classic signature of a convergence trade whose clock is too slow for the fixed 6-bar offset. Two frictions decide convergence speed and are missing from the parent: (i) a dislocation smaller than the round-trip immediacy cost is inside every liquidity provider's no-trade band, so nobody closes it and it only decays passively over minutes, and (ii) a dislocation is closed by *fills*, which arrive on the trade clock, not the wall clock — a name whose 10-second event intensity is currently self-excited will experience many more counterparty arrivals in the next 60 seconds than a dormant name. The child therefore fades only the part of the whitened dislocation that exceeds a per-name Roll-type no-trade band, and paces that fade by a Hawkes-style forecast of the name's next-minute event intensity, which moves the convergence into the fixed 6-bar window. The edge survives arbitrage because measuring it requires a staleness-corrected panel precision matrix at 10-second frequency and because the residual risk is exactly the slow-clock / wide-band tail that most relative-value engines (which trade on calendar time and ignore the band) systematically mis-time.
factors.name: Cost-band hinged precision dislocation paced by the trade clock

factors.trading_idea: Parent A's realised IC says the true microstructural fact is the opposite of its stated hypothesis: fresh displacement that arrives while ONLY this name is unusually busy reverses inside the next minute (an isolated 10-second volume burst is single-name liquidity demand walking a thin book — pure transient Bouchaud impact that decays as depth refills), whereas displacement that arrives while the WHOLE cross-section is busy does not revert in relative-value terms, because at 10-second sampling the trailing static beta is Epps-biased downward and understates instantaneous comovement in high-activity states, so much of what looks 'idiosyncratic' during a basket burst is really unabsorbed systematic repricing. The child therefore takes Parent B's horizon-matched Dimson-beta-purged 6-bar residual displacement (which strips the market leg that made Parent A's raw-increment legs a beta-timing bet) and routes its sign with Parent A's panel-synchronised activity attribution: the share of the last 6 bars' activity innovation that was own-excess versus panel-wide. Long residual pushes funded by common activity, short residual pushes funded by the name's own isolated burst. The interaction is edge neither parent has: A never removed the systematic leg from the displacement it attributed, and B's participation-shape entropy state describes the *shape* of trading but is blind to *who* funded the move, so its gap kept an unconditional beta-timing/momentum loading; here the attribution is cross-sectionally rank-centred so only the funded-by-whom interaction survives.
factors.name: Activity-commonality attributed Dimson residual reversal (6-bar)

factors.trading_idea: Parent A showed that the low-noise object in a bar is the endpoint's dislocation from the bar's high-low centre, and that this dislocation is mostly transient (it reverts); Parent B showed — via its contradicted sign — that volume executed while the mid stands still is a queue-depth / resilience proxy, and that displacement occurring against such thick, replenishing queues does NOT continue but decays. The child conditions A's dislocation signal on B's state variable: absorption at standstill, i.e. volume printed on bars whose price change is below the name's own effective grid quantum, measured in bars-of-average-volume and normalised cross-sectionally. The interaction is the edge: a sub-range dislocation only reliably mean-reverts when a deep queue is standing behind the touch to refill it, whereas the same dislocation in a thin, low-absorption book is either permanent repricing or pure quote flicker — so neither the unconditional dislocation (A, weak standalone IC) nor the absorption state (B, wrong-signed on its own continuation reading) captures it alone. Replacing A's ad-hoc 1/(1+V/medV) quiet weighting with a microstructurally-grounded resilience state also removes the branch-heavy machinery that A's report flagged as overfit.
factors.name: Standstill-absorption-gated range-centre dislocation reversion

factors.trading_idea: The parent's engine works (pooled, causally-calibrated continuation coefficients give a measured rather than assumed sign) but its conditioning variable — the ordinal shape of the 60-second price path — is pure microstructure and therefore nearly spanned by the existing book, which is why its marginal IC was negative. The child keeps the calibration engine and replaces the gate with information the micro book structurally cannot contain: the *width of the name's fundamental valuation band*. When a name has a tight, cheaply-verifiable accounting anchor (positive earnings yield, large tangible book relative to price, clean accruals, low intangibility, larger cap), fast statistical liquidity providers can confidently take the other side of a one-minute dislocation, so impact is transient and the move is repaid; when the anchor is wide/ambiguous (intangible-heavy, loss-making, small), providers widen and a larger fraction of the move is permanent, so it keeps accruing. The factor forecasts (a_t + b_t·Ambiguity)·displacement with (a_t, b_t) from a pooled trailing OLS over the whole cross-section, then removes the cross-sectional projection on plain displacement so only the ambiguity-differential (interaction) part is traded — an interaction term is naturally near-orthogonal to the main effect the book already owns. The edge persists because it requires joining point-in-time quarterly accounting to 10-second flow: minute-scale liquidity providers do not condition on accounting quality, and accounting-driven investors do not trade minute-scale reversion.
factors.name: Valuation-ambiguity-gated block continuation (pooled online calibration)

factors.trading_idea: Under the Merton/Christie leverage effect, equity is a levered claon on assets, so a genuine asset-value shock must move price AND expand equity volatility with an elasticity that rises in the firm's leverage: a real down-shock in a levered name mechanically raises equity vol, an unlevered name much less so. I therefore estimate, per bar and cross-sectionally, how much trailing short-run log realised vol expansion is explained by the signed 1-minute move interacted with ranked leverage (financialLeverage, debtToEquity) and size, and read the residual as a consistency test: a move whose vol response is *deficient* relative to its leverage-implied elasticity carries no asset-level information and is liquidity/inventory pressure, so it snaps back within the next minute, whereas a move whose vol response exceeds the leverage-implied level is a true repricing and continues. This flips the sign of the very-short-horizon reversal instead of just fading every move, so it is not plain reversal, and the edge survives because market makers condition on flow imbalance and raw volatility, not on whether a name's realised vol asymmetry is consistent with its balance-sheet elasticity — a joint cross-sectional estimation nobody runs at 10-second frequency.
factors.name: Christie leverage-elasticity gap gate on 1-minute moves

factors.trading_idea: Parent A measures how much of a name's kernel-implied response to the last common market shock is still *owed* (a systematic delivery gap that closes slowly), while Parent B measures how far a name closed inside its own heavy-volume bar range after sector-common flow is purged (an idiosyncratic, fast-decaying cost of immediacy). The child routes the two signals by the same trailing variance decomposition that makes each one valid: for names whose returns are largely market-explained (high trailing R-squared) the owed-beta deficit is the meaningful object, while for high-idiosyncratic-share names the participation-weighted range displacement is the meaningful object — and it then amplifies the blend where the two channels agree in sign and damps it where they disagree. The interaction carries edge neither parent has: sign concordance separates a *mechanical* repricing lag (a name that under-delivered the common impulse AND is sitting low in a heavy-volume range, i.e. still paying transient impact) from *news* (an under-delivering name that is nonetheless closing high on its own volume, where the gap is permanent and must not be chased). Because the fast liquidity-cost channel supplies the timing while the kernel deficit supplies direction and size, the combined signal fires exactly on the ~1-minute transient-impact decay window rather than drifting out to the parents' 24-bar peak.
factors.name: Kernel-deficit / transient-impact snapback routed by variance share

factors.trading_idea: The parent established that thin-volume mid drift continues while volume-paid drift reverts, but it decided *which* leg to trust from an activity (log-volume) innovation — a slow, noisy proxy that needed long look-backs and left a third of the panel unpriced and the IC peak stranded at 12 bars. The child replaces the gate with a price-side measure of whether the quote is actually alive during silence: the ratio of average absolute (vol-scaled) mid movement on quiet bars to that on traded bars, cross-sectionally standardised so a market-wide lull cannot masquerade as name-specific repricing. Mechanism: if a name's mid keeps moving as much without trades as with them, the market maker is actively re-pricing on inventory/private information, so the accumulated quiet displacement is unfinished repricing that completes as the next order arrives (~1 minute); if the mid barely moves when nobody trades, the quotes are frozen and any thin-bar tick is stale-quote/discreteness flicker, in which case the name's displacement is mostly trade impact and decays. The edge survives arbitrage because monetising the continuation leg means crossing the spread in the names that are, at that instant, the least liquid in the cross-section, and it is falsified if quiet-bar drift continuation is independent of the silence volatility share (gate adds nothing over an ungated split) or if traded-bar drift does not revert faster in frozen-quote names.
factors.name: Quote-Liveness (Silence Volatility Share) Gated Fast Quiet/Traded Drift Split

factors.trading_idea: Every name has a characteristic *response delay* tau to market-wide innovations, set by how quickly its quoting and holder base re-optimise; a trailing wedge (parent) sums over all delays at once, which is why the parent's edge peaked at 12 bars rather than the fixed 6-bar offset. I estimate tau directly from the quadrature (imaginary) part of the trailing cross-spectrum between the name's 10-second returns and the cap-weighted market return at the ~4-minute band (complex demodulation, causal rolling DFT): under a pure delay model r_i(t)=g_i*m(t-tau_i), the name's next-6-bar return equals g_i times the market's ALREADY REALISED return over the window [t-tau_i, t-tau_i+6], which is fully observable whenever tau_i >= 6 — so the forecast is horizon-matched by construction instead of by luck. tau_i is shrunk toward the median delay of its payout-clientele quintile (dividend yield, payout ratio, FCF yield, negative share growth), because mandate-constrained income capital re-quotes slowly; the edge survives arbitrage because extracting tau requires a coherence-weighted quadrature estimate on very noisy second-level returns, and the per-name payoff is concentrated in thin, low-attention names where fast capital does not pay the fixed monitoring cost. Falsified if the coherence-weighted, delay-selected delivery term has no more predictive power than the undifferentiated trailing beta wedge, or if clientele quintiles do not order the estimated delays.
factors.name: Quadrature-phase delay-matched market delivery

factors.trading_idea: Parent A says a short-run equity impulse that de-levers into a large *implied asset shock* (Merton elasticity = assets/equity) cannot be fundamental over ~60 seconds and must revert; parent B says the reverting part is specifically the *volume-paid* move, while unpaid quote repricing in idiosyncratically quiet names keeps drifting. The child de-levers the signed-semivariance impulse and then splits it by bar-level participation: the same implausibly-large implied asset shock is faded when it was bought/sold through (paid transient impact, amplified by the liquidity-vacuum rank and by idiosyncratically elevated activity), but is followed when it was produced by quotes with no trades in a name that has gone silent while its peers keep trading (dealer repricing that completes as flow arrives). The interaction carries edge neither parent has: leverage de-levering supplies the *plausibility magnitude* that tells you the move is non-fundamental, and the quiet/traded split supplies the *sign of what happens next* — A blindly reverses non-fundamental impulses (including unpaid quote repricing that actually continues), while B has no way to know whether a mid move is large relative to what the balance sheet makes possible.
factors.name: De-levered asset shock split into quiet repricing vs traded impact, silence-gated

factors.trading_idea: Parent A shows that mid-price drift printed in (near-)zero-volume bars continues while drift paid for with aggressive volume decays, but it applies one common continuation/reversion coefficient to every name; Parent B built a jump-robust, tick-size-free per-name memory coefficient from Rice's inversion rho = cos(pi*p_flip) but measured it on the *pooled* tape, where it came out with the opposite sign to its hypothesis. The child estimates the Rice sign-concordance memory *separately inside each channel* — on adjacent non-overlapping block displacements built only from quiet bars, and only from active bars — and uses it to modulate A's split: quiet-bar drift is followed less the more its own signs persist (persistent quiet ramps are stale-mid trending in laggy names, i.e. lagged information that the market has already priced by the time an 80-minute concordance statistic can detect it), while traded-bar drift is faded harder the more its signs persist (a persistently-signed impact channel is a mature, crowded sliced metaorder whose remaining path is impact decay) and barely faded when its signs already flip (the bounce has been paid). The interaction carries edge neither parent has: A cannot tell an informative quiet repricing from a stale ramp and B cannot tell staleness-induced spurious persistence from genuine order-splitting persistence, because those two generators of rho live in different volume channels — separating rho by channel is exactly what makes B's coefficient sign interpretable and A's split name-specific.
factors.name: Channel-conditional Rice memory weighting of quiet vs traded drift

factors.trading_idea: The parent showed that the name-specific part of a valuation-neighbour hedged residual snaps back inside a minute while the tier-common part does not, but it treated the snapback clock as a property of the dislocated name alone. A relative-value desk cannot close such a dislocation without simultaneously trading the *hedge leg* — the valuation-neighbour basket — so the speed of closure is set by the executability of that basket, which has two multiplicative components: statistical hedge accuracy (trailing R-squared of the name on its basket, which the parent already used) and current hedge cost, proxied by whether the neighbourhood's own tape is presently active relative to its own norm. When the neighbour basket is quiet, the arbitrageur must pay impact on several thin legs and the dislocation persists beyond six bars; when the neighbourhood is active the hedge is nearly free and the purged residual reverts fast. Falsifiable: interacting the purged-residual snapback with kernel-averaged *neighbour* activity (not the name's own volume) must raise IC over the R-squared-only gate; if it does not, hedge-leg cost is not the binding constraint and the snapback clock is set purely by the dislocated name's own tape. The edge survives arbitrage because the gate is invisible from the target name's own order flow — it requires joining point-in-time per-share fundamentals to a 10-second tape to define the neighbourhood and then reading that neighbourhood's aggregate activity state, and capacity is capped by the small number of tight valuation tiers.
factors.name: Hedge-leg activity gated cluster-purged peer snapback

factors.trading_idea: A 60-second displacement can be built two ways: by one large market order sweeping the book (transient impact, mechanically reverts as depth is replenished over the following seconds) or by a metaorder split into many aligned child orders across bars (Lillo-Farmer / Toth order-splitting, which makes signed flow long-memoried, so impact keeps accruing while the parent order executes). The child therefore stops betting on the *level* of short-horizon memory and instead reads the *microstructure of how the move was assembled*: the within-name anomaly of dollar-volume Herfindahl concentration and of the price-side jump share over exactly the 6 bars being forecast, plus whether the volume mass pushed in the same direction as the net move. Distributed, volume-supported displacement is forecast to continue over the next 6 bars; concentrated, single-bar, unsupported displacement is forecast to hook back. The edge survives arbitrage because reversion desks apply one common horizon coefficient to the whole book — the two sub-populations have opposite signs and roughly cancel in the pooled average, so harvesting the split requires continuous per-name re-estimation of each name's own concentration baseline for only a few basis points per name.
factors.name: Metaorder-splitting vs single-sweep concentration flip

factors.trading_idea: Firms running large actual repurchase programs have a mechanical, price-contingent, anonymous buyer standing in their own book: Rule 10b-18's safe harbour forces the desk to bid passively at or below the last independent bid, caps it near 25% of ADV, and most programs are VWAP-benchmarked, so the desk absorbs weakness and mechanically steps aside on rallies (Hong-Wang-Yu 'firms as buyers of last resort'; Busch-Obernberger RFS 2017 find repurchase flow supplies liquidity and pulls prices back toward value precisely on down-moves). The falsifiable claim is therefore an INTERACTION, not a level: after an idiosyncratic 1-minute dip, names whose quarterly repurchase dollars are large relative to their own realised dollar volume (i.e. the program has capacity to matter) should snap back more than equally-dipped names with no program, and the differential should be absent for equal-sized upward pushes and stronger when the stock is already below its trailing volume-weighted anchor (where VWAP-benchmarked desks buy hardest). We therefore compute the gated dip and Gram-Schmidt out every main effect (dip size, pop size, buyback intensity, VWAP gap), so only the pure interaction survives — this is what decorrelates it from the book's semivariance/reversal family. The edge persists because it requires joining a quarterly cash-flow-statement item to 10-second dislocations, buyback flow is untagged on the tape, and the absorption capacity itself is finite and non-arbitrageable (no instrument pays for it).
factors.name: Buyback-capacity-gated dip absorption

factors.trading_idea: Merton convexity says a downside burst in equity semivolatility is only *informative* when the firm's capital structure makes equity a genuinely levered claim on assets; for low-leverage names the same one-sided variance burst is almost pure inventory/depth withdrawal and must revert. The parent measured this state over 120 bars, so its content was a slow regime variable whose IC kept building out to 24 bars; the child instead measures a *shock*: the ratio of 6-bar downside semivol to the name's own 120-bar downside semivol minus the same ratio for upside semivol, which is a fast, mean-zero, quickly-decaying object matched to a 60-second horizon. That one-sided burst is then double-gated: damped for high debt-to-assets / high financial-leverage names (where the down-move plausibly re-prices default risk and continues) and damped when the burst arrived with abnormally high traded volume (information rather than a liquidity vacuum). The edge survives because HFT liquidity providers gate on volume and spread but not on balance-sheet-conditioned semivariance asymmetry, and the counterparty in the low-volume, low-leverage case is a fee-insensitive liquidator.
factors.name: De-levered downside semivol burst with volume-vacuum snapback

factors.trading_idea: Recurrence-quantification of the trailing de-marketed price path measures how *laminar* a name has been: the recurrence rate of the current level (fraction of the last L bars spent within an adaptive band of it) is high when the path keeps revisiting the same levels, i.e. when standing limit-order supply and resting stop orders have had time to pile up at the band edges and market makers have anchored their quotes there. When price finally clears that band, the defending depth has just been consumed and the stop cluster fires, so the escape continues over the next ~minute; when the path was already diffusive or jump-driven (low laminarity), the same 6-bar displacement is mostly transient price impact and overreaction, which is repaid. The child therefore multiplies the band-clearing escape magnitude by a cross-sectionally centred laminarity weight, isolating the *interaction* and discarding the unconditional reversal level that the book already spans — which is exactly why the parent, lumping all flow-unexplained displacement together, realised a net reversion sign. The edge survives arbitrage because it requires an adaptive-band recurrence estimator on market-neutralised paths, the two states partially cancel unconditionally (so plain reversal/momentum traders see nothing), and each event pays only a few basis points at one-minute capacity.
factors.name: Laminar-recurrence gated band-escape flip

factors.trading_idea: The parent assumed a per-name lag-6 autocorrelation and got the direction wrong because that per-name coefficient is tiny, noisy and regime-flipping — the sign of 1-minute block dependence is a *pooled, time-varying* quantity, not a name attribute. The child keeps the ordinal/jump-robust sign machinery but moves the information into the *shape* of the move: a 60-second displacement built from consecutive same-signed 10-second increments is the footprint of a sliced metaorder still working (flow autocorrelation ⇒ impact keeps accruing), whereas the same displacement produced by one large increment against several opposing ones is a liquidity-vacuum jump whose transient impact is repaid. Instead of hard-coding which way that maps into returns, the factor estimates the coefficients of predicted_z_next = (a + b·shape)·z_now by a causal, pooled, trailing OLS across the whole cross-section (millions of observations ⇒ the *sign* is measured, not assumed), and applies them to the current displacement. The edge persists because the average 1-minute AR coefficient is already arbitraged to ~0 (that is why the parent was noise), while the *interaction* between continuation and ordinal path shape requires joint per-state re-estimation, flips with the intraday execution regime, and pays only a few basis points per name.
factors.name: Online-calibrated shape-conditional block continuation

factors.trading_idea: The parent had the right architecture — a name-specific transitory share multiplying its current idiosyncratic dislocation — but estimated that share from a covariance/variance ratio of 6-bar blocks, an estimator with only ~100 effective observations that is dominated by a handful of jumps, so the conditioner was mostly estimation noise and contributed nothing over the book. Replace it with a duration statistic: for the market-residual price detrended by its own 5-minute anchor, the per-bar hazard of an excursion ending, h = (number of excursion starts)/(number of bars spent in excursion) = 1/mean excursion length, estimated separately for upward and downward excursions from strictly purged past bars (lagged one full horizon). This is a scale-free, outlier-immune Bernoulli-type estimator using ~900 observations, and it is side-resolved: h_up high means the ask side replenishes quickly and upward dislocations are handed back fast, i.e. a large transitory share on that side, while a low hazard on the side just moved means one-sided pressure is still being absorbed and the move is informational. The edge survives arbitrage because acting on it means supplying immediacy into the side of the book that is currently thin, at the moment inventory risk is largest — a liquidity-provision premium, not a costless arbitrage — and because run-length/hazard bookkeeping is not part of standard factor libraries.
factors.name: Side-resolved reabsorption-hazard dislocation wedge

factors.trading_idea: Ten-second cross-sectional returns are extremely heavy-tailed, so an OLS market beta estimated on them is dominated by a handful of co-jump bars; every desk that hedges with such a beta leaves residual factor exposure inside what it calls 'idiosyncratic' displacement. I therefore hedge each name twice over the same trailing window — once with plain OLS beta and once with a beta estimated on winsorized (2.5 mean-absolute-deviation) returns — and read the disagreement between the two hedges as a measure of how tail-contaminated the name's beta is. Where contamination is low the robustly-hedged 1-minute displacement is genuinely idiosyncratic inventory/liquidity pressure and snaps back over the next ~6 bars; where contamination is high the 'residual' is mostly mis-attributed, laggy factor exposure (Epps partial adjustment in slow names), which continues rather than reverts, so the gate flips the sign of the snapback. The edge persists because it is an estimator-bias effect inherited by anyone running a standard OLS covariance pipeline: correcting it requires trailing robust hedges on a 10-second panel, which is computationally awkward and not a standard market-making screen.
factors.name: Jump-contaminated beta wedge gate on idiosyncratic snapback

factors.trading_idea: A peer multiple-space dislocation only reverts as fast as the relative-value capital that trades the peer basket arrives, and that arrival is observable as *synchronous* trade activity across the peer group: when many members of a comparables group are printing trades in the same 10-second bars, basket/pair desks are live and a spread gap closes within seconds, whereas in synchronously quiet groups the identical gap decays over many minutes (which is exactly why the parent's IC kept rising out to 24 bars). The child therefore (i) measures the dislocation over a horizon-matched 6-bar anchor instead of a 5-minute EWMA, so the quantity being predicted decays on the same clock as the forecast offset, and (ii) replaces the static peer-dispersion gate with a dynamic peer *closure clock* — the product of the name's own and its group's recent trade-arrival frequency, normalised by its own trailing hourly norm. Falsifiable: if the interaction with peer-activity synchrony is flat (i.e. high- and low-synchrony groups show the same 6-bar reversion, or the horizon profile still peaks at 24 bars), the closure-speed mechanism is wrong and the signal is just peer-relative reversal. The edge should persist because it requires jointly maintaining point-in-time per-share fundamentals, a peer map, and cross-name activity synchrony at 10-second resolution, and because the fast leg it exploits is precisely where spread/impact costs deter marginal arbitrageurs.
factors.name: Multiple-space dislocation gated by peer closure clock

factors.trading_idea: Structurally (Merton / Christie leverage hypothesis) equity is a call on assets, so downside-heavy realised volatility asymmetry should scale with capital structure: high debt-to-assets and high financial leverage firms mechanically show more downside variance per unit of total variance. Realised downside asymmetry far in excess of what the firm's balance sheet justifies is therefore not a structural feature but transient one-sided liquidation or panic order flow, which is compensated over the following minute. The other side is a forced or fee-insensitive seller; the inefficiency survives because balance-sheet-conditioned vol asymmetry is not a screen HFT liquidity providers run.
factors.name: Merton-Implied Semivariance Asymmetry Residual

factors.trading_idea: At a 10-second sampling frequency each name's idiosyncratic price change is a mixture of transient liquidity-provision noise (quote flicker, inventory bounce) that mean-reverts within seconds and informed order-splitting that persists; the mixture weight is name-specific and switches with whether the move was volume-backed or quiet. I estimate each name's own lag-1 sign-persistence kernel separately in the volume-backed and the quiet regime (a robust, non-parametric estimate of the AR coefficient via the Gaussian arcsine inversion, empirical-Bayes shrunk toward the name's pooled kernel), then iterate that kernel exactly six steps and sum it — the forecast is by construction matched to the fixed 6-bar offset instead of being a slow state variable. The parent measured a persistent semivariance *level*, so its information paid off over many minutes; this child converts the same 'transient one-sided flow must unwind' idea into an explicitly horizon-truncated impulse-response, and lets the sign flip per name and per regime (negative kernel = bounce, positive = splitting). The edge survives arbitrage because the cross-sectional average kernel is near zero — a single momentum or reversal screen averages the two populations away — and capturing it requires per-name, per-volume-regime estimation plus a geometric truncation tied to the trading horizon.
factors.name: Volume-regime sign-kernel horizon-matched recoil forecast

factors.trading_idea: Parent A knows *which side* a variance burst sits on and strips out the slow Merton/Christie component by demeaning inside leverage x size buckets, but its vacuum test is a coarse 12-bar variance-per-volume ratio that cannot tell a thin-ask up-tick from a genuine inventory dislocation; Parent B has exactly that missing instrument — a per-bar, side-conditional elasticity baseline that measures how far a move travelled relative to what this name normally travels per unit of flow *in that direction* — but it spends it on raw signed returns with no structural conditioning. The child pushes B's per-bar flow deficit *inside* A's semivariance sums: each bar's squared idiosyncratic return is weighted by the fraction of that move which flow did not pay for, so the object measured is the share of recent realised variance that is unbacked-downside minus unbacked-upside, innovated against the name's own 120-bar version of the same statistic and demeaned within leverage-tercile x size-half buckets. The interaction carries edge neither has alone because side-conditioning kills the static thin-side illiquidity characteristic that contaminates A's aggregate gate, while A's structural bucket demeaning and one-sided (semivariance) decomposition tell us whether B's unpaid-for displacement was a leverage-justified repricing or a pure dealer-inventory excursion — only the latter must snap back inside the next minute.
factors.name: Flow-deficit-weighted semivariance asymmetry wedge

factors.trading_idea: Parent A shows (via its inverted realized sign) that trade-attributable mid displacement keeps going while quiet quote-driven displacement snaps back, and Parent B shows that how much of a standing peer-relative displacement unwinds inside 6 bars is governed by the propagator's age-dependent remaining-decay fraction. Neither parent conditions one on the other: A applies a fixed sign to the traded leg regardless of whether the metaorder is still slicing, and B applies the age front-loading weight to a displacement of mixed origin, so its fast, high-decay-fraction reversion is diluted by trade-driven continuation — which is exactly why B's IC only matures at 24 bars. The child decomposes the standing peer-residual displacement into trade-attributable and quiet legs with the participation share v/(v+trailing mean v), then routes them differently: the quiet leg is always faded with the propagator's remaining-relaxation fraction phi(age) (untraded quote displacement is transient book imbalance that refills fastest when fresh), while the traded leg is faded by phi(age) only when participation intensity has decayed (metaorder finished, impact now relaxing) and is followed with the flow when participation is still elevated (order-splitting autocorrelation). The interaction supplies the missing switch — origin tells you WHETHER a displacement will relax, age and liveness tell you HOW MUCH of that relaxation lands inside the fixed 6-bar window.
factors.name: Liveness-switched, age-attributed traded/quiet impact split

factors.trading_idea: The parent's realized IC sign (its gate was symmetric occupancy, and the data said pinned levels CONTINUE while vacuums REVERT) is exactly the permanent-vs-transient impact split: a displacement that had to grind through price levels which have historically absorbed real volume must have been paid for with genuine depth, so it is informative and the repricing sticks; a displacement that slid through a volume desert is pure slippage against a thin book, and once the pushing flow pauses market makers re-post and price snaps back. The child therefore measures the toll directly rather than through path shape: how much volume the price band just traversed has historically transacted, relative to a uniform-occupancy null over the same window (so it is a genuine volume-at-price shelf/desert measure, not a range statistic), combined with how much volume the push itself actually paid. That composite backing score, standardised per name in time, signs a deliberately fast 3-bar (30-second) displacement, because unpaid transient impact decays inside a minute — which is why the edge should now live at the fixed 6-bar offset instead of drifting out to 24 bars. The edge survives arbitrage because it requires maintaining a per-name, per-level volume-at-price histogram in real time and pays only a few ticks per episode, while its cause — where resting inventory actually sits and whether the flow consumed it — is a structural property of order books rather than a mispricing that can be traded away.
factors.name: Volume-at-price toll gated fast displacement permanence

factors.trading_idea: The parent's insight — displacement produced by quotes moving on their own persists, displacement paid for with aggressive volume decays — is a statement about *which channel excites which*, so it should be measured as an asymmetry between two point processes rather than accumulated over 30 bars (which is why the parent's edge only matured at 24 bars). For each name I treat large |mid-return| bars and large-volume bars as two marked event streams and estimate a Hawkes-style cross-excitation arrow: how often activity spikes follow quote-revision spikes within 1-3 bars versus the reverse, normalised by the independence expectation, so the statistic is a slow, structural property of the name's price-formation regime (maker-led vs taker-led). That slow gate then multiplies the *horizon-matched* 6-bar displacement: in maker-led names the fresh move is genuine repricing that later attracts confirming flow and continues over the next minute; in taker-led names it is transient impact and snaps back. Because the gate is cross-sectionally demeaned the factor carries almost no unconditional reversal/momentum exposure — it is pure interaction — and it is falsified if the conditional sign of 6-bar displacement is unrelated to (or ordered opposite to) the excitation arrow.
factors.name: Trade-Quote Cross-Excitation Arrow Gated Displacement

factors.trading_idea: The parent proved that splitting a hedged 10-second excursion into unpaid-for (quiet-bar) quote shading and paid-for (traded-bar) impact carries information, but it gated that split with a single market-WIDE commonality scalar, which cannot vary across names inside a bar and therefore adds almost no cross-sectional signal — hence the near-zero standalone IC. The child moves the same risk-transfer mechanism to the name level: whether a dealer's temporary impact gets repaid depends on whether that specific name's inventory can be laid off in the factor/basket, measured by the trailing share of its return variance spanned by the equal-weighted market (R²) plus the short-minus-long R² innovation, which detects an idiosyncratic-news-driven collapse in comovement. In hedgeable, high-R² names traded excursions are absorbable inventory imbalance that reverts within a few bars while quiet mids are merely stale factor drag; in low-R² / R²-collapsing names the dealer cannot hedge, so aggressive volume is likely informed and continues while unpaid-for quote shading reveals the dealer's private adverse-selection belief and continues more strongly. The edge persists because it requires jointly estimating per-name factor spannedness, a soft volume-participation decomposition of the residual path, and their interaction — a conditional (state-dependent) sign, not a directional factor, so simple impact-reversal arbitrageurs trading the unconditional average both dilute and sustain it.
factors.name: Hedgeability-gated soft quiet/traded impact split

factors.trading_idea: Parent B locates a dislocation in the right *space* (peer log-multiple spreads inside a comparable industry group) but dates it slowly, so its edge only matures at 24 bars; Parent A knows how to *date* and *classify* a displacement (12-bar one-sided variance innovation, gated by variance-burst per unit of volume-burst) but is blind to whether the displacement moved the name away from its relative-value anchor. The child fires only when a fresh, semivariance-concordant one-sided move (down-move-dominated variance innovation accompanying a downward multiple-space spread dislocation) has pushed a name off its comparability-gated peer multiple, and it *switches sign* on the vacuum diagnostic: in a thin book (large variance burst per unit participation) the dislocation is mechanical inventory impact inside a credible comparable set and snaps back within a minute, whereas the same spread move delivered with commensurate volume is informed peer-relative repricing and continues. Neither parent has this interaction — B always fades regardless of who moved the price, A fades variance bursts without knowing whether the burst created a relative-value gap worth arbitraging — and conditioning the fade on both freshness and execution-quality pulls the peer-spread edge forward from 24 bars onto the fixed 6-bar offset.
factors.name: Vacuum-switched peer-multiple dislocation with semivariance concordance

factors.trading_idea: At 10-second resolution a peer-residual mid displacement that arrives together with abnormal trade volume is the visible footprint of a sliced metaorder: execution schedules and self-exciting order flow make the same-side pressure recur, so that displacement *continues* for as long as the flow is still arriving, and only relaxes in the Obizhaeva-Wang/Bouchaud propagator sense once trade intensity has decayed back to its own baseline. Displacement that arrives on essentially no trade is quote-driven at this timescale — fleeting quotes, one-sided depth withdrawal that is replenished, stale-mid noise — and therefore mean-reverts. The child therefore keeps the parent's trade-attribution decomposition but makes the traded leg's forward coefficient *state-dependent* on metaorder liveness (tanh of a trailing z-scored log ratio of fast/slow volume EWMAs), which explains why the parent's ungated 'quiet minus traded' wedge realised the opposite sign: on net its traded leg sat in the still-live regime and continued rather than relaxed. The edge survives arbitrage because monetising it means either following possibly-informed bursts or supplying liquidity into them within a minute, on comparability cells built from point-in-time fundamentals (sector x size), a join that microstructure and relative-value desks do not make; it is falsified if the forward coefficient on the traded leg is flat (not increasing and sign-crossing) in trade-intensity excess, or if the quiet leg does not revert at 6 bars.
factors.name: Flow-intensity-gated traded continuation vs quiet snapback

factors.trading_idea: The parent's report is informative, not noise: the precision-metric dislocation (Sigma^-1 x, which up-weights moves along historically tightest linear combinations) predicted CONTINUATION, not snapback. The reason is that at a 10-second clock those low-variance directions are pinned mostly by non-synchronous quote updating rather than by arbitrage capital, so a name that walks off its basket is usually the *leader* in price discovery, and order-splitting (Hawkes-like flow autocorrelation) plus lagged peer updating make its own move persist for another ~minute. The child therefore keeps the regularized precision whitening but separates the two physically different populations that were mixed together and killed the parent: (a) sign-coherent whitened drift accompanied by above-normal traded participation = a metaorder in progress -> continuation over the next 6 bars; (b) the same-sized whitened dislocation on below-normal participation = pure quote noise / bounce -> reversal. Falsification: if the whitened dislocation is just relabelled univariate momentum, the cross-sectional projection on the plain 6-bar move (which we remove) would carry it and the residual IC would be zero; if participation is irrelevant, the two halves of the interaction would have the same sign and the product would have zero IC. The edge survives arbitrage because acting on it requires simultaneous multi-name execution against a stable rolling precision matrix and pays only a few ticks per episode, and because a signed interaction (dislocation x participation) with the univariate move projected out is invisible to standard momentum/reversal screens.
factors.name: Precision-whitened coherent drift, participation-split

factors.trading_idea: At the one-minute scale a name's move splits into a peer-common part (shared with its valuation-comparable industry basket) and a peer-idiosyncratic part; only the idiosyncratic part can be hedged instantly by trading the peer basket, so liquidity providers willingly absorb it and it snaps back fast, whereas the common part carries unhedgeable factor risk and is not repaired. Crucially, that absorption requires the hedge legs to be *tradable right now*: the reversal of an idiosyncratic dislocation should be strong when the peer basket is active and weak-to-absent when peers are quiet, which is a new, falsifiable conditioning variable (peer activity excluding self) rather than the parent's own-volume shock. The child therefore makes the impulse horizon-symmetric — the realised 6-bar change of the industry-demeaned log multiple, matched to the fixed 6-bar offset that the parent's 2.5/20-minute EWMA impulse missed — and calibrates its loading with a robust pooled sign-slope estimator fitted directly on the scored quantity (cross-sectionally demeaned realised 6-bar forward return), separately inside cells of (peer activity) x (own activity). The edge persists because it is a capacity constraint, not a mispricing: repairing an idiosyncratic valuation dislocation consumes hedging capital and simultaneous peer liquidity, so it cannot be arbitraged away in the states where that liquidity is missing.
factors.name: Peer-activity-gated sign-slope horizon-symmetric peer-move reversal

factors.trading_idea: A name's own displacement is only *permanent* to the extent it agrees with contemporaneous public information, and the cleanest available proxy for public information is the traded (volume-backed) price move of its sector peers. Quote-only repricing (drift printed in near-zero-volume bars) that agrees with peers' traded move is genuine information diffusion into a name that simply has not traded yet, so it is delivered over the next few bars; quote-only drift that contradicts peers is inventory shading or stale-mid noise and carries little forward signal, while traded drift that contradicts peers is pure liquidity-demand impact and mean-reverts hardest. The parent's edge grew with horizon because it summed 30 bars of drift into a slow level; here both legs use a linearly-decaying recency kernel (newest bars weighted most) plus a 6-bar peer window, so the object measured is the *still-undelivered* piece of repricing, which resolves within roughly a minute. The edge survives arbitrage because harvesting it requires crossing the spread in names that are, by construction, not currently trading — the profit is bounded by that spread, so it is unattractive to size-constrained arbitrageurs. Falsified if the peer-ratification interaction adds nothing, i.e. quiet drift continues equally whether or not it agrees with peers' traded move and traded drift reverts equally regardless of concordance.
factors.name: Peer-ratified unconfirmed repricing permanence wedge

factors.trading_idea: Parent A found the right *state variable* — a name's leave-one-out deviation from its valuation-comparable basket (industry x size half), which dealers repair by consuming hedging capacity — but it measured the repair speed in calendar time, so its edge kept accruing out to 24 bars. Parent B found the right *clock*: impact and dislocations are worked off per unit of volume traded, and near-term volume is forecastable at 10-second resolution because arrival is self-exciting, so only the share deliverable inside the next 6 bars should be scored.
