The child fits each name's repair loading in calendar time, converts it into a per-unit-volume decay rate kappa (kappa = -log(1+beta) / average basket volume in the fit window), and re-projects it onto a Hawkes-style EWMA forecast of the *comparable basket's* volume over the next 6 bars, giving an explicit in-window repair probability theta = 1 - exp(-kappa * Vhat_6). The interaction is the edge: the same dislocation is a 6-bar trade only when the basket's business clock is currently running fast enough to burn through the repair budget inside the window — neither the dislocation alone (too slow, peaks at 24 bars) nor the delivery clock alone (applied to transient impact legs, no 6-bar IC) identifies that state.
factors.name: Volume-clock repair delivery of comparable-basket dislocation

factors.trading_idea: A slow-quoting name's mid is frozen between re-quotes, so when it finally moves, that single jump is the maker's whole response to the market move accumulated over the exact frozen interval — which lets us regress the jump on the interval-matched market return on the name's own renewal clock, with no lag-truncation bias. The parent assumed such names still *owe* catch-up and went long the owed amount; its IC was negative because the delivery event systematically OVERSHOOTS: a maker who re-prices after being stale skews defensively (it must price the risk that the silence hid informed flow), and when no flow materialises the excess revision is retracted over the next few bars. The child therefore measures the residual of the jump beyond its interval-matched market-implied size and trades the give-back, weighting most heavily the re-quotes that arrived with little or no trade volume (pure quote revision = no information to justify the excess) and only when a genuine market impulse existed for the maker to respond to. The edge persists because extracting it requires reconstructing per-name inter-update intervals, matching the market's accumulated return to each variable-length interval, and estimating a renewal-clock beta at 10-second granularity — the affected names are thin, mid-attention quotes that fast market makers will not warehouse inventory in.
factors.name: Interval-matched re-quote overshoot give-back (6-bar)

factors.trading_idea: A net price displacement can be produced two ways with opposite futures: (a) by many small, unusually *compressed* increments — the signature of an execution algorithm slicing a large metaorder, which keeps arriving and therefore keeps repricing; or (b) by a few violent increments drawn from the tails of the name's own recent increment distribution — a liquidity-withdrawal overshoot whose impact is largely transient and relaxes as depth refills. The parent measured only the magnitude/direction of fresh pressure, so it loaded mainly on regime (b) and its IC came out negative; the child separates the two regimes with a purely nonparametric two-sample construction: a Wilcoxon rank-sum location shift of the last 6 increments against the name's own trailing 120-bar increment distribution, multiplied by a centred Mood-type *scale-compression* state (rolling variance of the uniformized increments below its uniform benchmark 1/12). The edge survives arbitrage because identifying an in-progress sliced order requires conditioning on the *shape* of the increment distribution rather than the size of the move, and the agent whose child orders create the drift cannot profit from front-running itself; net-of-spread capacity inside a one-minute window is tiny.
factors.name: Rank-drift × increment-compression metaorder wedge

factors.trading_idea: Parent B showed that peer-relative dislocations in multiple space close at a rate that must be *measured* at the forecast lag rather than assumed, but it fed the pooled regression a single undecomposed dislocation — a mixture of flow-backed (permanent, Kyle-lambda-explained) repricing and flow-unbacked pricing error, whose forward dynamics have opposite signs and therefore partially cancel inside one slope. Parent A supplies the decomposition (a trailing per-name lambda, shrunk by the regression R-squared, applied to high-pass-filtered cumulative signed flow) but hard-codes the belief that the unbacked leg fades and the backed leg persists, and calibrates persistence only per name from a noisy lag-6 autocorrelation. The child uses A's split to create TWO orthogonalisable channels and lets B's industry-pooled, hierarchically shrunk bivariate OLS at exactly the 6-bar lag estimate both loadings jointly, so the relative fade/continuation weights of backed versus unbacked displacement are fitted per group and per regime. The interaction is the edge: the partial coefficient on unbacked dislocation, conditioned on the backed channel, is a clean estimate of book-refill reversion that neither a single-channel pooled slope (contaminated by information-driven moves) nor a fixed-sign per-name fade (mis-signed whenever the group is genuinely repricing) can recover.
factors.name: Kyle-split peer-multiple dislocation with pooled dual-channel horizon slopes

factors.trading_idea: Parent A shows that a peer spread in multiple space only mean-reverts when the peer group's multiples are tight enough for the comparables to price the same cash-flow claim; parent B shows that flow state matters but got its clock backwards. The correct microstructure reading of B's realized sign is transient-vs-permanent impact: while flow intensity is still elevated the dislocation is liquidity-demanding impact being actively absorbed by market makers, so it snaps back inside a minute, whereas once the burst has decayed and the spread has *not* closed, the repricing was informational and unopposed and keeps drifting. The child therefore uses flow intensity state to sign the dislocation (elevated intensity -> revert, quiet/exhausted intensity -> continue) and uses A's comparability gate to size each leg asymmetrically: tight within-industry multiple dispersion makes the reversion leg credible, while wide dispersion means the 'spread' is a business-mix artefact and the move is name-specific information, which amplifies the continuation leg. Neither parent has this edge alone — A cannot tell mispricing from information (so its edge only accrues over many minutes), and B has no way to know whether the spread it is timing is a genuine comparable relation.
factors.name: Comparability-Gated Flow-State Dislocation Switch

factors.trading_idea: A short-run displacement is either an execution still in progress or an execution already finished, and those two states have opposite one-minute futures: while a metaorder is working, order-flow self-similarity keeps pushing the price (so the move continues), whereas once it stops, the transient part of its impact relaxes back within tens of seconds (so the move reverts). The lifecycle phase is readable from the *shape* of the trailing path rather than its level: project the last 18 bars of vol-standardised returns onto discrete orthogonal polynomials — the 0th moment is the net displacement, the 1st moment is the trend in returns, i.e. the curvature of the price path — and project log-volume onto the same 1st-moment weight to get the flow trend. Displacement that is back-loaded (convex path) with rising activity is a live execution and should extend; displacement that is front-loaded (concave, saturating) with decaying activity is a completed execution whose transient impact should unwind. The edge survives because harvesting it means crossing the spread inside a minute for a profit of order the spread, which only participants already resting in the queue can do, and because it is a *nonlinear interaction* (displacement × path-shape) that no linear reversal or momentum book can span — naive reversal traders supply the continuation leg and get run over.
factors.name: Metaorder-lifecycle flip: path curvature × flow trend

factors.trading_idea: A 10-second bar's geometry contains two mechanically distinct pressure signals with opposite next-minute consequences: the wick asymmetry (how much of the excursion was rejected, i.e. aggressive size absorbed by passive depth and retraced) and the accepted body move (net displacement the market kept). Absorption is paid liquidity provision and snaps back, while accepted displacement is the visible footprint of a sliced parent order and continues; a single pooled fade averages the two and therefore only survives at slow horizons, which is exactly why the parent's |IC| peaked at 12 bars rather than the traded 6. The child stops guessing the routing with an ad-hoc rank gate and instead solves, per name, a trailing two-regressor normal-equation system whose target is the *realised 6-bar-ahead idiosyncratic move* (paired causally as X_{t-6} against the return over t-5..t), ridge-stabilised and empirical-Bayes shrunk toward the panel, so the loadings — and hence the sign — are calibrated at precisely the fixed forecast offset. The edge persists because the absorbed/accepted mix and each name's depth-replenishment speed drift continuously with participation, so the correct 60-second loading must be re-estimated from within-bar geometry rather than memorised, and the payoff is compensation for immediacy provision whose capacity is bounded by visible depth.
factors.name: Two-channel bar-geometry projection solved at the 6-bar offset

factors.trading_idea: A price change is only permanent if flow paid for it: Campbell-Grossman-Wang / Kyle logic says moves backed by unusual volume carry information and persist, while moves achieved with little or no traded volume are inventory- or quote-driven and are unwound as the intermediary re-establishes its position. The parent measured only the *persistent level* of up-vs-down impact asymmetry — a slow illiquidity characteristic that carried no stable direction out of sample (its interaction even scored with the opposite sign) — so the child keeps the sign-split elasticity estimate but uses it merely as the *baseline*: each bar's move-per-unit-flow is judged against that stock's own trailing elasticity for bars of that same direction, and the resulting excess ('flow deficit') weights the signed return before it is reversed. Side-conditioning matters because in a persistently asymmetric book an ordinary up-tick in a thin-ask name would otherwise be mislabelled as a vacuum move; conditioning on the side removes that static characteristic and leaves only the transient inventory shock. The edge survives arbitrage because each reversal is a few basis points — below single-name round-trip cost — and is only harvestable as a diversified cross-sectional overlay built from side-conditional 10-second elasticity baselines, while the structural cause (dealers absorbing uninformed liquidity demand and unwinding within a minute) recurs continuously.
factors.name: Side-conditional flow-deficit reversal

factors.trading_idea: Parent A showed that an owed systematic-catch-up kernel deficit and an idiosyncratic participation-weighted range-position snapback are complementary, routed by how much of a name's variance is market-explained; Parent B showed that whether owed mass can be *paid* inside a fixed 6-bar window depends on the name's own re-quote intensity lambda, but it amplified the deficit monotonically in lambda and its sign flipped. The reason is that information content in lambda is hump-shaped, not monotone: for lambda*H >> 1 (mid re-quotes every bar) the backlog is already arbitraged away and the measured 'deficit' is bid-ask/latency noise, while for lambda*H << 1 the backlog is real but is delivered after the evaluation offset (exactly why A's IC drifts out to 24 bars) — so a monotone lambda gain loads the deficit channel precisely where the fast reversal channel actually dominates, inverting the sign. The child therefore routes with a two-dimensional state: a clock-matching kernel exp(-0.5(log(lambda*H))^2) times market-R-squared rank feeds the kernel-deficit channel (backlog whose re-quote interval matches the horizon and whose path is common), while a fast-clock weight lambda*H/(1+lambda*H) times idiosyncratic variance share feeds the transient-impact snapback channel (liquidity cost can only revert if the quote moves), and the sign-concordance amplifier is itself scaled by the Poisson deliverable share 1-exp(-lambda*H) so the 'mechanical repricing lag' premium is only claimed where the mid can physically move inside the window.
factors.name: Clock-matched kernel backlog vs transient-impact snapback

factors.trading_idea: Within-bar displacement (where the mid closes inside the range it printed) mixes two liquidity regimes with very different relaxation clocks: a single impatient aggressor that eats visible depth in one burst creates a purely transient dislocation that passive depth repairs within seconds, while a sliced metaorder keeps re-creating the same displacement bar after bar so its dislocation only unwinds over minutes. The parent averaged both together, which is exactly why its information decayed slowly and peaked far beyond the fixed 6-bar offset. The child isolates the fast-clock component by (i) taking only the *innovation* in participation-scaled displacement relative to its own trailing 6-bar level — the part not explained by an ongoing, persistent push — and (ii) up-weighting bars whose traded size is concentrated in that single bar (high share of the last 6 bars' volume), the microstructural fingerprint of one-shot immediacy demand rather than order splitting; the sector cross-sectional mean is removed because basket/sector flow displacement is information and persists. Falsifiable: if the displacement *level* forecasts 6-bar reversal at least as well as its innovation, or if reversal strength is unrelated to volume concentration in the displacing bar, the mechanism is wrong. The edge survives arbitrage because harvesting it means posting passive size into the same thin book that a possibly-informed aggressor just cleared, so capacity is bounded by adverse selection and the state resets every ten seconds.
factors.name: Burst-concentrated displacement innovation snapback

factors.trading_idea: After a metaorder ends, Bouchaud-style transient impact relaxes along a decaying propagator g(tau), so the *fraction* of the remaining peer-relative displacement that unwinds over the next 6 bars is a steeply decreasing function of the relaxation's AGE, not of its level: a displacement whose extreme was hit two bars ago gives back a large slice of itself in the next minute, whereas an equally large but week-old displacement gives back almost nothing inside 6 bars. The parent traded the displacement level (gated only by a velocity sign), which is why its information accumulated slowly and peaked at 24 bars; the child instead estimates, per name and per bar, the elapsed age of the current relaxation (bars since the trailing signed extreme of the peer-relative displacement) and the retracement fraction already achieved, and forms the propagator-implied decay mass expected over exactly the next 6 bars, additionally clocked by the name's own recent trade activity (decay progresses in event time, so fast-trading names deliver more of it per clock bar). This edge should persist because harvesting it requires reconstructing an idiosyncratic path against a live comparable basket and warehousing inventory in a name whose latent state (push still live vs. relaxation under way, and how far it has progressed) is only probabilistically observable, with per-event profit small relative to that inventory and hedging risk.
factors.name: Relaxation-age matched peer impact decay mass

factors.trading_idea: The parent showed that peer spreads in multiple space contain a real signal, but its 5-minute EWMA dislocation measured a slow displacement, so the edge only accrued over minutes; a 60-second edge needs a mechanism whose resolution clock is itself ~60 seconds. That mechanism is stale-leg repair: when a name's valuation-matched comparables (same industry, same side of the industry median multiple) are being repriced on active trade flow while the name itself sits quiet, the peer-relative spread opens not because the name absorbed information but because its quote is stale — and stale quotes are repaired by the next few arriving orders, i.e. within seconds, not minutes. The repair is credible only for names that are genuinely central comparables (their live multiples sit close to the peer median in MAD units); peripheral-multiple names have a business mix that legitimately decouples, so their spreads should not snap back. The edge survives arbitrage because it requires simultaneously knowing the point-in-time comparable set in multiple space and the relative flow intensity of the two legs, and because capturing it means paying the spread on the illiquid, quiet leg — a cost that caps capacity rather than eliminating the signal.
factors.name: Multiple-space stale-leg catch-up within valuation tier

factors.trading_idea: Parent A says a slow-clientele name owes the market a beta-implied move after a shock; parent B says which side of the book hosts hidden resting liquidity that rejects probes. The missing link is *permeability*: an owed catch-up only gets paid if the path in the required direction is clear — if the concealed size sits exactly on the side the name must travel toward (upside probes repeatedly rejected while the wedge demands a rise), the impatient aggressor pays spread into hidden supply and price is faded instead, so the same wedge flips sign. The child therefore forms the signed catch-up wedge and multiplies it by a smooth permeability term equal to minus the tanh of the bridge-standardised excursion asymmetry measured *along the wedge's own direction*, so obstruction reverses the trade rather than merely muting it — a directional interaction neither parent can express (A has no book-side state, B has no owed-direction reference).
factors.name: Absorption-Permeability Gated Beta Catch-Up

factors.trading_idea: Parent B knows WHERE a name should trade (its industry-demeaned multiple gap versus a horizon-matched 6-bar anchor) but treats every gap as equally reverting; Parent A knows HOW the last few minutes of price path was manufactured (evenly-scheduled participation versus a concentrated burst, and how monotone the resulting path was) but has no valuation anchor telling it which way price should snap. The child conditions B's peer-relative snapback on A's realized (not declared) evidence about impact permanence: a relative gap built by evenly-spread, low-information participation that nonetheless walked the price monotonically is mostly transient price impact and should be faded hard, whereas a gap built by concentrated, bursty prints is informed repricing whose 'error' is real and should barely be faded (or mildly extrapolated). Crucially the evenness innovation is industry-demeaned before it is used as a gate, so the strongly common, diurnal component of volume-shape (the likely reason Parent A collapsed to a 94% correlation with an existing book factor) is purged and only the name-specific 'am I being worked evenly relative to my comparables?' state survives — an interaction neither parent can express alone, because one lacks the anchor and the other lacks the peer frame.
factors.name: Transiency-gated peer multiple snapback (evenness × path-efficiency)

factors.trading_idea: The parent showed that splitting a 10-second bar into its trade-driven body (close-open) and its pure quote-relocation seam (open minus previous close) isolates a real per-name state variable, but it imposed the sign of the response (always fade the body) and measured reciprocation with a lag-1 correlation whose clock (12 bars) did not match the 6-bar target. The child instead *estimates* the horizon-matched impulse response directly: for each name a trailing OLS of the realized standardized 6-bar peer-neutral return on the body push and the seam push *as they stood 6 bars earlier* gives two coefficients (b_body, b_seam) that say, in return units, how much of each leg is given back or extended over exactly the forecast horizon. Because a 6-bar R-squared is tiny, the raw coefficients are shrunk empirical-Bayes style toward the cross-sectional (pooled) coefficient with weight (R2 - p*H/n)+/((R2 - p*H/n)+ + p*H/n), i.e. the excess fit over the null R-squared implied by the effective number of non-overlapping observations — so only names whose response genuinely departs from the pooled response get an idiosyncratic tilt. The edge persists because harvesting it means posting passive size against possibly informed aggressive flow for a fraction of the spread in exactly the names whose measured, horizon-matched give-back is large: an inventory-risk-bearing market-making activity, not a lift-able directional mispricing; it is falsified if the cross-sectional dispersion of the estimated body/seam responses is pure estimation noise, in which case the shrinkage weight collapses and the child degenerates to the pooled response with no incremental value.
factors.name: Horizon-matched seam/body response, EB-shrunk

factors.trading_idea: If the price-impact map around a name's current price is asymmetric — a unit of traded volume moves the mid further upward than downward — then even perfectly unbiased order flow produces a positive expected mid displacement, because E[dP] = (lambda_up - lambda_down)/2 * flow: a purely convexity-driven, non-martingale drift toward the thin side of the book. I estimate the local diffusivity landscape as a two-sided Kyle coefficient (sum of normalised squared returns divided by sum of normalised traded volume) computed separately over bars whose *pre-bar* state was above versus below a fast 5-minute EWMA price anchor, so slow volatility trends and the symmetric 'extremes are volatile' effect cancel in the log-ratio, and the per-volume normalisation removes the possibility that one side is merely busier. Prediction: the log-ratio of upper-side to lower-side impact per unit volume predicts positive 60-second returns, and the effect must be concentrated where current flow is non-trivial (hence the flow-intensity scaling) — it is falsified if the drift is absent, or reverses, once impact asymmetry is measured per unit volume rather than per bar. It survives arbitrage because it is a conditional *second*-moment-per-unit-flow statistic invisible to first-moment flow/momentum signals, harvesting it means crossing the spread exactly on the thin (expensive, adverse-selection-prone) side so the sub-spread drift is unprofitable for latency players, and the depth asymmetry it exploits is continuously regenerated by market-maker inventory management rather than being permanently arbitraged away.
factors.name: Depth-asymmetry diffusivity gradient drift

factors.trading_idea: Parent B predicts, from flow geometry alone, how much of a bar's market move was mechanical basket over-push in name i — (inverse-turnover-rank minus beta-rank) x program-weighted market displacement — while Parent A measures where the name actually moved in the *precision metric* (the Mahalanobis coordinate that up-weights historically low-variance, basket-spread directions). The child regresses, cross-sectionally each bar, the precision-whitened 6-bar dislocation onto the mechanically predicted over-push: the signed R-squared of that regression is a per-bar *attribution trust* statistic that says whether this bar's tight-spread dislocations really are lining up with weight-per-depth mechanics, and it is fused with the program-footprint detector into one gate. The flow-attributed component of the whitened dislocation is then faded in proportion to trust (mechanical liquidity demand must relax), while the component orthogonal to the predicted push is ridden as continuation (Epps/staleness information diffusion). The interaction is the edge: B fades the predicted push blindly, so it pays for bars where the push never landed in the low-variance directions; A rides a residual that pools relaxation and diffusion, so its two regimes cancel — only the cross-sectional projection of A's whitened dislocation onto B's predicted push separates them and cleanly allocates the fade to the confirmed part and the continuation to the leftover.
factors.name: Basket over-push attribution trust: precision-dislocation split

factors.trading_idea: A name's live peer spread in multiple space (log P/B, P/S, P/OCF minus the industry median of the same multiple) widens because someone is working an order, not because comparables were repriced — so the spread keeps widening while the order-flow impulse is still self-exciting and snaps back only once the impulse burns out. Modelling flow as an exponentially-decaying (Hawkes-style) intensity, I measure how far the fast intensity has already decayed from its own recent peak: that decay fraction is an event clock which times the reversion, and it is what turns a slow multi-minute reversal into a signal that fires at a ~60-second offset. The child therefore signs the same peer-spread dislocation *by* flow state — continuation while intensity is still climbing, reversion once it has faded — with amplitude proportional to how large the burst was. The edge persists because the timing requires jointly monitoring peer-group multiple spreads and per-name 10-second flow intensity, a monitoring/latency constraint rather than a capital one, and its sub-minute capacity is too small for slower relative-value desks; it is falsified if the reversion strength is invariant to flow exhaustion (no sign flip between accelerating and decaying intensity states).
factors.name: Peer Multiple-Spread Flow-Exhaustion Clock

factors.trading_idea: Firms carrying a negative fundamental surprise have elevated adverse selection at the tape level: informed participants (short sellers, event specialists) are disproportionately active, market makers quote defensively and thinly, and each aggression relocates the mid more permanently — so their 10-second price changes carry information and show positive short-horizon autocorrelation. Firms with a positive surprise attract two-sided uninformed flow (retail accumulation against profit-taking supply), so their minute-scale moves are dominated by transient liquidity imbalance and snap back. The child therefore uses the *polarity* of the latest point-in-time earnings/revenue surprise — explicitly orthogonalised across the cross-section to size, dollar-liquidity and price level so it is not a repackaged illiquidity/tick-size effect — as the variable that sets whether the last 6 bars of idiosyncratic move should be faded or extended; it is a pure interaction, so it is nearly uncorrelated by construction with the plain reversal and plain PEAD factors the book already holds. The edge survives arbitrage because it requires joining a quarterly point-in-time fundamental to second-scale tape and the reversal leg is inventory-capacity limited, while pure microstructure reversal traders are indifferent to news polarity and so leave this conditional heterogeneity unhedged.
factors.name: Surprise-polarity reversal/momentum wedge

factors.trading_idea: Parent A's durable content is the split of 60-second mid displacement into a quiet-bar leg (pure quote-side repricing, no trades) and an active-bar leg deflated by the square-root impact law (displacement in excess of the volume backing it = unbacked taker push); Parent B's durable content is that a per-name horizon-matched response coefficient is far better estimated from sign concordance (Rice: rho = cos(pi*p_flip), tick-size-free and jump-robust) than from noisy Pearson moments of fat-tailed 10-second returns. The child estimates a *separate Rice cross-concordance response* for each channel — how often a completed 6-bar move agrees in sign with that channel's displacement six bars earlier — and trades only the cross-sectional *deviation* of those two coefficients, then applies them with reversed polarity: both parents' evaluations show that (trailing response x current displacement) is negatively predictive, which is exactly what a liquidity-episode maturity clock implies — a name whose channel push has *unusually* been followed through relative to peers is late in its metaorder/crowding episode and the next minute delivers the relaxation, whereas a name whose pushes have unusually snapped back has over-bounced and impact reasserts. The interaction is the edge: neither the common (cross-sectionally averaged) response, which the book's reversal factors already span, nor a fixed-polarity channel split survives; only the per-name, per-channel relative response measured with a sign estimator that does not blow up on jumps, read as a state of episode completion rather than a stationary parameter.
factors.name: Rice channel-response dispersion with exhaustion polarity

factors.trading_idea: The parent's ARMA(1,1) filter forced the transitory pricing error to relax as a single exponential, so almost all of its forecastable mass sat at lag 1 and had evaporated by the pinned 60-second offset (its |IC| indeed peaked at 1 bar and died at 6). But liquidity provision is not one inventory cycle: many market makers with different holding horizons superpose, and a superposition of exponentials with dispersed decay rates is a power law, so the relaxation kernel of the observed mid is hyperbolic, not geometric — i.e. returns behave like fractional Gaussian noise with a name-specific self-similarity exponent H, whose autocovariance decays as k^{2H-2} and therefore still carries signed mass at lag 6. I estimate H per name from the slope of log-variance against log-aggregation-scale over scales 2..32 bars (a many-observation, heavy-tail-robust estimator, unlike the ratio of two tiny autocovariances that flipped the parent's sign; large scales also purge the pure bid-ask-bounce MA(1) component that carries no 6-bar information), then apply the exactly horizon-matched analytic best linear predictor of the cumulative 6-bar return, w = Gamma_p^{-1} c, built in closed form from the fGn autocovariance. Crucially I subtract the predictor evaluated at the cross-sectional median H, so the signal is only the *heterogeneity* of relaxation roughness and is orthogonal by construction to the common short-term reversal loading that the existing book already spans; the edge persists because harvesting it means supplying the inventory a slow-decaying liquidity provider is trying to shed, and because identifying the exponent requires cross-scale estimation over hours of data for a per-name tilt that is unattractive to size-constrained arbitrageurs.
factors.name: fGn roughness-heterogeneity best-linear 6-step predictor

factors.trading_idea: The parent compressed a short window into permutation-invariant Herfindahl concentrations, which throws away the one thing that identifies causality inside the window: the ORDER in which variance and trade flow arrived. I replace concentration with the trailing time centroid (normalised first moment of mass over the last k bars) of squared returns and of traded volume; the wedge L = C_vol - C_var is a scale-free, unit-free measure of whether flow led price (L<0: a metaorder is walking the book, impact is still being paid, so the move continues) or price led flow (L>0: the mid was repriced first and reactive/chasing volume arrived only afterwards, i.e. the marginal buyer is the late chaser, so the move overshoots and snaps back). Interacting -L with the same-window volatility-normalised signed move therefore forecasts continuation-or-reversal over the next minute, and the edge persists because desks monitor realised vol, volume and autocorrelation as contemporaneous levels and almost never test the temporal ordering of variance mass against flow mass inside a sub-minute window; the statistic is also sector-neutralised so it cannot be harvested by size/sector beta exposures. Falsifiable: if forward 6-bar returns are unrelated to the interaction of signed move with flow-minus-variance centroid ordering (or if the sign is negative), the mechanism is wrong.
factors.name: Flow-vs-price timing centroid lead-lag wedge

factors.trading_idea: Model a name's peer-relative dislocation as a superposition of Ornstein-Uhlenbeck components with distinct relaxation times (fast quote/inventory noise, minute-scale metaorder impact, multi-minute clientele imbalance).  Under that superposition the expected return over a *fixed* h-bar window is the sum over components of (1 - exp(-h/tau_i)) times that component's current amplitude, so the covariance-optimal h=6 predictor is NOT the dislocation level (which the parent used, and which is dominated by the largest-amplitude slow component and therefore peaks at 24 bars) but an amplitude-preserving mixture of difference-of-exponential band components weighted by their own within-window decay fraction and divided by the name's 6-bar return volatility (an ex-ante information ratio, the right quantity to rank cross-sectionally).  The band decay fractions are additionally self-calibrated from a causal, cross-sectionally pooled trailing AR(6) persistence of each band, so the mixture adapts if a timescale stops relaxing.  The edge survives arbitrage because harvesting the fast bands requires paying spread/impact for a small per-event profit while the slow band pays only over many minutes; relative-value desks are compensated on the slow leg, leaving the horizon-matched blend at the fixed 60-second offset thinly contested.
factors.name: Timescale-band horizon-matched relaxation mixture

factors.trading_idea: The parent's mistake was diagnostic: precision-whitening deliberately up-weights the *lowest-variance* cross-sectional directions, and those relative-value directions are exactly the slowest to relax — which is why its |IC| peaked at 24 bars instead of 6. The fix is to stop assuming a single relaxation speed: each eigen-direction of the trailing cross-sectional covariance (market mode, sector/basket modes, relative-value modes, plus the pooled idiosyncratic residual) has its OWN 6-bar continuation-vs-giveback coefficient, and that coefficient flips sign with the state of basket execution — when the cap-weight-tilted program footprint is elevated, the flow-loaded modes overshoot and give back within a few bars, whereas in quiet states the same modes diffuse (Epps/staleness catch-up) and continue. So we measure, strictly on past data, the direct regression of each mode's next-6-bar score sum on its trailing-6-bar score sum, separately in high- and low-footprint states, and reconstitute a horizon-matched per-name forecast. The edge persists because the fade leg is literally supplying liquidity to live basket programs (compensated inventory risk), and because the estimator needs a rolling eigendecomposition plus state-split horizon-matched regressions on 10-second bars, which is capacity-limited and decays too fast to be arbitraged by slower participants.
factors.name: Program-state conditioned eigenmode relaxation (direct h6 projection)

factors.trading_idea: The parent showed that slow-clientele names owe an unfinished beta response after a market shock, but it treated the whole 6-bar backlog as due immediately, so its edge actually landed at ~12 bars. The absorption *schedule* is estimable causally from the term structure of scale-betas: because price discovery in inattentive names is asynchronous (Epps effect), the trailing beta measured on k-bar aggregated returns rises with k, and phi(k) = beta_k / beta_long is a direct estimate of the cumulative fraction of a market shock absorbed within k bars. Projecting only the kernel mass that is scheduled to arrive in the *next* 6 bars — sum over shock ages j of (phi(j+7) - phi(j+1)) * beta_long * m(t-j) — plus a modest weight on the residual deficit against that schedule, matches the signal's timing to the fixed 6-bar offset instead of leaking into 12+ bars. The edge survives arbitrage because it is payment for immediacy in names whose natural holders (income/insurance mandates) do not re-optimise intrabar: capturing it requires taking inventory in slow, wide names where per-event profit is small relative to spread, and the schedule itself must be estimated from long trailing windows rather than read off the tape.
factors.name: Scale-Beta Absorption Schedule: horizon-matched owed mass

factors.trading_idea: Under the square-root impact law a bar's contribution to repricing scales with the square root of its executed volume, and under Bouchaud's propagator the impact of volume executed several bars ago is largely transient and relaxes, while flow arriving in the last few bars is mostly unfinished and keeps arriving (order-flow imbalance is strongly autocorrelated at second scales). The child therefore measures a name's sqrt-volume-weighted directional consistency over a fast window matched to the forecast horizon and subtracts the same statistic over a slow window: what remains is *fresh* one-sided pressure net of pressure that has already been impacted and is decaying. This replaces the parent's noisy volume-CV 'metronome' gate (a fragile z-score of a z-score) with a single scale-free statistic that is bounded in [-1,1], robust to single giant prints (sqrt weighting, not linear), and needs no per-name normalisation. Falsifiable: if forward 6-bar returns do not load positively on fresh-minus-stale sqrt-weighted flow pressure — in particular if the fast and slow components carry the same IC sign — the propagator/unfinished-order interpretation is wrong; the edge survives arbitrage because it lives inside a one-minute window where net-of-spread capacity is tiny and its exploitation does not cancel the child orders still to come.
factors.name: Square-root-law weighted flow pressure freshness wedge

factors.trading_idea: Parent B's propagator decay increment is right in substance but wrong in clock: impact from already-executed flow relaxes in EVENT time, not wall-clock time, which is why its edge drifted out to 24 bars. I therefore age each past unit of signed flow by the number of (volume-normalised) events that have since elapsed, and I project the kernel forward not by 6 bars but by the Hawkes conditional expected event count over the next 6 bars — Parent A's baseline-plus-self-excitation intensity — so busy names get their relaxation pulled inside the fixed 6-bar offset while dormant names correctly predict almost nothing. Parent A's second contribution supplies the missing permanence test: over the untraded stretch since the last active bar I compute path efficiency versus its k^(-1/2) random-walk null and align its sign with the burst direction, because a quiet excursion that travels efficiently WITH the flow is genuine reservation-price relocation (permanent impact, nothing to harvest) whereas inefficient wobble or an efficient one-way retracement confirms the transient component is still outstanding and is already unwinding. The interaction is the edge: neither the flow-age profile alone (which cannot tell permanent from transient impact) nor the quiet-path geometry alone (which has no idea how much impact is owed, and whose standalone IC is near zero) knows both how much snapback is pending and whether it will actually be paid within the next six bars.
factors.name: Event-clock propagator relaxation gated by quiet-path efficiency

factors.trading_idea: Parent A shows that displacement printed in near-zero-volume bars (pure quote repricing) continues while displacement paid for with volume decays, but it cannot tell a genuine unpaid-for revision from a stale-mid artefact; Parent B shows that the arrival ordering of flow around a move carries information but has no unconditional edge on its own, and its realized sign says that flow arriving AFTER the displacement — not before — is the informative one. The child conditions Parent A's quiet/traded state on Parent B's arrival-ordering statistic with the corrected direction: a quiet repricing that is *witnessed* by trade arrival in the next one-two bars is a maker's shaded quote that liquidity takers have now validated, so it keeps drifting, whereas a quiet repricing that no one ever trades against is stale-mid noise that snaps back; symmetrically, a high-volume displacement whose flow was fully spent at or before the print is an exhausted metaorder whose temporary impact decays, while one where flow keeps arriving afterwards is a metaorder still working and continues. The interaction carries edge neither parent has because it removes the stale-quote contamination that caps Parent A's short-horizon IC (that is exactly why A's IC only matured at 12-24 bars) and gives Parent B's ordering statistic the regime baseline it lacked, so the signal is concentrated in displacements 10-80 seconds old and matches the fixed 6-bar offset.
factors.name: Witnessed quiet repricing vs exhausted traded impact

factors.trading_idea: Parent A shows that the part of a minute-scale mid move that executed flow can explain (via a per-name no-intercept impact coefficient lambda) is transient and decays, while the flow-unexplained residual is a quote-setter belief revision that keeps propagating; Parent B shows that a repricing path only keeps walking when it is a *grind* (sign-persistent relative to the Rice/Gaussian null arccos(rho)/pi) rather than a magnitude-concentrated jump. The child keeps Parent A's regression decomposition intact and uses Parent B's Rice sign-flip gap purely as a slow, per-name *state variable*: the flow-unexplained (permanent) leg is followed in grind-state names and flipped to fade in jump-state names, while the flow-explained (transient) leg is always faded. The interaction carries edge neither has alone because Parent A's permanent-component leg is contaminated by exactly the failure mode a Rice gate detects — a single stale-mid gap in a thin tape is 'unexplained' by flow but snaps back rather than propagating — and Parent B's grind/jump null gains a mechanically meaningful object to condition (impact-residual displacement) instead of raw drift, with a cross-sectional rank gate replacing Parent B's tuned constants and dual subsequence estimators so it does not overfit.
factors.name: Grind-gated permanent vs transient displacement split

factors.trading_idea: Parent A shows that a smoothed one-minute displacement continues when it was *expensive* (much volume per unit of realised path, and it landed on a level the mid keeps revisiting, i.e. thick book) and reverts when it was free — but it applies that liquidity-cost gate to the raw move, which on many bars is mostly mechanical basket/program footprint rather than name-specific depth consumption; on those bars volume-per-path measures index-rebalance turnover, not information, so the gate is diluted. Parent B built exactly the machinery to isolate that mechanical part (predicted over-push = weight-per-depth-minus-beta wedge times the market displacement) but routed it the wrong way: its realised IC contradicted its fade hypothesis, which is what metaorder mechanics predict — over the next six bars a program that has already pushed a name is *still executing*, so the attributed push persists and only unwinds long after completion. The child therefore splits each name's smoothed displacement cross-sectionally each bar into a basket-attributed component (fitted on beta·M and wedge·M) and an orthogonal idiosyncratic remainder, relays the attributed component in proportion to the per-bar attribution trust (R² of that regression, i.e. how program-dominated the bar is), and applies A's liquidity-cost gate exclusively to the idiosyncratic remainder, down-weighting it when the bar is program-dominated and the depth reading is contaminated. The interaction is the edge: A cannot tell which part of a move its cost gate is licensed to judge, and B had no depth/cost reading at all to grade the remainder it left over.
factors.name: Basket-attribution split, cost-gated displacement relay

factors.trading_idea: The parent asserted a sign flip gated on an 'impact R-squared' whose regressor was the SAME bar's return sign times sqrt(volume) — so its beta was positive by construction and its R-squared merely measured |return|-vs-sqrt(volume) coupling, carrying no information about whether flow actually predicts future mid moves; that is why the asserted conditional sign realised ~zero IC and contradicted its declared direction. The child stops asserting signs and estimates them: each bar's volatility-standardised mid return is split continuously into a trade-backed part (weight v/(vbar+v)) and an unbacked quote-drift part, and a per-name, ridge-regularised two-coefficient response kernel is fitted causally on horizon-matched, NON-overlapping pairs (predictor dated t-6, realised 6-bar return ending at t), then empirical-Bayes shrunk toward the cross-sectional median coefficient by its own estimated standard error. Falsifiable claims: the fitted loading on unbacked drift should be systematically more negative than the loading on flow-backed drift (quote wobble snaps back, trade-backed relocation persists), and the shrunk forecast should have positive IC at 6 bars even after the common short-run reversal component is cross-sectionally removed. The edge persists because this conditional mean is name- and regime-specific (tick-size binding, maker mix, participation rate) and decays as those change, so it must be re-estimated online — a published static coefficient is arbitraged away, while a trailing estimator has limited capacity and stays noisy for anyone not maintaining it.
factors.name: Backing-weighted self-calibrated response kernel

factors.trading_idea: A price move made without traded volume has two possible sources that the parent factor lumped together: a single dealer relocating its own quotes to manage inventory (idiosyncratic, mechanically unwound within a minute) and information arriving between trades — macro/index ticks, sector news — which repositions the quotes of many names simultaneously with no single-name volume and is permanent. These are separable at 10-second frequency by the cross-sectional co-movement of the flow *deficit* itself: I build each bar's log-excess move-per-unit-flow against the stock's own side-conditional trailing elasticity, accumulate it with an exponential recency kernel matched to the ~30-second dealer unwind clock, then remove the trailing-beta projection of that accumulated deficit on its cross-sectional mean, so only the genuinely idiosyncratic (inventory) component is faded. The edge persists because each unwind is worth a few basis points — below single-name round-trip cost — and because it is a structural consequence of intermediaries absorbing uninformed liquidity demand and re-levelling quotes, which recurs continuously; it is only harvestable as a diversified overlay built from per-stock, side-conditional elasticity baselines.
factors.name: Breadth-purged flow-deficit inventory snapback

factors.trading_idea: The parent measured grind-vs-jump through a slow 20-minute Rice/Gaussian sign-flip statistic, so its information only accumulated at 12-24 bar horizons; here the same economic split is made *event-locally* and with a second, orthogonal witness. Using Mancini's threshold decomposition against a jump-robust bipower scale, the last 60 seconds of mid-price change is split into large-increment (jump) and small-increment (diffusive) parts, and the *trade volume that accompanied that minute* decides which part to trust: a large mid displacement executed on light volume is a quote gap into thin depth (a liquidity vacuum), which snaps back as depth refills within roughly a minute, whereas small same-signed increments accompanied by heavy volume are the footprint of a sliced parent order that is still working and therefore continue. The signal is a convex blend, w_grind * (normalised diffusive drift) - w_vacuum * (normalised jump drift), with the weights a logistic function of volume participation relative to the name's own 15-minute norm. It survives arbitrage because the profitable leg is exactly the low-participation, thin-depth state in which capacity is small, and because desks condition drift on volume levels but almost never on a threshold-based jump/diffusive *decomposition* of the drift itself; it is falsified if the participation gate adds nothing (equal weights) or if jump-part drift continues rather than reverts at 6 bars.
factors.name: Threshold jump vs grind split gated by trade participation

factors.trading_idea: Both parents declared that an un-absorbed systematic dislocation D = (Dimson beta x 6-bar market return) - (own 6-bar return) is a catch-up claim to be collected, and both realised the OPPOSITE sign, because at 10-second granularity genuine stale-quote catch-up is delivered within 1-3 bars (parent A's |IC| peaked at 3 bars) so nothing mechanical is left to harvest at the fixed 6-bar offset; what remains at t+1..t+6 is the persistence of the one-sided metaorder flow that produced the divergence in the first place, i.e. relative-return continuation, not reversal. The child therefore stops declaring the sign and instead estimates it: parent A's distributed-lag machinery is re-pointed from the market return onto parent B's dislocation variable, folding trailing loadings of vol-normalised own returns on D at lags 1..6 into a single horizon-matched response coefficient kappa (exactly the offset the run scores), and parent B's participation-shape state (volume-share entropy innovation: even/scheduled vs. bursty/sweep) is used to estimate that kernel SEPARATELY in the two states, so the same gap is collected where the data say gaps close and extended where the data say they extend. The interaction carries edge neither parent has because the per-name, per-state impulse response is the object that decides polarity, delivered mass is capped by A's Poisson re-quote/trade-clock share 1-exp(-lambda*6) (a gap only moves on bars the name actually prints), and the state-kernel disagreement |kappa_even - kappa_burst| is a falsifiable trust statistic that switches the factor off when participation shape carries no incremental information about closure.
factors.name: Self-calibrated beta-gap response kernel, participation-state conditional (6-bar)

factors.trading_idea: The parent's realized sign says the truth is the opposite of its story: minute-scale mid drift that arrives *with* trade volume reverts, while displacement that arrives with little or no trade continues. That is exactly the Bouchaud/Obizhaeva-Wang propagator picture — the part of a move that was paid for by executed flow is mostly *transient* impact and decays as depth replenishes over the next ~minute, whereas a mid revision with no inventory transfer is a pure belief update by quote setters (Hasbrouck's permanent component) and, because it still has to propagate to slower participants, it continues. I therefore estimate a per-name no-intercept price-impact coefficient λ from a trailing regression of volatility-standardized returns on tick-rule signed sqrt-volume, split the last 6 bars of displacement into a flow-explained (transient) and an unexplained (permanent) part, go long unexplained minus explained, and shrink the whole split by the trailing R² of that impact regression — the decomposition is only meaningful in names where flow magnitude actually explains return magnitude. It survives arbitrage because the profitable leg is the thin-tape, untraded-repricing state where capacity is tiny, and because desks typically apply one global lambda rather than a per-name, precision-weighted origin-fit impact coefficient.
factors.name: Flow-explained vs unexplained displacement (no-intercept impact split, R² trust gate)

factors.trading_idea: Parent A produces a timing-domain state variable — where a name sits on the unit circle relative to the cross-sectional mean field, whose entrainment term R·sin(psi−theta) says whether the name is a phase laggard or a phase leader — but it hard-codes the sign of the coupling K, which is why its edge only appeared far from the fixed 6-bar offset. Parent B contributes a scale-free, jump-robust way to *learn* a coefficient from signs alone (Rice: rho = cos(pi·p_flip)), but it applied it as an autocorrelation of a noisy series with itself, so bid-ask bounce contaminated estimator and regressor jointly and flipped its realized direction. The child fixes both: it estimates, per name, the trailing sign-concordance between the entrainment term as of the *start* of a 6-bar block and the idiosyncratic displacement realized *over* that block, and inverts Rice to get a per-name coupling gain rho_ent; the forecast is rho_ent · (current standardised entrainment term). Because predictor and target are built from disjoint bars, the Roll-bounce bias that reversed Parent B cancels, and the interaction carries edge neither parent has alone: the cross-section of coupling gains (some names are entrained toward the pack, others are the pack's front-runners and repel it) is exactly what a single common reversion/lead-lag parameter cannot capture at the fixed 60-second horizon.
factors.name: Rice-calibrated Kuramoto entrainment gain

factors.trading_idea: Parent B established that a 3-bar dislocation from a valuation-matched, beta-hedged peer basket snaps back over the next minute, but it imposed the conditioning by hand (multiply by hedge R-squared, divide by 1+relative volume); parent A tried to *learn* the volume-state conditioning but did so per name, so the estimated propagator loadings were noise and the edge vanished out of sample. The child keeps B's peer-hedged residual impulse as the signal and A's transient-vs-permanent volume-state logic as the conditioner, but estimates the response surface *pooled across the cross-section* on a trailing window: a no-intercept slope of the realised, non-overlapping forward 6-bar hedged residual on the lagged 3-bar hedged impulse, computed separately in each cell of a 2x2 grid (heavy vs light 3-bar volume shock) x (hedgeable vs poorly-hedgeable, i.e. above/below median trailing hedge R-squared), each cell shrunk toward the all-observations pooled slope. The interaction carries edge neither parent has: pooling gives thousands of observations per cell so the state-dependent reversion speed is measurable rather than fitted noise (A's failure), and it lets the tape decide *how much* a heavy-volume, well-hedged dislocation reverts instead of assuming B's fixed damping shape — including switching off or reversing the snapback in the light-volume 'pure quote revision' cell where impact is permanent.
factors.name: Pooled state-response valuation-matched peer snapback

factors.trading_idea: Transient microstructure noise (bid-ask bounce, fleeting quotes, inventory-driven skewing) has a *bounded* amplitude set by the spread, whereas informational repricing is unbounded; therefore the conditional mean of the forward return given the recent displacement is non-monotone — it fades moderate moves and is flat (or continues) for large ones. Standard rank-based reversal factors apply a monotone transform to the recent return and so mis-specify both tails; a redescending M-estimator score psi(z)=z·exp(-z^2/8) on the horizon-matched, own-noise-normalised idiosyncratic displacement isolates only the bounded, revertible part and by construction refuses to trade jumps. The reversal gain is then self-calibrated by each name's ordinal sign-flip rate over a slow 300-bar window: a distribution-free (heteroskedasticity- and jump-robust) measure of how bounce-dominated its price series is, so names whose increments alternate get a large fade and names whose increments run get a suppressed or reversed one. The edge persists because harvesting the bounded component requires supplying liquidity at exactly the moments when adverse selection is possible — capacity-limited compensation to market makers — and because the profitable region is deliberately the one where the informational (arbitrageable) content is smallest.
factors.name: Redescending bounce-gain calibrated transient fade

factors.trading_idea: Treat each name's peer-neutral price path as the workload of a single-server queue: standardized bar increments are 'arrivals' and the book's routine noise-absorption capacity is the 'service rate', so the unabsorbed directional pressure follows a two-sided Lindley recursion U_t=max(0,U_{t-1}+x_t-k), D_t=max(0,D_{t-1}-x_t-k) — a reflected random walk whose hard boundary at zero makes it un-spannable by any linear filter of returns. A queue only becomes non-empty when increments are one-sided *beyond* the name's own noise scale, which is precisely the signature of a live sliced metaorder rather than of quote flicker, so a non-empty and still-filling workload should keep pushing price the same way over the next minute, while the reflection event (queue emptying) marks the end of that push. Two path-dependent state variables condition the trade: the Pollaczek–Khinchine traffic intensity rho/(1-rho) (fraction of recent bars spent in a busy period — high traffic means slow clearing and long residual workload) and the average relative volume accumulated *during the current busy period* (confirming the workload was built by traded flow, not by an unbacked quote walk). The edge persists because monetising it means joining the same side as possibly-informed aggressive flow and paying the spread while carrying the risk of an abrupt reflection; the signal is also active only a small fraction of the time (state-contingent, low capacity), which caps how much arbitrage capital can crowd it.
factors.name: Reflected-workload (Lindley) flow-confirmed continuation

factors.trading_idea: Parent A shows that the doubly-orthogonalised residual of a name against its valuation-matched peer kernel (peer-beta hedged, then purged of the neighbourhood's own residual factor) mean-reverts on a ~1-minute clock, but it treats every residual tick alike; Parent B shows that price moves printed in (near-)zero-volume bars are quote repricing that continues while moves paid for with aggressive volume are transient impact that decays. The child decomposes the *purged name-specific residual* into a quiet-bar component and a traded-bar component and lets hedgeability (trailing R-squared of the name on its valuation basket) arbitrate between them: the traded-bar residual impulse is faded with weight R-squared, because only a cheaply hedgeable name gets its inventory pressure closed against the basket within seconds, while the quiet-bar residual drift is *extrapolated* with weight (1 - R-squared), because a poorly hedgeable name's silent quote shading is idiosyncratic information no relative-value desk can cheaply trade away. The interaction carries edge neither parent has: Parent A fades all residuals including the informative quiet ones (diluting IC), Parent B's quiet/traded split is contaminated by peer-basket and valuation-tier common moves that are neither inventory pressure nor private repricing, and only after the peer purge does the sign flip between the two volume states become clean at the fixed 6-bar offset.
factors.name: Hedgeability-split quiet repricing vs traded snapback in peer-purged residual

factors.trading_idea: Parent A estimates a per-name block autocorrelation from adjacent-block sign concordance (rho = cos(pi*p_flip)) on the *raw* 6-bar displacement — but that displacement is a mixture of two mechanically opposite channels: weight-proportional basket/program over-push, which relaxes and therefore manufactures sign flips (biasing rho negative and inverting the forecast, which is exactly why A's declared direction was contradicted), and sliced metaorder flow, which continues. Parent B knows how to identify the mechanical part (cap-weight-per-unit-depth elasticity wedge times the cap-weighted market move) but fades every push with one common intensity and has no per-name persistence estimate. The child projects each name's standardised beta-purged 6-bar displacement onto its own program-push proxy with a trailing self-calibrated loading, fades only that attributed projection, and applies Rice sign-concordance persistence *only to the purged residual*, where sign flips are no longer contaminated by push-relax cycles. The interaction is the edge: rho measured on the purged channel is a correctly-signed, dispersion-rich continuation coefficient that neither raw-displacement Rice (A) nor a uniform program fade (B) can produce.
factors.name: Basket-attributed vs Rice-persistent channel split

factors.trading_idea: A short-horizon price dislocation is the concession paid to liquidity providers who absorbed a net order imbalance, and it is repaid only as that inventory is worked off by the normal arrival of offsetting flow — so the predictable reversal has a *size* and a *clock*, both observable. The size is the mid minus the flow-weighted price at which the recent directional volume actually executed (the providers' mark-to-market loss); the clock is the accumulated BVC-signed imbalance divided by the name's normal per-bar volume, which is an estimate in bars of how long clearing takes, so only the fraction min(1, 6/H) of the concession is expected to be repaid by t+6. Conventional reversal signals standardise a raw return by realised volatility and discard the clearing-clock dimension entirely (execution algos likewise normalise flow by ADV, which cancels exactly this quantity), so the horizon-matched weighting is left un-arbitraged. It is falsifiable: the min(1,6/H) weighting must beat the unweighted dislocation, the loading on the dislocation must be negative, and the concordance gate (imbalance sign aligned with dislocation sign, i.e. a concession actually paid rather than a hidden absorber) must add IC.
factors.name: Clearing-clock matched concession repayment

factors.trading_idea: A bar's range-normalised shadow asymmetry is the *rejected* (transient) part of the price excursion a probing aggressor produced; its forward sign is not universal but depends on whether the flow that caused it is still alive. Under self-excited (Hawkes-like) order flow, when trade intensity is still accelerating relative to the name's own slower baseline the metaorder is still working, so the rejected excursion is merely transient impact decaying inside the bar and the mid resumes the probe direction; when intensity is decaying, the aggressor is exhausted and the queue refills (Obizhaeva-Wang resilience), so the rejected excursion is genuine absorption and the mid snaps back against the probe. The parent pooled both regimes and therefore printed the exhaustion (reversal) sign; conditioning the same volume-weighted excursion statistic on intensity acceleration should restore a signed, one-minute-horizon edge. It resists arbitrage because the continuation leg requires paying spread into an active, possibly informed sweep and the exhaustion leg requires posting size against a just-cleared queue, and the state is only valid for a handful of 10-second bars.
factors.name: Excursion rejection switched by trade-intensity acceleration

factors.trading_idea: Inside a fresh 90-second one-sided excursion, the bounce back off the extreme is either paid for by real two-sided volume or it is a hollow drift through an emptied book. Splitting the window at the extreme bar and comparing the price move *per share* on the retracement leg with the price move per share on the excursion leg (lambda_back / lambda_out) measures exactly that: a retracement that is large yet cost almost no volume is liquidity-provider inventory being handed back into a vacuum, not new information, so it fails and price resumes the original excursion direction over the next minute; a retracement that absorbed heavy volume is genuine repricing and tends to keep going. This is why the parent's IC came out with the opposite sign to its hypothesis: its 'completion clock' (flow intensity off its peak plus price lifted off the extreme) only fires *after* the transient impact has already been repaid inside the measurement window, so what remains is the permanent component plus the overshoot of a hollow bounce, i.e. continuation, not snapback. The edge should persist because it requires joint leg-resolved volume/geometry measurement at 10-second resolution, lives for ~1 minute, is capacity-limited by the very thinness it exploits, and is contrarian to the crowded 'buy the spike low' reversal prior.
factors.name: Unbacked-retracement leg-lambda resumption

factors.trading_idea: Transient price impact relaxes in *bet time*, and Kyle-Obizhaeva market-microstructure invariance says the bet-arrival rate of a name scales as (price x share volume x volatility)^(2/3), so the calendar-time relaxation rate is rho_i = a*(W_i/W_med)^(2/3).  Under an exponential relaxation kernel the stock of still-standing transient displacement is D_t = sum_s exp(-rho*s)*push_{t-s}, and the part of it that will actually be worked off inside the FIXED 6-bar window is exactly (1 - exp(-6*rho))*D_t — a delivery factor that is small both for very slow names (nothing relaxes in 60s) and for very fast names (the displacement already relaxed before t), unlike the parent's monotone 'owed-stock' gate which loaded on the fastest names where the payback had already happened.  Sector-common displacement is uninformed basket overpush and is treated as fully transient, while name-idiosyncratic displacement is only ~1/3 transient (the metaorder-impact-decay stylised fact), so the signal is the negative of the invariance-weighted, in-window-deliverable transient stock.  The edge survives arbitrage because harvesting it requires jointly estimating a per-name activity-scaled relaxation rate and separating common from idiosyncratic displacement on a 10-second grid, and the positions it takes are exactly the high-turnover states where capacity is capped by the very impact cost being predicted.
factors.name: Invariance bet-clock in-window transient payback

factors.trading_idea: The parent's realized sign says the excursion side is followed, not rejected, so re-read the geometry: on 10-second mid bars a volume-heavy excursion that retraces inside the bar is transient impact decaying (the aggressor cleared the offer, the quote refilled a tick wider, and the mid fell back toward its start) — not hidden supply defending a level. Because trade arrivals are self-exciting, the remaining child orders of the same metaorder keep arriving, so the permanent component of that overshoot is reasserted over the next minute and price drifts toward the side that was probed. The child therefore (i) weights each probe continuously by sqrt of its volume-intensity ratio rather than a lossy binary median gate — square-root impact law makes informativeness scale with sqrt(size) — and (ii) adds a genuinely new conditioning variable: whether the aggressor is STILL active now, measured as a fast volume-intensity EWMA relative to its own trailing distribution; stale probes whose flow has died should carry no drift. The edge survives arbitrage because harvesting it means racing an active aggressor into already-depleted depth and paying spread, and the state fully refreshes every ten seconds; it is falsified if the excursion-side sign is negative at 6 bars, or if the persistence conditioner is irrelevant (dead-flow probes drift as much as live-flow probes).
factors.name: Transient-impact overshoot with self-excited follow-through

factors.trading_idea: At a 10-second clock the contemporaneous covariance of a stock panel is Epps-attenuated by asynchronous quoting, so the low-variance eigen-directions that a naive precision matrix amplifies are partly a *staleness artefact* rather than genuinely tight relative-value spreads; correcting the covariance with the lag-1 cross-covariance (Sigma0 + Sigma1 + Sigma1^T, the Hayashi-Yoshida / Newey-West synchronisation term) rebuilds the metric that a real relative-value trader would use. The same lag-1 matrix supplies, for free, the state variable the parent could only proxy with rank(-log turnover) - rank(beta): the antisymmetric part row-sums measure directly whether a name *lags* the panel (its returns are predicted by peers' past moves) or *leads* it. A whitened dislocation in a laggard is unresolved lead-lag catch-up and therefore closes (the deviation mean-reverts), whereas the identical dislocation in a leader is fresh idiosyncratic information that peers have yet to follow, so the leader's own move continues over the next few bars. The edge survives arbitrage because it requires estimating and regularising a full lagged cross-covariance matrix on a 10-second panel, and the relative-value legs it points to are thin, high-impact and low-capacity — single-name latency arbitrageurs do not trade them.
factors.name: Lead-lag-corrected precision dislocation, split by measured lead/lag role

factors.trading_idea: Intraday risk and index flow is executed in *baskets* built on published fundamental characteristics (cheapness, quality, size), so the characteristic-mimicking portfolios themselves acquire minute-scale return autocorrelation while individual constituents, especially thinly quoted ones, update their mids with a lag. I therefore build per-bar characteristic-mimicking factor returns by cross-sectional weighting of vol-normalised returns on point-in-time fundamentals, accumulate them over the last two minutes, and compute for each name the gap between the move its own loadings imply and the move it actually printed; the part of that gap which is *not* a linear function of the name's own realised move (removed by a per-bar cross-sectional projection) is the style catch-up that plain short-horizon reversal factors cannot span. The edge persists because capturing it requires trading many names simultaneously for a few basis points each while paying the spread, exactly the trade basket-flow providers are already saturating, and because staleness is concentrated in names whose quotes are cheapest to leave un-updated. It is falsifiable: if intraday characteristic-basket returns are serially unpredictable, or if constituent mids re-price instantaneously, the projected residual gap carries no forward information and the IC collapses to zero.
factors.name: Characteristic-style basket catch-up residual

factors.trading_idea: Kyle's lambda is by construction the coefficient of the *permanent* (information) component of price impact, so the part of a 60-second mid displacement that a name's own trailing lambda attributes to aggressive signed flow is efficient-price revision and must not be faded; the parent mislabelled it as transient, which is exactly why its realized IC came out with the opposite sign. What is left over — mid displacement with no trades behind it — is Hasbrouck's pricing error: fleeting quotes, queue flicker and inventory-driven quote skew that revert as the book refills, so its reversal is the true source of edge. The child therefore (i) subtracts the flow-explained permanent part, shrinking that attribution by the trailing R-squared of the return-on-flow regression so noisy lambdas cannot over-subtract, and (ii) scales the resulting fade by each name's own horizon-matched non-persistence 1 - rho_6, the trailing lag-6 autocorrelation of its pricing-error series, so names whose unbacked displacement is empirically sticky get no bet. The edge survives arbitrage because it pays a fraction of the spread per event, requires per-name impact and reversion calibration, and is capacity-limited rather than informationally scarce. Falsified if the flow-explained component reverts as strongly as the residual (decomposition useless), or if the reversal IC is flat in 1 - rho_6 (the persistence scaling adds nothing).
factors.name: Flow-attributed pricing-error reversal, horizon-matched persistence scaled

factors.trading_idea: Basket/program flow allocates dollars by capitalisation weight, so its displacement of name i scales with weight-per-unit-depth (inverse dollar turnover, kappa), whereas information moves names by beta; the parent proxied the mechanical push with a heuristic program detector times the market return, which gives the whole cross-section only one noisy degree of freedom per bar. Instead I *measure* the mechanical push directly: each bar I run a two-characteristic cross-sectional regression of returns on beta and on kappa orthogonalised to beta, so the slope lambda_kappa,t IS the realised return of the pure weight/depth price-pressure factor — it is non-zero exactly when a basket program is executing and it carries its own sign, no detector needed. Because a single-bar cross-sectional slope is noisy, I shrink each lambda_kappa,t by its own cross-sectional precision (t^2/(t^2+2), a James-Stein-style trust gate), accumulate the shrunk slopes over bars t-7..t-2 (past the fast Epps/staleness catch-up), and fade that accumulation in proportion to each name's own orthogonalised elasticity loading, amplified by how much abnormal dollar volume the name actually absorbed during the same window. The edge persists because market-neutral books hedge index exposure with beta, leaving the beta-orthogonal weight/depth component of mechanical basket impact unhedged, and harvesting it requires simultaneous many-name execution inside a one-minute window; it is falsifiable in that fading the beta slope lambda_beta (news) must NOT work, dropping the precision shrinkage or the absorbed-flow gate must reduce IC, and inverting the sign must lose.
factors.name: Fama-MacBeth price-pressure factor return, precision-shrunk elasticity snapback

factors.trading_idea: Parent A splits the recent price displacement into a quiet-bar (maker repricing) leg and a traded-bar (taker impact) leg and trades the wedge, but it cannot tell WHEN each leg resolves, so its edge leaks out to 24 bars; Parent B knows how to time resolution via a non-parametric zero-crossing clock, but applies one clock to an undecomposed deviation that mixes both mechanisms with opposite dynamics. The child decomposes the linearly-decayed displacement into its quiet and traded components exactly (the two decayed sums add back to the total), then estimates a SEPARATE crossing clock for each component and gives each leg the kernel its own economics demands: the quiet/maker leg is a continuation trade so it is weighted by the slow-clock logistic T_q/(T_q+h) (the repricing has not yet retraced by t+6), while the traded/taker leg is a transient-impact reversal so it is weighted by the horizon-match kernel sech^2(0.5 ln(T_a/h)) = 4T_a h/(T_a+h)^2, peaking exactly when the impact relaxation period equals the fixed 6-bar horizon. Both legs are then multiplied by A's smooth maker/taker disagreement gate, and the traded leg is deflated by sqrt(relative volume) so only displacement in excess of the square-root impact law is faded. The interaction is the edge: a fast-relaxing traded push is only tradable at 6 bars if it actually oscillates on a ~6-bar clock, and a quiet repricing is only worth chasing if the name's quiet channel does not mean-revert inside the holding window — neither parent can condition a leg on that leg's own clock.
factors.name: Channel-clock matched maker/taker disagreement wedge

factors.trading_idea: The parent detected basket/program bars and then applied a *common* market displacement to a *static* per-name elasticity-minus-beta wedge, so it never looked at whether a given name actually got mispushed — its cross-section was one fixed tilt scaled by a scalar. The child measures the displacement directly: during bars whose cross-sectional dollar-volume allocation tilts toward the capitalisation-weight vector (a basket footprint), a name's beta-purged residual return is attributed to mechanical impact only when its sign agrees with the sign predicted by that name's own mechanical elasticity kappa_i = index weight x square-root-law impact coefficient (|ret| per sqrt traded dollars) times the market move; illiquid/high-kappa names should be over-pushed and revert, liquid/low-kappa names should be under-pushed and catch up. Fading only the footprint-concordant part of the residual keeps the liquidity-provision premium and discards idiosyncratic news, and the edge survives arbitrage because market-neutral books hedge index exposure with beta (leaving the weight/depth heterogeneity of basket impact un-hedged) and harvesting it requires simultaneous many-name execution inside a one-minute window. Falsifiable: the concordance gate must beat the ungated residual reversal, kappa = weight x sqrt-law impact must beat the parent's inverse-turnover proxy, program weighting must beat equal weighting, and inverting the sign must lose.
factors.name: Program-footprint concordant elasticity residual repayment

factors.trading_idea: Parent B established empirically that at a 6-bar offset short-run mid displacement is reversal-dominant, and Parent A established that the part of a pin-break impulse orthogonal to that generic reversal carries the opposite (continuation) sign — i.e. the true object of interest is not the displacement but the *cross-sectional dispersion of its reversal rate*. The child makes that explicit: it takes Parent B's horizon-matched standardised 6-bar displacement and multiplies it by a polarity weight built from Parent A's queue evidence — the effective tick-grid quantum, the volume absorbed while the mid was pinned inside half a quantum, and the volume printed on the unpinned (break) bars — collapsed into a single cross-sectionally ranked backing score, mapped to -1 (no queue was there, the push was unbacked → fade it hard) through +1 (a real resting queue was sat on and then consumed → the next level is thinner, let it run). Because the polarity weight is cross-sectionally centred and the plain 1- and 6-bar reversal carriers plus volume intensity are then projected out bar-by-bar, the unconditional reversal loading that both parents actually realised is removed by construction and only the interaction survives: queue-backed moves revert materially less (and at the extreme continue) than unbacked moves of identical size. Neither parent can express this — A had the queue state but signed it unconditionally as continuation, B had the displacement split but delegated polarity to a noisy per-name trailing regression that whipsaws.
factors.name: Pin-queue-backing conditioned reversal polarity

factors.trading_idea: Inventory acquired by liquidity providers against aggressive flow is repaid by later quote relocations, but that repayment is spread over several bars, whereas pure mid-quote noise (bid-ask/queue bounce) reciprocates entirely at lag 1; so estimating the per-name repayment kernel psi_k from lags k>=2 only isolates genuine inventory unwinding from mechanical one-bar noise reversal. Repayment is owed only on pushes that actually transferred inventory, so each bar's body (close-open) is weighted by the bar's trailing volume percentile before entering the kernel — quote drift on no volume creates no obligation. Given the estimated kernel, the expected cumulative relocation over exactly the next 6 bars is an analytic convolution of the *known* recent trade-backed bodies with horizon-summed kernel weights W_m = sum_{j=1..6} psi_{j+m}, which makes the forecast horizon-matched instead of relying on a hand-set fade and a noisy single cross-lag correlation gate (the parent's IC peaked at 12 bars because its gate mixed fast bounce with slow absorption).
