The edge persists because harvesting it requires posting passive size against possibly-informed aggressive flow for a fraction of a spread — market-making inventory risk that arbitrageurs cannot lift directionally — and the signal's per-name sign is estimated rather than imposed, so names whose flow propagates instead of reverting are forecast to continue.
factors.name: Bounce-purged trade-backed repayment kernel (h=6 convolution)

factors.trading_idea: The parent showed that the covariance-inconsistent piece of a 1-minute move *continues* rather than reverts at the 6-bar offset; the correct reading is that at a 10-second clock this component is not a liquidity-provision error being repaired but the visible footprint of a single-name metaorder being sliced along a historically tight (low-variance) direction, plus Epps-attenuated lagged transmission of the correlation structure. Both imply continuation over the next minute: remaining child orders keep pushing the same way (order-flow self-correlation / propagator), and peers have not yet caught up so no snap-back pressure exists yet — reversal only appears once the metaorder is exhausted, which is exactly why the parent's IC flipped sign around 24 bars. The child therefore (i) whitens with the covariance estimated at the *same 6-bar scale* as the dislocation (Sigma_6^{-1/2}, better-conditioned than the full inverse and Epps-consistent) and (ii) multiplies the whitened, univariate-orthogonalized dislocation by a gate built from the trailing sign-persistence of *idiosyncratic* signed order flow, so persistent (still-working) flow predicts continuation while anti-persistent (exhausted, liquidity-providing) flow predicts reversal. It is falsifiable: if the flow-persistence gate carries no interaction the product's IC collapses to the weak unconditional tilt; the edge survives arbitrage because it needs a stable multi-name scale-matched precision matrix, pays only a few ticks per episode along low-variance directions, and requires trading against a price-insensitive executor within a one-minute window.
factors.name: Scale-matched precision dislocation, flow-persistence gated

factors.trading_idea: Human limit-order placement clusters on round price nodes (…x.00, x.50, x.25, x.10, x.05), so the book carries excess resting depth exactly at those levels; the relevant node spacing is the one comparable to the distance price actually travels over the forecast horizon. A mid drifting *into* the nearest node therefore meets an abnormally thick wall and stalls/retreats, while a mid that has just *passed* a node has consumed that depth and faces a thinner book on the far side, so it continues. The child expresses this as a single antisymmetric function of the price's position inside its volatility-matched lattice cell, signed by the direction of travel — so it is resistance and post-breach continuation in one term whose time-series mean loading on plain reversal is ~zero (position within a cell is nearly uniform), which is why it is not another reversal clone. The edge survives arbitrage because each event is worth a fraction of a tick, it lives in the price *level modulo a lattice* — a non-scale-invariant feature that virtually every return-based model normalises away — and crossing the spread to harvest it costs more than the drift for anyone not already resting in the queue.
factors.name: Volatility-matched round-number lattice barrier asymmetry

factors.trading_idea: A displacement built by an execution algorithm slicing a parent order is *ordinally monotone* — nearly every pairwise price comparison inside the window is concordant — and its magnitude is spread almost evenly across many small child prints, so no single increment dominates; a liquidity-withdrawal overshoot produces the same net displacement with one or two tail increments and a non-monotone, jagged path, and under a transient-impact propagator that part relaxes as depth refills. The child therefore replaces the parent's noisy product of two cross-sectional ranks with two statistics that have natural, per-name nulls: a Mann–Kendall concordance tau (all pairwise sign comparisons over the last 7 and 13 closes, scale-free and tie-robust) for monotonicity, and a Herfindahl concentration of increment magnitudes whose *own-name* trailing percentile (not a cross-sectional rank) states whether the path was unusually diffuse or unusually jump-dominated — this removes the parent's confound of the gate with cross-sectional volatility/size, which the book already spans. The edge persists because identifying an in-progress child-order sequence requires joint ordinal *and* dispersion conditioning rather than move size, the agent whose own child orders create the drift cannot profit from front-running itself, and net-of-spread capacity inside a one-minute window is far too small for large arbitrageurs.
factors.name: Mann-Kendall monotonicity × increment-concentration grind/jump wedge

factors.trading_idea: A bar's within-bar body (close-open) is the displacement produced while trades arrive, while the seam (open minus previous close) is pure quote relocation by liquidity providers; regressing the trailing 6-bar seam sum on the body that preceded it gives a per-name, empirically measured total walk-back gain G — no assumption about whether a push is permanent. The parent then *predicted* reversal from the push alone; the child instead prices the push against the reciprocation that has already been delivered, forming a reciprocation DEBT = (expected total seam response to recent pushes) minus (seams actually observed since those pushes). Only the unpaid part of the walk-back can still be earned, so the debt is horizon-matched by construction to the 6-bar payback window used to estimate G, and names that already gave their push back score near zero instead of being double-counted as reversal candidates. The edge should persist because it lives inside a few basis points of quote relocation, requires per-name estimation of a walk-back kernel from open/close seam decomposition, and is only monetisable by patient, low-cost execution — directional arbitrageurs cannot cross the spread to collect it.
factors.name: Seam reciprocation debt (unpaid walk-back)

factors.trading_idea: The parent showed that folding an already-observed market path against a name's lagged loadings predicts a 6-bar catch-up, but six free trailing OLS loadings are an over-parameterised, high-variance description of an impulse response that is physically a single monotone decay; the estimation noise is what kept standalone IC near zero. This child replaces the six loadings with a two-parameter, shape-constrained kernel: a *delay centroid* tau (the correlation-weighted mean lag of the name's comovement with the cap-weighted market) sets a geometric decay exp(-l/tau), and a *total gain* g estimated from 6-bar cumulative-on-cumulative regression (immune to lag placement) sets its scale, so the owed catch-up is g times the kernel folded onto the already-realised market path. Trust is now internal rather than borrowed from fundamentals: only names whose comovement mass genuinely sits at lags >= 1 (high lag share) and whose bars often carry no trade can owe anything, and the whole forecast is switched off when the market move lacks cross-sectional breadth, because a cap-weighted move driven by one large name is idiosyncratic news that laggards do not owe. The edge persists because measuring a delay centroid requires a long trailing panel estimate that second-scale liquidity takers do not maintain, and the names it selects are precisely the thin, rarely-traded ones where attention and inventory capacity are scarcest.
factors.name: Lag-Centroid Geometric Response Kernel Catch-Up (breadth gated)

factors.trading_idea: Parent B's owed-beta deficit is real but slow: it is measured on close prices, so bid-ask bounce contaminates the 'already delivered' term, and it pools names whose gaps close in 6 bars with names whose gaps close in 30, which is why its IC peaks at 24 bars. Parent A supplies exactly the two missing pieces: (i) the range centre (H+L)/2 is a much lower-noise sample of the efficient price than the single close, so the horizon-matched response deficit D = beta_i * S_t - Y_t (6-bar cumulative common shock times a shock-selected trailing loading, minus the realized 6-bar centre-price path) becomes an uncontaminated measure of undelivered repricing; and (ii) the two-scale noise share phi = (1-VR_6)*6/5 is precisely the fraction of one-bar close variance that dies inside the fixed 6-bar horizon, so it is the correct per-name coefficient on how much of any gap actually closes by t+6 — used as a multiplicative state variable it selects the fast-closing names instead of averaging them with slow ones. The residual close-minus-centre endpoint dislocation, down-weighted on heavy-volume bars (permanent impact) and up-weighted on quiet bars (pure quote noise), is then the second, faster leg of the same total close-based gap and enters with the same sign, so the interaction gives a horizon-matched decomposition — owed efficient-price response plus decaying endpoint noise, both scaled by the measured 6-bar transient share — that neither parent has alone.
factors.name: Noise-share-scaled centre-price beta backlog

factors.trading_idea: Treat the traded volume stream as a shares-turnover clock and reconstruct, recursively, the cost basis of the *currently active* holder base: V_t = (1-k_t)V_{t-1} + k_t P_t with k_t proportional to that bar's turnover relative to the name's own normal turnover, so memory shortens exactly when inventory actually changes hands. The same volume clock gives the dispersion of that cost distribution, so the standardized overhang z = (P - V)/D says how many crowd-dispersion units of unrealized gain the marginal recent holder is sitting on; when D is small the whole recent crowd crosses break-even simultaneously and their realization flow arrives coherently within seconds. Prospect-theory realization asymmetry (gains are taken eagerly, losses are frozen and held) predicts the supply pressure from a gain overhang is materially stronger than the demand pressure from an equal loss overhang, and that pressure can only be executed where turnover is currently live and the float rotates fast — hence the asymmetric weighting and the activity/float-turnover amplitudes. The edge survives arbitrage because harvesting it means supplying liquidity to coherent profit-taking flow (inventory risk, capacity-limited) and because the object required is a per-name volume-time cost distribution, not a calendar moving average, so it is not spanned by the usual anchor-gap or displacement-reversal signals.
factors.name: Volume-clock disposition overhang with crowd-concentration gate

factors.trading_idea: Parent B locates *where* a name sits in peer multiple space but says nothing about *how* the gap was opened, so its slow spread level only pays out over minutes; Parent A dates a one-sided variance burst to the last two minutes and knows whether it was mechanical (variance per unit of participation high = thin-book vacuum) but has no notion of fair value. The child keeps only the fast, just-widened component of the gated peer log-multiple spread (anchor halflife ~2 minutes, freshness = spread widening versus 6 bars ago) and amplifies it exactly when the residual downside/upside semivariance asymmetry innovation is *concordant* with the direction of the dislocation and was produced in a liquidity vacuum: a peer-multiple gap opened by a one-sided, unbacked variance burst is inventory displacement and snaps back inside the next minute, while the same gap opened with commensurate volume or with the wrong-sided variance signature is genuine repricing and is left alone. The interaction is the edge: value distance without a formation diagnostic reverts too slowly for a 6-bar horizon, and a variance burst without a valuation anchor has no target to revert to — together they identify a fresh, mechanically-created, comparably-measured mispricing whose closure clock matches the fixed offset.
factors.name: Fresh multiple-space dislocation with semivariance-vacuum concordance

factors.trading_idea: Parent A showed that a *fresh* one-sided (down-heavy) realised-variance burst that capital structure cannot explain snaps back, and that the snapback is concentrated where the burst cost little volume (thin-book vacuum); Parent B's realised sign says the opposite of its declared story — bar-level displacement that arrives *with* trade prints is informed and continues, while displacement produced by pure quote revision with no prints is market-maker inventory/uncertainty flicker that reverts. The child fuses the two by attributing each bar's *squared* peer-residual return to a quiet channel (weight 1-g) and a traded channel (weight g, g = v/(v+trailing mean v)), building A's fast-vs-long-run semivariance asymmetry innovation separately on each channel, and taking the wedge quiet-minus-traded: a fresh down-heavy variance burst built out of untraded quote revision is mechanical and reverts up, whereas the identical asymmetry built out of printed volume is news and does not. The interaction carries edge neither parent has alone because A's vacuum gate is a coarse 12-bar variance-per-volume *stock* that cannot tell which bars inside the window were traded, while B's bar-level attribution was applied to signed drift (a noisy, sign-cancelling object) rather than to the one-sided variance that actually identifies liquidation pressure; conditioning the attributed asymmetry innovation on valuation-peer residualisation (removes common/sector variance) and demeaning inside leverage-tercile x size-half buckets (removes the Merton/Christie structural component) leaves only the mechanically displaced, still-relaxing part.
factors.name: Quiet-vs-traded semivariance asymmetry wedge under a thin-book vacuum

factors.trading_idea: Parent A's insight is that a quote move is only permanent once flow has paid for it, so the wedge between a volume-clock efficient-price anchor and a wall-clock anchor of the same nominal memory isolates displacement that trades never validated; Parent B's insight is that at 10-second sampling an OLS market beta is co-jump contaminated, so part of what looks like a name's own displacement is really laggy, mis-attributed factor exposure. The child builds the volume-time-vs-clock-time anchor wedge on the *robustly hedged idiosyncratic* log-price path (residual to a winsorized-beta hedge on the cross-sectional median return), and gates its sign by the OLS-vs-robust beta disagreement: where the beta is clean the unvalidated idio wedge is dealer inventory / stale-quote noise and snaps back, whereas where the beta is jump-contaminated the same wedge is Epps-style partial adjustment to the common factor and continues. The interaction is the edge: A fades every unpaid displacement including factor catch-up (its sector demeaning only removes the average of that effect), while B measures displacement with a plain 6-bar residual sum that mixes flow-paid permanent repricing with unpaid drift — only conditioning flow-validation on hedge-contamination separates snapback from catch-up name by name.
factors.name: Flow-validated idiosyncratic anchor wedge, beta-contamination gated

factors.trading_idea: A name that lags the market accumulates a measurable information debt: the gap between what its aggregated (distributed-lag) market beta says its last 6-bar return should have been and what it actually was. Whether that debt is worth trading is not a property of the debt but of the name's *delivery machinery*, so instead of gating on path-shape heuristics the child estimates the machinery directly: it decomposes the expected closure over the next 6 bars into P(bar is a moving-quote bar) x closure-per-moving-quote-bar plus P(bar is an active/traded bar) x closure-per-active-bar, where each per-event closure rate is a trailing, precision-shrunk regression of the realised return on the previous bar's normalised debt measured only inside that bar class, and frozen-mid quiet bars are excluded from the quiet class because a stale quote cannot deliver anything. The edge persists because the profitable state (debt exists AND the name's own recent history shows that class of bar actually pays debt down) is a per-name, per-regime conjunction that a static residual-reversal or lead-lag arbitrage does not condition on, and because the fast leg of the trade requires paying spread in exactly the thin, frozen-quote names where the signal is switched off. Falsifiable: sorting on (channel-probability-weighted closure rate) x (normalised debt) should predict 6-bar returns with positive sign, and should beat sorting on the debt alone or on the debt times an unconditional beta.
factors.name: Delivery-Rate-Decomposed Catch-Up Closure Speed

factors.trading_idea: The parent measured the right object (how much of its own habitual impulse-response a name still owes after a common shock) but ranked the raw owed stock, so its cross-section was dominated by names whose backlog drains over minutes — hence IC peaking at 24 bars, not at the fixed 6-bar offset. The child converts the owed stock into the amount expected to be *delivered inside the next 6 bars* by self-calibrating, per name and causally, the empirical horizon-6 delivery coefficient: a trailing regression of realised 6-bar delivery (minus the summed shortfall over the last 6 bars) on the deficit stock that existed 6 bars earlier, precision-blended with the cross-sectional prior via its own R-squared. Names whose backlog historically drains fast get amplified, slow-draining or non-converging names get shrunk or sign-flipped, so the signal is horizon-matched by construction rather than by luck. The edge persists because the delivery speed is a liquidity-provision property (spread, depth replenishment, participation) that is name-specific, non-stationary and must be re-estimated event-conditionally, and closing the gap means supplying liquidity into sub-minute transient impact where capacity is capped.
factors.name: Horizon-6 closure-calibrated kernel response deficit

factors.trading_idea: Order-flow bursts decompose into a market-common component (index/ETF baskets, portfolio rebalances, market-wide liquidity shocks) that carries no name-specific information, and an idiosyncratic component that is far more likely to be an informed metaorder. Kyle-type impact from uninformed common flow is transient and unwinds as intermediaries recycle inventory, whereas idiosyncratic informed flow leaves a permanent, still-incomplete price move; therefore the SAME recent displacement should be faded when the accompanying activity surprise was mostly common and followed when it was mostly idiosyncratic. I identify the split in real time by regressing each name's log-volume z-score on a robust cross-sectional activity factor over a trailing window and comparing the recent explained versus residual activity energy, then multiply the sign-flipped market-relative displacement by that (cross-sectionally ranked) commonality share, gated on an actual activity burst. The edge persists because it requires jointly estimating a per-name activity beta, classifying the current burst and taking the opposite side of heavy common flow within ~1 minute — a capacity-limited, inventory-risky liquidity provision that slow discretionary capital cannot pre-empt and that pure reversal or pure volume-spike signals mis-sign half the time.
factors.name: Activity-commonality transient-impact snapback

factors.trading_idea: The parent imposed a fixed polarity on a 6-bar displacement and therefore had to average a reversion regime against a continuation regime; its edge consequently leaked out to 24 bars and was largely spanned by the book's reversal factors. The child stops assuming the polarity and *estimates* it at exactly the forecast offset: the lag-1 autocorrelation of non-overlapping 6-bar beta-residual block returns is, by construction, the sign and strength of the map from the last 60 seconds of idiosyncratic displacement to the next 60 seconds, and it is estimated separately in traded-heavy and quiet states of the displacement window (bounce/quote-noise displacements revert; volume-backed metaorder displacements extend), with the currently prevailing state selecting the coefficient. Cross-sectionally centring that coefficient turns the factor into a pure predictability-dispersion trade — a name whose block rho equals the panel median carries zero weight — so the exposure to the common reversal factor the book already owns is removed and what remains is compensation for supplying liquidity precisely where the name-and-state-specific 60-second kernel says impact is transient, and for bearing adverse selection where it says impact is informational. It persists because the coefficient is a slowly drifting *state* that flips sign across names and volume regimes, so neither a static reversal nor a static momentum trader can harvest the conditional, and the horizon (60 s hold) sits below the cost-effective reach of slower participants.
factors.name: Traded-state conditional block autocorrelation dispersion (h=6)

factors.trading_idea: Whether a 30-second price move persists or unwinds should depend on whether that move occurred in a microstructural *context* that is statistically coupled to price formation, and coupling is measurable as pointwise mutual information (PMI) in a nonparametrically estimated joint density. I estimate, from a trailing pooled panel histogram, the joint distribution of (signed standardized move, relative volume surprise) and of (signed standardized move, path efficiency), and evaluate log p(z,x) - log p(z)p(x) for each name's current cell: positive PMI means moves of that signed size and that context genuinely co-occur more often than under independence, i.e. the displacement was produced by the coupled information/flow channel and is permanent; negative PMI means the cell is a decoupled (independence-consistent or anti-associated) corner — the price moved where price and its own context carry no joint information, which is the signature of an inventory/quote-noise displacement that is repaid. The signal is therefore the move itself multiplied by tanh of the summed PMI, so the sign of the bet on the same move flips with its measured information coupling. This edge is not arbitraged because the discriminating object is a regime-adaptive nonparametric copula-density lift pooled across names — practitioners almost always replace it with a fixed linear 'volume-confirmed' filter, which is mis-calibrated exactly in the rare, high-payoff cells (large move / vanishing support), and the per-trade payoff at a one-minute horizon is too small to attract capacity into the illiquid names that generate it.
factors.name: PMI context-coupling of signed moves

factors.trading_idea: Parent A measured which side's probe got rejected (range-normalised shadow asymmetry on bars that actually traded size) and its realized sign was the OPPOSITE of a naive 'rejection means reversal' reading — a rejected upside probe preceded HIGHER returns. Parent B supplies the state variable that explains why: when a name's bar-volume becomes metronomic, a scheduler is working an unfinished parent order, so an upper shadow is that buyer being temporarily absorbed by resting supply it will keep eating, and the level breaks (continuation); when volume is bursty, the excursion is one-off aggression whose displacement is transient impact and the rejection is genuine, so price should retreat from the tested side. The child therefore multiplies A's volume-weighted probe asymmetry by B's bounded volume-smoothness shock, flipping the polarity of the rejection statistic with participation regularity — an interaction neither parent has: A applied one fixed sign to both regimes (hence its contradicted hypothesis), and B applied its gate only to a coarse drift that carries no information about WHICH side of the book the pressure was tested against.
factors.name: Metronome-gated probe-rejection polarity split

factors.trading_idea: The parent proved that a per-name transient (reversible) price component exists, but it expressed it as a single-scale displacement whose reversal is delivered almost entirely in the first bar, so at the pinned 6-bar offset the signal was diluted to noise. Instead of guessing the decay shape from a two-scale Hurst law, estimate the name's own reversal kernel directly: trailing autocovariances gamma(l) of idiosyncratic returns give the exact horizon-matched linear projection E[R_{t+1..t+H} | r_t, r_{t-1}, ...] = sum_j (sum_{h=1..H} rho(j+h)) r_{t-j}, which mechanically discards the part of the transient that has already unwound and keeps only the part still to be delivered inside the forecast window. Second, transient impact relaxes in *event* time, not clock time: when current trade intensity is nu times the name's norm, the decay that normally needs l bars needs l/nu bars, so the kernel horizon is stretched/compressed by nu (implemented as a continuous blend of H = 3, 6, 12 kernels driven by log2 of relative volume). Desks apply one common clock-time reversion gain to the whole book, so the tradable residual is per-name dispersion in kernel shape and in event-time speed; it pays a few bps per name and needs continuous re-estimation, which is why it survives arbitrage. Falsifiable: if reversion were clock-time rather than event-time, the volume-clock blend would add nothing over the flat H=6 kernel and the IC would collapse to the parent's ~0.
factors.name: Horizon-matched autocovariance kernel on a volume clock

factors.trading_idea: Parent B established that the *idiosyncratic* part of a heavy-volume within-bar displacement is a transient cost of immediacy that snaps back over ~a minute; Parent A's realized (sign-contradicted) result says the same thing from the volume side — fresh repricing funded by a name's OWN volume burst reverses, while repricing that arrives while the whole panel is simultaneously busy is information-validated common flow and persists. The child therefore drops Parent B's sector labels and market-R-squared router and instead attributes each bar's displacement to its funding source with Parent A's causal activity-commonality decomposition (trailing z-score of log volume, split into panel-mean 'common' and positive 'idio' excess), and measures displacement with BOTH channels the parents used separately: within-bar close-location value (where the mid ended inside the bar it printed) and the vol-normalised across-bar increment. The interaction is the edge: sign concordance between the within-bar close location and the net increment on idio-busy bars identifies a *completed* one-sided liquidity-demand push (aggressor walked visible depth and left the mid stranded at the extreme), which is precisely when passive depth replenishment reverses the move, whereas the same displacement funded by market-wide bursts is left alone (small positive continuation weight) — neither parent can distinguish 'my own metaorder pushed me here' from 'the basket pushed everyone' while also knowing whether the push finished inside the bar.
factors.name: Activity-attribution gated immediacy-cost snapback

factors.trading_idea: The parent showed that slow, mandate-constrained (income/payout) shareholder bases leave systematic displacements unarbitraged, but it expressed this as a cumulative beta catch-up whose repair only completes near 12 bars. The child moves the same slow-capital mechanism onto the *idiosyncratic* residual and onto the exact forecast offset: a name's 6-bar beta-residual displacement is either informational and persists, or it is liquidity noise and snaps back, and which one dominates is governed by how quickly the marginal holder re-optimises. I therefore estimate each name's own horizon-matched lag-6 autoregression coefficient of its 6-bar idiosyncratic move and shrink it, empirical-Bayes style with a precision-based weight, toward a prior set by the payout-clientele score (deep income clientele => positive prior, i.e. continuation; fast/no-payout clientele => negative prior, i.e. reversion). The signal is the resulting conditional expectation rho_hat x current standardised residual displacement, so it is by construction a 6-bar-ahead forecast rather than a slow repair; the edge should persist because measuring per-name persistence requires long trailing panels and the payout clientele that creates it cannot re-optimise at second frequency. Falsified if the clientele prior carries no incremental information over the raw estimated coefficient, or if rho_hat has no monotone relation to realised 6-bar residual continuation.
factors.name: Clientele-prior empirical-Bayes idiosyncratic AR(6) forecast

factors.trading_idea: The parent showed that quote-driven (quiet-bar) drift continues while volume-paid drift decays, but it measured both over a fixed 30-bar window, so its state variable moved on a 5-minute clock and its forecast leaked into 24-bar horizons. The child re-times the same mechanism in *event time*: each high-volume print is a validation event that resets the tape's reference price, and the price displacement accumulated *since* that last validating print is repricing the tape has not yet confirmed. Such unconfirmed displacement is genuine maker information only while it is fresh — it is converted into realised return when the next flow arrives, on the name's own inter-print clock — whereas displacement that has survived many bars with no print is stale-mid noise and mean-reverts; the return printed *at* the validation event is transient impact and reverts as it ages out. Because the state resets at every print, its autocorrelation is a few bars long, so the forecast is front-loaded onto the fixed 6-bar offset instead of bleeding into multi-minute horizons; the edge survives arbitrage because harvesting it means quoting into thin, untraded states where spread cost is largest relative to the signal.
factors.name: Renewal-clock unvalidated displacement with age polarity flip

factors.trading_idea: During a no-trade silence the mid can move for two very different reasons: a genuine one-way relocation of the maker's reservation price (queue depletion / adverse-selection repricing), or flickering, round-tripping quotes that are pure stale-mid noise. These are separated by the *path efficiency* of the untraded excursion — net displacement divided by total absolute path travelled — whose null value under a driftless random walk is exactly k^(-1/2) after k quiet bars, so excess efficiency above that benchmark is a falsifiable measure of genuine repricing while negative excess efficiency flags wobble that should snap back. The parent gated this displacement by an *unconditional* per-name trade rate, which is essentially a static liquidity characteristic already spanned by the book; the child replaces it with a Hawkes-style *conditional* intensity (baseline plus exponentially-decaying self-excitation from recent trades) so the gate varies through time with the silence clock and measures whether the next order is genuinely imminent. The edge persists because monetising it means crossing the spread on names that are momentarily quiet and thin, exactly where the round-trip cost is unattractive to slow arbitrageurs, and it is falsified if excess path efficiency carries no incremental sign information over raw quiet displacement, or if the conditional hazard adds nothing over the static arrival rate.
factors.name: Path-Efficiency Filtered Quiet Repricing under Hawkes Arrival Hazard

factors.trading_idea: The parent forecast the *stock* of a peer-relative displacement and assumed a parametric relaxation clock, so its predictive mass was spread over many minutes and its IC kept rising to 24 bars. This child forecasts a *flow* that is deliverable inside 6 bars: it locates the last completed swing in the peer-relative log price (the extreme of the trailing 3-minute path), measures the retracement rate actually realised per bar since that extreme, and linearly extrapolates that measured rate over the next 6 bars, hard-capped by the amount of the swing that is still unretraced. Because the forecast is both rate-based (fast) and self-limiting (it goes to zero once the swing is spent), its predictive content is concentrated at the one-minute offset instead of accumulating over many minutes. The reversion leg is additionally gated by flow cessation — current traded volume relative to the name's own baseline — because transient impact only relaxes after the pushing metaorder stops; the edge survives arbitrage because harvesting it means holding names for ~60 seconds against the residual risk that the metaorder resumes, and the state (peer-relative retracement rate x volume die-off) must be measured per name per event rather than read off a level.
factors.name: Swing-retracement rate extrapolation with flow-cessation gate

factors.trading_idea: Algebraically, parent A's anchor-minus-mid gap is the sum of two very different objects: a cross-bar term (volume-weighted trailing traded level minus the current mid = level staleness) and an intra-bar term (upper-minus-lower shadow, i.e. parent B's rejected-probe asymmetry). Parent B's realized sign shows the true direction of the intra-bar term is the OPPOSITE of 'hidden supply': heavy-volume bars whose excursion printed above the closing mid are followed by higher returns, because the excursion is where inventory was actually transferred and the maker-skewed quote is dragged back to it while self-excited same-side flow keeps arriving. The child therefore separates the two channels — level staleness on the body-centre price (so it is orthogonal to wicks) and probe-gated range-normalised shadow asymmetry — and uses the wick state as a *concordance gate* on the level channel: score = ½(g + |g|·a). A dislocation whose sign is confirmed by heavy-volume traded excursions on the same side is a stale quote that snaps back within ~a minute, whereas an equally large dislocation carved out of clean bar bodies with opposing wicks is permanent, information-driven repricing and is zeroed out. That conditional discrimination — dislocation magnitude × probe-side confirmation — is edge neither parent has: A cannot tell repricing from staleness, and B has no magnitude of the dislocation to be right about.
factors.name: Probe-concordant trade-anchor staleness wedge

factors.trading_idea: The parent showed that the path-conversion ratio c (net displacement / probed path) separates a continuation regime from a snapback regime, but it applied c to slow 10-bar channels, so its information decayed over minutes and its power peaked at 24 bars. Here c is demoted to a pure STATE variable — a per-name estimate of book permeability (how many quanta of price the book gives up per unit of probed wick path), measured on a window that ends 3 bars before the present and z-scored against the name's own 240-bar history, hence mechanically decoupled from the current move — and it is used only to sign a genuinely FAST trigger: the dead-zoned, grid-quantum-scaled, beta-residual impulse of the last 3 bars. In a permeable (high-c) regime depth is thin, so a fresh impulse is mostly transient impact and snaps back as the queue refills; in an absorptive (low-c) regime price only moves when a persistent metaorder is eating real depth, so the fresh impulse continues. Because the switch is cross-sectionally centred, the factor's unconditional projection onto plain short-term reversal is ~zero by construction, so naive reversal harvesters cannot span it, and the profitable leg is exactly where supplying liquidity is expensive — a compensated risk, not a free lunch.
factors.name: Disjoint-window conversion efficiency switches the fresh impulse

factors.trading_idea: The parent's failure is diagnostic, not random: because mid-price bar returns carry an MA(1) bounce term, adjacent-block sign flips are mechanically over-frequent, so Rice inversion returns rho<0 for nearly every name and the factor degenerated into a blanket 60-second reversal — which lost, because most of a 6-bar mid displacement is *permanent* (efficient-price) and only the small endpoint noise component actually snaps back. The child therefore stops signing the whole displacement and instead decomposes it: a local-level (unobserved-components) model of the market-median-purged log price whose steady-state Kalman gain K is set analytically per name from trailing Roll moments (sigma_u^2 = -gamma_1, sigma_e^2 = gamma_0 + 2*gamma_1, q = sigma_e^2/sigma_u^2, K = (sqrt(q^2+4q)-q)/2), so bouncy names are smoothed hard while names with positively autocorrelated bars are barely smoothed at all. The forecast is then the theoretically correct sum of two oppositely-signed legs in the same log-return units: the filtered permanent drift over the last 6 bars, which continues while a sliced metaorder is still live (gated by current volume versus its own ADV), minus the residual pricing error P_t - m_hat_t, which is estimated inventory/bounce noise and must decay. The edge persists because desks apply one common reversion parameter to the whole cross-section; separating what should revert from what should continue requires continuous per-name noise-ratio estimation whose per-name payoff is tiny and only aggregates in a broad book.
factors.name: Roll-gain Kalman split: permanent drift vs bounce error

factors.trading_idea: The conditional mean of a 60-second forward return is NOT linear in recent displacement, and the book only spans the linear part. The Roll/bid-ask-bounce channel injects a roughly fixed-amplitude oscillation, so the transitory (reversible) share of a move shrinks as the move grows, while genuinely large idiosyncratic 60-second displacements are news- or cascade-driven and continue through self-excited (Hawkes-like) order flow. Expanding E[r_{t+1..t+6} | displacement] in Hermite polynomials of the own-volatility-standardized 6-bar idiosyncratic displacement x therefore predicts a POSITIVE cubic coefficient, so the un-spanned component is exactly H3(x)=x^3-3x — negative (reversal) for moderate |x| and flipping to positive (continuation) beyond |x|~sqrt(3) own-sigma, a threshold implied by the orthogonal-polynomial normalisation rather than tuned. Because continuation requires the excitation to still be alive, H3 is modulated by the name's contemporaneous flow-intensity ratio, and the linear reversal component is stripped out by an exact per-bar cross-sectional projection so the signal carries curvature only. It is falsifiable (if reversal instead strengthens super-linearly with size the IC must be negative) and hard to arbitrage: it is a non-monotone cross-sectional map that no linear blend of monotone reversal/momentum factors can reproduce, and its tail leg requires buying into an active cascade — inventory risk most liquidity providers decline.
factors.name: Hermite-cubic curvature of the 6-bar reversal kernel

factors.trading_idea: The parent showed that fresh sqrt-volume-weighted directional pressure precedes *lower* forward returns at 6 bars, the opposite of the propagator-continuation reading; the correct reading at a 60-second horizon is that most of the square-root-law displacement created by a burst of one-sided liquidity-taking is the *transient* component (Bouchaud's propagator relaxes as depth refills within seconds-to-minutes), so the mid mechanically walks back once the taking stops. The child therefore does not merely flip a sign: it estimates the *size in return units* of the transient displacement just created, I = sigma_bar * sqrt(6) * sqrt(Q_6 / Q_typical) * c, where sigma_bar is the name's trailing per-bar volatility, the participation ratio Q_6/Q_typical enters through the square-root impact law, and c is the sqrt-volume-weighted concordance of bar-return signs (near +/-1 only when the flow is one-sided, i.e. a metaorder rather than two-sided churn). It then purges the sector-common part of that displacement, because common displacement is news-driven and permanent while the idiosyncratic part is inventory/liquidity-driven and is what gets paid back, and goes long the most negative residual displacement. Falsifiable: the magnitude-scaled, sector-purged version must beat the parent's pure sign statistic, and the edge must concentrate in high-participation bursts; if IC is flat in participation and vanishes after sector purging, the transient-impact reading is wrong. It survives arbitrage because capturing a fraction of a one-minute, sub-spread relaxation requires paying the spread on the far side and has negligible capacity.
factors.name: Square-root-law transient impact magnitude — idiosyncratic payback

factors.trading_idea: Model log-price as random walk plus an AR(1) transitory pricing error; that model forces the return autocovariances to decay geometrically (gamma_{k+1}/gamma_k = phi), so phi, the error variance, and — crucially — the *fraction of the error that is repaid inside exactly h bars*, (1 - phi^h), are all identifiable causally from a name's own trailing autocovariance function. The parent's edge grew monotonically with horizon because it summed a mechanical drift that accrues over the whole anchor window; here the (1 - phi^6) factor explicitly down-weights names whose dislocation pays back slower than the fixed 6-bar offset and keeps only errors whose half-life matches it, so the IC should concentrate at the target horizon instead of leaking to 24 bars. Two further disciplines make it falsifiable rather than a re-tuned reversal: the dislocation is measured with a phi-tuned geometric filter (window self-selected per name, not a hand-set constant) and shrunk by the Wiener coefficient Cov(u,d)/Var(d), which automatically kills names whose recent path is dominated by permanent (random-walk) moves; and the whole forecast is gated by a specification test — gamma_3/gamma_2 must equal gamma_2/gamma_1 — so we only trade when the geometric-decay assumption that licenses the repayment estimate actually holds. The edge survives arbitrage because it is a 60-second, spread-paying, name-specific liquidity rebate on a small model-consistent subset, i.e. capacity-limited rather than information-based.
factors.name: Spec-test-validated transitory repayment (6-bar matched)

factors.trading_idea: Parent A splits the last 6 bars of log displacement into a square-root-law *paid* part (sign(ret)·lambda·sqrt(volume)) and a *flow-orthogonal, unpaid* part (mid revision nobody traded against); parent B measures where the current price sits inside the trailing volume-at-price occupation density (dense node vs low-occupancy void). The child conditions A's split on B's state: an unpaid quote revision that lands inside a dense volume node has standing resting inventory to lean against, so it is absorbed and snaps back hard, while the same unpaid move in a void meets no supply and is not reverted; conversely a volume-backed push only becomes permanent once it has *drained* into thinner price territory and the pressuring flow has ceased — inside a dense shelf the volume-backed push is pure absorption over-shoot that unwinds. Neither parent has this: A applies one reversion speed to every unbacked move and one cessation sign to every paid move regardless of the liquidity landscape it moved into, while B reads the landscape but has no idea whether the displacement that put the price there was paid for or free, which is exactly the variable that decides whether the resting mass absorbs or gets consumed.
factors.name: Occupancy-gated paid vs unpaid displacement split

factors.trading_idea: A mid-price dislocation is only tradeable at a 60-second horizon if it is the kind that market makers unwind within a minute, and the cleanest observable label for that is the *cross-sectional company the dislocation was born in*: when a name's deviation crosses its local anchor in the same bar as an unusually large fraction of the cross-section, the excursion was ignited by index-level liquidity demand / basket hedging / risk pulses that dealers absorb and reverse quickly, whereas a deviation born alone is name-specific news and keeps going. So I classify each live excursion by the (activity-normalised, self-excluded) breadth of simultaneous anchor crossings at its *birth bar*, and trade the standardised deviation with a signed weight that fades synchronised-birth excursions and rides isolated-birth ones, damped by an exp(-age/6) freshness kernel so only excursions whose remaining decay lands inside the fixed 6-bar window get weight. The edge should persist because it requires joint point-process bookkeeping across names (event birth cohorts, not return betas), the profits are small-amplitude and capacity-limited at the 10-second scale, and a book that measures reversal on deviation levels or on return-based common/idio splits cannot see which *events* were common-born.
factors.name: Crossing-birth cohort breadth fresh dislocation wedge

factors.trading_idea: Transient price impact relaxes in trade time, not clock time: a dislocation from a size-matched sector peer basket only completes the portion of its snapback that the next few bars of traded volume can pay for. The parent identified that a push had ended but gated on *falling* volume, which mechanically selected names sitting on a slow event clock — precisely why its IC kept growing out to 24 bars instead of landing at 6. The child keeps the price-based turn detection (the dislocation increment now points back toward the peer anchor) but replaces the flow-cessation gate with an explicit expected-relaxation-fraction phi = 1 - exp(-rho * v_fast / v_slow), so weight is concentrated in names whose trading rate is accelerating and whose relaxation will therefore finish inside the fixed 60-second window; the dislocation object is also rebuilt at the horizon scale (12-bar peer-residual cumulative return) rather than from a 60-bar anchor. The edge survives arbitrage because supplying it means warehousing inventory in a name that is only probabilistically 'done pushing', and the per-event profit is small relative to that inventory risk.
factors.name: Trade-clock relaxation-fraction size-peer snapback

factors.trading_idea: Take the empirical distribution of a name's own *horizon-matched* (6-bar) overlapping returns over the last 15 minutes and read it through a rank-dependent-utility kernel (Quiggin/Yaari dual theory): a symmetric inverse-S probability-weighting function puts POSITIVE weight on the tail quantile bins and NEGATIVE weight on the body bins, so the resulting L-statistic automatically contrasts tail asymmetry against body asymmetry of the same distribution, measured relative to an adaptive reference point (the trailing median block return) and in units of the name's own block volatility. Mechanically, tail asymmetry at 10-second resolution is created by rare liquidity-taking sweeps and stop cascades — transient impact that decays as depth replenishes — whereas body asymmetry is the slow grind of a sliced metaorder that keeps propagating; so forward 1-minute returns should load NEGATIVELY on tail asymmetry and POSITIVELY on body asymmetry, exactly the combination the inverse-S kernel forms. The distortion only converts into order flow where participants are present, so the statistic is scaled by an attention gate built from the name's trailing volume z-score. It should survive arbitrage because the object is level- and scale-invariant (it is a weighted combination of order statistics of centred, vol-normalised block returns, orthogonal by construction to last-return reversal, signed order-imbalance and realised-variance signals that desks actually run), it requires per-name overlapping-block quantile estimation rather than moments, and its 1-minute decay horizon caps capacity.
factors.name: Rank-dependent tail-salience vs body-skew split (attention gated)

factors.trading_idea: The parent showed that a name's *timing* (phase) relative to the cross-sectional mean field carries information, but it assumed one universal coupling constant and only used the instantaneous restoring torque, so its correction arrives on the oscillator's own cycle clock (IC peaked at 24 bars, not 6). The Adler equation dφ/dt = Δω − K·R·sin φ for a single driven oscillator says the entrainment outcome is governed by the *locking ratio* ρ = Δω/(K·R): when |ρ|<1 the name relaxes toward a fixed phase offset φ* = arcsin ρ at rate K·R·cos φ*, so the correction is delivered fast only for names whose empirically fitted coupling is strong; when |ρ|>1 the name has slipped out of lock and its phase runs at rate sign(Δω)·sqrt(Δω²−(K·R)²), which is continuation, not reversion. Estimating K per name by trailing regression of realised phase increments on the mean-field torque, and then weighting each name by the fraction 1−exp(−λ·6) of its phase correction that is actually delivered inside the fixed 6-bar horizon, converts the same physics into a horizon-matched forecast; the edge survives because standard lead-lag arbitrage is run in the amplitude/beta domain with one common adjustment speed and cannot separate a strongly-coupled 60-second laggard from a de-tuned name that merely looks late.
factors.name: Adler locking-ratio phase-slip delivery

factors.trading_idea: At the 60-second scale genuine news is priced almost instantly, so a name's measured 6-bar block sign-concordance (Rice-inverted rho, Parent A) is not a forecast of information continuation but a gauge of how much of its displacement is *mechanically accumulated* one-sided pressure (sliced metaorders / program flow) that still has to be repaid — which is why Parent A's realized direction is the fade, not the follow. Parent B supplies the missing per-bar state: the signed cross-sectional R-squared of the 6-bar dislocation regressed on the predicted weight-per-depth-minus-beta basket over-push tells us whether *this* bar's dislocations really are mechanical liquidity demand rather than idiosyncratic noise. The child therefore splits each name's dislocation into the flow-attributed part (faded with weight rising in both the bar's attribution trust and the name's own concordance, because a confirmed push inside an order-splitting name is pure accumulated transient impact) and the un-attributed remainder (faded in high-concordance grinders, but *ridden* in negative-rho, bounce-dominated names whose move has already snapped back and is thus fresh, un-repaid information). The interaction is the edge: B fades the predicted push blindly and pays for pushes in names that absorb them, while A applies one rho to a displacement that pools mechanical and informational sources — only routing A's per-name rho onto B's attributed/orthogonal decomposition puts the repayment where impact actually accumulated and lets the sign flip on the leftover.
factors.name: Rice-concordance-routed basket over-push repayment

factors.trading_idea: The parent's evaluation revealed the *opposite* of its stated story: magnitude-concentrated (jump-carried) 10s drift kept going over the next minute while sign-persistent (grind-carried) drift snapped back, and the effect was expressed too slowly (120-bar Rice window) to bite at the fixed 6-bar offset. The child rebuilds the same grind-vs-jump split as two order statistics of the *last 6 increments only*: the rolling median return is a magnitude-insensitive 'grind rate' (steady quote pressure / completed liquidity provision, which mean-reverts), while the mean-minus-median gap is an L-estimator of magnitude concentration (a trade-driven sweep). Trade-driven sweeps are self-exciting — a marketable order that clears depth begets further same-side orders and staggered information incorporation over a few tens of seconds (Hawkes kernel) — so the jump leg is gated by (i) the recency of the dominant increment inside the window and (ii) contemporaneous volume intensity relative to its 20-minute norm, which is exactly what makes the excitation decay-matched to a 60s forecast. Falsifiable: the jump leg must load positively and the median-grind leg negatively at 6 bars; if the jump leg reverses sign the mechanism is dead. It survives arbitrage because the counterintuitive direction (fade the smooth grind, follow the concentrated burst) is the wrong side of the naive short-horizon reversal trade, and capacity is capped by the impact cost of the very depth-clearing event that generates the signal.
factors.name: Order-statistic jump/grind split with Hawkes freshness gate

factors.trading_idea: An execution algorithm working a parent order releases child orders on a quasi-regular clock (POV/VWAP slicing every few seconds), which imprints a narrow-band *periodic* component on a name's 10-second bar volume; one-off aggression or news imprints a single broadband spike instead. Fisher's g-statistic — the share of a window's non-DC periodogram mass sitting in its single largest Fourier frequency — is the classical test for exactly this hidden periodicity and is null-normalised by construction, so it needs no per-name calibration window. The child therefore extrapolates a name's standardised 5-minute drift when its volume spectrum is peaked (unfinished schedule keeps pushing) and fades it when the spectrum is flat/broadband (transient impact that decays as depth refills). The edge persists because detecting a slicing clock demands per-name spectral estimation on sub-minute bars, the residual periodicity that survives an executor's deliberate size/timing randomisation is small and capacity-limited, and trading alongside the remaining child orders does not remove them.
factors.name: Fisher-g slicing-periodicity gate on short-run drift

factors.trading_idea: A 60-second beta-hedged displacement in a single name is either information about a fundamental factor its peers share, or it is that name's own liquidity demand / quote noise. The two cases can be separated with an instrument that the name itself cannot contaminate: the contemporaneous move of *industry peers that are not trading* in the same window. A quiet peer's quotes cannot be pushed by its own aggressive flow and cannot be dragged by basket execution that hits it in proportion to its own volume, so when quiet peers reprice in the same direction the displacement is common information and continues; when they stay still the displacement is name-specific pressure or quote shading and reverts. The child therefore follows displacement in proportion to silent-peer ratification and own aggressive-flow backing and fades it otherwise; the edge survives because harvesting it requires simultaneously monitoring the quiet side of the cross-section and warehousing 60-second directional risk in names whose flow may be toxic, which is exactly the risk market makers decline.
factors.name: Silent-peer-confirmed idiosyncratic displacement

factors.trading_idea: Parent A established that a sector-purged, participation-weighted close-location value reverts over the next minute because heavy traded size walks finite visible depth and the resulting displacement is mostly the temporary cost of immediacy. Parent B's state variable is the right conditioner but its economics were inverted: in 10-second bars evenly-spread volume is the signature of an *ongoing sliced metaorder* (order-splitting persistence, the most robust HFT regularity) whose footprint keeps pushing, whereas volume mass concentrated in one or two bars is a one-shot impatient sweep whose impact is overwhelmingly transient — which is exactly why B's 'even participation = uninformed, collect the gap' loading realized with the opposite sign. The child therefore keeps A's confirmed idiosyncratic displacement signal but scales the reversal by cross-sectionally centred *burstiness* (negative 30-bar volume-entropy innovation): full-strength snapback when the last 30 bars' volume is concentrated, attenuated and, in the most evenly-participating tail, flipped to continuation because the same liquidity demander will return to the book. The interaction carries edge neither parent has because it separates transient-impact displacement from live-metaorder displacement — A pools both and dilutes its reversal, B applies the state to a benchmark-gap leg the book already spans and with the wrong economic polarity.
factors.name: Participation-burstiness switched idio close-location snapback (6-bar)

factors.trading_idea: Only *unanticipated* order flow moves prices (Hasbrouck 1991): signed flow is long-memory because metaorders are sliced, so its predictable part is already impounded in the mid and the true state variable is the flow innovation e_t obtained by whitening signed (bulk-volume-classified) flow against its own trailing autocorrelation. The mid's response to such an innovation is not instantaneous — part is delivered over the following bars by slower quoters and correlated order splitting, and part relaxes as the book refills — so the object that actually forecasts a fixed 6-bar horizon is the *still-undelivered* portion of the response kernel, W_k = sum_{l=1..6} c_{k+l}, convolved with the last few innovations. The parent assumed the sign of that kernel (fade the flow-explained part, ride the quiet part) and therefore misdated its edge to 12 bars; here the sign and magnitude are *measured* per name and regime from trailing lagged covariances of returns on flow innovations, with per-lag empirical-Bayes t-stat shrinkage, so the forecast is horizon-matched by construction. The edge survives arbitrage because harvesting it means supplying liquidity against fresh flow within the same minute it arrives, capacity is bounded by the very impact being measured, and the kernel's sign flips across names and liquidity regimes so no static crowded momentum/reversal book can span it.
factors.name: Whitened flow innovation: undelivered impulse response over the next 6 bars

factors.trading_idea: Treat each large idiosyncratic 10-second move as a 'mainshock' whose transient (liquidity-taking) component must be repaid, and — as in the Omori–Utsu law for aftershocks — assume the repayment is metered not by wall-clock bars but by the *aftershock activity* that follows: repayment progresses with integrated post-shock trade/volatility flow via a hyperbolic saturation G = Acc/(Acc + kappa*Acc_typical), because depth only refills when someone actually quotes and trades. For every past shock the factor books what the name *should* have given back by now (phi*shock*G), compares it with what it actually gave back (the realized signed post-shock displacement), and forecasts (i) the fresh giveback increment expected over exactly the next 6 bars of projected activity plus (ii) an error-correction on the accumulated deficit or surplus, superposing all shocks in the last 30 bars ETAS-style. The edge survives arbitrage because ordinary reversal/impact-decay signals measure elapsed *bars*, so they systematically mistime repayment for names that went quiet after the shock (giveback still owed) versus names that churned heavily (already repaid, and any further retracement is an over-repayment that itself snaps back); the mispricing is small per event but events are frequent. Falsifiable: if repayment is governed by bar time rather than activity time the activity-clock deficit should carry no incremental information, and if over-retracement does not snap back the error-correction term should degrade the signal.
factors.name: Omori activity-clock giveback deficit

factors.trading_idea: Metaorders are sliced, so bulk-classified signed flow is strongly autocorrelated at the 10-second scale (Lillo–Mike–Farmer splitting); the *impact of flow that has not yet arrived* is therefore partly forecastable. Instead of decomposing displacement that already happened (the parent, whose continuation leg is slow and peaks past the fixed offset), this child builds an explicit forward object: a trailing AR(1) coefficient on BVC-signed sqrt-volume gives the geometric sum of expected signed flow over exactly the next 6 bars, which is converted into an expected return by the name's own origin-fit price-impact coefficient lambda and shrunk by the impact regression's R-squared. The sign is self-calibrating: names whose signed flow alternates (negative phi, maker-bounce regime) get a reversal prediction, names whose flow persists get continuation, so the factor is not disguised momentum. It survives arbitrage because the residual persistence is exactly the part liquidity providers cannot separate from informed splitting ex ante, and because harvesting it requires per-name lambda and phi estimates at 60-second capacity rather than one global impact constant.
factors.name: AR-persistent order-flow forecast times per-name impact (6-bar projection)

factors.trading_idea: Instead of splitting a name's flow (the parent's angle, which the book already spans), the child changes the mechanism: it builds each name a *synthetic twin* — the convex (non-negative, sum-to-one) combination of the other names whose 40-minute return path best replicates it — using exponentiated-gradient mirror descent on the simplex, refit on trailing windows only. The simplex constraint forces the tracker to be sparse and level-matched, so what is left over is a genuine relative-value spread between close substitutes rather than a diffuse OLS residual; such a spread is created by one-sided inventory demand in a single name and is closed by the very relative-value desks that watch substitute pairs, so it snaps back within about a minute. The falsifiable interaction is the gate: reversal strength must rise monotonically with (a) the twin's in-window tracking correlation and (b) the Herfindahl concentration of the twin's weights — a diffuse, poorly-tracking twin leaves mostly unhedged idiosyncratic news, which should show little or no reversal. The edge persists because per-name simplex tracking portfolios must be re-solved continuously across the whole cross-section and each closure earns only a fraction of the spread, making it capacity-limited rather than arbitraged away.
factors.name: Convex synthetic-twin pricing gap snapback

factors.trading_idea: Parent A's sqrt-volume-weighted freshness wedge is really a transient-impact meter: its realized IC is negative, i.e. fresh one-sided volume-weighted pressure at the 10-second scale is mostly unfinished inventory pressure that snaps back rather than information that continues — but fading it unconditionally is contaminated by pushes that are genuine delivery of a common shock. Parent B supplies exactly the missing state variable: a shock-selected distributed-lag kernel says how much systematic move a name still OWES (or has over-delivered) relative to the market impulse. The child fades the sector-purged fresh sqrt-weighted pressure only where the recent displacement was actually volume-backed (participation-weighted share of realized |return| executed in heavy bars — a router built from A's own square-root-law weighting, not from R-squared), leans on the owed-catch-up direction where the move happened in quiet bars, and amplifies the blend where the two channels concord (pushed against what it owes ⇒ pure transient impact, fade hard) while damping it where they disagree (pushed in the direction it owes ⇒ legitimate beta delivery, permanent, do not fade). The interaction is the edge: neither parent can distinguish transient impact from mechanical beta delivery, because A has no notion of what is owed and B has no notion of whether the displacement was paid for with volume.
factors.name: Backing-routed transient fade vs owed beta catch-up

factors.trading_idea: A given amount of short-horizon return autocorrelation can be produced two structurally different ways: many small same-signed increments (the footprint of a sliced parent order — Lillo–Farmer long-memory order splitting), or a few large increments of one sign embedded in otherwise alternating noise (a jump / liquidity-vacuum event). Rice's formula gives an exact, scale-free null linking the two: for a Gaussian process with lag-1 correlation rho, the probability that consecutive increments have opposite signs is arccos(rho)/pi, so the gap between the *observed* sign-flip frequency and that Gaussian-implied frequency isolates magnitude-concentration (gap > 0, jump-carried drift) from sign-persistence (gap < 0, grind-carried drift). Hypothesis: grind-carried drift keeps going over the next minute because the parent order is still working, whereas jump-carried drift overshot into thin depth and mean-reverts; the interaction gap x recent-return therefore predicts the next ~60s return with a negative sign. It is not arbitraged away because desks measure autocorrelation or momentum but almost never decompose it against a copula-based sign null, and the edge lives mostly in mid/small-cap names where capacity is capped by the very illiquidity that creates it.
factors.name: Rice-Formula Sign-Flip Excess: Grind vs Jump Decomposition of Drift

factors.trading_idea: Over a few minutes, the same signed price displacement means very different things depending on whether it was *paid for* with trades: the Bouchaud/Kyle propagator says the trade-aligned part of a move is largely transient inventory impact that decays as depth refills, whereas displacement that happens while the tape is quiet is pure quote revision and is close to permanent (and often still unfolding). I measure this without needing signed flow by comparing the trailing trend of price measured in *volume time* (correlation of price with the cumulative normalized-volume clock) against the same trend measured in *calendar time* (correlation with a linear ramp): the wedge is positive exactly when the displacement was concentrated in the window's heavy-volume bars, and negative when it accrued in the quiet bars. Because the calendar-time trend statistic is differenced out, the unconditional momentum loading is purged and only the trade-timing interaction survives, so the prediction is that high-wedge names revert and low-wedge (quiet-drift) names continue over the next minute. The edge should persist because it requires per-name path alignment between two clocks rather than any level of return or volume, it is a one-minute effect too small and too capacity-limited for slow capital, and trading it does not remove the inventory-unwind pressure that creates it.
factors.name: Volume-clock vs calendar-clock trend alignment wedge

factors.trading_idea: A metaorder worked by a scheduler spreads its child fills almost evenly across consecutive 10-second bars, so the *entropy of the bar-volume shares* over the last few minutes rises above the name's own recent level while price grinds directionally; the unfinished remainder of that parent order makes the grind continue over the next minute. A liquidity-consuming burst or news print does the opposite: volume mass concentrates in one or two bars (entropy drops) and the accompanying displacement is mostly transient impact that decays as depth refills, so the same displacement should be faded. The child keeps the parent's schedule-vs-burst split but expresses both legs with *bounded, scale-free* statistics — normalized Shannon entropy of volume shares (in [0,1]) minus its own trailing mean, times the Kaufman path-efficiency ratio (in [-1,1]) — eliminating the parent's fragile ratio-of-rolling-moments z-scores, clips and tanh that produced the in-sample/out-of-sample collapse. The edge survives arbitrage because detecting a schedule requires per-name conditioning on the *shape* of participation rather than its level, execution algos deliberately randomise size so the residual regularity is small and unrewarding to slow capital, and front-running the remaining children does not eliminate them — each new metaorder regenerates the signal.
factors.name: Volume-evenness entropy innovation gating path efficiency

factors.trading_idea: A peer-relative price displacement contains two unobserved states: one where a metaorder / information flow is still pushing the name away from its comparable-peer anchor (continuation), and one where the push has ended and Bouchaud-style transient price impact is relaxing back (reversion). The level of the displacement cannot distinguish these states — which is exactly why the parent's level-based OU weight only paid at 12–24 bars — but the *sign of the displacement's own velocity* can: once the displacement has stopped widening and started shrinking, the remaining transient-impact decay is front-loaded and lands inside a 60-second window. The child therefore trades the negated displacement multiplied by a smooth onset gate (velocity moving toward the anchor) and a flow-cessation gate (3-bar volume below its own 24-bar level, i.e. the push is over), which is a fast expression of the same relative-value idea. The edge persists because supplying it requires warehousing inventory in a name whose state (still-pushing vs relaxing) is only probabilistically identifiable in real time, and the per-event dollar profit is small relative to that inventory risk. Falsified if the IC at 6 bars is unchanged when the onset gate is replaced by a constant, or if still-widening displacements (gate ≈ 0) revert as strongly as already-turning ones.
factors.name: Reversion-onset (velocity-gated) peer-valuation displacement

factors.trading_idea: Parent A measures a locally explosive drift (kernel drift t-stat over a Newey-West HAC volatility) but classifies it only by the path's own Bartlett autocovariance texture, a slow statistic whose edge arrives at ~12 bars; Parent B shows the fast, decisive discriminator between mechanical dislocation and news is participation — variance burst per unit of volume burst — and that a one-sided (semivariance) burst is the dislocation's own signed footprint once leverage/size structure is demeaned out. The child uses BOTH displacement estimators as one confirmed signed displacement (kernel drift t-stat averaged with the bucket-residual downside-minus-upside semivariance innovation, which agree only when a genuine directional displacement just happened) and flips its sign with a two-channel state gate: order-splitting autocovariance texture (informed → continue) minus thin-book vacuum (variance far exceeding participation → mechanical → snap back). The interaction is what neither parent has: A's burst amplitude gets B's fast, volume-dated clock so the payoff lands inside the 6-bar window instead of leaking to 12 bars, while B's reversal signal gets A's drift-t-stat direction and persistence-texture veto, so informed metaorders are not faded.
factors.name: Vacuum/texture-gated confirmed drift-burst flip

factors.trading_idea: The parent assumed a fixed power-law propagator G(l)=(1+l/4)^-0.45; that kernel relaxes far too slowly for a 10-second clock, which is exactly why its predicted snapback only materialised by 24 bars.  Instead of assuming the kernel, I estimate it: at each bar the lag-profile R(l)=cov(idio z-return_t, z-flow_{t-l})/var(z-flow) for l=1..17 is measured from a trailing 300-bar window and shrunk 60/40 toward its cross-sectional (pooled) value, giving a noise-controlled empirical impulse response that lets the data say how fast — and with what sign — already-executed flow is still moving price.  The forecast of the next 6 bars is then the exact conditional expectation implied by that kernel, sum_k f_{t-k}[S(k+6)-S(k)] with S the cumulative response, so the signal is horizon-matched by construction and can predict continuation for names whose measured response is still rising and relaxation for names whose response has already turned over — a sign flexibility the parent's monotone kernel structurally forbade.  The edge persists because harvesting it means standing in front of (or behind) the tail of someone else's execution with inventory risk, and because the kernel must be re-estimated continuously per name — a capacity-limited liquidity-provision trade, not a static formula.
factors.name: Empirically-calibrated flow response kernel, 6-bar forecast

factors.trading_idea: Parent showed that the pooled precision-whitened dislocation is dominated by slow information diffusion (its IC only builds out to 24 bars), while the genuinely fast, mechanically reversible piece is the part of the move that a *basket program* just pushed into a name. This child keeps the parent's causal Mahalanobis geometry but replaces the single cap-weight scalar projection with a multi-basket GLS attribution: each bar's whitened cross-section is regressed (in the trailing precision metric, with block-constant sector cap-weight regressors) onto the sector-basket weight vectors, giving a per-name fitted mechanical displacement f. Transient impact relaxes only once liquidity demand stops arriving, so the accumulated 3-bar attributed push is faded only when the name's own attributed-push intensity has just collapsed relative to its exponentially-decayed recent level (a Hawkes-style cessation test), and only when the name was actually swept (its dollar-volume share during the push exceeded its own norm) — quote-drift displacement without trades is staleness catch-up and continues, which is why the unconditional version cancels. The edge survives arbitrage because it requires jointly observing the correlation-metric basket attribution, the cessation timing and the name-level participation within one minute; whoever supplies liquidity to the terminated program must be paid for inventory over exactly this horizon.
factors.name: GLS sector-basket push cessation relaxation

factors.trading_idea: Parent A splits recent drift into quote-driven (near-zero-volume bars) and impact-driven (traded bars) components but cannot tell genuine one-sided quote shading from stale-mid / bounce noise — which is exactly the falsification it flags. Parent B's Rice null, arccos(rho1)/pi, supplies that test, so the child estimates the sign-flip excess *separately on the quiet-bar subsequence and on the active-bar subsequence* (using only consecutive same-class, non-flat pairs, with the lag-1 correlation estimated on the identical masked pairs so the Gaussian null is apples-to-apples). Quiet drift is followed only when its own increments are sign-persistent (grind-like, gap<0 = a maker walking quotes one way) and discounted or fought when its increments flip more than the Gaussian null implies (gap>0 = stale-mid bounce noise); active drift is faded by default and faded hardest when it is magnitude-concentrated (jump into thin depth), while grind-like active drift — a sliced parent order still working — has its fade attenuated or reversed. The interaction carries edge neither parent has alone because the Rice gap is only interpretable once you know whether the increments were printed with volume, and the quiet/active drift split is only tradeable once noise-carried quiet drift has been separated from repricing-carried quiet drift; a short decay-weighted drift window (~12 bars, newest-weighted) keeps the signal anchored at the fixed 6-bar offset instead of drifting to the 24-bar peak of both parents.
factors.name: Quiet/Active Drift Split Gated by Regime-Conditional Rice Sign-Flip Excess

factors.trading_idea: Parent A knows *which* peer spreads are economically real (a dislocation in multiple space inside a tight, homogeneous peer group is a genuine relative-value spread, not a business-mix artefact) but not *when* the spread will close, so its edge leaks out to 24 bars; Parent B knows *when* relaxation starts (displacement velocity has turned back toward the anchor and the pushing flow has stopped) but measures the anchor in raw peer log-price space, where a wide, incomparable peer group makes the anchor itself noise. The child multiplies the two states: a comparability-weighted consensus dislocation across three independent multiple bases (P/B, P/S, P/OCF) is traded only when (i) the peer group's multiples are tight, (ii) the channels agree on the sign and size of the dislocation (a cross-basis coherence ratio that a single-basis parent cannot see, and which discriminates true price dislocation from denominator/step-function artefacts), and (iii) the dislocation's own velocity has turned toward the anchor with the flow having ceased. Finally, a horizon clock — the trailing lag-1 persistence of the dislocation mapped to the expected fraction (1 - rho^6) that decays inside six bars — sizes each name so the position is concentrated exactly where the relaxation lands at the fixed 6-bar offset, which is the failure mode both parents were flagged for. The interaction carries edge neither has alone: credibility without timing pays late, timing without credibility times noise, and the decay clock converts a slow relative-value spread into a horizon-matched one.
factors.name: Comparability-weighted multi-channel dislocation with onset and decay clock

factors.trading_idea: The parent proved that a peer-relative price residual is predictable, but its predictability was concentrated in slow scales, so the IC grew monotonically out to 24 bars: a level-based residual is a sum of frequency components whose relaxation half-lives differ by an order of magnitude, and components with half-life >> 6 bars contribute almost nothing to a 6-bar-ahead change (they behave locally like trends) while the very fastest component is largely bounce noise that has already relaxed inside the bar. The child therefore decomposes the sector-relative log price into near-orthogonal causal bandpass channels (cascaded EWMA differences with half-lives 2/6/18/54 bars) plus one interaction channel (fast dislocation signed by the standing slow displacement) and learns, by a trailing cross-sectionally-pooled ridge regression of the *realized* 6-bar peer-relative return on the state lagged by exactly 6 bars, the horizon-matched gain of each band. Because the target of the fit IS the 6-bar change, the estimator allocates weight only to the bands that actually pay at the fixed offset and can assign opposite signs to fast (reverting) and slow (trending) bands instead of forcing a single fade. The edge survives arbitrage because the profitable band is the mid-frequency one whose harvest requires ~60-second turnover at small per-event size, and because the band gains rotate with the liquidity regime, so a static reversal rule mis-times them.
factors.name: Multiscale band-gain pooled direct 6-bar projection

factors.trading_idea: Whether a 60-second, peer-relative price displacement reverts or sticks depends on who is resting on the other side of it: valuation-sensitive liquidity (value/quant limit orders, rebalancers) supplies size against moves that push a name *further* from the relative price its fundamentals justify, but steps aside — or joins — when the same move *closes* that gap, because then the move is information being incorporated rather than inventory being dumped. The child therefore does not trade the level of a slow anchor deviation (which is why the parent's edge only matured at 12-24 bars); it trades a horizon-matched, recency-weighted 6-bar sector-relative return multiplied by a signed interaction with a slow, quality-adjusted relative-valuation gap, so the fast reversal is amplified for gap-widening moves and flipped to continuation for gap-closing ones.
