The edge survives arbitrage because the profitable leg requires warehousing inventory in exactly the names where the fundamental anchor is contested, the per-event dollar profit is tiny relative to that inventory risk, and the conditioning object (a cross-sectionally quality-adjusted value residual refreshed only quarterly) is cheap to know but expensive to act on at 10-second frequency. Falsified if the interaction term carries no incremental IC at 6 bars over the unconditioned reversal (i.e. if reversal strength is independent of whether the move widened or closed the fundamental relative-value gap), or if gap-closing displacements revert as strongly as gap-widening ones.
factors.name: Value-gap-direction conditioned fast peer snapback

factors.trading_idea: A between-bar seam (open minus previous close) is a pure quote relocation, but it means two economically opposite things depending on what happened in the bar it follows: after a *traded* bar it is liquidity providers walking back the transient impact they just absorbed (reciprocation → fade the body push), while after a *silent* bar it is a maker ramping their reservation price during an inventory / adverse-selection search with nobody trading against it (continuation → ride the ramp). Parent A pooled all bars when estimating its reciprocation fingerprint, so silent-seam continuation contaminated its absorption estimate; parent B measured its silence channel on total bar returns, so within-bar impact contaminated the ramp. The child routes the seam channel by the smooth volume state of the preceding bar, estimates the two per-name response coefficients separately (traded-body→next-seam reciprocation, and silent-seam→next-seam ramp persistence), and uses each as the gate on its own horizon-matched fresh (fast-minus-slow EWMA band-pass) leg. The interaction is the edge: only the volume-state split makes the seam's sign identifiable, so the fade leg stops being diluted by ramps and the ramp leg stops being diluted by impact — something neither parent can do alone.
factors.name: Volume-state routed seam: ramp vs body reciprocation

factors.trading_idea: Parent B splits a short move into a flow-explained (transient, decaying) part and an unpaid-for (permanent) part, but treats every name's book as identical; Parent A shows that whether a mid sits pinned on a grid with volume being absorbed at the touch is itself a strong, measurable book state. The interaction is the edge: an unpaid-for displacement in a name that normally sits pinned (high quote inattention / grid-binding) is a genuine level revision that the pinned queue and slower quoters must still follow, whereas the same unpaid displacement in a freely diffusing name is mostly mid-bounce noise; symmetrically, flow-explained impact snaps back hardest where volume has been absorbed *without* the mid moving (a deep, refillable queue) and much less where the queue was thin, because there the move stuck for informational reasons. So the two Parent-A state variables — pin frequency and volume absorbed per pinned bar — gate the two legs of Parent B's decomposition differently, which neither parent can do alone: A had no way to sign its impulse (its declared direction was contradicted) and B had no way to know which book a move happened in. Kernel and beta windows are shortened to match the fixed 6-bar horizon.
factors.name: Pin-binding gated propagator permanence wedge

factors.trading_idea: For any hedged spread the Lo-MacKinlay variance ratio of the residual return series is the sufficient statistic for the sign of its own short-horizon predictability: VR(q)<1 means the summed autocovariances of the residual are negative, so a fresh residual impulse is expected to be given back over the next q bars, while VR(q)>1 means the residual is a slow information leak and the impulse should extend. The parent gated a *one-sided* snapback of the valuation-matched peer residual on hedge R-squared, which measures only whether the hedge fits and not whether the traded object (the spread) is actually stationary; that mis-signs the sizeable minority of names whose hedged residual is trending, which is the likeliest source of the parent's weak in-sample IC. The child therefore keeps the valuation-matched (multiple-space kernel) peer basket and the 3-bar beta-hedged impulse, but multiplies the impulse by (1 - VR) of that name's own residual measured at exactly the forecast horizon q=6, turning a pure reversal factor into a two-sided reversion/continuation factor whose sign is set by measured spread stationarity. Falsifiable: if the impulse's forward IC is the same for residuals with VR well below 1 as for those with VR above 1 (i.e. the (1-VR) interaction adds nothing over a flat reversal amplitude), the mechanism is wrong; the edge persists because estimating a per-name residual variance ratio against a point-in-time, fundamentals-matched peer kernel on a 10-second tape is operationally awkward and its capacity is capped by the thinness of each valuation neighbourhood.
factors.name: Variance-ratio-signed valuation-matched hedged-spread impulse

factors.trading_idea: The parent showed that a valuation-neighbourhood hedged residual carries edge, but it identified the 'tier-common' part with a noisy 360-bar second-stage regression loading and then simply threw that part away. The identifying statistic for whether a dislocation is inventory pressure or genuine tier repricing is not a trailing loading but the *contemporaneous cross-sectional geometry of the neighbourhood*: (a) the name's residual measured in units of the dispersion of its own neighbours' residuals (a relative-value z, not a time-series z), and (b) the sign coherence of the neighbourhood's moves, corrected for the effective number of peers so that small tiers do not look coherent by luck. When neighbours move incoherently, a large peer-dispersion-scaled residual is one desk pushing one name and it snaps back within a minute; when the whole valuation tier moves in concert, no single arbitrageur can close it (it requires trading the entire neighbourhood at once) so the tier impulse keeps propagating and laggards catch up. Falsifiable: if the coherence-weighted convex blend does not beat either leg alone — i.e. if incoherent-tier residuals do not revert faster than coherent-tier ones, or coherent tier impulses do not continue — the inventory-vs-information decomposition is wrong and the parent's edge was undifferentiated peer reversal. The edge survives arbitrage because it requires joining point-in-time per-share fundamentals to a 10-second tape to define the neighbourhood and then computing *within-neighbourhood* second moments and sign concordance each bar, and its capacity is bounded by the handful of tight valuation tiers.
factors.name: Tier-coherence split of peer-dispersion-scaled dislocation

factors.trading_idea: Parent A shows that a break out of a *laminar* (highly recurrent) band continues, because the depth that was defending the level and the stops clustered just outside it have just been consumed; Parent B shows that a purely peer-idiosyncratic dislocation is only repaired when the peer basket is live enough to hedge it. The child measures the recurrence-quantified laminarity and the band-clearing escape on the *peer-residual* price path (own log-price minus its leave-one-out industry basket path) — the only path a relative-value liquidity provider actually warehouses — and makes continuation require BOTH a defended residual level AND absent hedge capacity: the state weight is the multiplicative gate rank(laminarity) x (1 - rank(leave-one-out peer activity)), cross-sectionally centred. The interaction is the edge neither parent has: A's laminar escapes are silently mixed with peer-common drift and are arbitraged back whenever the hedge legs are quotable, while B's hedgeability gate has almost no standalone signal because it does not know whether the dislocation broke a defended anchor or merely diffused; only escapes that clear a long-defended residual band while peers are too quiet to hedge keep running over the next minute, and escapes failing either condition are transient impact that is repaid.
factors.name: Peer-residual laminar band escape gated by hedge-leg quietness

factors.trading_idea: Parent B knows *when* a market move is mechanical basket flow (the cross-sectional volume-allocation vector tilts toward the cap-weight vector) and *which* names should be over-pushed by it (impact elasticity in excess of their systematic loading), but it never checks whether the predicted over-push actually landed in the name; Parent A measures the name's true idiosyncratic displacement with a tail-robust double hedge but has no idea whether that displacement is flow or news. The child multiplies them: it uses the tail-robust (winsorized) beta — not the jump-contaminated OLS beta — inside the elasticity wedge, forms the *predicted* mechanical over-push (wedge x program-weighted standardised market move over the same 6 bars), and fades the robustly-hedged realized displacement with conviction proportional to sign-confirmation between prediction and realization; unconfirmed residuals are treated as information and de-weighted. The OLS-vs-robust hedge disagreement then acts as Parent A's laggy-adjustment gate: for jump-contaminated (Epps-slow) names the basket push has not finished landing, so the confirmed dislocation continues instead of reverting and the gate flips sign. The interaction carries edge neither has alone: attribution of a per-name dislocation to a *detected* liquidity-demand event, with the attribution measured by an estimator that is not itself corrupted by co-jumps.
factors.name: Program-flow attributed robust-hedge confirmation snapback

factors.trading_idea: Keep the parent's valuation-matched kernel peer basket (peers at a similar point in P/B, P/S, P/OCF space price the same kind of cash-flow claim, so the beta-hedged spread is a genuinely stationary object), but replace its two ad-hoc amplitude gates — hedge R-squared and a crude volume damp — with the quantity the signal-extraction problem actually calls for. Model the cumulated hedged spread as a local-level process, permanent random-walk component plus transient pricing error; the Roll identity says the trailing lag-1 autocovariance of the hedged spread increments equals minus the transient variance, so a purely trailing estimator gives each name a direct, model-based estimate of the fraction of its dislocation that is temporary, and the steady-state Kalman gain implied by that noise ratio gives the correct speed at which the permanent level should be tracked. Fade only the filtered transient deviation, scaled by the estimated transient variance share: names whose hedged spread is mostly permanent repricing get near-zero weight even if the raw dislocation is large. Falsifiable: if snapback strength is flat in the Roll transient-variance share, or if the adaptive-gain filtered deviation does no better than a fixed-window impulse, the signal-extraction mechanism is wrong and the parent's crude gates were doing the work; the edge persists because estimating a per-name permanent/transient decomposition on a valuation-matched hedge basket requires joining point-in-time per-share fundamentals to a 10-second tape, which pure microstructure arbitrageurs do not do, and capacity is capped by the small number of tight valuation neighbourhoods.
factors.name: Roll noise-share gated valuation-hedged spread snapback

factors.trading_idea: A name's running shortfall versus its beta-implied market response (the 'backlog') mixes two very different things: market information the name simply has not repriced yet (owed catch-up) and genuine idiosyncratic news traded through its own book (no catch-up, often later reversal). The child keeps the self-netting backlog state but weights its *composition* at the bar level: shortfall accumulated on bars where the name barely traded or its mid was frozen is trusted as unabsorbed market information, whereas shortfall accumulated on heavy-volume bars is discounted as idio news. It then multiplies the backlog by a per-name, empirically calibrated closure rate — the trailing OLS loading of realised 6-bar returns on the backlog observed 6 bars earlier (strictly causal) — so exposure concentrates in names that have demonstrably delivered their catch-up *at the fixed 6-bar offset* rather than instantly (already gone by t+1) or beyond it (where the parent's IC flipped negative). The edge persists because it is created by non-synchronous repricing in thin, inattentive names at 10-second frequency, where monitoring cost, not information, is the binding constraint; it is falsified if the inactivity composition share adds nothing over the raw backlog, or if the horizon-calibrated closure loading has no cross-sectional information (i.e. a constant loading works equally well).
factors.name: Inactivity-composition beta backlog with horizon-calibrated closure rate

factors.trading_idea: A mid move printed while nobody trades is a quote-only price revision: part of it is a genuine relocation of the makers' reservation price (queue depletion / adverse-selection repricing, which persists) and part is one-sided quote withdrawal and flicker (a transitory stale-mid artefact that snaps back when depth refills). Path efficiency versus its driftless k^(-1/2) null separates the two candidate states, but the *sign* of the permanence is not a universal constant — it depends on which population of quote revisions currently dominates a given name, which is exactly why the parent's pooled continuation prior was contradicted by the data. The child therefore stops asserting the direction and estimates it online: for each name it runs a trailing, horizon-matched (6-bar) univariate regression of realised normalised return on its own lagged quiet-displacement channels (efficient-relocation channel and wobble channel, kept separate because their permanence has opposite sign), shrinks the coefficients toward the cross-sectional pool by event count, and reports the fitted expected 6-bar return. The edge survives arbitrage because monetising it requires paying the spread in names that are momentarily quiet and thin — unattractive round-trip economics for slower participants — and it is falsified if the pooled efficient-channel beta is not positive, the wobble-channel beta not negative, or if the fitted expectation carries no more forward information than raw quiet displacement.
factors.name: Online-Calibrated Permanence of Untraded Quote Relocation (efficient vs wobble split)

factors.trading_idea: The parent showed that measured block persistence times displacement predicts with the opposite sign; the reason is diagnostic, not a constant to flip: a short-window autocorrelation estimate (SE ~0.17 vs true dispersion ~0.03) is dominated by the episode currently in progress, and an in-progress concordant run is a transient-impact chain (sliced metaorder, trend-chasing HFT) whose price overshoot decays within a minute, not a stationary property of the name. The child therefore separates the two objects that the parent conflated: a low-variance Rice-inverted concordance ACF over lags 1-11, weighted exactly as the h=6 block projection requires, estimated on a long window that is embargoed 12 bars before the current displacement window, measures the name's structural reversion speed; the same statistic over the last 90 bars measures the concordance *innovation* injected by the live episode. The effective projection coefficient is structural minus innovation (2*B_long - B_short) and is cross-sectionally demeaned so the common reversal level that the book already spans is removed, leaving only relative reversion-speed dispersion plus relative overshoot — an edge that persists because reversion desks apply one common speed to the whole cross-section and harvesting per-name dispersion requires continuous, heavy-tail-robust, embargoed re-estimation whose per-name payoff is tiny.
factors.name: Rice concordance-innovation overshoot

factors.trading_idea: A standing peer-relative displacement is not one object with one age: it is a superposition of impact increments of many ages, and under a power-law propagator G(t)=(1+t/t0)^-beta the slice of an increment that unwinds inside the next 6 bars is increment x [G(a)-G(a+6)], which is hugely front-loaded in a (the last bar contributes ~4x more decayable displacement than a bar 8 minutes old). The parent multiplied the whole *level* by a single scalar excursion age, so its predictor was still dominated by old, slowly-relaxing layers and its IC therefore peaked at 24 bars; convolving the *increments* of the peer-relative log price with the analytic remaining-decay kernel horizon-matches the predictor to the fixed 6-bar offset by construction, and it automatically distinguishes a displacement built by one fresh jump (mostly decayable now) from an equally large one accumulated slowly (mostly not). The raw kernel prediction is then converted into a calibrated expected return by a causal per-name trailing OLS gain of the realized standardized 6-bar peer-relative move on the lagged kernel predictor, empirical-Bayes shrunk to the cross-section, so names whose impact is permanent or self-exciting keep a continuation sign instead of being forcibly faded. The edge survives arbitrage because capturing the first-minute slice requires paying spread and turning inventory over every few bars for a few basis points per event, while the relative-value players who warehouse the same gap are paid on the slow multi-minute leg.
factors.name: Age-layered propagator increment relaxation (h=6)

factors.trading_idea: Parent B computes the horizon-matched Bouchaud decay increment sum_k f_{t-k}[G(k)-G(k+6)] — exactly how much of the already-executed flow's impact is *due* to relax over the next 6 bars — but it can only ever bet that this impact reverts, discounted by whether the metaorder is still running. Parent A supplies the missing state variable telling us whether that impact was ever transient at all: the Dirichlet-null wedge between the Herfindahl of squared-return shares (Dirichlet(1/2) null 3/(k+2)) and of volume shares (Dirichlet(1) null 2/(k+1)) over the same 6 bars separates a liquidity-vacuum jump (price concentration unmatched by flow → thin depth, mechanical transient impact that snaps back) from an evenly-sliced parent order carried by clustered flow (Lillo–Farmer → permanent repricing that keeps going). The child therefore uses the propagator increment purely as a signed, horizon-matched *amplitude* and lets the wedge decide the sign, with the two legs additionally gated by opposite sides of the same Hawkes liveness measure: relaxation is harvested only when the move was vacuum-like AND the execution has visibly died, continuation only when the price path was evenly sliced AND the flow is still self-exciting. Neither parent can do this: A knows the mechanism but measures amplitude with a stale price displacement, B knows the horizon-matched amplitude but has no way to tell transient impact from permanent repricing, so it dilutes both regimes into one reversion bet.
factors.name: Transient-fraction gated propagator relaxation (Dirichlet wedge × flow liveness)

factors.trading_idea: An intra-bar excursion that is given back before the bar closes is a mixture of a permanent (information) component and a transient (inventory) component, and the split is identified by how much size the excursion had to consume: if the probe was achieved while the book was deep (high traded volume per unit of relative range, i.e. low Kyle lambda), real hidden size was cleared and the mid is left temporarily *below* the level that aggressors were already willing to pay, so quotes drift back toward the wick over the next minute; if the same excursion happened on a thin book (little volume per unit range), it is mid-quote flicker with no cleared inventory and it mean-reverts away from the wick. This explains why the parent's realized sign contradicted its 'rejection' story: on heavy-participation bars the wick side is the informed side, not the rejected one, so the correct expression is a continuous interaction between range-normalised wick asymmetry and the bar's standardised depth state, which by construction predicts opposite forward signs for quiet-bar and deep-bar wicks. The edge persists because monetising it means taking liquidity exactly where resting size was just depleted (paying spread into a thin book) and the depth/geometry state refreshes every ten seconds, so it cannot be warehoused; it is falsified if quiet-bar and deep-bar wick asymmetry carry the same forward sign, or if the depth-weighted aggregate has no sign at 6 bars.
factors.name: Depth-conditioned excursion permanence wedge

factors.trading_idea: The parent's realized sign says common-flow bursts CONTINUE and idiosyncratic bursts REVERT — the opposite of an information story, but exactly what a metaorder-lifetime story predicts: basket / index flow is generated by slow, long-lived parent orders that are still being sliced, whereas a single-name burst at the 10-second scale is usually one aggressive sweep followed by quote replenishment. So the correct conditioner is not 'is this flow informed?' but 'how much of this order flow is still to come?', which is observable in real time from the persistence (lag-1 memory) of the name's activity innovation, the slope of the current burst (rising vs already decayed), and — as a weaker third proxy — the share of the activity innovation explained by a common activity factor. The child therefore continues a market-relative displacement when the accompanying flow is long-lived/accelerating and fades it when the flow was a one-off spike. The edge survives arbitrage because it requires per-name, per-bar estimation of flow lifetime and then taking inventory risk on the opposite side of a decayed sweep inside a minute — capacity-limited liquidity provision that a static reversal or volume-spike rule mis-signs roughly half the time.
factors.name: Flow-lifetime gated displacement relay

factors.trading_idea: Parent A showed the mid-drift printed in (near-)zero-volume bars continues while the drift paid for with volume reverts, but it treats every quiet bar alike — so genuine inventory/adverse-selection repricing is pooled with flickering stale-mid noise, exactly the falsification A flagged. Parent B's Rice/geometric run machinery is the natural discriminator, but on the pooled clock quiet grind and traded jumps are entangled, which is why it had no standalone edge and only worked as a state variable. The child subordinates time to the quiet bars themselves: it measures the *live* run length of consecutive same-signed quiet-bar increments against the geometric null implied by Rice's formula applied to the lag-1 autocorrelation of the quiet-bar subsequence, and uses that signed coherence to weight the quiet (long) leg; symmetrically it weights the traded (short) leg by how concentrated the traded-bar move was in a single depth-consuming print, since one-print impact is the transient part that decays while spread-out traded drift is informed. The interaction is the edge: only directionally coherent silent repricing is worth continuing and only single-print traded impact is worth fading — a distinction neither parent can draw alone.
factors.name: Quiet-clock run coherence vs concentrated traded impact

factors.trading_idea: At 10-second resolution the two dominant non-random forces are (a) parent orders being sliced by VWAP/POV schedulers and (b) one-off aggressive impact that decays as depth refills. These leave opposite fingerprints in the *shape* of the volume series: a working schedule makes a name's bar volume unusually metronomic (its own coefficient of variation collapses relative to its recent norm) while pushing price one way, whereas news-driven aggression makes volume bursty (CV spikes) and the accompanying price move is largely transient impact. So the same standardised drift should be extrapolated when volume has just turned smooth and faded when volume has just turned bursty; the factor is the product of drift z-score and a bounded volume-smoothness shock. The edge survives arbitrage because schedule detection requires per-name conditioning on volume regularity rather than level, and because executing algos deliberately randomise size — the residual regularity is small, unrewarding to slow capital, and its exploitation (following the unfinished parent) does not remove the remaining child orders.
factors.name: Metronome-volume schedule gate on short-run drift

factors.trading_idea: On 10-second mid bars the intra-bar high/low record where aggression actually reached while the bar-end mid is a stale sample, so an unconverted wick is either (a) a one-off depletion of a thin level that the mid catches up to within the next minute, or (b) evidence of hidden replenished size sitting at a level that keeps pushing price back. The state variable that separates these is *refill evidence*: how much volume traded in bars that re-tested the pre-existing local extreme without breaking it by more than one grid quantum — a single, normal-volume test means the queue was consumed and not refilled (continuation toward the probed side), whereas repeated heavy tests that all fail mean an iceberg/replenishing limit order is absorbing flow (reversion away from the probed side). The signal therefore keeps the parent's fresh probe-excursion geometry but replaces its slow, book-correlated beta-residual displacement channel with this fast level-test counter, so the polarity is resolved from information dated in the last 30–120 seconds and pays off over the fixed 6-bar offset. The edge persists because detecting non-replenishment requires per-name adaptive quantum and level bookkeeping at 10-second resolution and the expected move is a small multiple of the tick, so it is compensation for supplying/removing immediacy rather than a risk-free arbitrage; it is falsifiable — if refill evidence is uninformative, forcing polarity to a constant +1 should not degrade the IC.
factors.name: Level-refill-evidence switched probe catch-up

factors.trading_idea: Execution algorithms and reactive quoting are *policies*, so they stamp short repeating symbolic motifs onto the tape: 'tick up, pause on heavy volume, tick up' is a child order slicing into a resting queue, while 'up, up, up' on thin volume is a quote being walked with nothing behind it. Under the efficient/i.i.d. null the conditional mean of the next-minute return given any 3-symbol motif (quantized move sign/magnitude) crossed with the current activity state is exactly zero; if the policy mix is locally stationary per name, those conditional means are non-zero, name-specific and estimable in real time. The child is therefore a per-name nonparametric analog forecast: a hierarchical empirical-Bayes estimate of E[6-bar forward log return | motif x activity], shrunk cell -> motif -> unconditional, and cross-sectionally orthogonalised against the plain 6-bar move so that only motif *shape* (not net displacement) can drive it. It resists arbitrage because the estimate lives in small, rotating cells (the dominant algo and its slicing rhythm change within hours), it must be re-estimated per name per bar over a discrete state space rather than read off a linear feature, and its capacity is capped by the size of the child orders that create the motifs.
factors.name: Symbolic motif conditional drift (activity-split, hierarchical shrinkage)

factors.trading_idea: Resting depth accumulates inside the price region a name has been occupying and is thin outside it, so the informative question about a fresh escape from that occupation band is not 'was there volume?' but 'how much price did each unit of volume buy?'. An escape achieved with abnormally large displacement per sqrt(volume) reveals that the outside book is empty (quotes withdrawn, no absorption) and the mid must keep walking; an escape that required abnormally heavy volume per unit displacement reveals a thick outside book that is absorbing the metaorder, so the displacement is a paid-for overshoot that snaps back. The child therefore replaces the parent's raw participation/tightness gates (which conflate absorption with conviction and produced non-monotone horizon decay) with a single sqrt-impact-law efficiency z-score, and replaces the crude freshness fraction with an exponentially-decayed event clock counting bars since the mid was last inside its band, so the factor is sparse and fires only in the first few bars after ignition. The edge persists because the very shallowness that creates it caps capacity, and exploiting it requires per-name real-time joint estimation of an occupation band, an event-time clock and a relative price-impact-efficiency statistic within a few ticks.
factors.name: Value-area escape gated by impact efficiency (vacuum vs absorption)

factors.trading_idea: Pairwise lag-1 lead-lag scores between peers form an antisymmetric flow on the peer graph; by the Helmholtz-Hodge decomposition that flow splits into a *gradient* part generated by a scalar latency potential (a genuine leader/laggard ladder) and a *curl* part (cyclic, non-transitive noise that carries no ordering). The least-squares Hodge potential of that network collapses algebraically to a two-term object per name — the asymmetry between cov(own return today, peer-aggregate return k bars ago) and cov(peer-aggregate today, own return k bars ago) — so the ladder is computable exactly without any O(N^2) matrix, and antisymmetrising automatically annihilates the symmetric part of the cross-covariance (common autocorrelation and contemporaneous beta contamination), which is what makes ordinary lead-lag regressions unreliable. I then convert the per-lag gradient responses into a *horizon-matched* distributed-lag projection: summing the response kernel over the lags whose mass still falls inside the next 6 bars gives the fraction of the peer basket's last 60 seconds of movement that a laggard has not yet delivered, and that undelivered amount is the predicted 6-bar return; the estimate is shrunk by a gradient-stability gate (agreement between a long- and a short-window potential), which is a cheap proxy for gradient-vs-curl energy share. It is falsifiable: if the antisymmetrised kernel (beta_k - gamma_k) is replaced by the raw forward kernel beta_k the 6-bar IC should fall materially, and if the ladder were pure curl the stability gate would add nothing. The edge survives arbitrage because a latency ladder is only identifiable over long trailing windows while its members rotate, and harvesting it requires simultaneously executing a laggard against a peer basket for a few basis points of expected delivery, i.e. real inventory and hedge-slippage risk per event.
factors.name: Hodge-gradient latency ladder with horizon-matched owed delivery

factors.trading_idea: The parent confirmed the decomposition (name-specific flow impact continues, basket-common overpush and flow-unexplained quote shading revert) but drove every leg with the SAME business clock — more forecast volume meant faster delivery for all three — which is mechanically wrong for the reverting legs and explains why its 6-bar IC was flat while the 12-24 bar IC flipped sign: overpush does not relax while the metaorder is still executing, it relaxes in the quiet that follows, so busy names delivered continuation early and reversal late. The child forecasts the next-6-bar volume rate from a Hawkes-style exponentially-decaying excitation (current excess rate times the mean kernel decay over h=1..6, so the forecast mean-reverts toward the name's own base rate instead of persisting) and then ROUTES the same accumulated, still-owed displacement between two clocks: the permanent idiosyncratic leg and the stale-quote (quiet) leg are delivered by incoming trading (weight phi/(1+phi), since information is impounded and arbitrageurs correct shaded quotes only when they trade), whereas the basket-common overpush leg is delivered by the absence of trading (weight 1/(1+phi)). Falsifiable: the dual-clock composite should have higher 6-bar IC than the parent's single-theta gate and a horizon profile that no longer inverts by 12 bars; specifically the common-leg reversal should carry its IC in names whose forecast volume rate is decaying (phi<1) and ~none where phi>1, while the idio/quiet legs should show the opposite conditioning. The edge persists because it requires jointly estimating flow commonality, a per-name Kyle lambda, a volume-clock owed balance and a decaying arrival-intensity forecast on a 10-second grid, and the positions it takes are exactly the impact-cost-bounded fast states where arbitrage capacity is limited.
factors.name: Dual-clock (busy vs quiet) delivery split of idio, basket and quiet displacement

factors.trading_idea: At 10-second scale the map from a name's state (relative displacement, own-history volume intensity) to its expected market-neutral return one horizon ahead is a genuinely two-dimensional, non-additive surface: the same displacement is followed by snapback when it was produced while unusual volume was crossing a thin book, and by continuation when the mid moved on ordinary flow, so the informative part of the surface is its *interaction* curvature rather than either margin. Production alpha books are built from additive, sign-fixed terms and therefore span only the two marginals; the double-centred interaction (two-way ANOVA residual of the surface) is by construction orthogonal to any displacement-only reversal factor and any volume-only liquidity factor, which is why it is not already arbitraged. The child estimates this surface non-parametrically — a pooled, exponentially-weighted histogram regression on an ordinal 6x3 grid using only realised (backward, non-overlapping) horizon returns — so no direction is ever hard-coded and cross-name pooling replaces the noisy per-name fits that make such interactions look like noise. Falsifiable: if the interaction cells are pure estimation noise, or if the surface is additive, the factor's forecast has zero IC and adds nothing to the book; if the interaction is real and stable, the signal (an explicit conditional-expectation forecast) must have positive IC at the fixed 6-bar offset.
factors.name: Nonparametric displacement x flow interaction response surface

factors.trading_idea: A peer-relative price displacement is a superposition of components with very different relaxation times: 1-bar quote noise (un-harvestable), a mid-frequency transient-impact component that relaxes over tens of seconds, and a slow repricing component that only mean-reverts over many minutes. The parent traded the *level* of the displacement, which is dominated by the slow component — hence its IC grew monotonically out to 24 bars and was weak at the fixed 6-bar offset. The child first band-limits the displacement with a causal difference of two EWMAs whose half-lives bracket the 6-bar horizon (isolating exactly the fluctuation band whose decay mass lands inside the next 60 seconds), and then multiplies it by a *self-calibrated relaxation slope*: the trailing OLS coefficient of the realized 6-bar band change on the band level lagged 6 bars, i.e. the name's own measured mean-reversion speed evaluated at precisely the forecast offset, empirical-Bayes shrunk toward its sector-x-size peer group. The product is therefore a directly horizon-matched predicted 6-bar return rather than a level, and it flips sign for names whose band is currently trending. The edge survives arbitrage because harvesting it requires warehousing inventory in a name whose relaxation speed is only noisily identified in real time, and the per-event profit is small relative to that inventory risk; falsified if replacing the estimated slope by the constant -1 leaves the 6-bar IC unchanged, or if the raw level (no band filter) still peaks at 6 bars rather than 24.
factors.name: Horizon-band peer displacement with self-calibrated relaxation slope

factors.trading_idea: Parent A shows that a fresh, structurally-unexplained one-sided variance burst produced on little volume (a thin-book vacuum) is mechanical inventory displacement and snaps back; Parent B shows that such a displacement only actually gets repaired when it is peer-idiosyncratic AND the valuation-comparable peer basket is live enough to serve as the hedge leg. The child therefore keeps A's fast semivariance-asymmetry innovation but (i) strips out the peer-COMMON part of the burst with a leave-one-out mean inside industry x price-to-book comparability cells — the unhedgeable factor piece that never reverts — and (ii) scales the surviving idiosyncratic burst by a bilinear gate thin_book x peer_liveness, so the position is large only when the displacement was cheap to create and cheap to hedge, and mildly reversed (continuation) when a burst arrived on heavy volume while peers were dead. The interaction is the edge: A alone buys vacuum bursts that are actually basket-wide (unrepairable), B alone has almost no standalone impulse because it never measures the violence of the displacement; conditioning A's magnitude on B's hedge-capacity state separates repairable inventory shocks from unhedgeable factor news at the fixed 6-bar horizon.
factors.name: Hedgeability-gated vacuum semivariance innovation

factors.trading_idea: The parent's power-law propagator kernel was a fixed, universal one, so its predicted relaxation was spread over tens of bars and its IC peaked at 24 bars rather than the fixed 6-bar offset. The Bouchaud-Gerig-Farmer diffusivity constraint says the kernel's decay exponent is not universal but is pinned by the name's own order-flow persistence, beta ~ (1-gamma)/2 where the sign autocorrelation decays as C(l) ~ l^-gamma: names whose signed flow is strongly persistent (small gamma) must have a strongly transient, fast-relaxing kernel, while names with near-uncorrelated flow have almost permanent impact and no snapback at all. I therefore estimate gamma (and the level of C) per name by a trailing log-log OLS of the sign autocorrelation on lag, build that name's own kernel, and then isolate the part of the forecast that actually accrues in the next 6 bars by subtracting the per-bar relaxation rate expected over bars 6-24 and adding the impact of the flow the fitted autocorrelation predicts will still arrive inside the next 6 bars. The edge should persist because harvesting it means supplying liquidity into the tail of someone else's execution while its replenishment has already faded — capacity-limited and inventory-risky — and because the conditioning object (a per-name flow-ACF exponent, no price displacement at all) is not a standard screen.
factors.name: Diffusivity-implied propagator kernel with horizon-isolated relaxation

factors.trading_idea: The parent forecast a *level* (a standing peer-relative displacement) and therefore inherited the level's slow autocorrelation, so its information only cashed out over many minutes (IC rising monotonically to 24 bars). The correct horizon-matched object is not a level but the projection of the *next 6-bar* idiosyncratic return onto a profile of disjoint past return blocks (lags 1-2, 3-6, 7-18, 19-54), whose weights are estimated causally from realised (predictor at t-6, outcome over t-5..t) pairs pooled across the panel; blocks whose relaxation is slower than the window automatically receive near-zero weight instead of diluting the fast component. The crucial interaction is that this lag profile is state-dependent in trade flow: displacements built on light volume are almost pure liquidity-provider inventory and unwind front-loaded (large negative weight on the freshest block), whereas volume-backed displacements carry a permanent Kyle component and keep or extend their sign, so estimating one blended kernel — as the parent effectively did — cancels the fast, tradable part. The edge survives arbitrage because it pays a small vol-scaled premium per event for supplying immediacy precisely in the light-flow state where inventory must be warehoused with no confirming order flow, and because identifying the state-conditional kernel requires pooled estimation over heavily overlapping observations rather than a single visible price pattern.
factors.name: Flow-backing-split pooled lag-profile kernel (6 bars)

factors.trading_idea: Parent A splits a short-horizon displacement into a flow-explained (transient impact) part and an orthogonal (quiet repricing) part, but cannot tell whether the flow-explained part is a finished jump into a vacuum (mechanical snapback) or a still-working sliced metaorder (continuation), nor whether the orthogonal part is genuine sequential quote shading or a stale-mid gap. Parent B supplies that discriminator — the excess of the realised adjacent-sign-flip frequency over the Rice/Gaussian null arccos(rho)/pi, negative when autocorrelation is carried by many small same-signed increments (grind) and positive when carried by few large ones (jump) — but applies it to volume-partitioned raw returns where quote-driven and trade-driven increments are still mixed. The child measures the Rice carrier gap *inside Parent A's own regression channels*: on the per-bar fitted impact increment beta*flow (which is automatically non-zero only in traded bars, the clean active stream) and on the per-bar residual increment (the untraded repricing stream). The residual drift is then ridden only when grind-carried and muted when jump-carried (stale print), while the impact leg is faded when jump-carried and *ridden with flipped sign* when grind-carried — a signed state switch neither parent can express, because it needs the propagator regression to define the channels and the Rice statistic to identify each channel's carrier.
factors.name: Propagator-channel carrier: Rice-signed gate on impact vs quiet repricing

factors.trading_idea: Repair of a peer-idiosyncratic dislocation is not paid for in calendar time but in *execution* time: the arbitrageur must work the hedge leg (the valuation-comparable peer basket) while the dislocated name keeps absorbing its own forcing flow, so the fraction of the repair that lands inside a fixed 6-bar (60-second) window is governed by the wedge between the peer basket's trade-arrival clock and the name's own clock. The parent proved the dislocation itself is real but only repaired by ~24 bars; conditioning on the clock wedge is the mechanism that pulls that repair *into* the fixed 6-bar offset, since fast peer clocks compress a four-minute convergence into under a minute, while slow peer clocks leave the unabsorbed metaorder still pushing (mild continuation). Falsifiable: the IC of the plain (negated) idiosyncratic 6-bar residual dislocation must be materially positive in the top tercile of the peer-minus-own log clock speed and non-positive in the bottom tercile; if reversal strength is independent of the clock wedge the factor is dead. The edge survives arbitrage because it is a liquidity-timing constraint, not a mispricing: no amount of capital can manufacture peer-basket trading interest in the exact states where the hedge leg is asleep, so the conditional slowness of repair is not competed away.
factors.name: Hedge-leg clock wedge gated idiosyncratic snapback

factors.trading_idea: Parent B showed that the precision-whitened 6-bar dislocation does NOT snap back on average — it continues — because at a 10-second clock a move along a historically low-variance direction in a thin name is mostly slow information diffusion (Epps/staleness catch-up), while only the weight-proportional, basket-driven part of it is mechanical liquidity demand that must relax. Parent A supplied the geometry that identifies that mechanical part (cap-weight direction, volume-share tilt toward it, and the impact-elasticity wedge rank(-log turnover) − rank(beta)) but used it only as a multiplicative scalar gate on the pooled dislocation. The child instead uses A's geometry INSIDE B's precision metric: it computes the GLS/minimum-variance basket coordinate a_t = (wᵀΣ⁻¹x)/(wᵀΣ⁻¹w) — the amount of the recent move attributable to a push along the capitalisation-weight vector measured in the same Mahalanobis metric — subtracts the basket-attributed displacement a_t·w from the move, and trades the two pieces with opposite signs: the basket-orthogonal whitened residual as continuation (information catch-up, strongest in fragile/thin names that are not receiving basket flow), and the basket-attributed weight-proportional displacement as reversal, gated by a name-level program footprint (the name's own contribution to the cross-sectional volume-share/index-weight alignment) times its impact elasticity wedge. The interaction is the edge: A cannot see the correlation-structure dislocation it should be splitting, and B's two opposite populations cancel because it never projects out the basket direction in the metric that generated it.
factors.name: GLS basket-projected precision dislocation split

factors.trading_idea: Parent A showed the sign of short-horizon return autocorrelation flips with hidden depth, but its depth proxy (volume per unit of high-low traversal) is scale- and noise-contaminated and its carrier (k-bar displacement from an arbitrary past price) only paid off far beyond 6 bars; Parent B built the cleaner depth object — volume printed while the mid is pinned inside its own tick-grid quantum, i.e. revealed resting queue at a specific level — but wasted it on a sparse event impulse and declared the wrong direction. The child fuses them: the reference point for displacement is the *pinned-volume-weighted anchor level* over the last 6 bars (the price at which the queue actually rested and absorbed size), and the carrier is the volatility-standardised distance of the current mid from that anchor, gated by a bounded, own-history-standardised measure of how much volume that anchor absorbed. B's sign contradiction is explained rather than flipped: at 10-second resolution a pinned mid with heavy prints is a two-sided, continuously *replenished* level, not a queue about to be exhausted, so excursions away from a heavily absorbed anchor are liquidity-demand overshoots that get pulled back — exactly A's absorbed-move reversion — whereas excursions in a vacuum (no absorbed volume, gate below the cross-sectional mean) are informative repricing and continue. The interaction carries edge neither parent has: the anchor makes the reversion target a real microstructural magnet (so the snapback happens within the fixed 6-bar horizon instead of at 24 bars), and the pin-absorption gate supplies the depth state that decides whether the magnet exists at all.
factors.name: Pin-absorption anchor-gated displacement snapback

factors.trading_idea: Parent A's quiet-bar drift is contaminated by exactly the confound its own falsification clause names: a thin name whose mid drifts in quiet bars is often just mechanically catching up to market returns it has already seen, so that drift is already-owed beta delivery, not fresh quote shading — and beta catch-up does not persist the way inventory-driven quote shading does. The child uses Parent B's channel-split distributed-lag machinery as a *purifier*: it estimates the lagged-market impulse response separately inside the quiet and active volume streams, subtracts the stream-specific market-explained component bar-by-bar, and only then accumulates the quiet-minus-active drift split, so each leg is genuinely idiosyncratic (quote shading vs paid temporary impact). Parent B's stream-specific Rice sign-flip excess then verifies the delivery mechanism of each purified leg — the quiet leg is loaded only when it is grind-carried (many small same-signed quote steps, not a stale-mid gap), while the active leg's sign flips with its own excess (fade jump-carried impact into thin depth, follow a still-working sliced order) — and B's residual owed catch-up is re-added as a small horizon-matched tilt. The interaction is the edge: A's strong but confounded drift split becomes market-orthogonal and mechanism-verified, while B's weak-standalone state variable is finally applied to a signal with real standalone information instead of to its own thin forecast.
factors.name: Market-Purified Quiet vs Traded Drift (channel Rice gate)

factors.trading_idea: Depth is rebuilt where inventory actually changed hands, not where the quote merely wandered: the volume-weighted centroid of recent log-mid prices marks the price region where market makers hold offsetting inventory and where resting size is thickest, so a mid that has drifted away from that traded centroid is sitting in a region nobody has had to absorb and is pulled back within about a minute. The pull is only real while the centroid stays put — if the volume-weighted centroid has itself migrated with the price over the same 6 bars, then the traded region (and hence the depth and the dealer inventory anchor) has genuinely relocated and there is nothing left to revert to, so the reversion is switched off (and slightly inverted when the centroid outruns the price, i.e. a sweep). The parent's failure mode was a sparse triple product of noisy z-scores fired only on rare escape events; the child expresses the same depth-geometry idea as a dense, bounded, level-type statistic (Mahalanobis distance to the traded price distribution) with a single bounded gate, and only mildly partials out the plain 6-bar move so it is not spanned by the book's reversal factors. Falsifiable: if depth follows quotes rather than trades, the IC flips negative; the edge survives arbitrage because it must be estimated per name per bar from volume-weighted price moments and its capacity is limited by exactly the thin depth away from the traded region.
factors.name: Traded-value centroid magnet, gated by centroid migration

factors.trading_idea: Treat each name's sequence of 10-second mid-price tick directions as a two-state Markov chain and compute, in closed form, the chain-implied expected NET number of up-ticks minus down-ticks over the next 6 bars given the state observed right now: E[net ticks] = (u_t - pi_u)*sum_h lam_u^h - (d_t - pi_d)*sum_h lam_d^h, where lam = P(up|up) - P(up|not-up) is the chain's second eigenvalue. This is not momentum or reversal: the sign of the forecast is determined per name and per state by the estimated eigenvalue, so quote-bounce names (lam<0, mid oscillating inside a stable spread) get a fade signal while order-splitting names (lam>0, a working parent order repeatedly lifting the same side) get a continuation signal. Because the two microstructures coexist and are separated by trading intensity, the chain is estimated separately for transitions that begin in high- and low-volume bars, and the eigenvalue is empirical-Bayes shrunk by its own binomial standard error so that statistically indistinguishable-from-iid names contribute nothing. The edge survives arbitrage because the predictable component is a fraction of a tick per bar — invisible to anyone crossing the spread — and because its sign flips across names and states, so no static cross-sectional exposure spans it; harvesting it requires per-name, state-conditional estimation rather than a directional bet.
factors.name: Activity-split tick-direction Markov chain drift forecast

factors.trading_idea: The parent kept the right machinery (an Epps/lag-1-corrected precision-whitened, peer-orthogonal dislocation) but read the occupancy state backwards: the recurrence density is measured at the mid's *current* level, so it describes the resting depth the price will face over the NEXT six bars, not the depth already consumed. A level the mid has repeatedly revisited in the last few minutes has accumulated two-sided queue (local time = queue-building time), so a whitened idiosyncratic displacement into/away from it is absorbed and repaid inside a minute; a mid sitting in a region it has never occupied has no queue to lean on, and price discovery / stop cascades let the same displacement extend. This flip is exactly the direction the parent's realized IC showed, so the child states it as the mechanism rather than as a fitted sign. To make the edge live at the fixed 6-bar offset (the parent's slow 6-bar aggregate had its |IC| peak at 24 bars), the dislocation is built from the freshest 2-bar whitened innovation with the slow 12-bar whitened dislocation purged out cross-sectionally, isolating the transient component whose relaxation half-life is on the order of half a minute. The edge should persist because the resistance/vacuum state is a level-specific, non-price-path variable that plain reversal or momentum screens do not condition on, and acting on it requires posting into (or sweeping) a specific queue, which caps arbitrage capacity.
factors.name: Vacuum-polarity fast Epps dislocation

factors.trading_idea: Parent A showed that a 10-second mid path splits cleanly into a Roll-gain-filtered efficient component and a transitory pricing error, but it mis-signed the split: at a 60-second horizon the filtered displacement is mostly *transient metaorder impact* that decays, while the endpoint bounce error is already gone within a bar and only injects noise. Parent B has the right selector — fade a deviation only when its own reversion clock matches the holding horizon — but it counts zero crossings of the *raw* deviation, where the MA(1) bounce manufactures spurious crossings, biasing the estimated clock downward and systematically downweighting exactly the names whose slower, tradable oscillation is 6 bars long. The child therefore uses A's per-name steady-state Kalman gain (K from trailing Roll autocovariance moments) to denoise the path *before* running B's Kac level-crossing clock estimator, and then fades each leg with its own sech^2(0.5·ln(T/h)) horizon-match kernel: the filtered deviation earns nearly full weight where its noise-free clock is ~6 bars, and the bounce leg is automatically starved of weight because its clock is ~1 bar. The interaction is the edge: neither the unbiased clock (needs A's noise-ratio filter) nor the correct leg weighting (needs B's kernel) exists in either parent alone, and a live-volume damper delays the fade while the pushing metaorder is still executing.
factors.name: Roll-gain denoised crossing clock, dual-leg horizon-matched fade

factors.trading_idea: Relative-value dislocations in multiple space do not revert on an autonomous per-name clock; they revert (or widen) with the peer group's aggregate dispersion, because the flows that compress or stretch a comparable set arrive in clustered waves (stat-arb desks putting on / unwinding baskets, index and hedging trades hitting the whole industry at once). The group-level dispersion of standardized dislocations therefore trends over tens of seconds: if the industry's cross-sectional dispersion in multiple space has just been contracting faster than the market as a whole, each member's own dislocation is being pulled toward the peer median inside the next minute (reversion); if it has been stretching, the same dislocation keeps widening (continuation). Signing the group-level dispersion trend by the name's own dislocation therefore produces a signal that fires exactly at the fixed 6-bar offset, whereas the parent's level-only dislocation averaged reversion and expansion regimes together and consequently only paid off at long offsets. The edge persists because it requires jointly estimating a point-in-time multiple-space peer spread per name and its group's dispersion trajectory on a 10-second cross-section, and because it is a sign-flipping interaction: any book that trades the dislocation level with one fixed sign averages this term to roughly zero.
factors.name: Peer-dispersion trend gated multiple-space dislocation flip

factors.trading_idea: Mid-price drift accumulated *since the last trade* is an unconsummated quote relocation: the maker has moved its reservation price for inventory / adverse-selection reasons but no one has yet traded against the new level, so the displacement is still open and is confirmed (not reversed) by the next incoming order. Because the displacement resolves on the trade clock rather than the wall clock, its forecast content is concentrated in the handful of bars until the silence breaks — so I gate the open displacement by each name's empirical per-bar trade-arrival rate, i.e. the probability the next trade lands inside the 6-bar (60-second) offset; this replaces the parent's fixed 30-bar accumulation, which blended long-since-consummated displacement and therefore only paid off at 2-4 minutes. Against it I subtract the last 6 bars of return earned in high-volume bars, weighted by sqrt(volume surprise), since that is temporary impact which decays within a minute. The edge survives arbitrage because harvesting it requires crossing the spread precisely on names that are momentarily quiet, and it is falsified if the hazard gate does not concentrate IC at 6 bars or if open quiet displacement reverts like traded drift (pure stale-mid noise).
factors.name: Pending Untraded Quote Displacement, Trade-Arrival-Hazard Gated

factors.trading_idea: Transient impact relaxes along a propagator G(t)=(1+t/t0)^-beta, but relaxation is delivered in TRADE time, not clock time, and the fraction delivered inside a fixed 60-second window is overwhelmingly contributed by the freshest increments: the per-lag kernel w_k = G(a_k) - G(a_k + H) decays like a_k^-(beta+1), so a distributed-lag reconstruction of the standing displacement has an effective memory of ~8 bars instead of the many-minute memory of a level-based dislocation — which is exactly why the parent's level signal peaked at 24 bars. Two conditioners make the object economic rather than a plain reversal: (i) the ages a_k and the forward window H are measured in normalised traded volume, so during an activity burst even older increments still owe a large slice of decay inside six clock bars while in a lull almost nothing is owed; (ii) only the LIQUIDITY component relaxes, and the permanent (informative) component is identified by whether the name's own peer-relative increments lead its comparables' subsequent moves — names that lead their sector-and-size peers are repricing on information and are therefore purged from the fade. The edge persists because harvesting the front-loaded slice needs fast turnover for a few basis points per event while the arbitrageurs who warehouse the relative-value gap are paid on the slow multi-minute leg, and because the volume-clock/leadership decomposition requires per-name calibration that is uneconomic to run at scale on tiny per-event profits.
factors.name: Event-time propagator relaxation, leadership-purged

factors.trading_idea: Unsigned bar volume can be split into buy/sell halves with the bulk-volume classifier (Easley–López de Prado–O'Hara): a fat-tailed CDF of the intra-bar mid move standardised by a Parkinson range volatility gives a saturating *signed participation* per bar, so the resulting imbalance measures who was pressing the quote, not how far it moved. The economically decisive variable is not the imbalance itself but whether the recent flow is toxic: when a name's VPIN (mean absolute bucket imbalance) is unusually high for that name, the imbalance is informed, the maker's inventory is adversely selected and the quote relocation persists; when VPIN is unusually low, the same imbalance is uninformed liquidity demand that makers absorb and revert within a minute. The child therefore trades a pure interaction — cross-sectional imbalance rank multiplied by a signed toxicity gate centred at each name's own norm — so it carries no unconditional flow/momentum loading and should span an axis the book's flow and reversal factors do not (the parent's residual IC was ~0 because untraded-displacement variants are already all over the archive). It is falsifiable: if the sign of the imbalance–forward-return relation does not flip with own-name toxicity, the interaction IC collapses to zero; the edge survives arbitrage because acting on it means crossing the spread against informed flow exactly when adverse selection is highest, i.e. the payoff is compensation for bearing that selection risk rather than a costless anomaly.
factors.name: BVC flow imbalance with toxicity-conditioned sign flip

factors.trading_idea: Intraday volume is largely a deterministic calendar schedule (VWAP/TWAP algos, index and open/close-driven flow follow a U-shape), so the informative part of trading activity is the residual of volume against its own same-clock-time norm on previous sessions, not against a rolling trailing average as almost every short-horizon factor assumes. Price moves produced *during* bars with above-schedule (unscheduled) volume are information-motivated and their impact persists, whereas identical moves occurring on below-schedule volume are pure inventory/quote displacement by a fee-insensitive scheduled trader and mean-revert; the recency-weighted trailing covariance between diurnally-standardized volume surprise and the *within-bar* mid change (close−open, the impact actually paid) therefore predicts the next minute of returns with a single signed statistic. The mechanism is falsifiable in two ways: replacing the diurnal baseline with a plain trailing-ADV baseline should kill the incremental edge, and the effect should be strongest in large caps where scheduled algorithmic flow is the biggest share of volume (hence the mild size scaling). It survives arbitrage because latency-driven liquidity providers condition on rolling recent depth/volume and on spread, not on per-name cross-day calendar-conditional volume profiles, and because harvesting it requires holding ~1 minute — longer than queue-position strategies and shorter than typical stat-arb rebalancing.
factors.name: Unscheduled-flow impact (diurnal volume surprise × intra-bar impact)

factors.trading_idea: Basket / program executions allocate dollars by capitalisation weight but consume depth, so the displacement they cause in name i scales with weight-per-depth (inverse dollar turnover) rather than with beta; the cross-sectional wedge rank(kappa)-rank(beta) times the concurrent cap-weighted market move is therefore a flow-geometry forecast of the *mechanical* part of a name's 2-bar move, and the per-bar cross-sectional fit of the realised move onto that forecast tells us how much of it actually landed. The crucial missing conditioner in the parent is that this mechanical exposure has two opposite futures: a low-turnover name that has *overshot* gives back part of its path extremum inside the push window (depth refills, market makers relax inventory) and keeps reverting over the next minute, whereas a low-turnover name that is merely *stale* closes at the extremum of the window and continues catching up to the market (Epps effect). Measuring the fraction of the multi-bar path extremum already surrendered at the close therefore *signs* the attributed push instead of blindly fading it, and because it observes refill that is already in progress the payoff lands inside the fixed 6-bar (~1 minute) horizon rather than at 24 bars. The edge survives arbitrage precisely because the unconditional trade earns nothing — the overshoot and lag regimes cancel — so an arbitrageur must jointly estimate the cap-weighted market move, per-name beta, a turnover-based depth proxy and 10-second path geometry for a payoff that sits inside most participants' spread and latency budget.
factors.name: Basket over-push refill-polarity split

factors.trading_idea: Both parents estimate a per-name reversion timescale from *sign* statistics, but on different objects: Parent A counts zero-crossings of the price deviation (Rice inversion on the LEVEL, giving an implied AR(1) persistence phi = cos(pi/T)), while Parent B inverts Rice on the 6-bar INCREMENTS (rho_obs = cos(pi*p_flip)). Under a stationary OU/AR(1) level these two are analytically linked — the lag-h block-increment autocorrelation must equal rho_pred = -(1 - phi^h)/2 — so the wedge rho_obs - rho_pred (shrunk by the number of independent block pairs) is a model-free measure of directional persistence in excess of what the name's own crossing clock can generate, i.e. evidence that the deviation is being carried by transient order-flow/stale-quote lag rather than by a stationary oscillation. Parent B's realized sign (concordant displacements *revert*) says exactly this excess concordance is transient impact awaiting unwind, so the child fades Parent A's horizon-matched deviation with a gate that opens where the wedge is positive and closes where the observed block memory is already OU-consistent (nothing left to harvest at 6 bars). Neither parent has this: A ignores whether the deviation is stationary oscillation or live push, and B misreads its own rho as a forecast coefficient instead of as a departure from the level-implied benchmark.
factors.name: Rice-consistency wedge gated crossing-clock fade

factors.trading_idea: The parent asserted that a thin-book, 'exhausted' one-sided burst must snap back; the realized IC contradicted that, and the reason is mechanical: at 10-second sampling most of the mid-price displacement per unit of traded volume is liquidity providers *repricing* their fair-value estimate (or pulling depth ahead of information), which is a permanent price change that tends to extend through order-splitting / self-excited follow-on flow, whereas displacements that are heavily traded against are the ones where dealer inventory is warehoused and only the transient component relaxes. Instead of asserting which regime a name is in, the child *measures* it: for each name it estimates, from strictly trailing and horizon-aligned pairs, the correlation between its sector-purged square-root-law signed flow pressure and the return realized over the following 6 bars, shrinks that response coefficient toward the contemporaneous cross-sectional mean (a market-wide continuation-vs-reversal regime), and multiplies today's fresh pressure by it. The permanent/transient impact ratio is a slowly varying property of a name's liquidity provision (book depth, dealer risk aversion, share of informed flow) and of the market-wide volatility regime, so it persists for hours — long enough to be estimated and traded; the edge survives arbitrage because the signal flips sign across names and regimes, so neither a crowded reversal book nor a crowded momentum book can express it, and its capacity is bounded by a one-minute holding period.
factors.name: Self-measured impact-permanence switch on sqrt-law idiosyncratic flow pressure

factors.trading_idea: Kyle/Glosten adverse-selection logic says the fraction of a price push that is permanent rises with information asymmetry: for opaque, intangible-heavy, low-accrual-quality firms a burst of order flow is more likely informed, so its impact persists, whereas for transparent, tangible, high-income-quality firms the same push is mostly uninformed liquidity demand and decays within seconds. A name's own trailing 10-second AR(1) coefficient measures its reversal speed but is dominated by estimation noise; projecting it cross-sectionally onto ranked fundamental opacity (R&D intensity, intangibles/assets, income quality) with size and dollar-liquidity controls yields a low-variance, structurally-justified estimate of who reverts and who continues. The child therefore signs a recent standardised 3-bar push by the *cross-sectionally demeaned* fundamentals-implied reversal intensity, so it is a pure permanence-vs-transience split rather than plain reversal, and the edge survives because market makers set inventory/quote parameters from realised tick noise, not from fundamentally-projected impact permanence, and the fundamental leg is too slow-moving to be arbitraged away by latency.
factors.name: Opacity-implied impact permanence (reversal-speed projection)

factors.trading_idea: Chatterjee's rank correlation xi is *asymmetric*: xi(X->Y) measures how nearly Y is a measurable function of X, so xi(volume -> |return|) minus xi(|return| -> volume) is a distribution-free diagnostic of which side of the book-flow relation is many-to-one. When volume sometimes fails to move the mid (absorption by real depth) but every mid move is volume-backed, the asymmetry A is positive: displacement in that regime had to be paid for with size that depth could not absorb, so it is permanent repricing and continues over the next minute. When instead the mid reprices repeatedly on little or no volume while volume reliably moves price (thin, quote-driven book), A is negative and displacement is quote/inventory noise that snaps back. The edge should persist because production liquidity gates are linear or symmetric (Kyle lambda, spread, VPIN, depth, correlation, entropy) and are blind to conditional-determinism *direction*; xi-asymmetry is a second-order rank feature of the same two series, and it is cheap only if you know to compute the rank total-variation statistic. Falsifiable: bin names by A and regress forward 6-bar return on standardized displacement — the slope must increase monotonically in A and change sign, otherwise the factor's IC is zero.
factors.name: Chatterjee-xi flow/volatility dependence asymmetry gate

factors.trading_idea: For any increment process the lag-1 autocorrelation of adjacent non-overlapping k-bar blocks is identically rho_k = Var(D_2k)/(2 Var(D_k)) - 1, so the horizon-matched linear forecast of the next 6-bar move needs only a robust two-scale (6- and 12-bar) displacement-scale ratio — no Hurst/fGn parametrisation and no separate Roll noise correction, both of which biased the parent (subtracting 2*Var(eps) from both scales inflates the ratio and pushed the whole cross-section into apparent persistence, so the parent forecast continuation for everyone while the true common level at 10-second sampling is reversal — hence the flipped IC). The child therefore never bets on the *level* of rho: it cross-sectionally rank-centres the estimated block coefficient, so it is long the displacement of names whose noise-purged path memory is unusually persistent *relative to peers* and short it in names that are relatively transitory-dominated, leaving the common reversion level (already spanned by every reversion factor in the book) untraded. Because the transitory component reverts in trade time rather than clock time, the forecast is scaled by the name's current 6-bar dollar-volume participation (volume clusters, so recent participation forecasts near-future trade intensity), which sharpens the horizon match. The edge persists because reversion desks apply one common horizon-scale coefficient to the entire book: the residual is the *dispersion* of the block coefficient, whose harvest needs continuous per-name heavy-tail-robust (q=1) re-estimation and pays only a few basis points per name.
factors.name: Block variance-ratio memory dispersion with trade-clock tilt

factors.trading_idea: Parent B knows *which* names a program should have mechanically over-pushed (cap-weight-per-depth in excess of beta, times the footprint-weighted market move) but fades every push identically; Parent A knows how to *verify* attribution by regressing realized dislocation on the predicted push cross-sectionally each bar, but pools relaxation and diffusion into one residual so its regimes cancel. The child runs that attribution regression separately inside the two local-time states — names whose pushed price now sits in a recurrence vacuum (no resting queue to restore it) versus names sitting on a repeatedly revisited, well-supplied level (the push consumed a genuine one-sided queue) — and lets the fitted component carry opposite signs in the two states, scaled by each state's own goodness-of-fit trust, with the un-attributed remainder ridden as slow information diffusion. The interaction is the edge: only a *state-split* regression can tell a mechanically-caused, unabsorbed displacement (fade) from a mechanically-sized but queue-validated displacement (continue), and only the within-state R² tells us whether this particular bar's flow geometry actually explains the moves at all — B fades both cases blindly and A never conditions its trust statistic on where the push landed.
factors.name: Local-time split basket-push attribution flip

factors.trading_idea: The parent folded per-lag betas onto the horizon under the implicit assumption that all delayed market response is pure catch-up; empirically the delivered catch-up partly overshoots and reverses, which is why the parent's IC peaked at 1 bar and turned negative by 12-24 bars and only 0.007 survived at the evaluated 6-bar offset. The child replaces the iterated impulse-response folding with a *direct* h-step projection: for each name a trailing ridge regression of the realized 6-bar own return on two features of the market path that were observable exactly 6 bars earlier (a fresh 2-bar market shock and a stale 3-to-6-bar market shock), so the fitted coefficients absorb delayed delivery (positive loading) and overshoot reversal (negative loading) at precisely the offset being scored, instead of assuming the shape. Applying those coefficients to the currently observed market path gives a horizon-matched forecast whose sign is learned, not imposed; it is amplified where estimation is trustworthy (in-window explained variance, sign agreement between a long and a short estimation window) and where repricing is genuinely slow (high frozen-mid fraction, thin recent volume versus its own norm). The edge persists because second-scale arbitrage capital treats each name's market linkage as a single contemporaneous beta and does not estimate name-specific overlapping-horizon response timing; it is falsified if the direct projection carries no more 6-bar information than the parent's catch-up kernel, or if the fresh-shock coefficient is not systematically more negative than the stale-shock coefficient.
factors.name: Direct 6-bar market-path projection (overshoot-aware, trust gated)

factors.trading_idea: Silent quote repricing (mid moves in bars where essentially no volume prints) is a market maker walking their reservation price during an inventory/adverse-selection search; because the search is a ramp, its *level* is a slow state already visible to everyone, while only its *current rate of change* tells you where the quote will be 60 seconds from now. Traded-bar price change is dominated by temporary impact, whose transient part decays with a much shorter half-life, so its reversal content must also be measured fresh rather than averaged over minutes. The child therefore replaces the parent's equal-weight 30-bar level sums with two causal band-pass filters (fast EWMA minus slow EWMA) applied to a *smooth* silence-weighted return stream, and gates the silence leg by the probability that silence persists, since a ramp only continues while no one trades against it. The edge survives arbitrage because harvesting the silent leg means quoting into thin, rarely-traded names where the spread cost of the trip is comparable to the drift itself.
factors.name: Fresh silence-repricing rate vs traded transient kernel

factors.trading_idea: A one-to-two-minute mid-price displacement is a mixture of two physically different objects: a monotone 'grind' produced by a sliced metaorder or by information being impounded gradually (high path efficiency = |net move| / summed |bar moves|), and a spike-and-retrace produced by an inventory/liquidity shock that the tape has already begun to undo (low path efficiency). The horizon-matched continuation coefficient therefore depends on an *observable path shape*, not on a per-name autocorrelation that has to be estimated: the parent's Rice sign-concordance coefficient carried a binomial standard error of roughly 0.18 against a true block autocorrelation of order 0.03, so it multiplied displacement by estimation noise and its realized sign was never identified by the mechanism (hence the sign contradiction). The child estimates only two numbers for the entire panel — the common reversal gain and the *partial* path-shape wedge — via an EWMA-pooled trailing bivariate through-origin regression of realized standardised 6-bar returns on lagged displacement and its path-shape interaction (thousands of bars x all names, so the standard error is ~two orders of magnitude smaller), and it trades only the wedge, deliberately purging the common reversal gain that the existing 25-factor book already spans. The edge persists because high-frequency reversion desks apply a single reversion parameter to the *level* of a displacement without decomposing its intra-window path shape; per-name payoff of the wedge is tiny, and harvesting it requires continuous pooled recalibration across a broad book.
factors.name: Path-shape wedge in horizon-matched displacement (pooled partial gain)

factors.trading_idea: Quiet-bar (zero/near-zero volume) mid revisions are quote-shading that accrues only while the name stays untraded, whereas traded-bar impact relaxes only as further trades arrive (Bouchaud-style propagator decay runs in trade time, not wall-clock time). The parent summed both drifts in calendar time, so its predictive mass leaked far beyond the 6-bar offset; here each leg is multiplied by the expected number of bars of its OWN clock that will actually elapse in the next 6 bars, obtained by fitting a trailing two-state (quiet/active) Markov chain per name and propagating it exactly 6 steps forward from the current state. A name that is silent now and historically sticky-silent will deliver most of its quiet repricing within the horizon; a name about to be traded instead delivers impact relaxation, so the same raw drifts get opposite, horizon-calibrated weights. Falsified if the Markov-weighted prediction does not beat the unweighted quiet-minus-traded split at 6 bars (i.e. if quiet drift is stale-mid noise or if silence persistence carries no information); the edge survives arbitrage because harvesting it means quoting or crossing spread in names precisely when they are illiquid and untraded, which is capacity-limited.
factors.name: Markov silence-survival horizon-matched quiet/traded delivery

factors.trading_idea: The parent asked *whether* volume accompanied a move; the child asks *in which temporal order* activity and displacement occur for that name, which is what actually identifies who is informed. If a name's absolute displacement innovations are best predicted by *lagged* volume innovations, price is being pushed by liquidity demand (Kyle/Hasbrouck impact regime) and a measurable share of the last minute's move is transitory overshoot that decays; if instead volume innovations follow *lagged* displacement innovations, the dealer's mid is being revised ahead of flow and subsequent order flow chases the quote, so the move extends. The lead–lag difference is antisymmetric, so the strong common diurnal volume/volatility seasonality cancels out of it and what remains is a slowly varying, name-specific dynamic state; we use it only as a *sign gate* on the fresh 60-second drift, and cross-sectionally residualise the product against that drift so the factor contains none of the plain short-term-reversal component the book already spans. Falsified if the interaction has no incremental IC once raw reversal is projected out — i.e. if reversal strength is independent of the volume↔displacement causal direction.
factors.name: Activity–Displacement Lead–Lag Direction Gated Reversal
