factors.trading_idea: A slow repricer's expected 6-bar return is the inner product of its distributed-lag market kernel with the already-observed market path, but the parent estimated that kernel with *univariate* per-lag betas, which double-count because 10-second market returns are strongly autocorrelated (index-level bid-ask bounce), and it truncated the kernel exactly at the horizon so the post-horizon giveback loadings were never folded in — which is why its IC flipped sign by 12 bars. This child solves the exact Toeplitz (Yule-Walker/GLS) system b = Gamma^-1 c using the market's own trailing autocovariance matrix, and extends the kernel to lag 12 while keeping the fold matched to H=6, so lags 7..12 (the transient-impact giveback) enter with weight equal to the trailing 6-bar market sum and cancel the illusory part of the owed catch-up. The forecast is then purged cross-sectionally of the name's horizon-6 beta, so the bet is on the *shape* of the response (how much is still owed per unit of exposure) rather than on beta-level market timing, and it is weighted by the kernel's explained-variance reliability and by repricing slowness (frozen mids, thin recent volume) — the states where second-scale attention is scarcest. Falsified if the whitened, giveback-extended kernel carries no more 6-bar IC than the univariate truncated fold, or if the reliability/slowness weights fail to discriminate.
factors.name: Toeplitz-whitened Dimson kernel with post-horizon giveback fold (beta-purged)

factors.trading_idea: A 1-minute-ahead move after a short price displacement is not universally reverting or trending — its sign depends on whether the volume that produced it was *shared* liquidity demand or *name-specific* trading. Decomposing each name's current log-volume shock into the part explained by its trailing loading on the market-wide volume shock (basket / ETF / index-rebalance style demand, which is non-informational and must be absorbed by intermediary inventory) and an orthogonal idiosyncratic part (Kyle-style privately-informed trading), we predict that displacement accompanied by a mostly-common flow shock reverts over the next 6 bars, while displacement accompanied by a mostly-idiosyncratic flow shock continues. The edge persists because it is compensation for supplying inventory against uninformative correlated flow: capacity is bounded by risk limits, so the premium cannot be arbitraged away, only shared, and the required decomposition must be estimated cross-sectionally at second scale each bar.
factors.name: Flow-shock purity conditioned idiosyncratic reversal

factors.trading_idea: A hidden resting queue is anchored to a *price level*, not to a bar, so its true footprint is the repeated near-tied retesting of the same block extreme — noise realises an extreme once (scale-incoherent, it averages away), whereas a surviving iceberg produces several bars whose highs (or lows) pile up within a few percent of the block range of the same edge. I therefore replace the parent's single-bar wick shape with a scale-free level-retest count asymmetry measured over exactly the forecast block (6 bars), and interact it with the parent's one component that carried marginal value: block-level Kyle-inverse depth (block volume per unit of block displacement), trailing-ranked so it is a signed state variable rather than an unbounded multiplier. The falsifiable claim is a sign-flipping interaction: retests backed by heavy absorbed volume (high depth state) mean the queue is still there and price drifts away from the tested side, while the same retests on thin volume mean the level is depleted and price breaks through it. The edge survives arbitrage because the inferred size is never quoted — monetising it means crossing the spread into concealed depth, a cost quote-only statistical arbitrageurs decline to pay.
factors.name: Scale-coherent level retest × block depth interaction

factors.trading_idea: The parent measured the right state variable (local-time / occupancy density around the price) but read its sign backwards: the data say a move INTO a well-visited, well-supplied region continues, while a move into a recurrence vacuum snaps back. The Kyle-style reason is that permanence is proportional to inventory actually transferred per unit of price displacement — if a 30-second displacement had to grind through resting queues at levels the price has repeatedly occupied AND was accompanied by heavy volume, real inventory changed hands and the new price is information-bearing; if the same displacement happened on thin flow in unvisited territory, it is pure transient impact / quote drift and decays within a minute. The child therefore builds the *surplus* backing: log(relative volume) + log(occupancy density of the band the price just swept), residualised by trailing OLS on log|standardised displacement|, so the gate answers 'did this move consume more liquidity than a move of this size usually needs?' and is mechanically orthogonal to move size — no plain reversal/momentum loading survives. The edge persists because it requires a per-name nonparametric path statistic (local time over the swept interval) jointly with volume normalisation in real time, pays only the transient-impact residual of a few ticks, and its cause (where resting inventory sits and how much of it a print actually clears) is a structural property of order books, not a mispricing that can be deleted.
factors.name: Sweep backing surplus (liquidity consumed per unit displacement) gated continuation

factors.trading_idea: Parent A fades or extrapolates a name's whole short-run drift depending on whether its bar volume just turned metronomic (a scheduler working a parent order) or bursty (one-off aggression whose displacement is transient impact) — but that drift is contaminated by the part of the move mechanically *owed* to market returns that have already printed, which should never be faded. Parent B measures exactly that owed piece with a horizon-matched distributed-lag kernel, but is silent on the execution channel through which a laggard mid actually gets dragged to fair value in the next minute. The child splits the recent price path into (i) beta-owed catch-up and (ii) idiosyncratic drift, applies the metronome gate only to the idiosyncratic part (schedules continue, bursts revert), and uses volume smoothness as a *positive amplifier* on the owed catch-up, because an orderly, evenly-sliced tape is precisely the mechanism that pays a laggard's backlog gradually, whereas bursty volume means the catch-up was already paid in one gulp and may have overshot. The interaction carries edge neither parent has: it de-contaminates A's drift of a component whose sign must not flip with the gate, and it tells B's owed-return forecast when the market microstructure is in a state that will actually settle the debt inside six bars.
factors.name: Metronome-volume gate on owed market catch-up vs idiosyncratic drift

factors.trading_idea: Parent A splits the freshest displacement into quote-driven (thin/zero-volume) repricing and flow-paid (traded-bar) impact but decides their fate from an activity *innovation*, which says nothing about where the mid now sits inside the recent volume profile; Parent B knows exactly that — the share of recent traded volume resting within ~1.2 window-sigma of the current mid — but applies one permanence verdict to a single undifferentiated flow-implied displacement. The child conditions A's two legs on B's shelf state: on a heavy volume shelf a traded-bar move is a metaorder eating a real queue (permanent, extends) while a quiet-bar mid move is stale-quote flicker inside the value area (reverts); in a volume vacuum the same traded move is a dealer skewing quotes hard to absorb inventory (transitory, snaps back once counterparty volume arrives, hence the trade-clock clearing damper) while a quiet move is genuine name-specific liquidity withdrawal repricing toward a new level with nothing to lean on (continues). The interaction carries edge neither parent has: it is the *source* of the displacement (paid vs unpaid) crossed with the *support* under it (shelf vs vacuum), and because the shelf z-score carries a small transient-prior offset the average loadings still reproduce both parents' confirmed signs while the signal itself lives in the 2x2 cross term.
factors.name: Shelf-occupancy gated quiet vs traded drift permanence split

factors.trading_idea: The parent estimated the lag-6 block autocorrelation from the sign-flip frequency of adjacent 6-bar mid displacements; at 10-second sampling that statistic is contaminated by an additive -Var(noise)/Var(D) term from quote bounce and mid discreteness, which pushes essentially every name's rho_hat negative, so the parent effectively forecast reversal for the whole cross-section — and the realized IC flipped because the *efficient* 60-second price is mildly positively autocorrelated (sliced metaorder flow) for most liquid names. The child estimates the same coefficient on the efficient price instead: it recovers a per-name self-similarity exponent from mean-absolute displacements at two scales that bracket the horizon (6 and 24 bars, so fine-scale noise matters least) after subtracting the Roll-implied noise variance from each scale's displacement variance, then maps it to the fractional-Gaussian block autocorrelation rho = 2^(2H-1) - 1 and forecasts rho times the current MAD-standardised 6-bar residual displacement. Because rho is signed, the same displacement is followed in names whose noise-purged path is persistent (H>1/2) and faded in names whose path is genuinely anti-persistent (H<1/2), so this is not a common-level momentum or reversal bet. The edge persists because reversion desks apply one common horizon-scale reversion coefficient to the whole book: the tradable residual is the *dispersion* of the noise-purged roughness exponent, whose harvest needs continuous per-name, heavy-tail-robust (q=1) re-estimation with an explicit microstructure-noise correction and pays only a few basis points per name.
factors.name: Noise-corrected self-similarity block-rho forecast

factors.trading_idea: Parent B shows that volume-marked excursions beyond the bar endpoints are the footprint of a self-exciting metaorder slice and precede continuation, while Parent A shows that path which was actually *converted* into net residual displacement is transient impact and snaps back; neither parent can tell which regime it is in, so each averages continuation against reversion. The child measures both channels on the SAME exponential (halflife-3) Hawkes kernel — a marked excursion intensity imbalance and a market-demeaned net-displacement intensity, both in units of the name's own trailing residual volatility — and forms the conversion ratio c = |displacement| / (|displacement| + marked excursion path) from the two intensities jointly. The cross-sectional rank of c then continuously switches polarity: names whose probing size was absorbed without converting into a net move load long the excursion side (unfilled, still-arriving slices), names whose path was fully swept into displacement load against that displacement (impact decay). The excursion channel is purged cross-sectionally of trailing range position so the surviving edge is slicing persistence rather than endpoint noise, and everything is scaled by a saturating traded-size gate because both mechanisms require real size to have hit the book.
factors.name: Conversion-switched marked-Hawkes excursion vs swept displacement

factors.trading_idea: The square-root/Kyle impact coefficient is not a slow per-name constant: it has a large market-wide, time-varying component (commonality in liquidity), so a stale per-name lambda misattributes common liquidity shocks to idiosyncratic overshoot and leaves a slow, contaminated residual whose give-back only shows up over many bars.  This child re-estimates the impact line *instantaneously and cross-sectionally* — each bar, a through-origin regression across names of volatility-scaled |return| on sqrt(bar volume / ADV) prices that instant's liquidity — so a name's residual is displacement unjustified by what everyone else paid for size at the very same moment; that object is much closer to pure immediacy overshoot and is therefore given back fast (within ~1 minute) rather than slowly.  The same regression yields a per-bar identification statistic: its cross-sectional R^2 tells whether the instant's dispersion of moves was flow-priced (liquidity-demand regime → excess is overshoot, fade) or orthogonal to flow (information/quote-revision regime → excess is news, do not fade), and a per-name cessation clock says whether the flow that produced the last excess has already stopped, which is when the depth refill actually pays the excess back.  The edge survives arbitrage because exploiting it requires simultaneous cross-name estimation of the instantaneous liquidity price inside a 10-second bar, the payoff is a few basis points capacity-limited by the very thinness that creates it, and the sign flips with regime so unconditional reversal traders are whipsawed rather than competing it away.
factors.name: Cross-sectional impact-line excess with liquidity-regime flip

factors.trading_idea: Keep the parent's premise — mid moves printed with no trade are mostly permanent quote repricing, while moves paid for with volume carry transitory impact — but express it as a signal-extraction problem instead of a cumulative drift. For each name I estimate, separately for quiet bars and traded bars, Roll's variance decomposition of bar returns (lag-1 autocovariance gives the transitory-noise variance, the rest is permanent innovation variance) and convert each into the steady-state Kalman gain of a local-level model, so quiet innovations are absorbed almost fully into the efficient price while traded innovations are absorbed only partially. Running a local-linear-trend (Holt) recursion on the cumulative volatility-normalised price with these regime-switched gains yields two objects that are already horizon-matched: an unabsorbed-innovation gap (efficient level minus observed mid, which must close) and a filtered permanent drift (built mainly from silent repricing, which must continue), and their model-implied 6-bar forecast is the factor. The edge survives arbitrage because harvesting it means quoting into thin, currently untraded names — paying spread exactly when nobody else wants the inventory — and because the gains are name- and regime-specific rather than a universal constant.
factors.name: Regime-gain local-linear-trend signal extraction

factors.trading_idea: Parent B says a name owes a computable, horizon-matched catch-up to market moves it has already seen, but it never asks whether that debt is *payable*; Parent A knows exactly when a mid is mechanically frozen on the price grid and when the resting queue holding it there has been eaten, but its own directional impulse is contaminated by bid-ask bounce, so its sign flipped out of sample. The child lets A supply only unsigned state and B supply all sign: (i) the market loading is estimated ONLY on free-repricing bars (|Δmid| above the grid quantum), removing the mechanical attenuation that grid-pinned bars impose on beta, so the measured debt beta_free·M6 − R6 is the genuinely undelivered response rather than an artefact of quantisation; (ii) the debt is scaled by a release gate = (share of the last 6 bars pinned) × (1 − exp(−volume absorbed while pinned / ADV)), i.e. the joint evidence that the price is grid-bound AND that the queue defending the pin is being consumed, which is precisely the state in which the accumulated backlog is discharged inside the next 6 bars; (iii) the product is cross-sectionally purged of the generic reversal carriers (1- and 6-bar returns, volume intensity) so what survives is market-anchored deliverable debt, not the bounce that the book already spans. Neither parent has this: B's magnitude was agnostic about delivery capacity and its beta was biased low for pinned names, while A's queue state carried no market-information anchor and therefore no reliable sign.
factors.name: Pin-attenuation-corrected beta debt with release gate

factors.trading_idea: Parent A splits short-horizon drift into quiet-bar (quote-repricing) and active-bar (paid impact) components and assumes fixed signs (+quiet, -active); Parent B shows that a Rice/Gaussian sign-flip null can tell grind from jump, but it measures that null *inside* each volume stream, where the quote-vs-trade dialogue is invisible by construction. The child measures the Rice excess concordance on the *handoff pairs between* the streams — each quiet bar paired with the immediately preceding active bar (do makers chase the trade, i.e. adverse-selection repricing => permanent) and each active bar paired with the immediately preceding quiet bar (do aggressors validate the silent quote move, i.e. trade-confirmed repricing => continuation) — and uses each stream's excess concordance over the arccos(rho)/pi null to set the *sign and strength of the other stream's leg*. The interaction is what neither parent has: A cannot distinguish informative quote shading from stale-mid noise or permanent from transient traded impact, and B's within-stream texture cannot see whether trades ratified or fought the quote move; the cross-stream handoff statistic is exactly the confirmation/rejection channel, so the quiet leg is traded as continuation only when subsequent aggressive flow agrees with it and is flipped to reversal when flow leans against it, while the traded leg is faded hardest only when makers immediately fade it (temporary impact into a vacuum) and left alone when quotes follow it (permanent repricing).
factors.name: Cross-Stream Handoff Rice Confirmation Drift Split

factors.trading_idea: A peer multiple spread only pays inside the fixed forecast window if its dislocation actually decays over that window: under a locally AR(1) (Ornstein-Uhlenbeck) spread, the expected h-bar move is -(1 - rho_h) times the current dislocation, so the cross-section should be weighted by each name's *measured* 6-bar decay coefficient rather than by dislocation size alone — persistent (slow) spreads look identical in level but deliver their reversion only at 20+ bars, which is exactly why the parent's IC kept rising with horizon. Second, comparables should be selected in multiple space (sector crossed with own-valuation tercile), because a name's spread against similarly-priced sector peers is a genuine relative-value spread rather than a business-mix artefact, and third, only *quiet* dislocations (no abnormal traded volume) are inventory/liquidity noise, while volume-backed dislocations are information and continue. The edge persists because harvesting it requires jointly estimating comparables, the horizon-matched decay rate and the flow condition, and because the reversion is fast and small in dollar terms relative to the inventory risk a market maker must warehouse to supply it. Falsified if IC is unchanged when the (1 - rho_6) weight is replaced by a constant, or if high-volume dislocations revert as strongly as quiet ones.
factors.name: Horizon-Matched Snapback of Valuation-Comparable Peer Multiple Spreads

factors.trading_idea: Parent A (sign CONFIRMED) says a peer-relative dislocation must be attributed to its source — idiosyncratic aggressive flow (informed, permanent) versus sector-basket flow (uninformed pressure) versus an unbacked 'quiet' residual (quote shading) — and only the latter two are fadeable; Parent B's realised IC was the exact opposite of its declared quiet-minus-traded direction, which is the same statement read from the microstructure side: at 10-second resolution a bar that actually prints reveals a marginal buyer/seller and its displacement persists, while a mid that moves with no print is stale-quote flicker that snaps back when the book refreshes. The child therefore keeps Parent B's cheap, bar-by-bar propagator decomposition of the peer-residual return but replaces its crude binary traded/quiet participation split with Parent A's three-way flow attribution: each bar's residual displacement is divided into idiosyncratic-flow-backed, basket-flow-backed and quiet components (weights from the trailing OLS decomposition of own signed sqrt-volume on ex-self peer flow, times the bar participation share), each accumulated with an exponential remaining-relaxation kernel of halflife 3 bars so the mass of un-relaxed impact lands inside the fixed 6-bar horizon. The fade legs are then scaled by leave-one-out peer liveness (Parent A: the snap-back is only harvestable when the hedge basket is tradable) and amplified when the transitory push moved the name further from its own trailing valuation anchor. The interaction is the edge: Parent A had a valuation anchor but no bar-resolution decay clock (its |IC| peaked at 24 bars, far past the horizon), Parent B had the decay clock but no way to tell informed single-name prints from index-style basket prints (so its 'traded' leg mixed permanent and transitory impact and its IC was weak and sign-flipped) — attributing the propagator legs by flow origin and gating them by hedgeability isolates displacement that is both wrong and repairable within six bars.
factors.name: Attributed propagator triple-leg hedge gate

factors.trading_idea: The parent's real working part was not the quarterly 'valuation multiple' (which is a step function and therefore contributes nothing to a 6-bar change beyond the raw return) but the idea that identical short-run displacements have opposite futures depending on what produced them. This child keeps only that testable core and measures three cheap, orthogonal signatures of *production cost* over exactly the 6-bar forecast window: (i) depth actually consumed — aggressive volume per unit of gross price travel, z-scored against the name's own norm (a high-depth move was paid for and is Kyle-permanent; a low-depth move is quote shading and snaps back); (ii) path resistance — |net move| / gross travel, so a monotone unresisted path signals sustained one-sided pressure while a choppy path means the displacement is an accident of churn defended by resting liquidity; (iii) flow concordance — the signed-flow imbalance ratio in the direction of the move. The falsifiable claim is a *sign flip*, not a level effect: the sector-demeaned 6-bar displacement predicts continuation when this composite information score is positive and reversal when it is negative, so the unconditional loading on displacement is near zero and the factor cannot be spanned by any linear reversal/momentum book factor. The edge persists because it is a conditional second-moment interaction that must be re-estimated per name every 10 seconds and harvested inside one minute, so its capacity is capped by spread costs rather than by information decay.
factors.name: Depth-backed vs. resisted displacement sign flip

factors.trading_idea: A heavy-volume bar with a large upper shadow and almost no body is not evidence of hidden supply — it is evidence that a liquidity provider *absorbed* an aggressive buy metaorder at the top of the excursion and is now short inventory (and symmetrically for lower shadows). The provider must repay that inventory over the following seconds, and the permanent component of the absorbed flow is under-reflected at the bar close, so price drifts back toward the probed side; this is why the parent's realised sign was the opposite of its 'concealed supply' story. The child therefore (i) weights each bar by absorption *purity* — wick mass relative to body mass — because a bar whose body already moved with the probe was permanent impact with no inventory left to unwind, (ii) replaces the binary volume gate with a continuous size weight so bigger absorptions count more, and (iii) subtracts the part of the accumulated inventory signal already explained by the trailing 6-bar return, since inventory that price has already repaid carries no further drift. The edge persists because capturing it means standing in front of the same aggressive flow and warehousing inventory risk for ~a minute at ten-second refresh — it is LP compensation, not a free arbitrage.
factors.name: Wick-absorption inventory repayment residual

factors.trading_idea: Parent B predicts the next-6-bar snapback of already-executed flow from the propagator's decay increment sum_k f_{t-k}[G(k+h)-G(k)], but treats every name's impact coefficient as identical and never looks at price; Parent A does look at price and estimates a per-name impact beta, but it projects a stale 12-bar displacement, so its edge drifts to 12 bars. The child does the full impact accounting at the fixed 6-bar clock: it builds the propagator impact stock P_t = sum_k f_{t-k}G(k), calibrates the per-name price-impact coefficient lambda and the propagator's explanatory power rho^2 by trailing regression of the 6-bar move on the 6-bar change in P, then (i) converts B's horizon-matched decay increment into actual expected log-return lambda*U — fading only the fraction of impact mathematically due to relax within 6 bars, not the whole fitted level — gated by B's flow-extinction/Hawkes liveness term, and (ii) routes whatever the propagator cannot explain, the residual R - lambda*dP, into A's ride-the-quiet-repricing leg. The interaction is the edge: rho^2 is a per-name, per-time trust switch that says whether the propagator has any claim on this name's move right now, so the snapback prediction is only taken where flow genuinely prices the tape and the quiet-repricing continuation is only taken where it does not — neither parent can distinguish 'no relaxation owed' from 'relaxation owed but unmeasurable', which is exactly where B's dimensionless flow rank and A's stale projection both bleed IC.
factors.name: Lambda-calibrated propagator decay increment with trust-routed quiet residual

factors.trading_idea: Parent A showed that at 10-second resolution the *permanence* of mid displacement depends on whether the flow behind it is name-specific (informed, continues) or basket/sector-common (uninformed overpush, reverts), while Parent B showed that how much of a past push is still 'owed' is governed by business time — volume traded since the push relative to the volume expected over the horizon — not calendar time. B's declared direction failed precisely because it never split the flow: on a 10s grid high-participation bars are disproportionately sector-wide activity bursts, so B's 'backed' leg was dominated by basket overpush and therefore net-reverted, exactly as A's basket leg predicts. The child fixes this by applying B's horizon-matched volume-clock kernel *separately to each of A's legs*: only push that has not yet been worked off in business time is still live, so the idiosyncratic-impact continuation leg (metaorder splitting, still un-completed in business time) and the basket-impact reversion leg (makers have not yet reloaded because too little volume has traded) are both measured on the clock that actually governs their decay, while A's fixed 12-bar box-car diluted both with already-resolved history.
factors.name: Volume-clock owed split: idiosyncratic vs basket flow impact

factors.trading_idea: A basket/VWAP/TWAP program consumes liquidity on a clock, so the name it is working shows an unusually *regular* volume stream (low coefficient of variation versus its own norm) with *low* self-excitation (near-zero volume autocorrelation, unlike Hawkes-style informational bursts) while its price drifts in a near-straight line; that displacement is paid-for liquidity demand and relaxes within tens of seconds. Information arrival produces the opposite flow signature — bursty, clustered, self-exciting volume — and its price move keeps diffusing to slower participants (Epps effect). The child therefore keeps the parent's attributed-versus-unattributed split but replaces the slow, weakly identified ex-ante attribution (turnover-minus-beta wedge times a lagged market displacement, which only paid off at 24 bars) with a per-name, per-bar flow-shape discriminator that re-estimates every bar, so the fade/ride allocation of the sector-neutral 3-bar dislocation lands at the fixed 6-bar offset. It survives arbitrage because the schedule trader keeps buying regardless of price (inelastic demand), and detecting it requires volume-shape statistics rather than the price patterns everyone already mines; falsification is direct — replace the regularity/self-excitation gate with a constant and the IC must collapse, and flipping the gate's sign must invert the IC.
factors.name: Schedule-regularity gated over-push relaxation

factors.trading_idea: Parent B's edge is purely mechanical: the h-bar price block about to fall out of an N-bar trailing anchor moves every anchor-follower's estimate by a fully-known amount, and anchor-chasing flow pushes price the same way. But that mechanical drift should only bite when the expiring block was a *transient* blip rather than a genuine repricing — Parent A's sqrt(volume)-weighted directional-consistency statistic, evaluated back when that block was the fresh bar-set, measures exactly that: a displacement accompanied by strongly one-sided sqrt-volume pressure was volume-backed and permanent (anchor-followers already recalibrated their fair value, so no re-anchoring flow), while a displacement with balanced/thin backing was noise that will simply drop out. Second, Parent A's realized (contradicted-hypothesis) sign says fresh one-sided sqrt-weighted pressure precedes *reversal* at 6 bars, so the current freshness wedge tells us whether live flow will accommodate or fight the mechanical anchor drift; we amplify the drift when the imminent flow reversal points the same way and damp it when live pressure is still pushing against it. The interaction carries edge neither parent has alone: B fires indiscriminately on backed and unbacked expiring blocks (diluting its IC), and A's raw pressure wedge is a weak, book-redundant reversal proxy — conditioning A's backing/freshness state on B's known-in-advance mechanical clock isolates precisely the expiries whose flow will actually be expressed.
factors.name: Unbacked expiry-block anchor drift, freshness-concordance gated

factors.trading_idea: The parent's partition of displacement into a volume-paid part and a flow-orthogonal part is sound, but its sign logic inverted the *measurement* problem: a cessation clock does not tell you when transient impact will decay, it tells you whether the displacement you just measured is still contaminated by undecayed transient impact. If the window's traded volume is concentrated in its last bars, the measured push still contains the fresh immediacy premium and mean-reverts as depth refills; if the volume arrived early and has since stopped, the transient part already decayed *inside* the window, so the surviving displacement is the permanent (informational) impact and it continues. Symmetrically, at a 10-second scale a mid move that no trade paid for is mostly fleeting-quote / depth-flicker noise and should revert — but only the part that is idiosyncratic to the name: a sector-common unpaid move is genuine repricing, so we purge the sector mean before reverting. The edge persists because harvesting it requires simultaneously pricing the sqrt-law cost of the flow, timing the contamination filter on a 20–60 second clock, and separating peer-common from name-specific quote noise; naive reversal traders take the opposite side precisely when flow has just ceased.
factors.name: Flow-recency contamination filter on paid vs unpaid displacement

factors.trading_idea: Parent A's local-time pinning density and Parent B's Rice memory coefficient measure partly the same object: a name whose 10-second mid is bounce-dominated (negative lag-1 autocorrelation) mechanically revisits its own level far more often, so A's 'pinning' gate was largely B's rho in disguise — and empirically that memory channel loads with the *opposite* sign to the depth channel (a window of high sign concordance is a metaorder whose impact is about to relax, while bounce noise reverts inside one bar, not six), which is exactly why both parents' declared directions were contradicted. The child inverts Rice at lag 1 to get each name's bar-return autocorrelation, writes down the *exact* AR(1) occupation probability that autocorrelation implies for the last 90 bars (P(|k-bar displacement| <= 1 sigma) summed over k), and keeps only the excess local time: pinning that cannot be explained by the name's own return memory, i.e. genuine two-sided resting depth standing at the current level. The traded interaction is then B's horizon-matched standardised 6-bar idiosyncratic displacement times that purged depth state: a displacement produced *against* real occupation had to consume real inventory and therefore continues, whereas the same displacement at a level the path has visited less than its memory implies is an unbacked mid drift through a vacuum that snaps back as quotes refill.
factors.name: Rice-purged excess local time gated displacement

factors.trading_idea: Transient trade impact only starts to relax once the metaorder that created it stops arriving, so the fastest-resolving state is: mid displaced in excess of what the concurrent volume can justify under the square-root impact law, PLUS aggressive flow that has just gone silent, PLUS a quote channel that is walking the other way. The parent proved the polarity (quiet-bar mid drift continues, traded-bar drift reverts) but accumulated both legs with flat weights over 12 bars, so most of its exposure sat on the slow concordant information state and its IC kept climbing to 24 bars; the child replaces that with per-bar sqrt-law deflation (u_t / sqrt(v_t/v_base), i.e. impact per unit sqrt-volume, so only super-elastic displacement is treated as transient) and exponentially recency-weighted channel legs (halflife 2-3 bars), then multiplies the maker/taker disagreement gate by a flow-cessation gate built from the log ratio of slow to fast volume intensity. Because the payload is now the freshest, most transient displacement and the gate fires exactly when the sustaining flow has just ceased, the resolution should land inside ~60 seconds rather than minutes. The edge survives arbitrage because harvesting it means crossing the spread in thin, momentarily silent names at the precise moment liquidity has withdrawn, and the state itself is extinguished by the next handful of liquidity events.
factors.name: Flow-cessation gated sqrt-law-deflated channel disagreement

factors.trading_idea: Parent A's fresh-minus-stale sqrt-volume-weighted pressure wedge realized a NEGATIVE IC: at the 10-second scale a burst of volume-backed one-sided repricing is mostly paid cost of immediacy, not unfinished flow, so it repays rather than continues — which is precisely the transient-impact snapback that Parent B confirmed through participation-weighted within-bar close location. The child fuses the two into one repayment estimate on a common square-root-law weighting: A's cross-bar sign wedge supplies the size and direction of the immediacy debt, the sqrt-volume-weighted close-location value supplies the *unrepaid fraction* (was the push handed back inside the bar or is the mid still parked at the pushed extreme?), and sign concordance amplifies names where both channels say the displacement is still standing. Crucially the fade is then routed by the state variable that explains A's sign flip — a metaorder-termination proxy, the ratio of freshest to baseline sqrt-volume arrival intensity: where arrival is still elevated the child order flow is unfinished and the fade is switched off, where arrival has decayed the debt is unowed inventory that mean-reverts as passive depth refills. That conditional switch is edge neither parent has (A averaged the two regimes into a weak wrong-signed wedge; B needed kernel/market-R² machinery that made it 62% redundant with the book), and it uses no kernel projection, no sector labels and no fundamentals.
factors.name: Flow-cessation-routed sqrt-law pressure repayment

factors.trading_idea: The speed at which a one-minute price dislocation is arbitraged back depends on how precisely the fair value of the name is pinned down: for value-transparent firms (high earnings and free-cash-flow yield, tangible asset base) statistical liquidity providers know what the stock is worth and will lean against a transient move, so dislocations revert within a minute; for opaque, intangible-heavy firms the fair-value band is wide, liquidity providers step back rather than take inventory against an unknown, and the same dislocation is allowed to keep walking (information-uncertainty continuation, Zhang 2006). The child therefore drops the parent's 286-operator quiet/traded Rice machinery entirely and keeps a single, coarse mechanism: a vol-normalised, market-neutral dislocation level (log price minus its own exponential anchor) multiplied by a size-neutralised fundamental anchor-precision score, so the factor is long reversal in transparent names and long continuation in opaque names. The edge should persist because it *is* the fair-value uncertainty that limits arbitrage: HFT liquidity providers do not condition inventory pricing on quarterly fundamentals, and fundamental investors cannot act at a 60-second offset, so nobody spans the two data domains this factor joins.
factors.name: Anchor-precision conditioned dislocation reversal

factors.trading_idea: The parent's propagator split was right in spirit but slow: it needed a 180-bar per-name covariance beta and a 12-bar move to estimate the impact coefficient, so its information peaked two minutes out rather than at the fixed 6-bar offset. Kyle–Obizhaeva market-microstructure invariance supplies the impact coefficient from theory instead of estimation: for a stock with trailing trading activity W (dollar volume x volatility), the percentage impact of a signed imbalance Q is proportional to sigma * W^(1/3) * Q/V, and 'business time' passes at rate W^(2/3), so high-activity names relax their transient impact faster in calendar bars. Imposing that scaling lets me measure the displacement/imbalance pair over only the last 4 bars (no estimation lag), and lets me weight the fade leg by the invariance-implied fraction of impact that will actually decay inside exactly 6 bars, phi = 1 - exp(-w^(2/3)); a move larger than invariance-implied impact was not paid for by flow and keeps propagating, while a move fully accounted for by invariance-implied impact is mechanical and snaps back. The edge survives arbitrage because harvesting it means providing liquidity against the very flow that just moved the price on a one-minute clock, with capacity capped by the same thinness that creates the signal, and because the signal conditions on the origin of a move relative to a theoretical impact law rather than on its level, keeping it near-orthogonal to crowded momentum/reversal books.
factors.name: Invariance-scaled impact share with bet-clock relaxation split

factors.trading_idea: The parent proved that the Epps-corrected, precision-whitened, peer-purged 6-bar dislocation carries information the book does not span, but its occupancy gate had the mechanism backwards: a high-occupancy level is not evidence that costly informed flow ate real depth, it is evidence of a strong *restoring force* — the mid keeps returning there because two-sided resting depth is continuously replenished at levels the market has already agreed on. The child therefore measures the empirical occupation measure of the pre-move window and evaluates it at BOTH endpoints of the same 6-bar interval that we must forecast: if the whitened dislocation *landed* in a relatively well-occupied region it has arrived at a magnet whose refilling queues absorb it, so the idiosyncratic move is repaid within six bars; if it exited into a relatively empty region there is no resting depth to absorb the next marginal order, price impact per unit flow is locally maximal, and the excursion extends. Because the state variable is a density *contrast across the forecast interval* (not a slow 240-bar level z-score), its information decays on the same 6-bar clock as the forecast — fixing the parent's horizon mismatch — and it survives arbitrage because trading it requires simultaneously estimating a lag-1-corrected cross-sectional precision matrix and a per-name occupation measure at two evaluation points, and because the profitable leg is exactly where liquidity provision is either cheap (magnet) or dangerous (vacuum).
factors.name: Occupation-measure contrast across the move (landing-site split)

factors.trading_idea: Short-horizon agents anchor on rolling *volume-weighted* fair values (rolling VWAP), not equal-weighted means, so the mechanically-known part of the next-h-bar anchor move is exactly w/(1-w)·(A − p̄_exp), where w is the VOLUME share of the block about to expire from the N-bar window and p̄_exp is that block's volume-weighted price: an expiring block that was heavily traded and priced below the anchor guarantees the anchor ratchets upward over precisely the next h bars, and anchor-chasing flow pushes price with it. Volume weighting is the new conditioning channel the parent lacked — it turns a pure price-anomaly statistic into a flow-weighted amplitude that self-scales with h/N, concentrating the predicted move inside the 6-bar horizon instead of bleeding out to 24 bars, and it is falsified if the volume-share amplitude carries no incremental IC over the equal-weight block anomaly. Requiring sign concordance across the plausible anchor lengths (12/20/30/60/120 bars) isolates events where all crowd anchors drift the same way, i.e. where mechanical flow is unambiguous. The edge persists because each expiry is tiny, the arbitrageur must both know which windows are crowded and be willing to take the other side of flow that keeps arriving for the whole expiry span, and the statistic uses only prices/volumes from N−h..N bars ago so it is orthogonal by construction to current momentum and reversal.
factors.name: VWAP-anchor expiry volume-share drift (cross-window concordant)

factors.trading_idea: Parent A's AR(1) pricing-error machinery is right but it was pointed at the wrong channel: it identified rho from the *total* return autocovariance and then faded quiet (untraded) displacement, which on a 10-second mid-price feed is mostly genuine quote revision — hence its contradicted sign. Parent B shows where the transient component actually lives and where it is repaid: the within-bar body is impact accrued while trades arrive, and the following seams (open minus previous close) are the dealer re-centring that repays it, with corr(body_{t-1}, seam_t) a stable per-name fingerprint. The child identifies BOTH the repayment gain theta and its decay rho purely from trailing body→seam cross-covariances (theta = -c1/var(body), rho = c2/c1 — no forward returns, Parent A's trick applied to Parent B's channel pair), then runs a causal ledger of unpaid transient impact e_t = a·e_{t-1} + gain·traded_body_t + 0.5·seam_t that credits the give-back the seams have *actually* delivered instead of assuming it, and forecasts the horizon-matched fraction -(1-rho^6)·e_t. The interaction is the edge: rho converts B's ad-hoc 4-bar decay gate into a per-name 6-bar repayment clock and, unlike B's rank gate, lets names whose seams *extend* bodies (theta<0, informed order-splitting leaking across bar boundaries) be traded with the push rather than muted — so the same estimated kernel prices both liquidity-supply and adverse-selection regimes on one scale.
factors.name: Seam-reciprocation identified transient-impact ledger

factors.trading_idea: From OHLCV alone one can estimate which side of the book is thinner: for each traded bar compute the square-root-law impact coefficient |r|/sqrt(V) and take the trailing median separately over up-bars and down-bars. A high up-side coefficient means little volume is needed to lift the price (thin ask), a low down-side coefficient means large volume is absorbed on the way down (thick bid); depth asymmetry of this kind is persistent over minutes and is the classic order-book-imbalance predictor, so price should drift toward the thin side over the next ~1 minute. The edge survives arbitrage precisely because harvesting it requires crossing the spread in the direction the book is thin, i.e. paying the very impact the signal measures, and because the estimate is a per-name ratio (unit-free) rather than a tradeable price level. Falsified if the asymmetry precedes reversal (negative IC) or if per-name residualisation against the window's own cumulative return destroys the IC, which would show it is just relabelled momentum.
factors.name: Directional Resilience Asymmetry (up/down sqrt-impact thinness)

factors.trading_idea: A price path's mean-reversion speed is a nuisance parameter that ordinary short-term reversal signals average over: a deviation that decays with a 1-bar clock is already gone (and pure noise) by the time a 6-bar forecast is evaluated, while a deviation with a 100-bar clock has barely moved. I estimate each name's reversion clock non-parametrically as the mean spacing between zero-crossings of its deviation from a trailing anchor (a Kac/level-crossing counting statistic, dimensionless and immune to jumps and to volatility level, unlike AR(1)/variance-ratio half-life estimators that a single 10-second outlier destroys), and then trade the signed deviation only with weight sech^2-shaped in log(clock / horizon), i.e. maximal where the name's own oscillation period matches the fixed 6-bar holding window. Falsifiable prediction: the negative normalised deviation predicts 6-bar forward returns *monotonically in this clock-match weight* — names with clock far from 6 bars carry no 6-bar reversal edge, and a version with the weight removed or inverted should be materially weaker. The edge survives arbitrage because the profit is horizon-specific and per-name (capacity-limited, invisible to anyone who pools all names into one reversal book), and because estimating the crossing clock needs long trailing windows of high-frequency data whose payoff is a matching, not a level, effect.
factors.name: Crossing-clock horizon-matched deviation fade

factors.trading_idea: Parent A showed that a price deviation only pays over a 6-bar hold if its own zero-crossing (Kac) clock is ~6 bars, but it measured ONE clock on a deviation that is really the sum of two physically different processes: quote-side repricing printed in quiet bars and impact printed in traded bars. Parent B isolated those two channels but had no way to know when each resolves, so its rotated common/wedge pair had no standalone direction. The child decomposes the trailing anchor deviation *exactly* (linear-weight identity p_t - mean(p) = weighted sum of returns) into quiet-bar and traded-bar contributions, rotates them into a corroborated COMMON component and a maker-vs-taker WEDGE component, and then estimates a separate crossing clock for each rotated component, fading each with its own sech^2(0.5·ln(T/h)) horizon-match kernel. The interaction is the edge: the wedge (a standoff that clears at the next few liquidity events) typically carries a fast clock and receives full weight at h=6, while the common component's slow clock is automatically zeroed out — which is precisely why A's IC kept leaking to 24 bars (it was dominated by the slow concordant leg) and why B's wedge only ever helped as a conditioner.
factors.name: Channel-rotated crossing-clock wedge fade

factors.trading_idea: A bar's return splits into end-of-bar pressure (where the close sits relative to the bar's own range centre — the push accomplished in the last seconds) and centre relocation (where the range centre itself moved — the repricing the market actually ratified). Whether pressure is absorbed (next centres relocate against it, transient inventory push) or informative (centres relocate with it, permanent repricing) is not a fixed per-name constant as the parent assumed, but a switching, per-name state; I identify it causally with an exponentially-forgetting Gaussian likelihood-ratio between the two hypotheses q_t = ±g·p_(t-1), whose evidence term collapses to minus the standardized cross-product of prior pressure and current relocation. Conditioning the *sign* (not merely the magnitude) of the pushback trade on that posterior — shrunk by fast/slow concordance and by how identifiable the range channel is — should beat the parent's static [0,1] mute. The edge survives arbitrage because acting on it means posting passive size against possibly-informed end-of-bar aggression for a fraction of the spread (a market-making inventory risk), and because the regime label flips on a minutes timescale so no static rule captures it.
factors.name: Centre-relocation reciprocation regime posterior

factors.trading_idea: The parent bet on the *odd* part of the peer-hedged residual (a move up is followed by a move down), which is the same object dozens of book factors already express; its residual IC was thin because that sign structure is crowded. This child keeps the parent's machinery that worked — an industry/size-matched kernel basket, a beta-hedged idiosyncratic return, and a hedgeability (R-squared) gate — but changes the mechanism to an *even* one: the size of an idiosyncratic burst is treated as an attention/quote-refresh event whose direction of follow-through is set not by the burst's own sign but by the name's slow valuation position relative to its size-matched industry comparables. Valuation-aware slow participants (fundamental long-onlys, index-relative PMs, buyback desks) carry standing asymmetric interest — they supply into names rich versus close comparables and absorb in cheap ones — but that interest is only *executed* when local volatility refreshes quotes and pulls liquidity demand to the name; hence abnormal idiosyncratic burst magnitude times relative richness should predict negative returns, and the same interaction with negative sign in unusually quiet windows. It is falsifiable: if forward returns after an abnormal idiosyncratic burst are unrelated to size-matched relative richness (interaction coefficient ~0), the standing-asymmetric-interest mechanism is wrong and only the crowded odd/reversal part exists. The edge persists because the sign comes from quarterly point-in-time per-share fundamentals while the amplitude comes from 30-second hedged residual volatility — two clocks that pure microstructure desks do not join, and the trade requires waiting for a burst rather than trading a continuously visible spread.
factors.name: Size-matched relative-richness gating of idiosyncratic burst follow-through

factors.trading_idea: Quiet-bar price increments (a maker walking a reservation quote with nobody trading) and traded-bar increments (Bouchaud impact) are two coupled flows on the same price, and their coupling is what sets the one-minute clock: a silent walk invites the trades that either confirm or reject it, and a traded push provokes makers to re-quote either with or against it. I therefore drop the parent's standing displacement *level* entirely — the report shows its payoff lives at 24 bars — and instead fit, per name, a causal bivariate VAR(1) on 3-bar block sums of the two origin-attributed peer-relative increment channels (Yule-Walker, A = C1 C0^-1 from trailing moments, ridge-regularised, empirical-Bayes shrunk to the cross-sectional mean matrix and rescaled to spectral radius < 0.9). The signal is then the *exact* horizon-matched object e'(A + A^2)X_t, i.e. the model's cumulative forecast of the peer-relative return over precisely the next two 3-bar blocks = 6 bars, so a fast-reverting channel enters with a negative weight, a persistent grind with a multi-block positive weight, and an oscillatory (complex-eigenvalue) pair with whatever sign its phase has at 60 seconds. The edge survives arbitrage because the 2x2 coupling is name- and regime-specific, sign-flipping, and only visible after attributing increments to silent vs traded bars — the very market makers who generate it are the ones who would have to trade it away, and its capacity is one minute of a single name's idiosyncratic drift.
factors.name: Origin-channel block-VAR six-bar cumulative projection

factors.trading_idea: The parent proved that the Epps-corrected precision-whitened dislocation carries information the book does not span, but it traded the *instantaneous* Kuramoto derivative, so its edge lived at one bar and had decayed to noise by six. This child replaces the derivative with the finite-horizon solution of Adler's phase equation: a causal one-sided Gabor quadrature pair measures each name's slow (24-bar) oscillation phase and amplitude in the whitened relative-value metric, the antisymmetric lag-1 correlation row-sums build a coherent mean field out of the *measured leaders only*, and each name is then classified by the Adler locking criterion |ω_i − ω_L| ≤ |κ_i·R_L|. Only phase-locked names get a forecast, and that forecast is the full trigonometric displacement A[cos(θ + ω_L·h + Δφ·(1−e^{−λh})) − cos θ] with λ = |κR|·cos φ* the measured locking margin and h fixed at 6 — so names whose entrainment carries them past their turning point inside six bars are correctly predicted to give the move back, which is exactly the nonlinearity a one-bar derivative cannot see. The edge should persist because it requires jointly estimating a lag-1-corrected precision matrix, a coherent leader set and a per-name locking margin; each piece is individually weak and noisy, and the profitable subset (locked laggards near their turning point) is a small, state-dependent slice of the cross-section rather than a static exposure.
factors.name: Adler locking-margin leader-phase dislocation forecast

factors.trading_idea: The parent measured the *level* of sqrt-volume-weighted directional pressure and the book already spans it (71% correlated) while its realized IC was negative, i.e. fresh pressure precedes relaxation, not continuation. The informative object is therefore not how much one-sided pressure exists but how *improbable* the current displacement is given the flow that produced it: the gap between the mid and the volume-weighted average price actually paid over the horizon-matched window is the unrealized transient impact of the live metaorder, and Bouchaud's propagator says its excess part relaxes as depth refills. We benchmark that gap non-parametrically instead of with a parametric sqrt-law: bucket each name's own history by trade-intensity tier (trailing rank of 6-bar volume) and standardise the current mid-minus-VWAP gap by the second moment of the same gap observed in the *same* intensity tier, then damp the predicted relaxation when intensity is still accelerating (metaorder still live and pushing). The edge survives arbitrage because it lives inside a one-minute window where net-of-spread capacity is tiny, the flow that created the overshoot is itself the counterparty and cannot arbitrage its own impact, and the reversal is paid to inventory-bearing liquidity providers as compensation, not as free money.
factors.name: Intensity-tier-conditional transient-impact overshoot relaxation

factors.trading_idea: Both parents' realised ICs point at the same hidden law from opposite sides: Parent B showed that a peer-relative dislocation accompanied by heavy participation FADES over the next minute (depth absorbed the order, so impact was transient), while Parent A showed that a burst created in a thin book (high variance per unit of traded volume) KEEPS GOING even after visible aggressive flow rolls off its peak (a high-Kyle-lambda vacuum reprices the name permanently, and the pause is just the gap between child orders). The child therefore uses Parent A's purity variable — realised-variance burst divided by participation burst, i.e. price impact per unit of flow — as the *sign switch* on Parent B's basket-relative displacement: fade the dislocation when it was well-participated / cheap in impact terms, ride it when it was produced in a liquidity vacuum. Parent A's Hawkes-style side-aligned flow intensity survives only as a non-sign-flipping freshness weight (intensity relative to its own 12-bar peak), so the switch is applied hardest while the episode is still live and the position is muted once the flow event is dead; neither parent can express this because A has no peer-relative displacement to switch and B has no impact-per-flow measure to decide permanence.
factors.name: Impact-purity switched peer dislocation, flow-freshness weighted

factors.trading_idea: A first-moment (market-return) shock is arbitraged away within a bar or two at the 10-second scale, which is why the parent's lagged-beta catch-up peaked at 1 bar and turned negative by 12; a *second-moment* shock is not, because it acts through risk limits rather than through prices: when market or sector realized volatility jumps, VaR/inventory-constrained intermediaries and gamma hedgers must shed exposure, and that de-risking is executed by schedule over tens of seconds. Each name therefore has a measurable, persistent 6-bar cumulative response to a volatility innovation observed 6 bars earlier, and that response is estimated here directly at the fixed 6-bar offset and folded against the volatility innovation that is being delivered right now — after purging the contemporaneous market/sector moves and the lagged market move (i.e. the parent's own channel), so the forecast is orthogonal-by-construction to plain beta catch-up. The edge should persist because the exposure is a *second-moment* loading that needs a long trailing window and a leverage-effect purge to estimate (noisy, unattractive to latency-driven capital), and the binding constraint — risk limits — tightens exactly when fast arbitrage capital is itself constrained; it is falsified if the purged volatility-innovation loading carries no forecast power at the 6-bar offset (IC ~ 0), or if it is merely a relabelling of return-beta / realized-vol level.
factors.name: Systematic vol-shock de-risking response (market + sector channels)

factors.trading_idea: With only mid-prices and unsigned volume we cannot see the book, but we can *infer* it: the volume required to move the mid one unit upward versus downward over the last few minutes is an estimator of the inverse depth standing on the ask versus the bid. If it takes much less traded volume to lift the mid than to push it down, the ask side is thin relative to the bid (positive depth imbalance), and because market-order arrival is strongly self-exciting at the 10-second scale, the next wave of flow mechanically clears the thin side first — the Cont–Kukanov–Stoikov depth-imbalance result, recovered from trade-and-mid data alone. The signal is deliberately orthogonalised cross-sectionally against the window's drift and its activity level, so what remains is 'volume absorbed per unit of price move on each side' rather than momentum or liquidity size; falsified if the residual asymmetry carries no forward IC (i.e. per-side impact ratios are pure binning noise) or if it flips sign, which would mean thin sides are already exhausted rather than about to be cleared. The edge survives arbitrage because reconstructing depth imbalance without L2 data is non-obvious, the state decays within a minute, and monetising it requires paying spread on the thin side of thin names.
factors.name: Per-Side Impact Elasticity (Depth) Asymmetry

factors.trading_idea: Treat the panel's short-run standardised returns as an empirical distribution (a cross-sectional 'gas') rather than N independent time series: dispersion-compressing capital — pairs desks, basket/ETF arbitrage, dispersion traders — sells names that have separated upward from the bulk of their comparables and buys those that have separated downward, so the cross-sectional density relaxes toward its local mode in the McKean–Vlasov / Fokker–Planck sense, and each name inherits a drift proportional to the local gradient of that density. I estimate this drift directly as a Gaussian kernel mean-shift (leave-one-out) of a name's 3-minute vol-standardised return toward the local cross-sectional mode, multiplied by the leave-one-out local density, which by the mean-shift identity is exactly the density gradient ∇ρ at the name's position. This geometry makes two sharp, falsifiable claims that plain cross-sectional reversal cannot make: the pull is near zero for names sitting *inside* a dense cluster (no matter how large their move) and near zero for names in the sparse extreme tails (where separation is news-driven and no substitute exists), so the bet is concentrated on the distribution's shoulders; and because the compressing flow is executed by arbitrageurs who trade the most tradable names first, the pull is scaled by cross-sectional dollar-volume rank. It survives arbitrage because the effect *is* the arbitrage: what is left is the residual few ticks of an incomplete compression that requires real-time per-bar nonparametric density estimation across the whole cross-section and pays the spread on both legs.
factors.name: Cross-sectional return-density gradient relaxation

factors.trading_idea: Parent A showed that a peer-relative dislocation in log-multiple space closes at a rate that must be *measured* per industry at the exact 6-bar forecast lag, not assumed; Parent B showed that bar-level peer-residual displacement splits cleanly into a trade-attributable (transient, propagator-relaxing) part and a quiet quote-revision (permanent) part, but it hard-coded the wedge's sign and was contradicted. The child notes that A's dislocation level is *exactly* an exponentially decayed sum of past peer-residual returns, so it can be split additively into a traded-accumulated component D_a and a quiet-accumulated component D_b (D_a + D_b = d), and then runs one horizon-matched, industry-pooled two-regressor OLS of the realised 6-bar change in d on the 6-bar-lagged D_a and D_b (ridge-regularised, shrunk to the panel-wide solution), predicting the next 6 bars' closure as beta_a·D_a + beta_b·D_b. The interaction carries edge neither parent has: A applies a single blended coefficient to a state that mixes two channels with opposite relaxation dynamics (which is exactly why its IC kept drifting out to 24 bars), while B imposes a unit, fixed-sign wedge on two separately z-scored legs (destroying their relative magnitude and getting the sign wrong); estimating the two closure coefficients jointly lets the *wedge itself* — its sign, size and group/regime dependence — be fitted at the 6-bar offset, so the fast-relaxing traded inventory channel and the slow-persisting quiet-repricing channel are each weighted by their own live, measured half-life of reversion.
factors.name: Propagator-split pooled closure slopes in multiple space

factors.trading_idea: Parent A showed that peer-relative dislocations in multiple space carry a *measurable*, horizon-matched group response coefficient (sometimes reversal, sometimes continuation), but it treated every dislocation as one homogeneous object; Parent B showed that a displacement built by aggressive trade flow (Kyle-lambda-explained, transient, book refills) obeys completely different relaxation physics from one built by quiet quote repricing (informational, permanent) — yet it *asserted* the signs and got contradicted out of sample. The child splits the standardised peer-multiple dislocation into a flow-explained channel (own trailing Kyle lambda times exponentially-demeaned cumulative signed sqrt-flow) and a flow-unexplained quiet channel, plus a metaorder-persistence interaction on the flow channel, and then lets Parent A's industry-pooled, hierarchically-shrunk OLS estimated at exactly the 6-bar forecast lag decide the coefficient on each channel. The interaction carries edge neither parent has: a single-channel regression (A) averages a fast-decaying transient coefficient with a slow/continuing informational one and estimates something near zero, while an assumed-sign decomposition (B) is run over whenever the book's resiliency or the prevailing metaorder regime flips — measuring one coefficient per channel per group per hour recovers both the amplitude and the sign that the two parents each got wrong in a different way.
factors.name: Dual-channel pooled response: flow-explained vs quiet peer-multiple dislocation

factors.trading_idea: Parent A splits the last ~minute of displacement into a flow-explained (transient, Bouchaud-propagator) part and an unexplained (permanent, Hasbrouck quote-revision) part via a per-name no-intercept impact coefficient lambda, but its only trust gate is the regression R-squared, which measures magnitude fit and is blind to whether the residual repricing is genuine sequential quote shading or a single stale-mid gap. Parent B supplies exactly that discriminator — the excess of the realised adjacent-sign-flip frequency over the Rice/Gaussian null arccos(rho)/pi, negative for grinds (many small same-signed increments) and positive for jump-carried drift — but it applies it to volume-partitioned raw bars in which quote-driven and trade-driven increments are still mixed. The child applies the Rice gap to the *regression-decomposed streams themselves*: the residual (unexplained) series and the fitted lambda*signed-sqrt-volume (explained) series, which are the cleanest available separations of pure quote revision from paid impact. The permanent leg is trusted only when its own residual stream is grind-carried (real tick-by-tick belief propagation to slower participants continues over the next minute) and switched off when jump-carried (stale print), while the transient leg is faded hardest when the flow stream is jump-carried (a metaorder slammed into a vacuum, which snaps back) and left alone when the flow stream is a persistent grind (a still-working parent order that keeps pushing) — an interaction neither parent can express.
factors.name: Rice-gated lambda decomposition: grind-carried permanent vs jump-carried transient impact

factors.trading_idea: A quote move is only permanent once flow has paid for it, so the flow-validated anchor of a name over a short window is its volume-weighted average log price while the naive anchor is the equal-time average; their difference d = VWAP_log - TWAP_log is, by construction, exactly the component of the price-vs-average-anchor displacement that is orthogonal to plain reversal (it is proportional to the within-window covariance of traded volume with price level and is invariant to the displacement level itself). When d > 0 the recent excursion was transacted at the prices it reached (validated -> it persists); when d < 0 the excursion was quote-only drift on thin bars (unvalidated -> dealers and stale-quote correction pull it back). The parent expressed the same idea with a recursive volume-time EWMA plus a 390-bar OLS purge, which made it a slow state variable whose |IC| peaked at 12 bars; replacing the recursion+regression by the closed-form wedge over a 12-bar window and multiplying by the current trade-arrival intensity (correction only happens when trades actually arrive to test the quote) moves the reversion clock onto the fixed 6-bar offset with a fraction of the parameters. The edge survives arbitrage because each snapback is a few basis points, below single-name round-trip cost, and is only harvestable as a diversified, sector-neutral overlay.
factors.name: Flow- vs time-weighted anchor wedge, arrival-gated

factors.trading_idea: A peer spread in multiple space is not a single object: it is a superposition of frequency bands, and each band relaxes on its own timescale, so a statistic built as 'deviation from a 5-minute EWMA' is dominated by low-frequency content that only unwinds over many minutes (exactly why the parent's IC grew monotonically out to 24 bars). To forecast a fixed 6-bar (60-second) offset, I extract the matched band of the comparability-weighted log-multiple spread with a difference-of-EWMAs high-pass (half-lives 1.5 and 6 bars), whose autocorrelation decays on the horizon being forecast, and then scale it by each name's own causally estimated band-level reversion elasticity — the trailing OLS slope of the realised 6-bar spread change on the band value 6 bars earlier. Names where that slope is reliably negative are the ones whose 60-second multiple-space displacement is transient inventory/impact noise rather than genuine repricing, so the liquidity-provision premium is collected there and nowhere else. Falsifiable two ways: if the band-pass does not move the |IC| peak toward 6 bars, frequency matching is wrong; if the elasticity interaction adds nothing over the raw band-pass, the self-calibration channel is spurious. The edge persists because it requires joint point-in-time per-share fundamentals, cross-sectional comparability weighting and per-name high-frequency elasticity estimation, and because the underlying flow (peer-basket and ETF-driven displacement) is recurrent, not a one-off inefficiency.
factors.name: Multiple-Space Band-Pass Dislocation × Measured Reversion Elasticity

factors.trading_idea: Model each mid-price as an efficient random walk plus an autocorrelated microstructure/transitory component (Roll, Hasbrouck; Zhang–Mykland–Aït-Sahalia). The trailing multi-scale variance signature V(K)=E[(log p_t-log p_{t-K})^2]/K identifies BOTH the size of the transitory component (V(1)-V(6), the two-scale noise variance) and, through the curvature of that signature, its release speed rho: the ratio (V1-V2)/(V1-V6) tends to ~0.6 for i.i.d. quote noise that unwinds in one bar and to ~0.2 when the transitory component is long-lived (a metaorder still being worked). The signal-extraction gain implied by the estimated noise-to-signal ratio q gives the steady-state local-level Kalman weight alpha = (-q + sqrt(q^2+4q))/2, so the deviation of the observed mid from that optimally filtered efficient price is an identified pricing error, and only the fraction (1 - rho^6) of it can be harvested inside a 60-second horizon. The edge persists because standard reversal traders normalise deviations by realised volatility with a fixed lookback, which cannot separate quickly-unwinding quote noise from a slow metaorder-driven drift of identical magnitude; the names where the deviation does revert fast are also the ones where the deviation is small relative to the spread, so capacity is limited and the compensation for supplying liquidity is not competed away.
factors.name: Two-scale noise-release pricing error

factors.trading_idea: A stale name does not owe catch-up on a bar clock — it owes it on its own *repricing-arrival* clock: the market shock from l bars ago is still unincorporated only if no repricing event (trade / mid revision) has arrived since, which under a memoryless-with-self-excitation arrival model happens with probability (1-h_i)^(l+1). Replacing the parent's six free lag loadings with this two-parameter arrival model (one long-run Dimson-style total beta from k-bar cumulative regressions, one state-dependent hazard h_i) gives an *explicitly horizon-matched* forecast: expected delivery inside the next 6 bars = total beta × geometric undelivered stock × (1-(1-h_i)^6). This is a strict fix for the parent's mass drift, because the product is single-peaked in h: very fast repricers hold no undelivered stock (their adjustment is already done and their 6-bar return is dominated by transient-impact reversal, which is what drove the parent's negative 12–24 bar IC), while very slow repricers hold a big stock but deliver almost none of it inside the window — so only names whose arrival clock resonates with the 6-bar offset receive weight. The edge persists because it is a second-scale attention/latency effect concentrated in the thin, infrequently-repriced tail where monitoring capital is scarce, and it is falsified if the geometric arrival weighting and the within-horizon delivery probability add nothing over an unweighted trailing market wedge, or if the signal's IC keeps peaking at 1 bar rather than at the declared 6-bar offset.
factors.name: Arrival-clock undelivered beta stock (geometric repricing hazard)

factors.trading_idea: The parent imposed the Bouchaud/Hasbrouck sign a priori (flow-paid displacement is transient, untraded repricing is permanent) and paid for it with a horizon mismatch: the imposed split only pays at ~12 bars because the *speed* at which each channel resolves is name-specific, not universal. Here I stop assuming the sign and instead measure it exactly where it will be used: for each name I run a trailing two-regressor no-intercept OLS of the realized 6-bar block return on the 6-bar-lagged traded-flow channel (signed sqrt-volume) and the 6-bar-lagged flow-orthogonal quiet-displacement channel, so the coefficients ARE the empirical response of the fixed forecast offset to each channel (fast resilient books give a negative flow coefficient, slow/propagating books a positive one). Per-name coefficients over ~33 minutes are noisy, so they are pulled toward the contemporaneous cross-sectional mean by a James-Stein/empirical-Bayes weight tau^2/(tau^2+se^2) built from each regression's own coefficient variance, which keeps only the part of a name's idiosyncratic response that the data can actually resolve. The edge persists because it requires per-name, precision-weighted estimation of a *signed* 6-bar impact-response kernel rather than one global lambda and one global 'impact decays' assumption, and because the states it exploits (thin-tape quiet repricing and depleted-depth snapback) carry tiny capacity.
factors.name: Offset-calibrated two-channel impact response (EB-shrunk)

factors.trading_idea: Transient impact is only repaid when the opposite side of the book replenishes, so the *speed* of the snapback — not its existence — is what decides whether it lands inside a fixed 60-second window. Two observable quantities separate the two halves of that statement: bar-level directional purity |close-open|/range identifies which bars actually spent volume walking the book (a sweep creates impact debt, a two-sided churn bar does not), while a name's ambient volume-weighted churn over the preceding few minutes (traded participation that produces little net displacement) measures how fast its book two-sides and therefore how much of the debt is repaid per unit of clock time. The parent mixed fast- and slow-replenishing names, which is exactly why its IC kept growing out to 24 bars; tilting the same idiosyncratic, participation-weighted range-position displacement toward high-churn (high-resilience) names moves the mass of the repayment into the fixed 6-bar horizon. The edge survives arbitrage because harvesting it requires posting passive size against impatient aggressors in exactly the depth that generated the displacement, so capacity is capped by the illiquidity that creates the signal; falsifiable if the 6-bar reversion of sweep debt is independent of (or decreasing in) the lagged churn-resilience measure.
factors.name: Churn-resilience gated sweep-impact snapback

factors.trading_idea: Noise-trader risk theory (Shleifer–Vishny, Daniel–Titman) says transitory price displacement is absorbed slowly precisely in names whose fundamental value is hard to pin down: intangible/R&D-heavy, accrual-driven, glamour-priced, loss-making names, and names whose last report gave internally conflicting signals (EPS beat with revenue miss or vice versa). In those names a liquidity provider who takes the other side of a 1-minute push cannot mark the push against a sharp fundamental anchor, so she demands a wider transitory concession and the diffusive part of the displacement snaps back; in transparent names the same push is absorbed almost instantly and carries no reversal. The child therefore measures the *jump-truncated, beta-purged* 6-bar displacement (Mancini-style threshold at 3.5 robust sigmas, so news jumps are excluded and only diffusive, inventory-driven drift is counted) and scales its reversal only in proportion to a within-sector fundamental-opacity rank. It is falsifiable in a sharp way: the reversal coefficient must be monotone increasing in the opacity rank, and if opacity instead proxies for informed trading the interaction flips sign. The edge persists because the conditioning variable is a quarterly, point-in-time balance-sheet/estimate composite that fee-sensitive HFT market makers do not gate on — they gate on spread, depth and queue position — while the fundamental arbitrageurs who could bear the noise-trader risk do not trade at a 1-minute horizon.
factors.name: Fundamental-opacity-gated truncated idiosyncratic displacement snapback

factors.trading_idea: Parent A knows *within-bar geometry* (was aggressive size absorbed and retraced, or accepted?) but cannot tell a low close inside a heavy range from the mechanical delivery of an owed market beta move; Parent B computes exactly that owed amount as a horizon-matched distributed-lag kernel forecast (loadings on market returns at lags 1..6 folded against the already-observed market path, so all of its mass lands inside the fixed 6-bar offset) but is too weak to trade alone. The child purges the fast participation-weighted close-location displacement of the part linearly explained by B's kernel forecast (trailing per-name OLS residual), so only the *un-owed* displacement is faded, and then routes between fading that residual and riding the kernel with a two-sided state variable neither parent has: within-bar absorption (participation-weighted wick share) versus repricing staleness (frozen-mid fraction and thin relative volume). Absorbed pushes in fast-repricing names are pure paid-for immediacy and snap back inside 6 bars; body-dominated pushes in stale, slow-repricing names are unfinished beta delivery where the kernel's sign is the forecast — the interaction is the edge because absorption identifies *whether* the move was accepted while staleness identifies *whether the name still owes* it, and only the conjunction says which side of the trade is safe.
factors.name: Absorption-vs-Staleness Routed, Kernel-Purged Transient Snapback

factors.trading_idea: Within-bar displacement of the mid away from the range extreme is mostly the temporary cost of immediacy, and it reverts only once the depth that was consumed has been replenished — a *volume* clock, not a wall-clock. The repair time of a given push is therefore approximately (bar volume / normal bar volume) bars, so pushes built by enormous participation take minutes to unwind (their reversion IC lives at 24+ bars, which is exactly why the parent's participation-linear weighting mis-timed the fixed 6-bar offset) while pushes on near-normal size unwind within a few bars. Replacing the monotone participation weight with a log-normal kernel centred on a repair time of ~2.5 bars (geometric middle of the 1–6 bar window) selects exactly the displacements whose repair clock matches the fixed horizon, and the kernel simultaneously discards quiet bars (no traded size ⇒ displacement is quote repricing/information, not liquidity cost). Sector demeaning keeps only the name-specific, liquidity-provision part; the edge survives arbitrage because harvesting it means posting passive size into the same thin depth that produced the displacement, so capacity is bounded by the illiquidity that creates it.
factors.name: Repair-clock-matched transient displacement snapback
