factors.trading_idea: Parent A showed that efficient (one-way) mid displacement printed during no-trade silence predicts the OPPOSITE of genuine repricing on average — because on a 10-second mid feed most smooth quiet drift is one-sided quote withdrawal / stale-mid wobble that the next aggressor trades straight back through — while Parent B showed that a name's active-bar price-impact regression R-squared measures whether that name's price moves are actually flow-driven and informative. The child uses B's ACTIVE-SAMPLE impact R-squared as the cross-sectional state variable that decides the SIGN of A's quiet-excursion displacement: where flow genuinely explains returns (top of the R-squared rank) quiet drift is a real reservation-price relocation and continues, where it does not the quiet drift is quote noise and snaps back, and A's Hawkes hazard of a trade within the 6-bar horizon scales the whole term because only names whose silence is about to break can resolve within the forecast window. Symmetrically, B's flow-explained transient displacement is shorted only when the Hawkes hazard is LOW (isolated trade, depth replenishes, impact decays) and held long when the hazard is high (order splitting still in progress) — a decay-versus-continuation interaction neither parent has, since A never decomposes its active drift and B has no arrival clock to time impact relaxation.
factors.name: Impact-informativeness gated quiet-efficiency reversal flip

factors.trading_idea: A quiet-bar (unpaid) mid displacement is only a *claim* on future return: it converts into realized return at the moment the next trade arrives, so its payoff timescale is set by the name's conditional trade-arrival hazard, not by how quiet it has been. The child therefore replaces the parent's activity-*level* gate with an arrival-*imminence* gate built from a Hawkes-style exponential-kernel intensity ratio (fast self-excited event rate vs the name's own slow baseline) combined with the causal silence age: when arrival is imminent the quiet drift completes inside ~1 minute, while when flow is extinguishing the recently-paid transient impact has no further pressure behind it and decays, so the traded leg is the one to fade. This should pull the parent's IC peak in from 12 bars to the 6-bar target and, because the gate uses only short-warm-up EWM intensities and soft precision shrinkage instead of hard count/quantile masks, it prices far more of the panel (parent coverage was 68%). The edge survives arbitrage because harvesting it means crossing the spread precisely in names that are momentarily the least liquid in the cross-section, and the imminence estimate decays within seconds — capacity, not information, is the binding constraint.
factors.name: Arrival-Imminence Hazard Gated Quiet vs Traded Drift Split

factors.trading_idea: The parent's realized IC says the opposite of its story, and both of its legs say the same thing once you unwind the algebra: the parent was long minus-idiosyncratic-return in quiet names and plus-idiosyncratic-return in busy names, and it lost money in both — i.e. an idiosyncratic mid move CONTINUES when it happens without trade flow and REVERTS when it happens on heavy flow. That is the permanent/transient impact decomposition, not beta catch-up: a mid revision in a bar with negligible volume is a market-maker re-anchoring the quote on information or inventory with no transient liquidity component to unwind, whereas a move accompanied by unusually heavy flow is mostly the temporary price concession extracted by a sliced metaorder, which decays as inventory is laid off. The child therefore measures the decomposition bar-by-bar rather than through an aggregate staleness state: each of the last 6 bars' vol-standardised idiosyncratic return is signed by that bar's own two-way-demeaned activity innovation (own 240-bar norm removed, then the market-wide/diurnal activity burst removed cross-sectionally), so 'quiet' means quiet for this name at this instant, not merely a slow market. The edge survives arbitrage because the continuation leg lives in names whose quote is thin and frozen (crossing the spread there costs more than the drift) and the reversion leg requires taking the other side of an active, possibly informed metaorder — the two frictions that create the wedge are the same ones that deter the marginal arbitrageur.
factors.name: Attention-Weighted Idiosyncratic Drift Permanence Split

factors.trading_idea: The single strongest 10-second regularity is the self-similarity of *trade direction*, not of price: a parent order sliced by an execution algo produces a long string of same-side child fills, so the sqrt-volume-weighted average of bar trade-direction (an impact-law weighting, since impact grows like sqrt of size) is strongly autocorrelated over the next minute. What matters is the part of that one-sided participation that the price has *not yet paid for*: I therefore cross-sectionally regress the participation share on the contemporaneous standardized displacement at each timestamp and keep the residual, so the signal is by construction orthogonal to momentum and to the transient-impact/bounce reversal that lives in the displacement itself; what survives is persistent one-sided pressure that met resilient depth. The residual is then scaled by a bounded 'liveness' term (trailing percentile of current volume intensity), because a metaorder whose arrival rate has already decayed has no remaining children to push the price. The edge persists because it is generated by exogenous, continuously regenerated execution needs, and harvesting it requires bearing 10-second inventory risk with bounded capacity rather than possessing information; front-running some children does not remove the rest.
factors.name: Sqrt-impact participation share, displacement-purged, liveness-scaled

factors.trading_idea: Llorente-Michaely-Saar-Wang show that the sign of the return x volume interaction in short-horizon return dynamics is set by adverse selection: when trading is hedging/liquidity driven, volume-accompanied price moves are compensated and revert, whereas when trading is information driven the same moves are informed and continue. The parent factor only re-expressed peer-relative price reversal in multiple space, so its edge grew with horizon; here the fundamentals are used where they cannot be differenced away — as a slow, point-in-time information-opacity score (intangible intensity, R&D intensity, small size) that flips the sign of the interaction, and as a valuation-tier refinement of the comparable-peer basket used to strip out common industry repricing. The traded object is the pure interaction term (beta-hedged peer-residual 30-second displacement x detrended volume x centred opacity), which is orthogonal by construction to unconditional reversal and to unconditional volume effects, so the effect accrues over the order-flow clustering horizon of roughly one minute rather than drifting out to many minutes. The edge persists because harvesting it requires joining stale quarterly opacity characteristics to 10-second flow and taking idiosyncratic residual risk, and because a pooled reversal or momentum arbitrageur trading the unconditional effect earns approximately zero on this spread.
factors.name: Opacity-split volume-conditioned peer-residual flip

factors.trading_idea: Names differ not in their *level* of price impact but in how much their impact co-moves with market-wide impact: a high 'liquidity beta' (Acharya-Pedersen commonality-in-liquidity) identifies stocks warehoused by the same balance-sheet-constrained intermediaries, so a displacement in such a name is far more likely to be inventory/liquidity-driven than information-driven and must be bought back within a minute, whereas a displacement in a name with little systematic-liquidity exposure is idiosyncratically funded and mostly informational, so it persists. The child therefore does not forecast reversal per se — the book already spans plain and flow-unbacked reversal (62% correlated with the parent) — it forecasts the *cross-sectional slope* of the 1-minute reversal coefficient in excess liquidity beta, entered as a pure interaction (displacement z-score times a cross-sectionally centred, illiquidity-level- and volatility-orthogonalised liquidity beta) so it is mechanically near-orthogonal to any level reversal factor. The edge survives arbitrage because liquidity beta is a covariance that needs several hundred bars of per-name block-Amihud history to estimate and must be residualised against the illiquidity level to be distinct, and because the payoff sits in the high-impact tail of the cross-section where it is capacity- and cost-limited. Falsifiable: if the 6-bar reversal coefficient of idiosyncratic displacement is flat in excess liquidity beta (or if high-liquidity-beta names instead continue), the interaction has zero or negative IC.
factors.name: Systematic-liquidity-beta gated idiosyncratic snapback

factors.trading_idea: The parent showed that slow-clientele names owe the market a beta-implied adjustment, but it measured the debt as a crude 6-bar wedge, so the debt kept being repaid long after the 6-bar forecast offset (IC peaked at 12 bars). Here I identify the actual distributed-lag transfer function from prewhitened market innovations to each name's return (Box-Jenkins style: strip the index's own AR(1) so univariate lag betas recover the impulse-response coefficients), and project only the portion of the response that the estimated kernel says will arrive in exactly the next 6 bars — the shifted-difference of the cumulative kernel, so past shocks whose repayment is already complete contribute nothing. The behavioural conditioning is new: income-mandate holders (high dividend yield / payout / shrinking share count) are reluctant sellers, so their names absorb down-market shocks with a longer lag than up-market shocks, making the owed delivery sign-asymmetric; I therefore weight downside and upside innovation debts by opposite functions of the clientele score. The edge persists because reconstructing a per-name lag kernel at 10-second resolution and holding through a slow-clientele repayment schedule is uneconomic for latency-arbitrage capital, while the mandate-constrained holders themselves never re-optimise at this frequency.
factors.name: Prewhitened market transfer-kernel 6-bar delivery, clientele sign-asymmetric

factors.trading_idea: Easley–Lopez de Prado–O'Hara argue that the *permanence* of an order-flow imbalance's price impact depends on whether the flow is toxic: when the fraction of volume that is one-sided (VPIN) is abnormally high, market makers face adverse-selection risk, back away, and the imbalance's impact is permanent, so the move continues; when VPIN is low the same imbalance is uninformed inventory demand that dealers absorb and then reprice back, so the move reverts. The child therefore replaces the parent's semivariance-asymmetry core (74% redundant with the book) with a *signed* bulk-volume-classified order-flow imbalance whose sign is flipped by the name's own-history and cross-sectional toxicity state, and modulates the continuation branch by fundamental opacity (intangibles intensity, R&D intensity), where private information is more likely to be the driver. It is falsifiable: if flow impact permanence is unrelated to bulk-classified toxicity the interaction term has zero IC and the sign-flip structure adds nothing over plain flow momentum. The edge persists because liquidity providers gate on their own queue, spread and depth in real time, not on a cross-sectionally normalised volume-clock toxicity state interacted with balance-sheet opacity, and harvesting it requires standing on the *opposite* side of low-toxicity uninformed flow, which is capacity-limited and unattractive to latency-driven arbitrageurs.
factors.name: VPIN toxicity-gated bulk-classified flow impact flip

factors.trading_idea: A peer-relative price displacement has two economically opposite futures: the part that is *owed beta* — a common shock the name has not yet transmitted through its own estimated impulse-response kernel — should be *delivered* (continuation), while the part orthogonal to that owed response is transient liquidity-demand impact that should *relax*. Parent A applied one self-measured relaxation slope to the whole band displacement, so its slope was contaminated by the un-delivered beta hiding inside the band (a name that owes catch-up looks 'displaced' but will not revert); Parent B accumulated the delivery deficit but imposed a single constant sign on it, ignoring how fast each name actually closes gaps at the 6-bar offset. The child Gram–Schmidt-separates the two state variables, then estimates a *separate* trailing horizon-matched slope for each channel (realized 6-bar peer-relative return regressed on the channel lagged exactly 6 bars, empirical-Bayes shrunk to the sector×size peer group), and gates the relaxation channels by flow cessation while gating the delivery channel by flow resumption — because transient impact only decays once pushing stops, whereas owed beta only gets transmitted when trading restarts. The interaction channel (band × tanh(deficit), purged of both parents) captures the sign-conditional reversion speed that neither parent can express: the same displacement mean-reverts when no beta is owed in its direction and trends when it is.
factors.name: Delivery-deficit-purged band relaxation with dual horizon-matched slopes

factors.trading_idea: Binned trade activity of a Hawkes process has an INAR(inf) representation whose summed autoregressive coefficients equal the branching ratio n — the share of volume endogenously triggered by earlier trades; I estimate n per name by a trailing conditional-least-squares beta of diurnally-purged relative volume on an exponential-kernel EWMA of its own past. The parent's realized IC (opposite to its declared sign) says the true direction is that *clustered* (high-n, near-critical) names continue while metronomic (low-n) names revert, and the Hawkes algebra explains why: expected offspring flow over the next H bars scales with n and pushes price further, whereas the transient inventory/bounce component of the current displacement decays at a rate essentially independent of n, so continuation only wins above a critical n which the cross-sectional median rank locates empirically. The carrier leg is therefore replaced by a horizon-matched (6-bar) BVC-signed participation imbalance — the actual flow whose offspring are pending — rather than a slow 30-bar price drift, so the signal lives at the fixed 6-bar offset. The edge survives arbitrage because harvesting it means either standing with a live, adversely-selected cascade for one minute (capacity-limited, toxic to slow capital) or providing liquidity against maker churn, both of which are inventory-risk-bearing services rather than free information.
factors.name: Hawkes branching-ratio gate on horizon-matched signed flow imbalance

factors.trading_idea: Whether a 10-second-scale price dislocation is transient liquidity pressure or genuine information depends on how hard the name's fundamental value is to pin down: in a Glosten–Milgrom / Kyle world the market maker's willingness to lean against a move is set by the ratio of pricing-error variance to information variance, and that ratio is a fundamental property (accrual quality, asset tangibility, earnings predictability, R&D-driven real-option content). So for fundamentally *transparent* names dealers confidently absorb a one-minute idiosyncratic push and it snaps back, while for *opaque* names liquidity providers step away and the same push keeps going. The child therefore trades the pure interaction — market-beta-purged 60-second idiosyncratic dislocation times a sector- and size-neutral point-in-time transparency composite — so its unconditional reversal/momentum loading (which the book already spans) is purged and only the conditional modulation remains. The edge persists because it requires joining point-in-time fundamental quality data with 10-second bars: HFT market makers do not condition on accrual quality or R&D intensity, fundamental managers cannot trade at a one-minute horizon, and the signal is a conditional modulation rather than a standalone directional bet, so it is not the target of existing arbitrage capital.
factors.name: Fundamental-transparency-gated one-minute idiosyncratic reversal

factors.trading_idea: Extreme-value theory says a stationary series' tail exceedances arrive in clusters whose mean size is 1/theta, where theta is the extremal index; the runs estimator of theta has an exact i.i.d. benchmark (1-p)^K, so the gap between the benchmark and the realised theta is a clean, scale-free measure of genuine tail self-clustering rather than of tail heaviness or autocorrelation. Mechanically, clustering of extremes at the 10-second scale is produced by market makers pulling and re-posting depth after being run over (risk-limit-driven withdrawal), so an exceedance drawn from a strongly clustered tail is likely to be followed by further same-signed exceedances (continuation), while an exceedance from a tail that is *less* clustered than the i.i.d. null is an isolated absorbed print and mean-reverts. The child therefore signs the recent exceedance impulse by the direction-specific clustering excess and damps it by the residual cluster capacity 1/theta minus the exceedances already spent, giving a nonlinear interaction no linear extreme-return or volatility factor spans. It survives arbitrage because theta is a noisy second-order tail statistic needing long windows, the signal is only live in the small subset of bars containing a tail move, and trading right after a tail print is expensive (wide spreads, adverse selection), which caps capacity rather than the edge.
factors.name: Extremal-index cluster-gated tail impulse

factors.trading_idea: A name's forward return is partly mechanically determined by market returns it has ALREADY seen, through its distributed-lag transmission kernel b_1..b_L; the parent showed this owed catch-up carries independent information but its per-lag free betas are dominated by estimation noise, so the sign of the forecast is unreliable name by name. The child (i) makes the kernel parsimonious by projecting lags 1..12 onto three exponential (Laguerre-type) basis functions with the contemporaneous market return partialled out Dimson-style — the basis regressors and their horizon-matched folds are common series, so only three loadings per name must be estimated — and (ii) replaces the parent's noisy Rice sign-flip gate with a *test-retest reliability* weight: the cosine agreement between the loading vector fitted on the most recent window and the one fitted on the previous, disjoint window, which is a direct estimate of the signal-to-noise ratio of the kernel (Spearman-Brown reliability). Loadings are shrunk toward a turnover-tier pooled kernel with weight 1-reliability, and the cross-sectional bet size is scaled by reliability, so the factor becomes an explicitly precision-weighted state variable rather than an unconditional forecast. Falsifiable: the IC of the owed catch-up should be monotonically increasing in the reliability score (and near zero in the bottom reliability tercile); if reliability carries no information the child collapses to the pooled-kernel forecast. The edge persists because arbitrageurs trade the common market signal, not per-name heterogeneity in quote-update latency and attention, and separating genuine slow transmitters from fitted noise requires per-name kernel estimation that is structurally unrewarding to crowd into.
factors.name: Laguerre Lag-Kernel Owed Catch-Up, Reliability-Weighted

factors.trading_idea: Parent B shows that only the front-loaded slice of a transient peer-relative displacement can be harvested inside a fixed 6-bar window, and that slice is governed by the excursion's AGE through the propagator G(t)=(1+t/t0)^-beta; Parent A shows that the repair only happens when the hedge legs (the peer basket) are actually tradable. The child unifies them by making the propagator's relaxation timescale t0 itself a function of leave-one-out peer-basket activity: when peers are live, hedging capital can be deployed and the excursion's clock runs fast (small t0, large within-window decay fraction), when peers are quiet the same standing gap relaxes on a stretched clock and delivers almost nothing in 60 seconds. The resulting theory-driven impulse x = -z * g(age; t0(peer-liveness)) is then amplitude- and sign-calibrated by Parent A's robust pooled sign-slope estimator fitted separately inside cells of (excursion-age tercile) x (peer liveness), shrunk to the all-observation pooled slope. The interaction is the edge: age alone mixes fast and stalled repairs, peer activity alone does not know how much decay is still owed, and only their product identifies displacements whose remaining relaxation is both large AND currently financeable at the fixed 6-bar offset.
factors.name: Hedge-liveness-scaled propagator clock with age x peer-activity sign-slope calibration

factors.trading_idea: The parent proved that splitting mid-price drift into a quote-side (near-zero-volume) channel and a taker-side (volume-paid, sqrt-law-deflated) channel carries information, but it imposed a FIXED sign on each leg (quiet = continuation, traded = reversal) and that sign is only correct for the slow, information-driven state — which is exactly why its IC was negative at 1-3 bars and only bloomed at 24 bars. The child instead estimates, per name and per channel, the actual lag-1 persistence of that channel's own increments (a trailing, empirical-Bayes-pooled AR(1) coefficient) and converts it into the horizon-matched geometric gain rho*(1-rho^6)/(1-rho), so the direction of the bet is learned from each name's own microstructure (quote flicker with rho<0 gets faded, maker walk-the-book with rho>0 gets extrapolated) rather than assumed. The current channel state is an exponentially decayed (2-bar halflife) increment average, so the forecast object itself lives and dies inside ~60 seconds, and the quote leg is scaled by the Poisson probability 1-exp(-6*arrival_rate) that a liquidity event arrives within the horizon to actually settle the unbacked displacement. The edge persists because the sign of the state is name- and time-varying (no static rule harvests it) and because collecting it means paying spread in precisely the thin, sparsely-traded names where quote-side displacement goes unbacked.
factors.name: Self-Calibrated Channel Persistence (Arrival-Gated, h=6)

factors.trading_idea: Parent A shows that a name's 6-bar dislocation of its industry-demeaned valuation multiple snaps back only when the peer basket is live enough to hedge; Parent B shows that at 10-second resolution displacement backed by idiosyncratic (single-name) aggressive flow is information and persists, while displacement pushed by basket/index-style flow or by no flow at all (quote shading) is transitory. The child attributes the *valuation* dislocation itself to those three sources: it decomposes each name's normalized signed sqrt-volume into a sector-basket component (trailing OLS on ex-self peer flow) and an idiosyncratic residual, converts both to Kyle-lambda displacements over exactly the 6-bar forecast window, and subtracts them from the industry-demeaned 6-bar multiple change to leave the unbacked 'quiet' part. It then follows the idiosyncratic-flow-backed part and fades the basket-flow part plus the quiet part, scaling the fade by leave-one-out peer activity (hedge legs must be tradable) and amplifying it when the transitory push moved the name further from its own trailing valuation anchor. The interaction carries edge neither parent has: Parent A fades every idiosyncratic dislocation regardless of whether informed single-name flow caused it (so it dilutes true information with noise), while Parent B fades basket pressure with no valuation anchor telling it where the snap-back target and the overshoot are — combining flow attribution with the peer-multiple anchor and hedge-leg liveness isolates exactly the dislocations that are both wrong and repairable within six bars.
factors.name: Basket-flow-attributed peer valuation dislocation, hedgeability gated

factors.trading_idea: A liquidity provider only absorbs a name's peer-idiosyncratic dislocation if the hedge basket can be traded, and the repair therefore completes on the *peer basket's event clock*, not the calendar clock. The parent measured the impulse over a fixed 6 calendar bars, which mismatches the repair window whenever peer trading intensity deviates from its norm — hence its edge leaked to 24 bars. The child makes the impulse event-clock-symmetric: the lookback over which the industry-hedged dislocation is measured is stretched or compressed so that the peer volume accumulated behind the impulse equals the peer volume the trailing rate predicts will arrive over the next 6 bars, so the measured dislocation is exactly the one that is repairable within the fixed forecast offset. Falsifiable: the trailing pooled sign-slope of the demeaned 6-bar forward return on this event-clock-matched impulse should be more negative (stronger reversal) than on any single calendar-matched lookback, and should be strongest in the fast-peer-clock cell; the edge survives arbitrage because it is a hedging-capacity constraint — in slow-clock states there is simply no peer liquidity to complete the round trip.
factors.name: Peer-event-clock-matched hedged dislocation (fixed 6-bar)

factors.trading_idea: A recent order-flow imbalance can mean two mechanically opposite things over the next minute, and the discriminator is the *persistence* of the flow itself, not the size of the price move. If a name's signed flow is auto-persistent over the last half hour, the flow is being generated by split child orders of a metaorder that is still working, so its impact is still accumulating and price continues over the next ~60s; if its signed flow is anti-persistent (alternating, two-sided liquidity provision / bid-ask bounce), the same imbalance is pricing error that is corrected within seconds. The parent split the *price displacement* into traded vs untraded parts and found its edge only matured at 12 bars, precisely because the metaorder-decay leg is slow; conditioning on flow predictability isolates the two *fast* legs (bounce correction and still-building child-order impact) that both resolve inside 6 bars. The edge survives arbitrage because unconditional flow/reversal factors average the two regimes toward zero (so linear books do not span the interaction), and harvesting it requires trading on the same side as flow that is currently moving the price, i.e. paying spread and impact rather than collecting it.
factors.name: Order-splitting persistence gates the sign of flow impact

factors.trading_idea: The parent estimated ONE lag-6 block autocorrelation per name and applied it to every displacement; that is a misspecification, because the 60-second block AR is strongly nonlinear in the size of the displacement. Small mid-price displacements are mostly transient quote flicker / inventory bounce and alternate sign (p_flip > 1/2, rho < 0), while large displacements are the visible footprint of a sliced metaorder that still has residual size to work and therefore continue (rho > 0). A single pooled sign-flip frequency is dominated by the numerous body observations, so the parent applied a body (reversal) coefficient to exactly the large-displacement observations that occupy the cross-sectional tails of the signal — which is precisely why its realized IC came out with the sign opposite to its declared one, and why |IC| grew out to 12 bars. The child fits a threshold AR at the block scale: two Rice-inverted concordance coefficients, one conditional on a large (>1 sd) prior block and one on a small prior block, and applies the state-MATCHED coefficient to the current displacement. The edge persists because reversion desks fit a single linear reversion gain per name (the conditional mean of a mixture); harvesting the nonlinearity needs per-name, per-state re-estimation, and the large-displacement state is exactly where impact cost and inventory risk deter capital.
factors.name: Magnitude-state threshold block autocorrelation forecast

factors.trading_idea: The parent's realized IC was negative because at 10-second mid-price resolution the Hasbrouck decomposition runs the other way than it assumed: mid displacement that trades stand behind is the information-bearing (permanent) part and continues, while displacement with no aggressive flow behind it is market-maker quote shading / fleeting-quote flicker with no consensus behind it and snaps back. The child keeps that decomposition but adds a genuinely new conditioning variable by splitting the *flow itself*, not the price: a trailing OLS of a name's normalized signed sqrt-volume on the contemporaneous peer (within-sector, ex-self) signed flow separates single-name informed liquidity demand from basket/index-style flow that hits many sector names at once. Idiosyncratic flow carries name-specific information so its Kyle-lambda-implied impact is permanent and continues; basket flow is uninformed about any single name, so the *differential* push it delivers to names with a high loading on it is pure transitory price pressure and reverts as makers reload. The edge survives arbitrage because it needs per-name impact calibration plus real-time flow-commonality attribution, and each trade earns only a fraction of the spread, so it is capacity-limited rather than competed away.
factors.name: Basket-flow vs idiosyncratic-flow impact permanence split

factors.trading_idea: Parent A measures a single flow-to-return response kernel per name, but that kernel is a blend of two physically opposite regimes: flow absorbed by an intermediary who is sitting on a paper profit unwinds quickly (continuation in the flow direction), while flow that ran the intermediary underwater is held and instead relaxes as the book refills (reversal) — exactly the state Parent B isolates but whose sign it wrongly imposed a priori (and got contradicted). The child splits the signed-flow stream into two disjoint channels by Parent B's maker mark-to-market state at the moment the flow was executed (weighted by inventory-ownership clarity |N/G|, so two-sided bars are muted), estimates a SEPARATE trailing empirical propagator increment R+(l), R-(l) for each channel with pooled cross-sectional shrinkage, and forms the exact horizon-matched conditional expectation sum_k [f+_{t-k}(S+(k+6)-S+(k)) + f-_{t-k}(S-(k+6)-S-(k))]. The interaction carries edge neither parent has: A's state-blind kernel averages the two opposite responses toward zero and loses amplitude, while B's state has no calibrated magnitude or sign at the fixed 6-bar offset — letting the data set an independent sign and decay speed per P&L state both restores amplitude and resolves B's sign contradiction endogenously instead of by hand.
factors.name: Maker-P&L-state-split empirical response kernel, 6-bar forecast

factors.trading_idea: The parent's edge was a first-moment repricing gap whose IC grew monotonically out to 24 bars — i.e. it was a slow object being forced through a 6-bar window. This child changes the mechanism to a genuinely fast one: the cross-sectional dispersion of idiosyncratic returns is a strongly mean-reverting state at the 10-second scale (statarb/market-maker inventory cycles expand it and depth replenishment compresses it), and each name has a persistent SIGNED loading on dispersion innovations (it is habitually the bought or the sold leg when the cross-section fans out). Forecasting the dispersion state's own reversion (kappa from its trailing AR(1)) and multiplying by that persistent loading gives a directional forecast of the *transient* part of the current idiosyncratic displacement; the loading is only trusted where the name actually delivered the attributed move (a shrunk projection of realised 6-bar displacement onto the attributed displacement), which separates dispersion-cycle transients from idiosyncratic news. The edge persists because harvesting it means adding cross-sectional risk exactly when dispersion (and hence statarb book risk) is elevated — it is compensated inventory-bearing, not an information advantage.
factors.name: Dispersion-cycle loading with delivered-fraction attribution

factors.trading_idea: Queue memory at a price level decays in *volume* time, not clock time: the resting inventory that once sat at a level is consumed or re-priced by executed flow, so the right state variable is how much volume has traded since the mid last stood where it stands now (first-return time of the path, marked by traded volume). When a lot of volume has passed since the last visit, the current level is stale — the price has been swept into territory whose book has already been eaten, the displacement is mostly *transient* impact, and it springs back as the book refills within tens of seconds; when almost no volume has traded since the last visit, queues are still live and the move is a metaorder grinding through supported levels, which self-excites and continues. The parent factor's realized (sign-contradicting) result is exactly this asymmetry read through a slow, clock-time occupancy density; the child replaces that density with the volume-clock recurrence age at the current level, which distinguishes a warm retest from an unsupported sweep instead of conflating them. The edge survives arbitrage because it requires a per-name nonparametric path functional (level-visitation in volume time) recomputed every bar and pays only a few ticks per episode, and because its cause — queue consumption and refill — is a structural property of limit-order books rather than a mispricing that can be traded away.
factors.name: Volume-clock level freshness: transient-impact split

factors.trading_idea: Uniformizing each bar increment against the name's own trailing 120-bar increment distribution caps the contribution of any single violent tick at 0.5, so the cumulative sum of centred ranks (a rank-CUSUM / Page change-point path) measures *how many* increments were unusually one-sided rather than how large the biggest one was — it is by construction a grind detector and needs no separate dispersion gate. The genuinely new conditioning variable is the CUSUM path's *retracement from its own within-window extreme*: a metaorder still being sliced leaves the rank-CUSUM sitting at its running extreme (pressure is live and keeps repricing), whereas a displacement whose transient impact is already relaxing leaves the CUSUM well below its extreme even though the net level is still positive. Interacting cross-sectionally centred rank-drift with the retracement state therefore separates live grinds (continuation) from spent grinds (relaxation), which the parent's Mood dispersion gate could not do — it only measured increment scale, not whether pressure was still arriving. The edge persists because identifying live slicing requires the *shape and recency* of the rank path, not the size of the move; the slicing agent cannot front-run its own child orders, and one-minute net-of-spread capacity is far too small for a large arbitrageur.
factors.name: Rank-CUSUM retracement liveness wedge

factors.trading_idea: At 10-second resolution the sign of return autocorrelation is not a constant of nature: it is the sum of two opposing microstructural forces whose relative strength is directly observable. When participation is high, price changes are produced by sliced parent orders whose unfinished remainder keeps pushing the same way (positive horizon-matched autocorrelation); when participation is low, mid-price changes are dominated by quote flicker and transient depth removal that snap back (negative autocorrelation). Rather than *assuming* a direction — the parent declared continuation and realised the opposite — the child *estimates* the 6-bar-ahead regression coefficient per name separately in the high- and low-participation states from trailing non-overlapping block pairs, shrinks it empirical-Bayes style toward the name's unconditional coefficient and then the cross-section, and applies the coefficient matching the current state to the current 6-bar displacement. The edge persists because the calibration is name- and state-specific and must be re-estimated continuously, its per-event gross size is of order the spread (unattractive to slower capital), and its drivers — tick-size-induced bounce versus order-splitting persistence — are structural features of execution, not mispricings that can be arbitraged away.
factors.name: Participation-state calibrated horizon-matched autocorrelation forecast

factors.trading_idea: At 10-second resolution a name's peer-relative displacement is either paid for by informed single-name liquidity demand (permanent, continues) or delivered by sector-wide basket pressure / quote shading (transitory, snaps back). The parent tried to anchor this with quarterly valuation multiples, which are step functions that carry no 6-bar information; the child replaces that stale anchor with a live microstructural conditioning variable — the sign coherence of leave-one-out peer flow. When peer flow signs are coherent the marginal push on a high-loading name is index-style inventory demand and the unexplained part of its sector-demeaned move mean-reverts hard; when peer flow is incoherent the same unexplained move is more likely genuine single-name information and should be faded far less. The edge survives arbitrage because harvesting it requires simultaneous cross-sectional flow attribution plus a *live* peer basket to hedge against (we scale the fade by leave-one-out peer activity), so it is capacity-constrained and only tradable in exactly the bars where the hedge legs exist.
factors.name: Basket-coherence-gated flow-attributed displacement

factors.trading_idea: The parent's insight — that the *temporal ordering* of volume relative to a price move separates permanent (information) from transitory (reactive-chasing) displacement — is right, but it was estimated as a slow 60-bar correlation asymmetry gating a 12-bar displacement, which is why its edge only matured at 12-24 bars. This child estimates the ordering **at the individual bar level**: for a move that happened 2-4 bars ago I compare the volume surprise that arrived *at or before* that bar (informed order arrival precedes the print) with the volume surprise that arrived in the *following* bars (latecomers reacting to an already-displaced, thin-book quote), both of which are fully observable now. Each recent bar's volatility-scaled market-neutral return is then multiplied by this per-bar, cross-sectionally demeaned confirmation score, so the factor is a pure interaction term: it rides displacements whose flow led the move and fades displacements the flow only chased, with zero unconditional momentum/reversal loading. The edge persists because market makers and standard reversal books size on contemporaneous imbalance, size and spread, not on whether the trade burst arrived one bar before or one bar after the quote displacement; harvesting it means warehousing inventory against reactive chasers for tens of seconds, which is capacity- rather than information-limited.
factors.name: Arrival-order confirmed displacement interaction

factors.trading_idea: Over the next 60 seconds a mid-price is moved by two things only: order flow that has *yet to arrive*, and the relaxation of impact already delivered. Metaorder durations are power-law distributed (Lillo–Mike–Farmer order splitting), so the hazard of a signed-flow burst ending *decreases* with its age: for a Pareto duration the mean residual life grows linearly in the current run age times (mean run length − 1), which I estimate per name from the trailing sign-flip rate of smoothed signed flow. The child therefore forecasts the signed relative volume expected to arrive in exactly the next 6 bars (direction x current intensity x expected bars of burst survival, capped at the horizon) and subtracts the horizon-matched portion of already-delivered impact scheduled to decay over those same 6 bars (propagator weights exp(-k/tau)-exp(-(k+6)/tau)), converting each flow block to price via the concave square-root impact law and the name's per-bar volatility. This fixes the parent's problem — its level-based permanent/transient split describes a slow relaxation whose IC peaked at 12 bars, whereas both legs here are *increments* defined over the fixed 6-bar offset — and the edge survives arbitrage because monetising it means trading alongside an in-progress metaorder whose own capacity limits the trade, and because the key state variable is the age-conditional residual life of the burst, not the level of imbalance that desks already trade.
factors.name: Lindy metaorder residual-life flow vs propagator relaxation

factors.trading_idea: Dealer/HFT absorption capacity is one-sided: hidden size resting on one side of the book, short-sale and inventory-skew constraints mean the quote relocation that walks back an aggressive push is systematically stronger after up-pushes than after down-pushes (or vice versa) for a given name. So the right conditioning object is not a single symmetric body-to-seam correlation but a pair of trailing OLS reciprocation gains beta+ / beta- (slope of the between-bar seam on the previous within-bar body, estimated separately on up-body and down-body observations), each shrunk by its own t-statistic so only statistically real absorption speaks. Given the side-matched gain, the expected total seam giveback owed to the freshly accumulated push is beta_side x push; subtracting the giveback already delivered by recent seams leaves an *owed* balance in return units, which is what should be earned over the next ~minute. The edge persists because collecting it requires posting passive size against possibly-informed aggressive flow for a fraction of the spread — an inventory-risk-bearing market-making service, not a liftable directional mispricing.
factors.name: Side-asymmetric seam reciprocation ledger (owed giveback)

factors.trading_idea: Parent A shows that drift printed in a name's (near-)zero-volume bars is quote-driven repricing that continues, while drift paid for with aggressive volume is transient impact that decays; parent B shows that a dislocation is only repaired when the *hedge legs are live*, i.e. when the peer basket is actively trading. The child splits the recent drift twice: first into peer-common (industry-median, unhedgeable) and peer-idiosyncratic (instantly hedgeable) components, then each of those into quiet-bar and traded-bar drift, and lets leave-one-out peer trading activity sign the loading on the idiosyncratic quiet leg only. The interaction is the edge: quiet *idiosyncratic* repricing persists precisely when peers are silent (no hedge capital available to arbitrage it) and is absorbed/reverted when peers are live, whereas quiet *common* repricing persists regardless because it cannot be hedged at all — neither parent separates hedgeability of the drift's source from the liquidity state that permits its repair. Decay-weighted 12-bar windows keep the impulse fresh so the response lands inside the fixed 6-bar offset rather than at 24 bars.
factors.name: Peer-liveness-gated decayed quiet/traded idio-vs-common drift split

factors.trading_idea: Diagnosis of the parent: because intraday variation of log(P/BVPS) is just log P plus a constant, its 'multiple-space dislocation' was really a slow peer-relative price deviation, and its convergence clock was a noisy per-name AR(1) — hence the payoff arrived after the fixed 6-bar offset. The child keeps the horizon-matching logic but changes both the object and the clock: the object is the part of a name's last-minute *idiosyncratic* displacement that exceeds what the square-root impact law implies for the volume actually traded (a quote/inventory-financed move rather than an informational one), and the clock is structural instead of statistical — repricing is realised per unit of trading, so the residual is weighted by the EWMA-forecast trading intensity for the next minute (volume clustering makes intensity forecastable) and tilted toward names whose float turnover implies depleted quotes are refilled inside 60 seconds. The edge persists because it is the compensation market makers extract for financing an unbacked mid drift: it is small per unit, capacity-limited by exactly the thinness that creates it, and requires a per-name impact elasticity plus an event-clock forecast joined to point-in-time float, which level-based relative-value books do not compute.
factors.name: Replenishment-clock impact-residual snapback

factors.trading_idea: The parent showed that a name's 30-second dislocation from a valuation-matched peer basket snaps back, but its residual still mixed the plain industry factor with the valuation-clientele factor, so much of its edge overlapped generic peer reversal already in the book. This child double-differences: it builds the industry equal-weight basket AND the multiple-space kernel basket, forms the *clientele leg* (kernel basket minus industry basket, i.e. the return of 'peers priced like me' hedged of 'peers in my industry'), and takes the name's residual after a trailing two-factor hedge on both legs — the genuinely idiosyncratic impulse. The amplitude is gated by the *incremental* explanatory power of the clientele leg (its partial R-squared given industry), because only where that leg actually loads does a relative-value desk carry the pair and police the spread, and it is damped by abnormal traded volume, which marks permanent information. Falsifiable: if snapback strength is flat in the clientele leg's partial R-squared, or if the double-hedged residual reverts no better than the single industry-hedged residual, the valuation-clientele mechanism is wrong and the parent's edge was generic peer reversal; the edge persists because joining point-in-time per-share fundamentals to a 10-second tape to define the clientele leg is operationally awkward for pure microstructure arbitrageurs and capacity is bounded by the size of each tight multiple neighbourhood.
factors.name: Clientele-leg partial-R2 double-hedged residual snapback

factors.trading_idea: Two classic spread estimators disagree in an informative way: Roll's signed lag-1 autocovariance measures reversal noise that is *pervasive* across the whole trailing window (a mid oscillating around a stable anchor, i.e. inventory/tick noise), whereas the Corwin-Schultz high-low estimator averages positive-part *local two-bar* estimates and is therefore driven by episodic range expansions. When the pervasive component dominates, a name's last-minute displacement is oscillation about an anchor and snaps back within the next minute; when the episodic component dominates, the displacement is directional demand impounding information and continues. Adverse selection (Glosten-Milgrom) makes the continuation side stronger for information-opaque firms (high intangible intensity, high R&D/revenue), so opacity tilts the same displacement toward continuation, and transparent asset-heavy firms toward reversal. The edge persists because market makers screen on quoted spread and volume level, not on the *ratio* of window-level to pair-level bounce, and they never condition inventory pricing on balance-sheet intangibility.
factors.name: Roll-vs-Corwin bounce pervasiveness with opacity flip

factors.trading_idea: Parent A shows a peer multiple-space gap reverts over ~6 bars, and faster when relative-value flow is arriving; Parent B's realized (sign-flipped) result shows that FRESH minus stale sqrt-volume-weighted directional pressure is transient overshoot that unwinds, not continuation. The child uses B's freshness wedge — peer-demeaned so it captures idiosyncratic, not sector-common, pressure — as a *provenance test* for A's dislocation: when the last few bars of one-sided unfinished flow point the same way as the valuation gap, the gap is metaorder-driven transient displacement and snaps back hardest, whereas when fresh flow opposes the gap the relative-value trade is already in progress and the residual reversion is small. The superadditive interaction (concordance amplification, discordance damping) plus a sqrt-law closure clock — peer-group and own sqrt(volume) arrival relative to its hourly norm, since absorption capacity scales like sqrt(Q) — carries information neither parent has: A cannot tell an information-driven re-rating from a flow-driven one, and B cannot tell whether the transient pressure has actually pushed the name away from a fundamental anchor worth reverting to.
factors.name: Flow-freshness-concordant peer multiple dislocation with sqrt-law closure clock

factors.trading_idea: Institutional metaorders must be sliced into many child orders, which imprints long memory on signed order flow (Lillo–Mike–Farmer); when a name's flow memory is currently *elevated relative to its own baseline and to peers*, a parent order is still being worked and its remaining slices keep pushing price over the next minute, whereas when memory is depressed the observed flow is market-maker round-tripping and the same displacement bounces. The parent factor assumed one pooled response kernel for all names, but the sign of the 6-bar response is not universal — it is governed by exactly this latent execution state, so pooling averaged a mixture of continuation and alternation regimes and delivered the wrong sign; the child makes the state observable instead of averaging over it. We measure it with an aggregated-variance scaling exponent of the cumulative signed participation-rate process on a short (active) and a long (baseline) trailing window, and use the elevation to gate a horizon-matched, square-root-law-weighted flow imbalance. The edge persists because harvesting it means taking the residual side of an unobserved metaorder — real inventory risk, per-event payoff a fraction of the spread — and the cause (impact-minimising order splitting) is an institutional constraint, not a mispricing that can be arbitraged away.
factors.name: Order-Splitting Memory Elevation Gating Flow Continuation

factors.trading_idea: A quote-driven (thin-volume) mid displacement is an unvalidated repricing: it only turns into realised return once a trade actually arrives to confirm the new quote, and transient impact from a traded bar only reverts once enough replenishing flow has cleared the dealer's inventory. The parent up-weighted the quiet leg purely on *relative* quietness, so it loaded most heavily on names whose arrival clock was too slow to complete anything inside 60 seconds — which is exactly why its IC peaked at 12 bars rather than the 6-bar target. The child replaces that relative gate with an absolute, horizon-matched completion probability: a one-step-ahead conditional arrival intensity (a fast/slow EWM blend of trade-driven-ness shrunk by the name's own lag-1 activity autocorrelation, i.e. a nonparametric Hawkes-clustering predictor) is turned into the expected number of arrivals in the next 6 bars, and the quiet leg is weighted by P(at least one arrival) = 1-exp(-N) while the traded leg is weighted by the slower relaxation fraction N/(N+3). The edge survives arbitrage because harvesting it means crossing the spread in names that are, at that instant, the least liquid in the cross-section, and the gate is only computable from the name's own arrival-clustering history; it is falsified if completion-probability weighting does not shift the IC peak toward 6 bars or adds nothing over the parent's relative-activity gate.
factors.name: Arrival-completion calibrated quiet-vs-traded drift split

factors.trading_idea: Parent A shows that a peer multiple-space dislocation only pays inside one minute when the name's own AR(1)/OU clock says the gap closes that fast; parent B's realized (sign-flipped) result shows that at 10-second resolution the part of a displacement with NO aggressive flow behind it is quote flicker that reverts, while the flow-explained part carries genuine information and should not be fought. The child therefore attributes each name's current peer-relative valuation dislocation to *peer-relative order flow* (own trailing Kyle lambda on group-demeaned signed sqrt-volume) and splits it into a flow-explained (informational, possibly still being worked) piece and a quiet piece, then weights each piece by its OWN model-implied fraction expected to revert over exactly the fixed 6-bar horizon; the flow-explained piece is additionally de-weighted when signed flow is sign-persistent (metaorder still executing). The interaction is the edge: A alone fades information-driven dislocations and gets run over (its IC only matures at 24 bars), B alone has no fundamental anchor so it cannot tell noise from a justified re-rating, and only the joint object — a fundamentally anchored gap that is (i) not flow-backed and (ii) has a measured sub-minute convergence clock — is a clean, horizon-matched relative-value snapback.
factors.name: Flow-attributed peer multiple dislocation with horizon-matched OU clock

factors.trading_idea: For a panel of 10-second relative returns, the horizon-matched lead-lag covariance M[i,j] = cov(future 6-bar relative return of i, trailing 6-bar relative move of j) decomposes into a symmetric part — which is exactly what common-factor persistence and *shared* non-synchronous-quote staleness generate, and which is therefore crowded and already spanned by conventional momentum/staleness-catch-up factors — and an antisymmetric part A = (M - M')/2, which can only be produced by genuinely *directional* information transmission (j leads i but not conversely). Whitening A by the Newey-West(1)-corrected precision of the state vector and forcing a zero diagonal yields a forecast of each name's next-6-bar relative return built exclusively from peers' current dislocations, with zero own-history content, so it cannot collapse into momentum/reversal and it is horizon-matched by construction (the regressand *is* the 6-bar-forward return, unlike the parent whose one-bar velocity coordinate pushed all its content to a 1-bar offset). The edge should persist because the antisymmetric component is an order of magnitude smaller than the symmetric one and needs a stable trailing cross-covariance matrix at the 10-second scale to extract, and because monetising it requires taking liquidity in precisely the laggard names whose order books are slow — a capacity constraint that compresses but does not remove the circulation.
factors.name: Antisymmetric circulation transmission (horizon-matched)

factors.trading_idea: Parent B shows that basket/program flow mechanically over-pushes names in proportion to cap-weight-per-unit-depth (inverse dollar turnover) in excess of their beta, and that this over-push relaxes; Parent A supplies the missing state variable — whether the pushed price is currently standing on a level the mid has repeatedly revisited (a well-supplied, two-sided queue) or has been shoved into a local-time vacuum. The key interaction: a weight-proportional push that ends in a recurrence vacuum is pure unabsorbed liquidity demand with no counterparty at the level, so it decays fastest (fade it hard); a push that ends on a high local-time-density level has actually been consuming a real resting queue, which is the footprint of persistent one-sided interest, so the displacement is validated rather than transient and should not be faded (Parent A's realized direction — continuation at high recurrence density — instead of its declared one). Neither parent has this edge alone: B fades every program push with the same intensity regardless of whether resting inventory exists to restore the price, and A's path statistic has no way to know which moves were mechanically caused by weight-proportional basket flow rather than by information.
factors.name: Local-time vacuum gated basket over-push relaxation

factors.trading_idea: Parent B shows that exponentially-accumulated signed flow, converted to return units by a trailing Kyle-lambda and damped by the volume that can clear it, is on average a transitory dealer-inventory overshoot that snaps back; Parent A shows (in its realized, sign-contradicted direction) that what happens next depends on whether the mid is sitting on a level the path has repeatedly revisited or in a recurrence vacuum. The child fuses them: I replace Parent A's pure local-time count with a volume-at-price *shelf occupancy* — the share of the last 90 bars' traded volume that printed within ~1.5 window-sigma of the current mid — and use its own trailing z-score to switch the sign of Parent B's flow-implied dislocation. On a heavy shelf the maker can offload inventory into standing two-sided size at almost no quote skew, so whatever displacement the flow produced is mostly *information* about a queue being consumed and it extends; in a volume vacuum the maker had to skew quotes hard to absorb the same flow, so the displacement is mostly *transitory* inventory overshoot and it reverts once counterparty volume arrives (hence Parent B's trade-clock saturation is retained as a magnitude damper). The interaction carries edge neither parent has alone: Parent B applies one unconditional reversion sign to permanent and transitory impact alike (which is why it is 68% redundant with the book), and Parent A gates a raw price move that contains no information about who pushed it or whether the pusher still holds inventory — only flow-implied displacement times local volume-at-price tells you whether an overshoot has a book to lean on.
factors.name: Shelf-occupancy gated inventory permanence split

factors.trading_idea: The parent folded a name's distributed-lag loadings only against the ALREADY-OBSERVED market path, implicitly assuming the index itself is a martingale over the next six bars; at 10-second frequency it is not — the cap-weighted mid-price index carries its own short-run autocorrelation, and the name transmits that future index path through its *contemporaneous and near* loadings (coefficient C_k = sum_{l=0}^{H-k} b_l on the market return arriving at t+k). Omitting that second term is exactly why the parent's signal is strongest at 1 bar and flips sign by 12-24 bars: the observed-path catch-up is partly cancelled by the index's own mean reversion, which arrives with a lag matched to the horizon. The child computes the complete horizon-matched expectation E[sum_{j=1..6} r_{t+j}] = (observed-path fold) + (cumulative-loading fold against a trailing-calibrated direct multi-step index forecast), and weights it by the *measured reliability* of each name's market kernel (trailing correlation between realised returns and the kernel's own fitted series) rather than by a fundamental clientele proxy. The edge persists because slow repricers with high market-R2 are where second-scale attention is scarcest, while the correction term is invisible to anyone treating the index as unpredictable; it is falsified if the future-path term carries no incremental information over the observed-path fold, or if kernel-R2 fails to discriminate reliable transmitters.
factors.name: Market-Reversion-Adjusted Lagged-Beta Kernel (H6)

factors.trading_idea: Resting liquidity is not uniform across price levels: at some price levels the book is thick (a lot of volume trades for very little price movement, i.e. low realised impact per unit of size) and at others it is thin. Because the coarse-grained price is a diffusion whose local diffusivity is set by that depth map, its occupation density concentrates where impact is low, so a price sitting on the steep (thin) side of its own recent impact profile is pulled back toward the nearby thick level over the next ~minute. I estimate this by a causal, kernel-weighted local-linear regression of the bar-level square-root-law impact coefficient log(|r|/sigma) - 0.5*log(relative volume) on the *price offset* of each past bar from the current price (with a time-trend control that removes the recency/volatility-clustering confound), and take minus the fitted price-slope: negative slope means cheap-impact (thick) levels lie above, so price should drift up. The conditioning variable is path efficiency — the profile is only a valid map of standing depth in balanced windows, so the signal is damped when the trailing window is strongly directional and the depth map is being dragged along. It survives arbitrage because the attractor is created by liquidity providers' own resting size: trading toward the thick level is precisely the immediacy-provision trade that gets compensated, and estimating a *derivative of impact with respect to price level* (rather than a level of volatility, volume or displacement) requires second-moment conditioning that ordinary reversal signals never perform.
factors.name: Local depth-profile impact-gradient pinning

factors.trading_idea: Transient (propagator) impact only relaxes AFTER the metaorder that caused it stops printing; while slices are still arriving, the long memory of order flow (Lillo–Mike–Farmer splitting, Hawkes self-excitation) keeps pushing the same way, so at a 60-second horizon the *sign* of the forward coefficient on trade-attributable displacement is set by the liveness of the flow, not by the displacement itself. That is why the parent — which pooled both regimes into one unconditional 'quiet minus traded' wedge — realised the opposite sign to its declaration: in this sample the still-live continuation regime dominated, so traded up-displacement continued instead of relaxing. The child therefore keeps the valuation-tier peer residualisation and the participation-share trade attribution, but replaces the static quiet/traded wedge with an interaction between outstanding trade-attributable impact and a per-name flow-liveness score (short-vs-long trade-intensity acceleration plus lag-1 persistence of the trade-attributable increments): long recent traded up-moves whose flow is still accelerating and persistent, short traded up-moves whose flow has just died (those are pure outstanding transient impact with its relaxation still ahead). The edge survives arbitrage because harvesting the dead-flow leg means supplying liquidity against a possibly-informed decaying metaorder, and because it requires simultaneously maintaining a point-in-time fundamental peer map (to strip common moves) and a real-time per-name flow-liveness estimate — desks specialise in one or the other. Falsified if the forward 6-bar coefficient on the outstanding traded-impact leg is statistically the same for high- and low-liveness names.
factors.name: Metaorder-liveness gated peer-residual impact

factors.trading_idea: The parent's insight — volume traded per unit of price displacement measures the hidden depth a move had to eat through — is sound, but it was carried by a one-bar wick-shape statistic that is almost pure noise at a 6-bar offset. The child keeps the depth state and attaches it to a far higher signal-to-noise carrier: the name's own idiosyncratic displacement over exactly the forecast window. Llorente-Michaely-Saar logic says the autocorrelation of short-horizon returns is not a constant but a function of who traded: a move made against unusually deep, mostly hidden liquidity (high volume per unit of traversed price) is a liquidity-demand move that the surviving queue pushes back, so it reverts; a move made through a vacuum (low volume per unit of traversal) is informative repricing and continues. The factor is therefore the pure interaction term — the depth state is de-meaned both in time (per name) and cross-sectionally (per bar, killing intraday volume seasonality and market-wide liquidity waves), so the unconditional short-term-reversal component is removed by construction and only the state-dependent flip in the sign of autocorrelation remains. It survives arbitrage because acting on it requires paying the spread against concealed size in exactly the states where a naive reversal trader is run over (vacuum states), so quote-only reversal books cannot span the sign flip. Falsified if forward returns load on recent displacement with a slope independent of the depth state, i.e. if the interaction is flat.
factors.name: Depth-state conditioned displacement reversal flip

factors.trading_idea: The parent modelled the mid as efficient fractional-Gaussian price + one-bar white noise, purged the Roll noise variance and then bet on the *persistent* remainder — but the correct decomposition at 10-second sampling is random-walk efficient price + an AR(1) transitory pricing error whose half-life is tens of seconds (dealer inventory, sliced-metaorder overhang, quote relocation that has not yet been reciprocated). Because the Roll correction only removes the k=1 white-noise part, the parent literally deleted the *predictable* transitory component and then forecast continuation of what was left, which is why its realized IC was negative: at a 60-second horizon the dominant conditional-mean term is the *release* of the AR(1) pricing error, not efficient-price persistence. The child fits the three-parameter model Var(P_{t+k}-P_t) = k·sigma_m^2 + 2·sigma_u^2(1-phi^k) to the robust (q=1, MAD-based) trailing variance signature at k = 1,2,3,6,12,24,48 by weighted least squares over a grid of phi, extracts the current pricing-error state as the deviation of the residual log-price from an EWMA anchor whose half-life is the *fitted* error half-life, shrinks it by the Wiener gain sigma_u^2/(sigma_u^2 + sigma_m^2·h_eff), and forecasts minus the fraction of that state expected to be released over the next 6 bars, with the release clock rescaled into trade time by expected forward volume (impact decays on trades, not on the wall clock). The edge survives arbitrage because reversion desks apply one common lookback and one common reversion coefficient to the whole book; the tradable residual is the cross-sectional dispersion of the *fitted transitory timescale and its release rate*, which needs continuous per-name, jump-robust re-estimation and pays only a few basis points per name.
factors.name: Variance-signature AR pricing-error release

factors.trading_idea: Transient price impact decays in volume time, not calendar time (Bouchaud propagator / MDH subordination), so the same peer-hedged displacement has a completely different 60-second future depending on how fast that name's volume clock is running. I therefore measure the displacement over a fixed *quantity of traded volume* (the volume the name normally prints in 6 bars) and read off the number of bars that quota took: a burst that consumed the quota in a couple of bars is inventory/liquidity-driven demand for immediacy whose impact will be worked off within the next minute (Campbell-Grossman-Wang), while a quiet grind that needed many bars to trade the same quota is quote/queue-depletion repricing that carries. The parent tried to learn this sign per name from a lagged cross-covariance and got pure estimation noise; the child replaces that with an observable, almost noiselessly measured *duration* statistic, and the timing claim is precisely matched to the fixed 6-bar offset (fast clocks complete their decay inside the window, slow clocks do not). It resists arbitrage because harvesting it means supplying liquidity into exactly the names that are printing bursts, so the payoff is compensation for inventory and adverse-selection risk rather than a free mispricing.
factors.name: Volume-clock displacement, clock-speed-gated reversal

factors.trading_idea: Parent A splits recent drift into quiet-bar (quote-repricing) and traded-bar (paid-impact) components but treats each component as a raw sum, so its edge is dominated by slowly-amortising dislocations and peaks far past the pinned 6-bar offset; Parent B has the machinery to identify how much of a name's variance is transitory and how fast it is repaid, but applies it to the blended return stream where permanent quiet repricing and temporary traded impact are mixed. The child runs Parent B's unobserved-components identification SEPARATELY on each of Parent A's two return channels: a ridge-free profile grid over AR(1) decay rates fits the trailing k-bar variance curve Var_k - k*Var_1 = b*g_k(rho) per channel, giving each channel its own transitory variance and decay, a one-dimensional Wiener projection of the matched exponential return filter onto the latent error, and a volume-clock repayment fraction 1-rho^(6*speed) so only the part collectable inside 60 seconds is forecast. The interaction is the edge: the quiet channel's own measured transitory share is exactly Parent A's falsification test computed per name and per moment — when the quiet channel shows no mean reversion its drift is genuine repricing and is extrapolated, when it shows fast reversion it is stale-mid bounce and is faded with a horizon-matched weight — while the traded channel contributes only its horizon-repayable temporary impact instead of its whole drift. Neither parent can do this: A cannot tell repricing from stale noise, and B cannot tell which of its two latent components was quote-driven versus volume-paid.
factors.name: Channel-wise UC error repayment vs quiet-bar permanence (h=6)

factors.trading_idea: A laggard's expected next-6-bar return has two mechanically distinct pieces: (i) the part of the market impulse response that is still *owed* — obtained by convolving the name's estimated distributed-lag loadings b_1..b_8 with the already-observed market path, using for each lag l exactly the slice of past market returns that lands inside bars t+1..t+6 (a 6-bar sum lagged by l-6 when l>6), so slow responders are included with correct timing instead of being truncated; and (ii) the mean-reverting continuation of the name's own idiosyncratic innovation, folded over the same 6 bars with its trailing AR(1) coefficient (E[sum e] = e_t·phi(1-phi^6)/(1-phi)), which is exactly the overshoot term whose omission made the parent's IC flip sign by 12 bars. Forecasting both pieces in return units and adding them puts the predictive mass inside the fixed 6-bar offset rather than at 1 bar. The edge survives arbitrage because it lives in names where repricing is demonstrably slow (frozen mids, thin recent volume) and where the response profile itself says the adjustment is genuinely delayed — precisely where second-scale attention and inventory capacity are scarcest. Falsified if the long-lag (l>6) shifted kernel and the AR overshoot term add nothing beyond the parent's l<=6 kernel, or if the delay-share / model-fit conditioners fail to discriminate.
factors.name: Delay-Profile Folded Catch-Up minus Estimated Overshoot

factors.trading_idea: In a 10-second panel, information arrives to the whole cross-section almost simultaneously, so what matters is not whether a name is quiet in absolute terms but whether it is quiet *relative to the market's own clock*. A name whose mid is being shaded by makers while its peers are actively trading is behind the clock: the common information is already in peer transaction prices and the name's silent repricing is a lagged, un-validated adjustment that completes within roughly the next minute (continuation). When the entire market is in a lull, the same silent mid moves have no common-information carrier — they are maker inventory shading and one-sided quote flicker, which re-centre and therefore revert on the same fast clock. The signal is one bar-level channel whose weight is (own silence deficit vs the market clock) minus (market-wide lull depth), accumulated with a 6-bar decay kernel so the object's timescale matches the fixed 6-bar forecast; the edge survives because harvesting it means quoting/crossing in names that are, by construction, momentarily illiquid. Falsified if relative silence adds nothing beyond absolute silence — then both weights carry the same sign of predictability and the wedge collapses to zero IC — or if the IC again rises monotonically with horizon rather than peaking near 6 bars.
factors.name: Relative-Silence Deficit vs Market-Lull Quote Repricing Wedge

factors.trading_idea: The map from a short-run price push to what happens over the next minute is not linear but sign-flipping: small pushes that arrive on light volume and on a zig-zag path are quote/inventory noise and get repaid, whereas equally-sized pushes that arrive on heavy, monotone volume are slices of a metaorder and keep going — a single linear distributed-lag kernel (the parent) averages these opposite responses toward zero and leaks its mass to longer horizons. This child therefore estimates, per name and causally, the *conditional expectation of the realised 6-bar-ahead move given the current microstructural state*, where the state is a 12-cell bin of (push magnitude) x (volume surprise) x (path efficiency), with the response sign-folded on the push direction (odd-symmetry) and empirical-Bayes shrunk toward the pooled cross-sectional cell mean. Because the response is measured at exactly the 6-bar offset, the estimate is horizon-matched by construction rather than by summing a kernel whose tail lies beyond the window. The edge survives arbitrage because harvesting it means posting passive size against possibly-informed aggressive flow for a fraction of a spread, and the *location of the crossover* (how much volume a push needs before it persists) is a slowly-drifting, name-specific liquidity parameter that has to be re-estimated continuously rather than read off a public formula.
factors.name: State-binned local-projection response surface (h=6)

factors.trading_idea: Parent A's inverted sign is the key: volume printing heavily while the mid stays glued to one grid level is evidence of a LARGE resting queue that absorbed that flow, so the eventual excursion away from the level is transient inventory pressure, not permanent repricing — it reverts, which is precisely Parent B's value-area snapback with depth measured in *traded volume at the level* rather than in time-occupancy. The child therefore replaces B's crude median anchor with A's absorbed-pin anchor, measures displacement from it as A's beta-residual (market-neutralised) move in units of the name's own grid quantum, and predicts reversion with amplitude scaled by the absorbed volume (queue-size proxy) and by B's occupancy-kurtosis / anchor-stationarity gates; B's fast heavy-volume probe-displacement channel is itself gated by the same absorbed-depth state. The interaction is edge neither parent has: A knows *where and how much* depth was traded but reads its sign backwards, while B knows the shape of the occupancy law but anchors on a rolling median that ignores whether any size ever changed hands there — only their product isolates displacements from a depth-backed level that a sharply peaked, non-migrating book can pull back within a minute.
factors.name: Absorbed-pin anchor: beta-residual displacement snapback under sharp occupancy

factors.trading_idea: The parent's polarity switch (absorbed probe -> continuation, converted sweep -> snapback) is real, but it weighted the past path with a fixed calendar window, so it measured a slowly-varying *stock* of pressure whose response leaks out over minutes — which is exactly why its IC kept rising to 24 bars while the run is scored at 6. Impact and unfilled-probe pressure relax in *trade time*, not clock time: the per-bar retention of outstanding pressure is a_i,t = exp(-speed/kappa) where speed is the name's current volume relative to its own ADV, so the pressure stock is S = sum_tau a^tau x_{t-tau} and the portion that will actually be released inside the next 6 bars is (1 - a^6)*S. Ranking names by that release-in-window quantity — rather than by the total stock — mechanically re-centres the same economics onto the fixed 6-bar offset and simultaneously replaces the parent's ad-hoc absorption gate with a derived one (fast clocks release almost everything, slow clocks release little). The edge should survive arbitrage because it needs three jointly measured ingredients (intrabar excursion asymmetry, volume-backed conversion ratio, and the name's own clock speed) to know which polarity applies; a trader taking either polarity unconditionally earns ~0, and the largest release is precisely in the fast-clock names where crossing cost is highest.
factors.name: In-window release fraction: trade-clock weighted probe/displacement switch

factors.trading_idea: The parent estimated the horizon-scale block autocorrelation from the sign-flip frequency of adjacent 6-bar displacements; but adjacent blocks share the price at their common endpoint, so under a Roll/MA(1) microstructure-noise model the estimator carries a purely mechanical negative offset that at 10-second sampling dwarfs the genuine autocovariances — which is exactly why a real slow continuation effect (its |IC| *grows* monotonically out to 12 bars, the fingerprint of minutes-long metaorder execution, not of bounce) came back with the sign reversed. The fix is mathematical, not a sign flip: the block cross-covariance Cov(Σ_{h=1..6}r_{t+h}, Σ_{i=0..5}r_{t-i}) = Σ_{l=1..11} c_l γ(l) receives the entire MA(1) noise contribution through γ(1) alone, so I rebuild the same coefficient from lags 2..11 only, estimating each lag from *sign* autocorrelations of bar returns (drift-corrected, then Gaussian-copula inverted with ρ = sin(π·E[s_t s_{t-l}]/2), the exact Rice relation) — an estimator that is volatility-blind, jump/fat-tail robust, and uses every bar pair instead of n/6 independent block pairs. Multiplying this bias-purged, horizon-matched coefficient by the current standardised 6-bar displacement therefore forecasts continuation in names whose direction process is genuinely persistent (sliced parent orders) and reversal in names where persistence is truly negative, with the spurious bounce offset removed. The edge survives arbitrage because standard practice estimates autocorrelation *including* lag 1 and hence reads spurious mean reversion off every name, and because harvesting the cross-sectional dispersion of per-name persistence requires continuous robust re-estimation whose per-name payoff is tiny and only diversifies in a broad book.
factors.name: Bounce-purged sign-ACF block kernel forecast

factors.trading_idea: Parent A shows that already-executed signed flow carries un-relaxed propagator impact, but the *speed* at which that impact relaxes is a book-state variable it never measures — which is why its IC keeps growing out to 24 bars instead of paying at 6. Parent B measures exactly that state: volume absorbed per grid step tells you whether the touch is a deep, continuously replenished queue (mid pinned while volume prints) or a thin, just-cleared book. When the queue is deep and refilling, the propagator's decay increment is discharged fast — the snapback happens inside the next few bars; when the queue has been depleted (low absorption per grid step, level broken, flow still self-exciting) the impact is not transient at all, the book keeps being walked and the same flow direction continues.
