The child therefore uses Parent B's resilience state, crossed with Parent A's Hawkes extinction gate, as a two-way switch: resilience x extinction weights the horizon-matched propagator relaxation leg (reversal), while depletion x live-intensity weights a fresh signed-flow continuation leg (momentum) — an interaction that both fixes A's horizon mismatch and explains why B's raw break-continuation had no unconditional sign.
factors.name: Queue-resilience switched propagator relaxation vs depletion continuation

factors.trading_idea: The parent's realized sign says the opposite of its propagator story, and the honest reading is a timescale error: metaorders and the order flow that generates impact are autocorrelated over minutes, so within the next 60 seconds a *volume-backed* mid displacement keeps going (permanent/informational component plus live slices), while a *quiet* mid displacement is quote flicker or inventory skew and mean-reverts — relaxation of transient impact only dominates far beyond 6 bars. The child therefore stops treating the traded leg as the thing that decays and instead uses it as the information carrier, but moves the claim cross-sectionally: within a valuation-comparable cell (sector x slow valuation tier from point-in-time per-share multiples), price discovery concentrates in the members that are actually printing volume, so the dollar-volume-weighted, leave-one-out accumulation of peers' *trade-attributable* residual displacement is a credible information impulse that a peer whose own tape has been silent has not yet incorporated. The signal is that undelivered gap (peer volume-confirmed impulse minus the name's own accumulated move), gated on the name's own recent participation being abnormally low, i.e. on its mid being quote-stale. The edge survives arbitrage because harvesting it requires joining point-in-time fundamentals (to build valuation-tier comparability cells, which no microstructure desk maintains) with bar-level trade attribution, and because taking the stale side means providing liquidity against possibly-informed peer flow, so the catch-up is compensation for adverse selection rather than a free lag.
factors.name: Volume-confirmed peer leader vs stale follower catch-up

factors.trading_idea: Mid displacement accumulated in bars with essentially no prints is an *untested* quote walk: a maker skewing their reservation price without any trade validating the new level. Whether that displacement continues or snaps back is not a matter of horizon but of state — while the marked trade-arrival intensity stays below its own slow baseline the walk is uncontested and keeps going, whereas once arrival intensity re-ignites (Hawkes-style clustering of arrivals) the untested displacement is immediately contested and the mid retraces toward the last traded level. The parent's near-zero 6-bar IC with +IC at 1 bar and strongly -IC at 24 bars is exactly the fingerprint of a continuation-to-reversal crossing near 6 bars; the child makes that crossing *observable ex ante* by multiplying the fresh silent displacement by a signed intensity gate (positive when arrivals are dormant, negative when they are igniting) and by the path-efficiency of the silent walk, so monotone reservation-price ramps are kept and mid flicker is discarded. Falsifiable: if untested quote drift is state-independent, the intensity-gated product has no 6-bar IC and the gate's sign interaction adds nothing over the ungated silent drift; the edge survives arbitrage because capturing it requires quoting in dormant, thin names where the round-trip spread is of the same order as the drift, and because it needs the joint state (silent vs traded displacement AND arrival intensity), not a single price feature.
factors.name: Untested quote displacement gated by trade-arrival re-ignition

factors.trading_idea: The parent showed that a peer-cell displacement does revert, but its IC grew monotonically with horizon because the cross-section is dominated by names whose relaxation time is far longer than 60 seconds: at 24 bars almost every gap has partly closed, at 6 bars only the fast-clock names deliver. The fix is to stop ranking the *size of the gap* and instead rank the *amount of gap expected to close inside the fixed 6-bar window*: for each name I estimate its own relaxation time T from a robust, non-Gaussian-friendly ratio estimator (mean|displacement| / mean|1-bar displacement increment|, which for an AR(1) equals 1/sqrt(2(1-rho)), hence T = 2r^2), shrink log T toward its peer-cell median, and weight the displacement by the exponential closure fraction phi = 1 - exp(-6/T). Peer cells are sector x within-sector size tercile because liquidity-provision capacity and the marginal-holder clientele — the things that set the relaxation clock — segment by size/liquidity, not by valuation, at the 10-second scale; the anchor is a robust 30-bar rolling median of the peer-relative log price so the displacement object itself lives on a horizon-compatible timescale. The edge persists because harvesting it means warehousing single-name inventory during the exact minute in which the state (still-pushing vs relaxing) and the clock T are only noisily identifiable, and the per-event profit is a tick or two relative to that adverse-selection risk.
factors.name: Relaxation-clock weighted size-cell displacement

factors.trading_idea: The parent showed that a precision-whitened (Sigma^-1) dislocation carries information but pools reverting and continuing populations; it tried to separate them with a single market-wide program-footprint gate applied identically to every name, which is the wrong granularity. The natural unit of a precision-metric dislocation is the *eigen-direction*: whitening amplifies motion along low-variance eigenportfolios, and whether such motion snaps back is a property of that eigenportfolio's own dynamics, not of the market as a whole — a spread direction whose trailing Lo-MacKinlay variance ratio is below 1 is an active OU-like relative-value spread (liquidity-provided, so displacement relaxes), while a direction with VR above 1 is structurally re-pricing (correlation regime drift / slow Epps-type information diffusion) and displacement continues. I therefore replace Sigma^-1 by the signed operator V diag(kappa_i / lambda_i) V', with kappa_i = 1 - VR_i estimated strictly on the pre-window eigenportfolio path, purge the dominant market mode spectrally, and tilt kappa_i by the loading-weighted *relative* dollar-activity of that direction in the current bar (traded displacement is transient impact, so it reverts harder; untraded quote drift persists). The edge should survive arbitrage because it requires a rolling covariance eigen-decomposition plus per-direction stationarity estimation at a 10-second clock — an estimation-cost barrier, and each direction's sign is state-dependent so the naive unconditional trade in it averages to zero.
factors.name: Eigen-direction variance-ratio gated precision dislocation

factors.trading_idea: Decompose each name's 10-second mid-price into a random-walk permanent component plus an AR(1) transitory (liquidity/pricing-error) component: this model forces the return autocovariance function to be exactly geometric in the lag, gamma_k = gamma_1 * phi^(k-1), so the SHAPE of the trailing ACF identifies the name's book-resilience speed phi = gamma_2/gamma_1 while its LEVEL (gamma_1/gamma_0) identifies how much of the variance is transitory. I therefore estimate phi and rho_1 per name on a trailing window, soft-threshold rho_1 by its sampling standard error (1/sqrt(n)) so names with no statistically detectable short-run autocovariance are forced to abstain, and build the model-implied best-linear forecast of exactly the next 6 bars: a geometric kernel over past vol-standardised idiosyncratic returns weighted by the name's own phi, with amplitude rho_1*(1-phi^6)/(1-phi) that measures precisely the share of the pricing error that unwinds inside the fixed 6-bar offset. Because the sign of gamma_1 is estimated rather than assumed, the same estimator fades displacements in slow-replenishing books and rides them where short-run autocovariance is positive, so it is not a reversal prior. The edge should survive arbitrage because standard reversal/market-making books use a fixed-bandwidth window and thus mis-weight names by resilience speed; phi is a second-order ACF-shape statistic that is noisy and needs long windows to estimate, and the residual payoff is compensation for supplying inventory, which is capacity-limited rather than information-limited.
factors.name: Geometric-ACF shape-matched resilience kernel forecast

factors.trading_idea: The parent's insight — mid drift accrued while nobody has traded is an *unconsummated* maker repricing that the next incoming order confirms — survives, but its two engineering choices were wrong. First, inter-trade silences are strongly clustered and *aging*: their duration distribution is Weibull with shape k<1 in quiet spells, so the probability the silence breaks inside the next 6 bars depends on how long it has already lasted; the parent's unconditional per-bar arrival rate over-weights long-stale names, which is exactly why its IC smeared out to 12-24 bars instead of concentrating at 6. Second, not all silent drift is a relocation: a monotone one-way walk of the mid with no trades is a genuine reservation-price shift (cancel-driven quote fade), whereas an oscillating path of equal net size is stale-mid flicker, so I weight the open displacement by its path-efficiency |net|/|path| since the last liquidity event. Finally, to prove the edge is not a repackaged short-horizon reversal/momentum term (the book already spans the parent, residual IC -0.004), the signal is cross-sectionally orthogonalised each bar against the name's own total 6-bar normalised return, so only the hazard x straightness interaction can pay. The edge persists because capturing it means crossing the spread in names that are momentarily untraded and whose silence is statistically about to break — a fill-timing risk that quote-passive arbitrageurs cannot warehouse.
factors.name: Weibull-hazard gated monotone quote relocation (return-orthogonal)

factors.trading_idea: A price move printed in low-volume bars is an unconfirmed quote hypothesis: makers shaded the mid for inventory or belief reasons that nobody has yet paid to test. The first genuine liquidity-consuming trade after that silent drift is the test — if the taker pushes price further in the same direction, an informed agent has validated the repricing and the move relays forward; if the arriving trade pushes back (the stale side is picked off and depth refills), the shading was noise and the mid retraces. The edge is therefore an *interaction* between an untraded displacement and the sign of the next real trade's price impact, weighted by how large that trade was relative to normal; because it is an event-timed, order-dependent conditional it averages to zero for any unconditional momentum or reversal filter, and harvesting it requires crossing the spread on thin names within a minute, which keeps it un-arbitraged.
factors.name: Trade-Test Confirmed Quiet Repricing Relay

factors.trading_idea: In 10-second bars the return splits into a trade leg (close−open, made while aggressive flow arrives) and a seam leg (open−previous close, pure quote relocation with no trades in between): the seam is the observable footprint of how much of a trade-driven push liquidity providers endorse versus walk back. The parent measured that walk-back only one bar ahead and then assumed how it aggregates; the child instead measures it **horizon-matched** — regressing the cumulative seam relocation over a 6-bar span on the 6-bar-lagged body push — and conditions the gain on a dealer-inventory state: cumulative same-signed normalised aggressive flow over the last 10 minutes. The falsifiable claims are (i) the interaction coefficient is negative on average, i.e. pushes are walked back harder when market makers are inventory-saturated and shade quotes to attract offsetting flow, while pushes arriving on a flat book are informational and are endorsed by further relocation, and (ii) the fitted gain × current push predicts the sign of the next 6 bars of return. The edge survives arbitrage because it is a per-name, state-dependent inventory-risk premium that must be re-estimated from each name's own seam history and is only harvestable inside a minute at sizes that market makers themselves cannot net out.
factors.name: Inventory-saturation-conditioned seam reciprocation gain

factors.trading_idea: Minute-scale reversal is payment for supplying liquidity, so it is only earned in names where liquidity actually shows up when price falls; the local demand slope is a persistent, name-specific state variable that price-only signals cannot see. I estimate it non-parametrically as a Wilcoxon/AUC statistic — the average trailing volume-rank on down bars minus that on up bars over the last 30 minutes — which measures whether participation is *attracted* to declines (resting value bids, dip absorption) or *evaporates* on declines (fragile book, one-sided withdrawal). The forecast is the interaction of that cross-sectionally centred elasticity with the name's current position in its trailing 5-minute range: dip-absorbing names bounce from range lows and give back range highs, fragile names keep travelling in the direction of the current excursion. The edge should persist because the gate is a *state* of the standing book that must be re-estimated per name from conditional volume statistics (not from returns), it flips sign across the cross-section so it is invisible to unconditional reversal traders, and crowding into liquidity provision changes the state itself rather than eliminating the compensation.
factors.name: Dip-participation elasticity gating range reversal

factors.trading_idea: Every firm has an intrinsic information-renewal time-scale set by its business physics: a capital-heavy, high-payout, slow-turnover firm with a long cash-conversion cycle simply cannot generate genuine cash-flow news inside a ten-second bar, whereas an asset-light, R&D-intensive, fast-turnover, fast-growing firm can (pipeline, pricing, demand chatter). Therefore the *same* standardised idiosyncratic displacement means different things in the two populations: in slow-clock names it is almost purely inventory / liquidity pressure and must relax, while in fast-clock names a larger share of it is permanent repricing and it drifts. The child trades only that interaction — the displacement is sector-demeaned and vol-standardised, the fundamental-clock weight is cross-sectionally zero-mean, and the product is then explicitly orthogonalised each bar against plain reversal and against size-scaled reversal, so what remains is the slow-vs-fast-clock *differential* in reversal strength, not the crowded reversal level itself. The edge persists because it requires joining point-in-time fundamental balance-sheet dynamics to second-scale microstructure: HFT desks condition reversal on spread/depth/flow state, fundamental desks never trade a one-minute horizon, and neither side prices the operating-cycle conditioning of microstructure noise.
factors.name: Fundamental clock-speed gated idiosyncratic displacement split

factors.trading_idea: The parent measured *how much* of a trade-backed push gets repaid, a channel the book already spans; the child instead asks *which names repay at all*. The permanent-vs-transient split of price impact is governed by the information content of the aggressive flow (Kyle/Glosten adverse selection): where fundamental value has no hard anchor — high intangibles and R&D intensity, rich price/book, no dividend or earnings yield, weak cash-to-accrual earnings quality — a larger share of volume-backed order flow is information-motivated, so the push is permanent and continues; where value is well anchored by cash flows and tangible book, aggressive flow is dominantly liquidity/rebalancing driven, market makers lean against it, and the push is transient and reverts. The child therefore trades the *interaction only*: a volume-backed, sector-idiosyncratic, volatility-scaled push stock multiplied by a cross-sectionally centred ambiguity score that has first been orthogonalised against trailing volatility and dollar-volume ranks, so the signal carries essentially zero loading on unconditional reversal or on the liquidity channel the existing book already prices. It survives arbitrage because harvesting it means bearing inventory risk against possibly-informed flow on one leg while accumulating with it on the other, at sub-minute horizons, conditioned on a slow fundamental characteristic that quarterly value/quality investors never express intraday; it is falsified if reversal strength is homogeneous across the cross-section, or if the opposite (retail-noise-trader) channel dominates, in which case the realized IC is zero or negative.
factors.name: Valuation-ambiguity gated impact permanence

factors.trading_idea: Parent A can tell, cross-sectionally each bar, WHICH part of a name's precision-whitened (Epps-corrected) dislocation is mechanically attributable to basket over-push — the weight-per-depth-minus-beta wedge times the program-weighted market displacement — and how trustworthy that attribution is (signed R-squared of the per-bar cross-sectional regression); but it has no way to know whether the attributed push actually left the name standing somewhere it does not belong. Parent B supplies exactly that per-name state: the local-time (recurrence) density of the whitened spread says whether the current spread level is the name's habitually revisited, accepted relative value or genuinely unvisited territory. The child routes A's decomposition through B's local time: the flow-attributed push is faded only where the spread now stands in fresh, never-occupied territory (a true transient liquidity-demand excursion that must relax inside six bars), while the un-attributed orthogonal remainder is ridden as continuation only where the spread sits on a habitual, accepted level (an agreed repricing / Epps catch-up, tilted toward measured laggards). The interaction is the edge: A pays for attributed pushes that landed on levels the name already accepts and therefore never revert, and B's freshness gate fires indiscriminately on informational excursions it cannot distinguish from mechanical ones — only bar-level attribution trust crossed with name-level local time assigns fade and continuation to the right names.
factors.name: Spread local-time routing of basket over-push attribution trust

factors.trading_idea: Every covariance-stationary return stream splits (Wold) into a linearly predictable part and an innovation, and the Levinson-Durbin recursion hands you both the optimal predictor and an exact, bounded meter of how much variance is predictable: R2 = 1 - prod(1 - k_i^2) over the reflection coefficients (PACF). At 10-second resolution this memory is mechanical, not informational - discrete quote revision cadence, child-order slicing and delayed inventory unwinds imprint structure at lags 2..6, while the lag-1 term is nothing but the universally harvested bounce. The child therefore (i) fits a shrunk AR(6) via Levinson-Durbin, (ii) iterates it forward exactly 6 steps and sums, so the predictor's kernel is matched by construction to the fixed evaluation offset, (iii) weights each name by the share of its predictable variance that lives at lags >= 2, and (iv) cross-sectionally orthogonalises the forecast against the 1-bar and 6-bar raw returns so nothing survives that a plain reversal already spans. It resists arbitrage because the residual predictable amplitude is a fraction of a tick, it appears intermittently (R2 spikes), and capturing it requires crossing the spread at second scale, whereas here it is expressed as a dollar-neutral cross-sectional tilt. Falsified if the lag>=2 predictability share fails to discriminate IC, or if the orthogonalised multi-step forecast carries no information beyond the lag-1 bounce.
factors.name: Wold predictability budget: higher-lag kernel forecast

factors.trading_idea: With unsigned trade volume, Easley-Lopez de Prado-O'Hara's bulk-volume classification (BVC) recovers a probabilistic buy/sell split from standardized bar returns, and the resulting imbalance concentration (a VPIN-style toxicity ratio) tells us whether a recent price displacement was paid for by one-sided informed flow or by transient two-sided inventory pressure. Whether the impact is permanent also depends on how much of the *float* changed hands: consuming a large share of outstanding equity in a minute is repositioning, consuming a trivial slice is market-maker inventory that gets recycled. The child therefore does not forecast reversal or continuation, it forecasts the *permanence* of the last 12 bars of displacement: displacement is faded when BVC imbalance is diffuse and float turnover low, and extrapolated when imbalance is concentrated and float turnover high. It survives arbitrage because the switch is a sign-flipping interaction that a linear reversal book cannot represent (the conditioning weight is cross-sectionally centred, so the factor has almost no unconditional loading on plain reversal), and because float-normalised turnover requires point-in-time share counts rather than the raw volume market makers already condition on.
factors.name: BVC toxicity / float-turnover permanence switch

factors.trading_idea: Observed 10-second mid returns are an efficient (permanent) increment plus a transient MA(1) inventory/quote-noise term; the transient piece is identified at LAG 1, not at the 6-bar horizon scale, and Rice's sign law inverts the lag-1 flip frequency into rho1 = cos(pi*p_flip), so the noise variance share is psi = -2*rho1 in [0,1] — a tick-size-free, jump-robust, signs-only estimator. The parent measured Rice concordance at the horizon scale, where the same transient term u_t - u_{t-k} contaminates both adjacent blocks and biases p_flip upward: its rho_hat came out negative almost everywhere, converting a genuinely continuing idiosyncratic minute-scale displacement into a reversal bet, which is exactly why its realized IC had the opposite sign. The child therefore (i) deflates the minute displacement by its estimated permanent share (1 - psi) and takes it as continuation — sliced metaorders and gradual information diffusion make permanent moves keep going for the next minute — and (ii) subtracts, with weight psi, the increments that were already reversed by the immediately following bar plus the still-unconfirmed freshest bar, because those carry the transient component that snaps back as inventory unwinds. Falsifiable: low-psi names' displacement must predict positively while high-psi names' must predict negatively, and the confirmed and reversed sub-sums must predict with opposite signs; if they predict with the same sign the decomposition is wrong. It persists because reversion desks apply one common reversion speed to the whole cross-section, whereas exploiting the dispersion of the per-name noise share requires continuous sign-only re-estimation plus per-name path bookkeeping whose per-name payoff is tiny and only diversifies in a broad book.
factors.name: Rice lag-1 noise share × confirmed-vs-reversed displacement split

factors.trading_idea: Parent B's quiet-bar (quote-repricing) vs active-bar (paid-impact) drift split is the strongest raw signal, but its stated falsification — that quiet drift is just a stale-mid gap — is exactly what Parent A's Rice/Gaussian sign-flip excess measures; Parent A, however, only *shrinks* a leg toward zero when it looks jump-carried, throwing away the information that a stale-mid gap should itself snap back. The child keeps Parent B's baseline polarity (+quiet, −active) but adds a *signed* tilt from the stream-specific Rice gap, cross-sectionally de-medianed so it is a relative grind/jump state: a quiet leg that is much jumpier than peers flips to a reversion leg (stale print correcting), while an active leg that is unusually grind-carried (a metaorder still being sliced) loses its fade and can continue. Because the run pins the forecast to 6 bars, each leg is additionally weighted by the freshness of its own stream — an exponential kernel in the number of bars since the last quiet (resp. active) bar — so drift whose informative increments are already stale is down-weighted rather than carried at full size into a 60-second forecast. The interaction is what neither parent has: A cannot exploit the stale-mid case (it only mutes it) and B cannot distinguish it at all, and measuring the flip polarity within volume-conditioned streams plus horizon-matched freshness converts a slow, horizon-increasing signal into one anchored at the fixed offset.
factors.name: Rice-Polarity Flip, Freshness-Weighted Quiet/Traded Split

factors.trading_idea: Parent A isolates the Hasbrouck pricing error — the part of a 6-bar mid displacement that a name's own R^2-shrunk Kyle lambda cannot attribute to aggressive signed flow — but it fades that residual blindly, using only the residual's own autocorrelation to decide how hard to bet. Parent B shows that whether a one-sided variance event is a mechanical inventory dislocation or genuine news is identified by variance-burst per unit of volume-burst (thin-book vacuum) once the slow Merton/Christie leverage component of semivariance asymmetry has been demeaned inside leverage x size buckets. The child conditions A's signed pricing error on B's state: it fades the unbacked displacement only when (i) the burst was produced in a liquidity vacuum and (ii) the structurally-purged downside/upside semivariance-asymmetry innovation is *concordant* with the sign of the pricing error — i.e. the one-sided variance came from the same side on which the mid drifted without trades. Neither parent has this edge alone: A cannot distinguish a quote-flicker pricing error from a real, thinly-traded revaluation, while B's asymmetry innovation is direction-ambiguous about where the mid now sits relative to the flow-justified efficient price; the concordance of a signed flow-unbacked displacement with a vacuum-born one-sided variance burst is precisely the fee-insensitive liquidator's footprint.
factors.name: Vacuum-concordant pricing-error snapback

factors.trading_idea: Under the unobserved-components model p = random walk + AR(1) pricing error, the k-bar variance curve satisfies Var_k - k*Var_1 = 2*sigma_s^2*[(1-rho^k) - k(1-rho)], so the whole trailing variance-ratio curve (k = 2..12) identifies the transitory-error variance and its decay rho by a one-parameter grid plus a closed-form linear coefficient — a far better conditioned estimator than the two single autocovariances the parent used, and one that mechanically enforces the model restriction theta >= rho (permanent variance cannot be negative). That restriction is the sign fix: the optimal one-step forecast collapses analytically to (rho - theta) * sum_j theta^j r_{t-j}, which is necessarily a *reversal* of the geometrically-weighted recent displacement, whereas the parent's unrestricted quadratic root selection could flip theta below phi and turn the same formula into continuation — exactly the sign contradiction the report reports. Horizon matching at the pinned 60-second offset comes from two places: the memory theta of the displacement estimator is each name's own error persistence (so slow names are measured over a minute, not a tick), and the gain (1-rho^6)/(1-rho) up-weights precisely the names whose inventory-driven dislocation is still un-repaid inside the next six bars, with the forecast divided by the realised 6-bar return sigma to express it as an expected z-score at that offset. The edge persists because collecting it means warehousing the inventory the liquidity provider is shedding, and because the ranking requires the noise-to-signal ratio and decay speed of each name's pricing error — objects a pooled tick-reversal factor cannot see.
factors.name: Variance-ratio-curve identified transitory-error reversal (6-bar gain)

factors.trading_idea: Parent A splits a recent displacement by *who paid for it* (flow-explained transient impact vs orthogonal quiet repricing); Parent B splits it by *how the path was built* (magnitude-concentrated jump vs sign-persistent grind, measured against Rice's exact Gaussian sign-flip null arccos(rho)/pi). Neither axis alone identifies the trade, because a flow-explained move built as a slow sliced grind is a parent order still working (it should be ridden, not faded), while an unpaid-for move built as one concentrated tick is a quote gapped into a vacuum (it should be faded, not ridden) — each parent averages over exactly the cell that reverses its own sign, which is why both parents show diluted, horizon-drifted IC. The child cross-classifies the two axes and only takes the two unambiguous cells: fade the flow-explained (transient) component when the Rice gap says the path was jump-concentrated, ride the flow-orthogonal (permanent) component when the Rice gap says the path was a sign-persistent grind, and zero-weight the two ambiguous cells. To pin the edge at the fixed 6-bar offset (rather than the parents' 12-bar peak) everything is re-timed to the horizon: a 6-bar displacement, a tau=3 impact kernel, a 60-bar Rice state window, and a centre-of-mass freshness weight that up-weights names whose energy arrived in the last one or two bars, so the relaxation or continuation still lies inside the next minute.
factors.name: Rice-gated propagator split: jump-paid impact vs grind-unpaid repricing

factors.trading_idea: The parent's realized sign says the *labels* were swapped, and the microstructure reading is Glosten-Milgrom/Hasbrouck rather than Obizhaeva-Wang: on a 10-second grid a mid displacement that arrives with no trade is not a belief revision at all (nothing informative was conditioned on) but a change in quote configuration — fleeting orders, one-sided depth withdrawal, queue-position games — and it is mechanically undone as the book refills, so unbacked displacement is the transient part; displacement that arrives with abnormal traded volume is informed flow being absorbed at worse prices, and because metaorders are split and order flow is self-exciting (Lillo-Mike-Farmer / Hawkes), the same-sign flow keeps arriving over the next few slices, so backed displacement continues. The second, new ingredient is the clock: how long an increment is still 'live' is governed by business time, not calendar time, so each past bar's contribution is faded by a kernel that decays in *traded volume since that bar* relative to the volume expected to trade over the 6-bar horizon (6 x trailing mean volume) — fast-trading names forget quickly in wall-clock, quiet names slowly, which aligns the memory with the fixed horizon instead of a one-size exponential. The edge persists because harvesting it means joining recent informed flow at 10s latency (paying adverse selection) and posting against quote flicker (being run over sometimes): the P&L is compensation for inventory/adverse-selection risk, and it is expressed cross-sectionally on peer-residual displacement with a business-time kernel, which is not how a single-name market-making book is run. Falsified if backed and unbacked peer-residual displacement carry the same forward coefficient at 6 bars, or if the volume-clock kernel does no better than a calendar exponential of equal mean age.
factors.name: Business-clock backed vs unbacked displacement wedge

factors.trading_idea: At the 10-second scale a stock's mid-price absorbs *basket-level* information (market-wide and same-sector liquidity demand, index/ETF and program flow) with a name-specific, heterogeneous delay: quote-update latency and the identity of the liquidity providers standing in each book determine how much of a basket move ending at t is still un-transferred versus already over-transferred (HFT over-hedging) in that name. Rather than assume the direction, the child *measures* the transfer per name with a trailing horizon-matched regression of the name's one-bar return on the strictly lagged 6-bar robust-market displacement and on the market-orthogonalised 6-bar displacement of its sector peers (own name excluded), and forms the fitted linear predictor of the next 6 bars. This deliberately abandons the parent's own-price displacement decomposition — the crowded, book-spanning family whose sign it got wrong — and takes its signed content only from *other* names' paths, so it is close to orthogonal to the archive's own-displacement reversal factors. The edge survives arbitrage because the transfer coefficients are dispersed, non-stationary and require a robust cross-sectional factor construction plus per-name trailing calibration, and because the residual predictable move is on the order of one minute and a fraction of the spread, so it is capacity- and cost-limited.
factors.name: Self-calibrated basket-transfer lag response forecast

factors.trading_idea: Parent A isolates a clean event — the break of a multi-bar mid pin, measured as beta-residual displacement in grid-quantum units and gated by the volume absorbed while the mid was stuck (real queue clearing vs quote flicker) — but it loaded that event with ONE sign for every name and realised the opposite of its claim, because pooled across a 10-second mid feed most pin breaks are quote relocations that the next aggressor trades straight back through. Parent B supplies the missing state variable: an active-bar-only, no-intercept price-impact regression whose uncentred R-squared says whether a given name's price motion is genuinely flow-driven, plus a Hawkes-style arrival hazard that says whether the name's trade clock is fast enough for anything to resolve inside six bars. The child therefore keeps A's event and magnitude machinery but lets B's impact R-squared rank set the SIGN (continuation only in the top of the informativeness cross-section, snapback below a 0.6 pivot that reflects the snapback-dominant pooled base rate both parents measured), while absorbed-volume intensity and the arrival hazard set only the MAGNITUDE. The interaction is the edge: neither parent can distinguish a queue-consuming, flow-driven level clearing (which continues) from an equally large but uninformative quote-withdrawal break (which reverts), so both averaged the two regimes into near-zero, wrong-signed IC; conditioning the sign on informativeness and the size on absorbed depth makes the same displacement monotone in forward return.
factors.name: Impact-informativeness gated pin-break sign flip

factors.trading_idea: At 10-second sampling a name's mid-quote impounds only part of the common (mean-field) return immediately — the Epps/Lo-MacKinlay non-synchronous-adjustment effect — and how much is deferred is a measurable, name-specific object: the profile of lagged market betas b_1..b_K estimated on a trailing hour. The honest predictor of the next few bars is therefore the convolution of *past* market returns with the part of each name's lag profile that has not yet fired, i.e. sum_s r_m(t-s) * sum_{k=s+1}^{s+6} b_k, which is exactly the systematic return still owed to the name and due to arrive inside a 6-bar window; the horizon is dictated by the mechanism rather than fitted, which is what the parent's 24-bar quarter-cycle timing lacked. The edge survives arbitrage because the deferred names are precisely those with stale quotes, thin depth and wide effective spreads, so the one-minute catch-up is compensation for immediacy provision and cannot be scaled by fast liquidity takers; we sharpen this by weighting the prediction toward names that are currently stale (recent zero mid-moves / no prints), since only an un-updated quote can still catch up. Falsified if the lag-profile tail carries no forward information at 6 bars, or if the effect is identical in fully-updated (non-stale) names.
factors.name: Epps deferred-beta lag-profile catch-up

factors.trading_idea: A metaorder's transient impact does not relax while the order is still working — it relaxes only once execution stops (Bouchaud propagator / Brokmann-Bacry), so the *timing* of the fade is a hazard problem, not a level problem. A name's own execution burst can be tracked causally with two exponentially-weighted trade-intensity estimates: while a program is working, the fast-decay intensity sits above the slow baseline; the instant executions cease, the fast/slow log-ratio collapses from its recent peak, which is a real-time detector of the *onset* of relaxation. The child therefore fades only the displacement that is outstanding relative to the square-root impact law at names whose burst has just terminated (scaled by weight-per-depth susceptibility, i.e. inverse-turnover rank minus beta rank), and applies a small same-sign continuation tilt to names still visibly executing. This fixes the parent's failure mode — the parent faded a market-scalar predicted push at all times, so it averaged over the whole life of the push and its IC only accumulated by 24 bars, whereas the post-termination snapback is concentrated in the first minute, i.e. exactly the fixed 6-bar offset. The edge survives arbitrage because monetising it requires joint, 10-second-resolution monitoring of per-name intensity dynamics and outstanding displacement, and the counterparty is providing immediacy and bearing inventory for a small per-event payment.
factors.name: Metaorder termination hazard gated over-push snapback

factors.trading_idea: A peer-relative price displacement only has to be paid back if nobody traded to create it: the part of a characteristic-hedged (size / book-to-price / gross-margin neutral) return path that accumulates in bars whose volume is far below the name's own recent norm is quote- and inventory-driven repricing, carrying no information, whereas displacement accumulated in high-volume bars is order-flow-borne information and should persist. The speed at which the untraded part is repaid is name-specific: estimating the AR(1) persistence phi of the hedged price residual around its own recent level and weighting the dislocation by the implied 6-bar payback fraction (1 - phi^6) converts a slow reversion story into an expected-return-at-one-minute signal, which is exactly what the parent lacked (its IC grew monotonically out to 24 bars). The edge survives arbitrage because separating quiet-bar from traded-bar displacement requires joint bar-level volume and point-in-time fundamental hedging, and because the residual is by construction un-hedgeable factor-free inventory noise whose repayment is capacity-limited. Falsifiable: if quiet-bar and active-bar displacements have the same forward sign, or if the fast-relaxation (high 1 - phi^6) subset does not carry the 6-bar IC, the mechanism is wrong.
factors.name: Untraded Residual Displacement with Relaxation-Speed Split

factors.trading_idea: A slow-clientele name's response to a market innovation is spread over a lag kernel b_0..b_L rather than delivered at once, so the economically correct signal at a *fixed* 6-bar offset is not the open beta wedge but the part of the kernel that has not yet fired and will fire inside the next 6 bars: owed_t = sum_k ( sum_{j=1..6} b_{k+j} ) * innovation_{t-k}. This projection is horizon-matched by construction — it automatically discards response already delivered and response that will only arrive after bar 6 — which is exactly what the parent's crude 'beta x 6-bar market move minus own move' wedge could not do (its power leaked out to 12 bars). Per-name lag kernels are hopelessly noisy at 10-second sampling, so each name's kernel is shrunk toward the pooled kernel of its payout-clientele bucket (dividend yield, payout ratio, FCF yield, negative share growth), turning the clientele variable from a return multiplier into an estimation prior: income-clientele names genuinely share a slower, longer-tailed impulse response. The edge survives arbitrage because it requires simultaneously estimating a name-specific multi-lag response kernel and trading it in low-attention, mandate-constrained names whose marginal holders do not re-optimise intraday; it is falsified if only the k=0 (contemporaneous-shock) term carries IC, or if clientele-pooled kernels do not beat per-name kernels.
factors.name: Clientele-Pooled Distributed-Lag Owed-Return Projection

factors.trading_idea: At 10-second resolution a large share of traded volume is mechanical, market-wide flow (index/ETF arbitrage, basket and program trades) that consumes depth in every name simultaneously without carrying any name-specific information, while the remainder is name-specific flow that is far more likely to be informed and order-split. The classic volume-conditioned reversal treats all volume alike; the child instead decomposes each name's contemporaneous log-volume surprise into a common part (its trailing beta on the panel-wide volume surprise) and an idiosyncratic residual, and uses the *sign of that split* to flip the direction in which the last 30 seconds of idiosyncratic price move is traded: fade moves whose volume was common-driven (pure depth consumption, mean-reverting transient impact), follow moves whose volume was name-specific (informed, mechanically persistent metaorder flow). Falsifiable: reversal IC at 6 bars should be strongly positive in the common-volume half of the panel and zero-or-negative (continuation) in the name-volume half; if reversal strength is invariant to the split, the mechanism is dead. The edge survives arbitrage because separating program flow from informed flow in real time requires a cross-sectional volume-commonality estimate that a single-name liquidity provider does not compute, and the payoff is a fraction of the spread earned as compensation for supplying depth against recurring mechanical flow.
factors.name: Program-flow vs name-flow volume split: conditional reversal flip

factors.trading_idea: In the directional-change (intrinsic-time) representation of a price path, each run is described by two quantities that obey their own scaling laws: the overshoot beyond the confirmation threshold and the duration of that overshoot. Self-calibrating both to the name's own realised event-time distributions gives a dimensionless velocity residual: a run whose normalised price extension has outrun its normalised duration is a fast, mechanically-driven displacement (inventory unloading into thin depth) and snaps back, whereas a run whose duration exceeds its extension is a slow grind — informed accumulation being absorbed — and continues. The edge persists because the state variable lives in event time and is path-dependent: it requires maintaining per-name overshoot and duration distributions across directional-change events, whereas HFT liquidity provision and standard alpha libraries gate on calendar-time volatility, spread and depth, so nobody is bidding away the specific fast-vs-slow asymmetry. It is falsifiable: if extension speed carries no information, the signed residual (ps − ts) should be uncorrelated with 6-bar forward returns, and the reversal branch should not separate from the grind branch.
factors.name: Intrinsic-time overshoot velocity anomaly

factors.trading_idea: The parent showed that unexplained downside-heavy realised variance is compensated, but it measured a slow 120-bar *level*, so its information arrived as a persistent state and only paid off over many minutes. Two mechanism changes make the same idea act at a ~1-minute offset: (i) strip the structurally justified asymmetry at the *return* level by beta-residualising each name against the equal-weight market (Christie/Merton leverage asymmetry is generated by market co-movement, so removing systematic returns removes the mechanical part), then measure a short 12-bar idiosyncratic semivariance asymmetry as an *innovation* against the name's own 120-bar norm and neutralise it inside leverage buckets; (ii) time the snapback with an exhaustion gate — one-sided pressure only reverts once the marginal seller stops, i.e. when 3-bar downside quadratic variation and 3-bar volume have both decayed relative to their 12-bar norms. The edge persists because it requires jointly conditioning transient one-sided idiosyncratic flow on balance-sheet leverage buckets and on the decay of that same flow; naive reversal screens buy while pressure is still building and lose, so the exhaustion-conditioned side of the trade stays under-supplied.
factors.name: Idiosyncratic semivariance asymmetry with flow-exhaustion gate

factors.trading_idea: The parent's insight — mid moves printed in (near-)zero-volume bars are quote-side repricing while moves printed in high-volume bars contain transient impact — is right, but it expressed the idea as a flat 30-bar cumulative drift, which is a slow *state* variable and therefore forecasts best 2-4 minutes out rather than at the fixed 60-second offset. The child keeps the channel split and replaces the accumulation with the correct horizon-matched object: a Bouchaud-style distributed-lag propagator, estimated separately for the quiet and traded channels by cross-sectionally pooled trailing covariances of lagged channel increments with the contemporaneous idiosyncratic return, then aggregated into exactly the weights that project the *next 6 bars* of return (W_k = sum of beta_{k+1..k+6}). Because the estimated kernels decay in lag, the resulting signal is driven by the last handful of bars rather than a five-minute average, so its information is consumed on the 60-second scale the run scores; the sign of each channel is no longer assumed but read off the data, making the mechanism directly falsifiable (it predicts a positive quiet kernel and a negative traded kernel). The edge survives arbitrage because harvesting it requires real-time per-name volume-regime classification plus a pooled response estimate, and the per-event payoff is a fraction of the spread on exactly the thin names where quote shading happens — the market makers who could compete it away are the agents whose inventory constraints create it.
factors.name: Pooled Two-Channel Lag-Kernel Horizon-6 Projection

factors.trading_idea: Parent B shows that drift printed in near-zero-volume bars (quote repricing) continues while drift paid for with volume (temporary impact) reverts; parent A shows that a given amount of drift can be built either by many small same-signed increments (grind / order-splitting) or by a few concentrated increments among alternating noise (jump), measurable as the gap between the observed adjacent-sign-flip frequency and the Rice/Gaussian null arccos(rho1)/pi. The child estimates that Rice gap *separately inside each volume regime*, using a masked lag-1 covariance/flip estimator over consecutive quiet-quiet and consecutive active-active bar pairs. Economically the two regimes reverse the meaning of the gap: a quiet drift that is grind-like is a market maker deliberately walking the mid on inventory/adverse-selection beliefs (real, unpaid-for repricing that persists), whereas a quiet drift that is jump-like is a stale-quote flicker that snaps back; conversely an active drift that is jump-like is concentrated impact into thin depth (fast decay), while an active drift that is grind-like is a still-working parent order whose reversal should be muted. Gating the quiet leg by grind-ness and the traded leg by jump-ness therefore amplifies exactly the sub-populations where each parent's directional claim is true and neutralises the ones where it is false — an interaction neither the unconditional sign-null nor the unconditional volume split can express.
factors.name: Rice-Gap-Gated Quiet vs Traded Drift Split

factors.trading_idea: Parent B builds the right state variable — the conversion ratio c that says whether the last 100 seconds of probing was absorbed by the book (unfilled pressure, continuation toward the probed side) or fully converted into a swept net displacement (transient impact, snapback) — but it assumes a single fixed response speed, which is why its |IC| only peaks at 24 bars. Parent A owns the timing machinery: a per-name impulse response estimated on the name's own re-quote clock (bounce-purged innovations on bars whose mid actually moved), horizon-matched folding of already-observed pressure into the owed component of the next H bars, and a Poisson deliverable share 1-exp(-lambda*H) that says how much of that owed move can physically be paid inside a fixed 6-bar window. The child feeds B's switched pressure P = (1-c)*probe-excursion-asymmetry - c*residual-displacement into A's self-calibrated distributed-lag kernel and delivery clock, so the polarity comes from B's absorption state while the sign and magnitude of the lag loadings are learned per name — which also removes A's contradicted-sign risk, since nothing is assumed about direction. The interaction is the edge: it up-weights exactly the names whose measured lag-1..6 response mass is large AND whose re-quote hazard delivers inside the fixed offset, and it down-weights the slow deliverers that pushed B's information out to 24 bars and made A's stale-name amplification backfire.
factors.name: Conversion-switched pressure with update-clock delivery share

factors.trading_idea: The parent's noise-purged Hurst exponent was, mechanically, a disguised noise-share statistic: e1 = v1 - 2*Var(eps) deflates the fine-scale variance most for names whose 6-bar move is mostly transitory, which inflates e2/e1 and hence H-hat — so its 'persistent' names were exactly the high-pricing-error names, and they reverted, which is why the realized IC was negative. This child writes the underlying unobserved-components model down properly: for efficient price plus stationary pricing error u with AR(1) relaxation a, the variance signature satisfies Var(D_k)/k = sigma^2 + W(1-a^k)/k with W = 2Var(u), so a trailing multi-scale fit over k = 1,2,3,6,12,24 identifies sigma^2, W and a per name, and the optimal h-bar forecast is exactly -(1-a^h)^2 (W/2)/(h*sigma^2 + W(1-a^h)) times the current h-bar idiosyncratic displacement. The new, falsifiable ingredient is the relaxation SPEED: two names with identical transitory share should be faded very differently — a fast-relaxing pricing error (a^6 small) is fully harvestable in six bars, a slow-relaxing one (a^6 near 1) is not and must be left alone. The edge survives arbitrage because reversion books apply one common horizon-scale reversion gain to the whole cross-section; separating the size of the pricing error from its decay rate needs per-name, per-bar re-fitting of a three-parameter signature curve and pays only a few basis points per name, so it is capacity-limited rather than crowded.
factors.name: Relaxation-speed-gated transitory-share snapback

factors.trading_idea: Both parents measured fresh one-sided repricing and both realized a *negative* IC at six bars, so at 10-second resolution recent volume-weighted displacement is predominantly over-push that relaxes as depth refills — the correct base direction is to fade it. Parent B's realized sign says the relaxation is state-dependent: when the volume mass of the last few minutes is unusually *even* (a scheduler/passive-provision fingerprint, entropy innovation > 0) the mid has been walked away from a still-intact book and snaps back hardest, whereas when volume has just *concentrated* into one or two bars (entropy innovation < 0) the move is an aggressive sweep that self-excites and keeps going. The child therefore takes Parent A's cleanest pressure estimator — the sqrt(volume)-weighted fresh-minus-stale directional-consistency wedge, bounded, robust to giant prints, propagator-purged — and multiplies its fade by a baseline-plus-tilt weight (0.5 + tanh-standardised evenness innovation), so it fades hard in scheduled/even regimes, fades weakly in neutral ones, and flips to continuation only in genuine burst regimes. The interaction carries edge neither parent has alone: Parent A cannot tell relaxation from ignition and so averages the two opposite conditional responses, while Parent B's path-efficiency leg ignores executed size and therefore cannot distinguish a quote-drift grind from a volume-backed push.
factors.name: Evenness-innovation-tilted sqrt-flow freshness fade

factors.trading_idea: The parent's H-bar response deficit is an accounting identity with two physically different halves: debt accrued on bars where the mid was FROZEN while the market moved (owed = beta*market summed over frozen bars, a mechanical repricing obligation that is paid only when the name re-quotes) minus the idiosyncratic move actually REALISED on bars where the mid did move (live order-flow / bounce component). The parent lumped them with one sign, so the realised-move half entered with the wrong sign and, worse, the whole thing collapsed to a cross-sectional beta-timing bet (rank of beta times a common market impulse), which loses whenever the 60-second index move gives back — exactly the contradicted sign the report found. The child separates the two halves, gives the frozen-debt half its mechanical + sign scaled by the Poisson chance of a re-quote arriving inside 6 bars, gives the active half a sign taken from the name's OWN horizon-matched (lag-6 on 6-bar sums) idiosyncratic autocorrelation, and then residualises the composite cross-sectionally against beta so no market-direction timing survives. It stays uncrowded because it needs bar-level attribution of the residual to frozen vs moving-mid bars plus a per-name horizon-matched persistence estimate at 10-second granularity, and the payoff sits in thin, mid-attention names that fast market makers will not warehouse for a minute.
factors.name: Frozen-bar beta debt vs active-bar idio drift (beta-neutral split)

factors.trading_idea: Model the observed mid as efficient price plus an AR(1) pricing error (Roll with persistent, not iid, transient impact): return autocovariances then identify the error's decay rate directly, rho = gamma_2/gamma_1, and the share of return variance that is reversible, phi = -gamma_1/gamma_0. The parent faded raw within-bar displacement and therefore mixed names whose impact unwinds in seconds with names whose half-life is minutes, which is exactly why its IC peaked at 12 bars rather than the mandated 6; here each name's displacement is scaled by the *fraction of its own pricing error that mathematically reverts inside the fixed 6-bar window*, (1 - rho^6), and shrunk by the transient variance share phi, so the signal is horizon-matched by construction rather than by window tuning. A bar-level Kaufman efficiency ratio further attenuates the fade when the last three bars traced a straight, accepted path (informed permanent flow) versus a choppy absorbed one. The edge persists because it is payment for immediacy and inventory risk in exactly the names whose depth refills slowly enough to be measurable but fast enough to pay inside a minute — arbitraging it requires warehousing that inventory, so the compensation cannot be competed to zero, only re-priced.
factors.name: Roll-OU horizon-matched transient payback

factors.trading_idea: Parent B knows *where* absorbing depth should be (the modal band of a leptokurtic trailing occupancy distribution) but not whether the depth at the current tail is actually being replenished; Parent A observes exactly that replenishment — same-side failed excursions repeating across consecutive bars, the signature of iceberg/refresh liquidity — but its sign is ambiguous because it averages rejections that occur deep in a thin tail together with ordinary queue churn inside the value area. The child conditions B's snapback on A's state: the mean-reversion hinge on the robust displacement from the trailing median is scaled up when the *excursion side* is the side being repeatedly rejected (hidden supply above a high tail, hidden bid below a low tail) and shrunk toward zero when the rejections are happening on the mode-facing side, which means the tail is being accepted and the displacement is genuine repricing. A freshness weight (few recent bars spent outside the dead zone) selects excursions that are just beginning to be absorbed, pulling the reversion into the fixed 6-bar window instead of the 12–24-bar window where B's ungated version peaks. The interaction carries edge neither parent has alone: A supplies the direction-resolving evidence that turns B's undifferentiated snapback into a defended-tail trade, and B supplies the occupancy state that disambiguates A's sign.
factors.name: Value-area tail excursion gated by persistent wick defense

factors.trading_idea: The parent measured *time-series* clustering of a name's own tail (extremal index) and found the declared continuation sign reversed; the missing variable is not how a name's extremes cluster in time but whether they cluster with the *market's* extremes. Multivariate EVT gives a clean estimator: chi = P(market exceeds | name exceeds), with an exact independence null equal to the market's own exceedance rate, so chi - p isolates genuine systematic tail dependence from tail heaviness. Mechanistically, an extreme 10-second print in a name whose tail is tail-*independent* of the market is a liquidity event (depth swept, market maker inventory shock) whose impact is transient and unwinds as depth replenishes within the next minute, whereas an extreme print in a name whose tail is tail-*dependent* on the market is common-information repricing that peers share and that diffuses gradually, so it continues over the next minute. The edge persists because chi is a second-order conditional-tail probability requiring hundreds of bars of exceedances to estimate (it is not spanned by beta or by any linear reversal factor), the signal is live only in the sparse subset of bars containing a fresh exceedance, and trading immediately after a tail print is expensive (wide spread, adverse selection), which caps capacity rather than the alpha.
factors.name: Co-exceedance tail-dependence split of extreme impulses

factors.trading_idea: We cannot see the book, but we can invert the square-root impact law to *estimate* it: on bars where the mid rose, log|return| - 0.5*log(volume) is a per-bar estimate of the inverse depth of the ask side; on bars where it fell, of the inverse depth of the bid side. The geometric-mean difference between the two sides over a trailing 15 minutes is therefore an implied depth tilt: cheap-to-move-up / expensive-to-move-down means resting supply is thin and resting demand is deep, and the queue-imbalance result (Cont-Kukanov-Stoikov; Gould-Bonart) says the thin side depletes first, so the mid drifts up over the next several bars. Unlike the parent - which summed signed pressure and was 71% redundant with the book and sign-contradicted - this is a *ratio of conditional elasticities* (a liquidity-supply property, not a displacement), and we explicitly project out the cross-sectional fast (6-bar) and slow (90-bar) trailing returns so the factor cannot be a repackaged momentum/reversal signal. The edge survives arbitrage because harvesting a sub-tick depth-implied drift requires either winning a queue position on the thin side or paying the spread, both of which cost more than the drift, while the tilt itself is created by inventory-motivated participants who refuse to pay for immediacy.
factors.name: Side-asymmetric log impact elasticity (implied depth tilt)

factors.trading_idea: Treat the last quarter-hour of a name's price formation as a symbol stream (down/flat/up ticks) and its volume as a second binary stream (busy/quiet), and measure the algorithmic complexity of both with block statistics: the number of distinct 3-letter words observed and the Herfindahl concentration of word frequencies. When one mechanical agent dominates price formation — a scheduled slicing algorithm, a pegged quoting engine, an inventory-unwinding maker — the joint symbol stream loses complexity (few words, highly concentrated), because a deterministic policy is generating the ticks; the next minute is then a continuation of that policy, so the current displacement extrapolates. When complexity is high relative to the name's own recent norm, many competing agents plus quote flicker are producing the path, price is close to efficient and the displacement is dominated by transient noise that mean-reverts over the next minute. The signal is therefore the *interaction* between a self-normalised complexity-collapse score (centred, so it carries no net momentum or reversal exposure) and the market-demeaned 6-bar displacement; it is falsified if the continuation coefficient on displacement is invariant to word complexity. It survives arbitrage because the gate is a discrete combinatorial statistic of the sign/activity path — invisible to linear, moment-based factor models and to volatility conditioning — and because the payoff accrues over ~60 seconds where capacity is bounded by impact.
factors.name: Word-complexity collapse gate on horizon-matched displacement

factors.trading_idea: Basket/program executions displace a name in proportion to its capitalisation weight per unit depth (inverse dollar turnover) rather than its beta, and that displacement is most visible in the historically low-variance (basket-spread) eigen-directions of the trailing return covariance — i.e. in the precision metric. At a one-minute (6-bar) offset the accumulated dislocation is the wrong state variable: what matters is the *freshest* whitened increment that is attributable to weight-per-depth mechanics, combined with whether the pressing program is still arriving. I therefore build a Hawkes-style flow-concordance intensity (per-bar cross-sectional correlation between dollar-volume share deviations and cap-weight deviations, scaled by activity) and take its fast-minus-slow exponential slope as a liveness derivative: when arrival intensity is still accelerating the attributed push keeps moving the name (continuation), when it decays the mechanical liquidity demand stops and the low-variance dislocation snaps back within seconds. Falsifiable: if the interaction between intensity slope and the attributed whitened innovation carries no information, IC at 6 bars is zero; the edge survives arbitrage because harvesting it means supplying depth to the very programs creating the push — compensated but strictly capacity-limited by that depth.
factors.name: Over-push innovation gated by program-intensity slope

factors.trading_idea: Parent A shows that drift printed in (near-)zero-volume bars is quote-driven repricing that continues while drift paid for with volume is transient impact that decays, but it treats every quiet move alike; Parent B shows that a name's peer-demeaned valuation multiple is the anchor telling you where price *should* sit and that flow which hits a whole sector basket is uninformed pressure whereas single-name residual flow is information. The child decomposes BOTH of Parent A's legs against the sector: it splits the freshness-weighted quiet drift and traded drift into a beta-loaded peer-basket component and an ex-self residual, then follows quiet residual repricing with a weight that is amplified when the quiet move is walking the name *toward* its industry-median log-multiple anchor and damped when the same silent move is pushing an already-expensive name further above peers, while the fade is concentrated on the basket-attributed traded component and scaled by leave-one-out peer activity so the hedge leg is actually executable. The interaction carries edge neither parent has: Parent A cannot tell an informative silent quote update from stale-mid overextension (the anchor does that), and Parent B has no way to know whether the dislocation was printed silently or paid for with volume (the quiet/traded split does that), so intersecting them isolates silent repricing that is both unpaid-for and anchor-justified from traded basket pressure that is both paid-for and hedgeable.
factors.name: Anchor-aligned quiet repricing vs basket-attributed traded impact

factors.trading_idea: The parent's evaluation reversed its declared sign, and the honest reading is Hasbrouck's, not Bouchaud's: a trade is the only *costly* signal in the book (it pays the spread), so displacement that arrives with executions is consensus revision and is permanent, whereas mid displacement that arrives with no prints is mostly mechanical — one-sided depth withdrawal, fleeting/flickering quotes and queue-position games move the midpoint without anyone paying for it, and it snaps back as the book replenishes within seconds. The child therefore stops decaying impact on the wall clock and instead builds an *execution-validation clock*: a causal scalar Kalman/variable-gain filter on each name's valuation-tier peer-residual log price whose gain is the bar's participation share g = v/(v + trailing mean v), so the filtered state is the trade-validated efficient price and the residual gap is exactly the drift that no execution has ratified; the gap is cleared by prints, not by time, so it can persist for many bars in a quiet name and vanish instantly on a burst. Prediction: this unvalidated gap mean-reverts over the next ~60 seconds (factor = minus the gap), while the trade-validated component is already absorbed in the state and carries no reversion. The edge survives arbitrage because harvesting it means posting liquidity into a walking quote and bearing adverse selection when the walk *is* news, and because it needs a point-in-time fundamental peer map (to strip tier-common repricing) joined to bar-level trade attribution — HFT liquidity desks never build the fundamental map and relative-value desks cannot act inside a minute.
factors.name: Execution-validation clock: unvalidated peer drift snapback

factors.trading_idea: A schedule-constrained execution algorithm imprints a low-entropy, repeating (direction x size) pattern on consecutive bars, while genuinely competitive two-sided flow produces a near-maximal-entropy symbol stream; so the *predictability* of a name's own recent symbol sequence tells you whether its current directional pressure is the visible tail of an unfinished metaorder or just noise. I therefore estimate per name, on trailing data only, (a) the Miller-Madow-corrected mutual information between consecutive symbols drawn from {up,down} x {heavy,light volume} — a model-free, nonlinear measure of how much of the next bar is already determined — and (b) a volume-weighted sign-propagation coefficient lambda that says whether heavy-volume moves are followed by same-signed moves (unfinished informed metaorder) or opposite-signed moves (transient impact of a liquidity-demanding print). The signal follows the last minute's volume-weighted directional pressure when lambda > 0 and fades it when lambda < 0, with conviction scaled by the symbolic mutual information; it is falsified if pressure alone carries the IC, if the mutual-information weighting adds nothing, or if lambda < 0 names show the same pressure-return sign as lambda > 0 names. The edge should persist because the pattern is manufactured by participation-constrained execution algos that cannot conceal their regularity, while liquidity providers gate on spread and depth and the standard alpha stack measures order flow with linear autocorrelations and imbalance sums — a plug-in, bias-corrected mutual information on a discretised joint (sign, size) alphabet is nonlinear and non-differentiable, hence invisible to those estimators.
factors.name: Symbolic mutual-information gated flow propagation

factors.trading_idea: Parent A shows that a FRESH escape of the mid out of a tight, heavily-traded occupation band walks into thin resting depth and extends; Parent B shows that when the cross-sectional dollar-volume allocation vector tilts toward the capitalisation-weight vector (a basket/program footprint), a name's systematic displacement contains a mechanical over-push of size (inverse-turnover elasticity minus beta) that must relax. The child uses Parent B's machinery as the *causal attribution* for Parent A's event: it asks whether the coil escape was pushed out of the band by weight-proportional program flow (escape direction concordant with wedge_i x program-weighted market move over the same 6 bars) or happened despite/against it. Program-attributed escapes are liquidity demand into a book that will be refilled, so their polarity flips to snapback; unattributed (idiosyncratic) escapes keep the continuation polarity, and the multiplier is strongest when the escape ran *counter* to the mechanical push. The interaction carries edge neither parent has: Parent A cannot tell an information ignition from a basket-induced dislodgement (so it averages continuation and reversal together), and Parent B has no event clock — it fades program pushes uniformly instead of only where the push actually dislodged price out of its depth pocket; each bar the child is cross-sectionally orthogonalised against BOTH the plain 6-bar move and the raw parent-B fade signal, so any surviving IC comes from the interaction alone.
factors.name: Coil-escape polarity split by index-weight elasticity attribution

factors.trading_idea: Parent A shows that drift printed in near-zero-volume bars is quote repricing that continues while drift paid for with volume is transient impact that reverts, but it measures a slow 30-bar stock and only pays off far past the fixed 6-bar offset; Parent B shows that whether a fast displacement is news or mechanical dislocation is decided by variance-burst per unit of participation (the thin-book vacuum state), after the slow Merton/Christie structural level is removed. The child makes the quiet/traded split (i) fresh — a 12-bar innovation of each component relative to the name's own 90-bar per-bar drift rate, so the event is dated to the last two minutes and must resolve inside the next minute — and (ii) state-switched: the loading on the quiet leg is continuation when variance is accompanied by commensurate volume (deliberate, informed quote shading) and flips to reversal in a liquidity vacuum (stale-mid / mechanical mid-drift on no depth), while the traded leg's reversal coefficient is switched *on* only in the vacuum state and switched off when the burst was volume-confirmed news. The interaction carries edge neither parent has: A cannot tell informed quote repricing from stale-mid noise (its own stated falsification condition) and therefore bleeds its signal out to 24 bars, while B has no notion of *who* produced the displacement (quote-only vs traded), so it applies one reversal prior to both; conditioning A's decomposition on B's vacuum state supplies exactly the missing discriminator and re-dates the signal to the 6-bar horizon.
factors.name: Vacuum-state-switched quiet/traded drift innovation

factors.trading_idea: Parent B splits recent drift into quiet-bar (untraded quote repricing, persists) and traded-bar (paid impact, decays) components but treats every name in isolation; Parent A shows that at 10-second resolution the *source* of a push — sector-basket flow versus single-name idiosyncratic flow — determines its permanence, and that fades only pay when the peer hedge legs are live. The child crosses those two axes: the quiet-bar drift is followed only to the extent the ex-self industry peer basket is quietly repricing the same way (shared untraded information = genuine repricing; a lone name's mid drifting with no volume and no peer move is stale-quote flicker), while the traded-bar drift is decomposed via trailing OLS of the name's signed sqrt-volume on ex-self peer flow into a basket-flow-implied Kyle displacement (faded hardest, scaled by peer activity so the hedge is executable and amplified when the push stretched the name further from its industry-demeaned book-multiple anchor) and an idiosyncratic-flow-implied displacement (followed, because informed single-name demand continues). The interaction is the edge: Parent B fades all traded drift including informed idiosyncratic prints and follows all quiet drift including pure stale-mid noise, whereas Parent A has no untraded/traded partition at all — attributing each partition separately tells you which sixty-second displacements are wrong *and* repairable inside the six-bar horizon.
factors.name: Peer-confirmed quiet repricing vs basket-attributed traded impact

factors.trading_idea: The parent's realized sign says the propagator reading was wrong at a 60-second horizon: trade-backed peer-residual displacement CONTINUES and quiet (no-print) mid displacement REVERTS. The mechanism is that equity trade flow is strongly self-exciting — metaorders are sliced, so a burst bar predicts more same-direction flow, and the impact of the *not-yet-executed* remainder accrues well before the propagator's relaxation dominates; conversely, a mid that moves with no print is mostly top-of-book quote flicker/bounce in the (bid+ask)/2 definition, which is transitory noise. The child therefore keeps the valuation-tier peer residualisation (which the report credited with genuine, book-orthogonal information) but replaces the fixed propagator sign with two new per-name conditioners that make the coefficient on each leg cross-sectionally state-dependent: the trailing lag-1 autocorrelation of the name's own volume (flow self-excitation / branching strength — high means the metaorder is still slicing so the traded push extends, low means a one-off block whose impact relaxes) and the trailing negative autocorrelation of its own peer-residual return (mid-noise share — high means quiet moves are flicker and snap back, low means quiet moves are genuine belief revision and persist). The edge survives arbitrage because harvesting it requires simultaneously estimating per-name flow self-excitation, per-name quote-noise share, and a point-in-time fundamental peer map inside one minute — microstructure desks never build the fundamental comparability groups and relative-value desks cannot act at this clock speed. Falsified if the forward 6-bar coefficient on the trade-attributable leg does not increase with own-volume autocorrelation, or if the quiet leg's reversal coefficient is unrelated to the name's return-autocorrelation noise share.
factors.name: Flow self-excitation gated traded push vs quiet flicker split

factors.trading_idea: A pro-rata basket/index program trades roughly $F·w_i in each name, so its instantaneous price impact is proportional to a *known* mechanical loading m_i ≈ w_i/(dollar ADV_i) rather than to beta; a robust per-bar cross-sectional regression of vol-standardised returns on the demeaned loading therefore identifies the scalar basket-flow coordinate f_t and, orthogonally, a genuinely idiosyncratic residual e_t,i. The parent proved that assuming a sign for each piece is the failure mode (its whitened residual continued while the basket piece relaxed, so the pooled object cancelled at 6 bars and only survived at 24). This child never assumes a sign: it estimates, from strictly past *non-overlapping* 6-bar blocks, the response coefficients θ_t = slope of the next 6-bar flow coordinate on the previous one and φ_t = pooled slope for the idiosyncratic residual, and emits the horizon-matched forecast θ_t·f_sum_t·m_i + φ_t·S_t,i — i.e. the signal is literally an estimate of the 6-bar-ahead return, making the fixed offset a design constraint rather than an accident. The edge should persist because harvesting it means supplying liquidity into program flow at the moment of maximum impact, a compensated inventory risk whose payoff is bounded by spread and only identifiable if you jointly model cap weight, dollar liquidity and volatility at a 10-second clock.
factors.name: Impact-loading identified basket flow, block-calibrated 6-bar response

factors.trading_idea: A basket/tilt programme moves a whole characteristic direction, and that displacement splits into a permanent part paid for with real trade volume and a transient part that is pure liquidity pressure (quote walking, inventory absorption) which decays over tens of seconds — which is exactly why the parent's persistence relay had NEGATIVE IC at 1-3 bars and only turned positive at 24 bars: at short offsets the transient component dominates and reverts, so relaying measured persistence pushed the wrong way. The child therefore estimates, in characteristic space, both the per-bar factor return F_k (ridge cross-sectional regression of returns on point-in-time value/size/quality loadings) and the per-bar characteristic net order flow G_k (same regression applied to BVC-signed, ADV-normalised volume), forms the flow-unbacked displacement as the residual of F_k on a trailing Kyle-lambda regression against G_k, and relays a *self-calibrated* horizon-matched coefficient (trailing regression of realised 6-bar factor return on the 6-bar-lagged unbacked displacement, shrunk by its own precision) back onto each name's loadings, weighted by the name's own recent trade participation because that is where the programme's inventory actually landed. It is falsifiable in three ways: if the calibrated coefficients are statistically zero, if replacing the unbacked residual by the raw cumulative factor return gives the same IC (then the flow decomposition is doing nothing), or if the participation weighting is irrelevant, the transient-impact-in-characteristic-space mechanism is wrong. The edge should survive arbitrage because harvesting it needs live point-in-time loadings, per-bar cross-sectional estimation of two orthogonal panels and high-turnover trading of a capacity-limited execution footprint rather than a mispricing anyone can hold.
factors.name: Flow-Unbacked Characteristic-Space Displacement Relay

factors.trading_idea: A 60-second idiosyncratic displacement is part permanent (information) and part transitory (spread bounce plus decaying metaorder impact); the fraction handed back over the next 60 seconds is exactly the block-to-block elasticity phi = Cov(S_t, S_{t+6})/Var(S) of adjacent non-overlapping 6-bar idiosyncratic sums, which is estimable from strictly past block pairs and is a persistent name characteristic (it is a monotone function of relative tick size, spread-to-volatility and market-maker inventory capacity) plus a state effect (down blocks and low-participation 'vacuum' blocks are more liquidity-driven, so they revert more). The parent estimated a conceptually similar coefficient but its trailing window overlapped the block it was about to trade, so beta_hat times the current innovation degenerated into a proxy for the just-realised run and was punished by exactly the reversal it was trying to measure — hence the contradicted sign; the child lags the whole estimation panel by one full horizon so the coefficient carries no information from the current block, and estimates the elasticity directly on the 6-bar object rather than on a 1-bar innovation that has to be extrapolated. The signal is then the *cross-sectional deviation* of a name's own state-specific elasticity times its current displacement, so it isolates the differential transitory share rather than the average reversal the book already spans. The edge persists because harvesting it means supplying immediacy into a name that just moved, at the moment its spread and inventory risk are widest — it is a liquidity-provision premium, not a free arbitrage.
factors.name: Horizon-matched block-reversion elasticity dispersion
