factors.trading_idea: The parent assumed high local-time density at the current price supplies a restoring force; the realized IC says the opposite, and the reason is that occupation density is not a spring, it is a receipt: a move that ends at a level the path has already dwelt on was absorbed by two-sided depth and is therefore permanent (no giveback), whereas a move that ends where the path has never lingered is still in flight against the book and is dominated by the transient (Kyle-Obizhaeva) impact component that relaxes within a minute. The child measures in-flight-ness directly with two fast, scale-free path-geometry markers available at t: (i) path efficiency of the last 6 bars, |net move| / summed |bar moves| — a straight-line run is the footprint of a single liquidity-demanding metaorder walking the book; and (ii) level dwell, the fraction of the last 18 bars whose log mid lies within one bar-sigma of the *current* mid — low dwell means the price has not been accepted at this level. The signal is the pure interaction −(standardized 6-bar move) x (cross-sectionally centred in-flight score), so its average loading on plain reversal is zero: it pays only by knowing *which* recent moves are transient. The edge persists because the conditioning state lives about a minute, must be estimated as a nonparametric per-name path statistic in real time for a few ticks per episode, and its cause (execution-algorithm footprints versus genuine absorption) is a structural property of order flow rather than a mispricing that arbitrage can delete.
factors.name: In-flight run vs settled-level dwell reversal split

factors.trading_idea: Bouchaud's propagator model says the mid-price is the superposition of trade impacts decaying as a power-law kernel G(l)=(1+l)^(-0.5) plus news/quote revisions: the flow-explained part of a recent displacement is mechanically transient and must bleed off over the next few bars, while the part of the displacement that no traded flow can explain (mostly accumulated in quiet bars, where the parent factor found its signal) is precisely the *permanent* news/quote-revision component and therefore continues. This is why the parent's declared sign was contradicted: it labelled unexplained quiet-bar displacement as inventory noise to be repaid, when the propagator decomposition identifies it as the permanent component and the traded-bar displacement as the payable one. The child forecasts the 6-bar return as (i) the kernel-implied decay of currently-embedded transient impact, sum_l [G(l)-G(l+6)] f_{t-l} scaled by a name-specific trailing impact coefficient (entering with a minus sign), plus (ii) continuation of the flow-orthogonal residual displacement. The edge persists because it needs an unsigned-volume tick-rule flow proxy, a fitted power-law propagator and per-name trailing impact calibration to separate the two components, and because both legs are one-minute-scale, cost- and capacity-limited. Falsifiable: if the flow-explained displacement continues and the flow-orthogonal residual reverts over 6 bars, the decomposition is wrong.
factors.name: Propagator-split news continuation vs transient-impact decay

factors.trading_idea: Over minutes-long windows the mid-price does not diffuse uniformly: it spends most of its time pinned inside a narrow band where resting depth has accumulated (a sharp 'value area') and makes brief excursions into thin tails, so the time-at-price distribution is strongly leptokurtic. Where that occupancy distribution is genuinely peaked, an excursion into the thin tail is a queue-driven displacement that the accumulated depth at the modal price absorbs, and the mid snaps back within roughly a minute; where occupancy is flat/diffuse or the modal price itself is migrating, the same displacement is genuine repricing and does not revert. The child therefore trades the *shape* of the occupancy distribution (robust Crow-Siddiqui kurtosis of trailing prices, anchor stationarity, and whether the excursion side carried below-average volume per bar), not the displacement itself. The edge survives because plain distance-from-mean reversal averages sharp-anchor and diffuse-anchor regimes together and nets to nearly zero after costs, and because each individual snapback is only a few ticks — capacity-limited for large arbitrage capital while still being a shape statistic no linear reversal factor spans.
factors.name: Occupancy-kurtosis gated value-area snapback

factors.trading_idea: Parent B forecasts the 6-bar return still *owed* to a slow repricer by folding its distributed-lag market loadings against the already-observed market path, but it measures both the loadings and the starting point with the closing print, which Parent A shows is the noisiest single sample of the efficient price: (H+L)/2 averages two order statistics of the intrabar mid path and so carries far less microstructure noise. The child therefore rebuilds Parent B's kernel on the range-centre price — killing the errors-in-variables attenuation that biases lagged betas toward zero and biases the market regressor — and then adds, in the *same return units*, the piece of the current close-to-centre dislocation that provably dies inside the horizon: phi * (centre - close)/close, where phi = (1 - VR_6)*6/5 is the two-scale share of one-bar variance that is transient, discounted by 1/(1 + V/medV) so only quiet-bar dislocations (noise, not permanent impact) count. The interaction is the edge: the forecast target is close_{t+6} - close_t, so the correct prediction is efficient-price drift owed by the lag kernel PLUS mechanical decay of the noise wedge between the observed close and the efficient anchor — a name can be owed catch-up while its last print already overshot, and neither parent can tell those states apart, while the noise-robust anchor also makes the catch-up loadings themselves more accurate; the whole backlog is amplified where the centre price is frozen (genuine staleness).
factors.name: Endpoint-noise-anchored lag-kernel beta backlog (h=6)

factors.trading_idea: Parent A estimated one signed block autocorrelation rho = 2^(2H-1)-1 on the pooled mid path, but that path is the exact additive sum of two processes with opposite memory: quote-side repricing printed in near-zero-volume bars (quote bounce / maker flicker, genuinely anti-persistent) and taker impact printed in traded bars (sliced metaorders, genuinely persistent) — so its pooled rho is a variance-weighted blend that matches neither leg, and its Roll noise correction was smeared across both channels, over-purging the traded leg for exactly the high-bounce names, which is a concrete reason its realized sign contradicted the hypothesis. The child uses Parent B's exact quiet-bar / traded-bar split of the return path and estimates a SEPARATE noise-purged self-similarity exponent per channel, attributing the Roll bounce variance only to the channel where the bounce actually lives (quiet bars), then forecasts each channel's own 6-bar residual displacement with its own signed rho. Parent B's crossing-clock sech^2 kernel is retained but demoted to a non-negative horizon-relevance weight (not a sign), which kills channels whose anchor deviation oscillates far slower than six bars — precisely the slow concordant leg that made B's edge leak to 24 bars. The interaction is the edge: signed per-channel persistence gives cross-sectional direction that B's pure fade cannot express, while channel attribution gives A's noise correction the right target and stops the two channels' opposite memories from cancelling.
factors.name: Channel-attributed noise-purged block-rho forecast

factors.trading_idea: A 10-second displacement only has to relax when it was *paid for* by a live liquidity-demanding program, and it only relaxes *after* that program stops trading — so the parent's basket geometry was right but its timing variable was missing, which is why its edge lived at 24 bars instead of 6. This child replaces the static cap-weight basket direction (which is essentially a size tilt and carries almost no cross-sectional information) with a time-varying, per-sector *participation-anomaly* direction, and GLS-projects the 6-bar whitened move onto each sector basket in the trailing precision metric to get the displacement genuinely attributable to program flow. That attributed displacement is then signed by metaorder liveness: order-splitting makes participation strongly autocorrelated at the 10-second clock, so names whose abnormal participation is still accelerating keep being pushed (continuation over the next ~60s), while names whose participation has just collapsed back toward their own norm carry accumulated transient impact that decays within seconds (reversal). The edge survives arbitrage because harvesting it requires supplying liquidity exactly to the names a program has just abandoned, which is capacity-limited and risky whenever the liveness classification is wrong.
factors.name: Sector-GLS flow-attributed displacement × metaorder liveness

factors.trading_idea: The parent's continuation/reversal switch was the *level* of trade arrival intensity, which is exactly the coordinate every sibling in the book already gates on (max |corr| 0.59, participation ratio fell). This child keeps the fundamentally-defined valuation-tier peer map (the part that gave the parent independence) but replaces the intensity switch with a scale-free one: the generalised diffusion exponent delta of the name's peer-residual price path measured in ITS OWN VOLUME CLOCK, estimated as the log-log slope of |cumulative residual displacement| against cumulative normalised volume across five nested trailing scales (6..96 bars). A path that grows super-diffusively per unit of volume traded is the signature of persistently one-sided sliced flow (order splitting, self-similar with exponent above the diffusive baseline) and its displacement keeps running; a sub-diffusive path is churn being absorbed — the same displacement per unit volume was bought back within the window — and it fades. Because delta is a ratio of logs it is invariant to how much volume happens to be trading, so it is orthogonal to the volume-level gates the book already spans; the edge survives because harvesting it means holding alongside possibly-informed persistent flow (adverse selection) or against absorbed churn (inventory risk) at 10-second latency inside fundamentally comparable peer cells.
factors.name: Volume-clock diffusion exponent gated peer-residual continuation

factors.trading_idea: Basket/program flow (ETF create-redeem, index programs) buys every constituent in proportion to capitalisation weight, so inside a single peer basket it displaces each name by weight/depth — i.e. by its inverse-turnover elasticity kappa — rather than by its loading on the basket. The resulting *peer-relative* dislocation (name vs its industry basket) is exactly the component a market maker can hedge instantly by trading the basket, so it is absorbed and snaps back within ~a minute, whereas the peer-common part carries unhedgeable factor risk and is not repaired. The child therefore accumulates the program-footprint-weighted industry-basket return over bars t-7..t-2, prices each name's mechanical over-push as its industry-demeaned wedge (rank kappa minus rank beta-to-its-own-basket), and fades that push only in proportion to leave-one-out peer-basket activity, because the repair requires the hedge legs to be tradable right now. The interaction is the edge: Parent A knows *when* a move is mechanical but fades it against the market (where beta hedges already live), and Parent B knows *which* component is hedgeable and *when* peers are live but has no impulse that is mechanically identified; combining them isolates a within-basket, weight-proportional over-push and only harvests it in the liquidity states where the snapback can actually occur.
factors.name: Program-footprint gated peer-relative elasticity snapback

factors.trading_idea: Rice's inversion rho = cos(pi * p_flip) is only valid for ZERO-MEAN increments: any local drift over the estimation window makes adjacent block displacements share a sign for trivial reasons, so the parent's raw sign-concordance did not measure the lag-6 block autocorrelation at all — it measured trailing drift-to-noise, and drift-intensity x displacement is just momentum, which loses money at a 60-second horizon (exactly the negative IC the report found). The child therefore computes TWO Rice estimates on the same tape: p_flip on raw block displacements (rho_raw, drift-contaminated) and on displacements centred by their own trailing mean (rho_cen, the honest AR(1) coefficient), and reads the non-negative gap W = rho_raw - rho_cen as a sign-only, jump-robust footprint of sustained one-directional (metaorder / order-splitting) execution. Mechanically, a name carrying a large W is carrying accumulated TRANSIENT impact, so its latest 60-second displacement is overpush that relaxes when the schedule pauses, while the honest rho_cen supplies whatever genuine block persistence remains; the traded coefficient is rho_cen - W applied to the standardised 6-bar displacement. The edge persists because reversion desks apply one common reversion speed to the whole cross-section and because correcting the Rice bias requires continuous per-name re-estimation of two sign statistics whose per-name payoff is tiny and only diversifies in a broad book.
factors.name: Drift-purged Rice block persistence minus overpush wedge

factors.trading_idea: Parent A's wick asymmetry realized the opposite sign to its 'rejection' story, and the reason reconciles it with Parent B: on heavy-volume bars the traded volume prints inside the shadow, so a dominant upper shadow means the bar's transaction centroid sits ABOVE the bar-end mid — the endpoint is displaced below where size actually changed hands, and the mid drifts back up. That is exactly Parent B's value-area snapback, but measured at bar/probe scale (fast enough for a 6-bar offset) instead of over 90 bars (where B's edge only matured at 24 bars). The child therefore takes the fast, volume-gated probe displacement AND a compressed 5-minute value-area displacement, and multiplies both by Parent B's state variables — Crow-Siddiqui occupancy kurtosis and modal-anchor stationarity — plus a freshness gate on the excursion. The interaction is the edge neither parent has: A fires on every heavy-volume wick with no knowledge of whether accumulated depth exists to absorb the displacement, while B knows the book state but only reads slow displacements; conditioning fast probe displacement on a sharply peaked, non-migrating occupancy law selects precisely the displacements that are absorbed within a minute.
factors.name: Probe-displacement snapback gated by occupancy sharpness

factors.trading_idea: A name's fitted loadings on *lagged* market returns imply it still owes a computable amount of catch-up to information the market has already delivered, and that debt splits into a quote-shading leg (quiet, untraded bars) and a traded-impact leg (active bars). But a positive lagged loading is only tradable if the causal arrow really runs market -> name; when the name is itself the leader (or the market proxy contains the name), the same fitted lag is an artifact and the name has typically over-shot, so the correct trade is the opposite one. The child therefore (i) purifies the market path with a per-name leave-one-out cap-weighted aggregate so self-inclusion cannot manufacture lagged loadings, and (ii) replaces the parent's Rice sign-flip gate with a directional information-flow purity index D = sum_l [corr(r_t, m_{t-l})^2 - corr(m_t, r_{t-l})^2] / sum_l [both], measured separately inside each volume channel, which signs the trust on each leg. The edge persists because followership at the 10-second scale is created by fragmented liquidity and quote-update latency in the slower names — the very frictions that make the catch-up trade costly to arbitrage away.
factors.name: Leave-one-out channel debt with lead-lag purity gate

factors.trading_idea: Parent A tells you HOW BIG a fundamental story a 10-second equity impulse would require: de-levering the move by the Merton equity/asset elasticity turns the same 30bp print into a huge implied asset shock for an unlevered name and a trivial one for a 5x-levered name, so large de-levered shocks are prima facie non-fundamental. Parent B supplies the missing state variable: a sign-split square-root impact coefficient (mean |idio return| per sqrt of normalised dollar volume, estimated separately on up bars and down bars over ~30 minutes) says which SIDE of the book is currently being absorbed cheaply and which side is paying full impact. The child conditions A's de-levered shock on B's asymmetry evaluated on the impulse's OWN side: a large implied asset shock printed on the abnormally cheap side is inventory pressure meeting a resilient counterparty and should snap back hard, while the same de-levered shock printed on the abnormally expensive (resilient, information-bearing) side is being genuinely paid for and instead tends to persist. Neither parent has this edge alone — A fades every big de-levered impulse indiscriminately (its symmetric volume-vacuum gate cannot tell absorbed flow from paid-for information), and B's asymmetry is only a liquidity state with no measure of how implausible the accompanying price move is, which is exactly why its standalone direction was unstable.
factors.name: De-levered asset shock gated by side-split impact asymmetry

factors.trading_idea: The parent's conditioning variable — the 1-bar cross-lag correlation between a bar's body and the next seam — is mechanically contaminated: body_{t-1}=c_{t-1}-o_{t-1} and seam_t=o_t-c_{t-1} share the same noisy endpoint c_{t-1}, so mid-price measurement noise alone manufactures a negative coefficient that carries no forecast, and the object is estimated at a 1-bar lead while we must forecast 6 bars. The child replaces it with a *noise-orthogonal instrumental estimate of the horizon-matched pass-through*: at each t we look back at a completed 4-bar peer-neutral body push (bars t-9..t-6), regress the realised subsequent 6-bar peer-neutral return on that push, and instrument the push with an earlier, non-overlapping push (bars t-13..t-10) which shares no price observation with either the push or the response — killing the bounce/noise bias while keeping the genuine flow autocorrelation that makes the instrument relevant. The estimation sample is restricted to bars whose volume exceeded the name's trailing median, so the coefficient measures inventory absorption by liquidity providers rather than stale-quote drift, and the resulting signed coefficient (negative = absorber that repays pushes, positive = order-splitting metaorder that extends them) *scales and signs* the fresh push instead of merely shrinking it. The edge persists because harvesting it means posting passive size against possibly informed aggressive flow — a market-making inventory risk, and the pass-through coefficient is only identifiable per name over hours of data, which is estimation work rather than a liftable directional trade.
factors.name: Noise-orthogonal IV horizon-matched push pass-through

factors.trading_idea: Basket, ETF and portfolio-tilt orders are executed in slices over minutes, so their footprint appears not in a single name but as short-run autocorrelation of the *cross-sectional factor returns* attached to point-in-time fundamental characteristics (book-to-price, sales-to-price, cash-flow yield, size, ROE): while a value-tilted programme is working, the value-mimicking return keeps drifting the same way for tens of seconds; when the recent factor moves are instead quote-bounce noise, the same factor return is anti-autocorrelated. The child therefore extracts per-bar characteristic factor returns by ridge-regularised cross-sectional regression of 10-second returns on live characteristic loadings, measures each factor's own trailing AR(1) coefficient, and relays the sign-and-size-conditioned continuation back onto each name's loadings, giving a directly horizon-matched 6-bar expected return instead of the parent's slow multiple-space spread reversion (whose IC only peaked at 24 bars). It is falsifiable: if the measured factor-return AR(1) coefficients are statistically zero, or if replacing the measured coefficient by a fixed positive constant produces the same IC, the slicing-footprint mechanism is wrong and the signal is just repackaged characteristic momentum. The edge should persist because exploiting it requires real-time point-in-time loadings, per-bar cross-sectional estimation and high turnover on a low-Sharpe execution-footprint signal that is capacity-limited rather than mispriced.
factors.name: Characteristic-Factor Slicing Persistence Relay

factors.trading_idea: Parent A forecasts the next 6 bars in return units (horizon-folded distributed-lag market catch-up plus a mean-reverting own-innovation term estimated with one unconditional AR(1) coefficient); Parent B knows from within-bar geometry whether a push was absorbed and retraced or accepted as a body move, but only uses that as a post-hoc router between two ranked channels. The child makes the participation-weighted wick (absorption) share the *state variable inside the estimation*: for each name it runs two trailing, state-weighted, directly horizon-matched regressions of the realised 6-bar idiosyncratic return sum on the shock observed 6 bars earlier — one weighted by the absorption state at that time, one by its complement — for both the close-to-close idiosyncratic innovation and the within-bar close-location displacement, then applies whichever response coefficient matches the *current* absorption state. The interaction is the edge: the reversion speed of a shock is not a name constant but a function of whether depth absorbed the flow, so A's single phi averages a snapback regime with a continuation regime and cancels, while B has no return-unit, horizon-matched estimate of how much of the displacement actually pays back inside the fixed 6-bar offset; the owed market catch-up is in addition trusted only where bars are body-dominated (moves are being accepted) and the name is a demonstrably slow repricer.
factors.name: Absorption-state split direct-h6 shock response with folded market catch-up

factors.trading_idea: A 60-second displacement is an additive sum of increments, and the increments come from two different generators: median-region ('core') increments, which is how an execution algorithm walks price while slicing a metaorder, and own-name tail increments, which is how a momentary depth withdrawal overshoots and then relaxes under the transient-impact propagator. The parent multiplied one location statistic by a coarse cross-sectional dispersion gate; the child instead *decomposes* the same nonparametric rank-drift into its core and tail parts and signs them oppositely — core-generated drift should continue over the next six bars, tail-generated drift should revert — and gates only the core leg by the trailing Spearman (rank) lag-1 autocorrelation of increments, because a genuine slicing schedule produces serially concordant child-order prints while an alternating core path is just noise. This is falsifiable in a sharp way: the two legs must carry opposite-signed ICs, and the core leg's IC must be larger when rank autocorrelation is positive; if tail-driven displacement instead continues (permanent news repricing), the combined IC flips negative. The edge should persist because it requires classifying each 10-second increment against the name's own conditional increment distribution and tracking its serial concordance, the agent whose child orders create the core drift cannot profit by front-running itself, and net-of-spread capacity inside a one-minute window is too small for size-constrained arbitrageurs.
factors.name: Core-vs-tail increment drift decomposition with Spearman persistence gate

factors.trading_idea: Price levels that a name has already occupied many times in the recent past (high local time / recurrence density of its market-neutral relative-value coordinate) are levels where resting liquidity and dealer inventory have accumulated: they act as attractors, so a fresh displacement toward/at such an accepted level is absorbed and snaps back within a few bars. Levels never visited in the recent window carry no resting book, so a displacement into them is either informed liquidity demand (continues) or pure quote noise — and traded-volume intensity separates the two: an excursion into unvisited territory on above-normal volume is real order-flow pressure that continues, while the same excursion on thin volume is quote flicker that mean-reverts. The child therefore routes the sign of the short-horizon displacement by (i) local-time acceptance and (ii) volume intensity, instead of by the parent's basket-over-push attribution, whose declared direction the report falsified. The edge persists because computing recurrence density in a market-neutral coordinate requires a level-occupancy statistic rather than a moving average, and because absorbing at accepted levels is precisely the inventory service liquidity providers are paid for — arbitraging it away would remove their compensation.
factors.name: Local-time acceptance routing of micro-displacement

factors.trading_idea: The parent's core statistic is sound — the bar's high-low midpoint averages several samples of the intrabar mid path and is therefore a lower-noise estimate of the efficient price than the single closing print, so C minus a short average of bar midpoints is mostly transient quote noise plus decaying transient impact. What the parent got wrong was hard-coding the *response* to that dislocation (always fade) and dressing it up with a volume weight and a variance-ratio scaler that did not survive out of sample. Here the response is estimated, not assumed: for each name we run a trailing, skip-one-purged OLS of the realized 6-bar return on its own dislocation lagged 7 bars (the one-bar skip removes the mechanical bid-ask-bounce bias that contaminates naive reversal regressions), and shrink the per-name slope halfway to the cross-sectional median. Names whose dislocation has recently been dominated by market-maker bounce get a negative slope and are faded, names whose dislocation reflects live order-splitting get a positive slope and are followed; the edge persists because capturing it requires quoting passively against the last aggressor and absorbing the adverse-selection risk makers are paid for, and because the bounce-vs-metaorder mix is name- and regime-specific, so no static reversal rule monetises it.
factors.name: Purged self-calibrated dislocation response beta

factors.trading_idea: For a stationary relative-value process the conditional drift is a *function of the state*, not a constant times the deviation: Fokker–Planck says the pull points toward denser regions of the trailing occupation measure, and its strength collapses where the process habitually sits and steepens at the edges of the visited range (and can even invert into continuation once the level is genuinely unvisited). I therefore estimate each name's drift non-parametrically — a causal Nadaraya–Watson average of past one-bar increments of its market-beta-neutralised, trailing-standardised cumulative idiosyncratic price, kernel-weighted by how close the past level was to *today's* level and exponentially decayed in time — and then subtract the linear (Ornstein–Uhlenbeck) drift fitted on the same weighted window. The residual is the purely nonlinear, state-local part of the reversion: it is what a book of linear reversal/z-score factors mathematically cannot span, because a single reversion speed averages the flat interior and the steep, asymmetric edges of the occupation density into one number. The edge should persist because harvesting it requires per-name nonparametric estimation of a locally varying (and vertically asymmetric, inventory-driven) reversion speed at 10-second resolution rather than another parameterisation of 'deviation times minus kappa', and its sign disagrees with the linear signal precisely in the states where linear arbitrageurs are most crowded.
factors.name: Occupation-kernel conditional drift wedge (nonparametric minus OU)

factors.trading_idea: Parent B showed that peer-relative displacement must be attributed to its source — idiosyncratic print-backed impact (permanent, follow it) versus sector-basket print-backed pressure and unbacked quiet quote shading (transitory, fade them) — but it read each leg as an accumulated *level*, an already-public slow state whose information is spread flat across 1–24 bars. Parent A showed the fix on the timescale axis: replacing an accumulated level with a causal band-pass (fast EWMA minus slow EWMA) isolates the component whose relaxation clock actually matches the fixed 6-bar offset, and that a smooth exponential silence kernel gated by silence persistence beats a hard traded/quiet split — but Parent A applied that filter to raw returns, so its fast component was dominated by sector-common moves that never revert, leaving IC near zero. The child band-passes each *attributed* leg of the peer-residual displacement: only the freshly-arrived, still-un-relaxed transitory mass (basket-pushed plus persistence-gated quiet drift) is faded, only fresh idio-print-backed displacement is followed, and both fade legs are scaled by leave-one-out peer liveness so the snap-back is hedgeable. The interaction is the edge: attribution tells you *which* displacement is repairable, the band-pass tells you *which part of it is still owed inside six bars* — neither parent has both.
factors.name: Fresh flow-attributed peer-residual band-pass legs

factors.trading_idea: A Student-t score-driven filter of the efficient price updates its level by w(z)·r with the bounded influence weight w(z)=nu/(nu+z^2), so it implicitly decomposes every observed 10-second idiosyncratic return into a permanent part w·r and a transitory part (1-w)·r, where z is the return measured in units of its own local scale AFTER dividing by sqrt(volume/ADV) — the square-root-impact yardstick for how much of a move the bar's trade flow can legitimately justify. The mechanism is the nonlinearity: moves that are large relative to the flow that produced them are attributed to inventory-bearing liquidity provision and are predicted to revert convexly (more than proportionally) in |r|, while equally large moves accompanied by proportionate volume are treated as information and are not faded. The signal is the exponentially discounted accumulation of these transitory attributions (decay half-life matched to the 6-bar horizon), then made orthogonal to the plain linear displacement by a trailing per-name OLS residual, so it prices only the flow-unjustified, convexity-driven part of the recent path. It survives arbitrage because harvesting it means absorbing exactly the inventory a liquidity provider is shedding within a minute, and because the split needs two per-name latent quantities — the local scale of the volume-standardized return and the influence weight it implies — that a pooled linear reversal or threshold-jump signal cannot represent; falsifiable prediction: replacing the influence weight (1-w) by a constant (the linear analogue) or removing the sqrt(volume) standardization should materially reduce the 6-bar IC.
factors.name: Bounded-influence permanent/transitory return split (volume-scaled score filter)

factors.trading_idea: Parent A found the event (a mid pinned on the tick lattice finally breaking) but hard-coded its polarity as continuation and was contradicted; Parent B found that response polarity is a name-specific, horizon-matched estimable state but applied it to a generic quiet/traded return split that the book largely spans. The child conditions B's calibration machinery on A's event state: the pin-break displacement is split into a queue-backed leg (volume was genuinely absorbed while the mid sat pinned AND printed in the break bar, so the resting queue was consumed and the next level is thinner) and an evaporated leg (the level vanished with no volume behind it), and each leg's forward sign is learned from a trailing regression of completed 6-bar returns on the same leg lagged exactly 6 bars, shrunk toward the cross-sectionally pooled coefficient. The interaction is the edge: whether a lattice break continues or snaps back is precisely a function of whether the queue was paid for, and neither parent could see that — A summed the two cases into one variance-dominated reverting blob, B never knew which bars were queue-clearing events. Finally the combined state is cross-sectionally purged of 1- and 6-bar return carriers, the step that turned A's raw IC positive in the diagnostic.
factors.name: Pin-clearing backing split with self-calibrated polarity

factors.trading_idea: The parent showed that the *level* of the path-conversion ratio c (net displacement / (net displacement + probed excursion)) correctly separates absorbed-probe continuation from swept-level snapback, but c is a slowly-drifting level, so its switch changes state over many bars and the resulting signal only pays off ~24 bars out. The event that actually times the next minute is the *innovation* in c: when c is rising, the book is being converted into net displacement right now (a sweep in progress) and transient impact snaps back within a handful of bars; when c is falling, fresh excursion is accumulating faster than it converts, i.e. aggression is being absorbed and the endpoint mid is a stale sample of where price was probed, so the mid catches up almost immediately. Localising every channel with a ~2-bar exponential recency kernel (instead of a 10-bar decay-linear sum) and cross-sectionally centring the switch variable (c has a large common, volatility-driven component) makes the signal a fast, name-specific state read rather than a slow common-activity read. The edge survives arbitrage because it is a second-order path statistic — it requires jointly measuring unconverted wick excursion, its conversion rate, and traded size at 10-second resolution — and its capacity is bounded by the same impact cost it measures.
factors.name: Conversion-velocity switched fresh-probe relay

factors.trading_idea: A relative-value desk cannot supply liquidity to a dislocated stock unless it can simultaneously take the offsetting side in a close substitute, so the speed of snapback is governed by whether the name's own valuation neighbourhood is dislocated the *other* way (an internal offset exists, hedge is nearly risk-free) or the *same* way (the whole tier moved together, so absorbing the flow means warehousing a tier-factor exposure). The child therefore keeps the parent's valuation-matched kernel basket and beta-hedged residual impulse, but replaces the parent's symmetric second-stage purge with a *signed* crowding statistic — the sign-aligned concordance between the name's residual impulse and the kernel-weighted residual impulses of its neighbours — and lets that statistic set both the size and the sign of the bet: strong reversal for offsetable dislocations, fading to zero and then to continuation for the most tier-concordant ones. Falsifiable: if reversal strength is not monotone decreasing in same-side neighbourhood concordance (i.e. the interaction gate adds no IC over the plain hedged-residual reversal, and the most concordant names revert rather than continue), the arbitrage-capacity/offset-availability mechanism is wrong. The edge persists because it requires joining point-in-time per-share fundamentals to a 10-second tape to define substitutability and then a *signed cross-name* aggregation of residual dislocations — an object a single-name microstructure model never forms — and its capacity is capped by the small number of tight valuation neighbourhoods.
factors.name: Tier-concordance offset-gated valuation-peer snapback

factors.trading_idea: The parent's statistic is algebraically the *signed rejected excursion* of a bar (shadow asymmetry = travel-from-open minus retained body), i.e. the transient component of price impact; the report shows its realized sign is continuation, not rejection, which is exactly what a propagator/transient-impact world predicts — a continuing metaorder pushes the mid, the transient part decays inside the bar (leaving a wick), and the surviving order-flow autocorrelation resumes the move over the next minute. But heavy-volume wick bars pool two opposite populations: bars that gave back part of the excursion yet still closed with a body in the probe's direction (continuing metaorder: transient decay + permanent repricing) and bars whose excursion was fully absorbed and reversed through the open (genuine hidden size / a wall that then pushes the other way). The child therefore splits the volume-gated rejected excursion by whether the bar's body confirms it, takes confirmed minus absorbed, and residualises the aggregate against the same-window gated body so the signal is the rejected-excursion *amplification* channel rather than one-minute momentum. The edge survives arbitrage because harvesting it means posting against a partially concealed, still-working metaorder or paying spread to impatient aggressors, and the state is refreshed every 10 seconds; it is falsified if the body-sign conditioning is irrelevant (confirmed and absorbed wicks carry the same forward sign) or if the body-residualised aggregate has no sign at 6 bars.
factors.name: Rejected-excursion / body-confirmation split

factors.trading_idea: Ten-second mid-price sequences are largely produced by mechanical processes — child-order slicing, queue refill after depletion, tick-grid bounce — which imprint *state-dependent* (non-linear) structure on returns that a linear autocorrelation filter cannot see: the 60-second continuation after a down bar on heavy volume is a different object from the same down bar on thin volume. I therefore build a small variable-order context tree over the alphabet (return-sign tercile at t, sign tercile at t-1, volume-intensity regime at t) and estimate, from trailing realised data only, the conditional mean 6-bar-ahead return for each of the 18 states, hierarchically shrinking each name's own state mean toward a cross-sectionally pooled state mean and then toward the global mean (the execution/queue map is mostly common across names, so pooling identifies it with far more data than any single name provides). The forecast is then cross-sectionally orthogonalised against the plain standardised trailing 6-bar return, so what is traded is purely the *state-conditional* part of the map, not linear reversal or momentum. The edge should persist because per-name the conditional drift is only a few basis points over one minute — below single-name round-trip cost — so it is only harvestable inside a large diversified cross-section, and because the map is non-stationary and must be recalibrated continuously rather than encoded as a fixed rule.
factors.name: Pooled context-tree state drift (residual of linear reversal)

factors.trading_idea: When a mid sits still for one or more 10-second bars, the volume that prints during that quiet spell is a direct read on the resting depth at the touch; the volume that prints in the bar the mid finally moves is a read on how much of that depth was actually taken. The child therefore does not gate on both volumes (the parent's error, which just re-expressed generic reversal and realised the wrong sign) but *splits* on their ratio kappa = per-bar absorbed volume / (absorbed + break-bar volume): kappa near 1 means a deep queue reformed behind a small print or a pure quote revision, so the pinned level acts as an attractor and the break is pulled back within a minute; kappa near 0 means the print dwarfed the absorbed depth (or the level was never tested at all), so the queue was genuinely consumed, the next level is thinner, and the move continues. The parent's own decay profile supports this: its blended, 8-bar-smoothed impulse was weakly continuing at 1-3 bars and increasingly reverting out to 24 bars, i.e. the reversion of the untaken-queue half dominates once you stop averaging over stale events — so the child keeps only fresh breaks (age 0-2 bars) so the pull-back lands inside the fixed 6-bar window. The edge survives arbitrage because each event is worth a fraction of a tick in exactly the tick-constrained, quiet names where crossing the spread costs a full tick: only passive liquidity can monetise it, so it is not competed away.
factors.name: Absorbed-queue share at a quiet-mid pin: reformation vs clearing split

factors.trading_idea: Parent A found the *event* (a volume-absorbing price pin that just broke) but hard-wired continuation and realised the sign of the transient overshoot; Parent B found the right *classifier* of a move's permanence (square-root-law volume backing) but tried to learn each name's polarity from a noisy per-name horizon-matched regression. The child uses B's classifier as a universal, cross-sectionally comparable polarity for A's event: 6-bar displacement is loaded NEGATIVELY in proportion to how far it exceeds the displacement its own traded volume can back under the sqrt impact law (unbacked taker push / quote evaporation reverts within a minute — which is exactly why both parents realised negative IC at 6 bars), and is loaded POSITIVELY only when two independent pieces of queue evidence agree: the pre-move window was pinned to the tick grid while absorbing volume (a real resting queue existed) AND the move itself was over-backed by volume (the queue was consumed, the next level is thinner). The interaction carries edge neither parent has because the unconditional 6-bar reversal carrier is then projected out cross-sectionally, so what remains is purely the state-conditional polarity — continuation priced only where queue-clearing evidence overrides the generic overshoot, reversal amplified where volume backing is absent.
factors.name: Queue-backed pin-break impact polarity (reversal-purged)

factors.trading_idea: The parent proved that flow-attributed and quiet displacement carry opposite-signed information, but it *assumed* the polarity (+idio, −basket, −quiet) and *assumed* a multiplicative volume-clock delivery gate; the evaluation shows the assumed polarity is only weakly right at 6 bars and outright wrong by 12-24 bars, and the IS/VAL sign instability is exactly what an assumed, un-calibrated response profile produces. The child instead estimates the response empirically at the pinned offset: a cross-name **pooled multivariate local projection** of realised 6-bar returns on four causal channels (own signed sqrt-volume flow, sector peer flow, fresh 1-3-bar peer-purged displacement, older 4-12-bar displacement), solved from trailing normal equations, so the multivariate partials themselves separate idiosyncratic flow, basket-common flow and flow-unexplained (quote-shading) displacement — no hand-set sign, no per-name Kyle-lambda noise. Because impact only resolves inside the window when the name's business clock is running, the coefficient vector is estimated separately in two turnover states (fast vs slow relative to the cross-sectional median of forecast/long-run volume rate), which converts the parent's assumed θ shrinkage into a falsifiable, estimated interaction. The edge should persist because pooling plus exact horizon matching is a statistical-efficiency edge, not a public formula: it requires jointly maintaining a panel of causal channel innovations and a rolling 4x4 pooled regression on a 10-second grid, and the positions it takes are concentrated in fast-turnover states where capacity is bounded by impact cost.
factors.name: Pooled local-projection response of flow & displacement, split by turnover regime

factors.trading_idea: The parent hard-coded the Llorente-Michaely-Saar-Wang adverse-selection sign onto a 10-second return×volume interaction and the data reversed it, because at this frequency the interaction is not governed by information asymmetry but by Bouchaud-style transient impact: a displacement accompanied by unusually heavy volume is mostly liquidity-taking pressure walking a thin book and decays as the queue refills, whereas a displacement achieved on *light* volume is a pure quote revision (inventory-free repricing) that persists. Rather than flipping a constant, the child estimates the interaction coefficient online for each name: a trailing, non-overlapping bivariate OLS of the realised 6-bar idiosyncratic return on the lagged peer-hedged displacement and on the lagged displacement×volume-shock interaction, keeping only the interaction loading so the over-mined unconditional reversal term is projected out empirically instead of by assumption. The fitted loading is shrunk toward its cross-sectional median (James-Stein style) and multiplied by the current interaction to produce a self-calibrating expected-return forecast, which is falsified if the estimated impact-decay loadings are pure noise (then the adaptive factor is no better than the fixed-sign parent). The edge survives arbitrage because it requires joining slow point-in-time comparability information (industry × live valuation tier peer baskets) to 10-second flow, per-name online calibration of an impact propagator, and bearing residual idiosyncratic risk that a pooled reversal trader cannot monetise.
factors.name: Propagator-calibrated flow-interaction snapback

factors.trading_idea: A market-wide impulse creates a per-name 'response backlog' e_t = beta_i*m_t - r_i,t; the backlog is only informative if the name is currently *unattended* — mid-price frozen for many of the last bars and volume running well below its own norm — because then no one has yet repriced it, and the missing move must be paid out over the next few bars. In names that are simultaneously being traded hard, the very same gap has the opposite meaning: the price is moving beyond its beta-implied response because informed flow is arriving, so the gap continues rather than reverts. The child therefore replaces the parent's slow quarterly payout-clientele gate (which diffused the edge to 12 bars) with a bar-by-bar attention state and expresses the backlog as an exponentially decaying recursive state (halflife 2 bars), so only *fresh* unabsorbed shock is counted and the payoff lands at the fixed 6-bar offset. The edge persists because inattention is caused by the same frictions that make the trade expensive — frozen mids, tick-size binding, thin queues — so the marginal arbitrageur is absent precisely where the wedge is largest; it is falsified if the actively-traded leg of the interaction carries the same-signed IC as the stale leg, which would mean this is ordinary beta lead-lag with no attention conditioning.
factors.name: Quote-Inattention Conditioned Beta Backlog Flip

factors.trading_idea: The parent assumed a name's 60-second block autocorrelation rho is a slowly-varying name attribute and estimated it from ~80 minutes of non-overlapping block pairs — only ~80 independent observations, so the resulting rho_hat was mostly estimation noise and the product rho_hat*displacement degenerated into a rescaled reversal signal (deflated t = -0.10, sign contradicted). The child keeps the one durable piece — Rice's scale-free, tick-size-free inversion p_flip -> rho = cos(pi*p_flip) — but relocates it to where the statistical power is: single-bar sign flips of market-purged returns, where an EWM estimate uses tens of effective observations per name and updates every 10 seconds. The mechanism is that the mixture weight between bid-ask/inventory bounce (transitory mid error, guaranteed to snap back within a minute) and sliced-metaorder flow (self-exciting, continues over the next minute) is a *fast-switching state*, not a constant: when a name is flipping signs more than its own long-run baseline it is currently bounce-dominated and its 6-bar displacement is mostly transitory pricing error; when flips have dried up relative to baseline, order flow is being split and the displacement continues. The factor is therefore a pure *interaction* — the sign-flip-rate innovation (Rice-inverted, cross-sectionally ranked and centred) times the current standardised 6-bar displacement — so it carries almost no unconditional reversal loading and cannot be spanned by the book's one-coefficient-for-everyone reversal factors; it persists because harvesting it needs continuous per-name regime nowcasting for a per-name payoff far below one spread, which only pays as a broad portfolio tilt.
factors.name: Rice flip-regime innovation × displacement interaction

factors.trading_idea: A peer-relative valuation dislocation is only closed when a relative-value desk can actually put on BOTH legs of the spread, so the speed of convergence is set by live hedge capacity, not by the size of the dislocation alone. Hedge capacity is directly observable at 10-second resolution as the joint trading activity of the name AND of its industry peer basket relative to their own hourly norms: when both legs are busy the spread is closed inside the next minute, when the peer basket is dormant the identical dislocation simply sits there and only bleeds off over many minutes — which is exactly why the parent's IC kept growing out to 24 bars instead of peaking at 6. The child therefore (i) measures the dislocation as a six-bar persistence area of the peer spread around its own slow anchor, so single-bar quote noise is diluted while genuinely held-open spreads survive, and (ii) multiplies it by a two-legged hedge-availability gate (geometric mean of own and peer-ex-self relative activity, squashed logistically). The edge persists because it is compensation for supplying immediacy to a hedged relative-value trade and is self-limiting: it is largest precisely when hedge capacity is available, and capacity itself caps how much capital can chase it. Falsified if the IC is unchanged between busy-peer and dormant-peer states, or if the area-based dislocation still peaks at 24 bars.
factors.name: Two-Legged Hedge-Capacity Gated Peer Multiple Dislocation Area

factors.trading_idea: At 10-second resolution the parent's 'valuation multiple' is degenerate — per-share fundamentals are quarterly step functions, so its 6-bar multiple change collapses into a peer-demeaned return and the fundamental machinery bought only complexity (hence tiny residual IC and negative marginal ΔIC). The child keeps the one component with real content — the flow-UNBACKED part of a peer-demeaned 6-bar move, i.e. displacement in excess of the name's own Kyle-lambda impact of its signed sqrt-volume — and replaces the degenerate anchor with the one thing quarterly fundamentals *can* legitimately supply intraday: a static cross-sectional measure of how hard the name is to value (low earnings/FCF yield, loss-making, R&D- and intangible-heavy, levered), sector-neutralised so it is not a sector or size bet. Mechanism: for transparent, cash-generating names many participants agree on fair value, so a quote move with no trade behind it is dealer inventory/quote-shading noise and snaps back within seconds; for opaque names price discovery genuinely happens in quotes rather than prints (information is expensive to verify), so the same unbacked move is slow-diffusing information and continues. The factor is therefore a *sign-flipping interaction*, near-orthogonal to the book's many unconditional 'quiet displacement reverts' factors, and the edge persists because HFT liquidity providers condition on order flow and depth, not on quarterly accounting opacity — the two data domains sit on different clocks and are rarely joined.
factors.name: Opacity-conditioned unbacked displacement split

factors.trading_idea: The parent's only durable asset was Rice's scale-free link between adjacent-sign statistics and Gaussian-copula correlation; its fragility came from splitting the tape into quiet/active subsequences and using the Rice gap as a multiplicative gate with many tuned constants. The child throws away the split and instead inverts Rice at the *horizon scale*: it measures how often a name's 6-bar (60-second) displacement is followed by a same-signed 6-bar displacement, and converts that sign-concordance frequency into a block autocorrelation via rho = cos(pi * p_flip) — a jump-robust, tick-size-free estimator of exactly the coefficient a 6-bar forecast needs. Economically, rho is name-specific and slowly varying because it is set by how much of a name's 60-second variance is inventory/bounce noise (rho < 0, displacement snaps back) versus order-splitting metaorder flow (rho > 0, displacement continues); the forecast is then simply rho_hat times the current standardised displacement, so the same signal produces reversal in bouncy names and continuation in schedule-executed names. The edge survives arbitrage because HF reversal desks apply one common reversion parameter to the whole cross-section — the *dispersion* of rho, not its average, is what is left on the table, and harvesting it requires continuous per-name re-estimation with a heavy-tail-robust estimator whose payoff per name is tiny and only diversifies away in a broad book.
factors.name: Rice-inverted block sign-concordance forecast

factors.trading_idea: Parent A showed that inside a valuation-tier peer frame the *quiet* (near-zero-volume) part of a name's displacement reverts while the traded part persists; parent B showed that in the raw, un-residualised frame the quiet drift mildly continues. Both are true at once if the quiet drift you should follow is the part the *cohort* shares (a genuine repricing the maker is walking toward) and the part you should fade is the idiosyncratic quiet wander (stale-quote noise) — so the peer-consensus fresh drift is the state variable that decides the sign of B's freshness legs, not a nuisance to be subtracted and discarded. The child therefore band-passes (fast-minus-slow EWMA, horizon-matched, silence-persistence gated) the peer-residual quiet and traded return streams, and gates each by its smooth concordance with the band-passed cohort-common drift: concordant fresh displacement is information/gap-closing and continues, discordant fresh displacement is stale quoting (quiet) or transient liquidity-demand impact (traded) and relaxes, with asymmetric continuation/reversion weights inherited from each parent's realised direction. The interaction carries edge neither parent has because A destroyed the cohort signal it needed to interpret its own residual, and B had no fundamental comparability map to define the consensus at all.
factors.name: Peer-consensus concordance gate on fresh quiet/traded displacement

factors.trading_idea: A 10-second mid dislocation from the last few minutes' volume-weighted price is a mixture of transient liquidity cost (which reverts) and genuine revision of fair value (which does not); the mixing proportion is not a microstructure quantity but a *valuation-transparency* quantity. Names whose fair value is pinned by realised, tangible, distributed cash flows (high FCF/earnings/dividend yield, high cash-conversion income quality, low intangibility, low R&D intensity, low sales multiple, low long-run growth duration) have a narrow rational fair-value band, so market makers treat a dislocation as inventory pressure and revert it; opaque long-duration names have a wide band, so the same dislocation is more likely to be information and reverts far less. The child therefore trades only the *interaction* — dislocation reversion scaled by a point-in-time fundamental anchor-tightness score — and is explicitly orthogonalised, row by row, against the plain dislocation-reversal vector, so the plain reversal family (which dominates the book) cannot explain it. The edge persists because it requires joining slow, quarterly point-in-time fundamental quality data to 10-second mid dynamics: HFT liquidity providers condition on book state and volatility, not on intangibles or FCF yield, while fundamental investors never trade at this frequency, and the surviving spread is an equilibrium difference in rational reversion intensity rather than a mispricing that can be closed by one arbitrageur.
factors.name: Valuation-anchor tightness gated intrabar dislocation reversion

factors.trading_idea: Parent A shows that a trade-backed price push is an inventory debt that liquidity providers amortise in volume time, and that what matters at a fixed 6-bar offset is the share of that debt expected to be discharged inside the window. Parent B shows that repayment capacity is not homogeneous: the peer-idiosyncratic part of a push can be laid off instantly against an active industry basket, while the peer-common part carries unhedgeable factor risk and can only be worked off by basket-wide counterparty flow. The child therefore splits the within-bar push into its industry-idiosyncratic and industry-common legs and gives each its OWN clock: the idiosyncratic debt amortises at a rate driven by own relative volume PLUS leave-one-out peer-basket volume (two ways out — attract flow or hedge in peers), the common debt only on basket-wide relative volume. The interaction is the edge: debt alone mis-times the unwind, and peer activity alone has no inventory to act on, but debt × channel-specific expected in-window repayment fraction tells you which names are actually scheduled to be repaired within exactly the next 6 bars, with the sign learned per channel by a robust pooled sign-slope shrunk with a per-name trailing beta.
factors.name: Hedge-clock split inventory debt with peer-paced repayment (h=6)

factors.trading_idea: Parent A identifies, from the whole trailing variance-ratio curve, *how large* and *how persistent* each name's transitory pricing error is (sigma_s, rho) but has no idea what caused the current displacement; Parent B identifies *who* pushed the price (accumulated tick-rule inventory converted to return units by a trailing impact elasticity) but has no idea what fraction of that push is transitory at all. The child uses A's estimates as an economic budget and clock for B's directional state: the dealer's inventory memory is set by the name's own estimated error half-life, the flow-attributed displacement lambda*Q is saturated in units of the identified pricing-error scale sigma_s (a push larger than the name's whole noise budget must be information, not inventory, so it is not faded), it is scaled by the transitory share of one-bar variance, and — the horizon fix — the fraction repaid inside the pinned 6-bar window is 1 - rho^{n_eff} with n_eff = 6 x (recent volume / normal volume), i.e. calendar decay rescaled onto the trade clock. The interaction carries edge neither parent has: A alone fades information-driven moves and over-weights slow errors whose IC only shows up at 24 bars, while B alone cannot tell an inventory overshoot from an informed sweep; ranking noise-budget-capped, volume-clock-accelerated inventory displacement isolates exactly the dislocations that are both transitory and clearable within 60 seconds.
factors.name: UC noise-budget capped inventory displacement with volume-clock repayment

factors.trading_idea: Dealers repay the transient impact of aggressive flow as *balancing volume arrives*, so the repayment clock is naturally set in volume time, not bar time: a per-name distributed-lag kernel estimated in bars therefore pools names/regimes whose relocation mass lands 2-3 bars out with those whose mass lands 12-15 bars out, and ranking their convolutions together at a fixed 6-bar offset averages a horizon-matched forecast with a horizon-mismatched one (exactly why the parent's IC peaked at 12 bars rather than 6). The child measures two state variables from the bounce-purged kernel itself — its mass-weighted repayment lag tau (centroid over lags 2..8, lag 1 discarded as mechanical quote bounce) and its sign coherence |sum psi| / sum|psi| — converts tau into an effective clock by dividing by the name's current relative trade intensity (repayment accelerates when volume arrives), and gates the horizon-matched convolution by how much of that clock actually fits inside 6 bars, zeroing slow-clock and incoherent-kernel names instead of forecasting them with a mismatched tail. Falsifiable: the child's IC profile should now peak at or before 6 bars and the gate must carry information — if fast-clock/high-coherence names do not repay faster, the child degenerates to a shrunken copy of the parent and its 6-bar IC will not improve. The edge survives arbitrage because capturing it means posting passive size against possibly-informed aggressive flow for a fraction of a spread: it is compensation for market-making inventory risk, which cannot be lifted directionally, and the per-name kernel sign is estimated rather than imposed so propagating names are forecast to continue.
factors.name: Volume-paced repayment-clock gate on the horizon-matched relocation kernel

factors.trading_idea: Parent B shows that liquidity is asymmetric and persistent: a sign-split square-root impact coefficient (|idio return| per sqrt(normalised dollar volume) on up bars vs down bars) tells you which side of the book is thin, but B fires on the state alone with no timing. Parent A supplies the clock — a pressure-driven displacement only pays back after the side-aligned Hawkes-style flow intensity has decayed off its own peak and price has lifted off the excursion extreme — but A's 'purity' (variance per unit participation) is direction-blind, so half of its supposedly mechanical bursts actually travelled into the *deep* side and kept going, which is the most likely reason its realized IC contradicted its declared reversal direction. The child fixes exactly that by making the vacuum measure side-resolved: a 12-bar displacement that travelled into the expensive/thin side (mechanical impact) AND whose side-aligned flow intensity has already decayed off its 30-bar peak is traded as a snapback, whereas a displacement that moved price *despite* paying cheap impact into a deep, absorbing side while its flow is still peaking is genuine information and is traded as continuation (amplified for levered names, where a down-move carries asset-value news). Neither parent can express this sign flip: A cannot tell which side was thin, B cannot tell whether the pressure has finished.
factors.name: Side-resolved impact vacuum × exhaustion switch

factors.trading_idea: Parent A measures *what is owed* — how far a name's live peer-relative valuation multiple (P/B, P/S, P/OCF) has dislocated from its own recent level, credible only inside tight, comparable peer groups — but it imposes reversion and its edge lives at slow horizons. Parent B measures *who is trading* — metronomic bar volume is a working VWAP/POV schedule that keeps repricing the name, bursty volume is one-off aggression whose displacement is transient overshoot — and it works as a conditioner rather than a standalone signal. The child estimates, per name and separately in the two volume-shape regimes, the trailing OLS loading of the realised 6-bar return on the comparability-gated multiple gap observed exactly 6 bars earlier, then folds the currently active regime's loading against the live gap. The interaction is the edge: in scheduled regimes the estimated loading is negative (the valuation gap is worked shut over the next minute), in bursty regimes it flips positive or dies (the gap was already slammed shut and over-paid), so the sign and the speed of closure are learned at the pinned 6-bar offset instead of assumed — something neither the valuation gap nor the volume fingerprint can deliver alone.
factors.name: Regime-conditional multiple-gap closure kernel

factors.trading_idea: Parent B showed that a standing peer-relative displacement reverts, but it fades every excursion identically, so its edge is diluted and only matures at 24 bars; Parent A showed (via its realised, sign-flipped IC) that within a bar the mid displacement that arrives *with* trades behaves differently from the displacement that arrives on quotes alone. The child therefore keeps Parent B's excursion object and its propagator remaining-decay-within-6-bars weight, but replaces the self-regression reversion coefficient with Parent A's trade-attribution measured over the *open excursion*: using a variable-length window that starts at the bar the peer-residual last sat at its anchor, it accumulates |u*g| (trade-backed displacement, g = v/(v+trailing mean v)) versus |u*(1-g)| (quiet quote-driven displacement) and forms the backing share phi. Unbacked excursions are dealer inventory skew / quote flicker with no information behind them and unwind fast, and the propagator kernel says that unwind is front-loaded at young ages — exactly inside the fixed 6-bar offset — whereas heavily trade-backed excursions are Kyle-permanent repricing plus a still-executing metaorder and must not be faded (their coefficient flips to continuation). The interaction is the edge: neither the age weight alone (which cannot tell an informed gap from a quote-noise gap) nor the trade split alone (which does not know whether the displacement is still standing, nor how much of its relaxation lands in the next minute) can decide *who* to fade and *how fast* the fade pays.
factors.name: Excursion backing-composition gated propagator fade

factors.trading_idea: Parent A knows *who* is standing on one side of the book (a 10b-18 repurchaser is a price-insensitive bid, a net issuer a standing offer) but measures the strength of that support only by crude relative volume; Parent B knows how to *measure* whether a resting queue was really absorbing flow (volume printed per unit of price displacement) but has no prior about which direction the hidden liquidity sits on. The child hinges the dislocation on corporate net share demand exactly as A, then scales it by B's absorption evidence: an idiosyncratic dip in a heavy repurchaser that occurred on heavy volume but small realised path (high volume-per-unit-displacement) is a corporate bid soaking up supply and snaps back within a minute, whereas the same dip on thin volume with a long price path is genuine adverse information and keeps going. The interaction is the edge: direction-known corporate flow tells you the sign of the latent liquidity, absorption tells you whether it is actually being exercised right now, and neither parent can separate a corporate-supported dislocation from an informational one alone.
factors.name: Corporate Bid/Offer Hinge Gated by Queue Absorption

factors.trading_idea: Both parents are really measuring the same latent state from opposite ends: Parent A downweights heavy bars because a dislocation printed into thin liquidity is permanent repricing, while Parent B's 'absorbed volume while pinned' is a direct proxy for a deep resting queue — and its realized sign was negative precisely because deep-queue levels are *defended*, so a print pushed off the local range centre gets pulled back rather than continuing. The child therefore measures the state variable itself — absorbed volume per unit of grid-quantum price movement (a trailing inverse-Kyle/queue-thickness estimate) — and uses it to SWITCH the sign of Parent A's range-centre endpoint dislocation: fade the dislocation in thick-queue names (transient penetration of a replenishing book, mean-reverts within a few bars) and ride it in thin-queue names (the same displacement there is genuine repricing that continues). The interaction carries edge neither parent has alone because Parent A's reversion is diluted by names where the displacement is informative, and Parent B mislabels defended levels as consumed queues; conditioning one on the other converts two weakly-signed effects into a single monotone signal at the fixed 6-bar offset.
factors.name: Queue-thickness-switched range-centre dislocation

factors.trading_idea: Treat each name's joint (price-deviation, activity-deviation) process as a 4-state cycle and ask whether it violates detailed balance: a reversible (equilibrium) chain has zero net probability current around the loop, while a driven one circulates in a definite direction. Positive circulation (quiet-low → active-low → active-high → quiet-high) means activity systematically LEADS price — liquidity demand is arriving before the repricing, the hallmark of a partially executed metaorder — whereas negative circulation means price leads activity, i.e. volume is reactive chasing whose impact is already paid. The Kolmogorov cycle affinity of the exponentially-weighted transition counts is a magnitude-free, outlier-immune estimate of that chirality, and under a locally rigid rotation of the loop the instantaneous predicted price velocity is proportional to (chirality × current activity deviation), largest on the 'loading' leg where price and activity deviations disagree in sign. The edge survives arbitrage because chirality is a slow per-name conditioning parameter estimated only from ordinal transition statistics (invisible to variance-, return- or dollar-volume-based screens), so a trader who reacts to volume surges without conditioning on it averages the accumulation and the chasing populations to roughly zero. Falsifiable: if loop chirality carries no information, the interaction has the same IC as the ungated activity-surge term alone and the factor is redundant with the book.
factors.name: Price-Activity Hysteresis Loop Chirality × Activity Surge

factors.trading_idea: Parent B showed that displacement printed in (near-)zero-volume bars continues while displacement paid for with volume reverts, but its 'quiet' leg still contains the decay tail of *earlier* trade impact and its 'active' leg shorts the whole traded drift regardless of how much of that impact has already bled off. Parent A supplies exactly the missing machinery — a Bouchaud power-law propagator G(l)=(1+l)^-0.5 with a per-name impact coefficient lambda — but applied it to an aggregate displacement, so its permanent/transient split was contaminated by mixing quiet and traded bars and its sign was contradicted. The child orthogonalises returns against the propagator *bar by bar* (e_t = r_t − lambda·dImpact_t, lambda fitted by trailing no-intercept OLS on traded bars only), then accumulates that innovation with a 6-bar-halflife decay over quiet bars only (pure quote-revision, permanent → continues) and separately shorts only the still-owed portion of embedded impact, lambda·Σ_l[G(l)−G(l+6)]f_{t−l}, which is the exact horizon-matched amount of transient impact scheduled to decay in the next 6 bars. The interaction carries edge neither parent has: the quiet leg is cleaned of impact-decay contamination that biases it against itself, the traded leg is age-weighted so fresh flow (which still owes reversal) is separated from stale flow (already repaid), and a concordance term up-weights names where the two independent mechanisms point the same way.
factors.name: Impact-orthogonalised quiet repricing vs kernel-owed transient decay

factors.trading_idea: The parent's realized (opposite) sign says the truth is simpler than its story: a mid sitting deep in the low-occupancy tail of its own recent price distribution is an *extended* excursion and snaps back, while a mid sitting on the occupancy mode is not extended and keeps drifting — the recurrence density was really measuring extremeness, not resting depth. What actually decides whether an excursion is owed back is whether inventory changed hands at the new level: I measure the volume local time (share of window volume traded within one bandwidth of the current log price) divided by the time local time (share of window bars spent there), a Laplace-smoothed ratio that equals 1 under uniform trading. A level reached on far less volume per unit time than the name's norm is a quote-driven, unpaid displacement (no counterparty absorbed it) and mean-reverts toward the occupancy median within a minute; a level reached on abnormally heavy volume per unit time has been paid for — real inventory was transferred at that price — so it is accepted and the displacement extends. The edge persists because it requires per-name nonparametric occupancy and volume-occupancy density estimated online at 10-second frequency for a few ticks per episode, and its cause (whether inventory transfer has occurred at a price) is a structural property of how books get repriced, not a mispricing that can be traded away.
factors.name: Volume-backing of the current price level splits excursion polarity

factors.trading_idea: Execution algorithms slice parent orders into child orders whose *sizes* live on a coarse lattice (round lots: multiples of 100, 500, 1000 shares), while HFT scalping, retail fragments and residual odd-lot prints are off-lattice; because a sum of round lots is still a round lot, bar volume inherits a detectable lattice signature that can be measured with the empirical characteristic function of volume at frequency 2*pi/L (a Rayleigh concentration statistic), debiased by its small-sample null 1/sqrt(m). A *rise* in that lattice concentration relative to the name's own longer baseline is evidence that a patient institutional parent order has just started working the book, and an unfinished metaorder mechanically extends its own price impact over the following minute, so drift printed while the lattice signature is fresh-high should continue, whereas the same drift printed under off-lattice (odd-lot / HFT) volume is transient inventory noise that decays. The edge survives arbitrage because nearly every quant pipeline normalises or log-transforms volume, destroying the integer lattice structure the signal reads, and monetising it requires paying spread on 60-second continuation — too thin for slow arbitrageurs but informative as a state variable. It is falsified if the interaction of drift with the lattice innovation carries no information beyond drift itself, or if the sign is negative (i.e. lattice-heavy flow marks completed rather than in-progress metaorders).
factors.name: Round-Lot Lattice Innovation Gate on Short-Run Drift

factors.trading_idea: A basket/program order displaces name i in proportion to cap-weight-per-depth (inverse turnover) rather than beta, so the mechanical push direction is the illiquidity-minus-beta wedge vector; applying a strictly-past shrunk precision matrix to that wedge (Sigma^-1 * wedge) expresses the push in the metric where it is arbitrage-cheap, i.e. concentrated in low-variance basket-spread directions that a stat-arb desk can close within seconds at almost no variance risk. Two changes make the mechanism live at the fixed 6-bar (60 s) offset: (i) the realised dislocation is measured over only the last 2 bars and only the part of it that is *confirmed* by the predicted push is faded (elementwise min of |realised| and |predicted|, same sign) — an unconfirmed move is treated as information, not mechanics; (ii) the fade is timed by the *derivative* of cross-sectional attribution concordance: while concordance is still rising the metaorder is still executing and the push keeps landing (ride it), whereas once concordance rolls over the program is finished and liquidity replenishment/spread closure delivers the snapback inside the next minute. The edge survives arbitrage because it requires joint real-time estimation of the precision matrix, the cap-weight-vs-dollar-volume tilt and per-name elasticity at 10-second resolution, and the payoff is a capacity-limited liquidity-provision premium bounded by displayed depth, not a free directional forecast.
factors.name: Whitened basket-push completion: confirmed over-push fade

factors.trading_idea: Parent B's beta catch-up wedge treats the whole shortfall between a name's beta-implied and realised move as an owed adjustment, but Parent A shows that shortfall has two origins with opposite futures: a flow-explained (transient impact) part that mechanically relaxes as the book refills, and a quiet unpaid-for (permanent) part that is genuine idiosyncratic repricing and keeps propagating. The child first strips the systematic component (beta x market move) from the 6-bar move, then projects the remaining idiosyncratic move onto an exponentially-decayed tick-rule-signed relative-volume flow kernel: the fitted part is transient, so its deficit is *doubly* owed (impact decay plus beta catch-up) and is bought; the orthogonal part is real news, so it is ridden rather than faded — resolving the sign conflict the two parents have over the permanent component. The interaction is the edge: the same measured wedge is bullish when flow-caused and information-bearing (hence non-mean-reverting) when quiet, and the whole repair clock is stretched by Parent B's slow-capital clientele score and market-shock switch, so the closure lands inside the fixed 6-bar horizon instead of leaking out to 12+ bars.
factors.name: Flow-Purged Beta Catch-Up vs Quiet Permanence, Clientele-Gated

factors.trading_idea: Sensitivity to mechanical basket/program pressure is a persistent *name* characteristic (index and basket membership, weight-per-depth, program footprint), not a per-bar market state, so the right attribution statistic is a trailing per-name regression of that name's precision-whitened dislocation on its own predicted weight-per-depth over-push — its correlation rho_i measures how reliably this particular name's low-variance-direction moves are mechanically caused. The parent instead collapsed attribution into one noisy cross-sectional R-squared per bar, which had to be smoothed over hundreds of bars and therefore only paid off far beyond the fixed offset. Second, transient impact relaxes fastest immediately after arrival (propagator decay is steepest at short age), so the object to fade is the *freshest* 2-bar predicted push, not a 6-bar cumulative push lagged 2 bars; fading the youngest transient in names where the push->dislocation coupling is validated puts the relaxation squarely inside 6 bars, while the component of the whitened dislocation orthogonal to each name's own predicted push is un-attributed information that keeps diffusing and is ridden as continuation. The edge survives arbitrage because supplying liquidity to inelastic basket demand is compensated risk concentrated exactly in low-turnover, thin-depth names, and because extracting it requires jointly estimating a shrunk cross-sectional precision matrix and a name-level attribution regression rather than a single tradable price pattern.
factors.name: Per-name push attribution: fresh transient fade vs un-attributed diffusion

factors.trading_idea: Parent A knows *when* the tape carries a capitalisation-weighted basket program and *which* names are mechanically over-pushed by it (inverse-turnover elasticity in excess of beta), but it applies one market-level displacement to every name and so cannot tell whether a given name actually absorbed the basket dollars yet. Parent B knows how to read that at the name-bar level: a displacement paid for with volume is transient impact that snaps back, while a displacement printed on a quiet bar is a dealer repricing his quotes ahead of flow that has not arrived.
