The child therefore beta-purges each name's return, weights every bar by the program-footprint intensity, and splits the resulting mechanical residual into a traded leg (basket dollars already absorbed → over-push relaxes) and a quiet leg (mid pulled along with the index while the name sat silent → the owed flow still has to arrive, so the drift completes), then scales the whole thing by the elasticity-minus-beta wedge that sets how large the mechanical push per basket dollar is. The interaction is the edge: neither the program flag nor the quiet/traded split alone tells you the *sign* of the coming move — only knowing that a high-elasticity name was pushed by a basket AND whether it has been paid yet does.
factors.name: Basket-footprint elasticity wedge, split by quiet vs traded participation

factors.trading_idea: Parent A shows that displacement from the trailing modal price (the occupancy mode of a leptokurtic, non-migrating value area) mean-reverts, but it decides whether a displacement is absorbable using raw volume level, which confounds absorption with aggression; Parent B shows that the informative state variable is size traded per unit of price movement (an inverse-Kyle-lambda depth proxy) — and its realized sign says that excursions accomplished on DEEP books (much volume, little movement) are the ones that get given back, while thin/vacuum moves persist.  The child therefore keeps A's occupancy-shape geometry (robust Crow-Siddiqui kurtosis of trailing prices + anchor stationarity, which identify a genuinely defended value area) and replaces A's volume-level gate with B's range-normalised state, measured as a leg-level Kyle lambda: total relative path travelled over the last ~90 seconds divided by volume consumed, percentile-ranked against the name's own recent history.  Low lambda means resting depth is absorbing and refilling around the mode, so the excursion snaps back; high lambda means the mid was repriced through a vacuum with almost no size cleared, leaving nothing to pull it back, so it continues — a continuous wedge whose forward sign flips with the state, which neither parent has (A only reverts, B has no value-area anchor and so applies the wedge to bars with no reference level).  Because the fixed 6-bar (one-minute) horizon is short, the wedge is further weighted by whether the predicted move is already in motion over the last 3 bars, which pulls the response into the first minute instead of the 2–4 minute band where A's plain snapback peaked.
factors.name: Occupancy-anchored excursion lambda permanence wedge

factors.trading_idea: A name's response to a market-wide innovation is completed in *trade time*, not calendar time: price only re-prices when quotes/trades arrive, so the calendar-time lag of the catch-up is roughly the inverse of the name's current trade-arrival intensity. The parent measured the outstanding systematic debt correctly (its residual IC was real) but let repayment run on wall-clock lags, so most of the mass landed after the fixed 6-bar offset (IC peaked at 12). This child keeps the prewhitened market innovation and the lag-vs-contemporaneous beta wedge (Hou/Lo-MacKinlay delayed response, undelivered mass = long-run aggregated beta minus contemporaneous beta) but multiplies it by an explicit exponential delivery fraction 1-exp(-lambda_i*6) whose hazard lambda_i scales with the name's *current* trade intensity and trade-arrival frequency relative to its own norm — so only the debt that will actually be repaid inside the next six bars is scored. It is falsifiable: if adjustment is calendar-time rather than event-time, the intensity gate adds nothing and the IC will stay flat/late; the edge survives arbitrage because it requires jointly estimating a per-name long-run beta wedge and holding through a state-dependent, activity-conditional repayment clock, which is unattractive to latency-arbitrage capital and invisible to slower cross-sectional models.
factors.name: Event-clock delivery of the undelivered beta response

factors.trading_idea: Parent A shows a name's live log-multiple spread versus its industry peers dislocates and reverts, but it hard-codes an exponential comparability gate and its edge lives at 24 bars, not at the 6-bar offset this run scores; parent B shows that a pooled cross-sectional regression of the realised forward 6-bar move on the lagged impulse lets the tape calibrate reversion speed at the exact horizon, but it applies that machinery to a beta-hedged price residual with a volume/R-squared grid. The child feeds A's multiple-space peer spread — split into a fast (deviation from a 2.5-minute EWMA) and a slow (2.5-minute vs 20-minute EWMA) component — into B's pooled estimator, fitting a trailing bivariate no-intercept response surface of the realised 6-bar forward spread change on both components separately inside each cell of a 2x2 grid of A's own state variable (tight vs wide within-industry multiple dispersion) crossed with B's (heavy vs light 3-bar volume shock), each cell shrunk to the all-observation pooled fit. The interaction is the edge: A's comparability gate becomes a measured, sign-flexible loading rather than an assumed damping, and because the fit is anchored on the realised 6-bar change the estimator automatically up-weights whichever of the fast/slow dislocation components actually pays at the fixed 6-bar offset — fixing A's horizon mismatch — while giving B a valuation-space impulse that needs no per-name beta hedge and therefore survives in thin, poorly-hedgeable names.
factors.name: Comparability-cell pooled horizon-matched multiple dislocation

factors.trading_idea: A market-wide shock creates a per-name *backlog* of undelivered beta response, but the parent showed the backlog of the slowest (deepest income-clientele) names is repaid mostly after 6 bars, so a monotone slow-capital tilt mis-matches a fixed 6-bar offset. The child therefore estimates each name's own repayment rate directly and causally: a trailing OLS of realised 6-bar idiosyncratic return on the shock-conditioned backlog observed 6 bars earlier gives theta, the fraction of backlog actually delivered inside exactly one forecast horizon; theta is shrunk toward the pooled mean of its payout-clientele tercile (slow-capital groups share a delay parameter, so pooling is the right prior), and the forecast is theta x current backlog. Delivery also needs someone to trade, so the signal is scaled by a Hawkes-style exponential trade-arrival intensity relative to the name's normal volume. The edge should persist because it requires estimating a name-specific, overlapping-sample response kernel on second-scale data for names whose marginal holders (insurers, income sleeves) do not re-optimise intraday — low capacity, small per-trade payoff, unattractive to fast liquidity takers. Falsified if theta-weighted backlog predicts no better at 6 bars than the raw backlog, or if the arrival-intensity scaling adds nothing (that would mean delivery-rate heterogeneity is noise, not a real clientele/attention parameter).
factors.name: Self-Calibrated Delivery-Rate Beta Backlog

factors.trading_idea: The parent imposed the sign of the return-x-volume interaction from stale quarterly opacity characteristics and the realized IC came out backwards, because at a 10-second horizon those characteristics mostly proxy thin-book impact capacity, not information asymmetry: in small/opaque names a volume-backed displacement is largely transient price impact that decays, while in liquid names the same displacement is efficient information incorporation that continues. Rather than re-guessing which characteristic sets the sign, this child estimates the LMSW interaction coefficient itself, per name and causally: it regresses the realized 6-bar peer-residual return that followed each past interaction observation (available only 6 bars later, so no look-ahead) on that interaction, over a multi-hour trailing window, and relays the cross-sectionally demeaned coefficient onto today's interaction term. The falsifiable claim is that the per-name interaction coefficient is persistent over hours — if it is pure noise the factor earns zero regardless of the underlying reversal/continuation balance. The edge survives arbitrage because it harvests cross-sectional heterogeneity in the transient-vs-permanent impact split (demeaning removes the pooled reversal everyone trades), requires a per-name second-moment estimate joined to 10-second flow, and leaves only idiosyncratic peer-hedged risk.
factors.name: Self-calibrated LMSW interaction-coefficient relay

factors.trading_idea: The parent's realized IC was the opposite of its declared sign, and that reversal is exactly what propagator/transient-impact theory predicts: the part of a 60-second mid displacement that is *explained* by contemporaneous aggressive flow is mostly transitory price impact, which decays as the book refills (Bouchaum-style propagator decay, Kyle-Obizhaeva resiliency), while the part of the displacement with *no* flow behind it is market-makers repricing quotes on information and is permanent, so it continues. This child therefore decomposes each name's 6-bar log displacement into a flow-explained component (own trailing Kyle lambda from a rolling OLS of bar returns on signed square-root volume) and an unexplained residual, and predicts continuation of the residual but decay of the flow-explained part. The genuinely new conditioning variable is metaorder persistence: the trailing lag-1 autocorrelation of signed flow, which distinguishes a one-off aggressive print (impact reverts fast) from a self-exciting, sign-persistent execution schedule still being worked (impact keeps pushing) — so the coefficient on the impact component is gated from -1 to +1 by cross-sectional rank of flow autocorrelation. The edge persists because it requires per-name impact calibration plus a metaorder detector to avoid being run over while fading dislocations, and the per-trade profit is a fraction of the spread, so it is capacity-limited rather than arbitraged away. Falsified if the impact component predicts continuation regardless of flow autocorrelation (gate useless), or if the flow-unexplained residual reverts rather than continues.
factors.name: Transient trade impact vs quiet repricing, metaorder-persistence gated

factors.trading_idea: Algebraically, the bar's end-price displacement from its own traded range centre is exactly ((H+L)/2 - C)/(H-L) = (w - b)/2, where w is Parent A's shadow asymmetry and b is the retained body: so the body enters the displacement *linearly with a negative coefficient*, which is why Parent A's discrete confirmed-minus-absorbed split (followed by orthogonalising the body away) inverted its own sign, while Parent B's body-blind w kept only half the displacement. The child measures the body-corrected, volume-gated probe displacement and then lets Parent B's occupancy state arbitrate its sign: when the trailing occupancy law of the mid is sharply peaked (high IDR/IQR) and its modal anchor is not migrating, resting depth exists to absorb the displacement and the mid snaps back toward the traded centroid; when the occupancy core is diffuse and the anchor is walking, the same heavy-volume bar is a working metaorder repricing the level, so the permanent body component continues instead. The interaction is the edge: Parent A fires on every heavy-volume wick with no knowledge of whether depth can absorb it (hence its pooled, contradicted sign), Parent B knows the book state but reads a body-blind displacement and only reaches full strength at 24 bars — conditioning the correctly-signed fast displacement on occupancy sharpness selects the absorbable displacements at the 6-bar horizon and routes the non-absorbable ones into the opposite (continuation) channel rather than diluting them.
factors.name: Occupancy-arbitrated body-corrected probe displacement

factors.trading_idea: Both parents' realized signs agree on one story once B's declared polarity is corrected: displacement that aggressive volume actually PAID for over the last minute is transient square-root-law impact and snaps back, while price motion that was probed-but-not-converted (wicks on heavy-volume bars) or revised without commensurate volume is incomplete discovery and continues. The child makes the switch between these two regimes a measured state variable that neither parent can build alone: c = |volume-paid net displacement| / (|volume-paid net displacement| + probed-but-unconverted excursion path), both expressed in the name's own robust tick-grid quantum, so c is literally the fraction of the paid path that got converted into a net move. Low c (size absorbed, wicks left behind) loads the continuation side, and there the unpaid mid-revision channel is only trusted when its sign is CONCORDANT with the volume-backed probed side — a mid drifting toward where aggression already reached is stale-quote catch-up, whereas an unpaid drift pointing away from the probes is Roll flicker and is down-weighted; high c (clean sweep, path fully converted) loads against the paid displacement. The interaction is the edge: parent A cannot see which part of the move was paid for, parent B cannot see the excursion that was never converted, and only their ratio identifies which of the two opposite-signed regimes the name is in at the fixed 6-bar offset.
factors.name: Conversion-gated paid/unpaid displacement with probe concordance

factors.trading_idea: At 10-second sampling a name's idiosyncratic return is not white noise plus a one-lag bid/ask bounce: market-maker inventory unwinding and metaorder slicing impose a quasi-periodic (damped-harmonic) component, i.e. an AR(2) pole pair rather than a single decay rate. Fitting AR(2) by Yule-Walker on trailing Huberized autocovariances of market-demeaned returns recovers that oscillator, and iterating its conditional-mean recursion six steps forward converts the *phase* of the cycle into a signed forecast — so the signal's sign flips with where the name sits in its own liquidity cycle, not with the sign of its recent return (this is what distinguishes it from momentum or plain reversal, and is directly falsifiable: replacing the recursion with -r_t should destroy the IC, and the IC should concentrate in names whose fitted discriminant phi1^2+4*phi2 is negative, i.e. genuinely complex poles). The edge survives arbitrage because the resonance frequency and damping drift with the liquidity regime (so no static filter or fixed-lag reversal captures it), each per-name forecast amplitude is of the order of the spread, and monetising it therefore requires simultaneous, capacity-limited cross-sectional aggregation of hundreds of tiny phase bets rather than one tradeable dislocation.
factors.name: AR(2) resonance-phase multistep idiosyncratic cycle forecast

factors.trading_idea: The parent's evaluation says the direction is inverted, and the inversion has a single microstructural explanation: at a 60-second offset a displacement that landed on a *fresh* (never recently occupied) price level keeps going rather than reverting, because resting limit-order supply is rebuilt only at levels the mid has repeatedly revisited — a fresh level is by construction a thin, untested book, so continuing flow walks the mid further, while a habitual (high local-time) level is a deep, repeatedly-refilled band that absorbs and snaps the deviation back. The second, independent read on the same latent state is whether the flow that caused the displacement is still running: modelling each name's bar-level activity indicator as a two-state Markov chain gives a horizon-matched survival probability p11^6 (the chance the burst persists over exactly the 6-bar forecast offset), which is high while a metaorder is still slicing and low once it has terminated. Averaging the two state estimates and multiplying by the beta-purged 6-bar idiosyncratic displacement therefore rides displacement where the book is thin and the flow is alive, and fades it where the level is habitual and the flow is dead. The edge survives arbitrage because capturing it requires paying the spread into a thin book while competing with the very metaorder that creates the drift — it is economically available mainly to participants already resting in the queue, so it is not competed away by signal-only arbitrageurs.
factors.name: Burst-survival routed fresh-level displacement

factors.trading_idea: Hardiman–Bouchaud show the branching ratio of a self-exciting (Hawkes) activity process can be read straight off the dispersion of event counts: Var(N_T)/E(N_T) → 1/(1-n)^2, so n̂ = 1 - 1/sqrt(Fano). That number measures *endogeneity*: when n̂ is near critical, current activity is mostly self-generated echo of its own recent flow (Filimonov–Sornette excess volatility), so trade-validated displacement is liquidity-demand noise that unwinds within a minute; when n̂ is low the same volume is exogenously driven (news/portfolio decisions) and the displacement is information that keeps being pushed by the remainder of the metaorder. The child therefore keeps the parent's fundamentally-defined valuation-tier peer map (the source of its independence) and its traded/quiet participation split, but replaces the fast/slow intensity *level* switch — which measures only that flow is elevated, not whether it is self-referential — with the reflexivity estimate n̂ from the count-dispersion (variance-time) curve, and scales the quiet-quote fade by the same reflexivity because unbacked quote skew in a reflexive regime is pure echo. The edge persists because harvesting it means taking the other side of near-critical, potentially cascading endogenous flow at 10-second latency inside fundamentally-comparable cells: the risk is exactly the crash-prone state, and the estimator needs multi-scale count statistics no fast desk prices. Falsifiable: the forward coefficient on trade-validated peer-residual displacement must flip sign across the cross-sectional median of n̂, and conditioning on n̂ must beat conditioning on the raw intensity level.
factors.name: Fano-branching reflexivity switch on traded vs quiet peer displacement

factors.trading_idea: A liquidity-provision pricing error is not repaid by the passage of calendar time but by the arrival of offsetting trade flow: the market maker sheds inventory (and the mid returns to the efficient price) only as counter-flow arrives, so the AR(1) decay of the transitory error is naturally indexed by volume time, exp(-kappa * u), not by bar count. The parent identified the error in calendar time, which is why its reversal was only fully repaid by ~24 bars; replacing the calendar clock with each name's own volume clock and self-calibrating kappa from the trailing predictive regression of returns on the volume-decayed displacement moves the repayment mass to precisely those names whose expected trade arrival over the next six bars is large enough to clear the dislocation inside the pinned horizon. The gain 1 - exp(-kappa * 6 * E[u]) is the fraction of the current displacement that the volume clock predicts will be repaid within exactly 6 bars, so the cross-section is sorted by *horizon-matched* expected reversal rather than by total eventual reversal. The edge survives arbitrage because harvesting it means taking the inventory the liquidity provider is shedding, and because the ranking needs two name-specific latent objects — the decay rate per unit of traded volume and the forecast of near-term volume arrival — that a pooled tick-reversal or calendar-horizon factor cannot see.
factors.name: Volume-clock repayment-rate identified transitory reversal (6-bar gain)

factors.trading_idea: Whoever absorbed the last few minutes of liquidity-taking flow is now carrying inventory, and the direction of their *closing* trade is fixed by the sign of that inventory (net taker buying ⇒ makers are short and must eventually buy back), while the *timing* is governed by their mark-to-market: an intermediary sitting on a paper profit closes fast (seconds-to-a-minute), whereas one sitting on a loss holds and instead lets the book refill, so the price relaxes back against the flow. I therefore estimate, per name, an exponentially-decayed taker inventory (tick-rule signed volume, decay matched to the 6-bar horizon), an average maker fill price using the bar's upper/lower half excursion (so the earned spread is inside the P&L), and combine flow imbalance with the maker's per-share unrealised P&L in volatility units: positive product = absorbed flow held at a profit, predicting continuation in the flow direction; negative product = a run-away move that left makers underwater, predicting propagator-style relaxation against the flow. The edge should survive arbitrage because harvesting it means standing in front of the intermediary's unwind inside one minute (an inventory-risk, not an information, premium), and because it is an interaction of imbalance with a path-dependent P&L state rather than any level of price, flow or volatility that crowded momentum/reversal books already span.
factors.name: Market-maker inventory mark-to-market unwind pressure

factors.trading_idea: Parent A shows that drift printed in (near-)zero-volume bars continues while drift paid for with aggressive volume decays, but it treats every quiet-bar path as equally informative; Parent B shows that a given amount of drift is only self-sustaining when it is *grind-carried* (sign-persistent relative to the Rice/Gaussian null arccos(rho)/pi) rather than *jump-carried* (magnitude-concentrated). The child estimates the Rice sign-flip gap separately on the quiet-bar increment subsequence and on the active-bar increment subsequence, then goes long quiet drift only when the quiet path is a grind (a market maker walking his quotes tick-by-tick on inventory/adverse-selection beliefs, which keeps walking) and fades active drift most aggressively when the traded path is jump-like (a vacuum print that overshot thin depth). The interaction carries edge neither parent has alone because it removes exactly the falsification Parent A feared — a single stale-mid gap in a quiet bar is jump-like and gets zero weight instead of being read as repricing — and it gives Parent B's scale-free sign null a conditioning state (traded vs untraded) that separates persistent quote revision from mechanically decaying impact, letting the signal act on the freshest few bars and therefore bite at the fixed 6-bar offset.
factors.name: Quiet-Quote Grind vs Traded-Jump Rice Gate

factors.trading_idea: A multi-bar pin of the mid on one grid level is a *defended level*: a large, repeatedly refreshed queue sits at the touch. Two very different things can end the pin — (a) an aggressive metaorder eats the queue, in which case the step off the level is mostly the transient impact of that burst and the patient provider re-posts, pulling the mid back (Bouchaud propagator: isolated-burst impact largely decays); or (b) nobody trades and the quote is simply relocated, a pure quote-driven fair-value update that tends to stick. The volume absorbed *while the mid was pinned* separates the two, and the parent's evidence supports this reading: the parent up-weighted heavily-absorbed breaks with a saturating gate and realized reversal, not continuation. The child therefore keeps the absorption machinery but converts it from a *level* into a *contrast*: at each bar the absorption rank is centred across simultaneous break events and the resulting signed impulse is cross-sectionally orthogonalized against the raw signed break displacement, so the signal carries (by construction) zero loading on the generic short-term-reversal factor the book already spans, and expresses only the differential 'traded-clearing reverts vs untraded-repricing persists' effect. It survives arbitrage because each event is worth a fraction of a tick and lives in low-turnover, grid-bound names where capturing it means crossing a spread at least one tick wide; it is falsified if, among same-bar breaks of the same direction, high-absorption and zero-absorption breaks show the same 6-bar forward IC.
factors.name: Absorption-contrast pin-break snapback (displacement-orthogonal)

factors.trading_idea: The parent had the right state variable (local time of a hedged relative-value spread) but the wrong polarity, and the report's sign contradiction tells us which way it actually runs: over 60 seconds a spread that has walked into territory where almost no inventory has changed hands continues, because the escape itself is evidence of an unabsorbed, self-exciting order-flow cluster and queues need tens of seconds to replenish; whereas a spread loitering on a level where a large share of the name's recent dollar volume was transacted sits inside an accepted value area defended by the inventory of everyone who traded there, so the last few ticks are bid-ask/Epps noise that reverts. The child therefore measures occupation in *dollar volume at the level* (market-profile value-area share) rather than in bar count — the mechanism is absorbed inventory, not time spent — and uses that vacuum score to switch the sign on the short-run spread innovation and to gate a Hawkes-style signed-flow excitation ratio (short-halflife signed dollar-flow imbalance scaled by its own clustering intensity), which is only ridden where there is no nearby attractor to absorb it. The edge survives arbitrage because the sign is state-dependent (unconditional reversal and unconditional order-flow-imbalance traders take the other side in exactly the wrong states) and because the payoff concentrates in thin, low-volume-node regions where price impact caps deployable capital.
factors.name: Volume-at-level vacuum routing of flow excitation

factors.trading_idea: Under a Bouchaud propagator G(t)=(1+t/t0)^-beta the return expected over the NEXT h bars from a past impulse of size e at lag l is e·[G(l+h)-G(l)] — a kernel whose mass sits almost entirely on impulses aged 0-8 bars, whereas the standing displacement (the parent's object) is dominated by old impulses whose remaining relaxation leaks out over many minutes, which is exactly why the parent's IC peaked at 24 bars. The child therefore convolves the *increment* sequence of peer-relative log returns with the horizon-differenced kernel K(l)=G(l+h)-G(l), so the predictor is horizon-matched to h=6 by construction. Each impulse is additionally *marked* by its own liquidity signature: price moves achieved on abnormally little volume (high instantaneous Kyle-lambda vs the name's own 240-bar norm) are quote-driven liquidity vacuums that refill within seconds and get the full relaxation kernel, while moves absorbed by abnormally heavy volume are informed/metaorder-driven and get a small positive continuation kernel instead. The edge survives arbitrage because it pays a few basis points per event on a 60-second clock and requires simultaneous peer-basket hedging and volume-conditioned marking; the arbitrageurs who warehouse the relative-value gap are paid on the slow multi-minute leg, not on the first minute's front-loaded slice.
factors.name: Vacuum-marked propagator increment kernel (h=6)

factors.trading_idea: Parent A treated every heavily-absorbed pin break as a queue-clearing event that should continue, and the data flatly contradicted it; Parent B supplies the missing state variable that explains why. A mid slipping off a grid level on which large volume has already printed is, in most names, a momentary depth depletion at the touch — the makers who were absorbing there simply re-post, so the beta-residual break snaps back; it is genuine repricing only in names whose price motion is actually flow-driven, i.e. whose active-bar no-intercept impact regression of volatility-standardised returns on tick-signed sqrt-volume has a high uncentred R-squared. The child therefore uses B's active-sample impact R-squared rank as a polarity switch on A's absorption-gated, beta-residual pin-break displacement (continuation at the top of the R-squared cross-section, refill snapback below), and scales the whole impulse by a Hawkes arrival hazard of the next trade inside the 6-bar window, because a depleted queue can only be refilled or re-cleared by flow that actually arrives. The interaction is what neither parent has: A had absorption size but no way to tell a real clearing from a refillable dent, B had informativeness but no queue-size event to condition on and no notion of the price grid.
factors.name: Absorbed-queue refill hazard polarity break relay

factors.trading_idea: Bouchaud's propagator says the price impact of a trade decays as a power law G(l)=(1+l/l0)^-beta, so the return expected over the NEXT h bars from flow that has ALREADY executed is exactly the kernel's decay increment, sum_k f_{t-k}[G(k+h)-G(k)] — a quantity whose weights are largest for freshly executed flow and ~0 for flow already relaxed, which is why it is intrinsically horizon-matched (the parent projected a stale 12-bar displacement and therefore peaked at 12 bars, not at the fixed 6-bar offset). Crucially, unrelaxed impact only actually relaxes if the metaorder that created it has stopped: while flow is being self-excited (Hawkes clustering) the book keeps being walked and impact is continually replenished, so I discount the predicted decay by a relative continuation-intensity measure of same-direction flow in the last few bars. The signal therefore uses no price-displacement level at all — only the *age profile* and *liveness* of signed flow — which makes it nearly orthogonal to the crowded reversal/momentum and quiet-vs-traded-split families, and the edge survives arbitrage because harvesting it means supplying liquidity into the tail of someone else's execution, a capacity-limited, inventory-risky trade rather than a free statistical bet.
factors.name: Horizon-matched propagator decay increment, flow-extinction gated

factors.trading_idea: A name whose price absorbs market-wide information with a distributed lag owes a known amount of catch-up, but the parent's version mis-specified the *phase* of that debt in two ways: it truncated the response kernel at the horizon (so debts owed from shocks 7-12 bars old — precisely the ones landing inside the next 6 bars for slow repricers — were invisible) and it estimated lag loadings against raw market returns, so serially-correlated index returns and bid-ask bounce leaked negative, fast-reverting loadings that spent their predictive mass within one bar. The child whitens the market to an AR(1) innovation series (making the dropped future market terms exactly mean-zero and the per-lag loadings consistent estimates of the impulse response), projects the estimated kernel onto the non-negative cone (delivery mass cannot be negative; negative estimates are bounce noise), extends it to 12 lags, and folds each loading against exactly the observed market-innovation window that maps into bars t+1..t+6. Crucially the debt must be *payable inside the window*: the fold is scaled by the probability that the name's mid updates at least once in 6 bars (1-(1-u)^6 from its trailing update rate), so the signal peaks at intermediate-latency names — slow enough to still owe, fast enough to pay — instead of the ultra-stale names whose delivery lands at 12-24 bars (exactly where the parent's IC turned negative). The edge survives arbitrage because the payoff requires per-name distributed-lag estimation plus a delivery-feasibility model, and the names that owe most are thin and slow, so taking liquidity for size in them costs more than the few basis points of catch-up.
factors.name: Innovation-whitened extended-lag delivery fold with feasibility weight

factors.trading_idea: A firm actually executing a 10b-18 repurchase is an anonymous, passive, one-sided buyer that must bid at or below the last independent bid and is size-capped near 25% of ADV, so its footprint is not a single bounce but a *persistent state*: over minutes, sell volume gets absorbed cheaply (small price move per unit dollar traded) while buy volume still pays full impact. The child therefore replaces the parent's one-shot dip impulse — which decayed by 6 bars because it was a re-labelled reversal — with a slow-moving, sign-split Kyle/square-root impact coefficient (mean |idio return| per sqrt(normalised dollar volume) on down bars vs up bars) estimated over 30 minutes, and interacts that asymmetry with the firm's repurchase capacity (quarterly buyback dollars per day divided by daily dollar volume, plus share-count shrinkage) and with distance below the 65-minute volume-weighted anchor where VWAP-benchmarked desks lean hardest. Falsifiable: the positive interaction must vanish for names whose repurchase dollars are ~zero, and the mirror-image asymmetry (upside cheap) must carry no predictive drift for high-capacity names; every main effect (asymmetry, capacity, anchor gap, 6-bar reversal and its downside part) is cross-sectionally purged so only the interaction can score. The edge persists because it requires joining a quarterly cash-flow-statement item to 10-second sign-conditional impact estimates, buyback flow is untagged on the tape, and the absorbing capacity itself is finite and non-securitisable, so arbitrage cannot compete it away.
factors.name: Repurchase-capacity-gated signed impact asymmetry

factors.trading_idea: Parent B showed that each name's 6-bar impulse response is a mixture of quote-noise (negative lag-1 kernel) and informed order-splitting (positive kernel), with the mixture weight switching on a crude volume regime; Parent A showed that the true state variable is directional — one side of the book can be persistently absorbed (small square-root impact per unit dollar traded) while the other pays full impact. The child conditions B's per-name sign-persistence kernel on A's *signed* absorption state: bars whose move points into the cheaply-absorbed side are liquidity-provision noise and should recoil, while bars pushing into the expensive side are information that keeps travelling, so the kernel is estimated separately for cheap-side and expensive-side conditioning bars, EB-shrunk to the pooled kernel, arcsine-inverted and geometrically summed over exactly six steps. The interaction carries edge neither parent has: A's asymmetry was only a slow level (and was crippled by a stale quarterly gate, hence its sign flip), B's regime was sign-symmetric and therefore averaged the absorbed and unabsorbed directions together; a small bounded buyback-yield tilt keeps A's economic story that persistent one-sided absorption is often a real repurchase program, without letting a quarterly field drive the signal.
factors.name: Absorption-side-conditioned sign-kernel recoil

factors.trading_idea: Algorithmic execution and market-maker inventory cycles stamp short, repeating symbolic motifs onto the sequence of idiosyncratic 10-second repricings (slice-slice-pause, push-push-pullback, quiet-quiet-jump), so the conditional mean of the NEXT 60 seconds of peer-relative return is a nonlinear function of the last few repricing symbols rather than of the standing displacement level. The parent imposed a fixed power-law propagator on a displacement LEVEL, which is a slow state variable and therefore delivered its information at 24 bars; the child instead estimates the horizon-matched conditional expectation directly — a causal variable-order Markov (context-tree, order 3→2→1 backoff with cross-sectional empirical-Bayes pooling) table of forward 6-bar residual return keyed on the current ternary motif — so the object being forecast is by construction the 6-bar offset, and names whose own table says 'continue' keep their sign instead of being force-faded. Predictions are weighted by the lag-1 mutual information of the name's own symbol stream (a compressibility / predictable-structure gate): only names whose repricing process is measurably mechanical are trusted. The edge survives arbitrage because the motifs are name-specific, non-stationary and low-Sharpe per event, and capturing them requires estimating a nonlinear discrete conditional expectation that linear factor books cannot span; falsified if (a) collapsing to order-1 context (or to the imposed reversal sign) leaves the 6-bar IC unchanged, (b) low-mutual-information names forecast as well as high-MI ones, or (c) the IC term structure again peaks at 24 bars rather than at or before 6.
factors.name: Variable-order symbolic motif drift (MI-gated)

factors.trading_idea: The parent inferred a lag-by-lag repayment kernel and then extrapolated it into a 6-bar forecast; because the kernel mixed fast quote-bounce with slow inventory absorption, its predictive mass actually landed near 12 bars. The child estimates the *same* economic object — the relocation still owed on trade-backed pushes — with a direct h-step projection: the realized 6-bar idiosyncratic return is regressed causally (with a 6-bar lag) on two orthogonalised state variables, the freshest trade-backed push (which carries mechanical bid-ask/queue bounce) and the *unpaid balance* of older pushes (age 1-5 bars, credited with the relocations already realised since each push). Forming the signal from the partial coefficient on the unpaid balance only means bounce is absorbed as a control rather than dropped by fiat, so what remains is genuine inventory debt whose repayment is, by construction of the estimand, timed to the fixed 6-bar offset; a rolling R2-based trust weight makes the factor a state variable that is loud only where the flow-repayment relation currently holds. The edge survives arbitrage because collecting it requires posting passive size against possibly-informed aggressive flow for a fraction of a spread (dealer inventory risk, not a directional mispricing), and because the per-name sign is estimated, so names whose flow propagates rather than reverts are forecast to continue.
factors.name: Unpaid inventory balance, direct 6-bar projection (bounce partialled)

factors.trading_idea: A 6-bar displacement is followed by snapback when it was produced by inventory/quote pressure on ordinary flow, and by continuation when it was produced by informed metaorder flow, so the informative object is the *differential* slope of forward return on displacement across flow-intensity groups — not the 18-cell nonparametric surface the parent fitted. The parent's cells were badly unbalanced (large displacement co-occurs with large volume), so its unweighted ANOVA double-centring did NOT project out the marginals: a share of the huge displacement main effect (reversal) survived inside the 'interaction' with distorted weighting, which is the most likely reason its realized IC sign contradicted the declared one. This child estimates the same interaction in a design that is balanced by construction (cross-sectional flow terciles, so equal cell mass every bar), removes both marginals exactly (within-group demeaning of the state plus a row-wise projection of the final signal out of displacement), collapses 18 noisy cells into three pooled slopes for statistical power, and trades only the part of the slope differential on which a fast (300-bar) and a slow (1200-bar) exponentially-weighted estimate agree in sign. The edge should persist because production alpha books hold sign-fixed additive reversal and liquidity terms; a state-dependent slope *difference* is orthogonal to both marginals by construction and must be re-estimated online, so it is not spanned by static, sign-fixed factors.
factors.name: Balanced flow-tercile differential reversal slope

factors.trading_idea: Parent B says the transitory (basket-flow-pushed plus flow-unbacked 'quiet') part of a name's industry-demeaned valuation-multiple dislocation is what snaps back, while Parent A says how much of any owed push actually resolves is set by business time — the volume the next six bars are forecast to trade. The child fuses them non-additively: the transitory dislocation is first re-weighted by Parent A's still-owed × deliverable share (min(owed volume-clock weight, Hawkes-style forecast volume rate)) and then HARD-CLIPPED to the maximum price move six bars of forecast flow can physically produce, cap = lambda · 6 · E[|f|] · directional-efficiency, expressed in the same trailing return-sd units as the dislocation itself. The interaction is the edge: Parent B fades dislocations that are too large to be repaired inside the fixed 6-bar offset (hence its IC keeps growing to 24 bars), and Parent A shrinks its whole leg differential with no idea of where the snap-back target is or how big the repair must be — only the clip of a valuation-anchored repair distance by a Kyle-lambda × forecast-volume capacity gives a signal whose realizable component is matched to exactly six bars, while the informed idiosyncratic-flow leg is followed with a forecast-rate (not owed-capped) weight because continuation needs fresh flow, not worked-off flow.
factors.name: Delivery-capped flow-attributed valuation repair

factors.trading_idea: Christensen-Oomen-Renò show that locally explosive drift ('drift bursts') can be measured as a kernel-weighted drift over a HAC (Newey-West) volatility, and that some bursts are news-driven (they persist) while others are pure liquidity gaps (they snap back). The discriminator I use is the *texture of the path that produced the burst*, taken directly from the HAC correction term: when the Bartlett-weighted return autocovariance of the burst window is unusually positive relative to the name's own recent norm, the move was built by persistent, order-splitting (informed) flow and should continue; when it is unusually negative, the move was built out of bounce/quote-flicker noise against thin depth and should revert. Because the same autocovariance object both corrects the variance estimate and classifies the burst, the signal is an interaction (burst size x noise-regime excess) rather than a directional drift bet, which is why it should act as a state/conditioning variable in a book. It survives arbitrage because market makers condition on inventory, spread and order-flow imbalance, not on a kernel drift t-stat multiplied by its own HAC-correction anomaly; falsification is direct — if drift bursts revert (or persist) irrespective of the sign of the autocovariance excess, the interaction IC collapses to zero.
factors.name: Drift-burst t-stat flipped by noise-regime excess

factors.trading_idea: The parent's confirmed result — purging the valuation-neighbourhood-common part of a hedged residual raises the reversal IC — logically implies that the discarded component is not noise but a *tier-level* re-rating whose closure requires trading a whole valuation neighbourhood simultaneously, so it cannot be arbitraged on a one-minute clock and should therefore CONTINUE rather than revert. The child trades both halves of the same decomposition with opposite signs: it fades the name-specific (doubly-orthogonalised) impulse, scaled by hedgeability, and simultaneously follows the name's fitted exposure to its neighbourhood's own residual factor over a slower 12-bar window, scaled by neighbourhood coherence (the share of the name's hedged-residual variance the cluster factor actually explains), because in loose neighbourhoods that 'factor' is estimation noise and carries no information. The edge persists because the reversal leg is capacity-capped single-name inventory pressure while the continuation leg requires simultaneous execution across an entire point-in-time-fundamental valuation tier — expensive for microstructure arbitrageurs and invisible to anyone not joining quarterly per-share fundamentals to a 10-second tape.
factors.name: Tier-common continuation vs idiosyncratic snapback split

factors.trading_idea: Parent A shows that mid displacement accumulated since a name's last trade, gated by the probability the next order arrives inside the horizon, is *confirmed* rather than reversed; Parent B shows that weighting that same displacement by excess path efficiency over the k^(-1/2) random-walk null flips the realized sign. The reconciliation is mechanical: inside a silent window near-unit efficiency is produced almost exclusively by a SINGLE uncorroborated quote relocation (one tick, then nothing), i.e. a stale-mid artifact with no repeated maker commitment, and that snaps back the moment flow finally tests it — whereas sub-null / moderate efficiency means many successive small quote updates travelling the same way, a genuine grind of the reservation price that the next incoming order confirms. So B's efficiency excess is used as a *sign switch* on A's open displacement rather than a magnitude weight, and the resolution clock is set by B's Hawkes conditional intensity (baseline plus decaying self-excitation) rather than A's static per-name arrival rate; A's sqrt-volume-weighted traded return is subtracted as transient impact. Neither parent alone can separate corroborated grind-repricing (continuation) from lone-tick staleness (reversal): A pools both and dilutes its IC, B signs the pooled object the wrong way — the interaction is what carries the edge.
factors.name: Efficiency-Switched Untraded Displacement under Hawkes Arrival Gate

factors.trading_idea: Parent B says a quote move is only permanent once trades have paid for it, but it counts every traded dollar as equally validating; Parent A shows that a large share of dollars in basket/program bars are mechanical, cap-weight-allocated liquidity demand that carries no information at all. The child therefore discounts the volume clock by the estimated program component of each name's bar volume (aggregate excess dollar volume in a basket-footprint bar, allocated by index weight), builds a second 'informed-flow' anchor alongside the ordinary volume-time anchor, and fades the wedge between them — the displacement that only mechanical basket dollars paid for. The difference of two anchors that both track price automatically purges plain price-vs-moving-average reversal (Parent B needed a trailing OLS for this), and the wedge is up-weighted by Parent A's impact-elasticity-in-excess-of-beta rank, since a given program dollar displaces a thin, high-cap-weight name far more than its beta justifies. Neither parent has this: A knows when mechanical flow is present but only fades a market-level move through a static elasticity tilt, while B measures a name-level pricing error but cannot tell mechanical dollars from informed ones.
factors.name: Program-discounted flow-validation anchor wedge

factors.trading_idea: Names whose shareholder base is dominated by mandate-constrained income capital (high dividend yield, high payout ratio, steady buybacks, stable cash-flow yield) are held by insurers, income funds and retirement sleeves that do not re-optimise at second-level frequency, so less attentive arbitrage capital stands ready to enforce their beta-implied response to a market-wide shock. After a sharp cross-sectional market move these carry-clientele names should complete their beta-implied adjustment with a measurable lag of tens of seconds. Falsified if the catch-up wedge predicts equally well across clientele deciles, which would mean this is ordinary beta-lag and not a clientele/slow-capital effect.
factors.name: Payout-Clientele Gated Beta Catch-Up

factors.trading_idea: The parent declared a priori that lagged market loadings imply positive catch-up; the report shows the realized sign is the opposite, which is exactly what happens when the *common* part of a 10-second move is mostly transient index-level inventory pressure (ETF/basket market-making) that decays within a minute, while the *idiosyncratic* part splits into an informed, volume-confirmed component that persists and a quiet, unconfirmed quote-drift component that snaps back. Rather than asserting these three signs, the child decomposes each name's last-6-bar standardized move into (i) beta×market, (ii) idio×volume-confirmation weight, (iii) idio×(1−weight) and *estimates* the horizon-matched coefficients on all three by a purged, pooled, ridge-regularised trailing OLS of realized 6-bar returns on their own 6-bar-lagged channel values, so the forecast is the fitted conditional mean with data-determined signs. The falsifiable claim is that these pooled repricing coefficients are persistent over ~hour timescales (driven by slowly varying market-maker inventory capacity), so past-estimated coefficients generalise 6 bars ahead; if the coefficients are pure noise the factor has zero IC. It resists arbitrage because the mixture of transient and permanent repricing is a moving target that must be re-estimated continuously and harvested with second-scale execution in names where spread and impact cap capacity.
factors.name: Purged pooled common/idio × volume-split online forecast

factors.trading_idea: The parent's edge was real but too slow: it matched the *average* zero-crossing clock of a name to the 6-bar horizon, so it selected names that revert on a 6-bar timescale on average, not names whose current deviation will actually be closed inside the next 6 bars — hence IC that kept rising out to 24 bars. The child replaces the static, window-averaged clock with a *state-dependent* first-passage estimate: from the current signed deviation and its trailing OLS velocity we extrapolate the time tau = dev/(-velocity) until the path hits its anchor, and fade the deviation only with the scale-free kernel 4*tau*h/(tau+h)^2, which peaks exactly when the *remaining* travel time equals h = 6 bars and vanishes both for already-closed excursions (pure quote noise) and for excursions still widening or crawling back too slowly to pay inside the window. Because an extrapolated hitting time is meaningless when the velocity is statistically indistinguishable from path noise, the fade is shrunk by the velocity signal-to-noise ratio slope^2/(slope^2+var(slope)), and tilted toward *quiet* corrections (recent volume below its own norm), where the walk-back reflects inventory/liquidity unwinding rather than fresh information that would overshoot the anchor. The edge should persist because it is a per-name, state- and horizon-conditional selection (which bar of which excursion pays in the next minute), invisible to books that pool all names and all excursion phases into one reversal signal, and it is capacity-limited by the small size of the residual travel it harvests.
factors.name: Kinematic first-passage horizon match (quiet reversion)

factors.trading_idea: The parent showed that a name's *long-run* sign-flip frequency (Rice rho over 80 minutes) is essentially a static per-name constant, so multiplying it by the current displacement collapses into a level bet on cross-sectional reversal that the book already spans and whose sign the data rejected. The child keeps only the distribution-free sign machinery and changes the mechanism: alternation is a *state*, not a name parameter — when a sliced metaorder is working, consecutive 10-second mid-return signs cluster into unusually long runs, and when quoting/inventory noise dominates, signs alternate more than chance. I measure this with the conditional (Wald–Wolfowitz-style) runs statistic over a 5-minute episode window — the observed adjacent-flip frequency minus the 2q(1-q) frequency implied by the window's own up/down imbalance, scaled by sqrt(pair count) — so a drift-driven sign imbalance cannot masquerade as persistence. Removing both the name's own 1-hour norm and the cross-sectional median leaves a pure two-way-demeaned interaction: relative to peers and to itself, a name in an unusually persistent, volume-confirmed state should continue its last 60-second displacement, while a name in an unusually alternating state should snap back. The edge survives arbitrage because reversion desks apply one common reversion coefficient (or a slow per-name one) to the whole cross-section; harvesting the *state* term needs continuous per-name re-estimation with the imbalance-conditioned null, and the per-name payoff is tiny and only diversifies away in a broad book.
factors.name: Conditional-runs alternation state, volume-gated displacement

factors.trading_idea: Intraday volume and variance follow a strong deterministic time-of-day profile, so a bar's volume looks 'heavy' and its displacement looks 'large' mostly because of *where in the session* it sits; every trailing-window standardisation therefore mixes a mechanical clock effect into the paid-versus-unpaid dislocation split. This child estimates the market-wide diurnal shape of |return| and of volume causally from prior days' same-time bars (pooled cross-sectionally for robustness), deseasonalises both channels, and only then measures the dislocation and the volume surprise: what remains is a genuine conditional surprise — displacement per unit of *expected* noise, paid for with *unexpectedly* aggressive volume (temporary impact that decays, hence reversal) or printed on unexpectedly quiet tape (quote repricing that persists, hence continuation). To make the claim falsifiable and non-redundant, the score is cross-sectionally purged each bar of the conventional trailing-window dislocation and of the trailing-window volume-gated dislocation, so only the diurnal correction survives. The edge persists because the correction requires multi-day, cross-name estimation of a seasonal profile that convenience-driven intraday signals skip, and it is largest at low-liquidity times of day where spread costs deter high-capacity arbitrage.
factors.name: Diurnal-clock-normalised paid/unpaid dislocation (purged of the trailing-window version)

factors.trading_idea: The parent selected names whose *unconditional* mean crossing period equalled the 6-bar horizon, but excursion durations of price deviations are heavy-tailed and aging: conditional on an excursion having already survived a bars, the expected remaining time to the next zero-crossing is far longer than the unconditional mean, which is exactly why the parent's reversal payoff leaked out to 12-24 bars instead of landing at 6. The child replaces the unconditional clock with a non-parametric *mean residual life* estimator — from the trailing empirical set of that name's completed excursion durations, the mean excess (D - a | D > a) at the current excursion age a — and fades the standardised deviation from a short (20-bar) anchor only where that conditional expected time-to-crossing matches the fixed 6-bar offset. Falsifiable: the IC decay profile should now peak at or near 6 bars rather than rising monotonically to 24, and replacing the age-conditional residual life with the unconditional mean duration (the parent's statistic) should shift the peak back out and weaken the 6-bar IC. It survives arbitrage because it requires per-name survival-analysis bookkeeping on the ongoing excursion (age, empirical duration set) rather than a pooled level signal, and its payoff is a horizon-specific, capacity-limited timing effect invisible to anyone trading a single blended reversal book.
factors.name: Excursion-age-conditional residual-life matched deviation fade

factors.trading_idea: Parent A shows that a FRESH escape of the mid out of its trailing occupation band walks into thin resting depth and extends — but it rides every escape, including the ones that were merely mechanical: basket/program dollars allocated by capitalisation weight rather than beta push high-weight-per-depth names out of their value areas without any information, and that displacement must relax. Parent B predicts exactly that mechanical component (inverse-turnover-minus-beta wedge times the footprint-weighted market displacement) but fades it blindly, so it pays on bars where the push never actually dislodged anyone from their occupation band. The child makes A's escape event the dependent variable of a per-bar cross-sectional WLS regression on B's predicted over-push, where the regression weights are A's own conviction score (coil tightness vs the sqrt(N) random-walk benchmark plus relative participation) so that only genuine, heavily-traded coils vote on the attribution slope; the signed R-squared of that weighted fit is an attribution-trust state that, fused with the program-footprint z-score, splits the escape into a mechanically-attributed part (faded, because basket liquidity demand relaxes) and an un-attributed remainder (ridden with A's polarity, because that is the escape into shallow depth). The interaction is the edge: escape geometry tells you WHERE the book is thin, flow attribution tells you WHO pushed, and only their product separates ignition-continuation from over-push snapback — a distinction invisible to either parent, and the reason A's standalone IC does not survive as marginal value.
factors.name: Coil-weighted value-area escape: basket-attribution trust split

factors.trading_idea: The parent showed that a move living in a historically LOW-variance (high-precision) direction predicts *continuation*, not reversal, over the next several 10-second bars — the opposite of its declared sign. The correct reading is microstructural: at a 10-second clock, a basket-inconsistent move along a tight eigen-direction is the footprint of a single-name metaorder being sliced, not of a mispriced spread; child orders arrive with positive autocorrelation (order-splitting / Hawkes self-excitation), so the whitened pressure persists for tens of seconds before liquidity providers and stat-arb capital eventually pull it back (hence the parent's IC turning positive only near 24 bars). The child therefore (i) keeps the regularized precision-whitening and the cross-sectional projection-out of the plain univariate move, so the surviving signal is still orthogonal to the book's reversal/momentum factors, and (ii) stops guessing the direction: it estimates each name's own trailing AR(1) coefficient of its whitened residual pressure and forms the horizon-matched conditional forecast sum_{j=1..6} rho^j of the filtered pressure, weighted by whether the metaorder is still live (recent volume vs its own average). Falsification: if the whitened pressure has no persistent AR structure (rho ~ 0 on average) or if that persistence is not itself persistent across windows, the projection has zero IC even though the raw whitened dislocation had non-zero IC. The edge survives arbitrage because each episode is worth a few ticks, requires a stable rolling precision matrix plus per-name persistence estimation, and its sign is name- and regime-dependent, so univariate reversal/momentum screens cannot capture it.
factors.name: Whitened idiosyncratic pressure, self-calibrated AR(6) projection

factors.trading_idea: Resting limit-order supply is not spread evenly over price: it accumulates at the levels the mid has actually revisited, because passive quoters re-post where they were filled and where queues already exist. I measure that directly as a scale-free local-time (recurrence) density: the fraction of the last 90 bars whose log mid sits within one window-sigma of the *current* mid, which under a martingale has a universal (arcsine/local-time) distribution, so an unusually high value for that name means the price is presently sitting on a genuinely well-supplied, two-sided level while an unusually low value means it has walked into territory with no resting inventory. Mechanism: at a high-density level the standing book supplies the restoring force, so the last minute's move is absorbed and gives back; in a low-density vacuum there is nothing to absorb the flow, so the same move extends. Because the gate is centred per name in time and the signal is the pure interaction (gate x recent move), the average loading on the plain 6-bar move is zero, so the factor is invisible to reversal/momentum screens and pays only a few ticks per episode — too little to attract capital that must estimate a nonparametric path statistic per name in real time, while the cause (where resting liquidity actually is) is a structural property of order books rather than a mispricing arbitrage can delete.
factors.name: Local-time pinning density gates reversal vs extension

factors.trading_idea: Campbell–Grossman–Wang: price changes produced by liquidity demand require a concession from risk-averse liquidity providers and therefore revert, whereas price changes that occur without unusual volume are quote/information drift and do not. The informative object is not the size of a name's recent move (a mined main effect, which the parent's sqrt-volume pressure wedge essentially re-expressed and which the book already spans at 71% correlation) but WHICH bars paid for it: I purge the trailing drift from each bar return and measure the covariance of the residual bar moves with the name's own bounded volume-surprise weight. A positive covariance means the excess displacement was bought/sold through unusual volume — it is inventory-driven and reversible; a negative covariance means the excess displacement happened on quiet bars — it is repricing and persists. Because the drift is removed before the covariance is taken, the statistic has zero expectation under the null and is nearly orthogonal by construction to plain momentum/reversal factors, so it is an interaction rather than another main effect; the edge survives arbitrage because it is the fee paid for bearing one-minute inventory risk, not a mispricing that vanishes when identified.
factors.name: Volume-concordance of the reversible displacement (CGW fade)

factors.trading_idea: The parent showed that displacement not paid for by flow reverts, but it summed those deficits on the calendar clock and so peaked at 24 bars rather than the 6-bar target: dealer inventory is worked off in *volume time*, not clock time. The child therefore treats each unbacked (side-conditional flow-deficit) move as an increment to a latent intermediary inventory that decays with the *cumulative traded volume arriving after* it, and then multiplies the surviving inventory by the fraction expected to be relieved over the next six bars, estimated from the stock's own persistent (Hawkes-like autocorrelated) flow-arrival rate. Volume-confirmed moves are given zero weight rather than being extrapolated, because Kyle/CGW logic says they are permanent repricing and carry no unwind obligation. Falsifiable: sorting on relief-flow arrival rate, the 6-bar reversal of unbacked displacement should be concentrated in high-arrival names and be slow (>12 bars) or absent in silent names — if the two buckets revert at the same 6-bar speed, the volume-clock mechanism is wrong. The edge persists because each unwind is a couple of basis points, below single-name round-trip cost, and is only harvestable as a diversified 10-second cross-sectional overlay, while dealers absorbing uninformed liquidity demand and offloading against arriving flow recurs continuously.
factors.name: Unbacked-displacement inventory with volume-clock relief

factors.trading_idea: Recent traded volume at a price level is a record of where resting liquidity has actually been consumed and (via queue reconstruction) is most likely to be replenished, so the local volume profile behaves like a two-sided barrier: the mid traverses low-volume 'cliffs' quickly and is blocked by high-volume 'shelves'. The mechanically trivial part of that asymmetry is just where the mid sits relative to the recency-weighted volume centroid (a VWAP-deviation reversal signal the book already spans), so I regress the side-mass asymmetry on that standardised centroid deviation with a causal per-name trailing OLS and keep only the residual — the pure shelf-vs-cliff *shape* of the profile. Direction comes from the residual (unusually heavy mass below and thin above ⇒ downside is defended and upside is a vacuum ⇒ positive forward return), and magnitude comes from unsigned net signed-volume pressure over the last six bars, because a barrier only pays when something is actually pushing on it — this is why the signal resolves inside a minute rather than the parent's 24-bar inventory-unwind clock. The edge survives arbitrage because reconstructing volume-at-price shape and purging it of the centroid requires the full trailing path per name, and the payoff is a small, size-limited liquidity rebate rather than a directional forecast.
factors.name: Centroid-purged volume shelf/cliff barrier under flow pressure

factors.trading_idea: For a one-dimensional diffusion the stationary Fokker–Planck relation inverts exactly to mu(x) = (sigma^2/2) * d/dx log p(x): the local drift a price experiences is the logarithmic gradient of the density of time it has spent at nearby levels, because resting depth (and therefore the restoring force) accumulates where the mid has actually dwelt while unvisited regions are thin. The parent factor's realized sign contradicted its story precisely because its strongest branch was the liquidity-vacuum branch — a mid that has just walked above (below) everything it visited has all occupancy mass below (above) it and retraces — while at a recurrent level the parent still imposed a large loading even though the occupancy profile there is symmetric and predicts nothing; the log-gradient estimator fixes that by construction (it vanishes at the mode and is maximal in the vacuum). I estimate d/dx log p with a Gaussian kernel on an exponentially-leaky trailing occupancy (queue memory ages), which reduces analytically to the kernel-weighted standardized signed distance of past mids from the current mid, scale it by local diffusivity, shrink it by the estimator's own validity condition (a Lo–MacKinlay variance ratio: a trending window is non-stationary so the occupancy profile is a lagging artifact), and purge its trailing projection on the plain 6-bar move so the surviving signal cannot be reproduced by a reversal screen. The edge should persist because it pays only a fraction of a tick per minute-long episode, requires a per-name nonparametric density derivative in real time, and its cause — where limit-order inventory has physically accumulated — is regenerated by every new price excursion rather than being a mispricing arbitrage can delete.
factors.name: Fokker–Planck occupancy-gradient drift (variance-ratio trusted)

factors.trading_idea: Sparre Andersen universality says that for a symmetric random walk with *any* increment distribution, the probability that the latest point is the running extreme of the last n steps is jump-distribution-free — so an imbalance between new idiosyncratic n-bar highs and new n-bar lows is a variance-free, tail-robust detector of hidden directional pressure, immune to the volatility and bid-ask-bounce noise that swamp magnitude-based momentum at 10-second frequency. Extremes are not all alike, however: an extreme printed while the name is trading well above its own average volume is the footprint of a split metaorder whose remaining child orders keep arriving (long-memory order flow), whereas an extreme printed on thin or zero flow is quote flicker in a liquidity vacuum and is unwound as soon as depth returns. The child therefore runs two *weighted sign tests* on the same record events — one weighted by excess participation, one by participation deficit — and trades the wedge, shrinking the whole statistic when the observed record count falls below the Sparre Andersen null (a bouncy, non-persistent path carries no drift information). The edge survives arbitrage because harvesting the backed leg means trading in the same direction as an in-progress metaorder and paying its impact, and because the signal is an order-statistic (rank) object conditioned on per-name flow intensity, invisible to any factor built from return magnitudes, betas or calendar-time decay.
factors.name: Flow-backed vs. vacuum record asymmetry (Sparre Andersen sign test)

factors.trading_idea: The parent assumed every break of a pinned mid is informative; the realized sign says otherwise, and the reason is that pin breaks are a *mixture* of two physically different events that the absorbed-volume gate cannot separate. A break of exactly one grid quantum is a fleeting best-quote event — one resting order at the touch was cancelled or filled and the mid slid half a tick; because limit orders re-queue at the vacated touch within seconds (and the deeper the queue that was absorbed while pinned, the faster it reforms), such moves mechanically snap back. A break of several quanta in a single bar cannot be undone by one re-post: it requires depletion or withdrawal of multiple price levels, i.e. genuine order-flow imbalance whose self-excitation continues. The child therefore signs the beta-residual break by a wedge in the break's step multiplicity m (negative for m≈1, positive for m≳3) and amplifies only the reversion arm by the volume absorbed while pinned. It survives arbitrage because the reversion arm is worth a fraction of a tick and is only harvestable by winning queue priority at the vacated level, while the continuation arm requires crossing a widened spread precisely when adverse selection is highest — neither arm pays a spread-crosser, but both tilt a portfolio that is trading anyway. Falsifiable: if one-quantum and multi-quantum pin breaks show the same-signed 6-bar IC, the mixture story is wrong.
factors.name: Pin-break step-multiplicity refill wedge

factors.trading_idea: Parent A showed that a fresh, structurally-unexplained one-sided (downside-heavy) variance burst mean-reverts when it looks mechanical, but it measured 'mechanical' only crudely, as variance per unit of volume; Parent B showed that each bar splits into a traded body leg and an untraded seam leg (pure quote relocation between bar boundaries) and that some names' seams habitually walk the body back. The child therefore attributes the semivariance asymmetry innovation to the two legs separately: a downside-heavy variance burst accomplished at the *seams* is quote relocation with no trades behind it — inventory/impact displacement — while the same burst accomplished inside the *body* is informed and should not be faded, so the child longs the seam-leg innovation and shorts the body-leg innovation. It then trades that wedge only where Parent B's per-name reciprocation fingerprint (negative body→next-seam cross-lag correlation) says the book actually repays pushes at the seams within seconds, and only after removing the slow Merton/Christie structural component via leverage-tercile x size-half demeaning. The interaction is the edge: Parent A knew the *magnitude and asymmetry* of the dislocation but not whether it was traded or quoted, so its information leaked out to 24 bars; Parent B knew *which names reciprocate quickly* but its signed body push carried no dislocation magnitude, hence near-zero standalone IC — attributing one-sided variance to the untraded leg and gating it by the reciprocation clock dates the event to the last two minutes and forces it to pay inside the next minute.
factors.name: Seam-leg semivariance asymmetry reciprocation snapback

factors.trading_idea: Parent A produces a genuine finite-horizon *direction*: the Adler entrainment solution says where a phase-locked name's Epps-corrected precision-whitened dislocation should stand six bars from now, including the fold-over when entrainment carries it past its turning point. What it cannot know is whether the destination is reachable: a predicted displacement only completes inside six bars if it moves the spread *down* its own empirical potential, and Parent B's local time supplies exactly that potential — with U_i(u) = -log rho_i(u) from the trailing kernel occupation density of the whitened spread, moves toward habitually revisited levels are cheap and complete, moves into virgin territory stall or truncate. The child therefore evaluates the occupation density at BOTH the current level and the Adler-predicted target level and weights the displacement by the density gradient between them, while names that fail the locking criterion (no direction available) are instead pulled from fresh, unoccupied levels back to their habitual median. The interaction is the edge: A has direction with no notion of barrier, B's freshness gate is directionless (which is precisely why its declared fade sign was contradicted — freshness says a level is unaccepted, not which way it resolves), and only the signed density difference between origin and destination converts occupancy into a completion probability for a specific forecast.
factors.name: Adler locking displacement routed by spread occupation potential

factors.trading_idea: Parent A splits the precision-whitened 6-bar dislocation into a flow-attributed part F (the cross-sectional projection onto the mechanically predicted basket over-push, weight-per-depth minus beta times the lagged cap-weighted market displacement) and an orthogonal, information-like remainder U. Parent B measures whether the name is currently resting on a repeatedly-quoted, well-supplied price level (high local-time recurrence density) or has walked into a liquidity vacuum. The child lets that single pinning gate act with OPPOSITE sign on the two components: mechanical over-push that ends in a vacuum is unbacked liquidity demand and must relax (fade), while the same push that comes to rest on a repeatedly-supplied level has been absorbed and validated by two-sided depth and is permanent (ride); conversely the un-attributed informational remainder keeps diffusing where there is nothing to absorb it (ride in vacuum) and stalls against standing depth (fade at pinned levels). That is exactly the edge neither parent has: Parent B pooled both channels into one raw move and therefore measured only the net of two opposite-signed effects (hence its 'contradicted' sign — the flow channel dominates the pooled move), and Parent A faded/rode its two components with a noisy regression-R² trust gate that knows nothing about where the resting liquidity actually is.
factors.name: Pinning-gated basket over-push attribution split

factors.trading_idea: The parent showed that a name's expected next-6-bar return contains a computable debt to market information it has already seen, but it estimated the impulse response as six free, noisily-fitted lag loadings and therefore threw away all response mass beyond lag 6 — which is exactly why its IC peaked at 12 bars rather than at the traded 6-bar offset. The child replaces the truncated fold with a two-parameter geometric adjustment kernel (gain g, per-bar retention lambda) fitted by trailing OLS of own return on an exponentially-weighted market path, for which the undelivered mass inside a horizon H has the closed form g*lambda*(1-lambda^H)/(1-lambda) times the current EW market state: slow adjusters' debt beyond lag 6 is now extrapolated instead of discarded, and the six noisy loadings collapse to two parameters, so the forecast is horizon-matched by construction rather than by truncation. Because rank IC rewards probability of delivery and not merely expected delivery, the debt is trusted only in proportion to (i) the kernel's trailing explanatory power (model-averaging weight across adjustment speeds) and (ii) the update-clock probability that at least one quote revision — the only mechanism by which the debt can actually be paid — arrives in the next H bars, estimated as 1-(1-p_up)^H from the trailing frequency of non-zero mid changes. The edge survives arbitrage because the debt is largest precisely in names whose mid updates sluggishly and lumpily, where paying spread and queueing risk to harvest a few basis points of lagged beta is unattractive to fast arbitrageurs.
factors.name: Geometric-kernel extrapolated owed catch-up, update-clock trusted

factors.trading_idea: Parent A shows that 3-6 bar mid displacement which was *paid for* by executed flow is transient impact and decays, while displacement with no inventory transfer is a quote revision; Parent B's realized (contradicted) sign shows that queue-consuming, grid-bound break impulses also revert. The synthesis is that the *permanent* leg is not universally permanent: its polarity depends on Parent B's state variable, tick-grid binding. In coarse-grid, pinned names one grid-quantum of untraded mid revision is a genuine belief update by the quote setters that still has to propagate to slower participants (continuation), whereas in finely-priced, continuously-repricing names an unexplained mid wiggle is mostly quote noise / stale-quote flicker and mean-reverts — so the coefficient on the unexplained component flips sign with grid binding while the flow-explained (transient impact) component is short everywhere. Neither parent has this interaction: A applies one polarity to all names, B only ever looks inside the grid-bound state and never conditions the impact decomposition on it.
factors.name: Grid-binding gated polarity of the flow-explained / unexplained displacement split

factors.trading_idea: Parent A measures how much of a name's own kernel-implied response to the last common market shock it has still not delivered, but assumes every such gap is owed and will close; Parent B knows that a displacement is transient inventory impact when it was paid for with trades and near-permanent quote revision when it accrued while the tape was quiet — but it applies that test to raw price, which is dominated by the common beta response. The child applies B's two-clock test to A's object: it builds the *residual* path (realized minus kernel-implied vol-normalised return since the last large common shock) and asks whether that residual accumulated in the heavy-volume bars (corr with the cumulative volume clock) or in the quiet bars (corr with the calendar ramp). A trade-aligned residual is transient impact, so the discounted deficit is genuinely owed and closes over the next few bars (long positive deficit); a quiet residual is a permanent, still-unfolding repricing, so the same deficit will widen rather than close and the sign flips. Neither parent can make this distinction: A signs all deficits the same way, B has no benchmark path against which to define a residual, and the interaction is what converts a 24-bar catch-up effect into a 6-bar one by discounting the accumulation with a ~4-bar half-life so only the still-open, fast-decaying part survives.
factors.name: Shock-deficit residual split by volume-clock permanence

factors.trading_idea: Parent B's sqrt(volume)-weighted fresh-minus-stale directional pressure realized a NEGATIVE 6-bar IC, which is exactly what transient impact predicts: at the 10-second scale most fresh one-sided pressure is immediacy cost paid into passive depth and it relaxes rather than continues — but B pools two economically opposite bars together, so its sign is an average of fade and follow. The child uses Parent A's within-bar/local geometry as a bar-level *weight* to split B's wedge in two: pressure delivered on bars whose size was absorbed and retraced (high wick share, low 3-bar directional efficiency) is faded, while pressure delivered on body-dominated, path-efficient bars is accepted flow whose imbalance autocorrelation keeps it going. Both wedges are then orthogonalised (trailing per-name OLS) against Parent A's shock-selected owed-systematic-delivery gap, so we never fade a push that is merely the mechanical delivery of a beta move the name still owes, and that owed gap enters as its own directional term. The interaction is the edge: A's absorption geometry has no size-weighted flow measure to apply itself to, and B has no way to know whether the volume it weighted was absorbed or accepted — which is precisely why its unconditional sign flipped.
factors.name: Absorption-split sqrt-flow freshness wedge, owed-delivery purged
