factors.trading_idea: The parent measured fresh-minus-stale sqrt-volume-weighted directional pressure and realized a *negative* IC: at a 10-second scale the sqrt-weighted one-sided repricing of the last minute is dominated not by unfinished informed flow but by the transient part of Bouchaud's propagator — liquidity demanders pay to walk the mid, depth refills, and the displacement is partly handed back within tens of seconds. The economically correct sign therefore has to be reversal, and the mechanism predicts *how much* is handed back: repayment is the complement of the permanent (information) share, so it must shrink — and can invert to continuation — for names where a one-sided burst is more likely to be informed. I therefore condition the reversal on a purely fundamental adverse-selection proxy (intangibility, R&D intensity, low tangible-asset backing, low net margin: hard-to-value, high-PIN firms) and first purge market/sector-common pressure, because common flow reprices risk permanently while idiosyncratic one-sided flow is dealer inventory. Falsifiable: the reversal IC must be monotone in fundamental transparency (strong for tangible, profitable, low-R&D names; ~zero or continuation for the most opaque tercile); the edge survives arbitrage because harvesting it means providing liquidity against a still-arriving metaorder inside a one-minute window where net-of-spread capacity is tiny, and because the fundamental conditioner enters only multiplicatively and so cannot be captured by any static value/quality tilt.
factors.name: Opacity-conditioned transient-impact repayment wedge

factors.trading_idea: Parent A's Rice inversion rho = cos(pi * p_flip) is really a jump-robust, tick-size-free *regression coefficient* estimator for Gaussian-copula pairs, but A applied it to a single pooled series and then asserted the direction, so it mixed two economically opposite populations of 60-second displacement (mechanical basket over-push, which relaxes, and sliced/informational flow, which diffuses) into one coefficient — which is exactly why its realized sign contradicted the hypothesis. Parent B knows how to *separate* those populations from flow geometry alone (weight-per-depth minus beta wedge times the standardised market displacement predicts the mechanical part of a name's residual move) but fades the predicted push with a blindly-signed, market-wide gate, so it pays on bars where the push never landed. The child splits each name's 6-bar residual displacement cross-sectionally into the flow-attributed component F (projection on B's predicted over-push) and the orthogonal remainder U, and then estimates, *per name and separately for each component*, the trailing sign-concordance between that component and the following non-overlapping 6-bar displacement, converting each frequency into a predictive correlation via Rice. The interaction is the edge: the coefficients are no longer asserted but measured on the correct sub-population and at the exact forecast offset, so a name whose mechanically-pushed blocks snap back gets a negative loading on F while its information-driven blocks still get a positive loading on U — a per-name, per-mechanism decomposition neither parent can express.
factors.name: Rice sign-regression on basket over-push components

factors.trading_idea: A multi-bar pin on one price level is a large resting queue; but the *break* of that level is two different events depending on how much trading accompanies it. If the break bar's volume is small relative to the volume already absorbed at the level, the queue was not consumed — the quote was simply pulled/re-priced into a thin book, so the mid displacement is mechanical (Roll/quote-bounce, transient impact) and snaps back once depth replenishes; this is why the parent, whose gate was monotone in absorbed volume alone, realised a *reversal* IC while declaring continuation. If instead the break bar prints volume comparable to or larger than the whole absorbed queue, the resting depth was genuinely eaten by an aggressive metaorder and the beta-residual displacement is permanent repricing that keeps drifting. The child therefore signs the beta-residual break displacement by a self-calibrated log-ratio of break-bar volume to absorbed queue volume (centred and scaled by each name's own trailing moments of that ratio over its past break events), plus a constant transient-reversal offset that encodes the parent's measured average behaviour. It is falsifiable: the 6-bar IC of the residual break displacement must be significantly more positive for high volume-backing breaks than for low ones; if the IC is flat in that ratio the mechanism is dead. The edge survives arbitrage because each event is worth a fraction of a tick in exactly the low-turnover, grid-bound names where crossing the spread eats the profit.
factors.name: Pin-break volume-backing ratio: transient vs permanent displacement flip

factors.trading_idea: When a dealer absorbs one-sided demand in a sector, it lays the risk off in the sector's most liquid proxy names, so those proxies get repriced by quote adjustment and hedge execution rather than by their own informed trade flow. The observable fingerprint is a multi-minute displacement in a liquid name whose OWN volume clock is running slow while its sector peers' volume clock is running fast; that displacement is dealer inventory, not information, and it is walked back as the hedge is unwound. Conversely, a displacement that arrived on the name's own heavy volume is trade-supported and largely permanent, so the same displacement should be followed, not faded — the reversal coefficient is therefore predicted to be monotone increasing in the peer-minus-own flow deficit and to change sign for the heaviest own-flow names. The edge persists because harvesting it means warehousing the inventory the dealer is shedding, and because the ranking needs three simultaneously-observed per-name states (own volume clock, peer volume clock, and liquidity-proxy status inside the sector) that a pooled calendar-time reversal factor cannot see.
factors.name: Dealer hedge-footprint reversal (peer-flow minus own-flow split)

factors.trading_idea: A trade-driven push accomplished inside a bar (body = log close - log open) has exactly two places to land at the next bar boundary: the name's OWN seam (log open - log previous close) can walk it back, which is the signature of liquidity providers absorbing inventory-driven, transient impact, or the PEERS' seams can move with it, which is the signature of a push that carried common information that comparable-name quote-setters must reflect. Estimating both cross-lag couplings per name on trailing windows yields a signed state variable - the impact-destination wedge (own reciprocation minus peer transmission) - which says whether a fresh push is inventory noise to be faded or information to be followed over the next ~60 seconds. The edge persists against arbitrage because acting on the absorber leg means posting passive size against possibly-informed aggressive flow for a fraction of the spread (market-making inventory risk, not a liftable directional mispricing), while the propagator leg requires the per-name conditional estimate to know when NOT to fade - most short-horizon reversal traders fade unconditionally and are exactly the counterparty.
factors.name: Impact destination: own-seam absorption vs peer-seam propagation

factors.trading_idea: The parent showed that a rank-based location shift only predicts at 6 bars once it is conditioned on the *shape* of the increments, but its conditioning statistic (a Mood-type variance of uniformized returns) is permutation-invariant: it cannot tell a genuine sliced-metaorder grind from a random reshuffle of the same increments. Slicing is fundamentally a statement about temporal ORDER — child orders arrive repeatedly on the same side at roughly constant clip, so the recent path shows (i) positive serial concordance of increment signs (a Wald-Wolfowitz-style run deficit) and (ii) squared increments spread evenly across bars (low Herfindahl of realised-variance energy). A liquidity-withdrawal overshoot instead concentrates almost all realised variance in one or two bars and shows no sign persistence, and under transient impact that displacement relaxes within a minute as depth refills. So the child replaces the order-blind dispersion gate with an order-aware two-part grind score (sign-run persistence + energy evenness) and smooths the location statistic across two scales, which should raise both the standalone IC and the marginal contribution relative to the parent. It survives arbitrage because the profitable side is the metaorder's own continuation: the agent creating the drift cannot front-run itself, and one-minute net-of-spread capacity on a rank-shape signal is far too small for large arbitrageurs.
factors.name: Order-persistence x energy-evenness grind wedge

factors.trading_idea: The parent showed the idio/basket flow split has real, book-orthogonal content but expressed it as a *stock* of still-owed push weighted toward the freshest bars, which is a low-pass level and therefore predicts slow drift (its IC peaked at 24 bars, not 6). The fix is that the two legs resolve on different business-time schedules: idiosyncratic (informed) push keeps accruing only while the parent metaorder is still executing, so its next-60-second continuation is governed by a *survival* low-pass in volume traded since the bar; basket/sector-common overpush stays plateaued while the burst is still being worked and only starts being paid back once execution completes, so what reverts over the *next* horizon is push whose business-time age sits near the completion scale — a *band-pass* in volume-clock age, not a fresh-weighted low-pass. Applying a survival kernel to the idio leg and a horizon-differenced delayed-relaxation kernel (g(V) − g(V+V_h), g plateau-then-decay) to the basket leg selects exactly the displacement that is due to move within 6 bars, so the edge should migrate from 24 bars to the fixed 6-bar offset. It survives arbitrage because harvesting it requires jointly estimating each name's flow-commonality loading, its Kyle lambda and its volume clock at 10-second resolution, and the payoff is a few basis points of maker-side timing that is uneconomic for anyone crossing the spread.
factors.name: Completion-clock dual-kernel idiosyncratic vs basket impact split

factors.trading_idea: The parent's edge was real but slow because its switch variable (the conversion ratio) and its impulse were computed on the SAME 100-second path, so the signal was dominated by a persistent path statistic and its IC kept rising out to 24 bars. The child separates timescales: conversion is re-cast as a slowly-varying structural property of the name's book — volume-weighted fraction of probed intrabar path that gets converted into net body displacement over ~40 minutes — which estimates permeability (thin, easily swept book) versus absorption (deep book that eats probes), while the traded signal is only the freshest 3-bar innovation (wick asymmetry relative to the name's own baseline, and beta-residual displacement in robust-scale units), gated by contemporaneous trade arrival. In absorptive names (low permeability) unfilled aggression printed as a wick keeps pushing the stale endpoint mid toward the probed side; in permeable names the fresh residual displacement is transient sweep impact that snaps back — so the same freshly-arrived event must be traded with opposite polarity depending on a state variable that is *not* measurable from the event itself. The edge persists because it requires jointly estimating a slow book-structure regime and acting on a 30-60 second impulse whose capacity is tiny; an unconditional wick-continuation or unconditional reversal trader averages the two regimes to zero, which is exactly what the parent's contradictory single-polarity ancestors showed.
factors.name: Permeability-regime-switched fresh probe impulse

factors.trading_idea: Parent B identifies *which* part of a name's recent move is mechanical, unpaid-for liquidity demand — the component proportional to cap-weight-per-unit-depth in excess of beta, incurred during bars whose volume allocation tilts toward the capitalisation-weight vector (a program footprint) — but it fades every such push at the same intensity and in calendar time, which is why its edge lives out at 24 bars. Parent A supplies the missing clock: a liquidity-provision error is repaid only as offsetting trade flow arrives, so the outstanding error is the survival-weighted sum of past increments under exp(-kappa·u) in volume time, and the fraction repaid inside exactly six bars is 1 − exp(-kappa·6·E[u]). The child accumulates *only the program-attributed* increments on the volume clock and scales the fade by that horizon-matched repayment fraction: information-driven moves never enter the accumulator (A's defect — it treats all returns as candidate error), and program pushes on names whose forecast trade arrival is too slow to clear the dislocation inside 60 seconds are down-weighted (B's defect). The interaction is exactly the intersection of 'mechanically caused, hence repayable' and 'counter-flow will actually arrive in time to repay it', which neither elasticity wedge nor volume-clock reversal can see alone.
factors.name: Volume-clock repaid basket over-push attribution

factors.trading_idea: At a 10-second clock the common (sector) component is absorbed at very different speeds by different names: sparsely-updating, wider-spread names load on the *lagged* sector return rather than the contemporaneous one (the Epps / non-synchronous-quote mechanism), so after a sector move they still owe a catch-up that completes over roughly the next minute. I estimate each name's lag loading directly — a trailing bivariate OLS of its one-bar return on (i) the previous 6-bar leave-one-out sector return and (ii) its own previous 6-bar return, keeping the coefficient on the peer term so the loading is purged of the name's own bid-ask/inventory autocorrelation — then demean the loading inside the sector and multiply it by the volatility-standardised sector move just completed. The signal uses NO own recent return, only (name-specific adjustment speed) x (peer move), so it is structurally orthogonal to the reversal/momentum factors that dominate the book. The edge survives arbitrage because harvesting it means simultaneously trading many of the slowest-updating, widest-spread names for a fraction of a tick each, and because the lag loading must be estimated per name rather than assumed pooled.
factors.name: Purged lag-loading sector catch-up

factors.trading_idea: A 10-second mid-price change has two very different origins: aggressive volume walking the book (liquidity demand, whose impact is largely transient and decays over the next minute per the Bouchaud propagator), or liquidity suppliers repricing/cancelling *ahead* of trades on information, with trades then chasing the new quote (Hasbrouck's quote information share, a permanent revision). These two regimes leave opposite fingerprints in the time-reversal asymmetry of a name's own price-volume cross-correlation: trade-driven names satisfy corr(|r_t|,V_{t-1}) > corr(|r_{t-1}|,V_t), quote-driven names the reverse. The child estimates that asymmetry causally per name over a trailing 40-minute window and uses it purely as an interaction that signs the response to the last 6 bars of sector-neutral, volatility-scaled displacement: fade displacement in trade-driven (impact-dominated) names, ride it in quote-driven (information-dominated) names. The edge persists because the reverting amplitude on impact-dominated names is of the order of the half-spread plus depth-consumption cost, so it is harvestable only as a passive queue-position tilt, and because unconditional short-horizon reversal traders get whipsawed precisely on the quote-led names this factor refuses to fade.
factors.name: Price-volume lead-lag asymmetry gated idio displacement

factors.trading_idea: Parent B knows *how far* a name is dislocated (a leverage-matched peer anchor gives a signed, sized reversion target) but has no reliable timestamp for when the push ended, which is why its edge kept accruing out to 24 bars; Parent A knows *when* and *why* (a 12-bar one-sided realised-semivariance innovation, structurally unexplained by capital structure, produced in a thin book) but has no anchor telling it how far the price should snap back. The child trades the negated peer displacement only when that displacement is *sourced* by a fresh, structurally-unexplained semivariance burst of the matching side (down-heavy variance under a below-peer price, up-heavy above) and when that burst was produced on little volume (high variance-per-unit-participation, i.e. mechanical inventory/impact rather than news). The interaction is the edge: sign-alignment converts A's unsigned asymmetry event into an attribution of B's displacement to transient impact, and it stamps B's slow level with a two-minute-old event date, so the front-loaded Bouchaud relaxation lands inside the fixed 6-bar window rather than 24; conversely, displacements accompanied by two-sided variance with commensurate volume are informed and are down-weighted instead of faded.
factors.name: Semivariance-sourced, vacuum-gated peer displacement snapback

factors.trading_idea: The parent's single-AR(1) pricing-error model lumps every transitory dislocation into one decay rate, so its filter loads mostly on the slowest, largest-variance error component — which is why its IC kept growing out to 24 bars while only a sliver was repaid inside the pinned 60-second offset. The child instead models the transitory error as the sum of TWO independent AR(1) components (fast, rho=0.80, half-life ~3 bars; slow, rho=0.98, half-life ~34 bars): the k-bar variance curve Var_k - k*Var_1 = b_f*g_k(rho_f) + b_s*g_k(rho_s) is exactly linear in the two component variances, so a ridge-stabilised, non-negativity-projected weighted LS over k = 2..34 identifies each component's variance, and a closed-form two-channel Wiener/GLS projection of two matched exponential return filters onto the two latent levels recovers the current fast and slow displacements separately. Only the analytic fraction of each component that is repaid within the horizon enters the forecast, and that fraction is measured on the name's own trade clock (effective bars = 6 x recent/normal volume rate), so the ranking at exactly 6 bars is dominated by names whose dislocation is genuinely collectable in 60 seconds rather than by names carrying a large but slowly-amortising error. The edge survives arbitrage because collecting it means warehousing the inventory a liquidity provider is shedding, and because the ranking requires each name's noise-variance split across two timescales plus its repayment speed — objects a pooled short-term reversal signal cannot see.
factors.name: Two-timescale pricing-error decomposition with 6-bar repayment weights

factors.trading_idea: Whether a short-run price displacement continues or snaps back is not a constant of nature: it depends on the current liquidity state (are market makers absorbing the flow, or is informed/order-split flow walking the book?), and that state is persistent over intraday time. So instead of hard-coding a reversal or momentum sign, I estimate each name's own response at exactly the traded offset — a trailing two-variable OLS of the realized 6-bar return on the *previous, disjoint* 6-bar normalized displacement and on that block's sqrt(volume)-weighted sign concordance (the parent's flow-backing statistic) — and apply the freshly-estimated, cross-sectionally shrunk coefficients to today's displacement and flow-backing. Because the calibration target is the 6-bar-ahead return itself, the signal's information is horizon-matched by construction, fixing the parent's defect of peaking at 24 bars; and the decomposition separates the price-path channel from the flow-backing channel so the model can simultaneously fade unbacked displacement and ride backed flow when the state warrants it. The edge survives arbitrage because it is not a static formula: its sign flips by name and regime, so static reversal/momentum books trade against it in exactly the states where the response has inverted, and the per-name online recalibration is the scarce input.
factors.name: Horizon-matched response calibration (displacement vs sqrt-flow)

factors.trading_idea: The parent's state variable (the level of volume-per-unit-price-traversal z-scored over 120 bars) is a slow, highly persistent name characteristic, which is exactly why its interaction with displacement only paid off 24 bars out: a predictor's forecast timescale inherits the autocorrelation time of its conditioning variable. The child keeps the Kyle-inverse depth measurement but replaces the slow level with its transient innovation — current 3-bar depth versus the same name's own 40-bar depth — whose decay time is on the order of tens of seconds and therefore matches the fixed 6-bar (60 s) offset. Mechanistically, a book that has just *stiffened* (volume rising per unit of traversed price) shows the resting queue that absorbed the recent move is still alive, so that move is liquidity demand and recoils within the next minute; a book that has just *softened* means the move went through a vacuum and is informative repricing that continues. The edge persists because quote-only reversal books cannot observe the traded-volume-per-traversal innovation and get run over precisely in the vacuum states, so they cannot span the sign flip; it is falsified if forward 6-bar returns load on the decay-weighted recent displacement with a slope independent of the depth innovation (flat interaction), or if only the slow depth level, not its innovation, carries the interaction.
factors.name: Depth-stiffening innovation gated fast recoil

factors.trading_idea: The parent proved that unpaid (quote-revision) displacement created under heavy liquidity demand is immediacy overshoot that is later given back, but it measured that overshoot with a flat 6-bar box window, so it mixed pushes that have already relaxed with pushes from slow-relaxing names whose give-back only lands 24 bars out — exactly why its IC peaked far beyond the fixed horizon. The child replaces the box with an age-resolved exponential survival kernel: each bar's unpaid increment is multiplied by the bar's activity share (only immediacy-driven displacement is transient; quiet-bar repricing is permanent), accumulated with the name's own relaxation rate, and then scaled by the fraction of that still-outstanding transient that will be repaid *inside* the next 6 bars, (1 − e^{−β·6}). The relaxation rate β is estimated causally per name by inverting the closed-form Ornstein–Uhlenbeck variance ratio of its unpaid increments at exactly the 6-bar scale, so the cross-section is sorted by give-back that is actually collectable at the traded horizon rather than by raw accumulated overshoot. The edge survives arbitrage because it is a liquidity-provision rent — the give-back is the price paid to whoever refills depth after an immediacy burst — and harvesting it requires taking the residual inventory risk on names whose relaxation clock is fast, not merely observing a past price move.
factors.name: Horizon-matched repayment fraction of immediacy-driven unpaid displacement

factors.trading_idea: In a propagator (linear-response) market, the price change over the *next* h bars implied by already-observed flow is not the level of any displacement component but the convolution of past flow with the FUTURE increments of the empirical response function: E[r_{t+1..t+h}] = sum_k f_{t-k} * sum_{j=1..h} c_{k+j}, where c_l = E[r_t f_{t-l}]/E[f^2] is the measured per-lag response increment. Each increment c_l is the net of two forces that the tape reveals directly — continued correlated liquidity taking (order splitting, which pushes price further) versus book refill / liquidity-provider inventory relaxation (which pulls it back) — so the estimator self-calibrates its own sign per name and per regime instead of assuming decay. Because the summation window is exactly the forecast horizon, the object is horizon-matched by construction, which is precisely what the parent lacked (its decomposed displacement *level* peaked at 12 bars). The edge survives arbitrage because harvesting it means quoting against the very flow that just moved the price inside one minute, bearing adverse-selection and inventory risk that scale with the same flow the signal reads; and it uses no price-level/displacement channel at all, so it is structurally distinct from the crowded reversal and quiet-vs-traded-split families.
factors.name: Response-increment tail convolution (horizon-matched propagator forecast)

factors.trading_idea: Within a 10-second bar, the parts of the range that lie *beyond* the open and close endpoints are pure failed excursions: price probed a level and was pushed back. Under a Brownian bridge pinned at (open, close) with locally estimated diffusion scale, the two one-sided overshoots have a known scale, so their standardised asymmetry isolates which side hosted hidden resting liquidity (icebergs, refreshed passive size) that rejected the probe. If a high-volume upside probe is repeatedly rejected, real supply is sitting above and price should drift toward the untested side over the next minute; the counterparty is the impatient aggressor who keeps paying spread into concealed size. Falsified if excursion asymmetry is symmetric noise from mid-quote flicker, in which case its volume-weighted average carries no forward sign.
factors.name: Bridge-Standardised Excursion Rejection / Absorption Wedge

factors.trading_idea: Price impact and its relaxation unfold in business (trade) time rather than calendar time (Kyle–Obizhaeva invariance), and because trade arrivals are long-memory (ACD / Hawkes self-excitation) the amount of business time that will elapse over the next 60 seconds is itself forecastable from a name's own recent, self-normalised activity. The parent's traded-vs-quiet displacement state predicted cumulative residual drift with a relaxation constant of several minutes, so at the pinned 6-bar offset only a fraction of it was delivered — and that fraction is systematically larger for names whose predicted business clock runs fast. The child therefore time-changes both channels by a causal forecast of the next-6-bar activity rate and replaces the parent's noisy per-name betas with a panel-pooled, horizon-matched trailing bivariate regression, so the sign of each channel is still estimated rather than declared but with an order of magnitude more effective observations. The edge survives arbitrage because harvesting the traded leg means standing in front of possibly-informed persistent flow (adverse selection) exactly in the names where competition for immediacy is fiercest, while the quiet leg is paid for supplying liquidity against transient quote noise (inventory risk); neither leg is a free option, and the construction requires joining a forward activity forecast with peer residualisation and pooled horizon-matched calibration.
factors.name: Business-clock (predicted-activity) time-change of pooled two-channel impact state

factors.trading_idea: The parent tried to identify whether flow leads price with a 60-bar rolling cross-correlation asymmetry — an estimator so slow that its information only resolved at 12-24 bars. The child obtains the same identification *event-by-event* by deliberately lagging the displacement window: measure a 3-bar idiosyncratic move that completed 3 bars ago, then compare the normalised trade volume in the 3 bars BEFORE it with the 3 bars AFTER it, which are now observable. Volume that arrives before the move is information-led (the price change is a permanent revision and continues); volume that arrives after it is reactive chasing into a thin book (a transitory inventory shock that market makers must absorb, so it decays). The edge persists because liquidity suppliers and standard reversal books condition on contemporaneous imbalance, size and volatility, not on the arrival *order* of flow relative to a completed quote displacement, and the payoff is inventory-capacity-limited compensation for filling latecomers rather than an information rent.
factors.name: Post-move flow-arrival timing split of displacement

factors.trading_idea: Parent B knows WHEN a name has just ignited out of its occupation band into thin outside depth, but it cannot tell WHY: a fresh escape can be an informed idiosyncratic walk or merely the footprint of a basket/program that allocates dollars by capitalisation weight rather than beta and therefore over-displaces illiquid, low-beta names whenever the market moves. Parent A supplies exactly that attribution — the (inverse-turnover minus beta) wedge times the contemporaneous cap-weighted market displacement — together with a per-bar trust statistic (cross-sectional R^2 of regressing the escape field on the predicted push). The child regresses the fresh-escape field on the predicted push each bar and routes the two orthogonal pieces through DIFFERENT halves of B's conviction gate: the attributed piece is ridden with the coil-tightness gate (a program still working an order walks a book that was already thin just outside a compressed value area, so displacement extends over the next minute), while the un-attributed piece is ridden with the participation gate (an idiosyncratic escape only extends if real volume backs it; thin-volume escapes are quote noise). The interaction is the edge: A alone prices attributed pushes without knowing whether the name actually left the depth pocket, and B alone applies one blended gate to escapes of completely different provenance — heavy volume flatters mechanical basket footprints and tight coils flatter noise-driven ones — so only attribution-trust-weighted routing sends coil geometry and participation evidence to the names each one actually diagnoses.
factors.name: Value-area escape routed by basket-push attribution: coil vs participation channels

factors.trading_idea: An observed 10-second mid-price is an efficient random walk plus a transitory pricing error created by inventory-bearing liquidity provision; that error is not white noise but decays at a name-specific speed, which makes the observed return series exactly ARMA(1,1). Matching the trailing lag-1 and lag-2 autocovariances of market-neutral returns identifies (phi, theta) in closed form by method of moments, and the *analytic* 6-step aggregation of that ARMA forecast, (phi*r_t - theta*a_t)*(1-phi^6)/(1-phi), is the optimal linear predictor at exactly the pinned offset: names whose pricing error decays inside one bar get a small 60-second forecast even if their reversal coefficient is large, while names whose error decays slowly have almost the whole dislocation forecastable over the next minute — and names dominated by order-splitting (positive autocorrelation) get a continuation forecast instead. The parent failed because it tried to estimate a signed 6-bar response from ~50 effective overlapping observations split across 8 cells (pure noise, hence the sign flip); here the same conditional-mean object is recovered from two low-order autocovariances with ~480 effective observations plus cross-sectional empirical-Bayes shrinkage, so the estimand is stable. The edge survives arbitrage because collecting it means absorbing the inventory the liquidity provider is trying to shed, and because separating the transitory from the permanent part requires the noise-to-signal ratio, which a pooled reversal factor cannot see.
factors.name: Moment-matched ARMA(1,1) transitory-component filter (6-bar optimal forecast)

factors.trading_idea: Order-flow arrival obeys a fluctuation-scaling (Taylor's) law across names: Var(volume) ~ A * Mean(volume)^beta, with beta near 1 when child orders arrive as many small, quasi-independent events and beta rising toward 2 when a few large, synchronized participants dominate. Fitting that law cross-sectionally on a long window and then evaluating each name's residual with its *recent* volume moments yields a size-matched measure of how LUMPY the flow that produced the current price displacement was. Mechanism: a gap between the mid and the volume-weighted price at which flow actually executed is inventory pressure when it was built by a few impatient large prints (lumpy flow) — makers must unwind, so the gap closes within the next handful of bars — but it is the live footprint of an evenly sliced metaorder when the flow was smooth (residual size still to execute), so the gap extends. The edge persists because it is a pure state-dependent *interaction*: a plain reversal or plain momentum book gets the average loading, not the sign flip, and harvesting the reverting branch means quoting against large impatient prints in exactly the thin, lumpy names where adverse selection is worst, so it cannot be scaled by fast arbitrageurs.
factors.name: Taylor-law flow-lumpiness gate on the mid-vs-execution-price gap

factors.trading_idea: The parent forecast only the *remaining* delivery of a market shock using truncated lag-1..6 loadings, implicitly assuming a name's impulse response ends at lag 6; its IC profile (positive at 1-3 bars, negative at 12-24) shows the true response overshoots and then partially reverses, so the truncated kernel mis-signs the tail. The child estimates the full distributed-lag impulse response b_0..b_11 of each name to *whitened* market innovations (AR(1)-residualised cap-weighted index return, so univariate lag betas are unbiased IRF coefficients) and folds the observed innovation path against the exact horizon-matched estimand E[sum_{j=1..6} r_{t+j}] = sum_i [C(i+6) - C(i)] u_{t-i}, where C(l) is the cumulative response — an object that is automatically positive where delivery is still owed and negative where the name has already over-delivered and must give it back. The edge persists because second-scale IRF tails for slow repricers are noisy per name, require joint estimation plus cross-sectional shrinkage, and the over-delivery leg is inventory-driven overshoot by liquidity providers who absorbed the systematic shock — capital that is scarce and inattentive at this frequency. Falsifiable: if the cumulative-increment weights beyond lag 6 (the reversal region) add nothing over the parent's truncated lag-1..6 fold, or if the response-lag-centroid gate fails to discriminate, the hypothesis dies.
factors.name: IRF cumulative-increment overshoot fold (6-bar)

factors.trading_idea: Treat each name's standardized displacement z from its own slow anchor as a particle in a potential U(z): the conditional 6-bar drift is the Kramers-Moyal first coefficient -U'(z), which I estimate per name by a trailing OLS of realized 6-bar log returns on the Hermite basis {z, z^3-3z} evaluated 6 bars earlier — so the *sign and curvature* of the local drift are learned from that name's own dynamics rather than imposed (a<0 = single restoring well, a>0 with b<0 = locally unstable barrier that lets the price escape before being caught in the tails). The tradable object is the precision-weighted *deviation* of each name's fitted drift curve from the contemporaneous cross-sectional consensus curve (empirical-Bayes shrinkage toward the pooled coefficients), i.e. how much faster or slower this book's liquidity providers restore price than the average book at the same displacement; the signal is that idiosyncratic drift function evaluated at the current z, damped when the current activity level (volume energy) is far above the estimation window's norm and the fitted potential is therefore off-calibration. The edge should persist because everyone applies a single, homogeneous short-horizon reversal prior, whereas the heterogeneity and anharmonicity of per-name resiliency is a second-order slope difference that requires noisy nonlinear conditional-mean estimation per name, is worth only a fraction of the spread per trade, and is therefore capacity-limited rather than arbitraged. It is falsified if the shrunk coefficient deviations carry no forward information (IC ~ 0), or if the anharmonic term adds nothing over the linear one, meaning the potential is universally harmonic and the factor collapses to plain reversal (which would also show up as redundancy with the book).
factors.name: Anharmonic Langevin drift (idiosyncratic restoring force)

factors.trading_idea: Kyle/Glosten-Milgrom says the permanence of a short-run price displacement is the market's estimate of how likely the pushing flow was informed; that likelihood is a *cross-sectional* property of the name's fundamental information environment, not of the tape alone. So the child splits each name's 6-bar sector-beta-residual displacement by whether concordant aggressive flow stands behind it, and then lets a slow, point-in-time opacity composite (accrual quality, intangible and R&D intensity, size, earnings unpredictability) set the sign of the flow-confirmed leg: in opaque names informed single-name flow dominates and confirmed displacement continues, in transparent names even flow-backed displacement is uninformed inventory pressure and snaps back, and displacement with no flow behind it (quote shading) reverts in both. The edge should persist because it lives in a data/horizon gap: HFT liquidity providers condition on order flow but not on accrual quality or intangibility, while the fundamental investors who own those characteristics do not trade minute-ahead reversals, so nobody arbitrages the interaction. It is falsifiable in the sharpest possible way: the coefficient on the flow-confirmed displacement leg must flip sign between the top and bottom opacity terciles — if it does not, the interaction is void and the factor collapses to a plain unbacked-displacement fade.
factors.name: Adverse-selection-gated permanence of flow-confirmed idiosyncratic displacement

factors.trading_idea: Parent A showed that a short-run equity impulse which de-levers (via Merton elasticity ≈ assets/equity) into an implausibly large *implied asset shock* is prima facie non-fundamental and reverts; parent B showed that whether one-sided pressure reverts or continues depends on volume confirmation, but applied that gate to a slow variance-asymmetry level with no 6-bar edge. The child conditions A's proven de-levered impulse on B's signed participation gate: the leverage de-levering measures *how much fundamental news the move would require*, while participation measures *whether any news actually arrived*. A large implied asset shock on below-normal volume is arithmetically impossible as information — pure quote withdrawal / one-sided liquidity demand — and snaps back within a minute, whereas the same large implied asset shock on above-normal volume is a genuine, low-leverage asset repricing that keeps diffusing, so the gate flips sign rather than merely amplifying magnitude (A's gate could only scale, never flip). The interaction carries edge neither parent has: A pays the same reversal to informed low-leverage repricings it should be trading with, and B's gate had no impulse worth splitting.
factors.name: De-levered asset-shock reversal/continuation split by participation

factors.trading_idea: Parent A asserts a fixed sign structure — quiet (zero/thin-volume) repricing continues, volume-paid displacement reverts — while Parent B shows that a pooled, self-calibrating conditional-expectation estimator can learn response coefficients but was pointed at the wrong state (raw displacement x volume, whose marginals the book already spans and whose double-centred interaction was estimation noise). The child keeps Parent A's volume-attributed decomposition of recent drift as the *predictor pair* (quiet-bar drift, active-bar drift) and uses Parent B's causal EWMA-pooled cross-sectional regression machinery to estimate the two response slopes — separately inside each own-history tercile of trading intensity, so the relative weight of continuation versus impact-decay adapts to the flow regime instead of being hard-coded ±1. The interaction carries edge neither parent has alone because the true economics is state-dependent: in a low-intensity regime a quiet mid drift is genuine inventory/adverse-selection repricing (continuation) whereas in a high-intensity regime the same quiet bars are stale mids inside an active metaorder and their drift is transient, and only a regime-conditional slope can express both without a sign fight; estimating slopes on an already-orthogonal decomposition (rather than an ANOVA residual of an over-mined surface) also puts the fitted signal at the fixed 6-bar offset where the realised horizon return is measured.
factors.name: Flow-regime-calibrated quiet vs traded drift slopes

factors.trading_idea: Liquidity providers repay a transient price push when counterparty flow arrives, i.e. in *volume time*, not calendar time — so the calendar-time repayment horizon is itself a random variable governed by trade-arrival intensity. That is why the parent's fixed calendar-lag kernel smeared its mass out to ~12 bars: in quiet stretches the unwind simply had not happened yet. The child instead carries an explicit state variable, the outstanding trade-backed inventory debt accumulated with a decay rate proportional to realised volume (a volume-clock EWMA), and multiplies it by the fraction of that debt expected to be discharged inside exactly the next 6 bars, forecast from volume clustering (trailing activity rate persists, Hawkes-style). A per-name, horizon-matched trailing regression of realised 6-bar returns on the *lagged* conditioned state learns whether flow reciprocates or propagates, so no sign is imposed; the edge survives arbitrage because harvesting it means posting passive size against possibly-informed aggressive flow for a fraction of a spread — inventory and adverse-selection risk, not a mispricing. Falsifiable: the interaction (debt x expected in-window repayment fraction) should have a higher IC at 6 bars than debt alone, and its IC profile should peak at 6 rather than 12 bars; if activity conditioning is irrelevant the two collapse to the same signal.
factors.name: Volume-clock inventory debt with in-window repayment fraction (h=6)

factors.trading_idea: Both parents agree in *realised* direction: drift printed in low-volume bars (unabsorbed quote repricing) keeps going over the next minute, while drift paid for with heavy volume is temporary impact that snaps back — Parent B's declared sign was contradicted precisely because volume-backed, jump-carried drift reverts. The child keeps Parent A's volume-stream split of drift but replaces A's slow, expensive 180-bar Rice/arccos gate with Parent B's *local* scale-free magnitude-concentration statistic (inverse participation ratio n·Σr⁴/(Σr²)², Gaussian null 3) computed separately inside each stream over the same short 24-bar window as the drift itself. The interaction is the edge neither has: a large single quiet-bar increment is a stale-mid gap (noise), so the quiet leg is trusted only when it is diffuse grind, whereas a concentrated heavy-volume increment is a jump into thin depth, so the active leg is faded hardest exactly then and left alone when it is a still-working sliced order. Finally the composite is cross-sectionally orthogonalised against the plain 24-bar normalised drift, so what survives is pure state-conditioning rather than the crowded momentum/reversal level that made Parent A marginally redundant.
factors.name: Locally IPR-gated quiet-grind vs traded-jump drift split

factors.trading_idea: The seam (open minus previous close) is structurally the leg where a maker relocates quotes with no trades in between, so Parent B's 'silent repricing' and Parent A's 'seam' are the same object seen from two angles — but their economics are opposite and a per-name state variable decides which one holds. I estimate each name's reciprocation gain as the trailing OLS beta of the peer-neutral seam on the previous bar's *traded* body (volume-weighted), i.e. the fraction of trade-driven impact handed back at the next quote relocation; in high-gain names the seam is absorption giving back transient impact, so the fresh traded body push should be faded, while in low/zero-gain names the seam is an unopposed reservation-price ramp, so its fresh band-passed rate (fast-minus-slow EWMA, gated by the persistence of silence) should be followed. The interaction is the edge: Parent A only ever fades and needs a gate to know where fading pays, Parent B always longs silence and shorts traded flow regardless of whether that name's makers actually reciprocate — routing B's two legs by A's reciprocation gain turns a weak always-on spread into a state-contingent one that resolves inside the 6-bar window.
factors.name: Silence-routed seam reciprocation gain split

factors.trading_idea: Parent B says slow-clientele names owe the market a beta-implied move after a shock, but its wedge cannot distinguish two very different reasons a name failed to follow: (i) its mid is mechanically stuck on a tick-grid level with real resting size being absorbed there — the owed move is undelivered, not refused, and it prints as soon as the queue clears; (ii) the name has been freely repricing and still did not follow — that is genuine idiosyncratic disagreement and no catch-up is owed. Parent A's machinery supplies exactly that missing state variable: the grid-quantum pin indicator plus the volume absorbed while pinned. The child therefore scales B's clientele-weighted beta wedge by A's pin-and-absorption block state, and then applies A's lesson about its own failure — the raw wedge is dominated by the −own-move term that generic short-term reversal already spans, so the gated wedge is cross-sectionally Gram-Schmidt purged of 1-bar and 6-bar returns and recent volume intensity, leaving only the queue-blocked, slow-capital catch-up component that neither parent isolates.
factors.name: Pin-Absorption Gated Beta Catch-Up (reversal-purged)

factors.trading_idea: Systemic liquidity stress (price impact per unit of participation) is strongly common across names and is a fast mean-reverting state variable: dealers withdraw depth in bursts and replenish it within a minute. If a name's return has trailing sensitivity b_i to innovations in its *peers'* stress state (leave-one-out sector mean, so the state contains none of the name's own price or volume), then the forecastable normalisation of that state, E[dS] = (1-phi^6)(S_bar - S_t) from a trailing AR(1)/OU fit, maps mechanically into a forecastable return b_i*E[dS] — the snapback is inherited through the transmission channel rather than read off the name's own recent move. The edge should persist because the carrier is a slow structural loading (a stress beta) crossed with a market-state clock, whereas market-makers and standard reversal arbitrageurs standardise by own realised volatility and hedge own-name displacement; nobody is paid to hedge the covariance of a name with the *replenishment cycle of peer liquidity*. Falsifiable: the peer stress state must be measurably mean-reverting, the signal must work with sign +1 (b_i times the predicted stress change, not minus it), and randomising or sign-flipping b_i across names must destroy the IC.
factors.name: Peer liquidity-stress OU transmission beta

factors.trading_idea: The 60-second response to an idiosyncratic mid displacement is not a fixed reversal constant: the *gain* of that response depends on how the move was manufactured — how much traded volume backed it (own-history flow intensity) and how directional the path was (net move / summed absolute moves). Instead of estimating conditional means per state cell (the parent's approach, which is contaminated by each cell's unconditional drift/level composition and needs stale long memory), I estimate a varying-coefficient regression: for each state cell, the pooled panel slope beta(u) of the realised next-6-bar market-neutral displacement on the current signed displacement. Because the regressor is signed, any cell-specific level or drift cancels exactly and both signs of a move contribute to the same slope, roughly doubling effective sample and removing the mis-identification that made the parent's surface anti-predictive. I then subtract the pooled unconditional slope, so the signal is the *deviation* of the local gain from the average gain times the displacement — arithmetically near-orthogonal to any fixed-gain reversal factor in the book, which is precisely why it is not arbitraged: production books carry one reversal term with at most a monotone liquidity tilt, not a jointly estimated, regime-tracking gain surface in flow x path-shape space.
factors.name: Varying-coefficient reversal gain over flow x path-shape grid

factors.trading_idea: A 10-second mid move is only *validated* to the extent that inventory actually changed hands while it happened: displacement printed in bars whose volume is far below the name's own norm is either a market-maker inventory skew (quotes shaded to attract the offsetting side) or one-sided cancellation flicker, neither of which transfers information, so it is unwound as soon as flow resumes; displacement printed on genuine volume is paid-for immediacy and is largely permanent. The child therefore builds a *continuous* confirmation weight w = 1/(1+v/v_median) per bar, splits the last 6 bars of standardised drift into an unbacked leg U (weighted by w) and a backed leg C (weighted by 1-w), each divided by its own iid standard error, and trades only the WEDGE U - C — which is nearly orthogonal to plain 6-bar reversal (that uses U + C) and is zero whenever displacement is spread evenly across confirmation levels. Because the unwind is executed in volume time, not clock time, the wedge is multiplied by a payback hazard pi = 1 - exp(-lambda), lambda = fast/slow EWM volume ratio: a skew only gets resolved inside a fixed 6-bar window if trade arrival is currently running at or above the name's normal rate. The parent's failure is the evidence base for the polarity: its adaptive per-name regression coefficient was too noisy a nuisance parameter and left the composite leaning continuation, while realised IC was negative at 1-6 bars — i.e. unvalidated quote displacement reverts fast, which is exactly what this child asserts and prices; the edge survives arbitrage because standard reversal engines pool backed and unbacked displacement (diluting the wedge to near zero) and because acting on it requires waiting on flow arrival, i.e. low, event-contingent capacity.
factors.name: Unbacked-vs-backed displacement wedge with volume-clock payback gate

factors.trading_idea: The parent assumed that a large repurchase program *implies* absorption of dips; but 10b-18 programs are lumpy inside the quarter (blackout windows, VWAP schedules, daily ADV caps), so the filing is only a noisy prior on whether an anonymous price-contingent buyer is standing in the book right now. The child therefore *measures* the state directly: for each name it estimates, from strictly past non-overlapping 6-bar blocks, the realised elasticity of the subsequent 6-bar idiosyncratic return to the size of the preceding idiosyncratic DOWN push (and separately to the UP push), and shrinks each firm's noisy elasticity toward a hierarchical empirical-Bayes prior whose cross-sectional mean is tilted by repurchase capacity. Because the 10b-18 safe harbour lets the desk bid only passively at or below the last independent bid, the absorption must show up as a positive down-leg elasticity with no matching up-leg elasticity, so the traded signal is the asymmetry wedge (shrunk down-elasticity x current dip minus shrunk up-elasticity x current pop) with dip, pop and capacity main effects purged cross-sectionally. This survives arbitrage because it needs a quarterly cash-flow item joined to a per-name, rolling, block-lagged elasticity estimated at 10-second resolution, and because the absorbing liquidity itself is finite: no instrument pays for it, and consuming it destroys it.
factors.name: Buyback-prior-shrunk dip-absorption elasticity wedge

factors.trading_idea: Whether a 60-second idiosyncratic displacement continues or snaps back is not a universal constant: it is governed by the sign of that name's own block-to-block autocovariance at exactly the forecast horizon, and that quantity is a persistent structural property of the name's microstructure (tick-size binding, queue thickness, whether its flow is dominated by market-maker inventory oscillation or by sliced metaorders). I estimate it robustly and horizon-matched: the quadrant (Blomqvist) concordance between adjacent NON-overlapping 6-bar idiosyncratic blocks, inverted through the Gaussian copula (rho = sin(pi*C/2)), then cross-sectionally demeaned so the factor carries only the *dispersion* in reversal speed and not the panel-average reversal the book already spans. The parent's error was to assume one fixed direction (queue-clearing continuation) for every name and then purge the carrier it was actually loading on; the child instead lets each name declare its own direction, so the realized sign cannot contradict the hypothesis without the autocorrelation estimate itself being unstable. It survives arbitrage because the edge lives in per-name calibration of a slow structural coefficient, and the largest coefficients sit precisely in the noisy, spread-wide names where crossing costs eat a generic reversal trade.
factors.name: Blomqvist-inverted block autocorrelation reversal-speed wedge

factors.trading_idea: Keep the parent's useful insight — peer groups must be comparable in *multiple space*, not by industry text — but replace its slow multi-minute spread-dislocation with a mechanism that acts on the exact 60-second horizon: a name's very recent move relative to its true comparables is either quote/inventory noise or information, and the discriminator is whether trades actually printed. On LOBSTER-style 10-second bars the mid can drift several ticks with almost no signed trade volume (one-sided quote repricing, market-maker inventory skew), and such displacement is mechanically pulled back once the resting book refills, whereas the same displacement accompanied by an idiosyncratic volume burst is informed and continues. So the sign of the coefficient on the peer-residual 6-bar impulse should FLIP with trade confirmation, measured as the name's own volume surge net of its peer group's surge (which strips sector-wide news bursts). The edge survives arbitrage because it requires joining point-in-time per-share fundamentals (to form valuation-tier comparability groups) with 10-second trade data — pure microstructure desks never build the fundamental peer map, and fundamental relative-value desks cannot act in one minute — and the per-trade edge is small enough to be capacity-limited. Falsified if the impulse coefficient is the same for high- and low-confirmation names (then it is just peer-relative reversal), or if valuation-tier grouping adds nothing over plain sector grouping.
factors.name: Valuation-tier peer impulse with trade-confirmation flip

factors.trading_idea: The parent folded lagged market loadings b_1..b_6 onto the observed market path but truncated the kernel at lag 6, so for a shock aged k bars it silently dropped all response mass at lags (6, k+6] — the mathematically correct horizon-matched coefficient on m_{t-k} is C(k+H)-C(k), a *differenced* cumulative response, not C(H)-C(k).  Truncation both under-counts genuine catch-up and, crucially, throws away the negative tail of the response (the inventory-driven overshoot) that shows up as the parent's IC sign flip between 6 and 24 bars.  The child estimates the whole impulse response in a smooth three-timescale exponential basis (4 trailing-OLS parameters instead of 6+ noisy free betas, with a shared market-side Gram matrix), so the kernel extends past the horizon, can change sign, and folds analytically into E[sum_{j=1..6} r_{t+j}] = sum_h a_h G_h psi_h(t).  The forecast is then scaled by an explained-covariance 'kernel trust' term (empirical-Bayes weight on the lag terms' partial R^2), amplified where repricing is demonstrably slow (frozen-mid fraction, bars since the last mid update, thin relative volume), and switched on only when the aggregate move is a genuine common shock (cross-sectional sign breadth), because with low breadth there is no common information to catch up to.  It survives arbitrage because harvesting it needs simultaneous second-scale execution in exactly the slow-updating, thin names where spread and impact cap capacity, and because the kernel *shape* (which timescale, which sign) is name-specific and non-stationary.
factors.name: Horizon-differenced exponential-basis impulse kernel (trust & breadth gated)

factors.trading_idea: The parent's edge lived in intra-bar wick geometry (excursion vs endpoint), which the book already spans; this child throws that away and instead uses the *topology of consecutive bar ranges* to split the same displacement into two physically different components. Because [low,high] of bar t either overlaps bar t-1 or is disjoint from it, every log return decomposes exactly into (i) a GAP part — the signed disjoint jump between ranges, i.e. price relocated to a region where the market never rested — and (ii) a GRIND part — displacement achieved while price kept re-trading inside an overlapping band. Gapping means levels were cleared without the market spending time (and, when volume is thin, without any trade validating the new price): it is a liquidity-vacuum overshoot that liquidity providers get paid to fade, so it reverts. Grinding against resting liquidity with real traded size is the footprint of a sliced metaorder whose order flow is strongly autocorrelated, so it continues over the next minute; the churn/discovery regime is read from the trailing Jaccard overlap of consecutive ranges and used to weight the two legs. The edge persists because harvesting it means supplying liquidity exactly where the book just gapped, and its capacity is bounded by that same thin depth.
factors.name: Range-overlap decomposed gap-vs-grind displacement split

factors.trading_idea: A basket/program execution deposits inventory into every market maker in proportion to capitalisation weight divided by that name's depth, so the *cross-sectional shape* of signed order flow in a program bar is proportional to z_i = weight_i / dollar-ADV_i (exactly Parent A's inverse-turnover elasticity, exp(kappa)); I recover the program's signed dollar size each bar as the cross-sectional OLS slope of ADV-normalised signed flow on z, shrunk by the bar's explained cross-sectional variance, and keep only the fitted (mechanically allocated) part of each name's flow. That basket-attributed flow is uninformed by construction, so unlike Parent B's total signed-flow inventory it carries no adverse-selection/permanent-impact component: I accumulate it with an exponential inventory kernel, convert it to return units with Parent B's shrunk Kyle-lambda, subtract the part a beta hedge already removes (name beta times the cap-weighted average program push, i.e. Parent A's 'elasticity in excess of beta' written as a hedging residual), and damp it by Parent B's saturating trade-clock clearing fraction 6-bar expected volume / (expected volume + |inventory|). The interaction is the edge: Parent A knows *when and where* a move is mechanical but has no per-name inventory or clearing clock and so cannot time the snapback, while Parent B has the clock but feeds it flow that mixes informed with mechanical order flow, which is why its edge only matures at 24 bars — purging the informed component makes the reversion fast and complete, i.e. it lands on the fixed 6-bar offset.
factors.name: Basket-attributed dealer inventory, beta-purged and cleared on the trade clock

factors.trading_idea: Parent A shows that dislocations of a name from its valuation-matched, beta-hedged peer basket snap back on a ~1-minute clock, and damps the bet with *unsigned* volume — but unsigned volume conflates two opposite states: two-sided churn (pure liquidity, maximally transient) and one-sided metaorder flow (informed, permanent). Parent B supplies the missing signed decomposition, and its sign inversion tells us how to use it correctly: on a mid-quote tape the flow-*unexplained* part of a displacement is quote shading / stale-mid flicker and mean-reverts, while the part a name's own trailing Kyle lambda can account for is genuine, at least partly permanent, impact. The child therefore estimates the idiosyncratic lambda by regressing the *valuation-hedged residual* increments (not raw returns) on signed sqrt-volume, splits the 3-bar hedged dislocation into lambda-explained impact and quiet residual, fades the quiet part with amplitude proportional to hedge R-squared (hedgeability is the economic prerequisite for fast arbitrage), and fades the impact part only when signed flow lacks lag-1 persistence — standing aside when a metaorder is demonstrably still being worked. The interaction is the edge: neither the unsigned volume damper (A) nor the sector-demeaned return decomposition (B) can tell a hedgeable, flow-free, churn-driven spread wobble (fade hard) from an unhedgeable, flow-backed metaorder push (do not touch).
factors.name: Valuation-hedged idiosyncratic Kyle-lambda quiet snapback

factors.trading_idea: A name's beta-owed adjustment to a market shock is not paid in continuous time — it has to be paid at the price grid, and a large resting queue at the touch acts as a dam. So the same absorbed-volume-at-a-pin state that Parent A measures tells us where in the payment cycle a name is: while the mid is pinned and heavy volume is being absorbed, the owed catch-up (Parent B's beta wedge) is dammed and about to be released within a few bars, which is precisely why the wedge should pay off at the fixed 6-bar offset rather than drifting out to 12+ bars; once the level actually breaks, the part of the displacement that exceeds what the concurrent market move justified is a metaorder chewing through the wall — transient impact, not information — and it snaps back, which explains why Parent A's declared continuation sign was contradicted. The child therefore keeps an owed-versus-delivered budget per name: clientele-weighted dammed backlog (buy the un-paid beta debt of slow-capital names whose queue is nearly consumed) minus absorption-weighted post-break overshoot (fade the beta-unjustified part already over-delivered), with a market-shock switch that tilts weight toward the backlog leg after sharp market moves and toward the queue-clearing reversion leg in quiet regimes. The interaction is the edge: the wedge alone cannot time closure (it is blocked by the grid), and the pin-break displacement alone cannot tell an informative repricing from an over-payment of an existing beta debt.
factors.name: Dammed beta backlog vs queue-clearing overshoot

factors.trading_idea: Parent B shows that drift printed in near-zero-volume bars (quote repricing) continues while drift paid for with volume (temporary impact) reverts; parent A shows that a given amount of drift can be grind-carried (sign-persistent, many small same-signed steps) or jump-carried (magnitude-concentrated relative to the Rice/Gaussian sign-flip null arccos(rho)/pi), and that the two decay differently. The child computes the Rice sign-flip gap *separately within each volume regime* — over adjacent quiet-quiet return pairs and adjacent active-active pairs — and uses each regime's own gap as the continuation weight on that regime's drift leg: concentration (gap>0) means the move was information-like and keeps going, sign-persistence (gap<0) means a working order or a stale-mid ladder whose push is already spent and snaps back. The interaction carries edge neither parent has because the quiet leg's grind/jump character is precisely the falsification test B named (stale-mid noise vs genuine adverse-selection repricing), and the active leg's gap separates informed liquidity-vacuum jumps from mechanical slicing impact — a discrimination that A, which pools all bars into one autocorrelation, cannot make.
factors.name: Regime-Split Rice Gap: Quiet vs Traded Drift Continuation

factors.trading_idea: A metaorder being sliced into the book leaves an *ordinal* footprint rather than a magnitude footprint: its child orders nudge the mid in one direction repeatedly, so the trailing price path contains an unusually long monotone chain even when the net displacement is tiny and buried in bid-ask bounce. I measure this with the length of the longest non-decreasing subsequence of the last n mids minus the longest non-increasing one (Ulam's problem; standardised by the Tracy-Widom fluctuation scale n^(1/6), which is the correct null scale for i.i.d. increments), average it over two window scales, strip out the part explainable by the plain trailing return via a per-bar cross-sectional regression, and up-weight names that traded in most bars of the window (continuous slicing footprint, not one block print). The residual therefore isolates *magnitude-free ordinal persistence*, which reflects an execution program still working and should continue over the next ~minute, whereas the magnitude component it is orthogonalised against is where transient-impact reversal lives. It survives arbitrage because the longest-monotone-chain statistic is a non-smooth extreme order statistic that moment-based models (autocorrelations, drift t-stats, propagator fits) are structurally blind to, and because monetising it means queueing alongside a live hidden aggressor in the same thin depth, so capacity is capped by the very liquidity scarcity that creates the pattern.
factors.name: Ulam monotone-chain excess (ordinal slicing footprint)

factors.trading_idea: The parent's realized IC sign says that fresh sqrt-volume-weighted directional pressure at the 10-second scale precedes *reversal*, not continuation — the natural reading is that most one-minute mid-price pushes are transient impact from an execution that has already finished, and the price relaxes as depth refills. Whether a push continues or relaxes therefore should not be read from the push itself but from whether the order flow that produced it is still arriving: under Hawkes self-excitation and metaorder splitting, child orders arrive in bursts whose arrival intensity accelerates while the parent order is unfinished and decays once it completes. The child multiplies the sqrt-law directional pressure of the last 6 bars by a peer-demeaned arrival-intensity tilt (fast vs slow EWMA of sqrt-volume), predicting continuation when a name's flow is still building relative to the cross-section and reversal when it is dying — an interaction, so it is nearly orthogonal to the plain reversal already in the book. The edge persists because it requires joint, sub-minute conditioning on flow direction *and* arrival-intensity dynamics, and its capacity is bounded by spread costs, so exploiting it does not remove the still-to-arrive child orders that generate it.
factors.name: Arrival-intensity tilt gated square-root flow pressure

factors.trading_idea: Parent B splits recent drift by *whether* a bar traded; Parent A splits it by *how much* a per-name impact coefficient lambda says the observed flow should have moved the price. The child does both at once: within the last 12 bars it isolates (i) drift printed in quiet bars (no inventory transfer at all), (ii) the part of traded-bar drift that exceeds lambda*flow (a quote revision the tape did not pay for), and (iii) the part lambda fully explains (transient impact that decays as depth replenishes) — and it gates the whole decomposition by the trailing uncentred R-squared of the impact fit. The R-squared gate is the interaction neither parent has: quiet-bar drift is only credible *repricing* in names whose prices demonstrably respond mechanically to flow, because in low-R-squared names a move with no trade is exactly parent B's falsification case (stale-mid / bounce noise) and carries no information; conversely lambda-residuals are only interpretable where lambda itself is identified. Weighting the last 12 bars with a linear decay puts the displacement centroid ~4 bars back so the transient/permanent contrast is matched to the fixed 6-bar forward offset rather than the 24-bar horizon where both parents peaked.
factors.name: Trust-gated triple split: quiet repricing vs lambda-residual vs paid impact

factors.trading_idea: At 10-second granularity a price path is produced by a mixture of two agents whose identity persists for tens of minutes: (i) parent orders being sliced by execution algorithms, whose long-memory child-order flow imprints POSITIVE minute-scale return autocorrelation, and (ii) liquidity providers recycling inventory, whose transient impact and quote bounce imprint NEGATIVE autocorrelation. Rather than assuming reversal or continuation, the child *measures* which agent currently dominates each name — a causal trailing OLS of the 6-bar return on the previous 6-bar return — shrinks that estimate toward a mechanism-driven prior by its own statistical reliability (empirical Bayes with weight rho^2/(rho^2+rho0^2)), where the prior centre is set by the persistence of the name's deseasonalised bar volume (autocorrelated volume = a parent order still being worked = continuation prior), and then applies the shrunken response coefficient to the live standardised shock. The edge is falsifiable: if the participant mix were not persistent, this interaction would earn zero IC even though both plain momentum and plain reversal are non-degenerate; it survives arbitrage because harvesting it requires per-name, per-episode state estimation and takes the *opposite* side in different names at the same instant, so it cannot be crowded by a single directional reversal or momentum book.
factors.name: Empirical-Bayes adaptive shock-response state (order-splitting memory vs inventory recycling)

factors.trading_idea: Parent A measured how much market-driven repricing a name still owes and how fast its quote clock can pay it; parent B measured whether recent volume arrived as an even schedule or as a concentrated burst — and both parents' realized signs say the same thing once read together: information arrives in bursts, while evenly-sliced participation is uninformative liquidity demand whose price effect is transient impact that makers unwind within a minute. The child therefore takes A's Dimson-purged idiosyncratic displacement (the 6-bar move left after removing contemporaneous and lagged market beta, i.e. the part that is genuinely the name's own repricing) and ROUTES its sign with B's volume-concentration state: extrapolate the idio displacement when the last 30 bars' volume mass just concentrated (entropy innovation negative → informed burst, permanent impact, order-flow self-excitation continues), fade it when participation just turned unusually even (scheduler → transient impact). The whole thing is then scaled by A's Poisson deliverable share 1−exp(−λ·6) on the name's own re-quote hazard, because neither continuation nor reversal can be realized inside a fixed 6-bar window if the mid does not re-quote. The interaction is the edge: the displacement alone is sign-ambiguous (continuation and impact-decay cancel), the concentration state alone is a pure conditioning variable with no direction, and the re-quote hazard alone only sets magnitude — only their product identifies displacement that is both informative AND physically payable at the fixed 6-bar offset.
factors.name: Burst-informativeness routed Dimson idio backlog (6-bar)

factors.trading_idea: Both parents split 6-bar displacement into a volume-backed and a volume-unbacked piece, but each hard-coded the polarity of the two pieces: parent A signed the traded piece with a flow-cessation clock, parent B scaled both pieces by a single unconditional Roll noise share. The child measures transience *conditionally on the flow regime itself*: it estimates two separate Roll relations per name, phi_active from the trailing subsample of high-flow (burst) bars and phi_quiet from the low-flow bars, and it partitions the last 6 bars of log displacement with the same mask into a burst-bar sum and a quiet-bar sum. Displacement accumulated in quiet bars is faded in proportion to the name's measured *quiet-state* flicker share (depth withdrawal/refill noise no trade paid for), while displacement accumulated in burst bars is faded in proportion to phi_active only while flow is still running — and ridden in proportion to the permanent share (1 - phi_active) once the flow-cessation clock says the burst has stopped and the move has survived. The interaction is the edge: knowing *where in the flow regime* a name's transient variance actually lives tells you which of its two displacement channels is refundable, something neither an unconditional noise share (parent B, deflated t ~ 0) nor a clock without a measured transience amplitude (parent A) can express.
factors.name: Flow-regime-masked Roll transience split of displacement

factors.trading_idea: Scheduled (TWAP/POV/iceberg-refresh) parent orders leave a *line spectrum* in a name's bar-volume series — a narrow periodic component at the child-order clock (tens of seconds to a few minutes) — whereas informed or liquidity-shock flow arrives as broadband, heavy-tailed bursts. If the recent price drift was produced by a still-working scheduled executor, its mechanical impact keeps accruing and the drift continues over the next minute; if it was produced by a burst, the move overshot and reverts as liquidity replenishes. The child therefore forms a pure interaction: recent idiosyncratic drift times a *self-referenced* spectral fingerprint of volume (Fisher's g concentration of the trailing 60-bar volume periodogram minus volume dispersion, each z-scored against the name's own history), scaled by the current volume rate because both impact accrual and replenishment run on the trade clock. It is falsifiable — the interaction coefficient must be positive at 6 bars while the drift alone carries little cross-sectional information — and it should not decay to zero at short horizons because the mechanism is a currently-active execution, not a slowly amortising dislocation. It resists arbitrage because the profitable side is warehousing risk alongside a forced executor who may stop at any moment, and because the gate needs each name's own volume spectrum relative to its own norm, an object pooled reversal/momentum signals cannot see.
factors.name: Execution-schedule periodicity gate on impact continuation vs burst reversal

factors.trading_idea: The parent proved that the Epps/lag-1-corrected precision-whitened dislocation is a real relative-value coordinate and that the antisymmetric lag-1 correlation identifies who leads and who lags, but it expressed the trade through a one-bar velocity (phase), so all of its predictive content was realised in the first bar and only noise-inflated variance was left by bar six. The child replaces the instantaneous-phase expression with a *self-calibrated horizon-matched projection*: the dislocation is first split into a persistent component (short EWMA, which removes the quote-noise part whose one-bar reversal does not survive into the mid-price six bars later) and, on a trailing window, each name's own six-bar reversion coefficient beta_i is estimated by regressing the realised six-bar change of that persistent spread on its own six-bar-lagged level, so the signal is literally the conditional expectation of the move that accrues over exactly the fixed offset, not a move that completes instantly. Exposure is then scaled by the measured quality of that per-name regression (rho^2 shrinkage), by the share of dislocation variance that is persistent rather than transient, and by the confirmed lead/lag role (laggards get positive coupling and converge, measured leaders get negative coupling and extend), with a slow turning gate replacing the parent's one-bar phase: a spread still widening on a six-bar scale gets no convergence size. The edge should persist because it requires jointly estimating a 360-bar lag-1-corrected precision matrix, per-name six-bar reversion rates and lead/lag roles across the panel — a low-per-name-IC, capacity-limited mid-frequency relative-value trade that is uneconomic for latency arbitrageurs and invisible to single-name reversal models.
factors.name: Self-calibrated 6-bar reversion rate on Epps-corrected precision dislocations

factors.trading_idea: The parent forecast summed *marginal* (univariate) betas on lagged market returns; because 10-second market returns are themselves autocorrelated (nonsynchronous trading), those marginal loadings double-count the same shock, which inflates the owed catch-up and explains why its predictive mass leaked past 6 bars and turned negative (overshoot) at 12–24 bars. The child solves the *joint* distributed-lag normal equations — the design matrix of lagged market returns is common to all names, so one trailing 6×6 Gram matrix is inverted per bar and folded against per-name cross-moments — with the contemporaneous lag included as a control and a lags-5..12 block regressor whose loading measures response mass that lands *outside* the window. It then multiplies the owed balance by the probability that the name actually reprices inside the 6-bar window, 1-(1-u)^6 with u the name's own trailing per-bar repricing-event rate (non-frozen mid or non-zero traded volume): this deliberately inverts the parent's staleness amplification, whose sign was wrong at a fixed offset because the stalest names pay their debt after the evaluation window. The edge survives arbitrage because the object being predicted is mechanical delay in quote updating rather than mispricing: fast capital can only harvest it on names it can trade at the moment the update fires, and the joint-loading correction plus delivery weighting is what keeps the payoff inside the six bars.
factors.name: Orthogonalised Lag-Kernel Catch-Up × Within-Horizon Delivery Probability

factors.trading_idea: Parent A measured how much market-driven move a name still 'owes' but never subtracted the name's own realised move, so it degenerated into a beta-timed bet on 1-minute market reversal; parent B measured the *shape* of participation (even scheduler-like volume vs. one-bar bursts) but applied it to raw own-path momentum, which the book already spans. The child builds a proper horizon-matched dislocation D = (Dimson beta x trailing 6-bar market return) - (own trailing 6-bar return), i.e. the unabsorbed systematic move net of what the name actually did, and lets B's participation-shape state decide whether that gap is a liquidity error to collect or information to respect: when the last 30 bars' volume is spread evenly across bars (uninformed / scheduled provision, entropy innovation high) an idiosyncratic gap versus the beta-implied path is transient inventory pressure and closes inside the next minute, so trade D long; when volume mass is concentrated in one or two bars (sweep / news print, entropy innovation low) the displacement is informed and keeps extending, so the same gap must be faded.
