The interaction carries edge neither parent has because it converts a benchmark-relative dislocation of known sign ambiguity into a state-dependent trade, purging the unconditional beta-timing loading (A) and the unconditional momentum loading (B) that killed both parents.
factors.name: Participation-shape switched Dimson beta gap (6-bar)

factors.trading_idea: Splitting each bar into a traded leg (close-open) and a pure quote-relocation seam (open-previous close) lets one *measure*, per name, the whole distributed-lag profile g_1..g_8 of how much of a trade-driven push the name's liquidity providers walk back at each subsequent seam — not just a single lag-1 gain. Because market-maker inventory-unwind latency is a per-name policy artifact (queue position, hedging cadence), some names give the push back in one bar and owe nothing later, while others pay it back over 2-8 bars; only the portion of the kernel mass that lands strictly inside the next 6 bars is forecastable at the fixed 6-bar offset, so the child projects exactly that remaining mass (sum of g_j for j in (k, k+6] against the push made k bars ago) instead of assuming the giveback is imminent. A second, complementary state is the unpaid ledger: when realized seams have under-delivered the kernel's scheduled relocation, the balance is still owed and should be paid inside the horizon. The edge survives arbitrage because the kernel is only identifiable from a joint seam/body decomposition over a long per-name trailing window, its payoff is a few basis points at the one-minute scale, and it is capacity-limited and invisible to any pooled (cross-sectionally averaged) impact model.
factors.name: Walk-back lag-kernel window mass with unpaid-giveback ledger

factors.trading_idea: Inventory-pressure dislocations against a valuation- and size-matched peer basket do not decay on a wall-clock schedule: they are cleared by *trading*, one unit of traded volume at a time, so the economically relevant state variable is the volume-clock-discounted sum of past tier-relative residuals (the imbalance that has *survived* the trading that has already happened), not a fixed 3-bar impulse. The forecastable part of that survivor over the next 6 bars is only the fraction expected to clear inside the horizon, which is governed by the name's expected trade intensity (10-second volume is strongly persistent), so the same dislocation predicts a big snapback in a busy name and almost nothing in a dormant one. As in the parent, the neighbourhood-common part of the survivor is a genuine omitted tier factor that cannot be closed by one desk trading one stock, so it is purged — but with a unit loading (kernel-demeaning) instead of a 360-bar per-name regression, removing two noisy nuisance parameters that made the parent's in-sample IC collapse. Falsifiable: if a fixed clock-time window plus the parent's R-squared gate predicts as well as the trade-time survivor times the expected-clearing gate, then trade-time decay is not the operative clock; the edge survives arbitrage because it needs point-in-time per-share fundamentals joined to a 10-second tape to define the neighbourhood plus a per-name trade-time state recursion, and its capacity is capped by the small number of tight valuation/size neighbourhoods.
factors.name: Trade-clock surviving tier dislocation with expected-clearing gate

factors.trading_idea: Parent B showed that the persistence of a 10-second idiosyncratic move (bounce vs. order-splitting) is a per-name kernel that flips with the volume regime; Parent A showed that a name's short-horizon conditional drift map lives on a richer discrete microstructure state, but it estimated the wrong object — an unsigned drift *level* — and threw away the magnitude of the current shock. The child estimates, per name and per state cell (sign of the innovation x alignment with the prior 3-bar idiosyncratic drift x volume-backed/quiet), the trailing mean of the realised 6-bar-ahead idiosyncratic return *multiplied by the sign of the innovation that generated it*: a directly horizon-matched signed response coefficient rather than a drift level or a one-step AR kernel that must be extrapolated. That coefficient is empirical-Bayes shrunk toward the name's pooled response, and — the key interaction — A's chi-square between-cell dispersion statistic is used as a *relay weight on the state deviation only*, so the factor collapses gracefully to Parent B's pooled kernel-times-innovation forecast when the state map is statistically indistinguishable, and only pays attention to the state table when the cells genuinely disagree. Neither parent has this: A had no shock magnitude and a poorly conditioned estimand, B had a state space too coarse (volume alone) and needed a geometric extrapolation approximation, while the child's estimand is bounded, sign-aligned, exactly matched to the 6-bar offset, and its extra state resolution is admitted only when it is paid for by measured between-state dispersion.
factors.name: State-conditional signed response kernel with confidence relay

factors.trading_idea: Relative-value desks trade spreads in multiple space (P/B, P/S, P/OCF), not in raw price space, and the credibility of a peer spread depends on how homogeneous the peer group's multiples are: tight within-industry dispersion means the comparables genuinely price the same cash-flow claim, wide dispersion means the 'spread' is a business-mix artefact. High-frequency dislocations of a name's live multiple away from its own recent level, relative to its industry median multiple, should therefore revert within a minute mainly inside tight, comparable peer groups. Falsified if the reversion strength is invariant to peer dispersion, which would imply the signal is just a repackaged peer-relative price reversal.
factors.name: Peer Multiple-Space Dislocation with Comparability Gate

factors.trading_idea: Parent A shows that a volume-backed pin break is a superposition of a mechanical transient overshoot (fades) and a queue-clearing informational move (continues), but it had no state variable telling it which one it just observed — so it realised the sign of the reverting part. Parent B built exactly that state variable: rotating the drift printed in quiet (zero/low-volume, maker-shading) bars against the drift printed in traded (taker) bars into a COMMON component (both channels agree: corroborated repricing) and a WEDGE component (maker inventory vs taker liquidity standoff), and its own report says it earns its keep as a conditioner rather than standalone. The child uses the cross-sectionally demeaned concordance kappa = (|common| - |wedge|)/(|common|+|wedge|) as a *polarity router* for the pin-break displacement (measured in tick-grid quanta and scaled by absorbed-while-pinned and break-bar volume): when the two channels corroborate, the consumed queue was genuine information and the break continues; when the wedge dominates, the same displacement is inventory-driven transient and reverts. Because kappa is demeaned each bar the output is a pure interaction with no net loading on the raw break displacement (which both parents proved is a reverting carrier), and it is additionally purged cross-sectionally of 1- and 6-bar return ranks — edge neither parent has alone, since A supplies the event and B supplies the sign.
factors.name: Pin-break displacement routed by maker/taker channel concordance

factors.trading_idea: Parent A carries a clean state variable — the outstanding, volume-time-discounted stock of trade-backed price-impact debt — but it is blind to whether the metaorder that created that debt is still running: while a parent order is alive, incoming volume *extends* the push rather than repaying it, so A's repayment intensity is mis-signed exactly in the busiest names. Parent B identifies push cessation (displacement velocity turning back toward its peer anchor plus a fast/slow volume contraction) but has no clock, so its relaxation forecast is diffuse and only fully pays out at 24 bars. The child builds A's debt stock out of B's *peer-residual* (sector x valuation-tercile) price increments — removing the common factor that is never repaid by a market maker — and then makes the sign of the volume-clock repayment term a function of B's cessation probability: expected 6-bar relocation = D_t * (1 - exp(-lambda*6*E[u])) * (p_end - kappa*(1 - p_end)). The interaction is the edge: the same forward-flow forecast predicts snap-back when the push is over and further displacement when it is alive, which neither the unsigned debt-repayment of A nor the clockless onset gate of B can express, and it front-loads the payoff into the fixed 6-bar window.
factors.name: Peer-residual impact debt: volume-clock repayment with cessation polarity

factors.trading_idea: Parent B showed that the transitory, inventory-driven pricing error is really two components (a fast one and a slow, large-variance one), but it amortised both on a *calendar* clock with fixed rho's, so its ranking was dominated by the slow error whose repayment mostly lands past the pinned 6-bar offset (IC still climbing at 24 bars).  Parent A showed the error is actually repaid in *volume time* — the market maker sheds inventory only as counter-flow arrives — but with a single blended channel its filter could not separate the fast error from the slow one, so its self-calibrated decay landed in between and its standalone IC was tiny.  The child runs A's volume-time survival filter twice, at a fast and a slow repayment rate per unit of normalised traded volume, recovers the two displacements separately, and identifies their reversal loadings jointly with a trailing sign-restricted two-channel OLS of the idiosyncratic return on each channel's realised volume-clock repayment increment; each displacement then enters the 6-bar forecast weighted only by the fraction 1 - exp(-kappa_x * 6 * E[u]) that the name's own forecast trade arrival will actually repay inside 60 seconds.  The interaction is the edge: collectability-at-6-bars of the slow, high-variance error is nearly constant across names on a calendar clock (B) and invisible when the two errors are blended (A), but on a per-name volume clock it disperses enormously — a big slow dislocation in a name whose trade arrival is running hot is collectable now, while the same dislocation in a stalled name is not, and only the two-channel split lets the ranking spend its budget on the collectable part.
factors.name: Two-channel volume-clock repayment split (fast/slow error, 6-bar collectability)

factors.trading_idea: The parent asserted a fixed story (flow-paid displacement reverts, untraded repricing continues), but whether executed flow's impact has already decayed by the 6-bar mark is a per-name, per-regime property: it is governed by the shape of the impact response curve R(l) = E[log p_{t+l} - log p_t | signed flow at t], i.e. Bouchaud's propagator / Obizhaeva-Wang resilience rate. Instead of assuming the sign, I estimate R(l) directly for each name from completed trailing (flow, forward-move) pairs at every lag l = 1..11, precision-shrink each estimate by its own t-stat (James-Stein style, so noisy lags vanish), and then build the model-implied expected mid-move over exactly the next 6 bars from flow that has already printed: sum_k [R(k+6) - R(k)] * x_{t-k}. Names with fast resilience get negative loadings on recent flow (impact still unwinding), names with slow/permanent response get positive loadings — the direction is learned, not imposed, which is why it should work at the pinned 6-bar offset where the parent's hard-coded sign washed out. The edge persists because it requires estimating a per-name decay kernel rather than one global lambda, the exploitable state is thin-tape names where capacity is small, and the kernel is non-stationary so it must be re-estimated continuously.
factors.name: Horizon-matched propagator-kernel flow forecast

factors.trading_idea: The parent knew *where* a snapback should happen (a thin tail of the trailing occupancy law defended by repeating same-side wick rejections) but keyed on a slow state variable — distance from a 45-bar median — so its reversion accrued over minutes and peaked at 24 bars.  This child keys on the *timing* of the relaxation instead of the level: it estimates when a directional impulse's price progress goes extinct (last-2-bar signed progress collapsing relative to the 6-bar impulse rate, and that deceleration itself just increasing), requires the leading side's failed-excursion wedge to be *building* (hidden depth refreshing in front of the move, not merely present), requires effort to stay high while result dies (3-bar volume above its 60-bar norm — absorption, not evaporation of interest), and requires the new price to sit in a locally *unsupported* region (few of the last 45 mids within a fifth of a robust sigma of it, so no resting inventory was ever accumulated there).  An extinction event is a timestamp, not a distance, so the transient component of impact unwinds immediately after it: the edge should be concentrated in the next handful of bars rather than smeared over 24.  It survives arbitrage because trading it requires taking the opposite side of a metaorder exactly while a hidden queue is still refreshing — an inventory-risk service that is only compensated when the absorption signature is genuine, and the conditioning set (progress deceleration × wedge acceleration × effort × local occupancy void) is not observable from any single-field statistic.
factors.name: Impact-extinction onset with hidden depth and thin support

factors.trading_idea: With no depth feed, the volume it actually took to move the mid up versus down is a consistent estimator of latent book imbalance: displacement-per-unit-sqrt-volume on up bars measures inverse ask depth, the same statistic on down bars measures inverse bid depth. When the ask is thin relative to the bid, mechanically balanced order flow drifts the mid upward (buys travel far, sells travel little), and queue-replenishment rates are strongly autocorrelated over minutes, so the asymmetry survives well past one bar. Crucially the statistic is built from magnitudes only and is then cross-sectionally orthogonalised against the 6-bar and 60-bar net returns, so it is not a repackaged reversal/momentum signal — it is the wedge between price-based and volume-based directionality. The edge persists because harvesting it requires taking or posting on the thin side, where net-of-spread capacity at the one-minute scale is tiny, and any size traded on that side refills the very depth hole that produced the signal.
factors.name: Side-split realized inverse depth wedge (momentum-purged)

factors.trading_idea: Basket/program executions push every name in the sleeve at once in proportion to capitalisation weight divided by available depth, whereas information pushes a name in proportion to its beta; the mechanical part of a push is uncompensated liquidity demand and relaxes within tens of seconds, while the informational part keeps diffusing. The parent measured attribution trust with ONE number per bar (the cross-sectional R-squared of a whitened dislocation on a predicted push), so it could not say WHICH names' pushes actually landed, and it leaned on a 360-bar precision matrix whose eigen-dislocations only relax over ~24 bars — which is exactly why its IC was near zero at 6 bars and largest at 24. The child moves the attribution to the name level and to the mechanical timescale: for each name we measure how much of its very recent variance is explained by the cap-weighted market flow (short-window R-squared minus its own long-run R-squared = comovement-purity excess, a direct microstructural fingerprint of simultaneous basket participation), combine it with the weight-per-depth-minus-beta wedge into a per-name mechanical-attribution probability, then fade that name's beta-attributed 6-bar move in proportion to the probability (times a market-level program-footprint gate) while riding its idiosyncratic residual move with the complementary weight. Falsifiable: if purity excess carries no attribution information, the interaction term will not beat the wedge-only fade, and the child's IC will stay concentrated at 24 bars instead of flattening across 1-12 bars; the edge survives arbitrage because per-event profit is a fraction of the spread and absorbing mechanical flow bears real inventory risk, so it is a compensated liquidity premium rather than a free lunch.
factors.name: Per-name basket-push attribution: comovement-purity x depth split

factors.trading_idea: The parent knew *whether* a bar's mechanical basket push had landed (a market-wide trust scalar) but not *which names* absorbed it nor *how old* their push was, so its fade mixed still-executing pressure (which continues) with already-landed pressure (which relaxes) — hence negative IC at 1-3 bars, positive only far out. The child fixes both: (i) it estimates each name's *realized* push elasticity as a trailing correlation between its vol-standardised return and its own predicted mechanical push rate (weight-per-depth wedge x program-footprint-weighted market displacement), turning the conditioner from one number per bar into a cross-sectional, name-level identification of who is actually inside the program's basket; (ii) it splits the push by age — the last 2 bars of push are still being executed and are ridden, while push accumulated 3-8 bars ago is in its transient-impact relaxation phase and is faded, but only where the precision-whitened dislocation actually confirms it in sign. Unattributed names' whitened dislocations are ridden as slow Epps/staleness information diffusion. The edge persists because the fade is compensation for absorbing capacity-limited, inventory-risky mechanical liquidity demand, and identifying it requires joint cross-sectional covariance whitening plus per-name elasticity estimation at 10-second granularity — statistically expensive rather than free arbitrage.
factors.name: Per-name push elasticity with age-split basket over-push

factors.trading_idea: Parent B found a mechanically pre-known signal — the 6-bar price block about to drop out of 30/60/120-bar trailing anchors — but hard-wired both its polarity and its conditioning weight (1-|sqrt-volume backing|), so its forecast mass leaked to 24 bars; Parent A showed that the only way to keep mass at the traded offset is to *estimate* each channel's loading from the name's own trailing lag-6 relationship with realised 6-bar residual displacement. The child makes B's backing state a genuine *regime label* rather than a multiplicative weight: for each name we run two horizon-matched calibrations in parallel — one restricted (via soft membership weights) to bars whose expiring block was unbacked/transient, one to bars whose block was volume-backed/permanent — and let the data decide the sign and strength of the expiry-drift, sqrt-pressure-wedge and unconverted-probe channels in each regime separately. The interaction is what carries the edge: B's mechanical clock supplies a *known-in-advance* event time at which flow must be expressed (so a 6-bar-offset correlation is actually identifiable rather than noise), while A's calibration removes B's imposed polarity and imposed unbackedness weighting, and the state split prevents the backed regime (where drift is absent or reversed) from averaging away the unbacked regime — the very averaging that pushed both parents' peak IC out to 24 bars.
factors.name: State-split expiry-clock polarity calibration

factors.trading_idea: A dealer will only absorb (and therefore repair) a single-name dislocation if the peer basket actually replicates that name, and the honest measure of replication is *out-of-sample* basis risk, not in-sample fit: residuals taken with a beta estimated on data ending before the impulse retain the true dislocation, whereas in-sample residuals are mechanically orthogonalised and their persistence is biased away. So the child conditions on trailing predictive R-squared of the leave-one-out industry basket for the name (1 - MSE of lagged-beta residuals / own return variance), measured strictly before the impulse window: where hedge precision is high the 6-bar idiosyncratic residual is cheap inventory and snaps back within the same 6-bar clock, where basis risk is large the same residual is unhedgeable information and continues. The factor is therefore a pure interaction (signed by the cross-sectional rank of hedge precision), which makes it nearly orthogonal to plain reversal and falsifiable in two directions at once: if the interaction is noise, both halves of the cross-section should show the same sign. The edge survives arbitrage because it is a basis-risk/capital constraint on the liquidity provider, not a mispricing: nobody can warehouse a residual whose hedge does not track it, and that condition is measured, not assumed.
factors.name: OOS hedge-precision sign-flipping peer-residual dislocation

factors.trading_idea: At 10-second frequency the fraction of a price move that is permanent rather than transient is a name-specific, slowly drifting quantity set by queue depth, tick-size binding and the inventory horizon of whoever is making that name's market: the identical 60-second move continues in one stock and snaps back in another, and within a stock it tends to continue when it arrives with abnormal trade volume (informed flow, permanent impact) and to revert when it does not (inventory pressure or liquidity withdrawal). Instead of imposing a sign or a heuristic gate, the child estimates each name's two permanence coefficients ONLINE by exponentially-weighted recursive least squares fitted at exactly the 6-bar forecast lag — regressing each realised 6-bar idiosyncratic (market-beta-residual) return on the preceding 6-bar idiosyncratic return and on its interaction with the contemporaneous volume z-score — ridge-regularised and precision-shrunk toward the panel-mean coefficient vector, and emits the fitted 6-bar-ahead expected return. The edge survives arbitrage because the coefficient flips sign across names and across regimes, so the aggregate signal carries almost no unconditional momentum or reversal loading and looks like noise to any fixed-sign relative-value trader; it is falsified if replacing the per-name coefficients with their panel means (or with a constant negative loading) costs no information content.
factors.name: Online RLS move-permanence coefficient (flow-split)

factors.trading_idea: The parent folded a distributed-lag beta kernel truncated at L = H = 6 against the observed market path, but truncating the kernel at the horizon is exactly wrong: the 6-bar-ahead conditional mean also contains contributions from shocks 7-18 bars old, whose loadings are *negative* because fast repricers overshoot and then correct (this is why the parent's IC flipped sign at 12-24 bars and nearly vanished at the fixed 6-bar offset). Two fixes give the same mechanism predictive mass inside the evaluation window: (i) regress own returns on AR(2)-whitened market *innovations*, so univariate lag loadings are genuine orthogonal impulse-response coefficients rather than mutually contaminated lagged-return betas; (ii) extend the kernel to L = 12 > H so the already-in-flight overshoot correction is subtracted instead of ignored, folding each lag l against the correct market-innovation window (last l bars for l <= 6, a 6-bar sum lagged l-6 for l > 6). Heterogeneity in delivery speed now enters as the *shrinkage target* — the kernel is shrunk toward a pooled kernel estimated within cross-sectional cohorts of repricing clock speed (frozen-mid fraction, thin relative volume) — so slow repricers inherit a long positive tail and fast repricers a fast-then-negative shape, rather than being merely amplified by a gate. The edge survives arbitrage because exploiting it requires simultaneous small trades in many thin, slowly-updating names where second-scale impact exceeds the per-name catch-up, and it is falsified if lags 7-12 carry zero pooled loading or if cohort kernels are statistically indistinguishable.
factors.name: Orthogonalised market-innovation impulse response with overshoot tail (clock-speed cohort shrinkage)

factors.trading_idea: The parent proved the *direction* law (name-specific push continues, basket-common push reverts) and measured how much push is still 'owed' in business time, but it ranked the owed *stock*, and a stock of owed impact only resolves as volume actually arrives — so its IC kept growing out to 24 bars, dominated by slow names whose settlement lies beyond the 6-bar window. The child replaces the owed-stock kernel with an owed-*flow* kernel: for each past bar it computes the fraction of still-unresolved displacement that a causal Hawkes-style self-exciting volume forecast says will be worked off inside the next 6 bars, min(V̂_{t+1:t+6}, remaining volume-life)/total volume-life, and does NOT re-normalise that gate away, so a name whose trading is about to burst carries a large signed expectation while a currently quiet name with identical owed push is shrunk toward the cross-sectional middle. Falsifiable prediction: this reweighting should move |IC| mass from 24 bars onto the fixed 6-bar offset (6-bar IC should exceed the parent's +0.0047 and the IC curve should flatten or peak near 6), and if the delivery-rate gate is pure noise the child will simply reproduce the parent's slow decay profile. The edge survives arbitrage because harvesting it requires jointly estimating each name's flow-commonality loading, its Kyle lambda, and a short-horizon volume-arrival forecast, and the payoff is a few basis points per 60 seconds — inside the cost band of anyone who is not already the liquidity provider.
factors.name: Delivery-rate gated idiosyncratic vs basket impact split

factors.trading_idea: The parent's realized IC says fresh one-sided flow pressure at 10-second scale precedes *lower*, not higher, returns — which is exactly the Grossman–Miller / transient-propagator prediction that the part of a recent price move mechanically bought from liquidity providers is a premium they earn back, not information. The child therefore stops measuring directional *consistency* (which is volume-scale-free and so throws away the size of the inventory the dealers absorbed) and instead estimates the absorbed inventory as a displacement in return units: signed root-volume over the last 6 bars times the name's own trailing square-root-law impact coefficient lambda = mean|r| / mean sqrt(volume). Because market-wide/sector-wide simultaneous pressure is information (index, ETF and macro flow) whose displacement is permanent, only the *sector-idiosyncratic* part of this estimated impact is dealer inventory that must be unwound, so the signal is the negative of the sector-demeaned estimated impact. The edge persists because it is the compensation liquidity providers require inside a one-minute window: harvesting it consumes the very spread and depth that pay for it, so it cannot be arbitraged away, only shared.
factors.name: Sector-idiosyncratic sqrt-law impact inventory reversal

factors.trading_idea: The Merton/Christie leverage effect makes a firm's downside share of realised variance a *slow, structural* state variable (it moves with capital structure and the prevailing vol level), which is why the parent's 120-bar asymmetry level only paid off over many minutes.  Transient one-sided liquidation, by contrast, appears as a fast *innovation*: the last ~3 minutes of downside variance share jumping above the firm's own pre-existing (leverage- and vol-justified) asymmetry baseline.  Purging the innovation of the cross-sectional level that leverage, current volatility and their interaction predict leaves a shock that is order-flow, not information, and it is absorbed within roughly a minute — so the reversion is concentrated at the fixed 6-bar offset instead of leaking out to 24 bars.  We additionally tilt by the impact-per-dollar of the burst (realised vol of the window divided by dollar volume, z-scored against the name's own norm): one-sided moves achieved on *little* traded volume are impatient/vacuum liquidation rather than participated information, and revert hardest; the edge survives because balance-sheet-conditioned, volume-normalised asymmetry innovations are not a screen liquidity providers run.
factors.name: Impact-gated downside semivariance asymmetry innovation

factors.trading_idea: Systematic style flow (ETF creation/redemption baskets, risk-model rebalances, quant metaorders) is worked over minutes and touches every name sharing a fundamental characteristic simultaneously, so the return of a characteristic-sorted long-short spread is positively autocorrelated at the 10-second scale even while individual names' idiosyncratic displacements mean-revert; individual-name bounce noise diversifies away inside the spread, so the spread return is a far cleaner read on ongoing flow than any single name's price path. The child therefore estimates, bar by bar, purely-fundamental orthogonalised spread returns (size, value, quality, investment, leverage), converts each into a flow z-score that is up-weighted only when the spread's own constituents are simultaneously unusually active in volume (real basket execution leaves a volume footprint; noise-driven spread moves do not), and projects that flow back onto each name through its characteristic loading — deliberately discarding the idiosyncratic residual, which is exactly the over-mined carrier that made the parent 71% redundant with the book. It is falsifiable in two independent ways: if 10-second characteristic-spread returns are not positively autocorrelated over the next 6 bars the flow-propagation reading is dead, and if volume-unbacked spread moves continue as strongly as volume-backed ones the footprint gate is spurious. The edge survives arbitrage because monetising it requires holding the crowded style tilt across dozens of names for ~one minute, where the round-trip spread cost across the whole basket caps capacity, and because the flow itself is mandated rebalancing that keeps being generated rather than being competed away.
factors.name: Volume-backed fundamental spread-flow relay

factors.trading_idea: The parent proved that the lag-1 cross-covariance of a 10-second panel carries real information, but it compressed that N-by-N matrix into a single scalar per name (row-sums of its antisymmetric part) and then spent its variance budget on inverting a covariance matrix — a family the book already spans, hence ~zero marginal IC. Asymmetric random-matrix theory (Livan/Bouchaud) says the singular spectrum of a lagged correlation matrix of independent series obeys a quarter-circle law, and that for real equity panels only the top one or two singular triplets escape that noise bulk: the genuinely predictable lead-lag structure is LOW-RANK, and everything else a naive VAR/precision estimator amplifies is pure estimation noise. So I estimate the lag-1..3 cross-correlation matrix with its diagonal removed (own autocorrelation is bounce/partial-adjustment, already mined), soft-clip its singular values at the noise edge (the smaller of the theoretical 2*sqrt(H*N/T) edge and 2.48*median of the empirical spectrum), and apply only the surviving operator to peers' most recent standardised moves — a direct estimate of the return a laggard still owes. I then hedge out cross-sectionally the two channels arbitrageurs already farm (the name's own recent move and its contemporaneous market beta), keeping only lag-loading in excess of contemporaneous beta, and scale by trade liveness because a catch-up is only delivered in the next six bars if the laggard is actually being quoted/traded. Falsifiable: if all significant lead-lag content is the market-lag channel, the beta-hedged residual has zero IC; the edge persists because it needs an RMT-cleaned asymmetric matrix on a fast clock and pays out only in thin, low-capacity basket-vs-basket legs that single-name latency arbitrageurs ignore.
factors.name: RMT-clipped lead-lag SVD propagation, beta- and own-move hedged

factors.trading_idea: Parent B splits recent drift into a quiet (no-trade quote-repricing) component that should continue and a traded component that should revert, but it cannot tell genuine quote repricing from stale-mid catch-up — exactly its own stated falsification risk. Parent A supplies the missing state variable: on the *subordinated clock of the selected bars only*, the excess of the observed adjacent-sign-flip frequency over the Rice/Gaussian null arccos(rho1)/pi separates sign-persistent grinding (gap<0, a maker slowly walking its quotes or a parent order being sliced) from magnitude-concentrated jumps (gap>0, one stale-mid snap or a liquidity vacuum). The child therefore measures the Rice gap separately on the quiet-bar and active-bar return subsequences and uses each gap to modulate the corresponding leg: quiet drift is followed at full weight only when its micro-structure is a grind and is switched off when it is a single stale-print jump, while traded drift is faded hardest when it was jump-carried (overshoot into thin depth) and left neutral when it was a grind (order splitting still working). The interaction carries edge neither parent has alone because Parent A's gap has no directional anchor at short horizons and Parent B's split has no way to reject noise-driven quiet drift; conditioning one on the other removes B's dominant false-positive mode, and the deliberately short 12-bar drift window (vs 30) pulls the payoff forward to the fixed 6-bar offset.
factors.name: Rice-Gap Gated Quiet Repricing vs Traded Impact

factors.trading_idea: Treat each name's causally band-passed log-price (fast minus slow EWMA) as a weakly coupled oscillator and locate it on the unit circle from its normalised deviation and velocity, so its *timing* (phase) is measured independently of its amplitude. Basket/ETF hedging and index-arb flow act as a mean field that entrains individual names toward the cross-sectional order parameter R·e^{iψ}, so Kuramoto dynamics dθ_j/dt = ω + K·R·sin(ψ−θ_j) imply an excess return of −A_j·sinθ_j·R·sin(ψ−θ_j): rising names whose phase *lags* the pack are accelerated (buy) while rising names that *lead* the pack are held back (fade), and antiphase or in-phase names get nothing. This survives arbitrage because conventional lead-lag arbitrage is estimated in the amplitude/return domain (betas, correlations), which averages over timing and cannot see a name that is correctly-sized but a quarter-cycle late; extracting it needs simultaneous multi-name phase estimation at 10-second granularity plus spread-crossing in the laggard. Falsified if the phase-lag interaction term carries no forward information once the pack is unsynchronised (small R) or if signal strength is independent of the per-name tradability (coupling) weight.
factors.name: Kuramoto mean-field phase entrainment lag

factors.trading_idea: The parent's insight — displacement that is *volume-backed* behaves differently from displacement that is not — is right, but its expression (a rolling-anchor drop-out clock) accrues over tens of bars, which is why its IC kept rising to 24 bars. The fast version of the same idea decomposes the last 6 bars of log-price displacement per name into (a) the part explained by the square-root impact law, sign(ret)·lambda·sqrt(volume) with lambda estimated causally from a trailing per-name regression of |ret| on sqrt(volume), and (b) the flow-orthogonal residual, i.e. mid-price revision that trades did not pay for. Bouchaud's propagator says the trade-impact part is largely transient but its decay is only *expressed* once the pressuring order flow stops (order-flow autocorrelation keeps refreshing impact while the burst runs), so we revert the explained component in proportion to a flow-cessation clock (recent sqrt-volume versus the burst's own prior peak) and let it continue while flow persists; the flow-orthogonal component is quote-revision information (Hasbrouck: limit-order updates carry a large information share) and should persist, more strongly the thinner the traded volume in the window. The edge survives arbitrage because harvesting it requires taking the reverting side only after cessation — a state that is invisible to naive reversal traders and that forces inventory risk exactly when flow is still one-sided.
factors.name: Square-root-law impact decomposition with flow-cessation clock

factors.trading_idea: Parent B established that the doubly-orthogonalised residual (name hedged on its valuation-kernel peer basket, then purged of that neighbourhood's own residual factor) is the object that genuinely snaps back on a one-minute clock, while Parent A's evaluation revealed — against its declared story — that trade-backed displacement does NOT relax faster than quiet displacement; if anything the trade-attributable part persists and the quiet, untraded part is what reverts. The economically coherent reading is Hasbrouck's: displacement that arrives with abnormal print volume is trade-revealed information (permanent impact, order-splitting continuation), whereas mid displacement with no prints is market-maker quote flicker / inventory skew against a stale book — pure transitory noise. The child therefore applies Parent A's participation-share attribution g = v/(v + trailing mean v) and its exponential propagator remaining-relaxation kernel (halflife 3 bars, horizon-matched to 6 bars) to Parent B's *clean* name-specific residual, and fades the quiet leg roughly four times harder than the traded leg, all scaled by hedgeability (trailing hedge R²). The interaction is the edge: Parent A's split was contaminated because it was applied to a crude peer-median residual whose 'quiet' leg still contained non-reverting tier-common re-rating, and Parent B's flat 3-bar impulse fades informed trade-backed moves it should be holding — only the purged residual makes the trade/quiet decomposition an honest permanent-vs-transitory split.
factors.name: Cluster-purged residual: quiet-leg-dominant snapback

factors.trading_idea: The parent proved that routing a market-wide state onto the traded leg of a hedged excursion adds combination value, but its state variable (share of cross-sectional variance carried by the equal-weighted market factor) is only a proxy for the thing that actually decides whether temporary impact gets repaid: the price the market is currently charging for risk transfer. The child measures that price directly as an aggregate Kyle elasticity — the trailing regression slope of |market-factor return| on cross-sectional mean relative participation — so a HIGH slope means each unit of aggregate flow is moving prices a lot (thin risk-bearing capacity, single-name traded excursions are inventory imbalance that is repaid within seconds), while a collapse in the slope means flow is being absorbed and volume-driven moves are informational and continue. Second, the child fixes what the parent's traded leg actually contains: instead of summing all active-bar residual drift (which mixes permanent, flow-justified repricing with over-payment), it subtracts each bar's own square-root-law expected impact, estimated per name as a trailing slope of |residual return| on sqrt(volume/typical volume), so the faded object is the EXCESS displacement beyond what the flow paid for — the mechanically transient part. The edge survives arbitrage because it requires jointly estimating a per-name impact elasticity and an aggregate liquidity-price state at 10-second resolution, and because the traded leg's sign flips with the regime, so anyone trading the unconditional version earns roughly nothing and does not compete the conditional version away.
factors.name: Aggregate impact-elasticity gated excess-paid vs unpaid drift split

factors.trading_idea: Parent A splits the last 6 bars of log displacement into a square-root-law *paid* part (sign(ret)·lambda·sqrt(volume)) and a *flow-orthogonal unpaid* part, and parent B measures where the price currently sits inside its own volume-at-price occupation density; both parents' realized ICs contradicted their priors in exactly the way a propagator + resting-inventory story predicts, and the child encodes that corrected physics as a joint state. Paid displacement is over-push while the metaorder is still running (revert) but becomes the permanent Kyle component once flow ceases — and permanence only survives if the price has travelled into a low-occupancy void where no resting limit-order mass remains to push it back; so the paid component's sign is the *average* of the cessation clock and the void state, which is strongly directional only when the two agree (flow stopped AND price sits in vacuum ⇒ continue; flow still running AND price parked on a thick volume cluster ⇒ snap back). Unpaid (quote-revision) displacement is genuine repricing only when it happens in a void; against an occupancy cluster it is flicker of the mid over untouched resting size and mean-reverts, so it is faded in proportion to the local occupancy mass. Neither parent has this edge alone: A's cessation clock cannot tell a permanent post-burst move from one that stopped in front of a wall of resting inventory, and B's density shape carries no information about whether the displacement that reached that point was paid for by volume.
factors.name: Void–cessation joint state gating of paid vs unpaid displacement

factors.trading_idea: On 10-second bars a heavy-volume bar with an upper wick is a sliced buy metaorder whose transient impact was absorbed by hidden supply — Parent A's realized (sign-corrected) evidence says such absorbed probes are followed by continuation, because the aggressor is not finished and the permanent component of impact leaks in over the next few bars. Whether that leakage converts into drift or dies depends on whether anything justifies the flow: if the name is simultaneously dislocated CHEAP in peer multiple space (live log P/B, P/S, P/OCF spread versus a comparable industry median has just fallen below its own recent level, inside a tight, high-comparability peer group), the absorbed buying is informed value accumulation and the probe extends; if the name is dislocated RICH, the same absorbed probe is distribution into a stretched valuation and the rejection sticks, so the probe's sign should be flipped. Parent A knows WHO is trading but not WHY, so its continuation is direction-blind; Parent B knows the valuation state but has no arrival trigger, which is exactly why its edge only strengthens far beyond the pinned 6-bar horizon. The product term (probe intensity × comparability-gated cheapness) supplies trigger and justification together, delivering a signed 6-bar read that neither parent carries alone.
factors.name: Probe-Confirmed Multiple Dislocation Polarity Switch

factors.trading_idea: The parent's Rice inversion, rho = cos(pi*p_flip), is unbiased only if all block pairs are drawn from ONE mechanism; in reality a 10-second mid-price tape mixes two: (a) many small, quote-noise / inventory-driven 60-second displacements that alternate sign, and (b) far fewer large displacements produced by sliced metaorders whose impact keeps accumulating. Because the sign-flip counter weights every pair equally, the noise regime — which supplies the large majority of pairs — dominates p_flip, so the parent estimated a negative rho almost everywhere and turned into an indiscriminate reversal signal; that is exactly why its realised IC came out with the opposite sign to the declaration. The child estimates Rice's concordance separately conditional on the magnitude regime of the *previous* block (|standardised displacement| above vs. below one sigma) and applies the coefficient belonging to the regime the name is currently in, so the same formula reverses small displacements and extends large, flow-driven ones with per-name coefficients. Falsifiable core: rho estimated on large-|prev| pairs should be systematically more positive than rho on small-|prev| pairs, and the regime-matched forecast should carry positive IC at 6 bars; the edge persists because reversion desks apply one common, magnitude-blind reversion coefficient, and separating the two regimes requires continuous per-name re-estimation whose per-name payoff is tiny.
factors.name: Magnitude-split Rice block concordance forecast

factors.trading_idea: Under the mixture-of-distributions view, informed trading makes *volume lead volatility*: order flow arrives first and price adjusts to it, so the resulting displacement is a permanent revision and continues. Momentum-ignition / reactive chasing has the opposite temporal ordering — the price moves first (thin-book quote displacement) and volume arrives afterwards as latecomers react — so the displacement is a transitory inventory shock that decays. I therefore estimate, per name, the *asymmetry of the trailing lagged cross-correlation* between normalised flow and normalised idiosyncratic volatility, corr(|r|_t, v_{t-1}) − corr(v_t, |r|_{t-1}), and use its cross-sectional rank to flip the sign of the name's recent beta-neutral displacement: fade the displacement where volatility leads flow, ride it where flow leads volatility. The edge persists because market makers and most systematic reversal books condition on contemporaneous imbalance, spread and depth, not on the Granger *direction* of the volume–volatility relation, and the profit is compensation for supplying liquidity to reactive chasers, which is inventory-capacity limited rather than information limited.
factors.name: Flow-volatility causality-direction gated displacement flip

factors.trading_idea: The parent showed that the phase (timing) of a lag-1-corrected, precision-whitened relative-value dislocation carries information, but it scored the *instantaneous* Kuramoto derivative dtheta/dt, which is a one-bar object — hence its IC peaked at 1 bar and had decayed by 6. Here the same oscillator is integrated forward exactly 6 bars: each name's angular frequency omega_i and its phase-locking value are estimated by circular statistics on trailing per-bar phase increments, the leader-weighted mean field is advanced at its own frequency, and the signal is the finite-difference predicted change rho*(cos(theta_{t+6}) - cos(theta_t)) rather than its derivative. This matters because at the fixed 6-bar offset the cross-section is dominated by *who crosses a turning point within six bars* (Delta_theta ranges from ~1 to ~4 radians across names), which is a strictly different ranking from -sin(theta); names whose phase does not rotate coherently get down-weighted by the phase-locking gate instead of contributing noise. The predicted change is finally orthogonalised cross-sectionally against the dislocation level itself, so the factor carries only the timing information and cannot collapse into the already-mined dislocation-reversal family; the edge survives arbitrage because it requires jointly estimating an Epps-corrected precision, a lead/lag role matrix and per-name phase kinematics from a 6-minute trailing window, which is re-estimated faster than a discretionary or slow-fitting arbitrageur can follow.
factors.name: Horizon-integrated leader-Kuramoto phase advance of precision dislocations

factors.trading_idea: Llorente–Michaely–Saar–Wang show that whether a price move accompanied by volume continues or reverses depends on the mix of informed versus liquidity/hedging trade in that name: liquidity-motivated volume creates transitory pricing errors that revert, informed volume creates permanent revisions that continue. Rather than imposing a market-wide regime sign (the parent's commonality share) I let each name *estimate its own* response function: a trailing two-regressor OLS of its beta-hedged, sector-demeaned 6-bar residual return on (a) the previous non-overlapping 6-bar residual return and (b) that residual interacted with detrended own volume, then form the fitted forecast of the next 6-bar residual from the current state. Because the coefficients are fitted at exactly the 6-bar mapping, the signal is a direct conditional expectation at the traded horizon rather than a slower reversal proxy, and the volume interaction is the per-name discriminator between inventory noise and information. The edge persists because the profitable leg is inventory-bearing liquidity supply (a compensated risk), and because almost all deployed short-horizon reversal signals hard-code a single sign and no volume interaction, so they average the reverting and continuing populations together.
factors.name: LMSW volume-interaction self-calibrated residual response

factors.trading_idea: The parent's realized (sign-flipped) result says something specific: whether price is sitting on a high-recurrence level or in a vacuum, the next minute's return points back toward the centre of mass of the recent price-occupation measure — the interaction with the recent move was just a noisy proxy for the direction-to-centre. I therefore measure that pull directly and locally as a Nadaraya–Watson mean-shift vector on the volume-weighted occupation density of the last 60 bars: resting inventory rebuilds where time was spent AND volume was traded (makers re-post and unwind where they were filled, stops/limits cluster there), so price is magnetically drawn to the *nearest* such node within roughly one horizon's diffusion distance. Using a Gaussian kernel of bandwidth ~sqrt(6)·sigma makes the object local rather than a moving-average distance: in a genuine trend the nearest mode travels with price and the mean-shift is ~0, so the signal does not blindly fight drift, which is what separates it from plain MA/VWAP reversion; the estimate is gated by mass concentration so we only trade when a well-defined node actually exists within reach. It survives arbitrage because it requires a per-name, per-bar nonparametric mode estimate for a payoff of a couple of ticks per minute, and because the cause (where queues rebuild) is a structural property of order books, not a mispricing that can be deleted.
factors.name: Volume-weighted kernel mean-shift to nearest liquidity node

factors.trading_idea: Model each name's hedged log mid as efficient price plus an AR(1) pricing error: displacement that arrives with prints is an efficient-price innovation (permanent, and by order-splitting/Hawkes clustering it keeps arriving), while displacement with essentially no prints is dealer quote-skew / flicker that decays at rate rho. The parent estimated the two channel gains by trailing horizon-matched OLS on realised forward returns, which at 10-second resolution is noise-dominated and slow; here both gains are *identified without any forward return* from trailing return autocovariances — under the model gamma_j = -sigma_e^2(1-rho)^2 rho^(j-1), so rho = gamma_2/gamma_1, the transient variance share is -gamma_1/gamma_0, and the traded leg's own lag-1 autocorrelation is the continuation coefficient — giving an exactly horizon-matched forecast -(transient share)(1-rho^6)*(decay-accumulated quiet displacement) + phi*(6-bar traded footprint) that uses every bar of data. The edge persists because harvesting the quiet leg means supplying liquidity against a dealer re-centring its quote (inventory risk) and the traded leg means aligning with possibly-informed persistent metaorder flow (adverse selection); neither is free, and the cross-sectional ordering depends on per-name dispersion in the *identified* noise persistence, which requires jointly estimating participation and the autocovariance structure rather than reading a single reversal window.
factors.name: Autocovariance-identified transient gain, quiet/traded split

factors.trading_idea: Llorente-Michaely-Saar-Wang show that the sign of the volume-conditioned return autocorrelation is governed by information asymmetry: when a price move is accompanied by abnormal volume it continues in names where trading is likely informed, and reverses in names where volume mostly reflects liquidity/hedging demand. The parent's edge came from a slow balance-sheet-conditioned variance state whose information only accrues over minutes; here the fundamentals instead set the *prior on impact permanence* (accounting opacity: intangibility, goodwill, R&D intensity, weak cash-backing of earnings, small size), while the fast trigger is a fresh 6-bar sector-neutral move scaled by its own volatility and interacted with a 6-bar volume surprise — an object whose predictive content lives exactly on the one-minute clock, matching the fixed horizon. To make the test sharp, the triple interaction return x volume-surprise x opacity is cross-sectionally residualised against plain reversal, volume-conditioned reversal, and the static opacity tilt, so only the differential loading predicted by the mechanism survives. It persists because market makers condition on spread, queue and volume, not on point-in-time accrual quality or asset intangibility, so the cross-name variation in how much of a one-minute impact is permanent is not arbitraged away; it is falsified if the residual interaction carries no IC at 6 bars while the plain reversal leg does.
factors.name: Opacity-conditioned volume-return permanence wedge

factors.trading_idea: A peer-relative price displacement persists exactly as long as the idiosyncratic directional order flow that created it keeps arriving: same-sign trade arrivals are self-exciting (Hawkes-like), so the transient impact component is *held open* by the residual intensity of that flow and only relaxes once the intensity collapses below the name's own baseline or flips sign. The parent conditioned relaxation speed on the calendar AGE of the excursion, which is only a weak proxy for whether the sustaining flow has actually stopped — hence its predictability leaked out to 24 bars. The child replaces the age clock with a directly measured *event clock*: an exponentially-kernelled idiosyncratic signed-flow intensity normalised by its own long-run scale, aligned with the sign of the displacement, so that names whose sustaining pressure has already exhausted or reversed are the ones expected to snap back within the next minute, while names still being hammered by same-sign flow keep their sign (continuation). The edge survives arbitrage because harvesting it requires per-name flow-state inference at 10-second resolution with fast turnover for small per-event profit, whereas relative-value arbitrageurs are paid on the slow multi-minute leg.
factors.name: Flow-exhaustion gated peer relaxation onset

factors.trading_idea: Raw volume shocks conflate three things: the deterministic intraday U-shape, a name's slowly drifting activity level, and market-wide activity waves — only the residual innovation carries information about whether a price move was caused by an informed metaorder or by mere quote drift / scheduled participation. Removing all three (own time-of-day profile from prior days, own 30-minute level, and the contemporaneous cross-sectional mean) leaves a clean surprise; a 60-second move accompanied by high surprise volume is the visible part of a split parent order whose remaining children keep arriving, so it continues, while a move accompanied by below-normal surprise volume is mid-quote noise / immediacy demand that is paid back as liquidity providers unwind, so it reverts. The child therefore predicts the *sign of the autocorrelation coefficient itself* to flip with volume innovation rather than predicting reversal or momentum outright, and the interaction is purged cross-sectionally of both main effects so it cannot be a re-labelled reversal. The edge survives arbitrage because the reversal leg is compensation for supplying immediacy (a genuine risk premium) and the continuation leg requires estimating and subtracting per-name intraday seasonality in real time, which most short-horizon signals proxy crudely with a trailing volume mean.
factors.name: Diurnal-purged volume innovation gates reversal vs continuation

factors.trading_idea: A dislocation in a name relative to its peer basket only snaps back fast if a market maker can actually neutralise it, and hedgeability is a *measurable spectral property* of the peer group: when the group's trailing covariance is close to one-factor (high average pairwise correlation, estimated from the variance of the cross-sectional mean of vol-standardised returns), the basket spans the name's risk and the hedge residual is almost riskless, so it is repaired within seconds; when the group's spectrum is spread across many directions the 'residual' is genuine idiosyncratic information and is never repaired. Second, the hedge must be executable across several comparable names at once, so the state variable is the *effective number of live hedge legs* — the participation ratio (sum(w)^2/sum(w^2)) of size-comparability weights restricted to peers that actually traded in the last minute — rather than raw aggregate peer activity, because a hedge concentrated in one peer imports that peer's own idiosyncratic risk. Falsifiable prediction: the reversal loading on a horizon-matched 6-bar comparability-hedged residual displacement is strongly negative in high-cohesion / many-live-legs cells and ~0 in low-cohesion or few-legs cells, and (unlike the parent) the conditioned signal's information should peak at ~6 bars because high-cohesion repairs have a sub-minute half-life while the slow, 24-bar component lives entirely in the low-cohesion cells. The edge survives arbitrage because it is a hedging-capital and simultaneous-liquidity constraint: in the states where the constraint binds the trade is unattractive, and in the states where it does not bind the profit is precisely the compensation for supplying that capacity.
factors.name: Peer-cohesion & effective-hedge-leg gated comparability-hedged snapback

factors.trading_idea: Parent B's distributed-lag kernel says how much *market* return a name still owes over exactly the next 6 bars, but it must trust that the name's price will actually be repriced in that window; parent A's volume-regularity shock is precisely a detector of whether a mechanical, price-taking participant (a VWAP/POV scheduler) is currently working the name. So metronomic volume is used as a positive *confidence weight* on the owed market catch-up (a scheduler mechanically delivers the missing beta over the next minute), while the same regularity state is used as a *sign-flipping* gate on the market-orthogonalised drift — continued when volume is smooth (unfinished parent order) and faded when volume is bursty (transient one-off impact). The interaction carries edge neither parent has: B's forecast is otherwise applied blind to whether repricing capacity exists (its staleness gate is a slow clientele proxy, not a live execution fingerprint), and A's drift is contaminated by exactly the lagged-beta catch-up component that B can price analytically, so purging it leaves a cleaner schedule-continuation signal.
factors.name: Schedule-regularity gated lag-kernel catch-up vs idiosyncratic drift split

factors.trading_idea: A mid move nobody paid for is a dealer's quote revision — information still pending confirmation — whereas a move bought with volume is mostly transient impact that relaxes. The parent proved this split, but it thresholded volume against a 150-bar quantile and pooled 12 flat-ish bars, so it priced only 68% of the panel and its information only fully cashed out at ~12 bars. The child (i) attributes *each bar's* return continuously into an unbacked part and a flow-backed part using that bar's volume relative to the name's own EWM volume scale (no threshold, no long warm-up), and (ii) makes the payoff horizon-matched: an unbacked repricing only completes when the confirming order actually arrives and impact only relaxes on the trade clock, so both legs are amplified by the name's expected number of material flow arrivals inside the next 6 bars (cross-sectionally ranked trade-clock speed). Falsified if the arrival-clock amplitude adds nothing over the ungated attribution, or if the IC horizon profile still peaks far beyond 6 bars; the edge survives arbitrage because harvesting it means crossing the spread in names that are, at that instant, the thinnest in the cross-section, and because horizon matching needs per-name clock estimation that calendar-time models discard.
factors.name: Unbacked-share attributed drift, arrival-clock horizon matched

factors.trading_idea: The parent showed that 10-second characteristic factor returns reverse at 1-3 bars and continue at 12-24 bars, so at the pinned 6-bar horizon the unconditional relay sits exactly on its zero crossing: it is a mixture of two opposite populations. The separating state variable is *where the traded volume sits along the characteristic axis*: a genuine sliced basket/factor-tilt programme buys one tail of a characteristic and sells the other, so abnormal volume concentrates at BOTH extremes of that characteristic's loading (positive cross-sectional slope of abnormal volume on |loading|), whereas quote-bounce noise leaves volume unrelated to the characteristic. The child therefore measures, per bar and per characteristic, the ridge cross-sectional factor return AND this magnitude-only tail-volume concentration slope, and relays the recent 6-bar factor return onto names with a sign given by whether tail-volume concentration is above or below its own trailing norm — continuation when a programme is demonstrably trading the axis, reversal when it is not. It is falsifiable: if replacing the tanh(z) tail-concentration gate by a fixed constant (+1 or -1) reproduces the IC, or if the gate's slope is statistically zero, the execution-footprint mechanism is wrong and this is repackaged characteristic momentum. The edge persists because it needs real-time point-in-time loadings, per-bar cross-sectional estimation of both a return and a volume-shape moment, and high turnover on a capacity-limited execution footprint rather than a mispricing anyone can hold.
factors.name: Tail-Volume-Concentration Gated Characteristic Factor Relay

factors.trading_idea: A single failed excursion beyond a bar's endpoints is mostly mid-quote flicker; genuine concealed liquidity (iceberg / repeatedly refreshed passive size) reveals itself by rejecting probes on the SAME side in consecutive bars, i.e. the rejection process is self-excited rather than sign-alternating. So the informative part of the excursion asymmetry is only the component whose side repeats the previous bar's side; the alternating component is symmetric noise whose average sign is unstable across samples (exactly the parent's IS/OOS sign flip). Keeping only the persistent component and measuring it scale-free as a share of the bar range (no fitted diffusion scale to estimate, hence far fewer degrees of freedom) should give a stable negative forward sign at the one-minute offset: repeated rejected upside probes imply real supply above, so price drifts toward the untested side. The edge survives arbitrage because it is a statement about hidden, non-displayed depth that cannot be read off the quote and is unprofitable to trade at size for slower participants; it is falsified if the persistence-filtered wedge has no larger |IC| than the unfiltered wedge, or if the alternating component carries the same sign.
factors.name: Self-Excited Refill: Persistent Failed-Excursion Wedge

factors.trading_idea: Recent inventory in a name was acquired at prices distributed as its trailing volume-at-price profile, so the current mid determines what share of that inventory is sitting on an unrealized gain; I estimate that share in closed form from the volume-weighted first three moments of trailing log prices via a Cornish-Fisher (skew-corrected Gaussian) CDF evaluation at the current mid, rather than from the price move itself. Holders in profit realise gains (disposition effect / risk-limit-driven inventory unwinding) and therefore supply liquidity into further advances, so an advance that leaves most recent volume underwater keeps running while one that leaves most volume in profit meets predictable supply and partly retraces within a minute; the effect should be asymmetric because loss-averse holders are reluctant to sell at a loss. To avoid collapsing into plain short-horizon reversal, the overhang is residualised on trailing 6-bar and 120-bar returns, so only the part driven by the *shape* of the volume distribution (its dispersion, skew and where volume actually traded) is traded. The edge persists because harvesting it means warehousing the other side of mechanical, second-scale inventory liquidation — a liquidity-provision premium limited by inventory capacity, not by information — and it requires maintaining a per-name volume-weighted price distribution rather than a price signal.
factors.name: Cornish-Fisher volume-profile gain overhang fade

factors.trading_idea: The parent's edge lived in a 120-bar level of downside-variance asymmetry, which is a slow state variable — hence its IC kept growing out to 24 bars and was weak at the pinned 6-bar offset. The child keeps the semivariance-asymmetry lens but converts it into an *innovation*: the last ~90 seconds of idiosyncratic downside variance share minus the name's own 120-bar structural share, cross-sectionally stripped of the part justified by leverage (debtToAssets, financialLeverage) and size, so what remains is transient one-sided pressure whose half-life is tens of seconds, matching the fixed horizon. Crucially the child adds a new conditioning variable: whether that one-sided move was accompanied by trade volume. One-sided mid-price drift on *below-normal* participation is a liquidity vacuum (market makers widening / withdrawing inventory, no information), so it snaps back within a minute; the same asymmetry on *above-normal* participation is informed liquidation being absorbed and continues. The edge persists because it requires jointly conditioning realised semivariance asymmetry on balance-sheet structure and on volume confirmation, a screen that neither statistical-arbitrage reversal books (which use raw returns) nor HFT inventory models (which ignore fundamentals) run.
factors.name: Volume-vacuum-gated idiosyncratic semivariance asymmetry innovation

factors.trading_idea: When liquidity demand pushes a name's 6-bar displacement beyond its own trailing 90th/10th percentile of displacements, the *excess* beyond that conditional support is not information but an inventory concession extracted from market makers, and it is repaid as the inventory is unwound over roughly the next minute. The size of the concession a market maker demands scales with the cost of warehousing that particular name: firms with fragile working capital — long cash-conversion cycle, weak quick ratio, poor accrual quality (low incomeQuality), fast receivable/inventory build — carry a higher probability of adverse fundamental news arriving while inventory is held, so their transitory concessions are larger and unwind harder, whereas cash-rich short-cycle firms show only weak snapback. This gives a falsifiable monotone prediction: the reversal IC of the thresholded excess should increase across working-capital-fragility tiers, and the factor is void (zero) whenever no name is beyond its own trailing support. The edge persists because it requires joining quarterly working-capital/accrual data to second-scale threshold events and it fires rarely and only in the tails — low-capacity, mandate-irrelevant conditioning that fast market-making capital does not parametrise its inventory policy on.
factors.name: Working-capital-fragility gated threshold concession snapback

factors.trading_idea: The parent proved the opposite of its own story: fast displacement funded by a name's *own* activity burst (panel quiet) does not continue at one minute, it gives back — exactly what transient-impact theory predicts, since peak impact of a metaorder exceeds its permanent component and the mid relaxes toward the reference price as depth refills. The missing conditioner is *whose* reference price: relaxation requires patient counterparties who are confident about fair value, so the snapback should be fast and reliable for names with a precise fundamental anchor (tangible assets, positive cash-backed earnings, non-glamour multiples, low leverage) and should fail — or even invert into information-driven continuation — for hard-to-value names where market makers simply widen and let the mid drift. The child is therefore a pure *interaction*: minus the idiosyncratic-activity-attributed displacement, multiplied by a centered cross-sectional anchor-precision score built from point-in-time fundamentals, so the plain (already heavily mined) reversal carrier cancels in the cross-section and only the conditioning content is expressed. The edge survives arbitrage because it needs a point-in-time fundamental panel joined to panel-synchronised 10-second activity attribution: latency shops do not carry valuation-precision data, fundamental investors do not trade one-minute snapbacks, and the capacity is spread-limited.
factors.name: Anchor-precision gated idiosyncratic-burst snapback

factors.trading_idea: The parent's edge was a beta catch-up wedge, but it compressed the whole adjustment into one 6-bar 'beta x market move minus own move' difference, which is why its information peaked past the fixed horizon. Here the mechanism is stated properly: each name's response to the market factor is a distributed-lag impulse-response kernel b_0..b_L estimated causally on 10-second bars, so at time t the part of the recent market path that has NOT yet been transmitted is exactly the convolution of the past L market shocks with the *tail* of that kernel — a quantity whose natural arrival time is the next few bars, matching the 6-bar offset. The slow-transmission names are those whose kernel mass sits at lags >= 1, and we further gate by measured quote/trade staleness (share of recent bars with no volume and no price change, plus depressed recent relative volume), because unabsorbed factor information is mechanically stored in names that are not being continuously repriced. The edge should persist because harvesting it requires per-name lag-kernel estimation and taking liquidity precisely in the least active names, where inventory and impact costs deter fast arbitrage capital; it is falsified if the kernel-tail convolution has no more forward power than the raw contemporaneous beta wedge, or if the staleness gate is flat across its deciles.
factors.name: Unabsorbed market impulse from an estimated lag-beta kernel, staleness-gated

factors.trading_idea: Parent A shows that drift printed in (near-)zero-volume bars continues while drift paid for with aggressive volume decays, but its own stated falsification is that quiet-bar drift may just be stale-mid noise; Parent B supplies exactly the statistic that separates those cases — the gap between the realised adjacent-sign-flip frequency and the Rice/Gaussian-copula null arccos(rho)/pi, which is negative for many small same-signed increments (a grind: a maker walking its quote tick by tick, or a sliced parent order) and positive when the same autocorrelation is carried by a few large increments (a stale-print gap or a jump into thin depth). The child therefore computes the Rice gap *separately inside each volume stream* — pairing each quiet bar with the previous quiet bar and each active bar with the previous active bar — and uses it as a state gate: the quiet-bar repricing leg is trusted only when it is grind-carried (genuine sequential quote shading) and switched off when it is jump-carried (stale-mid artefact), while the active-bar leg is faded hardest when its drift is jump-carried impact into a vacuum and left alone when it is a still-working grind. The interaction is what neither parent has: A cannot tell informative quote repricing from stale-mid noise, and B applies one blunt gap to the pooled return series where quote-driven and trade-driven increments are mixed and cancel, so measuring the gap within the volume-conditioned streams recovers a much cleaner sign-persistence estimate at the fixed 60-second offset.
factors.name: Rice-Gated Quiet Repricing vs Traded-Impact Split

factors.trading_idea: The parent's confirmed finding is that resting depth lives where the mid has already traded and is thin outside it, so price yields toward the thin side. The child measures that depth field directly and continuously instead of waiting for a rare 'escape event': for each name it splits the trailing 10-minute local price neighbourhood into the region just BELOW and just ABOVE the current mid and computes each side's absorbed volume PER BAR OF DWELL TIME — a per-side liquidity-consumption rate that is a direct proxy for local book depth. Because the volume is divided by the time spent on that side (and each bar's volume is first normalised by the name's own trailing average), the statistic is invariant to how much of the window the price spent above vs below, which is exactly the price-position-in-range component that plain momentum/reversal and count-based volume-profile factors already span; what survives is pure depth asymmetry. With roughly balanced arriving flow, asymmetric depth implies asymmetric impact and therefore a drift toward the thin side, scaled by how much flow is currently arriving — so the signal is depth asymmetry times relative participation. The edge persists because the same shallow side that creates it caps the size that can be traded against it, and because estimating absorption-per-dwell-time requires joint real-time tracking of trade volume and time-at-price per name rather than any single observable quote statistic.
factors.name: Dwell-time-normalized absorption depth asymmetry

factors.trading_idea: The parent measured a name's lag-6 block sign concordance and used it as a continuation coefficient; the realized IC was negative because a high trailing concordance is not a forecast of continuation but the *footprint of a push already in progress* — at the 10-second scale, long runs of same-signed 60-second displacements are produced by sliced metaorders, and the run is most visibly long precisely when the schedule is closest to finished, after which the transient part of impact relaxes. The child keeps Rice's scale-free, tick-size-free machinery but re-uses it as a calibration device instead of a coefficient: given the name's own trailing flip probability p between adjacent non-overlapping 6-bar blocks, block-sign run lengths are geometric, so F = 1 − (1−p)^(L−1) is a probability-integral transform of the current run length — uniform under the null and therefore directly comparable across names whose normal alternation rates differ by an order of magnitude. We bet *against* the direction of anomalously improbable runs, and gate the bet on block volume receding below its own recent norm, which separates an exhausted metaorder (impact decays) from one still being worked (flow continues). The edge persists because reversion desks apply one common reversion speed and unconditional windows to the whole cross-section; the per-name geometric calibration of what counts as an unusual run, plus the flow-fade condition, is what is left on the table, and each event pays too little to be worth harvesting outside a broad diversified book.
factors.name: Rice-calibrated streak improbability with flow-fade reversal

factors.trading_idea: The parent estimated the sign-concordance autocorrelation of *increments* and treated a positive estimate as continuation; that object is nearly unidentified over 80 minutes and a positive reading actually flags names being pushed by sliced metaorder flow whose accumulated displacement is largely transient — which is why the realized direction contradicted the declared one. The child moves the same Rice orthant inversion from increments to *levels*: for the deviation x of log-price from its own causal EWMA anchor, P(sign(x_t) != sign(x_{t-6})) = arccos(phi_6)/pi, so phi_6 = cos(pi*p_flip) is a variance-free, jump-immune estimate of how much of a current dislocation still survives 6 bars, and by stationarity the implied forecast (phi_6 - 1)*x is *always* reversal with a name-specific decay fraction kappa = 1 - phi_6. Because a fixed anchor filter imposes the same baseline phi on every name, only the cross-sectional *dispersion* of kappa is informative, so the signal is the per-bar cross-sectional residual of -kappa*z on z itself: it is orthogonal by construction to the heavily-arbitraged common short-term reversal and pays only if fast-crossing (bounce-dominated) names revert more than slow-crossing (metaorder/persistent) names. The edge persists because reversion desks apply one calibrated half-life per book or liquidity bucket; extracting the residual requires continuous per-name re-estimation with a sign-only estimator that survives the fat ticks which corrupt OLS/variance-based half-lives, and each name's contribution is tiny and only diversifies in a broad book.
factors.name: Level-crossing OU-speed dispersion reversal wedge

factors.trading_idea: Parent B forecasts the market response a laggard still *owes* over exactly the next 6 bars (distributed-lag loadings convolved with the already-observed market slices) plus the folded AR(1) continuation of its own idiosyncratic innovation, but it judges 'slowness' with ad-hoc staleness proxies; Parent A shows that the local path itself reveals whether the mid is mechanically free to move — the conversion ratio c = |residual net displacement| / (|residual net displacement| + probed excursion path), both in grid-quantum units. The child uses c as the *delivery-speed state variable* for the owed catch-up: when c is high the book has been swept and quotes travel freely, so the owed beta move is actually delivered inside the 6-bar window and the converted displacement is transient impact whose AR snapback is real; when c is low the probes were absorbed by resting liquidity, the mid is pinned so the owed catch-up will NOT arrive in 6 bars, and instead the unfilled probe excursion (volume-gated wick asymmetry, in return units) is what the stale mid must catch up to. Neither parent has this: A never removes the owed systematic component from its displacement channel (so its two polarities are contaminated by market beta) and B never conditions delivery on whether the local book absorbs or converts, which is exactly why A's edge leaked out to 24 bars while B's catch-up piece fired unconditionally.
factors.name: Conversion-gated owed market catch-up vs absorbed probe pressure

factors.trading_idea: Extreme-value theory for a driftless random walk fixes how often a price should print new N-bar extremes; a name that has churned inside its 10-minute range while printing *fewer* new extremes than its own random-walk norm has been reflected off standing limit-order walls, whereas a name printing an excess of new extremes has met a liquidity vacuum and the barriers have been removed. The strength of those walls is corroborated by how much of the window's traded volume was absorbed while price sat in the outer quartiles of the range: real size resting at the edge produces high edge-volume share, thin quote drift does not.
