Hence range position is not a reversal signal per se — its forward sign is *switched* by the record-count deficit/excess and the edge-absorption share, so the factor is a state-conditioned dislocation rather than a plain reversal, and it acts inside one minute because posted walls and depleted queues both live on that timescale. The edge survives arbitrage because monetising it means quoting passively at a tested range edge against possibly-informed sweep flow for a fraction of a spread — inventory risk that cannot be hedged directionally.
factors.name: Record-deficit / edge-absorption gated range position (h=6)

factors.trading_idea: A basket/program execution (ETF create-redeem, index program) allocates dollars in proportion to capitalisation weight, so the displacement it inflicts on name i is w_i times its measured price impact per dollar (Amihud lambda_i) — a cross-sectional direction that is *not* beta. Rather than assuming this mechanical push equals the market return times a rank wedge (the parent's weakness: a static loading times a market-return scalar, so it can only ever detect basket flow whose sign matches the index move), the child *estimates the realised price of the elasticity direction each bar* by a contemporaneous cross-sectional OLS of returns on the beta-orthogonalised elasticity loading, so a basket redemption inside a rising tape (or a creation inside a falling tape) is detected with the correct sign. Only elasticity-price moves that are confirmed by a basket-shaped volume footprint (the cross-sectional slope of each name's excess dollar-volume share on its cap-weight direction) are treated as mechanical liquidity demand and faded, with an exponential propagator kernel over the un-relaxed part; names that simultaneously attracted extra idiosyncratic (non-basket) flow relax faster and get the larger fade. It survives arbitrage because market-neutral books hedge index exposure with beta, leaving the weight-per-depth heterogeneity of mechanical basket impact structurally unhedged, and harvesting it needs simultaneous many-name execution inside ~a minute.
factors.name: Basket elasticity price snapback (flow-confirmed, beta-orthogonal)

factors.trading_idea: The parent showed that a beta-residual displacement does get repaired, but it traded the *onset* blindly: its clock came from unconditional zero-crossing counts, so it mixed names whose repair had not begun (payoff far beyond 60s, hence the IC peak at 24 bars) with names already mid-repair. The child conditions on the repair being observably *in flight*: the pre-impulse residual displacement (bars t-L..t-k) sets the direction that must be paid back, the last k bars measure how much of it has already been retraced, and the residual edge lives only in the incomplete remainder — inventory unwinding is executed as a schedule, so a partially executed tranche predicts the remaining tranches. Completion time is projected as remaining/observed-repair-speed, then rescaled by the volume-arrival burst ratio, because impact decay is paced by trade arrivals: repair achieved during an unsustainable volume burst will take more calendar time to finish, so it is downweighted. Only setups whose projected completion sits on the 6-bar holding window are traded (sech^2 kernel), which should move the IC peak from 24 bars onto the fixed horizon; the edge survives arbitrage because it requires jointly estimating an idiosyncratic (beta-purified) unfinished quantity, its realized repair velocity and the local liquidity pace, none of which is a standalone tradable price pattern.
factors.name: Repair-onset progress with volume-paced completion clock

factors.trading_idea: At 10-second resolution common shocks travel along *characteristic* lines (value, quality, leverage, size, turnover) as much as along GICS lines, because factor-ETF creation, risk-model hedging and systematic programs trade characteristic baskets, not industry baskets. I therefore strip each name's 6-bar standardized move of its fitted characteristic-factor component with a per-bar cross-sectional WLS on point-in-time fundamental loadings (loadings held fixed inside causal blocks, refreshed from the snapshot available at the block start) and fade only the residue that is idiosyncratic *after* characteristic neutralization. Two name-level conditioners carry the edge: (i) crowding — names sitting in a dense neighbourhood of the characteristic manifold absorb the most mechanical basket churn, so their post-neutralization residue is more inventory-driven and reverts harder; (ii) hedge disagreement — when the characteristic-neutral residual and the ordinary industry-neutral residual have opposite signs, the industry-hedged stat-arb crowd is leaning the wrong way, so the dislocation is not being competed away and its snap-back within six bars is larger. The edge persists because the arbitrage capital that would erase it is overwhelmingly industry/sector-neutral by mandate and risk model, so exactly the industry-vs-characteristic misattribution it creates stays unhedged; it is falsified if the signal's IC vanishes once ordinary industry-neutral reversal is controlled for, or if the crowding and disagreement gates carry no incremental IC over the ungated residual.
factors.name: Characteristic-manifold-neutral residual reversal, crowding & hedge-disagreement gated

factors.trading_idea: The parent measured *timing* through an oscillator phase, but a full Kuramoto entrainment cycle only resolves over ~24 bars, which is why its information showed up far past the fixed 60-second offset. The same timing idea has a strictly faster expression: estimate each name's free-form distributed-lag response kernel b(1..L) to the leave-one-out market mean field, and forecast only the *not-yet-delivered* part of already-observed common shocks, F = Σ_m [Σ_{i=1..H} b(m+i)] · M_{t-m} — an explicitly horizon-matched projection instead of a cycle-scale sinusoid. The new conditioning variable is the name's own event clock: information is impounded on trade arrivals, not on wall-clock time, so a name currently trading faster than its own baseline compresses its remaining lag profile (effective horizon H_j ≈ 6·λ̃_j), and we blend H∈{3,6,12} kernels by that relative activity. The edge survives arbitrage because naive lead-lag arb estimates a single contemporaneous beta and assumes immediate catch-up, thereby paying the laggard's spread while carrying timing risk; converting the deficit into an intensity-conditional expected return requires joint per-name lag-kernel and arrival-rate estimation at 10-second resolution, and it is only profitable on the fast subset, which caps deployable capital.
factors.name: Event-clock warped distributed-lag catch-up kernel

factors.trading_idea: The parent showed that *total* fresh volume-weighted displacement reverses at the 6-bar horizon, which is exactly what you expect if a large share of fast repricing is mechanical basket/liquidity-demand pressure rather than name-specific information. I therefore split each name's recent displacement by the *contemporaneous source of the activity that produced it*: increments that arrived while the whole cross-section was simultaneously busy (common liquidity demand — index/ETF/macro sweeps) are largely transient under the Bouchaud propagator and overshoot in relative-value terms, whereas increments that arrived while only this name was unusually busy reflect an idiosyncratic metaorder whose order flow is strongly autocorrelated at second scales and keeps arriving. The factor is the contrast between the idio-activity-weighted and the common-activity-weighted mean normalised increment over the last 6 bars, so the level of aggregate displacement (the already-mined reversal carrier) largely cancels and only the attribution survives. Falsifiable: if the two legs have the same IC sign, or the contrast has zero IC, the common-vs-idiosyncratic attribution of fast repricing is wrong; the edge survives arbitrage because deciding in real time whether a 10-second move was funded by basket flow requires panel-wide synchronisation and its correction offers only one-minute, spread-limited capacity.
factors.name: Activity-commonality split displacement contrast

factors.trading_idea: Parent A shows that drift printed in quiet (near-zero-volume) bars continues while drift paid for with aggressive volume decays, but its edge is slow (peaks near 24 bars) because quiet repricing only becomes a tradeable price once someone actually trades against the shaded quote. Parent B supplies the two state variables that fix this: (i) path efficiency versus the k^(-1/2) random-walk null, which separates genuine one-way relocation from flickering round-trip quote noise, and (ii) a Hawkes conditional arrival hazard, i.e. the probability that a trade lands within the next 6 bars. The child therefore signs each of A's two legs by the purity of its own path — quiet drift is continued only when its quiet sub-path is efficient and faded when it is wobble; traded drift is reverted only in proportion to how churny (inefficient, hence transient-impact-dominated) the traded sub-path was — and then weights the continuation leg by the arrival hazard and the reversion leg by (1 − hazard). The interaction is the edge: the hazard is a clock that converts A's slow quiet-repricing continuation into a signal realised inside the fixed 6-bar offset (repricing only pays when the silence is about to break), while temporary impact decays fastest exactly where self-excitation has died out, so neither parent's leg alone carries this horizon-matched, purity-conditioned information.
factors.name: Hazard-Matched Efficiency Split of Quiet vs Traded Drift

factors.trading_idea: The parent showed that classifying dislocations by the cross-sectional company of their *birth* carries information the book does not span, but it traded a slow object (deviation from a 20-bar anchor) whose relaxation mostly lands beyond the fixed 6-bar offset. The child keeps the birth-cohort idea and sharpens it two ways: (i) events are magnitude-thresholded *signed* impulses (a marked point process), so the cohort can be split into same-direction co-arrivals (index-level / basket liquidity demand that dealers warehouse and unwind within seconds) and opposite-direction co-arrivals (cross-sectional rotation, i.e. evidence the name moved on its own account); (ii) only impulses born in the last 5 bars are traded, and the traded quantity is the *peer-relative unpaid displacement* accumulated since the impulse, measured in the impulse's own volatility units, so the remaining relaxation is forced to overlap the fixed 6-bar forward window. Prediction: relative displacement born inside a same-signed co-arrival burst reverts within a minute, while displacement born against the cross-sectional flow (low or negative net co-arrival lift) continues; the edge persists because it needs joint signed point-process bookkeeping across names at the 10-second scale and the payoff is small-amplitude and capacity-limited.
factors.name: Signed-coarrival impulse cohort reversal

factors.trading_idea: At any instant the cross-section of vol-standardised, sector-demeaned 3-minute displacements has a Gaussian-shaped core (the central limit consequence of many small, common liquidity shocks) plus a small set of names sitting far outside that shape; only the latter represents a genuinely idiosyncratic order-flow event that has just consumed local liquidity, and it is those names — not the core — whose displacement is repaid by liquidity providers over the next minute. I therefore fit, every bar, a robust normal-probability (Q-Q) line to the *interquantile core only* (|Φ⁻¹(rank)| ≤ 1) and treat the residual of each name from that line, expressed in units of the fitted core scale, as its 'excess stretch'; the signal fades that excess stretch. Two things make this falsifiable rather than a repackaged reversal: (i) if short-horizon reversal were uniform (linear) in cross-sectional rank, the Q-Q residual would carry no incremental information over plain rank reversal and the IC would be ~0, and (ii) if the shape line is calibrated on the whole cross-section instead of the core, tail names drag the fit and the signal must weaken. The edge survives arbitrage because the definition of 'extreme' is regime-adaptive (it rescales automatically when market-wide dispersion jumps, where fixed z-thresholds misfire), and because capacity is bounded by exactly the thin, event-hit names that generate the effect — standard linear reversal books put most of their risk in the crowded, informationless core.
factors.name: Cross-Sectional Q-Q Core-Calibrated Tail Stretch Snapback

factors.trading_idea: A lagging name receives an owed market impulse through two physically distinct routes: free quote-side repricing by market makers reading the index (mid moves with no commensurate aggressive volume) and trade-driven impact when someone actually lifts the offer (volume-paid moves). Parent B's distributed-lag 'owed catch-up' forecast averages blindly over both routes, and Parent A's paid/unpaid split ignores why the mid should move at all; the child conditions each on the other. Owed catch-up is trusted where the name's recent displacement has been route-open, i.e. predominantly unpaid quote revision, and is discounted where the recent move was bought with volume, because square-root-law paid displacement at 10-second scale is largely transient Bouchaud impact that decays inside the next minute rather than a genuine repricing; correspondingly the residual (market-orthogonal) part of the move continues on its unpaid leg and fades on its paid leg, with the split weighted by the name's own measured Roll transient-variance share phi. This also fixes Parent A's realized-sign contradiction with mechanism rather than a sign flip: single-lag autocovariance (phi) captures bounce that has *already* reverted within the bar, so it is the low-phi names whose paid impact still has decay left to harvest, while in high-phi names the informative motion is the quote-side leg that carries the delayed index adjustment forward.
factors.name: Quote-route gated owed catch-up with paid/unpaid residual polarity

factors.trading_idea: Instead of the parent's occupancy geometry (67% correlated with the book, and with the wrong declared sign), the child measures dislocation in the *precision metric* of the trailing return covariance: y = Sigma^{-1} x, the Mahalanobis / Kritzman-Li whitening of the last 6 bars of vol-standardized returns. Inverting Sigma up-weights moves along historically low-variance eigen-directions - i.e. tight relative-value spreads inside industries/baskets - so a large |y| flags a move that is inconsistent with the recent correlation structure, the signature of size-driven, basket-inconsistent liquidity demand rather than information; market-maker inventory limits and stat-arb capital close such spreads on a ~1-minute clock, so the whitened deviation should predict its own reversal. Crucially, the whitened deviation is orthogonalized cross-sectionally against the plain 6-bar standardized move, so what survives is only the correlation-structure-inconsistent piece: if the information were carried by the univariate move alone, the residual would have zero IC (that is the falsification test). The edge persists because each episode is worth a few ticks along a low-variance direction, requires simultaneous multi-name execution and a stable, regularized rolling precision matrix (eigenvalue-floored, diagonally shrunk), and is invisible to univariate reversal / momentum screens which we explicitly project out.
factors.name: Precision-whitened low-variance dislocation snapback

factors.trading_idea: Whether a 10-second mid-price displacement continues or snaps back is not a universal constant: it depends on the name's current microstructural state (sign of the last tick, direction of the prior half-minute drift, and whether the bar carried above- or below-normal participation), and the state-to-drift map itself differs across names and across the hour. Instead of imposing a reversal or momentum sign, the child estimates that map online — a per-name, trailing, non-parametric conditional expectation of the next 6-bar volatility-standardised return given a 12-cell discrete state, shrunk empirical-Bayes toward the name's own unconditional trailing drift and then *net of* that drift, so pure momentum/reversal levels are differenced out and only genuine state-dependence survives. The edge persists because the sign of the conditional drift flips across names and regimes, so any pooled static reversal rule averages it to zero, and HFT liquidity providers gate on spread and depth rather than maintaining per-name conditional transition tables over the last hour of bar sequences; the falsifiable claim is that predictability is concentrated in names whose between-state dispersion of conditional means is statistically large (the chi-square-like confidence gate), and that removing the unconditional mean does not kill the IC.
factors.name: State-conditional analogue drift table with confidence gate

factors.trading_idea: A trade-backed price push carries two mutually exclusive microstructural interpretations, and the multi-bar price path itself reveals which one holds: if the bar closes at the extreme of the last few bars' path, aggressive flow is still in control of the queue and the displacement is not yet owed back (continuation); if price has already retraced inside that path, liquidity providers have visibly absorbed the flow and hold inventory that must be repaid through subsequent relocations (reversal). The parent lumped both states into one per-name kernel estimated on calendar lags 2..8, which mixed the two opposite responses and pushed most forecast mass past the 6-bar horizon (its IC peaked at 12 bars). The child therefore (i) splits each volume-weighted body push softly by its own trailing-ranked retracement state and (ii) replaces the summed one-step kernel with a *direct* horizon-matched regression of the realized bounce-purged 5-bar-ahead return on lagged split pushes, so every estimated coefficient describes mass that actually lands inside the fixed 6-bar window. Falsifiable: the pooled cross-sectional coefficient should be positive for the unretraced (still-pushing) channel and negative for the retraced (absorbed) channel, and the split forecast should beat an unsplit one; the edge survives arbitrage because capturing it requires posting passive size against possibly-informed aggressive flow for a fraction of a spread, i.e. bearing market-making inventory and adverse-selection risk rather than lifting a directional mispricing.
factors.name: Retracement-state split, direct 6-bar push response

factors.trading_idea: On LOBSTER-style mid-price bars there is no bid-ask bounce, so the negative serial dependence a naive estimator sees at the 10-second scale is almost entirely a *level* artefact of transient quote noise (each m-bar variance is inflated by a constant 2*omega^2 that telescopes away), while the genuine dynamics of the efficient price are order-flow driven and persistent (metaorder splitting gives long-memory trade signs, and permanent impact accrues gradually). The parent measured the noise-contaminated dependence — hence it estimated reversal for nearly every name and its realized IC came out with the sign flipped; the child removes the noise level analytically (omega^2 from the lag-1 return autocovariance) and then reads the *efficient-price* self-similarity exponent H from the slope of log variance versus log aggregation scale, converting it to the horizon-matched block autocorrelation with the exact fractional-Gaussian identity rho = 2^(2H-1) - 1, which is scale-invariant and therefore is precisely the coefficient linking one 6-bar block to the next. Forecast = rho_hat times the current standardised 6-bar displacement, so names whose corrected exponent shows flow persistence continue while the (now much rarer) genuinely anti-persistent, inventory-dominated names revert. The edge persists because the obvious uncorrected version of this statistic has the wrong average sign — a desk running raw variance ratios or raw sign-flip concordance is pushed into systematic fading of continuation — and harvesting the corrected version requires per-name, continuously updated noise-variance estimation whose per-name payoff is tiny and only diversifies in a broad book.
factors.name: Noise-corrected self-similar memory block continuation

factors.trading_idea: Transient price impact from aggressive flow is repaid as market makers unwind inventory, and that unwinding happens on the *trade clock*, not the wall clock (a Bouchaud-style propagator in volume time): the still-unrepaid share of a push made m bars ago decays like exp(-lambda * volume traded since), and the share that will be repaid inside exactly the next 6 bars is 1 - exp(-lambda * expected volume over those 6 bars), forecastable from the well-documented self-exciting clustering of trade arrivals. So rather than estimating a noisy per-name calendar-time lag kernel (the parent's weakness — high complexity, edge drifting to 12 bars), the child carries a single state variable, the outstanding trade-backed debt stock D_t, and interacts it with the horizon-matched repayment intensity: two names with identical recent price paths get different forecasts depending on how much volume has already absorbed the push and how much volume is about to arrive. Falsifiable: if impact decayed in calendar time, or if quiet names reverted as much as busy ones, the volume-clock conditioning would add nothing and IC would not be positive at the fixed 6-bar offset. The edge survives arbitrage because capturing it means posting passive size against possibly-informed aggressive flow for a fraction of a spread (inventory risk, not a riskless arb), and it needs joint price/flow bookkeeping that plain price-based reversal signals do not carry.
factors.name: Volume-clock impact-repayment debt × expected forward flow

factors.trading_idea: The parent measured a *symmetric* local-time density around the current mid, which cannot distinguish the two opposite states it mixes: transacted/visited mass sitting AHEAD of the price along the axis of travel (a shelf that must be eaten, so the move is absorbed) from mass sitting BEHIND it (levels just vacated, which act as a support shelf and let the move extend). After a 6-bar move the recently occupied levels are mechanically behind the price, so a high symmetric density is dominated by the 'support behind' state — which is exactly why the parent's realized IC came out with continuation sign rather than the reversal sign it declared. The child therefore signs the occupancy along the direction of travel: it computes the time-and-volume mass that historically sat in a horizon-matched band immediately ahead of the mid versus the mirror band immediately behind, and predicts absorption (reversal) when the shelf is ahead and extension (continuation) when the shelf is behind and the path ahead is a vacuum. The edge should persist because it requires maintaining a per-name volume-by-price occupancy profile and a directional band scaled to the name's own 6-bar volatility, pays only a few ticks per episode, and its cause — where resting/transacted inventory actually sits relative to the current quote — is a structural property of order books rather than a mispricing that arbitrage can delete.
factors.name: Forward-vs-rear occupancy mass asymmetry (absorption split)

factors.trading_idea: Parent B's Rice inversion (rho = cos(pi*p_flip)) is a scale-free, jump-robust way to read a per-name persistence coefficient off sign statistics, but applied to the *undifferentiated* tape it mixes two economically opposite streams — quote-side repricing in silent bars (information, continues) and taker impact in traded bars (transient, pays back) — so the pooled coefficient is mis-signed, exactly the contradiction its report flagged. The child estimates the Rice coefficient separately for each of Parent A's two channels, and estimates it as a *cross*-concordance (does the sign of last block's quiet-only / traded-only displacement match the sign of the following non-overlapping 6-bar total move?), so each channel's coefficient is a directly predictive, self-calibrated slope whose sign the name's own history determines rather than the researcher. Exposure is then concentrated by Parent A's disagreement gate: when quotes walk one way while aggressive flow pushes the other, the maker-inventory / taker-liquidity tug-of-war must be settled at the next handful of liquidity events (inside ~60 seconds), which is precisely the fixed 6-bar horizon, whereas concordant states are slow information that only pays out at 24+ bars. The interaction carries edge neither parent has: A supplies the state decomposition and the fast-resolving gate but had no per-name coefficient (only fixed +0.5/-1.0 weights), while B supplied the estimator but pointed it at a contaminated single stream — channel-wise Rice coefficients let bouncy names revert and schedule-executed names continue *within each channel independently*.
factors.name: Quiet/Traded Rice Cross-Concordance Forecast under Maker-Taker Disagreement

factors.trading_idea: The parent showed that splitting recent drift into zero-volume (quote-repricing) and high-volume (paid-impact) components carries information, but its order-blind cumulative sums bet on a slow catch-up that only pays off over several minutes. The *ordering* of the two channels inside the window is a much faster statistic: because a 10-second bar is either quiet or traded, the pair (cumulative quiet return, cumulative traded return) traces an exact staircase whose signed Lévy area measures chirality — whether quotes moved first and trades then followed (quote-led, information being validated by liquidity demanders, so the displacement continues over the next minute) or trades moved first and quotes merely drifted after (trade-led, i.e. the tail of transient impact, so the displacement decays). The area is invariant to a joint sign flip of both channels, so it is a pure lead-lag/rotation measure that can be multiplied by the window displacement to produce a conditional continuation-vs-reversal bet; it flips as soon as leadership flips, which is why the edge lives at the 6-bar offset instead of 24. It survives arbitrage because harvesting it requires bar-level volume partitioning plus a path-ordering functional, and the naive unconditional bets (momentum or reversal on the same displacement) are roughly a wash — the money is in the conditioning; falsified if the sign of the chirality carries no interaction with forward returns, i.e. quote-led and trade-led displacements decay identically.
factors.name: Quiet/Traded Channel Lévy-Area Chirality Gated Displacement

factors.trading_idea: The parent's realized sign says the truth is the reverse of its book-support story: a 1-minute move that leaves the price in a *rarely-occupied* region of its own recent path snaps back, while a move that keeps the price inside the well-occupied core continues. The correct mechanism is transient impact, not resting depth — an excursion out of the recent occupation support is mostly mechanical (a metaorder walking a thin, freshly-quoted region plus quote noise), and mechanical displacement decays; a move that stays inside the occupied core has not consumed anything and simply drifts. The genuinely new conditioning axis is whether the excursion was *paid for*: displacement achieved on abnormally low traded volume is almost pure impact and reverses hardest, whereas displacement accompanied by an abnormal volume burst is information being absorbed and is permanent (Hasbrouck-style permanent component), so the extreme-volume branch flips to continuation. All windows are shortened (kernel-occupancy horizon 30 bars, recency halflife ~6 bars, recency-weighted 6-bar move) so the statistic turns over on the same clock as the fixed 6-bar forecast instead of the parent's 90/240-bar clock, which pushed its power out to 24 bars. The edge survives arbitrage because it requires a per-name nonparametric kernel local-time estimate interacted with a volume-surprise state, pays only a few ticks per episode, and its cause (transient impact is larger where the price has not recently traded) is a structural property of order-book replenishment rather than a mispricing that can be traded away.
factors.name: Occupancy-deficit excursion snapback, volume-paid modulated

factors.trading_idea: A name's response to market-wide information is a *shape*, not a lag: it can be split into an owed catch-up at short lags and a payback (overshoot correction) at longer lags, and both land inside a fixed 6-bar window. The parent truncated the impulse response at L=H=6 with shrunk free betas, so it could only ever see catch-up owed in the next 1-2 bars — which is why its IC peaked at 1 bar and flipped sign by 12 bars. The child estimates the whole distributed-lag kernel out to 18 lags via exact trailing multivariate OLS on three orthogonalised exponential (Almon/Laguerre-type) basis filters of the cap-weighted market path, then analytically folds that kernel against the *already observed* market path to get E[sum of returns over bars t+1..t+6]; lags l>6 contribute only to the mid/far part of that window and can carry negative loadings, so the forecast nets catch-up against scheduled payback at the exact evaluation offset. The edge survives arbitrage because the state variable that makes it work is measurement-heavy (a 4-parameter rolling kernel plus a partial-R^2 trust statistic) and concentrated in slow-repricing names (frozen mids, thin recent volume) where second-scale attention is scarcest; it is falsified if the lagged-basis block adds no partial R^2 over the contemporaneous beta, or if the folded far-lag component has no incremental 6-bar information over the parent's 6-lag trailing fold.
factors.name: Smooth-basis lag kernel: horizon-matched catch-up minus scheduled payback

factors.trading_idea: A name's idiosyncratic 60-second dislocation is closed by relative-value traders only if the name has cheap, redundant substitutes to hedge against; the right mathematical object for 'neighbourhood redundancy' is the discrete Ricci curvature of the co-movement graph, and Forman's combinatorial curvature gives it in closed form from the weighted k-nearest-neighbour correlation network. Names sitting in a strongly negatively-curved (dense, redundant, many-substitute) region of the network are cheap to hedge, so any idiosyncratic excursion is arbitraged back inside the minute; names in a flat/peripheral region have no substitute basket, so their idio move is un-hedgeable, is left alone by stat-arb desks, and instead drifts as the only carrier of its own information. The factor is therefore a pure interaction — reversal strength as a signed, cross-sectionally centred function of network curvature (orthogonalised to market beta so it is not a beta wedge) — which mechanically nets out the plain reversal component and isolates the arbitrage-capacity channel. It should persist because it is compensation for hedging risk and estimation cost, not a mispricing: the substitute network is time-varying and must be re-estimated continuously, and the very desks that would compete it away are the ones constrained by it.
factors.name: Substitute-network Forman curvature reversal wedge

factors.trading_idea: A slow repricer owes a known amount of market-driven catch-up, but that backlog can only be paid out on bars where its mid actually re-quotes; therefore the fraction of the backlog that lands inside a FIXED 6-bar window is governed by the name's quote-update intensity, not by its staleness level. The parent amplified the stalest names, which is exactly where the owed mass is delivered after the evaluation offset (hence its IC turning negative at 12-24 bars); the child instead estimates the per-update impulse response on the name's own update clock (bars with a moving mid, after purging Roll-bounce autocorrelation from the regressand) and multiplies the owed quantity by the Poisson deliverable share 1-exp(-lambda*6), where lambda is the trailing per-bar update rate. It is further conditioned on a falsifiable trust statistic: the share of total response mass carried by lags 1..6 versus lag 0 - if lagged loadings carry no incremental information the signal is switched off. The edge survives arbitrage because measuring delivery capacity requires joint estimation of a distributed-lag kernel and a per-name re-quote hazard at 10-second granularity, and the names with high backlog but adequate update capacity are mid-attention, thin-quote names that fast market makers do not warehouse.
factors.name: Update-clock deliverable backlog share (6-bar)

factors.trading_idea: The parent's evaluation showed a robust interaction but the *opposite* sign to the one declared, and the correct reading is the propagator (Obizhaeva-Wang / Bouchaud) one rather than the information one: bar-level mid displacement that arrives together with abnormal trade volume is mostly *transient* price impact from liquidity demand (metaorder slices, inventory offloading) and mechanically relaxes as the book refills, whereas displacement that arrives with little or no trade is pure quote-driven revision of the market-maker's belief, which is permanent and tends to be extended by the follow-on latent flow. So the correct object is not a product of two noisy ranks but a *decomposition*: split each bar's peer-residual return into a trade-attributable and a quiet part using the bar's participation share v/(v+trailing mean v), then weight past bars by the propagator's remaining-decay kernel (exponential, halflife 3 bars) so the signal is dominated by impact that still has most of its relaxation ahead of it inside the next ~60 seconds — this is what moves the peak IC from 12 bars to the fixed 6-bar offset. The edge persists because harvesting it means supplying liquidity against possibly-informed bursts (you are paid the impact-decay premium for bearing that adverse-selection risk), and because it requires joining point-in-time per-share fundamentals (to build valuation-tier comparability groups that strip common factor moves) with bar-level trade attribution — microstructure desks never build the fundamental peer map and fundamental relative-value desks cannot act in a minute. Falsified if the trade-attributable and quiet components of the same peer-residual displacement carry the same forward coefficient at 6 bars, or if the wedge disappears once peers are formed by sector text alone.
factors.name: Valuation-peer propagator split: quiet-repricing vs traded-impact relaxation wedge

factors.trading_idea: Keep the parent's one genuinely microstructural insight — that mid displacement printed in (near-)zero-volume bars is quote-side repricing while displacement printed on volume thinner than the square-root impact law implies is an unbacked taker push — but throw away the beta-backlog / payout-clientele scaffolding that the report shows is already spanned by the book (residual IC ~0, corr 0.55 to an existing catch-up factor) and peaks far too slowly (24 bars). The child instead asserts that the *sign* of each channel's forward response is a slowly-varying, name-specific state, not a universal constant: in quote-led regimes (informed limit-order repricing) quiet-bar drift continues, while in taker-pushed regimes the impact-deflated active-bar drift reverts, and each name's current polarity is estimable causally from a horizon-matched trailing regression of completed 6-bar returns on the same two channel predictors lagged exactly 6 bars. The edge persists because arbitrageurs almost universally hard-code one polarity (always fade the taker push, or always follow the quote), which gets whipsawed whenever a name flips regime; estimating and soft-thresholding a two-channel response coefficient per name is a noisy nuisance-parameter problem that is unattractive to standardise, and the state itself is refreshed by exogenous changes in who is supplying liquidity. Falsifiable: if channel response polarity were constant across names and time, the sign-agreement-filtered trailing coefficients would carry no incremental information and the factor's IC would collapse to that of a fixed-sign reversal/continuation combination.
factors.name: Channel-conditional response polarity (quiet-quote vs impact-deflated taker leg)

factors.trading_idea: For a quasi-periodic idiosyncratic excursion dev(t)=A·sin(omega·t), the lag-k autocorrelation of non-overlapping k-bar displacements is exactly cos(omega·k); Parent A's Rice inversion rho=cos(pi·p_flip) therefore collapses to the identity half-period T = k / p_flip, where p_flip is the trailing sign-flip frequency between adjacent k-bar displacements — a tick-size-free, jump-robust clock estimator that needs no volatility or spectral moments. This is why Parent A's declared sign was contradicted: it treated rho as a persistence coefficient, when rho is a *phase* object (rho near +1 means a slow clock, i.e. the current displacement sits near the excursion peak and is about to snap back), so rho·displacement systematically forecast the wrong way. The child feeds that concordance clock straight into Parent B's horizon-matched phase projection, where the excursion age tau since the last zero crossing decides whether the extreme is still being approached (extend) or already passed (revert), and cross-validates it against an independent Kac crossing-count clock. Finally the projection is cross-sectionally orthogonalised against the raw standardised deviation, stripping out the slow-accruing pure-level reversal component that made Parent B's IC peak at 24 bars and leaving only the age-conditional phase term, which is genuinely horizon-matched to 6 bars.
factors.name: Rice-concordance clock excursion-phase projection

factors.trading_idea: The parent read the trailing volume-at-price profile as a Fokker-Planck stationary density and traded price back toward the nearest occupation mode; the realized IC was consistently the opposite sign at every horizon, which is exactly what latent-liquidity microstructure predicts: over 10-second scales the occupation measure is not a potential well, it is a map of *already-absorbed* inventory — levels where lots of volume has traded are levels where resting queues have been tested and refilled, i.e. resistance — while thinly-visited price regions have no queue to absorb marketable flow, so a given amount of order flow moves price much further there (Weber–Rosenow / Bouchaud latent-book: price follows the path of least resistance). The child therefore measures, in a band whose width is horizon-matched to how far the price can plausibly travel in 6 bars (±c·sigma·sqrt(6)), the *asymmetry* of volume-weighted occupation mass immediately above versus below the current price, and predicts drift toward the thin side, with force proportional to the magnitude of the ongoing 12-bar push and gated by whether that push is backed by elevated traded volume (an unbacked drift into a void is quote noise and reverts, a flow-backed one keeps travelling). To avoid re-mining the value-area-escape / distance-to-VWAP trade, the raw interaction is orthogonalised per name against the volume-weighted linear deviation from the same profile over a trailing 240-bar window, keeping only the local band-shape information; the edge persists because it requires maintaining a per-name occupation histogram and evaluating an asymmetric, horizon-scaled band around the live price every 10 seconds, and the payoff is a fraction of the spread, so capacity is small relative to the effort.
factors.name: Horizon-band void asymmetry (flow-backed drift)

factors.trading_idea: Parent B knows *when* a one-sided (semivariance-asymmetric) burst can turn — only after the one-sided flow abates and price lifts off the burst extreme — but it judges *whether* the burst was informative with a crude linear leverage damping. Parent A knows *whether* a move was informative — a Merton/Christie consistency test asking if realised-vol expansion matched the elasticity implied by the firm's leverage — but it fires on every bar with no notion of flow phase, so its reversal leg is often entered while the liquidation is still running. The child estimates the Christie elasticity on the *semivariance-asymmetry channel* (per-bar cross-sectional OLS of log short-run RV expansion on |move|, signed move, downside-asymmetry excess, and that excess interacted with ranked leverage and ranked size) and uses the residual as an informativeness state, then splits by flow phase: an uninformative burst (deficient vol response vs its leverage-implied elasticity) is traded for snapback ONLY once volume contracts and price is off the extreme, while an informative burst (excess vol response) is traded for continuation ONLY while volume is still expanding and price still pinned at the extreme. The interaction carries edge neither parent has: informativeness tells you the sign, flow phase tells you the clock, and mismatching the two (A's early reversals, B's leverage-blind fades) is exactly where each parent leaks.
factors.name: Christie elasticity-gap gated semivariance-burst phase split

factors.trading_idea: The parent's decomposition of 6-bar displacement into a volume-paid (square-root-law) part and a flow-orthogonal part carries real information (|IC| peaks exactly at 6 bars, deflated t≈5.8) but the parent assigned the wrong polarity: at a 10-second sampling frequency a mid-price revision that no trade paid for is overwhelmingly Roll-type transient noise — quote flicker, one-sided depth withdrawal and refill, fleeting orders — and it mean-reverts, whereas displacement that aggressive volume actually paid for is the trade-information component (Hasbrouck's trade information share is non-trivial and its impact is only partially transient over a single minute), so it persists. The child therefore reverts the unpaid component and continues the paid component, and — this is the new conditioning variable — scales each side by a *measured*, per-name transient share estimated causally from the Roll relation phi = -2·cov(r_t, r_{t-1})/var(r): names whose own return process is dominated by negative first-order autocovariance are precisely the names whose unpaid moves are flicker (revert hard), while low-phi (efficient-quote) names are where paid displacement should be allowed to run. The edge survives arbitrage because the reverting amplitude on liquid mid-price series is comparable to half-spread and depth-consumption cost, so it is only harvestable as a passive/queue-position tilt, and because unconditional reversal traders are whipsawed on the low-phi, information-driven names that this factor explicitly refuses to fade.
factors.name: Roll noise-share gated unpaid-displacement reversal

factors.trading_idea: Keep the parent's phase-plane coordinate — a name's band-passed log-price displacement and its velocity locate it on a unit circle, so timing is measured separately from amplitude — but throw away the slow mean-field entrainment that only paid off a full cycle later. Instead, transient impact relaxes in *trade time* (Bouchaud-style propagator decay is paced by executed volume, not by the wall clock), so each name's phase advances at an empirically measured angular speed that is stretched or compressed by how briskly it is currently trading. The forecast for a fixed 6-bar offset is then the chord of the oscillation, A[cos(theta + dphi) - cos(theta)], where dphi = omega_hat * 6 * (current activity / normal activity): fast-clock names complete a quarter-to-half turn inside the window so their displacement is repaid (reversal), slow-clock names have not yet turned so their velocity carries (continuation). It survives arbitrage because standard reversion and momentum signals are estimated on fixed calendar windows and are blind to *when* the repayment lands relative to the trader's horizon; capturing it needs per-name estimation of phase-plane rotation speed and a volume-clock rescaling. Falsified if replacing the activity ratio by a constant (or the measured omega by a cross-sectional constant) leaves the IC unchanged, or if the rotation-consistency gate carries no information.
factors.name: Trade-clock phase advance chord switch

factors.trading_idea: The parent's per-name Rice coefficient had ~80 independent block pairs, so its cross-sectional dispersion was mostly estimation error that leaked the *recent path shape* into the coefficient: names whose last few minutes were persistently one-directional were assigned rho>0 and bought, which is precisely why the realized IC came out negative — sustained one-directional 10-second drift is the fingerprint of a sliced metaorder walking the book, and that displacement is largely transient impact that relaxes when the schedule pauses (Bouchaud propagator / Bacry-Lehalle metaorder relaxation). The child therefore drops per-name coefficient estimation entirely and measures the *shape* of the displacement directly with a nonparametric Kendall/Mann-Kendall time concordance (tau_a of idiosyncratic price level versus time over 5 minutes), then compares each name's monotonicity percentile to its volatility-scaled displacement percentile: for a given move size, a rank-monotone 'grind' path reverts, whereas a lumpy path (one or two large increments, low concordance for its size) is news-driven permanent repricing and does not. The edge persists because reversion desks condition on move size, volume and spread but not on path rank-shape; extracting shape needs per-name pairwise concordance statistics whose payoff per name is tiny and only diversifies in a broad cross-section, and the broker who actually knows the schedule will not trade against its own client.
factors.name: Grind-vs-jump path monotonicity wedge

factors.trading_idea: Under a Bouchaud-style propagator a 10-second mid displacement is a mixture of transient (liquidity-demand) and permanent (information) impact, and the mixture depends on WHO was trading when the move happened: bars where only this name was unusually busy versus bars where the whole panel was busy simultaneously. The parent hard-coded the direction of that attribution (idio-funded continues, common-funded relaxes) and the data contradicted it, which is exactly what you expect if the response coefficients of the propagator are state-dependent — resilience, depth-refill speed and the informativeness of single-name bursts all vary with the liquidity regime — so no fixed-sign formula can span them. This child therefore does not guess a sign: it measures two level-free 'activity tilts' of the last six bars of beta-residual displacement (tilt toward own-excess-activity bars, tilt toward market-wide-burst bars) and estimates the panel-pooled response of the realised 6-bar-ahead residual return to those two tilts on a trailing ~2-hour ridge regression, then forecasts with the fitted coefficients. It survives arbitrage because it needs synchronised panel-wide activity measurement plus continuous online recalibration at 10-second frequency, the coefficients flip with regime so a static alpha cannot replicate it, and its capacity is spread-limited at the one-minute horizon.
factors.name: Online-calibrated propagator response to activity-tilted displacement

factors.trading_idea: Whether a mid-price relocation printed in a *quiet* (near-zero-volume) bar is information or noise is not a universal constant — it is a persistent property of the name's quoting ecology: where quotes are repriced by informed liquidity providers protecting against adverse selection the untraded displacement is confirmed, whereas where quotes flicker (fleeting orders, thin one-side depth) it is stale-mid noise that snaps back; symmetrically, drift printed in heavy-volume bars is transient impact whose decay speed depends on how fast depth replenishes. The parent hard-coded these responses (+1 quiet, −0.5 traded) and was therefore just another fixed-sign drift factor that the book already spans; the child instead *measures* each name's own horizon-matched response coefficients with a trailing, causal, ridge-regularised 2-variable OLS of the realised 6-bar forward return on the quiet-bar and active-bar components of the preceding 6-bar return, shrinks them empirical-Bayes style toward the panel median, and outputs the resulting predicted 6-bar return. Because the sign of the loading is name- and time-specific rather than fixed, the signal is structurally close to orthogonal to the book's directional drift/reversal factors, and it survives arbitrage because harvesting it requires continuously re-estimating a slowly drifting per-name response coefficient and crossing the spread on momentarily quiet names. Falsifiable: if the panel-median quiet-channel coefficient is not positive and the active-channel coefficient not negative, or if per-name coefficients have no hour-to-hour persistence (so predictions are estimation noise), the IC collapses to zero; the horizon-matched construction also predicts |IC| peaks at 6 bars rather than 12.
factors.name: Empirical-Bayes response kernel on quiet vs traded drift channels

factors.trading_idea: Parent A's finding — a fresh, high-participation escape out of a tight trailing occupation band walks into thin resting depth and extends — is measured on raw mid price, where it is contaminated by market beta, staleness and Epps effects; Parent B builds the right coordinate (a lag-1/Epps-corrected precision-whitened, move-purged relative-value spread) plus the *role* of each name in the lead/lag field, but has almost no standalone direction. The child runs A's event geometry inside B's coordinate: it detects when the whitened relative-value spread escapes the 15/85 band it has been occupying, keeps only escapes that are fresh (spread was still inside the band within the last 6 bars), that came out of a genuinely coiled band (width tight versus the sqrt(N) random-walk benchmark) and that carry abnormal participation — and then signs the escape by the name's measured lead/lag role from the antisymmetric lag-1 correlation. The interaction is the edge: a *leader's* spread escape is information the peer field has not yet absorbed, so nothing is owed back and the dislocation extends into shallow depth; a *laggard's* escape is the delivery of catch-up already owed to the field, so it is complete and snaps back. Neither parent can tell these apart — A has no role information and no relative-value coordinate, B has no ignition event and so applies convergence to spreads that are simply escaping.
factors.name: Whitened-spread band escape, lead/lag-role gated

factors.trading_idea: Price changes accumulated in bars with (near-)zero traded volume are quote-driven repricing: market makers shading their quotes because of inventory or adverse-selection beliefs that no one has yet traded against. Price changes accumulated in high-volume bars already contain temporary impact that mechanically decays. Therefore the same 60-second drift should be *continued* when it was produced silently and *reverted* when it was paid for with aggressive volume; the persistence of this split is protected by the fact that trading the quiet component requires paying spread on thin names. Falsified if quiet-bar drift is simply stale-mid noise, in which case it reverts just like traded drift and the two components carry the same sign.
factors.name: Quiet-Bar Quote Repricing vs Traded-Bar Impact Split

factors.trading_idea: Algebraically the parent reduces to (H+L)-(O+C) over the range, i.e. it is long names whose *endpoints* sit below their bar's high-low centre — so the realized positive sign is not 'hidden supply above' but reversion of the endpoint toward the bar's range centre. The reason is statistical: (H+L)/2 averages two order statistics of the intrabar mid path and therefore carries far less microstructure noise than the single closing sample, so C-(H+L)/2 is mostly transient quote/bounce noise plus decaying transient impact, and it dies within a few bars. This child makes that mechanism explicit and testable by (i) isolating only the closing dislocation from the bar's own range centre, (ii) weighting each bar by 1/(1+V/median V) so *quiet* bars — where the dislocation is noise, not permanent impact — dominate, exactly inverting the parent's heavy-volume gate, and (iii) scaling by a horizon-matched two-scale noise share phi=(1-VR_6)*6/5 that measures what fraction of a name's 1-bar return variance actually dies inside 6 bars. The edge persists because harvesting it means quoting passively against the last aggressor and absorbing the adverse-selection/inventory risk that market makers are already compensated for; a taker who crosses the spread earns nothing, so the sub-spread dislocation is never arbitraged away.
factors.name: Noise-share-weighted endpoint dislocation reversion

factors.trading_idea: Parent A showed that what predicts a 6-bar snap-back is not the size of a peer-relative dislocation but the AGE of the excursion (the propagator's front-loaded remaining-decay fraction g(a)=1-G(a+6)/G(a)), yet it had to guess who was trending via a noisy self-calibrated kappa; Parent B could tell informed single-name prints from basket pressure and quiet quote flicker, but pushed every leg through one common halflife-3 kernel, so it had no clock telling it how much of each leg is still un-relaxed. The child makes the standing displacement an exact exponentially-weighted sum of residual bar returns (dis_t = rho*(dis_{t-1}+u_t)), splits that same filter into idiosyncratic-flow-backed, basket-flow-backed and quiet legs, and — crucially — computes for each leg its own exponentially-weighted mean contribution age via the recursion B_t = rho*(B_{t-1}+A_{t-1}), so a name can carry a fresh quiet push on top of a stale basket push and be scored separately on each. Each fade leg is then scaled by a leg-specific power-law propagator remaining-decay fraction (quiet flicker relaxes fastest: small t0, large beta; basket pressure slower), the idio leg is followed rather than faded, and the fade is gated by leave-one-out peer liveness. The interaction is the edge: age tells you WHEN the reversion lands inside six bars, attribution tells you WHETHER it lands at all, and only the product isolates displacement that is both wrong and repairable within the fixed horizon — neither parent can condition one on the other.
factors.name: Attribution-resolved excursion-age propagator leg relaxation

factors.trading_idea: Reaction to a price move is triggered by *contrast*, not absolute size: discretionary traders and alert/screen-driven algos only respond once a move exceeds a just-noticeable difference (Weber-Fechner), measured in units of the name's own recent typical move, and they discount moves that are already *justified* by tape volume or by a simultaneous market-wide move (attribution). This implies forward return is a non-monotone, sign-flipping function of the same normalised move that linear reversal factors use: sub-threshold moves are uncontested and drift on, moves just past the threshold recruit contrarian liquidity and profit-taking and snap back, and very extreme moves are damped again because they are usually genuine information. The edge survives arbitrage precisely because a linear factor averages the continuation and reversal regimes to near zero, so the signal is invisible unless you know the threshold in the correct per-name units and net many small sub-threshold positions; and because attention/justification is a hard behavioural constraint rather than a capital constraint. Falsified if the relation between the justification-scaled move and the forward 6-bar return is monotone (pure reversal or pure continuation at all magnitudes), or if the crossover threshold does not shift outward when the move is volume-backed or market-wide.
factors.name: Just-noticeable-difference threshold with justification-scaled reaction

factors.trading_idea: The parent showed the quiet-bar / traded-bar drift split carries information, but its return-response regression (R^2 ~ 1e-4 on overlapping 6-bar returns) produced coefficients that were mostly estimation noise, so the factor collapsed onto the slow 'corroborated news' component whose information only resolves out at 24 bars. This child keeps the channel split but (i) orthogonalises the fresh 6-bar push against the name's own immediately preceding 36-bar drift, so what remains is displacement NOT explained by an ongoing trend — i.e. inventory / quote-shading / taker-impact pressure rather than news — and (ii) calibrates how much of that displacement is expected to be handed back over exactly 6 bars using the *persistence of the displacement signal itself* (lag-6 autocorrelation of each rotated component), not a noisy return-response coefficient. Because a mean-reverting component of a cumulative price path must be given back in price, E[r_{t->t+6}] = -(1 - rho_6) x displacement is an accounting identity once rho_6 is known, and rho_6 is estimable with orders of magnitude more precision than a return beta; this also explains the parent's contradicted sign, since at a 60-second offset the only thing that resolves is the transient give-back, which is negatively related to the displacement. The edge survives arbitrage because harvesting it means supplying liquidity into thin, quiet names precisely where the standoff arises, and the persistence weights drift with the liquidity regime so they must be re-estimated continuously.
factors.name: Trend-orthogonal quiet/traded push with persistence-calibrated give-back

factors.trading_idea: The parent proved that thin-volume (quote-driven) mid drift continues while volume-paid drift reverts, but it gated the two legs on a *level* variable (relative activity), which is a slow state — so the payoff peaked at 12 bars rather than 6. The child replaces the gate with a horizon-matched *timing* variable: an unpaid quote displacement only gets validated when the next trade actually arrives, and paid transient impact only decays once the metaorder stops arriving, so the correct weight on each leg is the probability that a trade arrives within exactly the next 6 bars. I estimate that probability per name from a trailing Weibull duration model of inter-arrival times (shape k from the dispersion of log durations, scale from their mean — the Engle–Russell duration/aging logic written out), evaluated conditionally on the currently elapsed silence: names whose next arrival is imminent get the continuation (quiet-drift) leg, names whose flow has just gone dormant get the reversal (traded-drift) leg. The edge persists because harvesting it means crossing the spread precisely in names whose queue is about to be hit, i.e. at the moment liquidity is scarcest, and because the conditional hazard requires modelling duration aging rather than reading a volume level. Falsified if quiet-bar drift continuation is independent of the Weibull-implied 6-bar arrival probability (a constant gate does as well), or if traded-bar drift does not revert faster when the arrival hazard is low.
factors.name: Weibull arrival-hazard gated quiet vs traded drift split

factors.trading_idea: Traded size lives on a lattice: impatient, uninformed liquidity demand (retail market orders, dealer inventory offloads, discretionary clicks) is entered in round lots — 100/200/500 shares — whereas information-driven institutional execution deliberately slices into odd, randomised child orders to hide from the tape. A Fourier probe of the share-count lattice, cos(2*pi*volume/100), therefore measures how 'round' (impatient) versus 'odd' (hidden/sliced) the flow in a bar is, entirely independently of how much volume there was. Mechanism: a price displacement produced while flow is unusually odd-lot-heavy is the footprint of a persistent hidden meta-order and continues over the next minute, while the same displacement produced by unusually round-lot flow is spread-paying impatience with no information content and relaxes. The edge survives arbitrage because virtually every research pipeline aggregates size into notional/turnover and destroys the lattice information, and because the digit signature cannot be removed by the traders who create it: retail and inventory flow is structurally round-lot, and slicing algorithms randomise size precisely to stay hidden.
factors.name: Volume-lattice odd-lot slicing continuation

factors.trading_idea: When a name's mid sits pinned on the price grid for several bars while volume keeps executing, the pin is evidence of a large resting queue at the touch, not of inattention. The break of such a level is therefore informative rather than tick noise: the queue has just been consumed, the next level is thinner, and directional flow is self-exciting (Hawkes-style depletion clustering), so the part of the break that is NOT explained by the name's beta-implied response to the concurrent market move should CONTINUE over the next minute. This is exactly why the parent's declared sign was contradicted: among quiet/pinned names the beta-residual displacement persists instead of reverting, and the variable that separates a real level-clearing from a quote flicker is the volume absorbed while the mid was pinned (flicker breaks on near-zero volume carry no queue information). The edge survives arbitrage because each event is worth a fraction of a tick and can only be harvested by crossing a spread that is at least one tick wide in exactly the low-turnover, grid-bound names where the effect lives; it is falsified if high-absorption breaks show the same or opposite-signed 6-bar IC as zero-absorption breaks.
factors.name: Pinned-level absorption break (beta-residual continuation)

factors.trading_idea: The parent assumed a name's mechanical sensitivity to basket flow equals marketCap/dollar-volume (inverse turnover) and subtracted an unconditional beta as the 'fundamental' loading; that proxy is a slow, static characteristic, which is why the standalone IC is thin. Instead, I estimate the wedge directly from data: split trailing bars into program-footprint bars (the cross-sectional dollar-volume-share deviation tilts toward the capitalisation-weight vector, i.e. a basket is being executed) and information bars, and run two separate trailing zero-intercept regressions of each name's return on the cap-weighted market return. The difference beta_program - beta_information is the *realised* over-push loading that mechanical, weight-proportional liquidity demand imposes on that name in excess of its news beta, and because it is pure inventory pressure it must relax; so I fade the recent program-weighted market displacement in proportion to each name's measured wedge. Falsifiable: the empirically-estimated dual-state wedge must beat the inverse-turnover-minus-beta proxy, the state split must beat using all bars for one beta, and inverting the sign must lose. It survives arbitrage because market-neutral books hedge index exposure with a single unconditional beta, leaving the state-dependent component of systematic loading un-hedged, and harvesting it needs simultaneous multi-name execution inside a one-minute relaxation window.
factors.name: Program-state conditional beta wedge snapback

factors.trading_idea: The sign of the short-horizon return-continuation coefficient is a function of information asymmetry (Llorente-Michaely-Saar-Wang): when a name's order flow is likely informed, a 60-second idiosyncratic displacement is permanent price discovery and continues, whereas when flow is uninformed it is inventory/immediacy pressure and reverts as makers unwind. The child estimates that state *ex ante* from slow, publicly observable fundamentals — bars elapsed since the last point-in-time report step (an information-event clock), the size of the last standardised EPS surprise, and asset intangibility / R&D intensity (hard-to-value names attract informed traders) — instead of a noisy self-calibrated per-name volume-return coefficient, and it deliberately keeps only the *interaction*: the raw displacement main effect and the characteristic tilt are cross-sectionally regressed out at every bar, so what remains is the polarity differential the book cannot already span. The edge persists because it is not a directional forecast anyone can arbitrage on its own: the reversal leg is compensation for supplying immediacy to uninformed flow, and joining a quarterly filing clock to a 10-second impact state is an unattractive data-plumbing problem for fast traders.
factors.name: Fundamental information-asymmetry polarity gate on idiosyncratic impact

factors.trading_idea: For a one-dimensional diffusion the stationary Fokker-Planck solution implies mu(x) ~ (sigma^2/2) * d ln p(x)/dx, so the local drift of a price can be read off the *shape* of its recent occupation measure rather than from its distance to a mean: price is pulled toward the nearest peak of the trailing volume-at-price density, where resting inventory and limit-order mass have accumulated. I estimate that log-density gradient non-parametrically with a Gaussian kernel over the last 60 bars, weighting each visited price by the volume traded there and by an exponential memory decay, which yields a *saturating* restoring force toward the nearest liquidity cluster instead of a linear pull toward the window mean. Because the linear distance-to-VWAP reversal is heavily mined, I regress the kernel drift on the volume-weighted linear deviation over a trailing 240-bar window and keep only the residual — i.e. the drift information contained in the *skew/multimodality* of the occupation profile — and shrink names whose current price sits in a low-occupancy void, where the density estimate is unreliable. The edge should persist because extracting higher moments of a per-name occupation measure every 10 seconds is computationally awkward relative to the trivial VWAP-gap trade, and the mispricing is of the order of a fraction of the spread, so capacity is small; it is falsified if the residual carries no IC once distance-to-VWAP is removed, or if the low-occupancy gate fails to discriminate.
factors.name: Occupation-density mode pull (volume-at-price profile skew wedge)

factors.trading_idea: The parent's realized sign says the opposite of its story, and the reason is that resting depth accumulates *inside* the price region the mid has been occupying and is thin *outside* it: a high local-time (coiled) name whose 6-bar move just carried it out of its occupation band is not being absorbed, it is escaping into a shallow book, so the move extends; a low local-time name has already wandered, so its 6-bar move is a late-stage extension that snaps back. The child expresses this as an event, not a state: it measures the signed distance by which log-mid has escaped its trailing 15%/85% occupation band, keeps only escapes that are FRESH (price was still inside the band within the last 6 bars), and gates them by a conviction score that is positive when the band was abnormally tight relative to the sqrt(N)-random-walk benchmark (a genuine coil) and when the escape carries abnormal participation (6-bar volume above the name's own norm) — thin-volume escapes are quote noise and are faded by the same gate. Because the freshness weight kills persistent trends, the response is concentrated in the first minute after ignition rather than accumulating over 20+ minutes as in the parent, and the final signal is cross-sectionally orthogonalised each bar against the plain standardized 6-bar move so it cannot be spanned by momentum/reversal factors. The edge should survive arbitrage because it is caused by the same shallow depth that limits its capacity, and because capturing it requires jointly estimating an occupation-concentration statistic, an event-time freshness clock and relative participation per name in real time for a few ticks per episode.
factors.name: Value-area escape: freshness x coil-and-participation gate

factors.trading_idea: A mid-price that walks in bars with (near-)zero prints is a maker repricing an untested reservation quote; the walk continues only for as long as no trade arrives to challenge it, and once a trade does arrive only the permanent share of the walk survives. So the correct 6-bar forecast is not a filtered level or rate of the silent drift, but the drift rate multiplied by the *expected number of still-silent bars inside the next six*, computed from a trailing, age-dependent trade-arrival hazard (silence spells age: hazard differs for fresh vs. long-lived quiet), minus the transient share of the already-accumulated untested displacement times the probability that it gets tested within the horizon. This makes the signal explicitly horizon-matched at the fixed 6-bar offset — names in a young, low-hazard silence spell get the full six bars of extrapolation, names whose spell is about to break or has just broken get the snapback instead. The edge persists because harvesting it requires quoting in thin, rarely-traded names where the round-trip spread cost is of the same order as the 60-second drift, so fast arbitrageurs cannot lift it away.
factors.name: Silence-spell hazard: survival-weighted quote-ramp extrapolation

factors.trading_idea: Large institutional programs (factor-model risk hedges, style rotations, quant basket executions) are entered over many minutes, so their footprint in the cross-section is a *characteristic-aligned* return pattern whose residual, unexecuted quantity keeps pushing the same characteristic portfolios for the next few minutes; by contrast single-name liquidity shocks mean-revert. I therefore measure, bar by bar, the realized return of sector-neutral characteristic (size / value / quality / margin / leverage / growth) portfolios, estimate how persistent each style's return is at exactly the 6-bar offset via a trailing lag-6 autocorrelation of 6-bar style returns, and project the persistence-weighted style drift back onto each name's loadings. The edge survives arbitrage because it is a few basis points per minute spread across a whole basket: harvesting it requires trading many names simultaneously while staying market- and sector-neutral, it is invisible to single-name reversal/momentum screens (the signal is orthogonal to a name's own recent return by construction of the projection), and daily factor investors do not trade at the minute frequency. Falsifiable: if minute-scale style-portfolio returns carry no lag-6 autocorrelation, the projected drift has zero IC.
factors.name: Within-sector fundamental style-flow persistence

factors.trading_idea: A name that responds to market information with a distributed lag owes a computable amount of catch-up to market returns it has already observed, but the lag profile is not sign-symmetric: inventory risk, short-sale/borrow frictions and defensive quote-widening make market makers reprice a name more sluggishly against down-market impulses than up-market ones, so the impulse response must be estimated as a *semi-kernel* (separate loadings on the positive and negative parts of the market return at each lag 1..6). Folding each semi-kernel against the horizon-matched trailing sum of the corresponding signed market path gives an exactly horizon-matched (L = H = 6) forecast of the catch-up still owed, decomposed into an up-leg and a down-leg. The parent's stream-paired Rice sign-flip machinery is replaced by a far cheaper and more direct trust statistic: the *coherence* of the two legs, |up+down| / (|up|+|down|) — when the net debt is the small residual of two large offsetting legs it is mostly estimation noise and must be shrunk, when both legs point the same way the debt is a genuine one-directional lag. Edge persists because the asymmetry requires hundreds of bars of per-sign, per-lag estimation with cross-sectional shrinkage and each instance pays only a fraction of the spread, so latency arbitrage only harvests the largest cases while the short-sale/inventory frictions that generate the asymmetry are structural.
factors.name: Signed Semi-Kernel Owed Market Catch-Up (coherence trusted)

factors.trading_idea: Parent B shows that basket/program flow displaces each name in proportion to cap-weight-per-unit-depth (inverse dollar turnover) in excess of beta, and that this mechanical over-push relaxes; what it cannot see is whether the pushed price ended up somewhere a counterparty exists. I supply that state with a Rice-type local-time estimator that needs no bandwidth constant: the number of times the trailing path crossed the price level the name is standing on right now (flats carried by the last non-zero sign). Zero crossings means the program flow has trended the mid into fresh, untested territory — unabsorbed liquidity demand with no resting queue to restore it, so the over-push is at its most fadeable; a level in the top quartile of its own crossing history is an already-absorbed, two-sided, repeatedly revisited anchor where the residual displacement is the footprint of persistent one-sided interest and continues rather than snapping back. The interaction is the edge: B fades every program push with identical intensity regardless of whether inventory exists at the level, while the crossing statistic alone has no way to know which displacements were mechanically manufactured by weight-proportional basket flow rather than by information, so only the product identifies unbacked mechanical push.
factors.name: Terminal-level crossing gated basket over-push split
